text: : Mục tiêu chính của nghiên cứu này là phân tích ảnh hưởng của đa dạng hóa (ĐDH) thu nhập đến rủi ro phá sản (RRPS) của các ngân hàng thương mại Việt Nam (NHTM), trong đó mức độ ĐDH thu nhập được đo lường thông qua chỉ số HHI (The Herfindahl-Hirschman Index) và RRPS của ngân hàng được đo lường thông qua chỉ số Z-Score. Kết quả hồi quy dựa trên phương pháp ước lượng moment tổng quát (GMM) thực hiện với bộ dữ liệu được thu thập từ 28 NHTM Việt Nam giai đoạn 2011–2020 cho thấy việc ĐDH thu nhập không có ảnh hưởng đến RRPS đối với các NHTM Việt Nam. Thay vào đó, kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy RRPS của ngân hàng bị ảnh hưởng chủ yếu bởi các yếu tố khác thuộc về đặc điểm ngân hàng như là RRPS của năm trước, an toàn vốn, tỷ lệ chi phí hoạt động, quy mô ngân hàng và tốc độ tăng trưởng tài sản.

Camera traps are increasingly used for wildlife monitoring, generating vast image datasets. Manually identifying species within these images is time-consuming and costly. This paper presents a first step towards automating mammal species recognition in camera trap images from a European temperate forest using artificial intelligence. We developed and evaluated several convolutional neural network (CNN) models, including transfer learning approaches using pre-trained weights. Our best performing model, a fine-tuned ResNet50, achieved an overall accuracy of 87% in identifying seven common mammal species. Results demonstrate the potential for AI-powered automation to significantly reduce the workload associated with camera trap data analysis, facilitating more efficient and large-scale wildlife monitoring efforts. Future work will focus on improving performance in challenging conditions, such as poor lighting and occlusions, and expanding the model to recognize a broader range of species and behaviors. Keywords: camera traps, species recognition, artificial intelligence, convolutional neural networks, wildlife monitoring, ResNet50, automation.

Nghiên cứu về hiệu quả hoạt động của các ngân hàng Ấn Độ sử dụng phương pháp phân tích bao dữ liệu (DEA) để đánh giá hiệu quả tương đối của các ngân hàng khác nhau. Dữ liệu được thu thập từ các báo cáo tài chính của các ngân hàng trong giai đoạn nghiên cứu, tập trung vào các yếu tố đầu vào như chi phí hoạt động, số lượng nhân viên và tài sản cố định, cùng các yếu tố đầu ra như tổng dư nợ, thu nhập từ lãi và phí dịch vụ. Kết quả phân tích cho thấy sự khác biệt đáng kể về hiệu quả giữa các ngân hàng, với một số ngân hàng hoạt động hiệu quả hơn so với các ngân hàng khác. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến hiệu quả hoạt động của ngân hàng, bao gồm quy mô ngân hàng, cơ cấu sở hữu và môi trường kinh tế vĩ mô. Các ngân hàng có quy mô lớn hơn và hoạt động trong môi trường kinh tế ổn định thường có xu hướng hoạt động hiệu quả hơn. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp thông tin hữu ích cho các nhà quản lý ngân hàng và các nhà hoạch định chính sách trong việc cải thiện hiệu quả hoạt động của ngành ngân hàng Ấn Độ.

Phát triển du lịch cộng đồng (DLCD) tại huyện Lang Chánh, Thanh Hóa đang đối mặt với nhiều thách thức pháp lý và thực tiễn. Việc thiếu quy hoạch tổng thể, chồng chéo trong quản lý đất đai, và sự hạn chế về nguồn lực đầu tư đang cản trở sự phát triển bền vững của loại hình du lịch này. Nghiên cứu cho thấy, cần có một khung pháp lý rõ ràng, sự phối hợp chặt chẽ giữa các bên liên quan, và sự tham gia tích cực của cộng đồng địa phương để DLCD thực sự mang lại lợi ích kinh tế - xã hội, bảo tồn văn hóa, và bảo vệ môi trường. Các giải pháp được đề xuất bao gồm việc hoàn thiện cơ chế chính sách, nâng cao năng lực cho người dân, và tăng cường quảng bá, xúc tiến du lịch.

Nuôi ăn qua sonde nhằm duy trì dinh dưỡng đường tiêu hóa, bảo vệ chức năng sinh lý hệ tiêu hóa, cung cấp dinh dưỡng sớm cho người bệnh nặng. Đây là biện pháp hiệu quả được khuyến nghị áp dụng trong vòng 48 giờ sau nhập viện. Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện nhằm đánh giá hiệu quả nuôi ăn qua sonde bằng súp nhỏ giọt cho người bệnh tại Bệnh viện Hữu nghị Đa khoa Nghệ An. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp tiến cứu và mô tả trên 255 người bệnh từ tháng 4/2022 đến tháng 6/2022 tại các Khoa: Hồi sức Tích cực, Hồi sức Tích cực Ngoại khoa, Chống độc, Nhiễm khuẩn Tổng hợp, Bỏng, Ngoại tiêu hóa và Trung tâm Đột quỵ. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy, năng lượng được cung cấp ngày đầu là 1.015,2 kcal, ngày thứ 7 là 1.409 kcal, tỷ lệ suy dinh dưỡng theo chỉ số MUAC (chu vi vòng cánh tay) tăng từ 6,7 lên 8,2%, chỉ số albumin huyết thanh giảm từ 78,6 xuống 76,2%, chỉ số SGA (công cụ đánh giá tổng thể chủ quan) tăng từ 54,9 lên 77,6%, năng lượng cung cấp tương đối đầy đủ và tình trạng suy dinh dưỡng được cải thiện.

Trong thiết kế nghiên cứu định tính, việc thu thập dữ liệu đóng vai trò then chốt, thường được thực hiện thông qua phỏng vấn sâu, thảo luận nhóm tập trung và quan sát. Phỏng vấn sâu cho phép người nghiên cứu khám phá quan điểm cá nhân một cách chi tiết, trong khi thảo luận nhóm tập trung tạo cơ hội để tìm hiểu sự tương tác xã hội và quan điểm đa dạng. Quan sát cung cấp cái nhìn trực tiếp về hành vi và bối cảnh tự nhiên của đối tượng nghiên cứu. Quá trình phân tích dữ liệu định tính bao gồm các bước như làm quen với dữ liệu, tạo mã, tìm kiếm chủ đề và diễn giải. Các phần mềm hỗ trợ như NVivo giúp quản lý và phân tích lượng lớn dữ liệu văn bản. Đảm bảo tính tin cậy và giá trị của nghiên cứu định tính đòi hỏi sự cẩn trọng trong từng bước, từ thiết kế nghiên cứu đến thu thập và phân tích dữ liệu, cũng như việc sử dụng các kỹ thuật kiểm tra tính hợp lệ như kiểm tra thành viên và đối chứng chéo.

This paper introduces a novel approach to molecule representation learning, incorporating chemical reaction awareness to enhance the accuracy and applicability of molecular embeddings. The objective is to develop a model that can effectively capture the complex relationships between molecules and their reaction pathways. Our method utilizes a graph neural network architecture, combined with a reaction-aware attention mechanism, to learn molecular representations that are informed by chemical reaction data. The results demonstrate significant improvements in molecular property prediction and reaction outcome forecasting, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. Key findings include the ability to identify crucial reaction intermediates and predict reaction yields with high accuracy. The proposed approach has important implications for drug discovery, materials science, and other fields where chemical reactions play a critical role. By leveraging chemical reaction awareness, our model contributes to the development of more accurate and informative molecule representations, enabling better decision-making in molecular design and optimization. Relevant keywords: molecule representation learning, chemical reactions, graph neural networks, reaction-aware attention, molecular property prediction.

Viêm thân đốt sống đĩa đệm thắt lưng do vi khuẩn Salmonella spp ESBL (-), AmpC (-) gây ra là một bệnh nhiễm trùng hiếm gặp nhưng nguy hiểm, có thể dẫn đến các biến chứng nghiêm trọng nếu không được chẩn đoán và điều trị kịp thời. Trường hợp này đặc biệt phức tạp do vi khuẩn Salmonella spp mang các đặc tính kháng kháng sinh ESBL (-) và AmpC (-), gây khó khăn trong việc lựa chọn phác đồ điều trị phù hợp. Bệnh nhân thường trải qua các triệu chứng như đau lưng dữ dội, sốt và suy giảm chức năng thần kinh. Chẩn đoán chính xác đòi hỏi sự kết hợp của các xét nghiệm lâm sàng, hình ảnh học như MRI và xét nghiệm vi sinh để xác định tác nhân gây bệnh và đánh giá mức độ kháng kháng sinh. Điều trị thường bao gồm sử dụng kháng sinh đường tĩnh mạch kéo dài, kết hợp với các biện pháp hỗ trợ và phẫu thuật nếu cần thiết để giải quyết các biến chứng như áp xe hoặc chèn ép thần kinh. Việc theo dõi chặt chẽ và điều trị đa chuyên khoa là rất quan trọng để đảm bảo kết quả tốt cho bệnh nhân.

Đổi mới quốc gia và xuất khẩu đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc thúc đẩy đầu tư doanh nghiệp, đặc biệt trong bối cảnh toàn cầu hóa. Nghiên cứu thực nghiệm từ bộ dữ liệu cho thấy, các quốc gia áp dụng chính sách đổi mới hiệu quả thường thu hút được nguồn vốn đầu tư lớn hơn, nhờ cải thiện năng suất và nâng cao năng lực cạnh tranh. Xuất khẩu cũng là yếu tố then chốt, giúp doanh nghiệp mở rộng thị trường, tăng doanh thu và tạo động lực đầu tư vào công nghệ, nhân lực. Tuy nhiên, mối quan hệ này phụ thuộc vào nhiều yếu tố như môi trường kinh doanh, chính sách hỗ trợ và khả năng thích ứng của doanh nghiệp. Kết quả nghiên cứu nhấn mạnh sự cần thiết của việc kết hợp hài hòa giữa đổi mới quốc gia và chiến lược xuất khẩu để tối ưu hóa đầu tư doanh nghiệp, góp phần phát triển kinh tế bền vững.

Vữa xây dựng sử dụng tro đáy của nhà máy nhiệt điện thay thế cát đang trở thành một giải pháp tiềm năng trong ngành xây dựng nhờ vào những tính chất vật lý và cơ học ưu việt. Tro đáy, một sản phẩm phụ từ quá trình đốt than, không chỉ giúp giảm thiểu ô nhiễm môi trường mà còn cải thiện độ bền và khả năng chống thấm của vữa. Các nghiên cứu cho thấy vữa này có khả năng chịu nén cao, độ dẻo tốt và khả năng kết dính vượt trội so với vữa truyền thống. Việc sử dụng tro đáy không chỉ tiết kiệm chi phí nguyên liệu mà còn góp phần vào việc tái chế chất thải, thúc đẩy phát triển bền vững trong xây dựng. Tuy nhiên, để tối ưu hóa hiệu quả, cần có các nghiên cứu sâu hơn về tỷ lệ pha trộn và các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến tính chất của vữa.

Chính quyền TP.HCM đang tiến hành thu hồi đất để phát triển tuyến Metro số 2, một trong những dự án giao thông trọng điểm nhằm giảm ùn tắc và nâng cao chất lượng vận tải công cộng trong thành phố. Tuyến Metro này sẽ kết nối các khu vực quan trọng, từ Bến Thành đến Tham Lương, với tổng chiều dài khoảng 11,3 km và 10 ga. Việc thu hồi đất được thực hiện theo quy định của pháp luật, nhằm đảm bảo tiến độ thi công và hoàn thành dự án đúng thời hạn. Dự kiến, tuyến Metro số 2 sẽ không chỉ cải thiện giao thông mà còn góp phần thúc đẩy phát triển kinh tế, nâng cao giá trị bất động sản và cải thiện môi trường sống cho người dân. Chính quyền thành phố cam kết sẽ thực hiện công tác bồi thường, hỗ trợ cho các hộ dân bị ảnh hưởng một cách công bằng và minh bạch.

The decentralized architecture and inherent technical complexity of Web3 present considerable barriers for non-technical users striving to interact with decentralized applications (DApps), thus significantly impeding the mainstream adoption of these novel technologies. For many, understanding concepts such as decentralized identity management, complex cryptographic keys, and blockchain interactions is far from intuitive; the requirement to handle private keys, perform manual backup processes, or navigate convoluted onboarding procedures frequently deters average users. To bridge this gap and foster inclusivity, the proposed approach leverages a combination of smart contracts, the Pedersen Distributed Key Generation (DKG) protocol, and Shamir secret sharing. By integrating these cryptographic tools, the solution aims to offload technical burdens from users—secret management, key recovery, and transaction approval can be abstracted behind user-friendly interfaces. Smart contracts automate essential Web3 features while the Pedersen DKG protocol distributes trust and strengthens cryptographic resilience, and Shamir secret sharing ensures that sensitive data is never exposed or stored in a single vulnerable location. Collectively, these advancements not only simplify Web3 onboarding and ongoing management for everyday individuals but also significantly elevate the standards of privacy and security, making decentralized technologies approachable and secure for a much broader audience.

This paper addresses the challenge of domain adaptation in machine learning, focusing on the unsupervised transfer of knowledge between distinct but related domains. The primary objective is to develop a technique that ensures the model generalizes well to a target domain with no labeled data, by learning domain-invariant features. Methods: We propose a novel framework leveraging domain-invariant adversarial learning to bridge the gap between source and target domains. Our approach employs an adversarial neural network architecture where a feature extractor is trained to minimize the classification error on the source domain, whilst simultaneously maximizing domain classification error, thereby promoting domain-invariant feature learning. This framework does not require target domain labels, thus operating under unsupervised conditions. Results: The proposed method was evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating improved performance over existing unsupervised domain adaptation techniques. Our approach showed a marked reduction in domain discrepancy and achieved superior classification accuracy within the target domain when compared to state-of-the-art models. It also exhibited robustness against diverse domain shifts, underscoring its effectiveness. Conclusion: This research advances the field of unsupervised domain adaptation by introducing a domain-invariant adversarial learning mechanism, which outperforms traditional methods by effectively transferring knowledge without the need for target domain labels. The results highlight the potential of adversarial strategies in achieving seamless domain adaptation, paving the way for practical applications in various cross-domain scenarios, including vision and language tasks. Keywords: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation, Domain-Invariant Features, Adversarial Learning, Machine Learning, Neural Networks.

Kernel Sparse Coding (KSC) has emerged as a powerful tool for nonlinear data representation. However, traditional KSC methods often suffer from instability and sensitivity to parameter selection, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper introduces Confident Kernel Sparse Coding and Dictionary Learning (CKSCDL), a novel framework designed to enhance the robustness and accuracy of KSC. CKSCDL incorporates a confidence-weighted regularization term that adaptively adjusts the impact of each kernel atom based on its relevance and reliability during the sparse coding process. Simultaneously, we learn an optimal dictionary that minimizes reconstruction error and promotes sparsity through an efficient alternating optimization scheme. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CKSCDL significantly outperforms existing KSC methods and other state-of-the-art sparse coding techniques in terms of classification accuracy and reconstruction quality. The proposed approach offers improved stability and generalization capability, making it suitable for various applications, including image recognition, signal processing, and data mining. Key words: Kernel Sparse Coding, Dictionary Learning, Sparse Representation, Nonlinear Data Analysis, Machine Learning.

Few-shot learning (FSL) has emerged as a promising approach to address the challenge of training machine learning models with limited labeled data. However, a critical issue in FSL is the presence of data shift, where the distribution of training data significantly differs from that of test data, leading to degraded model performance. This paper proposes a novel framework that leverages knowledge graphs (KGs) to combat data shift in few-shot learning scenarios. By integrating structured domain knowledge from KGs, our approach enhances the model's ability to generalize across diverse and unseen data distributions. We introduce a graph-based embedding mechanism that aligns the semantic relationships between training and test samples, effectively mitigating the impact of data shift. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing FSL techniques, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. The proposed framework not only addresses the data shift problem but also provides a scalable and interpretable solution for real-world applications where labeled data is scarce. This research contributes to advancing the field of few-shot learning by bridging the gap between limited data availability and model generalization, with potential applications in domains such as healthcare, natural language processing, and computer vision. **Keywords**: Few-shot learning, data shift, knowledge graph, graph embeddings, generalization, machine learning.

This paper presents a novel approach to object detection, introducing a Layout Transfer Network (LTN) that enables context-aware detection by transferring knowledge of object layouts across different scenes. The objective is to improve detection accuracy by incorporating spatial relationships and contextual information. Our method employs a deep learning-based approach, utilizing a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to model object interactions and scene layouts. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our LTN, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. Key findings include significant improvements in detection accuracy, particularly for objects with complex spatial relationships. The proposed LTN has important implications for various applications, including autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics, where context-aware object detection is crucial. Our research contributes to the advancement of object detection techniques, highlighting the importance of incorporating contextual information and spatial relationships. Relevant keywords: object detection, context-aware, layout transfer, deep learning, CNNs, GNNs.

A labeled graph is a directed graph in which both vertices, referred to as states, and edges bear labels. Each edge connects an initial state, or start vertex, to a terminal state, known as the end vertex. For a given state v, in-edges are the set of edges for which v is the terminal state, while out-edges comprise those where v acts as the initial state.

This paper introduces a novel benchmark for knowledge-augmented visual question answering, termed Select, Substitute, Search (SSS). The objective is to evaluate the ability of visual question answering models to incorporate external knowledge and reason about complex scenarios. Our approach involves designing a comprehensive dataset that requires models to select relevant knowledge, substitute it into the question context, and search for the correct answer. We propose a new evaluation metric that assesses the model's ability to effectively utilize external knowledge and demonstrate its superiority over existing metrics. Our results show that state-of-the-art models struggle to perform well on the SSS benchmark, highlighting the need for more advanced knowledge-augmentation techniques. The SSS benchmark contributes to the field by providing a challenging testbed for evaluating the limits of current visual question answering models and encouraging the development of more sophisticated knowledge-augmentation methods. Key contributions include the introduction of a new benchmark dataset, a novel evaluation metric, and insights into the challenges of knowledge-augmented visual question answering, with relevant keywords including visual question answering, knowledge augmentation, benchmarking, and multimodal reasoning.

We present the Multiview Extended Video with Activities (MEVA) dataset, a new and very-large-scale dataset for human activity recognition. Existing security datasets either focus on activity counts by aggregating public video disseminated due to its content, which typically excludes same-scene background video, or they achieve persistence by observing public areas and thus cannot control for activity content. Our dataset is over 9300 hours of untrimmed, continuous video, scripted to include diverse, simultaneous activities, along with spontaneous background activity. We have annotated 144 hours for 37 activity types, marking bounding boxes of actors and props. Our collection observed approximately 100 actors performing scripted scenarios and spontaneous background activity over a three-week period at an access-controlled venue, collecting in multiple modalities with overlapping and non-overlapping indoor and outdoor viewpoints. The resulting data includes video from 38 RGB and thermal IR cameras, 42 hours of UAV footage, as well as GPS locations for the actors. 122 hours of annotation are sequestered in support of the NIST Activity in Extended Video (ActEV) challenge; the other 22 hours of annotation and the corresponding video are available on our website, along with an additional 306 hours of ground camera data, 4.6 hours of UAV data, and 9.6 hours of GPS logs. Additional derived data includes camera models geo-registering the outdoor cameras and a dense 3D point cloud model of the outdoor scene. The data was collected with IRB oversight and approval and released under a CC-BY-4.0 license.

We propose a metric, Layer Saturation, defined as the proportion of the number of eigenvalues needed to explain 99% of the variance of the latent representations, for analyzing the learned representations of neural network layers. Saturation is based on spectral analysis and can be computed efficiently, making live analysis of the representations practical during training. We provide an outlook for future applications of this metric by outlining the behaviour of layer saturation in different neural architectures and problems. We further show that saturation is related to the generalization and predictive performance of neural networks.

This paper addresses the challenge of generating realistic images from scene graphs, focusing on improving the contextualized layout of objects to enhance visual coherence and semantic accuracy. The objective is to bridge the gap between structured scene descriptions and high-quality image synthesis, ensuring that generated images accurately reflect the relationships and attributes defined in the scene graph. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach that integrates a contextualized object layout refinement module into the image generation pipeline. This module leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to model object relationships and refine their spatial arrangements, ensuring better alignment with the scene graph's semantic structure. Additionally, we employ a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to synthesize high-resolution images from the refined layouts. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in both visual quality and semantic fidelity compared to existing methods, as validated by quantitative metrics and user studies. The proposed approach not only advances the state-of-the-art in scene graph-to-image generation but also offers practical applications in areas such as virtual reality, content creation, and human-computer interaction. Key contributions include the introduction of a context-aware layout refinement mechanism and a robust framework for generating semantically consistent images from complex scene descriptions. **Keywords**: Scene graph, image generation, graph neural networks, generative adversarial networks, object layout refinement, semantic fidelity.

This paper proposes a novel approach to graph neural networks, introducing Dynamic Graph Convolutional Networks (DGCNs) to effectively model complex, dynamic relationships in graph-structured data. The objective is to improve the representation learning of graphs with evolving topology and node/edge attributes. Our method employs a dynamic convolutional layer that adaptively updates graph filters based on the current graph state, allowing for more accurate predictions and better handling of temporal dependencies. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of DGCNs over existing graph convolutional networks in various tasks, including node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. The key findings highlight the importance of capturing dynamic graph patterns and the potential applications of DGCNs in real-world scenarios, such as social network analysis, traffic forecasting, and recommendation systems. By leveraging the strengths of graph neural networks and dynamic modeling, DGCNs contribute to the advancement of graph representation learning, enabling more accurate and robust analysis of complex, dynamic systems. Key keywords: Graph Convolutional Networks, Dynamic Graphs, Representation Learning, Node Classification, Link Prediction.

Một nghiên cứu thực nghiệm mới tại tỉnh đã chỉ ra rằng, các nhân tố như nhận thức về môi trường, giá cả, và sự ảnh hưởng của gia đình đều đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc quyết định hành vi tiêu dùng xanh của người tiêu dùng. Xây dựng cơ sở tri thức ngữ nghĩa và chatbot về du lịch Hà Nội là một hệ thống thông tin được thiết kế để cung cấp thông tin và hỗ trợ cho khách du lịch khi đến thăm thành phố Hà Nội. Hệ thống này dựa trên cơ sở tri thức ngữ nghĩa được xây dựng dựa trên các khái niệm và định nghĩa liên quan đến du lịch, văn hóa và lịch sử của Hà Nội. Hệ thống này bao gồm hai phần chính: cơ sở tri thức ngữ nghĩa và chatbot. This paper introduces a novel imaging system, the Dark Flash Normal Camera, designed to capture high-quality images under low-light conditions while minimizing visual disturbance. Traditional flash photography often produces intrusive light, which can be disruptive in sensitive environments. The proposed system leverages a combination of near-infrared (NIR) and ultraviolet (UV) illumination, paired with advanced computational algorithms, to reconstruct normal RGB images without the need for visible light. The approach involves a custom hardware setup and a deep learning-based image reconstruction pipeline that translates NIR and UV data into photorealistic RGB outputs. Experimental results demonstrate that the Dark Flash Normal Camera achieves comparable image quality to conventional flash photography while significantly reducing light pollution. The system’s performance is validated through quantitative metrics such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM), as well as qualitative user studies. This research contributes to the field of computational photography by offering a non-intrusive, energy-efficient imaging solution with potential applications in surveillance, wildlife monitoring, and medical imaging. The proposed method represents a significant advancement in low-light imaging, combining hardware innovation with state-of-the-art machine learning techniques. **Keywords**: low-light imaging, computational photography, near-infrared, ultraviolet, deep learning, image reconstruction.

Video super-resolution (VSR) aims to enhance the resolution of low-resolution videos, a crucial preprocessing step for action recognition. This paper introduces a novel two-stream framework tailored to improve action recognition performance via VSR. Our method employs a spatial stream to reconstruct high-resolution video frames and a temporal stream to preserve crucial motion information. Specifically, we propose a recurrent neural network architecture with enhanced motion compensation to effectively exploit temporal dependencies. Furthermore, we introduce a joint training strategy that integrates action recognition loss to guide the VSR network towards generating features more relevant for action classification. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including UCF101 and HMDB51, demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art super-resolution performance and significantly improves the accuracy of action recognition compared to existing VSR methods. The proposed framework offers a promising direction for enhancing video analysis tasks by integrating task-specific guidance into the super-resolution process. Keywords: Video Super-Resolution, Action Recognition, Two-Stream Network, Motion Compensation, Deep Learning.

This paper introduces RetainVis, a visual analytics system that leverages interpretable and interactive recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to analyze electronic medical records (EMRs). The objective is to improve the understanding and interpretation of clinical predictions made by RNNs, enabling healthcare professionals to make more informed decisions. Our approach combines a novel RNN architecture with interactive visualization techniques, allowing users to explore and understand the contributions of individual input features to the predicted outcomes. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of RetainVis in identifying meaningful patterns and relationships in EMRs, outperforming traditional machine learning methods in terms of accuracy and interpretability. Our system provides a unique framework for visualizing and interacting with RNNs, facilitating the discovery of new insights and improving the trustworthiness of clinical predictions. The contributions of this research include the development of a novel RNN architecture, an interactive visualization framework, and a comprehensive evaluation methodology, highlighting the potential of RetainVis to enhance the analysis and interpretation of EMRs in clinical practice, with key applications in healthcare analytics, medical informatics, and artificial intelligence.

Glass-like object segmentation presents unique challenges due to the transparent and reflective properties of such objects, which often blend into their surroundings. This paper introduces an enhanced boundary learning framework designed to improve the accuracy and robustness of glass-like object segmentation in complex scenes. The proposed approach leverages a dual-stream network architecture that combines global contextual information with fine-grained boundary details. A novel boundary-aware loss function is introduced to explicitly guide the model in learning precise object boundaries, addressing the limitations of traditional segmentation methods. Additionally, a synthetic dataset augmentation strategy is employed to enhance the model's generalization capabilities across diverse real-world scenarios. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing approaches in terms of both boundary precision and segmentation accuracy. The framework's ability to handle challenging cases, such as overlapping objects and varying lighting conditions, highlights its practical applicability in fields like robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous driving. This research contributes a significant advancement in glass-like object segmentation, offering a scalable and effective solution for real-world applications. **Keywords**: glass-like object segmentation, boundary learning, dual-stream network, boundary-aware loss, synthetic dataset augmentation, computer vision.

This graduation thesis addresses the growing need for effective English language learning solutions, particularly in the context of increasing global communication and technological advancements. Medical image processing plays a crucial role in modern healthcare, enabling accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. Deep learning techniques have recently revolutionized this field, offering unprecedented capabilities for image analysis. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of deep learning methods applied to medical image processing, encompassing various modalities such as X-ray, MRI, CT, and ultrasound. We examine commonly used deep learning architectures, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and transformers, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses in specific medical imaging tasks like image segmentation, object detection, and disease classification. Furthermore, we address key challenges currently hindering the widespread adoption of deep learning in clinical practice, such as limited labeled data, dataset bias, the need for explainable AI, and regulatory hurdles. Finally, we discuss promising future research directions, including federated learning, self-supervised learning, and the integration of multi-modal data, to overcome these challenges and unlock the full potential of deep learning for improved medical imaging and patient care. Keywords: Deep Learning, Medical Image Processing, Convolutional Neural Networks, Image Segmentation, Disease Classification, Artificial Intelligence.

The unit of information is called Summary Content Unit (SCU), i.e. words or phrases that are represent single facts. The Pyramid Evaluation method is based on the intuition that relevance of a SCU can be determined by the number of (ground-truth) reference summaries that include it. PRIMERA utilizes the Pyramid Evaluation method to identify salient sentences for masking. In particular, for a cluster of multiple documents, the more documents an SCU appears in, the more salient that information should be to the cluster. However, in the original Pyramid Evaluation, SCUs are human-evaluated. This is large-time consuming and expensive.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào hàm mô-men sinh (MGF) như một công cụ mạnh mẽ để phân tích xác suất và thống kê. MGF, về cơ bản là một hàm toán học, cho phép xác định các đặc trưng quan trọng của một biến ngẫu nhiên, bao gồm các mô-men như trung bình và phương sai một cách hiệu quả. This paper introduces MAGNet, a novel Multi-agent Graph Network framework designed to enhance deep multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). The primary objective of MAGNet is to address the challenges of complex agent interactions and dynamic environments commonly encountered in cooperative and competitive multi-agent tasks. MAGNet models agents as nodes in a learnable graph structure, where edges dynamically represent interactions based on context-sensitive features. Using graph neural networks, the framework enables efficient aggregation and dissemination of information among agents, fostering improved coordination and scalable policy learning. We evaluate MAGNet on a suite of benchmark MARL environments, including both continuous and discrete domains. Experimental results demonstrate that MAGNet significantly outperforms existing baselines in terms of sample efficiency, convergence speed, and final performance, particularly in scenarios with a large number of interacting agents. Our findings underscore MAGNet’s ability to extract and utilize latent relational structures, leading to more robust and generalizable multi-agent behaviors. This work presents a substantial advancement in MARL, with potential applications in autonomous robotics, distributed control systems, and cooperative AI. Key keywords: multi-agent reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, deep learning, coordination, scalability, MAGNet.

This paper presents an end-to-end approach for super-resolution imaging by revisiting and extending the classical Lucas-Kanade framework to operate directly on raw image bursts. The primary objective is to enhance image quality and detail extraction in scenarios where multiple low-resolution raw images are available, such as in consumer camera applications or scientific imaging. Our method integrates a modernized motion estimation technique with deep learning-based reconstruction, enabling accurate alignment and fusion of raw image sequences without the need for demosaicing as a preprocessing step. Experimental results on standard burst super-resolution benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements in both perceptual quality and quantitative metrics compared to state-of-the-art methods. The proposed system is robust to challenging real-world conditions, such as non-uniform camera motion and variable lighting, and can be efficiently deployed on edge devices. This work establishes a new paradigm for burst super-resolution by combining the strengths of classical optical flow with end-to-end learning, offering substantial benefits for computational photography, mobile imaging, and other applications requiring high-fidelity image recovery from raw data. Keywords: super-resolution, image bursts, Lucas-Kanade, deep learning, raw images, optical flow, computational photography.

The co-adaptive system exhibits superior scalability and robustness when tested across a variety of benchmark environments, significantly reducing inference time while maintaining high levels of accuracy and decision quality. Comparative analyses with existing methods underscore the model's enhanced adaptability and resource utilization. Conclusion/Implications: The co-adaptation of algorithmic and implementational innovations represents a significant advancement in the field of deep reinforcement learning. By offering a path towards more efficient and scalable DRL solutions, this research contributes to the broader movement of rendering AI technologies more practical and accessible in diverse applications. Key Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Inference, Co-Adaptation, Algorithmic Innovations, Implementational Strategies, Scalability, Computational Efficiency.

This paper presents a novel approach to depth prediction using fully convolutional residual networks, aiming to improve the accuracy and robustness of depth estimation in various environments. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant improvements in depth prediction accuracy and reducing errors in challenging scenarios. The key contributions of this research include the design of a robust and efficient depth prediction model, the introduction of a novel residual learning strategy, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in various applications, including autonomous driving, robotics, and 3D reconstruction. Our work has important implications for computer vision and robotics, enabling more accurate and reliable depth perception in complex environments, with relevant keywords including depth prediction, fully convolutional networks, residual learning, and computer vision.

Hyperspherical face recognition methods, such as SphereFace, enforce discriminative constraints by normalizing features to lie on a hypersphere. While effective, these methods often suffer from instability during training and suboptimal feature distribution. This paper revisits the SphereFace approach, analyzing its limitations and proposing a refined training strategy to enhance both stability and performance. Our method unifies various aspects of hyperspherical normalization, including margin design and temperature scaling, under a single framework. We introduce a novel adaptive margin adjustment technique that dynamically regulates the margin based on the training progress and feature distribution. Furthermore, we explore different temperature scaling methods to optimize the softmax probability distribution. Empirical results on several benchmark datasets, including LFW, CFP-FP, and AgeDB-30, demonstrate that our revived SphereFace outperforms existing hyperspherical face recognition methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance, while maintaining training stability. The proposed approach offers a robust and effective solution for large-scale face recognition. Keywords: Face Recognition, Hyperspherical Embedding, SphereFace, Deep Learning, Computer Vision.

Solar cell electroluminescence (EL) defect segmentation is an interesting and challenging topic. Many methods have been proposed for EL defect detection, but these methods are still unsatisfactory due to the diversity of the defect and background. In this paper, we provide a new idea of using generative adversarial network (GAN) for defect segmentation. Firstly, the GAN-based method removes the defect region in the input defective image to get a defect-free image, while keeping the background almost unchanged. Then, the subtracted image is obtained by making difference between the defective input image with the generated defect-free image. Finally, the defect region can be segmented through thresholding the subtracted image. To keep the background unchanged before and after image generation, we propose a novel strong identity GAN (SIGAN), which adopts a novel strong identity loss to constraint the background consistency. The SIGAN can be used not only for defect segmentation, but also small-samples defective dataset augmentation. Moreover, we release a new solar cell EL image dataset named as EL-2019, which includes three types of images: crack, finger interruption and defect-free. Experiments on EL-2019 dataset show that the proposed method achieves 90.34% F-score, which outperforms many state-of-the-art methods in terms of solar cell defects segmentation results.

As deep reinforcement learning (DRL) continues to be applied in critical domains requiring high safety standards, ensuring safe exploration and operation is paramount. This paper addresses the challenge of integrating safety measures into DRL processes, specifically targeting the need for systems to learn autonomously while adhering to safety constraints. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel framework that combines deep reinforcement learning with online Gaussian Process (GP) estimation to enhance safety. By leveraging GP's ability to model uncertainties, the proposed method dynamically evaluates potential risks in real-time, allowing the DRL agent to make informed decisions that prioritize safety. The framework integrates these estimations into the policy update processes, facilitating a fine-tuned balance between exploration and exploitation in a safe manner. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed safety-guided DRL framework. Results indicate a significant reduction in safety violations compared to traditional DRL approaches, while maintaining competitive performance metrics across various benchmarks. The integration of online GP estimation not only enhances safety but also accelerates the learning process by providing better coverage of the state space. Conclusion/Implications: Our research advances the field of safe reinforcement learning by providing a robust mechanism to incorporate safety constraints without compromising the agent's learning capabilities. The proposed framework opens avenues for its application in safety-critical systems such as autonomous driving and robotics, where safety cannot be compromised. The objective of this research is to investigate the scaling laws applicable to transfer learning processes in the field of machine learning. Traditional scaling laws have provided insights into model performance relative to resource allocation, yet their application in transfer learning remains under-explored. This study aims to fill this gap by systematically analyzing how model size, dataset scale, and computational resources influence the efficacy of transfer learning. Our approach involves utilizing a diverse set of neural networks, examining their performance across various tasks and domains, and identifying underlying patterns and principles. Key findings indicate that transfer learning performance does not linearly correlate with increased resources; instead, it exhibits distinct scaling behaviors that are contingent on task similarity and dataset characteristics. These observations suggest the presence of optimal transfer scenarios where performance gains plateau or even diminish despite additional resources. Our conclusions emphasize the nuanced nature of transfer learning scaling laws and propose guidelines for optimizing resource allocation in practical applications. The contributions of this work lie in enhancing the understanding of transfer learning dynamics and facilitating more efficient deployment of AI models in diverse settings. Key keywords include transfer learning, scaling laws, neural networks, and model optimization.

Currently there are two main types of inventory checks: periodic inventory checks and perpetual inventory checks. These are two types of inventory checks that any business has already applied or is currently using. Periodic inventory checks are a method of inventory management that relies entirely on the counting process. Business cycles often perform periodic inventory checks quite regularly, such as every 3 to 6 months, to verify the accuracy of inventory, check whether the quantity of goods matches sales data or not. In addition, perpetual inventory checks are a type of inventory check related to monitoring inventory quantities when goods are exported, imported, circulated or returned to the store. Perpetual inventory checks can be performed every day when goods need to be exported orimported, and this method tends to rely less on inventory levels to ensure accuracy.

This paper introduces a novel approach for temporal shape super-resolution through intra-frame motion encoding, leveraging high-frame-per-second (high-fps) structured light techniques. The objective of our research is to overcome the temporal resolution limits inherent in conventional 3D shape measurement systems, which often struggle to accurately capture fast-moving objects due to hardware and frame rate constraints. Our method encodes intra-frame object motion into captured structured light patterns by synchronizing high-speed projection and imaging devices. We propose a comprehensive reconstruction algorithm that analyzes the motion-blurred encoded patterns within each frame, enabling the accurate extraction of multiple sub-frame 3D shapes from a single exposure. Experimental results demonstrate that our system significantly improves temporal resolution and reconstructs finer details of dynamic scenes compared to traditional structured light methods. This advancement allows for precise visualization and analysis of rapid object movements, with applications in industrial inspection, biomechanics, animation, and robotics. Our contributions include the development of a robust intra-frame motion encoding strategy, an efficient shape reconstruction pipeline, and a demonstration of the system's enhanced temporal and spatial performance. Keywords: temporal super-resolution, high-fps structured light, 3D reconstruction, intra-frame motion encoding, dynamic scene analysis.

Super-resolution neural networks have gained significant attention for their ability to enhance image quality by reconstructing high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. However, the choice of loss function plays a critical role in determining the performance and generalization capabilities of these models. This paper introduces an adaptive loss function framework for super-resolution neural networks, leveraging convex optimization techniques to dynamically adjust the loss function during training. The proposed approach aims to address the limitations of fixed loss functions, which often fail to adapt to varying image characteristics and degradation patterns. By formulating the loss adaptation as a convex optimization problem, our method ensures efficient convergence and improved reconstruction accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the adaptive loss function outperforms traditional fixed loss functions, achieving superior peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) metrics. The framework also exhibits robustness across diverse image types and degradation scenarios. This research contributes to the field of image super-resolution by providing a novel, optimization-driven approach to loss function design, with potential applications in medical imaging, satellite imagery, and video enhancement. **Keywords**: Super-resolution, neural networks, adaptive loss function, convex optimization, image reconstruction, PSNR, SSIM.

Deep learning techniques have been widely applied to hyperspectral image (HSI) classification and have achieved great success. However, the deep neural network model has a large parameter space and requires a large number of labeled data. Deep learning methods for HSI classification usually follow a patchwise learning framework. Recently, a fast patch-free global learning (FPGA) architecture was proposed for HSI classification according to global spatial context information. However, FPGA has difficulty extracting the most discriminative features when the sample data is imbalanced. In this paper, a spectral-spatial dependent global learning (SSDGL) framework based on global convolutional long short-term memory (GCL) and global joint attention mechanism (GJAM) is proposed for insufficient and imbalanced HSI classification. In SSDGL, the hierarchically balanced (H-B) sampling strategy and the weighted softmax loss are proposed to address the imbalanced sample problem. To effectively distinguish similar spectral characteristics of land cover types, the GCL module is introduced to extract the long short-term dependency of spectral features. To learn the most discriminative feature representations, the GJAM module is proposed to extract attention areas. The experimental results obtained with three public HSI datasets show that the SSDGL has powerful performance in insufficient and imbalanced sample problems and is superior to other state-of-the-art methods. Domain adaptation is a critical challenge in machine learning, particularly when models trained on one dataset fail to generalize to another due to domain shifts. This paper introduces *Generate to Adapt (GTA)*, a novel framework leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to align source and target domains effectively. The proposed approach employs a domain-adversarial training mechanism, where a generator synthesizes target-like data from the source domain, while a discriminator distinguishes between real and generated samples. Simultaneously, a feature extractor and classifier are optimized to ensure domain-invariant representations and accurate predictions. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that GTA outperforms existing domain adaptation methods, achieving significant improvements in classification accuracy across diverse tasks. The framework’s ability to generate realistic domain-aligned data and its robustness to domain shifts highlight its potential for real-world applications, such as cross-domain image recognition and autonomous systems. This work contributes to advancing domain adaptation by integrating generative modeling with adversarial learning, offering a scalable and effective solution for bridging domain gaps. **Keywords**: Domain Adaptation, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Adversarial Learning, Cross-Domain Generalization, Machine Learning.

The approach involves integrating datasets from diverse repositories and applying ensemble methods such as bagging, boosting, and stacking to construct sophisticated predictive models. By employing these techniques, the study develops models that learn and adapt to the unique characteristics of each software dataset. Results/Findings: Our findings demonstrate a significant improvement in prediction accuracy when using multiple ensemble learning models compared to traditional machine learning approaches. The proposed models display enhanced performance metrics, such as precision, recall, and F1-score, when evaluated against established benchmark datasets. The results underscore the robustness of ensemble techniques in handling the variability and complexity inherent in software defect prediction tasks. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field of software engineering by presenting a comprehensive approach that integrates diverse datasets and advanced ensemble learning methods for defect prediction. The novel framework not only outperforms existing methods but also provides insights into effective model construction for defect prediction. The study's implications suggest that adopting ensemble learning can facilitate better quality control and risk management strategies in software development processes. Keywords: Software Defect Prediction, Ensemble Learning, Machine Learning, Bagging, Boosting, Stacking, Software Quality, Predictive Modeling.

We propose a novel approach to disentangle the generative factors of variation underlying a given set of observations. Our method builds upon the idea that the (unknown) low-dimensional manifold underlying the data space can be explicitly modeled as a product of submanifolds. This definition of disentanglement gives rise to a novel weakly-supervised algorithm for recovering the unknown explanatory factors behind the data. At training time, our algorithm only requires pairs of non i.i.d. data samples whose elements share at least one, possibly multidimensional, generative factor of variation. We require no knowledge on the nature of these transformations, and do not make any limiting assumption on the properties of each subspace. Our approach is easy to implement, and can be successfully applied to different kinds of data (from images to 3D surfaces) undergoing arbitrary transformations. In addition to standard synthetic benchmarks, we showcase our method in challenging real-world applications, where we compare favorably with the state of the art.

**Abstract** Traditional belief propagation algorithms are widely used for approximate inference in graphical models, but their computational demands often pose significant challenges in large-scale or real-time applications. This paper introduces an anytime belief propagation framework that leverages sparse domain representations to address these limitations. Our approach reformulates message computations by dynamically focusing on the most influential variables and restricting updates to sparse, high-impact regions of the solution space. This method allows for early extraction of approximate results with progressively improving accuracy as computation proceeds, enabling flexible trade-offs between inference quality and runtime. Experimental results on benchmark graphical models demonstrate substantial improvements in efficiency, with comparable or superior inference accuracy relative to conventional belief propagation and state-of-the-art anytime algorithms. Key contributions include a novel sparse domain message scheduling strategy and a principled procedure for error-bounded approximations at any time step. The proposed approach is broadly applicable to probabilistic inference tasks in domains such as computer vision, sensor networks, and machine learning. Our findings suggest that exploiting sparsity and anytime properties can substantially enhance the scalability and practicality of belief propagation in complex systems. **Keywords:** belief propagation, anytime algorithms, sparse domains, graphical models, approximate inference, probabilistic reasoning, scalable algorithms

Objective: Accurate prediction of genetic inheritance patterns from family pedigrees is fundamental for genetic counseling and disease risk assessment. However, existing machine learning approaches often act as “black boxes,” limiting clinical trust and actionable insights. This paper introduces EGIPP (Explainable Genetic Inheritance Pattern Prediction), a novel framework that combines high predictive performance with transparent reasoning. Methods: EGIPP represents pedigrees as graphs and applies a hybrid model integrating a Graph Neural Network (GNN) with an attention‐based explanation module. During training, the GNN learns to classify inheritance modes—autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked dominant, and X-linked recessive—while the attention mechanism highlights influential relatives and genotype configurations. Post hoc explanations are generated using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), providing feature‐level importance scores consistent with Mendelian principles. Results: On both synthetic pedigrees and a curated clinical dataset of 1,200 families, EGIPP achieved 92.3% overall accuracy, outperforming baseline random forests (85.7%) and standard GNNs (88.1%). In user studies with clinical geneticists, 87% of the generated explanations were rated as “highly interpretable” and “clinically meaningful.” Case analyses demonstrate how EGIPP correctly identifies carrier status and penetrance factors that traditional models miss. Conclusion: EGIPP advances inheritance‐pattern prediction by uniting robust graph‐based learning with clear, rule‐aligned explanations. This approach enhances decision support in genetic counseling and lays the groundwork for broader adoption of explainable AI in genomics. Keywords: genetic inheritance, explainable AI, interpretable machine learning, pedigree analysis, Graph Neural Network, genetic counseling.

Unlike conventional frame-based sensors, event-based visual sensors output information through spikes at a high temporal resolution. By only encoding changes in pixel intensity, they showcase a low-power consuming, low-latency approach to visual information sensing. To use this information for higher sensory tasks like object recognition and tracking, an essential simplification step is the extraction and learning of features. An ideal feature descriptor must be robust to changes involving (i) local transformations and (ii) re-appearances of a local event pattern. To that end, we propose a novel spatiotemporal feature representation learning algorithm based on slow feature analysis (SFA). Using SFA, smoothly changing linear projections are learnt which are robust to local visual transformations. In order to determine if the features can learn to be invariant to various visual transformations, feature point tracking tasks are used for evaluation. Extensive experiments across two datasets demonstrate the adaptability of the spatiotemporal feature learner to translation, scaling and rotational transformations of the feature points. More importantly, we find that the obtained feature representations are able to exploit the high temporal resolution of such event-based cameras in generating better feature tracks.

This paper introduces an iterative algorithm for fitting nonconvex penalized generalized linear models (GLMs) with grouped predictors. The objective is to address challenges in variable selection and estimation accuracy when dealing with grouped predictors in high-dimensional settings. Our method employs a novel adaptation of the iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) algorithm combined with a difference of convex (DC) programming approach to handle the nonconvex penalty. This enables efficient optimization while promoting sparsity at both the group and individual predictor levels. The proposed algorithm iteratively updates parameter estimates by solving a sequence of weighted least squares problems, where the weights are adaptively adjusted based on the DC decomposition of the penalty function. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our algorithm achieves superior performance in terms of both prediction accuracy and variable selection compared to existing methods, especially when dealing with highly correlated grouped predictors. The algorithm is computationally efficient and provides a practical tool for analyzing complex datasets with grouped structures. Keywords: Generalized Linear Models, Nonconvex Penalization, Grouped Predictors, Variable Selection, Iterative Algorithm, DC Programming.

Abstract: Color constancy is a fundamental challenge in computer vision, crucial for ensuring consistent color perception in varying illumination conditions. This paper introduces a novel Cascading Convolutional Color Constancy (C4) framework designed to enhance the robustness and accuracy of color correction in digital images. The proposed method employs a cascade of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), where each stage progressively refines the estimated scene illumination and corrects color biases. Unlike traditional single-stage models, our cascading approach allows for the integration of both global context and local image details, resulting in improved estimation accuracy. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on benchmark color constancy datasets, demonstrating that C4 consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of mean angular error and visual fidelity of corrected images. The results also indicate that the cascading design significantly mitigates error accumulation and adapts well to diverse lighting scenarios. The contributions of this research include the development of an end-to-end trainable architecture, enhanced feature extraction strategies for illumination estimation, and a thorough analysis of performance gains attributed to cascading. Our findings suggest that the C4 framework offers a promising solution for real-world applications such as digital photography, autonomous vehicles, and augmented reality. Keywords: color constancy, convolutional neural network, cascading models, illumination estimation, computer vision.

This paper introduces a novel approach to constructing tight Bayesian ambiguity sets for robust Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). Robust MDPs address decision-making under uncertainty in the transition probabilities. We propose a method for defining ambiguity sets based on Bayesian principles, leveraging posterior distributions over transition dynamics. Unlike existing approaches that often lead to conservative policies, our method constructs ambiguity sets that are provably tighter, resulting in less conservative and potentially higher-performing robust policies. We achieve this by carefully considering the concentration properties of the posterior distribution. Empirically, we demonstrate on benchmark MDPs that our approach yields robust policies that outperform those derived from alternative ambiguity set constructions, offering a better trade-off between robustness and performance. This improved performance is particularly notable in scenarios with limited data. Keywords: Robust MDPs, Bayesian Methods, Ambiguity Sets, Markov Decision Processes, Reinforcement Learning, Uncertainty.

Real image denoising is a critical challenge in computer vision, with significant implications for applications such as medical imaging, surveillance, and photography. This paper addresses the limitations of existing denoising methods, which often struggle with preserving fine details while effectively removing noise. We propose a novel deep learning-based approach that leverages feature attention mechanisms to enhance denoising performance. Our method integrates a multi-scale feature extraction network with an attention module, enabling the model to focus on noise-affected regions while preserving structural details. The proposed architecture is trained on a diverse dataset of real-world noisy and clean image pairs, ensuring robustness across various noise levels and types. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art denoising methods in terms of both quantitative metrics (e.g., PSNR and SSIM) and visual quality. The model achieves superior noise suppression while maintaining high fidelity in texture and edge preservation. This work contributes to advancing real image denoising by introducing a feature-attentive framework that balances noise removal and detail retention, offering practical benefits for real-world applications. **Keywords**: Image denoising, feature attention, deep learning, computer vision, noise suppression, real-world images.

Spatio-temporal forecasting, predicting future values based on historical spatial and temporal data, is crucial for various applications, including traffic management and environmental monitoring. This paper introduces HyperST-Net, a novel deep learning architecture designed to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of spatio-temporal forecasting. HyperST-Net leverages hypernetworks to dynamically generate the weights of a core spatio-temporal network, enabling adaptive modeling of complex dependencies. Unlike traditional static network architectures, HyperST-Net can adjust its parameters based on the input data, capturing intricate spatial and temporal patterns more effectively. We evaluate HyperST-Net on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in forecasting accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to 15% reduction in RMSE. The results highlight the efficacy of hypernetworks in capturing non-linear and dynamic relationships inherent in spatio-temporal data. HyperST-Net offers a promising approach for advancing spatio-temporal forecasting, providing a flexible and accurate framework for diverse applications. Keywords: Spatio-temporal forecasting, hypernetworks, deep learning, time series analysis, traffic prediction.

The Form view provides a comprehensive interface that displays customer details alongside various ticket-related fields (Figure 4.22), enabling users to both view and interact with their support tickets. This system ensures both accountability and timely resolution of customer issues.

This paper proposes a novel approach to visual object tracking using Spatially Supervised Recurrent Convolutional Neural Networks (SSRCNNs). The objective is to improve the accuracy and robustness of object tracking in complex scenes by leveraging the strengths of both convolutional and recurrent neural networks. Our approach employs a spatially supervised mechanism to guide the learning of recurrent connections, enabling the network to effectively capture temporal dependencies and spatial relationships between objects. The SSRCNN model is trained using a large-scale dataset and evaluated on several benchmark tracking datasets. Results show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art tracking algorithms, achieving significant improvements in terms of accuracy and robustness. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of spatial supervision to recurrent convolutional networks and the demonstration of its effectiveness in visual object tracking. This work has important implications for applications such as surveillance, robotics, and autonomous vehicles, where accurate and reliable object tracking is crucial. Key keywords: visual object tracking, recurrent convolutional neural networks, spatial supervision, deep learning, computer vision.

Causal discovery is a fundamental challenge in understanding complex systems, particularly in domains where interventions are costly or impractical. This paper introduces a novel framework for collaborative causal discovery using atomic interventions, enabling multiple agents to jointly infer causal relationships with minimal intervention efforts. The proposed approach leverages distributed learning techniques to share knowledge across agents while preserving data privacy and reducing redundancy in interventions. We present a scalable algorithm that integrates atomic interventions with causal graph inference, ensuring efficient and accurate discovery even in high-dimensional settings. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and intervention efficiency, particularly in scenarios with limited observational data. The framework’s robustness is validated across synthetic and real-world datasets, showcasing its applicability in fields such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems. This work contributes a significant step toward collaborative and resource-efficient causal discovery, offering practical insights for deploying causal inference in distributed environments. **Keywords**: Causal discovery, atomic interventions, collaborative learning, distributed systems, causal inference, high-dimensional data.

Bài viết nghiên cứu tác động toàn diện của quản trị doanh nghiệp đến hiệu quả hoạt động của 28 ngân hàng thương mại Việt Nam trong giai đoạn 2009-2020. Nghiên cứu sử dụng các kỹ thuật hồi quy dữ liệu bảng với các ước lượng mô hình hồi quy gộp, mô hình tác động ngẫu nhiên, mô hình tác động cố định và bình phương nhỏ nhất tổng quát. In this paper, we propose Multiresolution Graph Networks (MGN) and Multiresolution Graph Variational Autoencoders (MGVAE) to learn and generate graphs in a multiresolution and equivariant manner. At each resolution level, MGN employs higher order message passing to encode the graph while learning to partition it into mutually exclusive clusters and coarsening into a lower resolution. MGVAE constructs a hierarchical generative model based on MGN to variationally autoencode the hierarchy of coarsened graphs. Our proposed framework is end-to-end permutation equivariant with respect to node ordering. Our methods have been successful with several generative tasks including link prediction on citation graphs, unsupervised molecular representation learning to predict molecular properties, molecular generation, general graph generation and graph-based image generation.

This research paper addresses the challenging problem of recovering the textured 3D shape and motion trajectory of fast-moving objects captured in blurred images. Traditional methods often struggle with distinguishing blurred texture details and dynamic motion patterns, hindering accurate 3D reconstruction. Methods/Approach: We present an innovative approach that leverages advanced machine learning techniques to model and disentangle motion and shape from blurry images. Our method integrates a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to predict motion sequences. Additionally, we introduce a novel algorithm that enhances texture clarity and reconstructs precise 3D shapes despite the presence of motion blur. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, showcasing high accuracy in recovering 3D shapes and motion paths compared to existing techniques. Our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of reconstruction quality, particularly in scenarios with severe motion blur. The proposed model is validated on a variety of datasets, yielding robust performance and reliable shape recovery. Conclusion/Implications: This study provides a substantial contribution to the field of computer vision by surpassing limitations in motion-blurred image analysis. The developed methodology is anticipated to have wide-ranging applications in areas such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and surveillance systems, where accurate 3D reconstruction of moving objects is crucial. This research opens new avenues for future exploration in dynamic scene understanding and real-time processing in vision systems. Keywords: 3D reconstruction, motion blur, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, object tracking, CNN, RNN.

This paper introduces Deep Value Networks (DVNs), a novel framework for evaluating and iteratively refining structured outputs in machine learning tasks. The objective of this research is to address the challenge of generating high-quality structured outputs, such as sequences, graphs, or hierarchies, which are critical in applications like natural language processing, computer vision, and bioinformatics. Traditional methods often struggle with balancing output quality and computational efficiency, particularly in complex domains. To overcome these limitations, we propose DVNs, which leverage deep learning to learn a value function that evaluates the quality of structured outputs and guides an iterative refinement process. Our approach combines reinforcement learning with gradient-based optimization to efficiently explore the output space and improve results. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DVNs outperform existing methods in terms of both output quality and convergence speed. Key findings include significant improvements in tasks such as text generation, image segmentation, and molecular structure prediction. The framework’s ability to generalize across diverse structured output tasks highlights its versatility and potential for real-world applications. This work contributes a scalable and adaptive solution for structured output generation, paving the way for advancements in AI-driven decision-making and automation. **Keywords**: Deep Value Networks, structured outputs, iterative refinement, reinforcement learning, machine learning, AI models.

Hyperparameter optimization is a critical aspect of machine learning, significantly influencing model performance and efficiency. This paper introduces a novel spectral approach for hyperparameter optimization, aiming to improve the convergence speed and accuracy of machine learning models. Our methodology leverages spectral analysis to identify optimal hyperparameter settings, thus minimizing the computational overhead associated with traditional optimization techniques. By employing this spectral framework, we analyze parameter spaces more effectively, exploiting frequency domain transformations to gain insights into the hyperparameter landscape. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of our approach when compared to conventional methods such as grid search, random search, and Bayesian optimization across a variety of benchmark datasets. The findings indicate a marked improvement in model accuracy and reduced training time, highlighting the efficacy of spectral analysis in navigating complex hyperparameter spaces. This research offers significant contributions to the field by providing a robust tool for practitioners engaged in machine learning tasks, facilitating the development of more efficient and effective algorithms. Potential applications span various domains, from natural language processing to computer vision, where hyperparameter tuning is crucial. Keywords: hyperparameter optimization, spectral analysis, machine learning, parameter spaces, convergence, performance improvement.

Accurate forecasting of geomagnetic disturbances, particularly the Disturbance Storm Time (Dst) index, is critical for mitigating the impacts of space weather on technological systems. Traditional evaluation metrics often fail to capture the temporal alignment and variability inherent in Dst forecasts. This paper introduces Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) as a novel evaluation metric for assessing the performance of machine learning-based Dst forecasting models. Unlike conventional metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) or Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), DTW accounts for temporal shifts and non-linear patterns in time series data, providing a more robust assessment of forecast accuracy. We employ a machine learning framework utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to generate Dst forecasts and compare their performance using both traditional metrics and DTW. Experimental results demonstrate that DTW offers a more nuanced evaluation, revealing insights into the temporal alignment of predicted and observed Dst values that are overlooked by standard metrics. The findings highlight the potential of DTW as a complementary tool for evaluating time series forecasts in space weather applications, offering improved alignment with real-world operational needs. This research contributes to advancing the evaluation methodologies for geomagnetic forecasting and underscores the importance of temporal alignment in predictive modeling. **Keywords**: Dynamic Time Warping, Dst index, geomagnetic forecasting, machine learning, LSTM, time series evaluation.
