This paper addresses the challenge of accurate 3D object detection from RGB-D data, a critical task for applications such as autonomous driving and robotics. Traditional 2D image-based methods often struggle with depth and occlusion issues, necessitating a more robust approach to leverage 3D spatial information. Methods/Approach: We present Frustum PointNets, a novel framework that combines the strengths of deep learning with point cloud data processing. Our approach uses 2D object proposals generated from RGB images to define a 3D frustum, which then isolates point clouds that likely contain objects. These point clouds are processed using PointNet, an advanced neural network specifically designed to interpret unordered 3D data. This two-stage pipeline efficiently transforms 2D detections into accurate 3D bounding boxes. Results/Findings: Experiments conducted on the KITTI benchmark dataset demonstrate the superior performance of Frustum PointNets compared to existing methods. The proposed approach shows significant improvements in 3D object localization accuracy, achieving state-of-the-art results with robust detection rates and reduced false positives. Evaluation metrics such as precision and recall indicate enhanced performance over traditional 3D detection techniques. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Frustum PointNets represents a significant advancement in the field of 3D object detection, offering a scalable and effective solution for integrating RGB and depth data. This work not only improves detection accuracy but also paves the way for more sophisticated applications in automated systems and intelligent transportation. Future research can explore extending this framework to accommodate more complex environments and additional object classes. Keywords: Frustum PointNets, 3D object detection, RGB-D data, PointNet, autonomous driving, deep learning, point clouds, KITTI dataset.
Pandas cung cấp rất nhiều chức năng xử lý và làm việc trên cấu trúc dữ lệu này. Chính sự linh hoạt và hiệu quả đã khiến cho pandas được sử dụng rộng rãi.

Nghiên cứu ứng dụng mô hình học máy XGBoost và LightGBM để dự báo mực nước triều trên sông Sài Gòn, một vấn đề quan trọng trong quản lý rủi ro ngập lụt tại TP.HCM. Dữ liệu mực nước triều lịch sử được sử dụng để huấn luyện và kiểm tra các mô hình. Kết quả cho thấy cả hai mô hình đều có khả năng dự báo tốt, với độ chính xác cao và sai số thấp. So sánh giữa hai mô hình, LightGBM có phần nhỉnh hơn về tốc độ huấn luyện và khả năng xử lý dữ liệu lớn, trong khi XGBoost cho kết quả dự báo chính xác hơn một chút trong một số trường hợp. Nghiên cứu này mở ra hướng tiếp cận mới trong dự báo mực nước triều sử dụng các thuật toán học máy tiên tiến, có tiềm năng ứng dụng rộng rãi trong thực tế nhằm hỗ trợ công tác phòng chống thiên tai và quy hoạch đô thị.

Hoạt động cho vay ngang hàng (P2P lending) đang ngày càng phổ biến và có tác động đáng kể đến tính tự bền vững của các tổ chức tài chính truyền thống. Mô hình này cho phép người vay và người cho vay kết nối trực tiếp mà không cần thông qua trung gian, giúp giảm chi phí và tăng tốc độ giao dịch. Tuy nhiên, sự gia tăng của P2P lending cũng đặt ra thách thức cho các tổ chức tài chính truyền thống, buộc họ phải cải tiến dịch vụ, nâng cao hiệu quả quản lý rủi ro và tối ưu hóa chi phí để duy trì tính cạnh tranh. Bên cạnh đó, các tổ chức tài chính cũng cần chú trọng đến việc xây dựng lòng tin và minh bạch trong hoạt động để thu hút khách hàng. Sự kết hợp giữa công nghệ và kinh nghiệm quản lý truyền thống có thể là chìa khóa giúp các tổ chức này vượt qua thách thức và đảm bảo tính bền vững trong dài hạn.

Human activity recognition (HAR) in RGB videos is a challenging task due to variations in viewpoint, illumination, and background clutter. This paper presents a novel skeleton-focused approach for HAR, leveraging 3D human pose estimation to improve robustness and accuracy. Our method first extracts 3D skeleton data from RGB video frames using a state-of-the-art pose estimation network. Then, we propose a temporal graph convolutional network (TGCN) that operates directly on the skeleton sequences. This TGCN is specifically designed to capture the spatio-temporal dependencies between joints, effectively modeling human actions. We introduce a skeleton-aware attention mechanism to emphasize informative joints and suppress noise. Experimental results on the NTU RGB+D and Kinetics datasets demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing RGB-based and skeleton-based HAR techniques. The skeleton-focused approach is shown to be more resilient to visual variations, leading to improved generalization and accuracy in complex scenarios. Our work highlights the effectiveness of combining 3D pose estimation with deep learning for robust and accurate human activity recognition. Keywords: Human Activity Recognition, RGB Video, 3D Pose Estimation, Temporal Graph Convolutional Network, Skeleton Data, Deep Learning.

Bipartite matching is a fundamental problem with applications in diverse areas such as recommendation systems, resource allocation, and social network analysis. This paper introduces Neural Bipartite Matching (NBM), a novel end-to-end trainable neural network architecture for solving bipartite matching problems. NBM leverages learnable node embeddings and a customized attention mechanism to capture complex relationships between the two sets of nodes. Unlike traditional algorithms that rely on iterative optimization, NBM directly predicts the optimal matching in a single forward pass, significantly reducing computational time. We evaluate NBM on synthetic datasets and real-world recommendation datasets, demonstrating its superior performance in terms of matching accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods, including the Hungarian algorithm and other learned matching approaches. Specifically, NBM achieves up to a 15% improvement in matching accuracy while reducing computation time by an order of magnitude. These results highlight the potential of NBM as a scalable and accurate solution for large-scale bipartite matching problems. Keywords: Bipartite Matching, Neural Networks, Attention Mechanism, Recommendation Systems, Graph Neural Networks.

This paper addresses the challenge of credit assignment in multi-agent reinforcement learning, where the goal is to identify the contribution of each agent to the team's overall performance. Our objective is to develop a novel approach that enables efficient and effective learning in cooperative multi-agent environments. We propose a meta-policy gradient method that adapts to the credit assignment problem by learning a meta-policy that guides the optimization of individual agent policies. Our approach leverages the idea of meta-learning to learn a policy that can adapt to different credit assignment scenarios. The results show that our method outperforms existing credit assignment methods in several cooperative multi-agent tasks, demonstrating improved learning efficiency and scalability. The key findings of this research highlight the importance of adaptive credit assignment in multi-agent reinforcement learning and demonstrate the potential of meta-policy gradient methods in this domain. This work contributes to the development of more effective and efficient multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms, with potential applications in areas such as robotics, game playing, and autonomous systems. Key keywords: multi-agent reinforcement learning, credit assignment, meta-policy gradient, meta-learning, cooperative learning.

Một cuộc khảo sát đã được thực hiện tại tỉnh Phitsanulok nhằm tìm hiểu nguồn gốc của sản phẩm nông nghiệp và các sản phẩm phụ để phục vụ cho việc sử dụng hiệu quả hơn. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc xác định các loại sản phẩm nông nghiệp chủ yếu, cũng như các sản phẩm phụ có thể được tận dụng trong các lĩnh vực khác nhau như chế biến thực phẩm, sản xuất năng lượng và bảo vệ môi trường. Kết quả khảo sát cho thấy tỉnh Phitsanulok có tiềm năng lớn trong việc phát triển các sản phẩm nông nghiệp bền vững, đồng thời khuyến khích việc tái sử dụng và giảm thiểu lãng phí. Những thông tin thu thập được sẽ hỗ trợ các nhà hoạch định chính sách và nông dân trong việc tối ưu hóa quy trình sản xuất, từ đó nâng cao giá trị kinh tế cho cộng đồng địa phương.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc phân tích ảnh hưởng của một số tham số đến quá trình phân tích ổn định khung phẳng thông qua phương pháp phần tử hữu hạn. Các tham số được xem xét bao gồm vật liệu, hình dạng cấu trúc, và điều kiện biên, nhằm đánh giá sự tác động của chúng đến độ bền và khả năng chịu tải của khung. Kết quả cho thấy rằng việc lựa chọn đúng các tham số thiết kế có thể cải thiện đáng kể hiệu suất và độ an toàn của công trình. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng phương pháp phần tử hữu hạn là công cụ hiệu quả trong việc mô phỏng và phân tích các tình huống khác nhau, từ đó cung cấp những thông tin quý giá cho các kỹ sư trong quá trình thiết kế và thi công. Những phát hiện này không chỉ có giá trị lý thuyết mà còn mang tính ứng dụng cao trong thực tiễn xây dựng.

Nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc chế tạo lớp phủ hợp kim entropy cao (HEA) bằng phương pháp phun phủ laser, một kỹ thuật tiên tiến giúp cải thiện tính chất bề mặt vật liệu. Quá trình này bao gồm việc sử dụng laser để nung chảy và phun các hợp kim có thành phần phức tạp lên bề mặt nền, tạo ra lớp phủ có cấu trúc đặc biệt. Các lớp phủ HEA thường thể hiện các đặc tính vượt trội như độ cứng cao, khả năng chống ăn mòn và chống oxy hóa tốt, nhờ vào hiệu ứng entropy cao làm ổn định cấu trúc tinh thể. Việc kiểm soát các thông số phun phủ laser, chẳng hạn như công suất laser, tốc độ quét và tốc độ cấp bột, đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc tối ưu hóa cấu trúc và tính chất của lớp phủ. Phân tích cấu trúc hiển vi và thành phần hóa học của lớp phủ HEA cho thấy sự hình thành các pha khác nhau, ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến các tính chất cơ học và hóa học của vật liệu. Kết quả nghiên cứu cung cấp cơ sở khoa học và công nghệ cho việc ứng dụng lớp phủ HEA trong các ngành công nghiệp khác nhau, đặc biệt là trong môi trường làm việc khắc nghiệt.

Magento là một nền tảng thương mạ điện tử mã nguồn mở điược sử dụng phổ bến trên toàn cầu. Nếu chỉ tính 100,000 website hàng điầu, Magento xếp ở vị trí thứ nhất với 1,2%. Có thể thấy, Magento là lựa chọn phổ bến cho các doanh nghệp lớn và có nhu cầu tùy chỉnh cao.

Đặt vấn đề: Ibuprofen (IBU) là dược chất thuộc nhóm giảm đau, kháng viêm không steroid (NSAIDs) với dạng bào chế tại chỗ dùng trên da sẽ giúp giảm tác dụng không mong muốn và chuyển hóa qua gan lần đầu. Để đảm bảo nồng độ hiệu quả của thuốc qua đường dùng trên da, nghiên cứu này được tiến hành nhằm mục đích xây dựng công thức hydrogel chứa vi nhũ tương (VNT) IBU dùng trên da và đánh giá chất lượng sản phẩm. Đối tượng và phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu khảo sát độ tan của IBU, xây dựng giản đồ pha, khảo sát tỷ lệ các tá dược trong công thức và đánh giá các đặc tính của VNT như kích thước giọt, hàm lượng dược chất bằng phương pháp sắc ký lỏng hiệu năng cao, khả năng giải phóng hoạt chất ex vivo qua da tai lợn bằng thiết bị Hanson Research. Kết quả nghiên cứu: Công thức hydrogel gôm xanthan 1% chứa VNT IBU 5% (kl/kl) dùng trên da gồm capryol 90 12,5%, acrysol K140 33,33%, propylen glycol 16,67% và nước vừa đủ 100% (kl/kl) với kích thước giọt bằng 25,69±2,12 nm, phân bố kích thước bằng 0,226±0,095. Công thức hydrogel gôm xanthan 1% chứa VNT IBU 5% (kl/kl) có khả năng thấm qua màng da tai lợn gấp 45 lần so với công thức hydrogel chứa IBU nguyên liệu. Kết luận: Đây là dạng bào chế đầy tiềm năng, có khả năng cải thiện sinh khả dụng của IBU với đường dùng trên da.

Due to recent breakthroughs, reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated impressive performance in challenging sequential decision-making problems. However, an open question is how to make RL cope with partial observability which is prevalent in many real-world problems. Contrary to contemporary RL approaches, which focus mostly on improved memory representations or strong assumptions about the type of partial observability, we propose a simple but efficient approach that can be applied together with a wide variety of RL methods. Our main insight is that smoothly transitioning from full observability to partial observability during the training process yields a high performance policy. The approach, called partially observable guided reinforcement learning (PO-GRL), allows to utilize full state information during policy optimization without compromising the optimality of the final policy. A comprehensive evaluation in discrete partially observableMarkov decision process (POMDP) benchmark problems and continuous partially observable MuJoCo and OpenAI gym tasks shows that PO-GRL improves performance. Finally, we demonstrate PO-GRL in the ball-in-the-cup task on a real Barrett WAM robot under partial observability.

This paper investigates hierarchical representation learning within the context of Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), aiming to enhance the efficiency and scalability of sequential decision-making algorithms. We propose a novel framework that automatically discovers multi-level hierarchical structures in the state and action spaces of MDPs using deep learning techniques. Our approach integrates feature abstraction modules with hierarchical policy optimization, enabling agents to learn high-level state representations and corresponding sub-policies in a data-driven manner. We evaluate the method on a suite of benchmark environments ranging from discrete to continuous domains. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in learning speed, sample efficiency, and final performance compared to flat and non-hierarchical baselines. The hierarchical representations also facilitate better generalization and transfer to related tasks. These findings suggest that hierarchical representation learning holds considerable promise for addressing the challenges of high-dimensional state spaces and long-horizon planning in complex MDPs. Potential applications include reinforcement learning, autonomous robotics, and adaptive control systems. Key keywords: hierarchical reinforcement learning, Markov Decision Processes, representation learning, policy optimization, deep learning, abstraction, transfer learning.

This paper investigates the application of transformers to object detection, addressing limitations of existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods. We propose a novel transformer-based object detection framework that leverages self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies between image regions, enabling more accurate and context-aware object localization and classification. Our approach replaces the traditional CNN backbone with a transformer encoder, followed by a lightweight detection head. Experimental results on the COCO dataset demonstrate that our transformer-based detector achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art CNN-based detectors, while offering advantages in terms of architectural simplicity and the ability to model global context. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of different transformer configurations and attention mechanisms on detection accuracy. This research provides insights into the potential of transformers for object detection and opens avenues for future exploration in end-to-end object detection pipelines. Keywords: object detection, transformer, self-attention, computer vision, deep learning.

**Abstract:** The increasing integration of wind and solar energy sources into modern power grids necessitates high-resolution spatiotemporal data for accurate forecasting, grid stability, and resource management. The benchmark comprises multiple real-world and synthetic datasets, along with standardized evaluation protocols and metrics tailored for renewable energy applications. We assess a range of state-of-the-art super-resolution algorithms—including deep learning models and interpolation baselines—on their ability to enhance the resolution of wind speed and solar irradiance fields. Experimental results indicate that advanced neural network architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers, outperform traditional interpolation techniques in preserving key meteorological and spatial features. WiSoSuper provides valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of existing super-resolution approaches in the context of renewable energy. The benchmark and findings aim to guide future research toward more accurate and robust spatiotemporal upscaling methods, with significant implications for energy system forecasting, planning, and policy-making. Key keywords: super-resolution, wind data, solar data, machine learning, benchmark, renewable energy, spatiotemporal forecasting.

This paper introduces a novel approach for reasoning over knowledge graphs by leveraging entity-aware step mixture models. Our objective is to improve multi-hop reasoning accuracy and interpretability in complex knowledge graphs. We propose a model that combines graph neural networks (GNNs) with a hierarchical mixture mechanism. The GNN component learns entity embeddings and performs message passing to capture relationships between entities. The step mixture component dynamically selects relevant reasoning paths at each step of the reasoning process, allowing the model to adaptively focus on different aspects of the graph. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets for knowledge graph completion and multi-hop reasoning, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we show that the learned mixture weights provide insights into the reasoning process, enhancing the interpretability of the model. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of combining graph-based representations with adaptive reasoning strategies for knowledge graph reasoning. Keywords: Knowledge Graph, Reasoning, Graph Neural Networks, Step Mixture, Entity Embedding, Multi-hop Reasoning, Interpretability.

Link prediction in graphs is a fundamental problem in network analysis, with applications ranging from social networks to biological systems. However, traditional methods often struggle in few-shot scenarios, where limited labeled data is available for training. This paper introduces a novel subgraph-aware meta-learning framework for few-shot inductive link prediction, addressing the challenge of generalizing to unseen nodes and edges in dynamic graphs. The proposed approach leverages meta-learning to adaptively learn transferable knowledge from a set of training tasks, enabling effective prediction on new tasks with minimal labeled data. Specifically, we design a subgraph extraction mechanism that captures local structural patterns and relational features, enhancing the model's ability to generalize across diverse graph structures. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios with sparse or evolving graphs. The results highlight the framework's potential for real-world applications, such as recommendation systems and knowledge graph completion, where inductive learning and few-shot adaptability are critical. This work contributes a scalable and efficient solution to the problem of few-shot link prediction, offering insights into the interplay between subgraph representation and meta-learning in graph-based tasks. **Keywords**: link prediction, few-shot learning, meta-learning, inductive learning, subgraph extraction, graph neural networks.

This paper investigates the attention mechanisms in Graph Attention Networks (GATs), a popular deep learning model for graph-structured data. Our objective is to analyze the effectiveness of attention in GATs and identify potential limitations. We employ a systematic approach, combining theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations on benchmark datasets. Our results show that while GATs achieve state-of-the-art performance in many tasks, their attention mechanisms often prioritize node degrees over actual task-relevant information. We also find that the attention weights learned by GATs can be misleading, indicating a need for more interpretable and robust attention mechanisms. Our conclusions highlight the importance of carefully evaluating attention in GATs and propose potential improvements, such as incorporating additional attention supervision or regularization techniques. The key contributions of this research include a deeper understanding of GAT attention mechanisms, novel evaluation metrics, and insights into the development of more effective and interpretable graph neural networks, with implications for applications in social network analysis, recommendation systems, and graph-based AI models. Keywords: Graph Attention Networks, Attention Mechanisms, Graph Neural Networks, Deep Learning, Interpretability.

Predicting the trajectories of agents in dynamic environments is a crucial challenge with significant applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and surveillance. This paper introduces a novel approach called the Recursive Social Behavior Graph (RSBG) for trajectory prediction, designed to effectively capture complex social interactions among multiple agents over time. The proposed method models agents as nodes within a dynamic graph, where edges represent social relationships and influence. Our key innovation lies in the recursive update mechanism that allows the system to iteratively refine the representation of agent interactions by leveraging historical behavior and context information. To evaluate the effectiveness of RSBG, we implemented it with state-of-the-art recurrent neural network architectures and conducted experiments on widely used pedestrian trajectory datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves higher prediction accuracy and better handles crowded scenarios when compared to existing baseline methods. Notably, the recursive mechanism improves the system's ability to anticipate future movements by dynamically adapting to changing group behaviors. In summary, this work provides a robust and scalable framework for multi-agent trajectory forecasting by incorporating recursive social context modeling. The proposed RSBG establishes a new benchmark for socially-aware trajectory prediction and shows promising potential for deployment in real-world intelligent transportation and human-robot interaction systems. Keywords: trajectory prediction, social behavior, graph neural networks, recursive modeling, multi-agent systems, autonomous navigation.

Đặt vấn đề: Tổn thương thận cấp là rối loạn chức năng cơ quan thường gặp nhất ở các khoa hồi sức, làm tăng tỷ lệ tử vong và gây ảnh hưởng xấu tới kết cục của bệnh nhân. Việc xác định các yếu tố nguy cơ tổn thương thận cấp là cần thiết vì phương pháp điều trị tối ưu nhất hiện nay vẫn là phòng ngừa và phát hiện sớm tổn thương thận cấp trên các bệnh nhân có nguy cơ cao trước khi các biến chứng xuất hiện. Vì vậy, chúng tôi thực hiện nghiên cứu với mục tiêu xác định các yếu tố nguy cơ tổn thương thận cấp ở bệnh nhân điều trị tại khoa hồi sức. Mục tiêu: Xác định các yếu tố nguy cơ tổn thương thận cấp ở bệnh nhân điều trị tại khoa hồi sức. Phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu đoàn hệ tiến cứu trên 150 bệnh nhân nhập khoa hồi sức trong thời gian từ tháng 01/2020 tới tháng 06/2020. Kết quả: Tỷ lệ tổn thương thận cấp tại khoa hồi sức là 53,33%, trong đó tổn thương thận cấp giai đoạn 3 chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất. Các yếu tố nguy cơ độc lập của tổn thương thận cấp bao gồm: nhiễm khuẩn huyết (OR = 3,37, KTC 95% 1,03 - 11,01; p = 0,039), tiền căn bệnh thận mạn (OR = 3,4, KTC 95% 1,01 - 11,48, p = 0,042), điểm APACHE II (OR = 1,28, KTC 95% 1,11 - 1,47, p < 0,001) và sử dụng thuốc vận mạch (OR = 3,59, KTC 95% 1,02 - 12,69, p = 0,044). Với mục đích t ìm ra các gi ải pháp ki ểm soát b ệnh hi ệu quả, đề tài nghiên c ứu tác nhân gây b ệnh sau thu ho ạch trên qu ả chôm chôm ở Đồng Bằng Sông C ửu Long đã được triển khai trên khía c ạnh phân l ập, định danh và đánh giá đi ều kiện môi trư ờng nuôi c ấy trên s ự sinh trư ởng và ph át triển của nấm phân l ập. Kết quả nghiên c ứu đã phân l ập và đ ịnh danh đư ợc 7 chủng nấm gồm Lasiodiplodia pseudoth eobromae, Phomopsis mali, Lasmenia sp., Gliocephalotrichum cylindrosporum, Pestalotiopsis virgatula voucher, Pestalotiopsis clavispora và Fusarium verticillioides , tác nhân gây nên b ệnh th ối sau thu ho ạch trên qu ả chôm chôm. Tri ệu chứng bệnh th ối đặc trưng là thối lan m ờ và th ối đen. Các tri ệu chứng này có th ể nhận dạng và nhìn th ấy bằng m ắt thường. This paper explores the integration of policy gradient and Q-learning methods to enhance the performance of reinforcement learning agents. The objective is to develop a hybrid approach that leverages the strengths of both techniques, allowing for more efficient and effective learning in complex environments. Our method combines the policy gradient's ability to directly optimize policies with Q-learning's capability to learn accurate value functions. We employ a novel architecture that seamlessly integrates these two paradigms, enabling the agent to adaptively switch between policy gradient and Q-learning updates. Experimental results demonstrate that our hybrid approach outperforms traditional policy gradient and Q-learning methods in various benchmark tasks, achieving improved convergence rates and enhanced overall performance. The key contributions of this research include the development of a unified framework for policy gradient and Q-learning, and the demonstration of its potential to accelerate reinforcement learning in real-world applications. Our work has significant implications for the development of more efficient and scalable reinforcement learning algorithms, with potential applications in robotics, game playing, and autonomous systems. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, policy gradient, Q-learning, hybrid approach, deep learning.

Linear relaxation based perturbation analysis (LiRPA) for neural networks, which computes provable linear bounds of output neurons given a certain amount of input perturbation, has become a core component in robustness verification and certified defense. The majority of LiRPA-based methods focus on simple feed-forward networks and need particular manual derivations and implementations when extended to other architectures. In this paper, we develop an automatic framework to enable perturbation analysis on any neural network structures, by generalizing existing LiRPA algorithms such as CROWN to operate on general computational graphs. The flexibility, differentiability and ease of use of our framework allow us to obtain state-of-the-art results on LiRPA based certified defense on fairly complicated networks like DenseNet, ResNeXt and Transformer that are not supported by prior works. Our framework also enables loss fusion, a technique that significantly reduces the computational complexity of LiRPA for certified defense. For the first time, we demonstrate LiRPA based certified defense on Tiny ImageNet and Downscaled ImageNet where previous approaches cannot scale to due to the relatively large number of classes. Our work also yields an open-source library for the community to apply LiRPA to areas beyond certified defense without much LiRPA expertise, e.g., we create a neural network with a probably flat optimization landscape by applying LiRPA to network parameters. Our opensource library is available at https://github.com/KaidiXu/auto_LiRPA.

Remote heart rate (HR) measurement using video is gaining traction due to its non-contact nature and potential for various applications. However, existing methods often require extensive hand-crafted feature engineering and are sensitive to environmental variations. This paper introduces AutoHR, an end-to-end deep learning framework that leverages neural architecture search (NAS) to automatically discover optimal network structures for robust remote HR measurement. AutoHR employs a novel search space tailored for spatio-temporal feature extraction from facial videos, incorporating diverse convolutional and recurrent operations. The framework integrates a differentiable neural architecture search algorithm to efficiently explore the search space and identify high-performing architectures. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that AutoHR achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing existing methods with significantly reduced manual effort. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the NAS strategy and the discovered network architectures. AutoHR provides a strong baseline for future research in remote HR measurement, showcasing the power of automated machine learning in addressing the challenges of this domain. Keywords: Remote Heart Rate Measurement, Neural Architecture Search, Deep Learning, Spatio-Temporal Feature Extraction, Video Processing.

This paper introduces a novel context-aware and video-based risk descriptor designed to enhance cyclist safety by providing an assessment of risk levels in real-time. Methods/Approach: The proposed system utilizes machine learning algorithms to process video data captured from cameras mounted on bicycles or within surrounding environments. By incorporating sensor data and contextual information, such as weather conditions and traffic density, the model assesses the risk of potential collisions or hazardous situations. The system employs cutting-edge computer vision techniques to analyze cyclist behavior and evaluate environmental factors influencing safety. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of our risk descriptor, showing an improvement in the detection and prediction of high-risk scenarios for cyclists in various urban settings. Our approach outperforms existing methods by achieving a higher accuracy rate in real-world conditions. The implementation also allows for seamless integration with existing smart city infrastructure, offering real-time alerts to cyclists and potentially reducing accident rates. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes significantly to the field of intelligent transportation systems by introducing an innovative solution to enhance cyclist safety. The development of a context-aware risk assessment tool has profound implications for urban planning and smart city initiatives. Future applications could extend to other vulnerable road users, fostering a safer and more efficient traffic ecosystem. Our study lays the groundwork for further advancements in video-based and sensor-enabled safety technologies. Keywords: cyclist safety, risk assessment, context-aware, machine learning, computer vision, urban transportation, intelligent transportation systems.

Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces training time while achieving competitive pruning performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques. Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown remarkable success in various domains, particularly in continuous control tasks. However, a significant challenge lies in ensuring robustness to action perturbations, which can severely degrade performance in real-world applications. This paper addresses the problem of action robustness in RL by proposing a novel framework, Action Robust Reinforcement Learning (AR-RL), designed to enhance the resilience of policies to uncertainties and disturbances in action execution. Our approach integrates a robust optimization technique with deep RL algorithms, enabling the learned policies to account for potential action deviations during training. We evaluate AR-RL on a suite of continuous control benchmarks, including simulated robotic tasks, and demonstrate its superior performance compared to standard RL methods under various levels of action noise. Results show that AR-RL achieves higher task success rates and stability, even in the presence of significant perturbations. The proposed framework not only advances the theoretical understanding of robustness in RL but also offers practical implications for deploying RL-based systems in real-world environments where action uncertainties are inevitable. Key contributions include a scalable training methodology, empirical validation across diverse tasks, and insights into the trade-offs between robustness and performance. This paper addresses the challenge of learning invariant representations in machine learning models, particularly in scenarios where data exhibits local transformations such as rotations, translations, or scaling. The objective is to develop a robust framework that can effectively capture and utilize these transformations to improve model generalization and performance. We propose a novel approach that integrates local transformation-aware mechanisms into deep learning architectures, enabling the model to learn representations that are invariant to specific spatial or structural changes in the input data. Our method leverages a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformation-specific modules, which are trained end-to-end to optimize invariance while preserving discriminative features. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in tasks such as image classification and object recognition, achieving higher accuracy and robustness under varying transformation conditions. The findings highlight the importance of explicitly modeling local transformations in representation learning and provide insights into the design of more adaptable and generalizable machine learning systems. This work contributes to advancing the field of invariant representation learning, with potential applications in computer vision, robotics, and other domains where data variability is a critical factor. **Keywords**: invariant representations, local transformations, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, image classification, robustness.

This research addresses the limitations of the conventional Softmax with Cross-Entropy framework in neural network classifiers. It aims to explore how these classifiers can be redefined as mutual information estimators to enhance model interpretability and performance. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel methodology that reconceptualizes the role of the Softmax function in conjunction with Cross-Entropy loss. By employing information-theoretic principles, we reformulate the classification problem to focus on mutual information estimation. Our approach leverages a rigorous analytical model to quantitatively assess the informational content shared between inputs and their corresponding predictive outcomes, thereby optimizing the decision-making process of neural networks. Results/Findings: The proposed framework demonstrated a consistent improvement in classification accuracy and robustness across multiple benchmark datasets when compared to traditional approaches. Our findings indicate that treating the neural network classifier as a mutual information estimator leads to better alignment with theoretical maximum likelihood estimations. Furthermore, our model provides enhanced insights into uncertainty and decision boundaries, thus offering more reliable predictions. Conclusion/Implications: The study presents a transformative approach to neural network classifiers by aligning them with mutual information principles, offering unique benefits for understanding and improving model decision processes. This advancement opens pathways to more informed and efficient learning systems that can be utilized in diverse applications such as image recognition, language processing, and beyond. The results underscore the potential for rethinking fundamental machine learning algorithms to achieve superior performance and deeper insights. Keywords: Softmax, Cross-Entropy, Mutual Information, Neural Network Classifier, Information Theory, Classification Accuracy, Model Robustness.

This paper addresses the challenging problem of bimanual multi-object manipulation, where simultaneous coordination and effective interaction with multiple objects using two hands is required. The primary focus is on enhancing the performance and dexterity in robotic manipulation tasks by introducing a novel approach that integrates disentangled attention as an intrinsic form of regularization. Methods/Approach: We propose a disentangled attention mechanism that segregates attention into distinct components, allowing the system to effectively manage attention across different objects and tasks. The model leverages neural networks to learn representations that explicitly separate the attention dedicated to each object being manipulated. This intrinsic regularization serves to stabilize learning and improve adaptability in dynamic environments. Empirical studies were conducted using simulated robotic platforms equipped with advanced sensors to evaluate the system's capacity for bimanual coordination. Results/Findings: The findings demonstrate that our disentangled attention framework significantly enhances manipulation efficiency, reducing task completion time while improving precision in dynamic object handling scenarios. Comparative analysis with existing state-of-the-art methods exhibits superior performance in terms of accuracy and speed. Our approach also shows improved generalization capabilities when tested under varying environmental conditions and with different object sets. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of disentangled attention as intrinsic regularization distinguishes itself as a promising enhancement for robotic systems involved in complex, simultaneous object manipulation tasks. This framework not only advances the theoretical understanding of attention mechanisms in neural-based systems but also has practical implications for developing more sophisticated robotic applications in manufacturing, healthcare, and service industries. Future work includes expanding this approach to more intricate tasks involving even higher degrees of freedom and interaction complexity. Keywords: disentangled attention, bimanual manipulation, multi-object manipulation, intrinsic regularization, robotic systems, neural networks.

In the realm of sports video analysis, identifying key events in figure skating videos remains a significant challenge due to the sport's dynamic and artistic nature. This paper presents a novel approach to highlight detection by estimating blink probability, which correlates with viewer attention and emotional engagement, providing a unique perspective on capturing crucial moments in figure skating performances. Methods/Approach: We propose a comprehensive model integrating computer vision algorithms and machine learning techniques to estimate blink probability from video footage. The model extracts facial landmarks and utilizes a neural network to predict blink occurrences, correlating them with potential highlights. The dataset comprises annotated figure skating videos, allowing for training and testing of the predicted blink probability model. Results/Findings: Our approach demonstrates a significant improvement in highlight detection accuracy compared to traditional methods, which rely solely on performance metrics or manual annotation. The blink probability model achieves a high correlation with viewer-ranked highlights, offering a more nuanced understanding of engaging moments. Experimental results show that incorporating blink probability into video analysis enhances the precision of highlight identification by an average margin of 15%. Conclusion/Implications: This research introduces an innovative methodology for sports video analysis by leveraging human physiological responses as a proxy for viewer engagement. The incorporation of blink probability into figure skating highlight detection offers a fresh avenue for automated sports analytics, with potential applications extending to other sports and media industries requiring sophisticated event detection. By bridging physiological insights and computational models, this study contributes to advancing the paradigm of automated highlight detection in video analysis. Keywords: Blink Probability, Highlight Detection, Figure Skating Videos, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Sports Video Analysis.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown promise in learning representations for graph-structured data, but often struggle with long-range dependencies and computational bottlenecks. This paper introduces GraphiT, a novel approach to encode graph structure directly within Transformer architectures, leveraging self-attention mechanisms for enhanced graph representation learning. GraphiT converts adjacency information into positional encodings, allowing Transformers to effectively capture both local and global graph properties. We demonstrate GraphiT's performance on various graph-based tasks, including node classification, graph classification, and link prediction, using benchmark datasets such as Cora, PubMed, and ogbg-molhiv. Experimental results show that GraphiT achieves significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional GNNs and other graph Transformer variants, particularly on large and complex graphs. The ability to seamlessly integrate graph structure into Transformers opens new avenues for applying these powerful models to graph-related problems, offering a scalable and effective solution for graph representation learning. Keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Transformers, Graph Representation Learning, Positional Encoding, Self-Attention, Graph Classification.

The study investigates the implicit bias inherent in any algorithm, focusing on understanding how biases can be confined through the margin concept. As machine learning and AI systems become integral to decision-making processes, recognizing and managing algorithmic bias is critical to ensuring fairness and accuracy. Methods/Approach: This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing margin-based bounds to quantify and restrict implicit biases present in algorithms. By employing a theoretical framework that leverages margin theory, the study provides a method to systematically evaluate and limit bias without significantly sacrificing the model's performance. The approach is applicable across a range of algorithms, making it versatile for different machine learning models. Results/Findings: The research demonstrates that the margin-based method effectively bounds implicit bias in various algorithms, including widely used classification and regression models. Comparative analysis shows a significant reduction in bias with minimal impact on model efficacy. Experimental results validate the theoretical claims, illustrating how this method offers superior control over algorithmic bias compared to existing techniques. Conclusion/Implications: The findings illuminate the potential for margin-based constraints to serve as a robust tool for bias management in algorithmic systems. This approach not only enhances the transparency and fairness of AI-driven decisions but also contributes to the development of more equitable AI technologies. The implications extend to diverse fields where machine learning is applied, including finance, healthcare, and social services, promising more balanced outcomes for all stakeholders. Keywords: Implicit bias, margin-based approach, algorithmic fairness, machine learning, AI bias, model performance, bias management.

Visual Question Answering (VQA) traditionally depends on large sets of question-answer pairs for training, posing challenges in terms of data collection and model robustness. This paper introduces a novel approach to VQA that eliminates the need for direct question-answer pair training. Our primary objective is to investigate the feasibility of a VQA system that leverages unsupervised learning techniques to understand visual content and derive answers without pre-defined Q&A datasets. We employ a combination of advanced neural network architectures and transfer learning from pre-trained visual models to comprehend and infer answers from images. The proposed method dynamically synthesizes potential questions and derives answers through a context-aware inference mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive accuracy when compared to traditional VQA methods while significantly reducing the amount of labeled training data required. This research contributes a new paradigm for VQA, facilitating adaptability to diverse visual domains and enhancing scalability for real-world applications. Key innovations include the incorporation of visual context to generate implicit queries and a robust inference model that adapts to varying visual stimuli. Potential applications span areas such as automated visual content analysis, enhanced accessibility tools, and dynamic interactive systems. Key keywords: Visual Question Answering, unsupervised learning, neural networks, transfer learning, context-aware inference.

The generative adversarial network (GAN) framework has emerged as a powerful tool for various image and video synthesis tasks, allowing the synthesis of visual content in an unconditional or input-conditional manner. It has enabled the generation of high-resolution photorealistic images and videos, a task that was challenging or impossible with prior methods. It has also led to the creation of many new applications in content creation. In this paper, we provide an overview of GANs with a special focus on algorithms and applications for visual synthesis. We cover several important techniques to stabilize GAN training, which has a reputation for being notoriously difficult. We also discuss its applications to image translation, image processing, video synthesis, and neural rendering.

JavaScript is a versatile, high-level interpreted programming language that plays a crucial role in modern web development. As a web page loads, the browser’s JavaScript engine interprets the code, constructs the Document Object Model (DOM) to represent the page’s structure, and executes scripts to dynamically alter the content, visual style, and behavior. Despite being single-threaded—meaning it handles one command at a time—JavaScript enables highly responsive experiences through its support for asynchronous operations, such as callbacks, promises, and the newer async/await syntax, which allow time-consuming tasks to run in the background without blocking user interactions. Furthermore, JavaScript’s capacity to operate on both client and server sides allows for the creation of seamless, interactive, and responsive web applications that define today's internet experience.

Time-Travel Rephotography presents a novel method for enhancing historical image data by applying advanced computational techniques to recreate and visualize past scenes with stunning accuracy. The objective of this research is to address the challenges of deteriorated and incomplete archival photography and to provide a method for restoring and rephotographing historical moments as they originally appeared. Utilizing a combination of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), our approach employs deep learning algorithms and neural network architectures specifically designed for image restoration and 3D reconstruction. This process allows for the synthesis of high-fidelity images that are historically accurate and visually coherent. The key findings of our work indicate significant improvements in image quality, surpassing conventional restoration techniques in terms of accuracy and detail. By comparing our results with existing models, our method demonstrates superior performance in reconstructing scenes from limited or fragmented data sources, making it a valuable tool for historical studies and archival projects. In conclusion, Time-Travel Rephotography offers an important contribution to the field of digital archiving and historical research, providing a transformative tool for museums, historians, and the entertainment industry to reimagine and experience the past. Potential applications of this research extend to virtual reality (VR) experiences and educational platforms that benefit from engaging with rich, immersive historical content. This research not only advances technological capabilities in historical image processing but also opens avenues for exploring new dimensions of cultural heritage preservation. Key keywords include: rephotography, historical image restoration, AI, ML, deep learning, 3D reconstruction, and virtual reality.

Tăng cường gắn kết đô thị và nông thôn là một vấn đề quan trọng trong việc phát triển bền vững của các quốc gia. Để đạt được mục tiêu này, việc hình thành các đô thị quy mô nhỏ tại các khu vực nông thôn đang trở thành một giải pháp hiệu quả. Các đô thị quy mô nhỏ không chỉ mang lại cơ hội kinh tế và việc làm cho người dân nông thôn mà còn giúp giảm thiểu sự chênh lệch về phát triển giữa đô thị và nông thôn. Bằng cách tạo ra các trung tâm kinh tế và dịch vụ tại các khu vực nông thôn, người dân có thể tiếp cận được với các dịch vụ cơ bản như giáo dục, y tế và thương mại mà không cần phải di chuyển đến các thành phố lớn. Hình thành các đô thị quy mô nhỏ cũng giúp tăng cường gắn kết giữa đô thị và nông thôn thông qua việc tạo ra các mối quan hệ kinh tế và xã hội giữa hai khu vực. Điều này có thể giúp giảm thiểu sự chênh lệch về phát triển và tạo ra một cộng đồng phát triển bền vững. Tuy nhiên, việc hình thành các đô thị quy mô nhỏ cũng đòi hỏi sự đầu tư và hỗ trợ từ các cơ quan chức năng và các tổ chức quốc tế. Việc này cần được thực hiện một cách có kế hoạch và bền vững để đảm bảo rằng các đô thị quy mô nhỏ có thể phát triển và tồn tại trong thời gian dài.

Facial Expression Recognition (FER) remains a challenging task due to subtle variations in facial expressions and inherent ambiguities in expression perception. This paper introduces a novel AU-Expression Knowledge Constrained Representation Learning (AUEK-RCL) framework designed to enhance the discriminative power of learned features by explicitly incorporating Action Unit (AU) knowledge. The proposed framework utilizes a two-branch network: one branch learns global expression features, while the other leverages AU annotations to learn AU-aware representations. A knowledge distillation strategy is then employed to transfer the AU-specific knowledge to the global expression branch, effectively constraining the learned representations. Furthermore, we introduce a novel AU relation regularization term to enforce the consistency between the predicted AU intensities and expression labels. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including AffectNet and RAF-DB, demonstrate that the AUEK-RCL framework achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing existing methods. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the individual components of the proposed framework. The results highlight the importance of incorporating AU knowledge for robust and accurate FER. Keywords: Facial Expression Recognition, Action Units, Representation Learning, Knowledge Distillation, Deep Learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurately forecasting human trajectories and head poses in dynamic environments, a critical task for applications such as autonomous navigation, surveillance, and human-robot interaction. We propose a novel approach that jointly reasons on *tracklets* (short trajectory segments) and *vislets* (visual appearance features) to enhance prediction accuracy. Our method integrates spatiotemporal information from tracklets with contextual visual cues from vislets, leveraging a multi-modal deep learning framework. The model employs a transformer-based architecture to capture long-range dependencies and temporal dynamics, enabling robust predictions even in crowded and complex scenarios. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods, with a 12% reduction in trajectory prediction error and a 15% improvement in head pose estimation accuracy. The proposed approach not only enhances forecasting precision but also provides interpretable insights into the relationship between motion patterns and visual context. This work contributes to advancing human behavior understanding in real-world environments, with potential applications in robotics, augmented reality, and intelligent transportation systems. **Keywords**: trajectory forecasting, head pose estimation, tracklets, vislets, transformer models, multi-modal learning, human behavior analysis.

Đặt vấn đề: Bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ liên quan chuyển hóa (Metabolic associated fatty liver disease - MAFLD) là nguyên nhân hàng đầu gây bệnh gan mạn tính, trong dân số thừa cân, béo phì chiếm 50,7%. Bệnh nhân có bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ liên quan chuyển hoá tăng nguy cơ tử vong do mọi nguyên nhân với hazard ratio là 1,2. Tại Việt Nam tỷ lệ thừa cân, béo phì ở người trưởng thành chiếm ở mức cao với khoảng 16% và ngày càng gia tăng. Các nghiên cứu trước đây tại Việt Nam tiến hành trên định nghĩa cũ là bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ không do rượu mà đã loại bỏ đi những bệnh gan đồng mắc góp phần làm tăng mức độ nhiễm mỡ, xơ hóa gan. Do đó, chúng tôi thực hiện nghiên cứu này nhằm tìm ra tỷ lệ hiện mắc và đặc điểm lâm sàng ở bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ liên quan chuyển hóa góp phần quản lý toàn diện nhóm bệnh nhân này. Giá trị độ cứng gan và nhiễm mỡ gan trong nhóm bệnh nhân MAFLD cao hơn nhóm không MAFLD, p < 0,05. Kết luận: MAFLD chiếm 72,9% ở bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì. Trong nhóm bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc MAFLD có tỷ lệ các bệnh lý chuyển hóa, giá trị độ cứng gan và nhiễm mỡ gan cao hơn so với không MAFLD.

This paper presents an empirical evaluation of a Q-Learning algorithm for model-free autonomous soaring in unstructured atmospheric environments. The primary objective is to enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to exploit atmospheric updrafts, such as thermals, for energy-efficient flight without relying on predefined environmental models. The proposed method employs Q-Learning, a reinforcement learning algorithm, to dynamically learn optimal soaring strategies from sensor feedback and flight experience. Through extensive simulated flight trials, the performance of the model-free Q-Learning agent is assessed against traditional rule-based and model-driven soaring approaches. Results demonstrate that the Q-Learning algorithm can successfully identify and utilize thermal updrafts, achieving significant improvements in flight endurance and energy conservation. Notably, the system demonstrates adaptability to varying and unpredictable wind fields, outperforming baseline methods in both success rate and cumulative soaring time. The study highlights the practical potential of reinforcement learning for enhancing UAV autonomy in challenging and dynamic atmospheric conditions. These findings offer valuable insights for future developments in autonomous flight, environmental adaptation, and energy-aware UAV operations. Keywords: Q-Learning, reinforcement learning, model-free control, autonomous soaring, unmanned aerial vehicles, atmospheric energy harvesting.

This paper addresses the challenge of fine-grained fashion similarity prediction, which aims to accurately assess the visual similarity between fashion items by considering attribute-specific details. We propose a novel Attribute-Specific Embedding Learning (ASEL) framework that learns distinct embedding spaces for different fashion attributes, enabling a more nuanced similarity assessment. The ASEL framework consists of three key components: an attribute recognition module, an attribute-specific embedding module, and a similarity calculation module. The attribute recognition module automatically identifies key attributes from fashion images. The attribute-specific embedding module then learns attribute-specific embeddings using a contrastive loss function, pulling similar items closer in the embedding space for each attribute. Finally, the similarity calculation module aggregates the attribute-specific similarities to predict an overall similarity score. Experimental results on a large-scale fashion dataset demonstrate that the proposed ASEL framework significantly outperforms existing methods in fine-grained fashion similarity prediction, achieving state-of-the-art performance. The ASEL framework provides a powerful tool for various fashion-related applications, such as personalized recommendation and visual search, by improving the accuracy of visual similarity assessment.

The objective of this research is to address the challenges of scalability and efficiency in Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) algorithms, which are pivotal in handling large-scale machine learning tasks. We propose Asynch-SGBDT, an innovative asynchronous parallel stochastic gradient boosting decision tree algorithm employing a parameter server framework. Our method leverages the power of asynchronous communication to enhance computational efficiency and scalability, enabling efficient handling of vast data sets across distributed environments. By integrating stochastic techniques, Asynch-SGBDT reduces computational redundancy and speeds up convergence compared to traditional synchronous models. Experiments conducted demonstrate significant improvements in both speedup and accuracy on extensive datasets when compared to conventional GBDT algorithms and existing parallel solutions. The results highlight the superior performance of the proposed method in distributed machine learning environments. The implication of this research lies in its potential to significantly enhance large-scale machine learning applications across various fields such as data mining, financial modeling, and artificial intelligence. Key contributions include the design of an asynchronous parallel framework that effectively balances load and minimizes communication overhead. This study invites further exploration into asynchronous methodologies for accelerated machine learning processes. Keywords: Asynchronous, Stochastic Gradient Boosting, Decision Tree, Parameter Server, Parallel Computing, Large-scale Machine Learning.

Monocular depth estimation, a critical task in computer vision, aims to predict depth from a single image, enabling applications in robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous systems. This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating depth in complex scenes by proposing a novel deep multi-scale architecture. The proposed model leverages hierarchical feature extraction at multiple scales to capture both fine-grained details and global contextual information, enhancing depth prediction accuracy. We introduce a fusion mechanism that effectively combines features from different scales, ensuring robust performance across diverse environments. The architecture is trained and evaluated on widely used benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results show significant improvements in depth estimation accuracy, particularly in scenarios with occlusions, textureless regions, and varying lighting conditions. The proposed approach achieves a 12% reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) and a 15% improvement in root mean square error (RMSE) over existing methods. Furthermore, the model exhibits strong generalization capabilities, making it suitable for real-world applications. This research contributes to advancing monocular depth estimation by introducing a scalable and efficient architecture that bridges the gap between local and global feature representations. The findings highlight the potential of multi-scale learning for improving depth perception in computer vision systems. **Keywords**: Monocular depth estimation, deep learning, multi-scale architecture, feature fusion, computer vision, depth perception.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficient multi-label segmentation in images containing multiple "hedgehog" shapes—a class of objects characterized by complex, radially-oriented boundaries. We present a novel adaptation of the α-expansion algorithm, a graph-cut based optimization technique widely used for discrete energy minimization, to effectively handle the unique geometric and topological properties of hedgehog-like objects. Our approach incorporates shape priors and boundary directionality into the energy function, enabling more accurate delineation of each individual shape even in the presence of significant overlap or occlusion. Experimental evaluation on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrates that our method outperforms existing multi-label segmentation techniques in terms of boundary accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to noise. The proposed algorithm maintains scalability for images with a high number of objects and complex interactions. Our contributions include an enhanced formulation of α-expansion for specialized shape constraints, a practical graph construction for hedgehog modeling, and a comprehensive analysis of performance across varied datasets. These insights facilitate improved segmentation in medical imaging, biological studies, and automated object recognition where accurate boundary extraction of spiky or radiate forms is essential. Keywords: α-expansion, graph cuts, multi-label segmentation, hedgehog shapes, shape priors, computer vision.

Accurate object detection is a critical challenge in computer vision, with bounding box regression being a fundamental component of modern detection systems. This paper addresses the limitations of traditional bounding box regression methods, which often fail to account for prediction uncertainty, leading to suboptimal localization accuracy. We propose a novel approach that integrates uncertainty estimation directly into the bounding box regression process, enabling the model to predict both the bounding box coordinates and their associated confidence levels. Our method leverages a probabilistic framework to model uncertainty, improving robustness to ambiguous or noisy annotations. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including COCO and Pascal VOC, demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances localization precision compared to state-of-the-art methods. The results show a notable reduction in localization errors, particularly for challenging cases involving occluded or partially visible objects. Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for decision-making in complex environments, with applications ranging from robotics to game playing. However, the lack of standardized evaluation methodologies poses challenges in comparing and advancing RL algorithms. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of benchmarking frameworks designed for RL, aiming to address the need for consistent and reproducible evaluation practices. We analyze the key components of these frameworks, including environment design, performance metrics, and scalability considerations. Additionally, we compare the strengths and limitations of existing frameworks, highlighting their suitability for different RL tasks and domains. Our findings reveal significant gaps in current benchmarking practices, such as the underrepresentation of real-world scenarios and the need for more robust evaluation metrics. The survey concludes with recommendations for future research directions, emphasizing the development of unified benchmarking standards to accelerate progress in RL. This work contributes to the RL community by providing a structured overview of existing frameworks and offering insights into improving evaluation methodologies. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Benchmarking Frameworks, Evaluation Metrics, Reproducibility, Scalability, Performance Analysis.

This paper addresses the need for a versatile and computationally efficient framework for comparing probability measures in high-dimensional spaces, which is critical in various applications such as machine learning, statistics, and signal processing. We introduce the concept of Generalized Sliced Wasserstein Distances, extending the classical sliced Wasserstein metric to provide greater flexibility and effectiveness in capturing the underlying geometric structures of data distributions. Methods/Approach: Our approach is based on leveraging a novel integration of projection techniques with enhanced characteristic functions that allow for an adaptable definition of slices in the space of probability measures. By incorporating generalized projections and distribution features, we construct a scalable and robust distance metric that improves upon traditional metrics in both efficiency and accuracy. Results/Findings: We conduct extensive experiments to evaluate the performance of the Generalized Sliced Wasserstein Distances across several high-dimensional datasets. The results demonstrate a superior ability to differentiate between complex data distributions compared to existing metrics. In terms of computational efficiency, our method significantly reduces processing time while maintaining high accuracy levels, making it suitable for large-scale applications. Conclusion/Implications: The Generalized Sliced Wasserstein Distances present a novel solution to the challenges of high-dimensional probability measure comparison, offering advancements in both theoretical and practical realms. Our findings can impact diverse fields, enhancing techniques for data analysis, distribution comparison, and machine learning model optimization. This research introduces a valuable tool for practitioners and researchers seeking effective distance metrics in complex domains. Keywords: Wasserstein distances, probability measures, high-dimensional space, data distributions, machine learning, distribution comparison, computational efficiency.

Graph representation learning has emerged as a critical area in machine learning, enabling the extraction of meaningful features from complex graph-structured data. This paper introduces a novel approach, *Kernel-Regularized Graph Representation Learning* (KGRL), which addresses the challenge of preserving both local and global structural properties in graph embeddings. The proposed method integrates kernel-based regularization techniques into graph neural networks (GNNs) to enhance the representation of graph topology while maintaining computational efficiency. By leveraging spectral graph theory and kernel functions, KGRL ensures robust feature extraction across diverse graph types, including sparse and densely connected networks. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that KGRL outperforms state-of-the-art methods in tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph clustering, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and scalability. The framework's ability to balance local node interactions with global graph structure highlights its potential for applications in social network analysis, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems. This work contributes a scalable and theoretically grounded solution to graph representation learning, offering a new perspective on integrating kernel methods with deep learning architectures. **Keywords**: graph representation learning, graph neural networks, kernel regularization, spectral graph theory, node classification, link prediction.

This paper addresses the challenge of 3D object detection in point clouds, a crucial task in various applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and scene understanding. Our objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of voting-based 3D object detection methods. We propose a novel approach, Back-tracing Representative Points (BRP), which enhances the detection process by effectively selecting and back-tracing representative points in the point cloud. Our method utilizes a combination of geometric and semantic features to identify key points that contribute to the detection of objects. The BRP approach is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in detection accuracy and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that BRP achieves a notable increase in precision and recall, particularly in scenarios with complex scenes and occlusions. The proposed method has important implications for various 3D vision tasks, including object recognition, tracking, and scene reconstruction. Key contributions of this research include the introduction of a robust and efficient back-tracing mechanism, the integration of geometric and semantic features, and the demonstration of improved performance in challenging 3D object detection scenarios. Relevant keywords: 3D object detection, point clouds, voting-based methods, back-tracing, representative points, geometric features, semantic features.

This study addresses the challenges associated with document layout analysis by exploring a Human-In-The-Loop (HITL) framework to enhance automatic processing methodologies. Traditional algorithms often struggle with the complexity and variability found in document layouts across different formats and stylistic elements. Our research aims to improve the accuracy and adaptability of layout analysis by incorporating human insights and expertise into the computational process. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel HITL framework that integrates human feedback with advanced machine learning and image processing techniques. The system employs an iterative process where human experts can provide input on the layout interpretation, guiding the machine learning models in refining their predictions. Key components include an interactive interface for real-time feedback, a robust algorithm for detecting diverse layout patterns, and a training mechanism for continual improvement of the model based on human interaction. Results/Findings: The proposed system was evaluated against state-of-the-art automated layout analysis tools using a diverse dataset of digital documents. Results demonstrate a significant improvement in accuracy, with the HITL approach achieving higher precision and recall rates in identifying complex layout structures. The system also showed enhanced adaptability to new and unseen document styles compared to fully automated solutions. Conclusion/Implications: The integration of human expertise within the document layout analysis process offers substantial benefits, primarily in achieving greater accuracy and flexibility. Our findings suggest that the HITL framework can be a viable solution for industries requiring precise document processing, such as digital archiving, legal documentation, and content management systems. Furthermore, this approach highlights the potential of human-machine collaboration in advancing the capabilities of document management technologies. Keywords: Human-In-The-Loop, document layout analysis, machine learning, image processing, human-computer interaction, automation, digital documents.

Seasonal time series forecasting is crucial in various domains such as finance, retail, and climate analysis, where accurate prediction of periodic trends can drive effective decision-making. This paper proposes a novel two-stage framework designed to enhance the accuracy and robustness of seasonal time series forecasting. In the first stage, the framework employs advanced decomposition techniques to separate the input data into trend, seasonal, and residual components, thereby isolating the unique patterns present in each element. In the second stage, specialized predictive models are applied to each component, with particular emphasis on capturing seasonal fluctuations through tailored algorithms, before recombining the forecasts to generate the final prediction. Experimental results on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional single-stage and benchmark methods, achieving lower forecasting error and improved adaptability to complex seasonal variations. The findings suggest that the two-stage framework offers significant advantages in modeling both regular and irregular seasonal patterns, making it a valuable tool for practitioners and researchers in time series analysis. Keywords: seasonal time series, forecasting, decomposition, predictive modeling, two-stage framework, trend analysis.

The assessment of aesthetic attributes in images is a critical task in computer vision, with applications ranging from digital content curation to personalized recommendation systems. This paper addresses the challenge of automatically evaluating aesthetic qualities such as composition, color harmony, and visual appeal in images. We propose a novel deep learning-based framework that leverages multi-task learning to simultaneously predict multiple aesthetic attributes. Our approach integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with attention mechanisms to capture both global and local features that contribute to aesthetic perception. The model is trained on a large-scale dataset annotated with diverse aesthetic attributes, ensuring robust performance across various image types. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and generalizability. Furthermore, we provide insights into the interpretability of the model, highlighting the key visual elements that influence aesthetic judgments. This research contributes to advancing the field of computational aesthetics by offering a scalable and effective solution for image quality assessment, with potential applications in photography, social media, and e-commerce. **Keywords**: Aesthetic assessment, image quality, deep learning, multi-task learning, attention mechanisms, computational aesthetics.

Hoạt động quân sự đồng minh của Mỹ trong Chiến tranh Việt Nam là một phần quan trọng của cuộc chiến tranh kéo dài từ năm 1955 đến 1975. Mỹ đã tham gia vào chiến tranh với mục tiêu ngăn chặn sự lan rộng của chủ nghĩa cộng sản ở Đông Dương. Mỹ đã cung cấp hỗ trợ quân sự và kinh tế cho chính phủ Việt Nam Cộng hòa, đồng thời triển khai quân đội của mình vào Việt Nam. Tuy nhiên, hoạt động quân sự của Mỹ đã gặp phải sự phản đối mạnh mẽ từ người dân Việt Nam và quốc tế. Mỹ đã sử dụng nhiều chiến thuật quân sự khác nhau, bao gồm sử dụng bom đạn, pháo binh và các loại vũ khí khác. Tuy nhiên, hoạt động quân sự của Mỹ đã không đạt được mục tiêu mong muốn và đã gây ra nhiều hậu quả nghiêm trọng cho người dân Việt Nam. Theo các ước tính, số lượng người chết trong chiến tranh Việt Nam đã lên đến hàng triệu người, bao gồm cả quân nhân và dân thường. Hoạt động quân sự của Mỹ đã gây ra nhiều hậu quả lâu dài cho Việt Nam, bao gồm cả sự tàn phá của đất nước và sự chia rẽ của xã hội. Hiệp định này đã đưa đến việc kết thúc chiến tranh và tái thống nhất Việt Nam dưới sự lãnh đạo của Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam.

This paper presents Pix2Seq, a simple and generic framework for object detection. Unlike existing approaches that explicitly integrate prior knowledge about the task, we simply cast object detection as a language modeling task conditioned on the observed pixel inputs. Object descriptions (e.g., bounding boxes and class labels) are expressed as sequences of discrete tokens, and we train a neural net to perceive the image and generate the desired sequence. Our approach is based mainly on the intuition that if a neural net knows about where and what the objects are, we just need to teach it how to read them out. Beyond the use of task-specific data augmentations, our approach makes minimal assumptions about the task, yet it achieves competitive results on the challenging COCO dataset, compared to highly specialized and well optimized detection algorithms.
