This research addresses the challenge of automated evaluation of root canal therapy by introducing an innovative deep learning framework. The aim is to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of dental diagnostics using cutting-edge technologies while minimizing human error and subjective interpretation. Methods/Approach: We propose the Anatomy-Guided Parallel Bottleneck Transformer Network, a novel architecture that leverages transformer-based models specifically designed for dental radiographs. This network incorporates anatomical guidance to focus on clinically relevant features and employs parallel bottleneck modules to efficiently process high-dimensional data. The integration of transformer technologies allows for superior representation learning and feature extraction compared to traditional convolutional neural networks. Results/Findings: The proposed model demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency over existing methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. The anatomy-guided approach results in enhanced localization and assessment of root canal fillings. Comparative analyses show our network's superior capability in identifying procedural errors and therapeutic outcomes, with increased precision and recall metrics. Conclusion/Implications: This research presents a transformative step forward in the field of automated dental diagnostics by integrating advanced neural networks with domain-specific anatomical insights. The Anatomy-Guided Parallel Bottleneck Transformer Network has the potential to revolutionize how root canal therapy evaluation is conducted in clinical settings, offering a scalable solution that could be extended to other dental procedures. Future directions include real-time processing capabilities and expanded applicability to diverse dental imaging modalities. Keywords: Root Canal Therapy, Transformer Network, Dental Diagnostics, Deep Learning, Anatomy-Guided, Bottleneck Modules, Automated Evaluation.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning robust feature representations for visual data by introducing a novel Local Similarity-Aware Deep Feature Embedding framework. Traditional deep embedding methods often focus on global data relationships, potentially overlooking subtle yet crucial local similarities that contribute significantly to discriminative power. To bridge this gap, we propose an end-to-end deep learning approach that integrates local similarity metrics directly into the embedding space construction. Our method leverages adaptive neighborhood modeling and a similarity-aware loss function, enabling the network to preserve local structural information while maintaining global semantic consistency. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets in image retrieval and face verification tasks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art embedding techniques in terms of retrieval accuracy and clustering performance. Analysis of the learned embeddings reveals enhanced separation between classes and increased cohesiveness within classes. This work highlights the importance of local similarity modeling in deep embeddings and paves the way for improved performance in various computer vision applications, including image classification, content-based retrieval, and biometric identification. Keywords: deep feature embedding, local similarity, deep learning, image retrieval, metric learning.

Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are capable of learning robust representation with different regularization methods and activations as convolutional layers are spatially correlated. Based on this property, a large variety of regional dropout strategies have been proposed, such as Cutout, DropBlock, CutMix, etc. These methods aim to promote the network to generalize better by partially occluding the discriminative parts of objects. However, all of them perform this operation randomly, without capturing the most important region(s) within an object. In this paper, we propose Attentive CutMix, a naturally enhanced augmentation strategy based on CutMix. In each training iteration, we choose the most descriptive regions based on the intermediate attention maps from a feature extractor, which enables searching for the most discriminative parts in an image. Our proposed method is simple yet effective, easy to implement and can boost the baseline significantly. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet datasets with various CNN architectures (in a unified setting) demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, which consistently outperforms the baseline CutMix and other methods by a significant margin.

The aim of this paper is to improve the accuracy of copy-move forgery detection (CMFD) in image forensics by proposing a novel scheme. The proposed scheme integrates both block-based and keypoint-based forgery detection methods. Firstly, speed-up robust feature (SURF) descriptor in log-polar space and scale invariant feature transform (SIFT) descriptor are extracted from an entire forged image. Secondly, generalized 2 nearest neighbor (g2NN) is employed to get massive matched pairs. Then, random sample consensus (RANSAC) algorithm is employed to filter out mismatched pairs, thus allowing rough localization of the counterfeit areas. To present more accurately these forgery areas more accurately, we propose an efficient and accurate algorithm, evolving circular domains coverage (ECDC), to cover present them. This algorithm aims to find satisfactory threshold areas by extracting block features from jointly evolving circular domains, which are centered on the matched pairs. Finally, morphological operation is applied to refine the detected forgery areas. The experimental results indicate that the proposed CMFD scheme can achieve better detection performance under various attacks compared with other state-of-the-art CMFD schemes.

We experimentally investigate a collection of feature engineering pipelines for use with a CNN for classifying eyes-open or eyes-closed from electroencephalogram (EEG) time-series from the Bonn dataset. Using the Takens' embedding--a geometric representation of time-series--we construct simplicial complexes from EEG data. We then compare \epsilon-series of Betti-numbers and \epsilon-series of graph spectra (a novel construction)--two topological invariants of the latent geometry from these complexes--to raw time series of the EEG to fill in a gap in the literature for benchmarking. These methods, inspired by Topological Data Analysis, are used for feature engineering to capture local geometry of the time-series. Additionally, we test these feature pipelines' robustness to downsampling and data reduction. This paper seeks to establish clearer expectations for both time-series classification via geometric features, and how CNNs for time-series respond to data of degraded resolution.

Abstract: Understanding the complex relationships among various brain connectivity graphs is crucial for advancing research in neuroscience and neuroinformatics. This paper introduces a novel topology-aware generative adversarial network (TA-GAN) designed for the joint prediction of multiple brain graphs from a single observed brain graph. The proposed method leverages both the topological characteristics of brain networks and the adversarial learning paradigm to model intricate inter-graph dependencies, which traditional graph-generation approaches often overlook. Our approach integrates graph convolutional networks for topology-preserving feature extraction and a multi-head generator architecture to simultaneously predict diverse target brain graphs. Extensive experiments on publicly available brain connectivity datasets demonstrate that TA-GAN significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of graph similarity metrics, structural fidelity, and prediction accuracy. The results highlight the model’s ability to capture cross-graph topological patterns while maintaining individual graph nuances. This research provides a powerful framework for multi-graph brain analysis, with potential applications in brain disease diagnosis, neuroscience research, and computational connectomics. Keywords: generative adversarial network, topology-aware, brain networks, graph prediction, multi-graph learning, brain connectivity, graph neural networks.

The detection of fake images generated by AI models has become increasingly important. However, existing detection methods are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper investigates the creation of imperceptible adversarial examples that can effectively evade state-of-the-art fake image detectors. We propose a novel adversarial attack strategy based on a frequency-aware perturbation generation, which carefully crafts small, high-frequency noises imperceptible to human eyes but significantly reduces the detection accuracy of deep learning-based detectors. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets, including those generated by GANs and diffusion models, demonstrate that our approach can successfully fool existing detectors with minimal visual artifacts. Specifically, our attack achieves a success rate of over 90% while maintaining a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of over 0.98, indicating high perceptual similarity to the original fake images. This highlights a critical vulnerability in current fake image detection techniques and underscores the need for more robust and secure detection mechanisms. Keywords: Adversarial examples, fake image detection, deep learning, adversarial attacks, image forensics, GANs, diffusion models.

Objective: Scene graph generation (SGG) seeks to produce structured representations of objects and their relationships in images, but existing graph-based approaches often rely on uniform message passing that overlooks the specific interaction between each source–target pair. This can lead to suboptimal relation predictions, especially for less frequent or context-sensitive interactions. Methods: We introduce Target-Tailored Source-Transformation (TTST), a novel module that dynamically adapts source node features to each target node before message aggregation. TTST employs a lightweight cross-attention mechanism to generate pair-specific transformation weights, effectively filtering irrelevant context and enhancing the discriminative power of relation representations. Integrated into a standard graph neural network backbone, our approach jointly refines object and predicate embeddings through alternating TTST layers and relation-aware pooling. Results: On the Visual Genome benchmark, our model achieves mean Recall@50 of 25.6% and Recall@100 of 27.3%, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by up to 2.7% and demonstrating significant improvements on tail-class predicates (+4.1% mR@100). Qualitative analyses show more balanced and semantically coherent scene graphs, with notable gains in zero-shot relation detection. Conclusion: By tailoring source transformations to each target, TTST addresses key limitations of generic message passing and yields more accurate, balanced scene graphs. This advancement holds promise for downstream applications in image captioning, visual question answering, and autonomous navigation. Keywords: Scene Graph Generation; Target-Tailored Source-Transformation; Graph Neural Networks; Visual Relationship Detection; Cross-Attention.

This paper introduces SLIDE, a novel approach to single image 3D photography that leverages soft layering and depth-aware inpainting to generate high-quality 3D representations from 2D images. The objective is to address the challenge of capturing complex scenes with depth information from a single viewpoint. Our method employs a deep learning-based framework that combines a soft layering technique to separate objects in the scene and a depth-aware inpainting algorithm to fill in missing regions. The results demonstrate significant improvements in 3D reconstruction accuracy and visual coherence compared to existing methods. Key findings include the ability to handle complex scenes with multiple objects and varying depths, as well as robustness to occlusions and missing data. The implications of this research are substantial, enabling applications in fields such as computer vision, robotics, and virtual reality. By advancing the state-of-the-art in single image 3D photography, SLIDE contributes to the development of more sophisticated and realistic 3D modeling and reconstruction techniques, with potential applications in areas like 3D printing, gaming, and cinematic production, leveraging technologies such as deep learning, computer vision, and 3D reconstruction.

The paper presents Seglearn, a Python package designed to facilitate the learning of sequences and time series. It addresses the challenge of efficiently handling sequential data, which is prevalent in various domains such as finance, healthcare, and sensor networks. Methods/Approach: Seglearn leverages a novel framework that integrates sequence segmentation and feature extraction with machine learning algorithms. The package offers a comprehensive suite of tools for preprocessing, transforming, and analyzing time series data. It includes capabilities for handling both supervised and unsupervised learning tasks, as well as integration with popular machine learning libraries like scikit-learn. Results/Findings: Key findings demonstrate that Seglearn significantly streamlines the development pipeline for time series modeling. Benchmark evaluations reveal that the package can produce competitive results in classification and regression tasks, often outperforming existing methods in terms of processing speed, ease of use, and accuracy. Additionally, the flexibility of Seglearn's modular design allows users to customize their workflows effectively. Conclusion/Implications: Seglearn's introduction offers a valuable contribution to the field by providing a robust, user-friendly toolset for time series analysis and machine learning. Its open-source nature and compatibility with established Python libraries make it an accessible and adaptable resource for researchers and practitioners. Potential applications span various industries with temporal data challenges, highlighting the package's broad utility and innovative approach. Key Keywords: Seglearn, Python, time series, sequence learning, machine learning, feature extraction, data preprocessing.

Estimating causal effects from observational data is a fundamental challenge across various domains. This paper introduces a transfer learning framework to improve the estimation of causal effects using neural networks, particularly when target datasets are small or biased. We propose a novel approach that leverages knowledge learned from related source datasets with known causal structures to enhance the performance of neural network estimators on the target dataset. Specifically, we pre-train a neural network on the source dataset to capture invariant relationships and then fine-tune it on the target dataset using a modified loss function that incorporates causal constraints. We evaluate our approach on synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets, demonstrating that it significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of estimation accuracy and robustness, especially when the target dataset suffers from limited sample size or confounding bias. Our findings suggest that transfer learning can effectively improve causal effect estimation by leveraging external knowledge and reducing the reliance on large, unbiased target datasets, opening up opportunities for more reliable causal inference in real-world applications. Keywords: Transfer Learning, Causal Inference, Neural Networks, Causal Effect Estimation, Observational Data, Bias Reduction.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms often face challenges in exploration-exploitation trade-offs, particularly in environments with sparse or deceptive rewards. This paper introduces *Adaptive Symmetric Reward Noising* (ASRN), a novel technique designed to enhance exploration by strategically perturbing reward signals during training. The proposed method dynamically adjusts the magnitude and symmetry of reward noise based on the agent's learning progress, ensuring a balance between exploration and exploitation. ASRN leverages a lightweight adaptive mechanism that requires minimal computational overhead, making it suitable for a wide range of RL applications. Experiments conducted on benchmark environments, including sparse-reward tasks and complex control problems, demonstrate that ASRN significantly improves convergence rates and final performance compared to traditional exploration strategies such as epsilon-greedy and intrinsic motivation methods. The results highlight the robustness of ASRN in mitigating local optima and accelerating learning in challenging scenarios. This work contributes to the RL community by providing a simple yet effective approach to reward shaping, with potential applications in robotics, game AI, and autonomous systems. Key innovations include the adaptive noise mechanism and its symmetric design, which ensures unbiased exploration. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Reward Noising, Exploration Strategies, Adaptive Algorithms, Sparse Rewards.

Inferring graph structure from observations on the nodes is an important and popular network science task. Departing from the more common inference of a single graph and motivated by social and biological networks, we study the problem of jointly inferring multiple graphs from the observation of signals at their nodes (graph signals), which are assumed to be stationary in the sought graphs. From a mathematical point of view, graph stationarity implies that the mapping between the covariance of the signals and the sparse matrix representing the underlying graph is given by a matrix polynomial. A prominent example is that of Markov random fields, where the inverse of the covariance yields the sparse matrix of interest. From a modeling perspective, stationary graph signals can be used to model linear network processes evolving on a set of (not necessarily known) networks. Leveraging that matrix polynomials commute, a convex optimization method along with sufficient conditions that guarantee the recovery of the true graphs are provided when perfect covariance information is available. Particularly important from an empirical viewpoint, we provide high-probability bounds on the recovery error as a function of the number of signals observed and other key problem parameters. Numerical experiments using synthetic and real-world data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method with perfect covariance information as well as its robustness in the noisy regime.

Abstract: Action recognition in videos is often hindered by the low spatial resolution of input frames, which can obscure crucial motion and appearance details necessary for accurate classification. This paper introduces a novel two-stream video super-resolution framework specifically designed to enhance action recognition performance. The proposed approach integrates spatial and temporal super-resolution streams: the spatial stream reconstructs fine-grained texture details within frames, while the temporal stream focuses on refining motion continuity and consistency between frames. Both streams are jointly optimized with an action recognition-guided loss to ensure that the super-resolved videos not only attain high visual quality but also better preserve action-relevant features. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in recognition accuracy compared to conventional super-resolution methods, particularly under challenging low-resolution conditions. Furthermore, our method achieves competitive computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications. The findings highlight the importance of task-oriented video enhancement and suggest that specialized super-resolution models can substantially boost the performance of downstream vision tasks like action recognition. Key keywords: action recognition, video super-resolution, two-stream networks, deep learning, spatiotemporal modeling, video classification.

Time series forecasting is a critical task in information technology, with applications spanning finance, healthcare, transportation, and energy management. This paper addresses the theoretical foundations and algorithmic advancements in time series forecasting. We present a comprehensive analysis of existing predictive models, including autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), exponential smoothing, and state-of-the-art machine learning approaches such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. Building on these, we introduce novel algorithms that combine classical statistical techniques with deep learning architectures to enhance prediction accuracy and adaptability to various types of temporal data. Extensive experiments on diverse benchmark datasets demonstrate that our hybrid models outperform traditional and contemporary forecasting methods across multiple evaluation metrics, including mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE). Our theoretical analysis further provides insights into the stability, convergence, and generalizability of the proposed algorithms. The results highlight the advantages of integrating domain knowledge with advanced computational models, offering robust solutions for real-world time series forecasting challenges. This work contributes new perspectives and practical tools for improving forecasting systems, and lays the groundwork for future research in the development of interpretable and scalable prediction algorithms. Key keywords include time series forecasting, prediction algorithms, ARIMA, LSTM, hybrid models, machine learning, and temporal data analysis.

This paper addresses the objective of enhancing pedestrian detection in images and videos using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The purpose is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of pedestrian detection systems, which is crucial for various applications such as autonomous vehicles, surveillance, and smart cities. We propose a novel approach that utilizes a deep CNN architecture to learn robust features from images, allowing for accurate pedestrian detection. Our method involves training a CNN model on a large dataset of images with annotated pedestrians, enabling the network to learn effective features for distinguishing pedestrians from non-pedestrian objects. The results show that our proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, outperforming existing pedestrian detection methods. The evaluation metrics demonstrate significant improvements in detection accuracy, precision, and recall. In conclusion, this research contributes to the development of more accurate and reliable pedestrian detection systems using deep CNNs. The proposed approach has potential applications in various fields, including computer vision, robotics, and transportation systems. Key keywords: pedestrian detection, deep convolutional neural networks, computer vision, object detection, autonomous vehicles.

Xác định và điều khiển tư thế là phân hệ rất quan trọng đối với chất lượng thực hiện nhiệm vụ của vệ tinh khi hoạt động trên quỹ đạo. Phân hệ đảm bảo độ chính xác khi trỏ hướng và duy trì sự ổn định tư thế. Bài báo này trình bày quá trình phát triển một bộ công cụ thực hành cho xác định và điều khiển tư thế, tên gọi ADCS kít, tại Trung tâm Vũ trụ Việt Nam dựa trên cơ sở kết quả nghiên cứu chuyên sâu về phân hệ này. Việc sử dụng công cụ chuyên dụng trong quá trình đào tạo và thực hành về xác định và điều khiển tư thế rất cần thiết với đặc thù hoạt động của vệ tinh trong môi trường không trọng lượng, không ma sát. Bộ công cụ được trang bị những phần cứng cơ bản của phân hệ như cảm biến đo lường quán tính (Inertial measurement unit - IMU) và các bánh xe động lượng cùng với bàn gá có khả năng giả lập trạng thái không trọng lượng, không ma sát. Các bánh xe được gá lắp theo ba kiểu cấu hình khác nhau: ba trục tiêu chuẩn, kim tự tháp, tứ diện cho phép thực hiện những dạng bài thực hành điều khiển tư thế khác nhau. ADCS kít là sản phẩm được phát triển với sự tài trợ của Chương trình Phát triển Công nghệ, Viện Hàn lâm Khoa học và Công nghệ Việt Nam.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc mô phỏng các bộ lọc sóng hài thụ động (Passive Harmonic Filters - PHF) để giảm thiểu ảnh hưởng của sóng hài trong hệ thống điện, đặc biệt khi tần số thay đổi. Sóng hài là các thành phần tần số không mong muốn có thể gây ra nhiều vấn đề như quá nhiệt, giảm tuổi thọ thiết bị và sai lệch trong hoạt động của hệ thống. Việc sử dụng PHF là một giải pháp hiệu quả để loại bỏ hoặc giảm thiểu các sóng hài này. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp mô phỏng để đánh giá hiệu suất của các cấu hình PHF khác nhau trong các điều kiện tần số biến đổi, từ đó xác định cấu hình tối ưu nhất. Kết quả mô phỏng cung cấp thông tin quan trọng cho việc thiết kế và triển khai các bộ lọc sóng hài thụ động hiệu quả, giúp cải thiện chất lượng điện năng và độ tin cậy của hệ thống điện. Nghiên cứu này có ý nghĩa quan trọng trong việc đảm bảo hoạt động ổn định và hiệu quả của các hệ thống điện hiện đại, đặc biệt là trong bối cảnh ngày càng có nhiều thiết bị điện tử công suất được sử dụng.

Công nghệ blockchain cung cấp một nền tảng an toàn, minh bạch và đáng tin cậy để thực hiện các giao dịch tài chính. Với khả năng lưu trữ và truyền tải thông tin một cách tự động, blockchain giúp giảm thiểu rủi ro gian lận và tăng cường tính minh bạch trong quá trình thanh toán. Ứng dụng blockchain trong thanh toán bằng tiền điện tử cho phép người dùng thực hiện các giao dịch nhanh chóng và an toàn, không cần phải qua các trung gian như ngân hàng. Điều này giúp giảm thiểu chi phí và tăng cường tính linh hoạt trong việc thực hiện các giao dịch tài chính. Ngoài ra, công nghệ blockchain cũng cung cấp khả năng bảo mật cao, giúp bảo vệ thông tin cá nhân và tài chính của người dùng. Tuy nhiên, ứng dụng blockchain trong thanh toán bằng tiền điện tử cũng có một số hạn chế. Ví dụ, công nghệ blockchain vẫn còn đang trong quá trình phát triển và chưa được áp dụng rộng rãi. Ngoài ra, việc sử dụng tiền điện tử trong thanh toán cũng còn gặp nhiều khó khăn do sự không ổn định của giá trị tiền điện tử. Tổng thể, ứng dụng blockchain trong thanh toán bằng tiền điện tử có tiềm năng lớn để cải thiện tính an toàn, minh bạch và linh hoạt trong việc thực hiện các giao dịch tài chính. Tuy nhiên, cần phải giải quyết các hạn chế và thách thức hiện tại để đưa công nghệ này vào ứng dụng rộng rãi.

In the rapidly evolving landscape of digital media, centralized video sharing platforms dominate, often leading to concerns over privacy, copyright issues, and data ownership. This thesis explores the potential of a decentralized video sharing website powered by the Eueno framework and smart contracts, addressing the need for a more equitable and user-controlled alternative. The motivation behind this research stems from the growing demand for transparency, security, and user empowerment in online content sharing. The primary objective of this work is to design and implement a decentralized video sharing platform that ensures content ownership remains with the creators while facilitating fair revenue distribution. Specifically, the research aims to resolve issues surrounding data centralization, user privacy breaches, and the monopolistic tendencies of existing services by employing decentralized storage and blockchain technology. To achieve these goals, a comprehensive architecture leveraging Eueno's capabilities along with Ethereum-based smart contracts is proposed. This methodology involves the integration of decentralized storage systems to host video content and the use of blockchain for secure transactions and content attribution, ensuring a trustless environment for both creators and consumers. The expected outcomes of this project include the successful deployment of a functional prototype, demonstrating improved security and control for users while fostering a vibrant community of content creators. Contributions of this research extend to enhancing awareness of decentralized solutions within the digital media field and providing a foundation for future advancements in the architecture of decentralized applications. In conclusion, this thesis not only proposes a viable alternative to traditional video sharing platforms but also underscores the significance of decentralization in shaping the future of digital media. Future research should explore the scalability of such platforms and the broader implications of decentralized technologies in other sectors of digital content distribution.

This paper proposes a novel Multiresolution Graph Variational Autoencoder (MGVAE) designed to learn compact and meaningful representations of graph-structured data at multiple scales. The objective is to address the challenges of graph representation learning by capturing both local and global patterns in a unified framework. Our approach combines the strengths of graph convolutional networks and variational autoencoders, enabling the model to learn multiresolution representations that preserve the structural properties of the input graphs. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of MGVAE in graph classification, clustering, and link prediction tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The key findings highlight the importance of multiresolution representations in graph learning, leading to improved performance and interpretability. This research contributes to the development of more powerful and flexible graph representation learning models, with potential applications in network analysis, recommendation systems, and computer vision. Key keywords: graph neural networks, variational autoencoders, multiresolution representation learning, graph classification, link prediction.

Deep transfer learning has emerged as a powerful approach for advancing medical image analysis, enabling models to leverage knowledge from large, general-purpose datasets for domain-specific tasks with limited labeled data. This paper aims to systematically explore and understand the underlying mechanisms that drive the effectiveness of deep transfer learning in the context of medical imaging. We evaluate different transfer learning strategies—including feature extraction, fine-tuning, and layer-wise adaptation—across multiple medical imaging modalities such as MRI, CT, and X-ray. Our methodology involves comprehensive experiments on benchmark datasets, analyzing model performance, feature representation shifts, and domain adaptation processes. The findings reveal that both the selection of source models and the extent of adaptation significantly influence performance, with deeper layers requiring targeted fine-tuning for optimal results in complex medical tasks. Additionally, visualization of learned feature spaces uncovers how knowledge transfer reshapes model representations to better capture medically relevant patterns. The study highlights best practices for deploying transfer learning in medical image analysis, addresses common pitfalls, and suggests pathways for improving generalization to rare diseases or novel imaging scenarios. This work advances the understanding of deep transfer learning mechanisms, providing actionable guidance for researchers and practitioners working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, computer vision, and medical healthcare. Key keywords: deep transfer learning, medical images, domain adaptation, feature extraction, fine-tuning, medical image analysis, AI in healthcare, model interpretability.

Motion estimation methods Motion estimation is the process of determining motion vectors that describe the transformation from one 2D image to another; usually from adjacent frames in a video sequence. It is an ill-posed problem as the motion is in three dimensions but the images are a projection of the 3D scene onto a 2D plane. The motion vectors may relate to the whole image (global motion estimation) or specific parts, such as rectangular blocks, arbitrary shaped patches or even per pixel.

This paper introduces a novel approach to action anticipation from first-person video using Rolling-Unrolling Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The objective is to predict future actions from egocentric video streams, enabling applications such as human-robot interaction and smart wearable devices. Our method employs a rolling-unrolling LSTM architecture, which recursively rolls and unrolls the input sequence to capture long-term dependencies and anticipate future actions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in action anticipation tasks. The proposed Rolling-Unrolling LSTM achieves significant improvements in prediction accuracy, particularly in scenarios with limited contextual information. This research contributes to the development of more accurate and efficient action anticipation systems, with potential applications in areas such as robotics, healthcare, and surveillance. Key keywords: action anticipation, first-person video, LSTM, rolling-unrolling, egocentric vision, human-robot interaction.

Semantic segmentation has been a critical task in computer vision, aiming to assign a class label to each pixel in an image. This paper introduces Boundary Neural Fields (BNF), a novel approach designed to enhance semantic segmentation by integrating boundary information directly into the neural network model. The primary objective of our research is to address the common issue of boundary blurring in segmentation maps, which often leads to imprecise classification outputs. The approach involves a new architecture that incorporates boundary features as part of a neural field, which is trained alongside traditional segmentation networks. Our method refines pixel-wise classification by utilizing boundary awareness to enhance the distinction between adjacent regions. We evaluate the performance of BNF on multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating that our model significantly improves segmentation quality compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly at object edges. Key results show improved accuracy and precision near boundaries, with quantitative metrics marking a clear enhancement in mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) scores. This marks a significant contribution to the field, providing a more granular level of segmentation and giving rise to potential applications in various domains like autonomous driving, medical imaging, and satellite imagery analysis. In conclusion, Boundary Neural Fields present a robust framework for semantic segmentation, offering precise boundary delineation and better overall performance, making it a valuable addition to existing segmentation techniques. This work paves the way for further research into the integration of boundary-aware components in other computer vision tasks. Keywords include semantic segmentation, boundary detection, neural fields, computer vision, and image processing.

This paper introduces SI-Score, a novel image dataset designed to facilitate fine-grained analysis of robustness in computer vision models. The objective is to evaluate and improve model performance under varying object locations, rotations, and sizes. To achieve this, we employ a systematic approach to generate a diverse set of images with controlled transformations, enabling comprehensive assessment of model robustness. Our dataset comprises a wide range of objects and scenes, allowing for detailed examination of model behavior. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of SI-Score in identifying vulnerabilities in state-of-the-art models, highlighting the need for improved robustness to object transformations. The key findings and contributions of this research include the development of a standardized evaluation framework and the identification of critical factors influencing model robustness. This work has significant implications for applications requiring reliable computer vision, such as autonomous vehicles, robotics, and surveillance systems. By utilizing SI-Score, researchers can develop more robust models, ultimately enhancing the performance and reliability of computer vision systems. Key keywords: computer vision, robustness, object recognition, image dataset, fine-grained analysis.

The increasing complexity and variability in image data present significant challenges to achieving robust image classification. This research aims to address these challenges by developing advanced methodologies that enhance the resilience and accuracy of image classification systems under diverse conditions. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel approach based on advanced convolutional neural networks (CNNs) tailored to maximize robustness in image classification tasks. By employing ensemble learning techniques alongside data augmentation strategies, our model is designed to effectively handle noise, occlusions, and adversarial attacks. Additionally, the integration of attention mechanisms is utilized to improve focus on relevant image features, enhancing classification performance. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our proposed model significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods across multiple standard benchmark datasets. The system exhibits superior performance in terms of classification accuracy and resilience against adversarial manipulations. Notably, our approach achieves a consistent improvement in accuracy by an average of 5% over traditional CNNs, highlighting its robustness and effectiveness. Conclusion/Implications: This research presents a significant advancement in the field of image classification by introducing a robust model that can be effectively utilized in varied application scenarios, including autonomous vehicles, medical imaging, and security systems. The methodologies developed contribute to the body of knowledge by providing a framework that addresses current limitations in image classification, paving the way for future exploration in enhancing model robustness. Keywords include image classification, convolutional neural networks, robustness, ensemble learning, attention mechanisms, and adversarial attacks.

This paper addresses the challenging problem of auto-labelling markers in optical motion capture systems, a critical task for ensuring accurate biomechanics and movement analysis. Traditional methods for labeling are time-consuming and prone to errors, especially in complex motion scenarios. Methods: We introduce a novel approach utilizing permutation learning to automate the process of marker labeling. Our method employs an advanced permutation neural network designed to learn and predict optimal marker-label configurations directly from optical motion capture data. The network architecture incorporates both spatial and temporal features, enhancing its capability to discern patterns and accurately map markers to predefined labels. Results: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our auto-labeling approach achieves a significant reduction in labeling error rates compared to conventional semi-automated methods. The system also shows superior performance in dynamic and occluded scenarios, where traditional methods struggle. The proposed solution efficiently processes large datasets while maintaining high accuracy and reliability. Conclusion: The research provides a significant advancement in the domain of motion capture, offering a fully automated and robust solution for marker labeling. This work not only improves current methodologies but also opens pathways for further exploration in automated motion analysis and related applications. The implementation of permutation learning in this context presents a new frontier for enhancing the efficiency and precision of optical motion capture systems. Keywords: auto-labeling, optical motion capture, permutation learning, neural network, biomechanics, movement analysis.

This paper addresses the growing demand for efficient and compact models for single image super-resolution (SISR), which aim to produce high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. Traditional methods often require significant computational resources, limiting their practical applications. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel approach termed "Contrastive Self-distillation" to enhance SISR model compactness and performance. The technique leverages the power of self-distillation, an iterative process where a model learns from its predictions, augmented with contrastive learning principles. This framework enables the model to refine its internal representation and achieve a balance between size and accuracy. Key components of our methodology include a carefully designed contrastive loss function and an innovative data augmentation procedure tailored for SISR tasks. Results/Findings: Through extensive experiments, our method demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional SISR models of similar size. Notably, our compact model achieves higher fidelity in image reconstruction with a significant reduction in both model parameters and computational cost. The results reveal improvements in image quality metrics such as PSNR and SSIM, substantiating the efficacy of the proposed contrastive self-distillation approach. Conclusion/Implications: The proposed method substantially contributes to the field of image processing by enabling more efficient deployment of SISR models in resource-constrained environments. This research not only advances the state-of-the-art in compact SISR techniques but also opens avenues for further exploration in integrating self-distillation and contrastive learning across diverse applications. Potential applications span areas such as mobile photography, real-time video streaming, and medical imaging where compact and swift SISR models are crucial. Keywords: Single Image Super-Resolution, Contrastive Learning, Self-Distillation, Image Processing, Model Compression.

This paper introduces NightVision, a novel approach for generating synthetic nighttime satellite imagery from readily available infrared (IR) observations. The primary objective is to overcome the limitations of traditional nighttime satellite imaging, which is often hindered by cloud cover and the high cost of specialized sensors. NightVision leverages a deep learning framework, specifically a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN), trained to map IR data to corresponding visible light imagery. The method utilizes a custom loss function that combines pixel-wise similarity with perceptual and adversarial losses to ensure realistic and high-resolution image synthesis. Experimental results demonstrate that NightVision achieves superior performance compared to existing interpolation and statistical methods, generating visually plausible and accurate nighttime imagery even in challenging atmospheric conditions. The generated imagery holds significant potential for various applications, including urban monitoring, disaster response, and environmental studies. Key words: satellite imagery, nighttime, infrared, image synthesis, generative adversarial network, deep learning.

This paper introduces RotLSTM, a novel architecture for enhancing memory management in recurrent neural networks by integrating rotational transformations into long short-term memory (LSTM) units. The primary objective is to address the limitations of standard LSTM models in capturing long-range dependencies and mitigating memory bottlenecks, which often impede performance in complex sequential learning tasks such as natural language processing and time series analysis. RotLSTM incorporates a rotation-based memory mechanism within the cell state, enabling more flexible information encoding and improved retention of historical context. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets spanning language modeling, sequence classification, and signal prediction, RotLSTM demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional LSTM and gated recurrent unit (GRU) models, particularly in tasks requiring long-term information preservation. Key findings highlight enhanced sequence recall, faster convergence, and improved resilience to vanishing gradient problems. The results suggest that the rotational memory mechanism facilitates more efficient communication across time steps, leading to better generalization and robustness. In conclusion, RotLSTM represents a significant advancement in recurrent neural network design, with potential applications in speech recognition, text generation, and adaptive signal processing. Key keywords: RotLSTM, recurrent neural networks, rotational memory, LSTM, long-range dependencies, sequence modeling.

Image captioning, the task of generating descriptive sentences for images, remains a critical challenge in computer vision and natural language processing. While end-to-end deep learning architectures have become popular, intermediate structured representations such as scene graphs—graph-based descriptions capturing objects, attributes, and relationships within images—have often been underutilized or dismissed. This paper advocates for the renewed integration of scene graphs into the image captioning pipeline, presenting a systematic study on their effectiveness. We propose an enhanced scene graph extraction and encoding framework, combining advanced object detection, relationship modeling, and graph neural networks to bridge visual content with natural language descriptions. Experimental results demonstrate that leveraging scene graphs leads to notable improvements in caption relevance, coherence, and factual accuracy compared to purely end-to-end models, especially on complex scenes requiring relational reasoning. Our analysis further reveals that scene graphs facilitate better controllability and interpretability in caption generation. These findings underscore the importance of structured representations in achieving high-quality image-to-text systems. Potential applications include assistive technologies, visual content search, and AI-based storytelling. Keywords: scene graphs, image captioning, graph neural networks, structured representation, computer vision, natural language processing.

This paper addresses the challenge of generating realistic facial animations from speech signals using advanced deep learning techniques. The objective is to develop a robust system capable of synthesizing high-quality, synchronized facial expressions and lip movements driven solely by audio input. To achieve this, we propose a novel framework based on Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (cGANs), which leverages the temporal and spectral features of speech to conditionally generate corresponding facial movements. Our approach incorporates a multi-modal architecture that combines audio feature extraction with a generative model trained on paired audio-visual datasets. The system is evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of visual quality, synchronization accuracy, and realism compared to existing methods. Key findings reveal that our model effectively captures subtle nuances in facial expressions and lip dynamics, achieving state-of-the-art results. The implications of this research extend to applications in virtual reality, video conferencing, and digital content creation, where realistic speech-driven facial reenactment is critical. This work contributes to the field by introducing a scalable and efficient solution that bridges the gap between speech and visual animation, offering significant improvements over traditional approaches. **Keywords**: Speech-driven animation, facial reenactment, conditional GANs, deep learning, audio-visual synthesis.

This paper addresses the challenge of forecasting time series systems with unknown clusters of forecast tasks by introducing a novel approach to learn predictive leading indicators. The methodology involves training a model to learn predictive leading indicators that can be used to forecast future values of the time series. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving forecast accuracy and identifying unknown clusters of forecast tasks. The key findings indicate that our method outperforms traditional forecasting techniques, particularly in systems with multiple underlying patterns. The contributions of this research include the development of a new framework for learning predictive leading indicators and the application of clustering techniques to identify unknown forecast tasks. This work has significant implications for real-world applications, such as demand forecasting, financial forecasting, and resource allocation, where accurate predictions are crucial. Key keywords: time series forecasting, leading indicators, clustering, machine learning, predictive modeling.

Ứng dụng dự đoán năng lượng điện gió là một hệ thống thông minh được thiết kế để dự đoán lượng điện năng có thể được sản xuất từ các trang trại điện gió. Hệ thống này sử dụng các mô hình học máy và dữ liệu thời tiết để dự đoán lượng gió và năng lượng điện có thể được sản xuất. Ứng dụng này có thể giúp các công ty năng lượng điện gió tối ưu hóa sản xuất, giảm thiểu chi phí và tăng cường hiệu suất. Hệ thống dự đoán năng lượng điện gió này được xây dựng dựa trên các mô hình thống kê và học máy, sử dụng dữ liệu thời tiết và khí tượng để dự đoán lượng gió và năng lượng điện có thể được sản xuất. Ứng dụng này cũng có thể tích hợp với các hệ thống quản lý năng lượng điện gió hiện có, giúp các công ty năng lượng điện gió có thể theo dõi và quản lý sản xuất một cách hiệu quả hơn. Ngoài ra, ứng dụng này cũng có thể giúp giảm thiểu tác động môi trường của các trang trại điện gió, bằng cách tối ưu hóa sản xuất và giảm thiểu lượng khí thải carbon. Hyperspectral images (HSI) are essential in various applications, such as remote sensing and medical imaging, but often suffer from mixed noise due to environmental factors and data acquisition processes. This research addresses the challenge of removing such noise without requiring pre-labeled training data, aiming to enhance the quality and utility of hyperspectral imagery. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative unsupervised approach utilizing a Spatial-Spectral Constrained Deep Image Prior (SSC-DIP) that effectively removes mixed noise from hyperspectral images. Our method leverages the deep image prior paradigm, which enables noise removal through the implicit structure embedded in the data itself, without additional labeled datasets. By introducing spatial-spectral constraints, we exploit the inherent properties of hyperspectral data to preserve essential features while denoising. Results/Findings: The proposed SSC-DIP model demonstrates superior performance in noise removal compared to existing unsupervised methods. It effectively reduces various types of noise, such as Gaussian, impulse, and stripe noise, common in HSI datasets. Comprehensive experiments show that our approach outperforms traditional and recent state-of-the-art techniques, as evidenced by metrics such as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and visual quality assessments. Conclusion/Implications: This research highlights the potential of using unsupervised deep learning techniques for HSI noise reduction, offering a significant advancement over previous techniques that rely on supervised data. Our findings indicate that spatial-spectral constraints significantly enhance the denoising capability, making this approach particularly relevant for applications needing high-quality hyperspectral data, such as precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and diagnostic imaging. Future work may extend the framework to adaptively learn constraints for specific noise characteristics in diverse imaging contexts. Key Keywords: Hyperspectral images, mixed noise removal, unsupervised learning, deep image prior, spatial-spectral constraints, noise reduction.

Manifold learning, a critical area in machine learning, aims to uncover low-dimensional structures embedded in high-dimensional data. This paper explores the potential of deep neural networks (DNNs) to serve as locality-sensitive hash (LSH) functions for manifold learning tasks. We propose a novel approach where DNNs are trained to map high-dimensional data points into a lower-dimensional space while preserving local geometric relationships. By leveraging the inherent nonlinearity and adaptability of DNNs, our method achieves superior locality sensitivity compared to traditional LSH techniques. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves nearest-neighbor search accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we provide theoretical insights into why DNNs can effectively approximate LSH functions under specific conditions. The findings highlight the versatility of DNNs beyond conventional applications, offering a promising direction for scalable and efficient manifold learning. This work contributes to advancing both deep learning and manifold learning by bridging their theoretical and practical aspects, with potential applications in data compression, dimensionality reduction, and large-scale data retrieval. **Keywords**: manifold learning, deep neural networks, locality-sensitive hashing, dimensionality reduction, nearest-neighbor search.

Existing works in Continual Learning mainly focus on the Catastrophic Forgetting problem, while overlooking other factors. In this thesis, instead of traditional approaches where many methods were proposed to preserve old knowledge, I give a concrete analysis of the transferability of the representations in the CRE setting. Especially, I focus on the bad impact of traditional Cross-Entropy loss on the transferability and how to improve it.

Identifying disease genes is crucial for understanding disease mechanisms and developing effective treatments. Link prediction methods on biological networks offer a promising avenue for this task. However, existing methods often treat all relationships between genes equally, neglecting the varying importance of different relation types in disease etiology. This paper introduces a novel relation-weighted link prediction framework to prioritize disease gene candidates. Our method incorporates diverse biological relationships, such as protein-protein interactions, gene co-expression, and signaling pathways, and learns relation-specific weights based on their relevance to the target disease. We develop a network embedding approach that integrates these relation weights to generate gene representations. These representations are then used to predict novel gene-disease associations. Experiments on multiple disease datasets demonstrate that our relation-weighted approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art link prediction methods and achieves higher accuracy in identifying known disease genes. Furthermore, we validate novel gene-disease associations predicted by our method using independent biological databases and literature mining. The results highlight the importance of considering relation heterogeneity in disease gene identification and the effectiveness of our proposed framework. Keywords: Link prediction, disease gene identification, network embedding, biological networks, relation weighting.

This paper addresses the challenge of short-term load forecasting by introducing a novel reinforcement learning-based approach for dynamic model selection. The objective is to improve forecasting accuracy by adaptively selecting the most suitable model from a pool of candidates based on real-time data. Our method employs a reinforcement learning framework that learns to optimize model selection through trial and error, leveraging historical data to inform decision-making. The results show that our approach outperforms traditional static model selection methods, achieving significant improvements in forecasting accuracy. Key findings indicate that the dynamic selection of models based on reinforcement learning leads to better handling of non-stationary load patterns and improved adaptability to changing environmental conditions. The proposed approach contributes to the development of more accurate and reliable short-term load forecasting systems, with potential applications in smart grid management and energy efficiency optimization. Relevant keywords include reinforcement learning, dynamic model selection, short-term load forecasting, and energy forecasting.

Thuật toán đáp ứng nhanh (Fast Response Algorithm - FRA) được ứng dụng rộng rãi trong các hệ thống điều chỉnh tự động nhờ khả năng phản hồi nhanh chóng. Tuy nhiên, FRA tồn tại một số hạn chế cần được giải quyết để nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động. Một trong những hạn chế chính là sự nhạy cảm với nhiễu, có thể dẫn đến các dao động không mong muốn trong hệ thống. Ngoài ra, FRA có thể gặp khó khăn trong việc duy trì độ ổn định khi đối mặt với các thay đổi đột ngột trong tải hoặc các thông số hệ thống. Để khắc phục những nhược điểm này, các nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc tích hợp các bộ lọc nhiễu thích ứng, sử dụng các kỹ thuật điều khiển dự đoán để giảm thiểu ảnh hưởng của độ trễ, và áp dụng các phương pháp điều khiển thích nghi để tự động điều chỉnh các tham số của thuật toán FRA theo điều kiện vận hành thực tế. Việc giải quyết triệt để các hạn chế này sẽ giúp FRA phát huy tối đa tiềm năng trong các ứng dụng điều khiển tự động phức tạp.

Unsupervised representation learning techniques, such as learning word embeddings, have had a significant impact on the field of natural language processing. Similar representation learning techniques have not yet become commonplace in the context of 3D vision. This, despite the fact that the physical 3D spaces have a similar semantic structure to bodies of text: words are surrounded by words that are semantically related, just like objects are surrounded by other objects that are similar in concept and usage. In this work, we exploit this structure in learning semantically meaningful low dimensional vector representations of objects. We learn these vector representations by mining a dataset of scanned 3D spaces using an unsupervised algorithm. We represent objects as point clouds, a flexible and general representation for 3D data, which we encode into a vector representation. We show that using our method to include context increases the ability of a clustering algorithm to distinguish different semantic classes from each other. Furthermore, we show that our algorithm produces continuous and meaningful object embeddings through interpolation experiments.

In this paper, a driver's intention prediction near a road intersection is proposed. Our approach uses a deep bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with an attention mechanism model based on a hybrid-state system (HSS) framework. As intersection is considered to be as one of the major source of road accidents, predicting a driver's intention at an intersection is very crucial. Our method uses a sequence to sequence modeling with an attention mechanism to effectively exploit temporal information out of the time-series vehicular data including velocity and yaw-rate. The model then predicts ahead of time whether the target vehicle/driver will go straight, stop, or take right or left turn. The performance of the proposed approach is evaluated on a naturalistic driving dataset and results show that our method achieves high accuracy as well as outperforms other methods. The proposed solution is promising to be applied in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and as part of active safety system of autonomous vehicles.

This paper proposes a novel supervised classification algorithm, Projection Pursuit Forest (PPF), which integrates the strengths of projection pursuit and random forest techniques. The objective is to improve classification accuracy and robustness in high-dimensional datasets. The PPF algorithm works by projecting the data onto a set of optimal directions, identified through an iterative process, and then applying a random forest classifier to the projected data. Experimental results demonstrate that PPF outperforms state-of-the-art classification methods, including traditional random forest and support vector machines, on several benchmark datasets. The key findings highlight the effectiveness of PPF in handling complex interactions between variables and its ability to identify relevant features. The proposed algorithm has significant implications for applications in data mining, machine learning, and pattern recognition, particularly in domains with high-dimensional data. The novelty of PPF lies in its ability to combine the flexibility of projection pursuit with the robustness of random forest, making it a valuable addition to the suite of supervised classification techniques. Key keywords: Projection Pursuit, Random Forest, Supervised Classification, High-Dimensional Data, Machine Learning.

Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to language inference by leveraging multi-head automata trained via reinforcement learning. Traditional language inference methods often rely on fixed-rule systems or neural models that may struggle with complex language constructs and long-range dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose a framework that models formal language inference as a sequential decision-making problem, where multi-head finite automata serve as adaptive learners capable of simultaneously tracking multiple information streams within text. Our method utilizes reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize the automata's transition policies, improving their ability to generalize across diverse language structures. Experimental evaluations were conducted on standard language inference benchmarks, demonstrating that our approach achieves superior accuracy and efficiency compared to conventional automata and neural network-based models. The results highlight notable improvements in processing ambiguous or interleaved patterns, which are challenging for single-head or untrained automata. This research contributes a new perspective on integrating formal language theory with advanced machine learning techniques, offering practical implications for natural language understanding, symbolic reasoning, and the development of interpretable AI models. Key keywords include language inference, multi-head automata, reinforcement learning, formal languages, and sequential decision-making.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing the robustness and performance of deep learning models by introducing a novel data augmentation technique called GridMask. The method aims to overcome the limitations of existing data augmentation strategies in terms of preserving salient features while contributing to model generalization. Methods/Approach: GridMask involves the strategic masking of input data using a grid pattern, which dynamically adjusts the size and position of the masked regions. This approach is implemented to obscure parts of the image or data samples, forcing the model to learn discriminative features from incomplete information. Unlike conventional techniques, GridMask provides a more structured and controllable way of data modification, ensuring that critical parts of the input are selectively obscured in a repeatable manner. Results/Findings: Experiments conducted on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that GridMask significantly improves the performance of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures. The augmentation technique showed notable enhancements in classification accuracy and robustness against adversarial attacks compared to traditional methods like Cutout and DropBlock. Additionally, GridMask was effective in preserving essential data patterns while diversifying the dataset, which led to improved generalization across unseen data. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of GridMask represents a substantial contribution to the field of data augmentation, providing a versatile tool for researchers and practitioners in machine learning and computer vision. Its ability to enhance model performance with minimal computational overhead highlights its potential applications in various domains requiring high-performing and resilient AI models. Keywords: GridMask, data augmentation, deep learning, model generalization, CNNs, adversarial robustness.

This paper presents a novel framework integrating Bayesian inference and machine learning techniques to estimate parameters for Influence Models within the IM-RO (Influence Maximization under Realistic Optimization) paradigm. The primary objective is to enhance the accuracy and robustness of parameter estimation processes that underpin influence propagation analysis in complex networks. We employ Bayesian methods to incorporate prior knowledge and quantify uncertainty, while machine learning algorithms are leveraged to identify patterns and optimize parameter selection from large-scale data. The proposed approach is evaluated on multiple benchmark social network datasets, comparing its performance with traditional estimation techniques in terms of prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and adaptability to varying network structures. Results demonstrate that our hybrid framework consistently outperforms baseline methods, offering significant improvements in both parameter estimation precision and the predictive capability of influence spreads. These findings underscore the potential of blending probabilistic and data-driven models for influence parameter estimation, facilitating improved decision-making in applications such as viral marketing, information dissemination, and network optimization. The study contributes an effective methodology for Influence Maximization tasks, providing a scalable and interpretable solution for handling uncertainty and complexity in real-world networks. Keywords: Bayesian inference, machine learning, influence maximization, parameter estimation, IM-RO, social networks.

Understanding the inner workings of deep neural networks remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel divide-and-conquer approach to dissect complex deep networks into more manageable sub-networks, enabling a more granular understanding of their functionality. Our method involves systematically partitioning the network based on layer connectivity and analyzing the isolated behavior of each sub-network through targeted input perturbation and output analysis. The approach is applied to various convolutional and recurrent architectures trained on image classification and natural language processing tasks. Results indicate that specific sub-networks are responsible for distinct feature extraction and decision-making processes. Furthermore, comparative analysis reveals that the performance bottlenecks can be localized to certain sub-networks, suggesting targeted optimization strategies. This research provides a practical methodology for demystifying deep networks, paving the way for improved interpretability, robustness, and efficient network design. Keywords: Deep Networks, Interpretability, Divide-and-Conquer, Neural Networks, Feature Extraction, Sub-networks.

Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) has emerged as a prominent reinforcement learning algorithm due to its stability and performance across diverse tasks. However, its exploration efficiency remains a critical challenge, often leading to suboptimal policy convergence. This paper addresses this limitation by proposing an enhanced exploration mechanism integrated into the PPO framework. Our approach introduces a novel exploration strategy that dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation trade-off based on the policy's learning progress, ensuring more efficient sampling of the environment. We evaluate the proposed method on a suite of benchmark environments, including continuous control and high-dimensional state spaces. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in sample efficiency and final policy performance compared to standard PPO and other state-of-the-art methods. The enhanced PPO achieves up to a 25% reduction in training time while maintaining or surpassing baseline performance metrics. This work contributes to the advancement of reinforcement learning by providing a practical and scalable solution to improve exploration efficiency in policy optimization. The proposed method has potential applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and other domains requiring efficient and robust decision-making. **Keywords**: Proximal Policy Optimization, reinforcement learning, exploration efficiency, policy convergence, sample efficiency, autonomous systems.

**Abstract** Accurate and robust segmentation of lung tissues in computed tomography (CT) scans is critical for early detection and diagnosis of pulmonary diseases. However, the scarcity of diverse and well-annotated datasets, especially those containing various types and sizes of lung nodules, often limits the effectiveness of lung segmentation algorithms. This paper proposes a novel approach to augment CT imaging data by generating highly realistic lung nodule simulations using 3D conditional generative adversarial networks (3D-cGANs). Our method conditions the generative process on anatomical lung context, enabling the synthesis of heterogeneous nodules integrated seamlessly into authentic lung structures. We conducted extensive experiments to evaluate the realism of the simulated nodules and their impact on downstream segmentation models. The integration of the augmented dataset led to statistically significant improvements in segmentation accuracy, especially for nodules of smaller size and irregular shapes, compared to models trained on original or conventionally augmented data. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of 3D-cGAN-based simulation for augmenting medical imaging datasets and enhances the robustness and generalizability of automated lung segmentation. Our approach offers a scalable solution for improving computer-aided diagnosis tools, with applications in clinical screening and disease monitoring. **Keywords:** lung nodule simulation, 3D generative adversarial networks, CT imaging, lung segmentation, data augmentation, medical imaging.

This paper presents a novel approach to video surveillance of highway traffic events using deep learning architectures. The objective is to develop an automated system that can accurately detect and classify various traffic events, such as accidents, congestion, and road closures, in real-time. A convolutional neural network (CNN) based approach is employed, utilizing a combination of spatial and temporal features extracted from video feeds. The methodology involves training the model on a large dataset of annotated traffic videos, allowing it to learn patterns and anomalies in traffic flow. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system, achieving high accuracy and efficiency in detecting traffic events. The system's performance is evaluated using metrics such as precision, recall, and mean average precision, showcasing its potential for real-world applications. The contributions of this research include the development of a robust and scalable deep learning framework for traffic event detection, with implications for improved traffic management and safety. Key keywords: deep learning, computer vision, traffic surveillance, convolutional neural networks, intelligent transportation systems.

This paper introduces the CAMELS multifield dataset, a novel resource designed to facilitate the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in cosmology. The objective is to leverage AI techniques, particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), to learn the universe's fundamental parameters from multifield simulations. Our approach combines large-scale cosmological simulations with advanced ML algorithms to create a robust framework for parameter estimation. The CAMELS dataset consists of a large collection of simulated universes, each with varying cosmological parameters, providing a unique opportunity for AI models to learn complex relationships between these parameters and various observable fields. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of AI in accurately estimating cosmological parameters, outperforming traditional methods in certain scenarios. The key findings highlight the potential of AI-driven approaches in cosmology, enabling precise predictions and insights into the universe's evolution. This research contributes to the growing field of astroinformatics, paving the way for future applications of AI in understanding the universe's fundamental nature. This paper studies construction of above-ground biomass (AGB) prediction maps from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) intensity images. The purpose is to improve traditional regression models based on SAR intensity, trained with a limited amount of AGB in situ measurements. Although it is costly to collect, data from airborne laser scanning (ALS) sensors are highly correlated with AGB. Therefore, we propose using AGB predictions based on ALS data as surrogate response variables for SAR data in a sequential modelling fashion. This increases the amount of training data dramatically. To model the regression function between SAR intensity and ALS-predicted AGB we propose to utilise a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN), i.e. the Pix2Pix convolutional neural network. This enables the recreation of existing ALS-based AGB prediction maps. The generated synthesised ALS-based AGB predictions are evaluated qualitatively and quantitatively against ALS-based AGB predictions retrieved from a traditional non-sequential regression model trained in the same area. Results show that the proposed architecture manages to capture characteristics of the actual data. This suggests that the use of ALS-guided generative models is a promising avenue for AGB prediction from SAR intensity. Further research on this area has the potential of providing both large-scale and low-cost predictions of AGB.

The growing reliance on speech command classification systems in applications such as virtual assistants and voice-controlled devices has raised concerns about their vulnerability to adversarial attacks. This paper investigates the existence and impact of universal adversarial examples in speech command classification, which are perturbations capable of misleading multiple models across different architectures. We propose a novel approach to generate such adversarial examples by leveraging gradient-based optimization techniques and transferability properties across diverse neural network models. Our experiments demonstrate that these universal perturbations can significantly degrade the performance of state-of-the-art speech classification systems, achieving high success rates across multiple datasets and model architectures. Furthermore, we analyze the robustness of these systems under adversarial conditions and identify key factors contributing to their susceptibility. The findings highlight critical security challenges in deploying speech-based systems and provide insights into developing more robust defenses against adversarial attacks. This work contributes to advancing the understanding of adversarial vulnerabilities in speech processing and underscores the need for improved resilience in voice-enabled technologies. **Keywords**: adversarial examples, speech command classification, universal perturbations, neural networks, robustness, transferability.

Online decision trees are widely used in dynamic environments due to their adaptability and efficiency. However, their performance can degrade with complex data streams and concept drift. This paper introduces Online Local Boosting (OLB), a novel ensemble method that enhances the accuracy and stability of online decision trees. OLB maintains a pool of online decision trees, each focused on learning from different locally weighted instances based on their historical performance. The weights are dynamically adjusted using an adaptive boosting strategy, prioritizing challenging instances. The proposed method was evaluated on several synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in classification accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art online decision tree algorithms and ensemble methods. OLB effectively mitigates the impact of noise and concept drift by leveraging the diversity of locally specialized trees. The results highlight OLB as a promising approach for online learning in evolving data streams, offering enhanced prediction accuracy and adaptability. **Keywords:** Online learning, Decision trees, Ensemble methods, Boosting, Concept drift, Data streams.

Adversarial examples pose significant challenges to the robustness and security of modern machine learning models, especially in critical applications such as image recognition and autonomous systems. This paper presents a novel methodology for generating adversarial examples that are both fast to compute and exhibit minimal perceptual distortion. Our approach combines a gradient-based optimization technique with a distortion-aware objective function, enabling the rapid creation of imperceptible adversarial perturbations. We evaluate our method on standard benchmark datasets and compare its performance against existing state-of-the-art adversarial attack algorithms in terms of speed, distortion metrics, and attack success rate. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive or superior success rates while significantly reducing both computational overhead and the visual detectability of the perturbations. These findings suggest our approach offers a practical pathway for adversarial testing in real-time and resource-constrained environments. The proposed framework not only advances the understanding of adversarial vulnerability in neural networks but also provides valuable tools for stress-testing models to improve their robustness against subtle yet effective adversarial threats. Keywords: adversarial examples, neural networks, robustness, attack algorithms, low distortion, fast computation, image classification, security
