Recent advances in attention-based networks have shown that Vision Transformers can achieve state-of-the-art or near state-of-the-art results on many image classification tasks. This puts transformers in the unique position of being a promising alternative to traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs). While CNNs have been carefully studied with respect to adversarial attacks, the same cannot be said of Vision Transformers. In this paper, we study the robustness of Vision Transformers to adversarial examples. Our analyses of transformer security is divided into three parts. First, we test the transformer under standard white-box and black-box attacks. Second, we study the transferability of adversarial examples between CNNs and transformers. We show that adversarial examples do not readily transfer between CNNs and transformers. Based on this finding, we analyze the security of a simple ensemble defense of CNNs and transformers. By creating a new attack, the self-attention blended gradient attack, we show that such an ensemble is not secure under a white-box adversary. However, under a black-box adversary, we show that an ensemble can achieve unprecedented robustness without sacrificing clean accuracy. Our analysis for this work is done using six types of white-box attacks and two types of black-box attacks. Our study encompasses multiple Vision Transformers, Big Transfer Models and CNN architectures trained on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet.

This paper introduces BoA-PTA, a novel Bayesian Optimization Accelerated error-free SPICE solver designed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of circuit simulation. Traditional SPICE solvers often face challenges in balancing computational speed with precision, particularly in complex circuit designs. BoA-PTA addresses this limitation by integrating Bayesian optimization techniques to intelligently guide the simulation process, reducing redundant computations while maintaining error-free results. The proposed approach leverages probabilistic models to predict optimal simulation paths, significantly accelerating convergence without compromising accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that BoA-PTA outperforms conventional SPICE solvers in terms of both runtime and precision, achieving up to a 40% reduction in simulation time for benchmark circuits. Furthermore, the solver exhibits robust performance across a wide range of circuit complexities, making it a versatile tool for modern electronic design automation. The key contribution of this work lies in the seamless integration of Bayesian optimization with SPICE simulation, offering a scalable and efficient solution for error-free circuit analysis. This research has significant implications for the design and verification of next-generation integrated circuits, particularly in applications requiring high reliability and computational efficiency. **Keywords**: SPICE solver, Bayesian optimization, circuit simulation, error-free computation, electronic design automation, probabilistic modeling.

Point cloud analysis is critical in various applications, including 3D reconstruction, autonomous navigation, and object recognition. Farthest Point Sampling (FPS) is a widely used technique for point cloud downsampling and feature extraction due to its simplicity and efficiency in providing uniform coverage. However, FPS can be suboptimal in preserving local geometric details and capturing intricate structures. This paper introduces a novel sampling strategy, Adaptive Density-Aware Sampling (ADAS), that goes beyond traditional FPS by incorporating local density estimation to guide the sampling process. ADAS prioritizes regions with high geometric complexity and varying point densities, leading to improved feature representation. We evaluate ADAS on standard benchmark datasets for point cloud classification and segmentation tasks, demonstrating its superior performance compared to FPS and other state-of-the-art sampling methods. Our experiments show that ADAS enhances the accuracy and robustness of point cloud analysis, particularly in scenarios with non-uniform point distributions. The proposed approach offers a valuable alternative to FPS, enabling more effective point-wise analysis and improved performance in downstream tasks. Keywords: Point Cloud, Sampling, Farthest Point Sampling, Density Estimation, 3D Reconstruction, Point-wise Analysis, Geometric Features.

Then detection and identification of extreme weather events in large-scale climate simulations is an important problem for risk management, informing governmental policy decisions and advancing our basic understanding of the climate system. Recent work has shown that fully supervised convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can yield acceptable accuracy for classifying well-known types of extreme weather events when large amounts of labeled data are available. However, many different types of spatially localized climate patterns are of interest including hurricanes, extra-tropical cyclones, weather fronts, and blocking events among others. Existing labeled data for these patterns can be incomplete in various ways, such as covering only certain years or geographic areas and having false negatives. This type of climate data therefore poses a number of interesting machine learning challenges. We present a multichannel spatiotemporal CNN architecture for semi-supervised bounding box prediction and exploratory data analysis. We demonstrate that our approach is able to leverage temporal information and unlabeled data to improve the localization of extreme weather events. Further, we explore the representations learned by our model in order to better understand this important data. We present a dataset, ExtremeWeather, to encourage machine learning research in this area and to help facilitate further work in understanding and mitigating the effects of climate change. The dataset is available at extremeweatherdataset.github.io and the code is available at https://github.com/eracah/hur-detect.

The paper addresses the complex problem of airline crew pairing optimization, a critical task in airline operations focused on efficiently matching crews to flight schedules while adhering to regulations and minimizing costs. The objective of this research is to enhance the existing optimization processes by integrating advanced machine learning techniques to learn combinatorial patterns inherent in large-scale datasets. The approach involves the development and implementation of a novel algorithm that leverages deep learning models to identify and learn these patterns effectively, thereby providing valuable insights for decision-making in crew pairing. Our findings demonstrate that the proposed model significantly improves the performance of traditional optimization methods by reducing computation time and increasing the overall efficiency of the crew pairing process. Additionally, the system's ability to adapt to diverse flight scenarios and constraints showcases its potential to handle the dynamic nature of airline operations. The results indicate a substantial improvement in solution quality compared to conventional methods, leading to more cost-effective crew schedules and improved operational reliability. In conclusion, this research contributes to the field of operations research and airline management by introducing a machine learning-driven approach that offers scalable and efficient solutions for crew pairing optimization. The implications of this work extend to enhanced operational planning and reduced operational expenses for airline companies. Keywords: airline crew pairing, optimization, machine learning, combinatorial patterns, large-scale datasets, operations research.

It is a popular belief that model-based Reinforcement Learning (RL) is more sample efficient than model-free RL, but in practice, it is not always true due to overweighed model errors. In complex and noisy settings, model-based RL tends to have trouble using the model if it does not know when to trust the model. In this work, we find that better model usage can make a huge difference. We show theoretically that if the use of model-generated data is restricted to state-action pairs where the model error is small, the performance gap between model and real rollouts can be reduced. It motivates us to use model rollouts only when the model is confident about its predictions. We propose Masked Model-based Actor-Critic (M2AC), a novel policy optimization algorithm that maximizes a model-based lower-bound of the true value function. M2AC implements a masking mechanism based on the model's uncertainty to decide whether its prediction should be used or not. Consequently, the new algorithm tends to give robust policy improvements. Experiments on continuous control benchmarks demonstrate that M2AC has strong performance even when using long model rollouts in very noisy environments, and it significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods.

The main objective of this research is to investigate the efficacy of ImageNet as a robust dataset for transfer learning applications and to identify the critical elements that contribute to its success in enhancing performance across various computer vision tasks. Methods/Approach: This study employs a comprehensive analysis of ImageNet's structure, data diversity, and annotation quality. We utilize deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) pre-trained on ImageNet and conduct extensive experiments on a range of target datasets representing different domains and complexities. Our approach involves comparing the transfer learning results derived from ImageNet with those from other renowned datasets to evaluate its comparative advantage. Results/Findings: Our findings indicate that ImageNet’s substantial volume, variety in categories, and high-quality annotations significantly bolster model generalization capabilities when transferred to new tasks. The results demonstrate that models initialized with ImageNet pre-training consistently outperform those trained from scratch or pre-trained on other datasets, particularly in tasks such as object detection, segmentation, and fine-grained classification. Conclusion/Implications: This research underscores the critical elements of ImageNet that make it a powerful tool for transfer learning, emphasizing its expansive category representation and annotation precision. The insights derived from this study contribute to better understanding the transferability of deep learning models. The findings suggest that future dataset creation may benefit from mirroring ImageNet’s diversity and scale to optimize transfer learning across diverse applications. Key Keywords: ImageNet, transfer learning, convolutional neural networks, dataset diversity, model generalization, computer vision.

Objective: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated strong performance for node classification in static, closed-world settings. However, many real-world applications—such as social networks, citation graphs, and knowledge bases—evolve over time, introducing new node types and relationships that traditional GNNs cannot accommodate without full retraining. This paper addresses the open-world node classification problem by developing a lifelong learning framework for GNNs that incrementally incorporates novel classes while retaining knowledge of previously learned ones. Methods: We propose LLGNN, a continual learning architecture that integrates (1) a memory-augmented replay module to selectively store representative node embeddings from past tasks, (2) a dynamic graph expansion mechanism that updates the message-passing layers to incorporate newly added nodes and edges, and (3) a knowledge distillation loss to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. The system operates in two phases for each arriving batch of novel-class data: an update phase that efficiently fine-tunes the GNN and a consolidation phase that replays stored embeddings to reinforce prior knowledge. Results: Experiments on evolving citation and social network benchmarks show that LLGNN outperforms static retraining and state-of-the-art continual learning baselines by 8–12% in average F1 score over sequential tasks. Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of memory replay and distillation in reducing forgetting and improving adaption. Conclusion: LLGNN is the first scalable solution for open-world node classification under continual graph evolution. Its modular design enables integration with existing GNN architectures, offering a practical pathway for deploying long-lived, adaptive graph analytics in dynamic environments. Keywords: lifelong learning, graph neural networks, open-world classification, continual learning, node classification

This paper addresses the challenge of distribution matching, where the goal is to find the best representation among multiple samples. The objective is to develop an efficient algorithm that can effectively match distributions, even when the samples are diverse and numerous. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach that leverages a combination of statistical analysis and machine learning techniques. Our method, termed "Best-of-Many-Samples" distribution matching, utilizes a hierarchical clustering framework to identify the most representative samples, followed by a fine-tuning process to refine the matching. The results show that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, particularly in scenarios with high-dimensional data and large sample sizes. The key findings include improved distribution matching accuracy, reduced computational complexity, and enhanced robustness to noise and outliers. The implications of this research are significant, enabling applications in fields such as data integration, anomaly detection, and generative modeling. Our contributions include a novel algorithmic framework, a comprehensive evaluation methodology, and insights into the importance of representative sampling in distribution matching. Key keywords: distribution matching, statistical analysis, machine learning, hierarchical clustering, fine-tuning, data integration, anomaly detection, generative modeling.

This paper introduces a novel Periphery-Fovea Multi-Resolution Driving Model (PFM-DM) inspired by human visual attention mechanisms to enhance autonomous driving systems. The objective is to address the challenge of efficiently processing high-resolution visual data while maintaining real-time performance and safety. The proposed model mimics the human visual system by dividing the input into two streams: a high-resolution foveal region for critical details and a lower-resolution peripheral region for broader context. A lightweight attention-guided mechanism dynamically allocates computational resources based on the saliency of objects and road conditions. The model is trained and evaluated on a large-scale driving dataset, incorporating diverse weather, lighting, and traffic scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that PFM-DM achieves a 15% improvement in object detection accuracy and a 20% reduction in computational latency compared to traditional single-resolution approaches. Furthermore, the model exhibits robust performance in edge cases, such as detecting pedestrians in low-visibility conditions. The findings highlight the potential of integrating human-inspired attention mechanisms into autonomous systems, paving the way for safer and more efficient self-driving technologies. Keywords: autonomous driving, human attention, multi-resolution model, foveal-peripheral vision, computational efficiency.

Tracking pedestrian heads in dense crowds is a critical challenge in computer vision, with applications in surveillance, crowd management, and autonomous systems. This paper addresses the limitations of existing methods in accurately detecting and tracking heads in highly congested environments, where occlusion and overlapping are prevalent. We propose a novel deep learning-based framework that integrates a multi-scale feature extraction network with a robust tracking algorithm to enhance head detection and trajectory estimation. Our approach leverages spatial-temporal information and employs a lightweight attention mechanism to prioritize head regions, improving accuracy in cluttered scenes. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves a significant improvement in tracking precision and recall compared to state-of-the-art techniques, particularly in scenarios with extreme crowd density. The proposed system also exhibits real-time performance, making it suitable for practical deployment. This research contributes to advancing pedestrian tracking technologies by offering a scalable and efficient solution for dense crowd analysis, with potential applications in public safety and urban planning. **Keywords**: Pedestrian tracking, dense crowds, head detection, deep learning, computer vision, attention mechanism.

This paper introduces a novel Matlab toolbox designed for feature importance ranking, addressing the growing need for efficient and interpretable feature selection in data-driven applications. The objective of this work is to provide researchers and practitioners with a user-friendly, scalable, and versatile tool that simplifies the process of identifying the most relevant features in high-dimensional datasets. The toolbox integrates multiple state-of-the-art algorithms, including filter-based, wrapper-based, and embedded methods, enabling users to evaluate feature importance across diverse machine learning tasks. A modular architecture allows for easy customization and extension, supporting both supervised and unsupervised learning scenarios. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the toolbox's effectiveness in achieving high accuracy and computational efficiency, outperforming existing solutions in terms of runtime and scalability. The findings highlight the toolbox's ability to handle large-scale datasets while maintaining interpretability, making it a valuable resource for applications in domains such as bioinformatics, finance, and image processing. This research contributes to the field by offering an open-source, comprehensive solution that bridges the gap between theoretical feature selection methods and practical implementation, fostering innovation in data analysis and model optimization. **Keywords**: feature importance, feature selection, Matlab toolbox, machine learning, high-dimensional data, interpretability.

Nghiên cứu mới đây đã thành công trong việc phân lập và tuyển chọn các chủng nấm mốc sinh tổng hợp enzyme Laccase từ gỗ mục. Quá trình này bao gồm việc thu thập và xử lý gỗ mục, sau đó sử dụng các phương pháp phân tích và tuyển chọn để xác định và phân lập các chủng nấm mốc có khả năng sinh tổng hợp enzyme Laccase. Các chủng nấm mốc được tuyển chọn sau đó được sử dụng để sản xuất enzyme Laccase. Quá trình sản xuất này bao gồm việc nuôi cấy các chủng nấm mốc trong môi trường thích hợp, sau đó thu thập và tinh chế enzyme Laccase. Enzyme Laccase là một loại enzyme quan trọng trong quá trình phân hủy chất hữu cơ, đặc biệt là trong quá trình phân hủy gỗ mục. Nó có khả năng phân hủy các chất hữu cơ khó phân hủy, giúp giảm thiểu lượng chất thải và cải thiện môi trường. Nghiên cứu này có thể mở ra các cơ hội mới trong việc sản xuất enzyme Laccase từ gỗ mục, giúp giảm thiểu chi phí và tăng cường hiệu suất sản xuất. Đồng thời, nó cũng có thể giúp phát triển các sản phẩm mới từ gỗ mục, như các sản phẩm có chứa enzyme Laccase có thể được sử dụng trong các ứng dụng khác nhau như sản xuất thực phẩm, dược phẩm và các sản phẩm khác.

This paper addresses the significant challenge of semantic segmentation in fine-resolution remotely sensed images, a crucial task in fields such as urban planning and environmental monitoring. Current methodologies struggle with balancing detail preservation and computational efficiency. Methods: We propose A2-FPN, an advanced Adaptive Attention Feature Pyramid Network, designed to enhance feature representation across different scales. The network integrates a novel adaptive attention module, which dynamically weighs feature contributions, resulting in improved multi-scale feature fusion. The approach utilizes cutting-edge deep learning techniques, ensuring robust performance even on large and complex datasets. Results: Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that A2-FPN achieves superior segmentation accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The proposed model exhibits significant improvements in precision and recall metrics, especially in distinguishing fine object boundaries and complex textures. Performance analysis also highlights the network's efficiency, maintaining competitive inference speed and resource utilization. Conclusion: A2-FPN represents a significant advancement in semantic segmentation for fine-resolution remotely sensed images, offering enhanced detail preservation without sacrificing performance. The adaptive attention mechanism provides a flexible framework for accurately capturing diverse semantic information. This research contributes a powerful tool with potential applications in various remote sensing and GIS domains, paving the way for more precise and efficient image analysis. Key keywords include semantic segmentation, remotely sensed images, adaptive attention, feature pyramid network, deep learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of articulated shape matching, a critical task in computer vision and 3D modeling, by proposing a novel approach that leverages Laplacian eigenfunctions and unsupervised point registration. The objective is to accurately align and match articulated shapes, such as human or animal models, despite variations in pose and deformation. Our method utilizes the spectral properties of Laplacian eigenfunctions to capture intrinsic geometric features of shapes, enabling robust correspondence estimation. An unsupervised point registration framework is then employed to align these features without requiring labeled data, significantly reducing the dependency on annotated datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in scenarios involving complex deformations and partial occlusions. The proposed technique contributes to advancing applications in animation, medical imaging, and robotics, where precise shape matching is essential. Key innovations include the integration of spectral geometry with unsupervised learning, offering a scalable and generalizable solution for articulated shape analysis. Keywords: articulated shape matching, Laplacian eigenfunctions, unsupervised learning, point registration, spectral geometry, 3D modeling.

This paper presents an innovative deep vision system designed for accurate animal classification and detection in trail-camera images. The objective is to develop a reliable and explainable model that can automatically adapt to changing environmental conditions through post-deployment retraining. Our approach utilizes a custom convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, leveraging techniques such as transfer learning and attention mechanisms to enhance model performance. The system is trained on a large dataset of trail-camera images, annotated with various animal species, and achieves high accuracy in classification and detection tasks. Key findings indicate that our model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, with significant improvements in recall and precision. The automatic retraining mechanism enables the system to maintain its performance over time, even in the presence of concept drift. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and effective wildlife monitoring systems, with potential applications in conservation biology, ecology, and wildlife management. The use of explainable AI techniques provides insights into the decision-making process of the model, increasing trust and reliability in the results. Relevant keywords: deep learning, computer vision, animal classification, object detection, explainable AI, trail-camera images, wildlife monitoring.

The inverse design of inorganic materials poses a significant challenge due to the vastness and complexity of chemical space. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging generative adversarial networks (GANs) for efficient sampling of this space, targeting the discovery of materials with desired properties. Our method employs a GAN architecture trained on a dataset of known inorganic material compositions and their corresponding properties. The generator network learns to propose new material candidates, while the discriminator network distinguishes between generated and real materials, driving the generator to produce increasingly realistic and promising compositions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by targeting materials with specific band gaps and formation energies. Results show that our GAN-based sampling strategy significantly outperforms random sampling and other traditional optimization techniques in identifying materials with the desired properties within a reduced computational cost. This work offers a powerful tool for accelerating materials discovery, facilitating the design of novel inorganic compounds with tailored functionalities. Keywords: generative adversarial networks, GAN, inverse design, inorganic materials, chemical space, materials discovery.

Graph embeddings play a crucial role in representing complex relational data for various machine learning applications, including recommendation systems, fraud detection, and biological network analysis. Traditional embedding methods often struggle with generalization to unseen nodes and computational efficiency in large-scale graphs. This paper introduces a novel inductive graph embedding framework that leverages locality encodings to capture structural and feature-based information efficiently. Our approach constructs node embeddings by encoding local graph neighborhoods using a combination of positional and feature-aware transformations. Unlike transductive methods that require retraining when new nodes appear, our inductive technique enables dynamic embedding generation, making it suitable for evolving graphs. We design a locality-aware encoding mechanism that integrates topological patterns and node attributes, enhancing representation quality while maintaining computational efficiency. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art inductive graph embedding techniques in terms of accuracy, scalability, and adaptability to unseen nodes. Notably, our method achieves significant improvements in link prediction and node classification tasks while reducing computational overhead. These findings highlight the effectiveness of locality encodings in inductive graph learning, paving the way for more efficient and adaptable graph-based representations in real-world applications. Keywords: Graph Embeddings, Inductive Learning, Locality Encodings, Graph Neural Networks, Representation Learning, Scalable Graph Processing.

Solving inverse problems continues to be a challenge in a wide array of applications ranging from deblurring, image inpainting, source separation etc. Most existing techniques solve such inverse problems by either explicitly or implicitly finding the inverse of the model. The former class of techniques require explicit knowledge of the measurement process which can be unrealistic, and rely on strong analytical regularizers to constrain the solution space, which often do not generalize well. The latter approaches have had remarkable success in part due to deep learning, but require a large collection of source-observation pairs, which can be prohibitively expensive. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised technique to solve inverse problems with generative adversarial networks (GANs). Using a pre-trained GAN in the space of source signals, we show that one can reliably recover solutions to under determined problems in a `blind' fashion, i.e., without knowledge of the measurement process. We solve this by making successive estimates on the model and the solution in an iterative fashion. We show promising results in three challenging applications -- blind source separation, image deblurring, and recovering an image from its edge map, and perform better than several baselines.

This paper investigates the vulnerability of deep neural networks to membership model inversion attacks, where an attacker aims to infer whether a given data point was used in the training process of a target model. Our objective is to develop a novel approach to launch such attacks, exploiting the inherent properties of deep networks to compromise their privacy. We propose a method that utilizes a combination of adversarial examples and gradient-based optimization to invert the target model, allowing the attacker to determine the membership status of a data point with high accuracy. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, outperforming existing methods in terms of attack success rate and efficiency. The findings of this study have significant implications for the privacy and security of deep learning models, highlighting the need for robust defenses against membership model inversion attacks. Key contributions include the development of a novel attack methodology and the identification of potential vulnerabilities in deep neural networks, with important applications in areas such as AI security, privacy preservation, and model protection. Relevant keywords: deep neural networks, membership model inversion attacks, adversarial examples, gradient-based optimization, AI security, privacy preservation.

Nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc phân lập và đánh giá khả năng kháng khuẩn của các chủng xạ khuẩn nội cộng sinh trên cây màng tang, một loại cây có giá trị dược liệu. Data augmentation (DA) is a crucial technique for improving the performance of object detection models, especially when training data is limited. However, the selection of appropriate DA policies remains a challenge, often relying on heuristics or computationally expensive search methods. This paper introduces ADA, a novel game-theoretic framework for analyzing and optimizing DA strategies. We formulate the interaction between the object detector and DA policies as a non-cooperative game, where the detector aims to minimize its loss, and each DA policy aims to maximize the detector's loss by generating challenging augmented samples. We propose an efficient algorithm to find the Nash Equilibrium of this game, representing an optimal DA policy tailored to the specific detector and dataset. Experimental results on benchmark datasets such as COCO and Pascal VOC demonstrate that ADA significantly improves the detection accuracy compared to state-of-the-art DA methods. Furthermore, ADA offers insights into the robustness of object detectors and the effectiveness of different DA transformations. Our work provides a theoretical foundation for understanding DA and a practical approach for automatically discovering effective DA policies, enhancing the performance and generalization capabilities of object detection models. Keywords: Data Augmentation, Object Detection, Game Theory, Nash Equilibrium, Robustness.

Volumetric medical image segmentation is a critical task in healthcare, enabling precise diagnosis and treatment planning. However, existing methods often struggle with balancing computational efficiency and segmentation accuracy, particularly for high-resolution 3D data. This paper introduces a novel 3D coarse-to-fine framework designed to address these challenges. The proposed approach leverages a hierarchical architecture that first processes low-resolution volumetric data to identify coarse structures and then refines the segmentation at higher resolutions. By integrating multi-scale feature extraction and adaptive attention mechanisms, the framework effectively captures both global context and fine-grained details. Experiments on benchmark medical imaging datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The framework’s ability to handle large-scale 3D data with reduced memory consumption makes it particularly suitable for real-world clinical applications. This research contributes a scalable and robust solution for volumetric medical image segmentation, with potential implications for improving diagnostic workflows and patient outcomes. **Keywords**: 3D medical imaging, volumetric segmentation, coarse-to-fine framework, multi-scale feature extraction, adaptive attention, computational efficiency.

The growing demand for efficient and scalable neural network architectures has driven the exploration of Processing-In-Memory (PIM) systems, which aim to reduce data movement and energy consumption. However, PIM systems are inherently susceptible to noise and variability, which can degrade the performance of neural networks. This paper introduces a novel noise-aware normalization technique designed to enhance the robustness of neural networks deployed in PIM environments. Our approach dynamically adjusts normalization parameters to account for noise-induced variations during computation, ensuring stable and reliable performance. We evaluate the proposed method on benchmark datasets using a simulated PIM framework, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy and resilience compared to traditional normalization techniques. The results highlight the effectiveness of noise-aware normalization in mitigating the impact of hardware-level noise, making it a promising solution for deploying robust neural networks in PIM systems. This work contributes to advancing the reliability of AI applications in next-generation computing architectures, with potential implications for edge computing, IoT, and energy-efficient AI systems. **Keywords**: Processing-In-Memory, neural networks, noise-aware normalization, robustness, AI hardware, edge computing.

Few-shot learning aims to enable machine learning models to quickly adapt to new tasks with limited labeled data, a capability vital for practical applications where data collection is challenging. This paper addresses the challenge by introducing a meta-learning framework for automated neural architecture search tailored specifically for few-shot learning scenarios. Our approach leverages a meta-learner that jointly optimizes both the architecture and the parameters of neural networks across a diverse set of tasks, encouraging the discovery of architectures with strong generalization ability. We employ an efficient search strategy that considers task-specific adaptation while mitigating computational overhead, making the method scalable to complex datasets. Experimental results on standard few-shot classification benchmarks demonstrate that our meta-learned architectures consistently outperform manually designed baselines and previous architecture search methods, in terms of both accuracy and adaptation speed. The proposed framework significantly advances few-shot learning performance without requiring extensive computational resources, highlighting its potential for real-world deployment where rapid learning from limited data is essential. Keywords: meta-learning, neural architecture search, few-shot learning, automated machine learning, task adaptation.

We approach structured output prediction by optimizing a deep value network (DVN) to precisely estimate the task loss on different output configurations for a given input. Once the model is trained, we perform inference by gradient descent on the continuous relaxations of the output variables to find outputs with promising scores from the value network. When applied to image segmentation, the value network takes an image and a segmentation mask as inputs and predicts a scalar estimating the intersection over union between the input and ground truth masks. For multi-label classification, the DVN's objective is to correctly predict the F1 score for any potential label configuration. The DVN framework achieves the state-of-the-art results on multi-label prediction and image segmentation benchmarks.

Video object detection is a critical task in computer vision, aiming to accurately identify and localize objects across video frames. Despite significant advancements, challenges such as object occlusion, motion blur, and appearance variations persist, limiting the performance of existing methods. This paper introduces a novel *Object-aware Feature Aggregation (OFA)* framework designed to enhance video object detection by leveraging temporal and spatial information more effectively. The proposed approach integrates a multi-level feature aggregation mechanism that dynamically fuses object-specific features across frames, ensuring robust representation even under challenging conditions. Additionally, we introduce an attention-based module to prioritize relevant features while suppressing noise, further improving detection accuracy. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including ImageNet VID and YouTube-VOS, demonstrate that OFA outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant improvements in both precision and recall. The framework’s ability to handle complex scenarios, such as fast-moving objects and occlusions, highlights its practical applicability in real-world video analysis tasks. This research contributes to the field by providing a scalable and efficient solution for video object detection, with potential applications in surveillance, autonomous driving, and video content analysis. **Keywords**: Video object detection, feature aggregation, object-aware representation, attention mechanism, temporal modeling.

Phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang mô tả có phân tích với 61 mắt (40 bệnh nhân), 28 mắt PXG, 33 mắt POAG được chụp OCTA đánh giá mật độ mạch máu vùng hoàng điểm (mVD) quét khối 3*3 mm và mật độ mạch máu quanh gai (pVD) quét khối 4,5*4,5 mm. Bề dày lớp sợi thần kinh võng mạc quanh gai (pRNFL) và bề dày phức hợp tế bào hạch (GCC) được đánh giá bằng máy Spectral domain - OCT. Tương quan giữa các chỉ số mạch máu, cấu trúc và chỉ số trên thị trường Humphrey được kiểm định bằng hệ số tương quan Pearson. Kết quả: Chỉ số mật độ mạch máu vùng hoàng điểm (mVD) trung bình ở mắt glôcôm giả tróc bao thấp hơn mắt glôcôm góc mở nguyên phát (24,37% so với 28,34% với p < 0,05). Không có sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thống kê giữa chỉ số mật độ mạch máu quanh gai ở nhóm PXG và nhóm POAG (42,62% so với 41,05% với p > 0,05). Generative models have become essential tools in a variety of information technology applications, including image synthesis, data augmentation, and anomaly detection. However, guaranteeing their reliability and robustness, especially under adversarial perturbations, remains a significant challenge. This paper addresses the critical problem of certifying the Lipschitz continuity of generative models, which is closely related to their stability and generalization performance. We introduce a novel framework for provable Lipschitz certification that can be applied to a broad class of generative architectures, such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). Our approach leverages analytical bounds, efficient algorithms, and architectural constraints to certify upper limits on the Lipschitz constant of a given generator. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, we demonstrate that our certification method rigorously and efficiently estimates Lipschitz constants without sacrificing model expressiveness or quality. Comparisons with existing heuristic methods highlight superior performance in terms of both computational efficiency and certification tightness. The proposed Lipschitz certification enables more robust deployment of generative models in safety-critical and regulated environments. Our contributions advance the field by providing a practical and theoretically sound solution for automated verification of generative model robustness. Key keywords: generative models, Lipschitz continuity, certification, robustness, adversarial attacks, machine learning.

Face age progression aims to synthesize realistic facial images at different ages, a challenging task due to the complex and subtle changes in facial appearance over time. This paper introduces a novel framework for face age progression that incorporates attribute manipulation to enhance the realism and control of the generated results. Our approach leverages a conditional generative adversarial network (GAN) to disentangle age-related features from identity information. Specifically, we manipulate facial attributes such as wrinkles, skin texture, and facial shape, guided by age labels. We introduce a novel attention mechanism within the GAN architecture to focus on age-sensitive regions of the face, enabling more precise and realistic age transformations. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of visual quality and age estimation accuracy, surpassing existing methods. The proposed framework also allows for controlled attribute manipulation, enabling users to customize age progression by adjusting specific facial features. This work contributes a more controllable and realistic approach to face age progression, with potential applications in entertainment, forensics, and age-invariant face recognition. **Keywords:** Face Age Progression, Generative Adversarial Networks, Attribute Manipulation, Image Synthesis, Facial Attributes, Deep Learning.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of bias in machine learning models by exploring adversarially fair representations that enhance both fairness and transferability across different domains. As AI and machine learning systems become increasingly integrated into society, ensuring the elimination of bias is paramount to guarantee equitable outcomes. Methods: We introduce a novel framework that leverages adversarial learning techniques to foster representations that are resilient to biases present in the data. Our approach integrates a dual-component structure consisting of a primary model for feature extraction and a secondary adversarial network aimed at identifying and mitigating biases. This hybrid model ensures that learned representations maintain fairness while being adaptable to various applications and domains. Results: Experimental evaluations on standard datasets demonstrate superior performance in achieving fairness compared to traditional methods. Our model not only minimizes bias effectively but also enhances the transferability of the learned representations. This dual achievement indicates that our approach can be generalized to diverse datasets without sacrificing performance, thereby broadening the applicability of fair models. Conclusion: The proposed framework highlights a significant advancement in developing machine learning models that are both adversarially fair and transferable. This dual benefit underscores our method’s potential to drive ethical and adaptable AI applications across multiple sectors. By addressing these two key aspects concurrently, our research contributes to the growing field of fair and reliable AI systems that can be deployed responsibly across various domains. Keywords: Adversarial Learning, Fairness, Transferable Representations, Bias Mitigation, Machine Learning.

Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) images from their low-resolution (LR) counterparts. While deep learning-based SISR methods have achieved remarkable progress, they often struggle to recover fine-grained details, resulting in overly smooth or texture-lacking reconstructions. This paper introduces a novel texture transfer approach to enhance texture fidelity in SISR. Our method leverages a pre-trained texture encoder to extract texture features from a reference HR image and subsequently transfers these features to the upscaled LR image. We propose an adaptive texture fusion module that selectively integrates texture information based on local image characteristics, preventing artifacts and preserving structural integrity. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method significantly improves perceptual quality, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of texture similarity metrics while maintaining competitive PSNR and SSIM scores. The results showcase the unreasonable effectiveness of texture transfer in generating visually appealing and detailed HR images from single LR inputs. Keywords: Super-resolution, Texture Transfer, Image Reconstruction, Deep Learning, Perceptual Quality.

The objective is to optimize energy consumption in residential settings by developing an intelligent controller that learns to make informed decisions based on extracted features from high-dimensional state-time data. Our method employs a CNN-based architecture to identify relevant patterns and relationships in the data, which are then used to inform a reinforcement learning agent. The results demonstrate significant improvements in energy efficiency and reduced peak demand, outperforming traditional rule-based control methods. Key findings include the ability of the CNN to effectively extract meaningful features, leading to better decision-making by the reinforcement learning agent. The implications of this research are substantial, enabling the widespread adoption of intelligent load control systems in residential settings, with potential applications in smart grids and energy management. This work contributes to the growing field of reinforcement learning and CNNs, highlighting the benefits of integrating these technologies for real-world applications, particularly in the context of energy efficiency and sustainability, with relevant keywords including deep learning, reinforcement learning, load control, and smart grids.

The complexity of the visual world creates significant challenges for comprehensive visual understanding. In spite of recent successes in visual recognition, today's vision systems would still struggle to deal with visual queries that require a deeper reasoning. We propose a knowledge base (KB) framework to handle an assortment of visual queries, without the need to train new classifiers for new tasks. Building such a large-scale multimodal KB presents a major challenge of scalability. We cast a large-scale MRF into a KB representation, incorporating visual, textual and structured data, as well as their diverse relations. We introduce a scalable knowledge base construction system that is capable of building a KB with half billion variables and millions of parameters in a few hours. Our system achieves competitive results compared to purpose-built models on standard recognition and retrieval tasks, while exhibiting greater flexibility in answering richer visual queries.

Recent advances in camera equipped drone applications and their widespread use increased the demand on vision based object detection algorithms for aerial images. Object detection process is inherently a challenging task as a generic computer vision problem, however, since the use of object detection algorithms on UAVs (or on drones) is relatively a new area, it remains as a more challenging problem to detect objects in aerial images. There are several reasons for that including: (i) the lack of large drone datasets including large object variance, (ii) the large orientation and scale variance in drone images when compared to the ground images, and (iii) the difference in texture and shape features between the ground and the aerial images. Deep learning based object detection algorithms can be classified under two main categories: (a) single-stage detectors and (b) multi-stage detectors. Both single-stage and multi-stage solutions have their advantages and disadvantages over each other. However, a technique to combine the good sides of each of those solutions could yield even a stronger solution than each of those solutions individually. In this paper, we propose an ensemble network, SyNet, that combines a multi-stage method with a single-stage one with the motivation of decreasing the high false negative rate of multi-stage detectors and increasing the quality of the single-stage detector proposals. As building blocks, CenterNet and Cascade R-CNN with pretrained feature extractors are utilized along with an ensembling strategy. We report the state of the art results obtained by our proposed solution on two different datasets: namely MS-COCO and visDrone with \%52.1 mAP_ is obtained on MS-COCO val2017 dataset and \%26.2 mAP_ is obtained on VisDrone test-set.

This paper addresses the challenge of global image editing driven by textual descriptions, aiming to enable seamless and coherent modifications of images according to user-defined language inputs. The research investigates how language-guided transformations can be effectively learned and applied to diverse image processing tasks. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel deep learning framework that integrates natural language processing with image editing capabilities. The model utilizes advanced transformer architectures to interpret textual descriptions and generate corresponding edit operations across entire images. By leveraging a combination of pre-trained language models and image synthesis networks, our approach is designed to capture complex textual semantics and translate them into visual alterations. Results/Findings: The proposed model demonstrates robust performance in altering images in accordance with textual instructions, showcasing superior flexibility and accuracy compared to existing methods. Our experiments across various datasets indicate the system's ability to maintain image consistency while applying global edits, achieving high satisfaction scores in user evaluations. Quantitative metrics also reflect significant improvements in the alignment between text instructions and visual outcomes. Conclusion/Implications: This study advances the field of image editing by introducing a method that combines the contextual understanding of text with sophisticated image generation techniques. The approach not only enhances automated image editing capabilities but also opens avenues for creative applications in digital art, content creation, and interactive media. UltraSR provides a novel approach to arbitrary-scale image super-resolution by integrating spatial encoding into implicit image functions, addressing a critical gap in existing methodologies. The objective of this research is to enhance the adaptability and accuracy of super-resolution techniques over a wide range of scaling factors. Our method introduces a spatial encoding mechanism that encapsulates the positional context of pixels, significantly improving the precision of reconstructed images. Leveraging advanced machine learning architectures, UltraSR demonstrates a flexible and scalable model that surpasses traditional fixed-scale super-resolution algorithms. Initial evaluations showcase substantial improvements in image quality metrics, including PSNR and SSIM, across diverse datasets and varying resolution requirements. Compared to existing approaches, UltraSR exhibits superior performance in preserving texture and structural details at arbitrary scales. The implications of this work suggest significant advancements in fields requiring dynamic resolution adjustments, such as digital media, remote sensing, and medical imaging. Through UltraSR, spatial encoding emerges as a pivotal component, facilitating enhanced performance and opening new avenues for future research in super-resolution technologies. Key keywords include super-resolution, spatial encoding, implicit image functions, and arbitrary-scale.

Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms learn optimal policies through interaction with an environment. A critical aspect of successful RL is the exploration strategy, which balances exploiting known rewards with discovering new, potentially better actions. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of exploration methods in RL, categorizing and analyzing various approaches including epsilon-greedy, optimistic initialization, upper confidence bound (UCB), Thompson sampling, and intrinsic motivation. We examine the theoretical underpinnings of these methods, comparing their performance across different problem domains, from discrete to continuous action spaces and from model-free to model-based settings. Furthermore, the survey discusses recent advances in exploration techniques, such as exploration driven by deep neural networks and hierarchical exploration. The analysis identifies the strengths and weaknesses of each approach, highlighting their suitability for specific types of RL problems. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions in the field of RL exploration, including lifelong learning and safe exploration. This survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners seeking to understand and apply effective exploration strategies in reinforcement learning. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Exploration, Exploitation, Epsilon-Greedy, Upper Confidence Bound, Thompson Sampling, Intrinsic Motivation.

This paper proposes an Efficient Coarse-to-Fine Non-Local Module designed to enhance the detection of small objects in images. The objective is to address the challenge of accurately identifying tiny targets within complex scenes, which is a common issue in various computer vision applications. Our approach employs a novel two-stage framework, combining a coarse-level attention mechanism with a fine-level non-local feature refinement process. This method enables the model to capture both global context and local details, leading to improved detection performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our module outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant gains in accuracy and efficiency. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a hierarchical non-local module and a sparse attention mechanism, which reduce computational costs while maintaining high detection accuracy. This work has important implications for applications such as object detection, surveillance, and autonomous driving, where the accurate detection of small objects is crucial. Keywords: object detection, non-local module, small object detection, computer vision, attention mechanism.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing the resolution of brain MRI images, a crucial aspect for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. Our objective is to develop a novel super-resolution technique that leverages overcomplete dictionaries and nonlocal similarity to improve image quality. We propose a method that utilizes a dictionary learning approach to capture intricate image features, combined with a nonlocal similarity metric to exploit the redundant information within the image. Our approach is tested on a dataset of brain MRI images, yielding significant improvements in image resolution and quality. The results demonstrate that our technique outperforms existing super-resolution methods, with enhanced visual clarity and reduced artifacts. The contributions of this research lie in its ability to effectively integrate dictionary learning and nonlocal similarity, resulting in a powerful tool for brain MRI image enhancement. This work has important implications for medical imaging applications, particularly in the fields of neurology and radiology, where high-resolution images are essential for precise diagnosis and treatment. Key keywords: super-resolution, brain MRI, overcomplete dictionaries, nonlocal similarity, medical imaging, image enhancement.

By integrating this method into path-planning, we achieve results that closely approximate optimal trajectories while maintaining computational feasibility. Our experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in complex and dynamic environments. The ability to dynamically adjust path-planning based on real-time measurements opens new avenues for applications in robotics, surveillance, environmental monitoring, and autonomous navigation. Ultimately, our research contributes to the field by providing a scalable, effective solution for optimizing path-planning through informative measurement strategies. Key concepts explored in this work include dynamic programming, path-planning optimization, and real-time information gathering.

Multi-objective optimizations are frequently encountered in engineering practices. The solution techniques and parametric selections however are usually problem-specific. In this study we formulate a reinforcement learning hyper-heuristic scheme, and propose four low-level heuristics which can work coherently with the single point search algorithm MOSA/R (Multi-Objective Simulated Annealing Algorithm based on Re-seed) towards multi-objective optimization problems of general applications. Making use of the domination amount, crowding distance and hypervolume calculations, the proposed hyper-heuristic scheme can meet various optimization requirements adaptively and autonomously. The approach developed not only exhibits improved and more robust performance compared to AMOSA, NSGA-II and MOEA/D when applied to benchmark test cases, but also shows promising results when applied to a generic structural fault identification problem. The outcome of this research can be extended to a variety of design and manufacturing optimization applications.

Some historical and more recent printed documents have been scanned or stored at very low resolutions, such as 60 dpi. Though such scans are relatively easy for humans to read, they still present significant challenges for optical character recognition (OCR) systems. The current state-of-the art is to use super-resolution to reconstruct an approximation of the original high-resolution image and to feed this into a standard OCR system. Our novel end-to-end method bypasses the super-resolution step and produces better OCR results. This approach is inspired from our understanding of the human visual system, and builds on established neural networks for performing OCR. Our experiments have shown that it is possible to perform OCR on 60 dpi scanned images of English text, which is a significantly lower resolution than the state-of-the-art, and we achieved a mean character level accuracy (CLA) of 99.7% and word level accuracy (WLA) of 98.9% across a set of about 1000 pages of 60 dpi text in a wide range of fonts. For 75 dpi images, the mean CLA was 99.9% and the mean WLA was 99.4% on the same sample of texts. We make our code and data (including a set of low-resolution images with their ground truths) publicly available as a benchmark for future work in this field.

The results show that state-of-the-art fake detection models achieve high accuracy in identifying manipulated facial features, with a particular emphasis on eye and mouth regions. However, the performance of these models degrades when faced with high-quality DeepFakes. The study concludes that the evolution of DeepFakes poses significant challenges to fake detection, highlighting the need for continuous improvement in detection methods. The contributions of this research include a detailed analysis of facial region manipulation in DeepFakes and the development of a robust fake detection framework. Key findings have important implications for the development of more effective fake detection models, particularly in applications such as facial recognition, surveillance, and social media. Relevant keywords: DeepFakes, fake detection, facial recognition, computer vision, machine learning, AI models.

This paper introduces a novel method for learning low-dimensional state embeddings and identifying metastable clusters directly from time series data. The objective is to reduce the complexity of high-dimensional time series by representing them in a lower-dimensional space while preserving essential dynamical information. Our approach combines a time-lagged autoencoder with a clustering algorithm to simultaneously learn embeddings and identify metastable states. Specifically, the autoencoder learns a low-dimensional representation that captures the temporal dependencies in the data, while the clustering algorithm groups similar states in the embedded space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on synthetic datasets and real-world molecular dynamics trajectories, showing that it accurately identifies metastable states and captures the underlying dynamics with significantly reduced dimensionality. The results indicate improved performance compared to traditional dimensionality reduction and clustering techniques. This method provides a powerful tool for analyzing complex time series data in various scientific domains, including molecular dynamics, climate science, and financial modeling. Keywords: time series analysis, dimensionality reduction, metastable states, clustering, autoencoders, state embeddings.

Understanding how convolutional neural networks (CNNs) learn representations and generalize is crucial for advancing their application in diverse fields. This paper addresses the challenge of capturing feature learning effects in finite-width CNNs using Gaussian Processes (GPs), providing a theoretical framework that enhances our grasp of CNNs’ behavior beyond large-width assumptions. Methods/Approach: We develop a self-consistent theoretical foundation integrating the probabilistic modeling capabilities of GPs with the structural characteristics of finite-width CNNs. By leveraging this approach, we analyze CNN dynamics and feature learning mechanisms, employing a novel adaptation of mean field theory that accounts for finite network sizes. Results/Findings: Our findings demonstrate that the proposed GP-based model reliably captures the feature learning dynamics of finite CNNs, offering a robust approximation to real-world neural network behavior. The theory reveals critical insights into how CNNs adjust feature maps as they learn, and simulations indicate strong correlation of our model’s predictions with actual network performance across various tasks. Our results are benchmarked against existing large-width theories, highlighting superior accuracy in feature learning and generalization predictions. Conclusion/Implications: The research provides a significant breakthrough in modeling and understanding CNNs of practical dimensions, overcoming limitations of traditional infinitely wide models. These insights hold potential for guiding the design of efficient and effective CNN architectures in real-world applications. This work opens avenues for further research in combining theoretical models with empirical practices, offering deeper insights into the intersection of neural networks and probabilistic models. Keywords: Gaussian Processes, Convolutional Neural Networks, Feature Learning, Finite-width Networks, Mean Field Theory, Neural Network Dynamics.

Link prediction in dynamic graphs is crucial for various applications, but faces challenges with new nodes and limited labeled data. This paper introduces a novel subgraph-aware meta-learning framework for few-shot inductive link prediction. Our approach, termed SAME, learns transferable knowledge from meta-training tasks constructed from historical graph data. SAME utilizes a subgraph extraction module to identify relevant neighborhood structures around query links, enabling the model to focus on informative patterns. A meta-learner then adapts this subgraph-specific knowledge to predict links for unseen nodes in new graphs with only a few labeled examples. Experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that SAME significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, especially in scenarios with extremely limited labeled data. The results highlight the effectiveness of subgraph-aware meta-learning for addressing the cold-start problem in inductive link prediction. Keywords: Link Prediction, Inductive Learning, Meta-Learning, Graph Neural Networks, Few-Shot Learning, Subgraphs.

This research addresses the critical issue of roof fall hazards in underground mining, which pose significant risks to worker safety and operational efficiency. The aim is to develop an advanced method for detecting such hazards using cutting-edge artificial intelligence techniques. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in combination with transfer learning to enhance the detection of roof fall hazards. Our model leverages pre-trained CNN architectures to effectively recognize patterns indicative of potential collapses. This approach allows for accurate hazard detection even with limited labeled data, by transferring learned features from large, generic datasets to the specific task of mining safety. Results/Findings: The proposed model demonstrates superior detection capabilities, achieving high accuracy and precision in identifying roof fall risks. Comparative analysis with traditional methods highlights significant improvements in detection rates and reduced false positives. Our results indicate that the use of transfer learning considerably enhances the model's ability to generalize over diverse mining environments and complex datasets. Conclusion/Implications: This study contributes to the field of mining safety by introducing an efficient, AI-driven solution for early hazard detection. The findings underline the potential of integrating modern transfer learning techniques with CNNs to improve safety measures in mining operations. The implementation of our model can lead to proactive hazard management, thereby minimizing accident rates and ensuring safer working conditions. Keywords: roof fall hazard, convolutional neural networks, transfer learning, mining safety, hazard detection, AI in mining.

Bài báo trình bày kết quả đánh giá khả năng dự báo của mô hình phân giải mây (Cress) đối với các đợt mưa lớn ở khu vực Trung Trung Bộ trong thời kỳ 2021-2022. Điều kiện biên sử dụng là nguồn dữ liệu GFS 0,5, mô phỏng đánh giá với số liệu mưa radar thông qua các chỉ số thống kê cho các hạn dự báo từ 24 h đến 48 h với các ngưỡng mưa khác nhau. Kết quả cho thấy mô hình CRESS có khả năng dự báo khá ổn định ở các hạn từ 24-48 giờ, với độ tương đồng cao. Tuy nhiên, khi ngưỡng mưa tăng, chỉ số phát hiện (POD) giảm mạnh, trong khi tỷ lệ cảnh báo sai (FAR) tăng, làm giảm khả năng phát hiện mưa lớn, đặc biệt với ngưỡng mưa từ 50-100 mm. Đánh giá định lượng kỹ năng dự báo cho thấy lượng mưa dự báo thường cao hơn thực tế, không có sự khác nhau quá lớn giữa các hạn dự báo. Đối với tổng số 13 đợt mưa trong hai năm 2021- 2022, lượng mưa dự báo cao hơn thực tế và điểm sô số thành công CSI của CRESS đối với ngưỡng có mưa khoảng hơn 40% hạn 24-48 h. Đối với ngưỡng mưa vừa 20-25 mm/ngày dao động khoảng 10-28%, đối với các hạn 24, 36, 48 và không có sự sai khác nhau giữa các hạn quá nhiều. Đối với ngưỡng 50-100 mm/ngày CRES dự báo này báo được 3-8%. Điều này khá tương đồng với kĩ năng hiện nay tại Trung tâm Khí tượng Thủy văn Quốc gia. Kết quả cho thấy, trong đợt mưa điển hình do bão, mô hình CRESS dự báo cường độ mưa cao hơn thực tế, đặc biệt khi bão tiến gần bờ và suy yếu. Diện mưa được dự báo sát hơn vào giai đoạn cuối của đợt mưa, khi hoàn lưu bão suy yếu. Sai lệch về cường độ và diện mưa một phần do mô hình mô phỏng sự di chuyển của bão chậm hơn thực tế.

Công trình Âu Kim Đài tại khu vực Nam Ninh Bình đã được đánh giá về khả năng ngăn mặn và hớt ngọt, nhằm xác định hiệu quả trong việc bảo vệ nguồn nước ngọt cho khu vực này. Nghiên cứu chỉ ra rằng công trình có khả năng ngăn chặn sự xâm nhập của nước mặn từ biển vào các vùng đất nông nghiệp, góp phần bảo vệ sản xuất nông nghiệp và cải thiện chất lượng nước. Bên cạnh đó, việc hớt ngọt cũng được thực hiện để duy trì mực nước ngọt ổn định, phục vụ cho nhu cầu sinh hoạt và sản xuất của người dân. Kết quả đánh giá cho thấy công trình hoạt động hiệu quả, tuy nhiên cần có các biện pháp bổ sung để nâng cao khả năng chống chịu trước biến đổi khí hậu và tình trạng nước biển dâng. Việc duy trì và cải tạo công trình là cần thiết để đảm bảo an toàn nguồn nước cho khu vực trong tương lai.

Hiện nay khi xã hội ngày càng phát triển, tri thức càng được coi trọng, bên cạnh đó nhu cầu được học hỏi và chia sẻ kiến thức ngày càng rộng mở. Nhưng không phải ai cũng có nhiều thời gian để đi học điều mình muốn hoặc không đủ khả năng chia sẻ kiến thức của mình cho tất cả mọi người, Chính vì vậy chúng ta cần một hệ thống để mọi người dễ dàng, thuận tiện chia sẻ và học hỏi tri thức với nhau. Thực tế hiện nay đã có nhiều các website, diễn đàn dạy học trực tuyến để mọi người học hỏi tri thức. Tuy nhiên đa số các website đó đều cần trả phí, dù miễn phí thì tính đa dạng lĩnh vực chưa cao, đồng thời người dùng chưa thể tự chia sẻ kiến thức của mình. Để giải quyết vấn đề đó em lựa chọn đề tài đồ án của mình là xây dựng website “Chia sẻ và học hỏi kiến thức”. Hệ thống sẽ là nơi cho tất cả mọi người giao lưu, chia sẻ tri thức trong mọi lĩnh vực cuộc sống bằng các bài giảng do tự mình tạo ra, đồng thời học hỏi những khóa học của mọi người để trau dồi kiến thức của bản thân.

Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) systems are vulnerable to performance degradation when tested on unseen domains. This paper addresses the domain generalization problem in FAS by proposing a novel Pseudo-Domain Label (PDL) approach. Our method aims to learn domain-invariant features by automatically discovering and assigning pseudo-domain labels to the training data, thereby mitigating the need for explicit domain annotations. We introduce a clustering-based technique to generate PDLs and incorporate them into a domain adversarial learning framework. Specifically, we train a feature extractor to minimize the spoofing classification loss while simultaneously maximizing the uncertainty of domain classification based on the assigned PDLs. This forces the model to learn features that are discriminative for spoofing detection but invariant to domain variations. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our PDL approach achieves significant improvements in cross-domain FAS performance compared to state-of-the-art domain generalization methods. The proposed approach provides a practical solution for deploying robust FAS systems in real-world scenarios by reducing the reliance on labeled target domain data. Keywords: Face Anti-Spoofing, Domain Generalization, Pseudo-Domain Label, Domain Adaptation, Deep Learning.

This paper presents a novel approach to modelling Bahdanau attention mechanisms using election methods aided by Q-Learning. The objective is to improve the efficiency and accuracy of attention-based neural networks by incorporating a reinforcement learning framework. Our method utilizes Q-Learning to optimize the election process, allowing the model to selectively focus on the most relevant input elements. The proposed approach is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in performance compared to traditional attention mechanisms. Key findings include enhanced accuracy and reduced computational complexity. The conclusions highlight the potential of this innovative approach to advance the state-of-the-art in natural language processing and related applications, with implications for improved language understanding and generation capabilities. The use of Q-Learning and election methods in attention modelling introduces a new paradigm, offering a unique combination of reinforcement learning and deep learning techniques. Relevant keywords: Bahdanau attention, Q-Learning, election methods, reinforcement learning, deep learning, natural language processing.

Nghiên c ứu này th ực hiện nhằm đánh giá đa d ạng sinh h ọc và các d ịch vụ môi trư ờng rừng qua đó xác định chi trả dịch vụ môi trư ờng của huy ện Ba B ể, tỉnh B ắc Kạn. Ph ỏng vấn cán b ộ chủ chốt (n = 6) và đi ều tra nông h ộ (n = 256) là hai phương pháp ch ủ yếu được sử dụng để thu th ập số liệu. Kết quả nghiên c ứu chỉ ra rằng huy ện Ba B ể đa dạng về các loài đ ộng thực vật, nhi ều loài n ằm trong sách đ ỏ của Việt Nam và th ế giới. Ngoài ra, trên đ ịa bàn huy ện còn đa dạng các h ệ sinh thái phân b ố ở các ki ểu địa hình khác nhau. S ự đa dạng về loài đ ộng th ực vật và phong phú về các h ệ sinh thái đ ã cung c ấp đa d ạng các lo ại hình d ịch vụ môi trư ờng có giá tr ị. Tuy v ậy, các d ịch vụ trên chưa được khai thác và s ử dụng hi ệu quả nên chưa khuy ến khích đư ợc các ho ạt động bảo tồn tài nguyên r ừng trên đ ịa bàn huy ện. Do đó, trong th ời gian t ới huy ện cần thực hiện tốt hoạt động bảo vệ rừng, b ảo tồn đa d ạng sinh h ọc nhằm duy trì kh ả năng cung ứng các d ịch vụ môi trư ờng đồng th ời đẩy mạnh vi ệc thực hiện các chương tr ình chi tr ả dịch vụ môi trư ờng tạo ra ngu ồn thu đ ể phục vụ cho công tác b ảo tồn tài nguyên r ừng và nâng cao thu nh ập cho người dân đ ịa phương.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving offline reinforcement learning (RL) by proposing an innovative method that overcomes limitations in learning from static datasets. Current offline RL approaches often struggle with generalization due to limited exploration, necessitating advanced techniques to enhance performance. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel framework that integrates residual generative modeling into traditional offline RL algorithms. Our method amplifies learning efficiency by generating synthetic data that mimics potential future states and actions, thus enriching the diversity of the training set. This approach employs a generative model that learns the residuals between observed data and potential unseen transitions, leveraging these insights to guide the policy learning process. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms baseline offline RL algorithms across multiple benchmark tasks. Notably, the proposed method shows superior adaptability and robustness, improving convergence rates and policy performance. By enhancing the dataset with synthetic yet realistic samples, our framework achieves a balance between exploration and exploitation, enhancing overall RL efficacy in static environments. Conclusion/Implications: The integration of residual generative modeling into offline RL represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a powerful tool for applications where real-time data collection is impractical. This work contributes to the development of more effective decision-making systems, with potential applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and other areas requiring offline learning capabilities. Our findings provide a foundation for future research into hybrid models that combine the strengths of generative technologies and reinforcement learning. Keywords: Offline Reinforcement Learning, Residual Generative Modeling, Synthetic Data, Policy Learning, Decision-Making Systems.

Dân số già hóa tại Quận 10, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh đang đặt ra nhiều thách thức trong việc chăm sóc sức khỏe, đặc biệt là đối với người cao tuổi mắc bệnh tăng huyết áp. Tình trạng này không chỉ ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng cuộc sống của người bệnh mà còn gây áp lực lớn lên hệ thống y tế địa phương. Nhu cầu khám chữa bệnh, theo dõi huyết áp thường xuyên và điều trị lâu dài ngày càng tăng cao. Tuy nhiên, việc tiếp cận dịch vụ y tế chất lượng vẫn còn hạn chế do thiếu cơ sở vật chất và nhân lực chuyên môn. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, cần có sự phối hợp chặt chẽ giữa chính quyền, bệnh viện và cộng đồng trong việc nâng cao nhận thức, cải thiện dịch vụ y tế và hỗ trợ tâm lý cho người cao tuổi.

Trong phạm vi đồ án tốt nghiệp, sử dụng các kỹ thuật khai phá dữ liệu từ văn bản kết hợp với phương pháp học máy điểm xây dựng module phân cụm, module nhúng cục bộ, tạo mẫu mô típ đại diện cho siêu dữ liệu của dữ liệu văn bản để xây dựng cây phân loại chủ đề tự động trên một lĩnh vực cụ thể. Sau đó dựa vào kết quả thu được xây dựng Ontology cho lĩnh vực đó và ứng dụng cho hệ thống Ontology quản lý thông tin các chuyên gia được đề cập trong bài toán được đưa ra.

Lớp phủ vàng trên bề mặt màng PET đã trở thành một ứng dụng quan trọng trong nhiều lĩnh vực công nghệ. Tuy nhiên, quá trình lắng đọng lớp phủ vàng truyền thống thường gặp nhiều hạn chế về hiệu suất và độ chính xác. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, các nhà khoa học đã áp dụng phương pháp phún xạ magnetron để tạo ra lớp phủ vàng trên bề mặt màng PET. Phương pháp phún xạ magnetron là một kỹ thuật tiên tiến giúp tạo ra lớp phủ mỏng và đều trên bề mặt vật liệu. Quá trình này dựa trên nguyên tắc phún xạ, nơi mà các ion kim loại được phún lên bề mặt vật liệu để tạo ra lớp phủ. Phương pháp này cho phép tạo ra lớp phủ vàng với độ dày và độ đều cao, đồng thời cũng giúp giảm thiểu sự mất mát vật liệu. Lớp phủ vàng tạo ra bằng phương pháp phún xạ magnetron trên bề mặt màng PET có nhiều ứng dụng quan trọng. Chúng có thể được sử dụng trong sản xuất các sản phẩm điện tử, y tế, và công nghệ sinh học. Ngoài ra, lớp phủ vàng cũng có thể được sử dụng để tạo ra các sản phẩm có tính thẩm mỹ cao, như các sản phẩm trang sức và đồ trang trí. Tóm lại, phương pháp phún xạ magnetron đã giúp tạo ra lớp phủ vàng trên bề mặt màng PET với hiệu suất và độ chính xác cao. Điều này đã mở ra nhiều khả năng ứng dụng trong các lĩnh vực công nghệ khác nhau.
