Token JWT có ba phần chính: header, payload và signature. Header chứa các thông tin về loại token và thuật toán mã hóa được sử dụng. Payload chứa các thông tin về người dùng và các quyền truy cập của họ. Signature chứa chữ ký số để xác thực tính toàn vẹn của token.

Bà toán trích xuất thông tin từ ảnh tài liệu là một lớp bài toán con trong lĩnh vực nhận diện ký tự quang học (thường được gọi là bài toán OCR Optical Character Recognition). Mục tiêu của bài toán này là việc phân loại các hộp văn bản vào những trường thông tin tương ứng được định nghĩa trong từng loại tài liệu. Trong bộ dữ liệu đơn thuốc thu thập từ bệnh viện Việt Nam, những trường thông tin bao gồm: diagnose (chẩn đoán), medical name (tên thuốc), quantity (số lượng), usage (cách dùng), date (ngày tháng). Để thực hiện được bài toán này, cần phải thực hiện được hai bài toán trước đó là định vị và nhận diện văn bản. Đầu ra của hai bà toán là đầu vào của bà toán trích xuất thông tin trong tài liệu.

The purpose of this research is to address the challenge of error detection in noisy knowledge graphs, which are critical repositories used for various applications such as semantic search and recommendation systems. We aim to enhance graph embedding techniques by leveraging path-ranking methods to improve precision in identifying inaccuracies within these graphs. Methods/Approach: Our approach combines advanced graph embedding techniques with path-ranking algorithms. By guiding the embedding process through path-ranking methods, we create a more structured representation of the graph that highlights potential errors. This hybrid method enhances the detection of erroneous links and nodes within the knowledge graph, reducing the noise that can impair the graph's utility. Results/Findings: The experimental evaluation shows that our proposed method significantly improves the accuracy of error detection over traditional graph embedding approaches. By integrating path-ranking strategies, our approach demonstrates increased robustness in identifying errors within complex, noisy datasets. When compared to standard techniques, our method shows a notable increase in precision and recall metrics, indicating its effectiveness in maintaining clean and useful graph data. Conclusion/Implications: This research presents a novel approach to refining graph embeddings by incorporating path-ranking methods, which substantially enhances error detection in noisy knowledge graphs. The findings have significant implications for fields reliant on accurate graph information, such as AI-driven data analytics and automated knowledge discovery. Our contributions provide a foundation for further advancements in error mitigation strategies within knowledge graph technologies. Keywords: graph embeddings, path-ranking methods, error detection, knowledge graphs, graph noise reduction, semantic search, AI-driven analytics.

Hành vi tiêu dùng xanh đang trở thành xu hướng quan trọng trong bối cảnh bảo vệ môi trường ngày càng được chú trọng. Nghiên cứu thực nghiệm từ người tiêu dùng tại một tỉnh cụ thể cho thấy, các yếu tố như nhận thức về môi trường, giá cả, chất lượng sản phẩm và ảnh hưởng xã hội đóng vai trò quyết định trong việc thúc đẩy hành vi tiêu dùng xanh. Người tiêu dùng có nhận thức cao về tác động môi trường thường có xu hướng lựa chọn sản phẩm thân thiện với môi trường, dù giá cả có thể cao hơn. Bên cạnh đó, sự hỗ trợ từ chính sách và các chương trình khuyến khích của chính phủ cũng góp phần nâng cao ý thức và thúc đẩy hành vi tiêu dùng bền vững. Kết quả nghiên cứu này cung cấp cơ sở quan trọng để các doanh nghiệp và nhà hoạch định chính sách đưa ra chiến lược phù hợp nhằm thúc đẩy tiêu dùng xanh trong cộng đồng.

Văn hóa công sở, một khái niệm đa diện, được tiếp cận qua nhiều góc độ pháp lý khác nhau. Các văn bản quy phạm pháp luật hiện hành không đưa ra định nghĩa thống nhất về văn hóa công sở, nhưng nội hàm của nó được thể hiện gián tiếp thông qua các quy định về chuẩn mực đạo đức, ứng xử của cán bộ, công chức, viên chức trong hoạt động công vụ. Một số văn bản tập trung vào các hành vi bị cấm, coi đó là những biểu hiện đi ngược lại văn hóa công sở. Cách tiếp cận này nhấn mạnh tính kỷ luật, trật tự trong môi trường làm việc nhà nước. Bên cạnh đó, một số văn bản khác lại chú trọng xây dựng các quy tắc ứng xử văn minh, lịch sự, tạo môi trường làm việc thân thiện, hợp tác. Cách tiếp cận này đề cao yếu tố con người, khuyến khích sự sáng tạo và tinh thần phục vụ. Sự khác biệt trong cách tiếp cận cho thấy văn hóa công sở là một phạm trù phức tạp, cần được nghiên cứu và hoàn thiện để đáp ứng yêu cầu của xã hội hiện đại.

The increasing prevalence of video data necessitates efficient methods for video understanding. This paper addresses the challenge of adapting the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture, which has shown remarkable success in image recognition, to the more complex domain of video. We introduce a novel spatio-temporal transformer model that efficiently encodes video data by treating a video as a sequence of frame-level patch embeddings. Our approach, named Video Transformer (VidTr), reduces the quadratic computational complexity inherent in standard transformer models by incorporating a factorized attention mechanism, separating spatial and temporal attention. VidTr significantly outperforms existing 3D convolutional neural networks and inflated 2D networks on benchmark video action recognition datasets, including Kinetics-400 and Something-Something V2, while requiring fewer computational resources. Specifically, VidTr achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with a reduced parameter count and faster inference time. These results demonstrate the potential of transformer-based architectures for video understanding and provide a foundation for future research in efficient video representation learning. Keywords: Video Transformer, Action Recognition, Vision Transformer, Spatio-Temporal Modeling, Attention Mechanism, Deep Learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of inducing hierarchical compositional models in generative networks, a critical step toward achieving interpretable and structured representations in artificial intelligence. We propose a novel approach that leverages sparsity constraints within a generator network to naturally uncover hierarchical structures in data. By systematically sparsifying the network's connections, our method encourages the emergence of compositional patterns that align with the underlying data hierarchy. The proposed framework is evaluated on synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its ability to recover meaningful hierarchical representations without explicit supervision. Experimental results show significant improvements in interpretability and model performance compared to traditional generative approaches. Furthermore, the induced hierarchical models exhibit robustness across diverse tasks, including image generation and structured data synthesis. This work contributes a scalable and unsupervised technique for discovering compositional hierarchies, offering potential applications in explainable AI, data compression, and domain-specific knowledge extraction. Keywords: hierarchical models, sparsity, generative networks, unsupervised learning, interpretability, structured representations.

Nghiên cứu đánh giá khả năng thích nghi và phát triển của cây giống Bách bộ in vitro ở giai đoạn V, giai đoạn quan trọng để chuyển cây từ môi trường ống nghiệm sang điều kiện tự nhiên. Các yếu tố như giá thể trồng, chế độ dinh dưỡng và điều kiện ánh sáng được kiểm soát chặt chẽ nhằm tối ưu hóa tỷ lệ sống và tốc độ tăng trưởng của cây con. Kết quả cho thấy, việc lựa chọn giá thể phù hợp, bổ sung dinh dưỡng hợp lý và điều chỉnh cường độ ánh sáng đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc giúp cây Bách bộ con thích nghi thành công với môi trường mới. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp cơ sở khoa học cho việc nhân giống và bảo tồn cây Bách bộ, một dược liệu quý có giá trị kinh tế cao, đồng thời góp phần vào việc phát triển các quy trình sản xuất cây giống in vitro hiệu quả hơn.

Tracking-by-detection methods have demonstrated competitive performance in recent years. In these approaches, the tracking model heavily relies on the quality of the training set. Due to the limited amount of labeled training data, additional samples need to be extracted and labeled by the tracker itself. This often leads to the inclusion of corrupted training samples, due to occlusions, misalignments and other perturbations. Existing tracking-by-detection methods either ignore this problem, or employ a separate component for managing the training set. We propose a novel generic approach for alleviating the problem of corrupted training samples in tracking-by-detection frameworks. Our approach dynamically manages the training set by estimating the quality of the samples. Contrary to existing approaches, we propose a unified formulation by minimizing a single loss over both the target appearance model and the sample quality weights. The joint formulation enables corrupted samples to be down-weighted while increasing the impact of correct ones. Experiments are performed on three benchmarks: OTB-2015 with 100 videos, VOT-2015 with 60 videos, and Temple-Color with 128 videos. On the OTB-2015, our unified formulation significantly improves the baseline, with a gain of 3.8% in mean overlap precision. Finally, our method achieves state-of-the-art results on all three datasets. Code and supplementary material are available at http://www.cvl.isy.liu.se/research/objrec/visualtracking/decontrack/index.html .

Bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ liên quan đến chuyển hóa (MAFLD) là một tình trạng phổ biến ở bệnh nhân mắc bệnh vảy nến, đặc biệt là những người có các yếu tố nguy cơ như béo phì, tiểu đường và rối loạn lipid máu. Nghiên cứu gần đây chỉ ra rằng tình trạng viêm mãn tính và rối loạn miễn dịch trong bệnh vảy nến có thể đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc thúc đẩy sự phát triển của MAFLD. Các bệnh nhân này thường có nguy cơ cao hơn đối với các biến chứng gan nghiêm trọng, bao gồm xơ gan và ung thư gan. Việc quản lý bệnh cần kết hợp giữa điều trị bệnh vảy nến và kiểm soát các yếu tố chuyển hóa, đồng thời theo dõi chức năng gan định kỳ để phát hiện sớm các dấu hiệu bất thường. Các biện pháp can thiệp lối sống như giảm cân, chế độ ăn lành mạnh và tập thể dục cũng được khuyến khích để cải thiện tình trạng bệnh.

Mới đây, tại Vịnh Nghi Sơn, huyện Tĩnh Gia, tỉnh Thanh Hóa, đã diễn ra một số giải pháp nhằm phát triển nghề nuôi cá lồng biển. Đây là một trong những khu vực nổi tiếng về nuôi trồng thủy sản, với tiềm năng lớn để phát triển kinh tế biển. Để thúc đẩy phát triển nghề nuôi cá lồng biển tại Vịnh Nghi Sơn, các giải pháp được triển khai bao gồm: - Tăng cường đầu tư vào công nghệ nuôi cá hiện đại, giúp tăng năng suất và chất lượng sản phẩm. - Phát triển các mô hình nuôi cá lồng biển bền vững, giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực đến môi trường. - Tăng cường đào tạo và hỗ trợ cho người nuôi cá, giúp họ có kỹ năng và kiến thức cần thiết để phát triển nghề nuôi cá hiệu quả. - Tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho việc xuất khẩu sản phẩm, giúp người nuôi cá có cơ hội tiếp cận thị trường quốc tế. Những giải pháp này sẽ giúp thúc đẩy phát triển nghề nuôi cá lồng biển tại Vịnh Nghi Sơn, tạo cơ hội việc làm và tăng thu nhập cho người dân địa phương, đồng thời góp phần phát triển kinh tế biển của tỉnh Thanh Hóa.

Hệ thống truyền năng lượng dùng sóng siêu cao tần TS. Đoàn Hữu Chức là một công trình nghiên cứu và phát triển mới trong lĩnh vực năng lượng tái tạo. Hệ thống này sử dụng sóng siêu cao tần để truyền năng lượng từ nguồn đến đích, giảm thiểu tổn thất và tăng hiệu suất truyền tải. Hệ thống được thiết kế và chế tạo dựa trên nguyên lý sóng siêu cao tần, với tần số hoạt động lên đến hàng chục GHz. Công nghệ này cho phép truyền tải năng lượng với tốc độ cao và độ chính xác cao, giảm thiểu sự can thiệp của môi trường và tăng hiệu suất truyền tải. Quá trình thiết kế và chế tạo hệ thống bao gồm các bước như: thiết kế nguyên lý, chế tạo bộ phận truyền sóng, thử nghiệm và hiệu chỉnh hệ thống. Các bước này đòi hỏi sự chính xác cao và kỹ năng chuyên môn để đảm bảo hệ thống hoạt động ổn định và hiệu quả. Hệ thống truyền năng lượng dùng sóng siêu cao tần TS. Đoàn Hữu Chức có tiềm năng lớn trong việc ứng dụng trong các lĩnh vực như năng lượng tái tạo, công nghệ truyền thông và công nghệ quân sự. Hệ thống này có thể giúp giảm thiểu tổn thất năng lượng, tăng hiệu suất truyền tải và giảm thiểu sự can thiệp của môi trường.

Video summarization is a critical task in multimedia analysis, aiming to condense lengthy videos into concise, informative summaries. Traditional methods often struggle to adapt to diverse query conditions and dynamic content, limiting their effectiveness. This paper introduces a novel Query-Conditioned Three-Player Adversarial Network (QCTPAN) for video summarization, designed to address these challenges. The proposed framework leverages a three-player adversarial architecture, consisting of a generator, a discriminator, and a query-conditioned encoder, to generate summaries tailored to specific user queries. The generator produces candidate summaries, while the discriminator evaluates their relevance to the query. The query-conditioned encoder ensures that the generated summaries align with the semantic context of the input query. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that QCTPAN outperforms existing methods in terms of summary relevance, diversity, and query alignment. Key findings reveal that the adversarial training process enhances the model's ability to capture query-specific features, resulting in more accurate and context-aware summaries. This research contributes a robust, query-driven approach to video summarization, with potential applications in video retrieval, content recommendation, and multimedia indexing. Keywords: video summarization, adversarial networks, query-conditioned learning, multimedia analysis, deep learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of few-shot learning, a scenario where models must generalize from a limited number of examples. We propose a novel approach leveraging sparse spatial transformers to enhance model performance in few-shot learning tasks. Methods/Approach: Our approach employs spatial transformers with a sparsity constraint, allowing the model to focus on relevant regions of the input data. By integrating these sparse spatial transformers into existing few-shot learning architectures, we aim to improve their ability to identify and generalize critical features with minimal data. Results/Findings: The experimental results demonstrate that our sparse spatial transformers significantly outperform traditional methods in few-shot learning benchmarks. We highlight improvements in accuracy and efficiency over standard spatial transformers and competing few-shot learning models. Notably, our model exhibits superior capability in adjusting to novel categories with limited examples, showcasing robustness across various datasets. Conclusion/Implications: This research introduces a promising technique for few-shot learning, with sparse spatial transformers offering a compelling solution for learning from scant data. Our findings suggest potential applications in fields requiring rapid adaptation to new data types or categories, such as personalized AI systems and dynamic content classification. This advancement opens new avenues for research in efficient model training and deployment in data-scarce environments. Keywords: sparse spatial transformers, few-shot learning, spatial attention, model generalization, data efficiency, AI models.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) with hybrid action spaces, combining discrete and continuous actions, presents a significant challenge due to the complexity of optimizing policies across heterogeneous action dimensions. This paper introduces Parametrized Deep Q-Networks (PDQN), a novel framework designed to address the limitations of existing RL methods in handling discrete-continuous hybrid action spaces. The proposed approach leverages a parametrized Q-network architecture that decouples the selection of discrete actions from the optimization of continuous parameters, enabling efficient exploration and learning in complex environments. We evaluate PDQN on a suite of benchmark tasks, including robotic control and autonomous navigation, demonstrating its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art hybrid RL methods. Experimental results show that PDQN achieves higher sample efficiency, faster convergence, and improved policy optimization, particularly in scenarios requiring precise control over continuous parameters. The framework's scalability and robustness make it a promising solution for real-world applications, such as robotics, gaming, and autonomous systems. This research contributes to advancing RL methodologies by providing a unified and efficient approach to learning in hybrid action spaces, paving the way for broader adoption in practical domains. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Hybrid Action Space, Deep Q-Networks, Parametrized Q-Learning, Robotics, Autonomous Systems.

The Dual Contradistinctive Generative Autoencoder (DCGAE) is introduced as a novel approach to unsupervised learning and data generation. Addressing limitations in existing generative models, the DCGAE leverages a dual autoencoder architecture coupled with a contradistinctive learning objective. This framework promotes the generation of high-quality, diverse samples by explicitly encouraging both reconstructive accuracy and feature disentanglement. The model employs two autoencoders trained adversarially, compelling each to capture distinct, complementary aspects of the input data distribution. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CelebA, demonstrate that the DCGAE achieves superior performance in terms of both reconstruction fidelity and sample diversity, outperforming traditional Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Furthermore, qualitative analysis reveals improved disentanglement of latent space representations, enabling more controlled and interpretable data generation. This work provides a significant advancement in generative modeling, offering a robust and effective method for learning complex data distributions and generating realistic samples with enhanced control. Keywords: Generative Autoencoder, Unsupervised Learning, Contradistinctive Learning, Data Generation, Disentanglement.

NKVM không chỉ gây kéo dài thời gian nằm viện, tăng chi phí điều trị mà còn ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng sống của người bệnh. Các yếu tố nguy cơ gây NKVM rất đa dạng, bao gồm cả yếu tố liên quan đến bệnh nhân như tuổi tác, tình trạng dinh dưỡng, bệnh nền và yếu tố liên quan đến phẫu thuật như thời gian phẫu thuật, kỹ thuật mổ, và môi trường phẫu thuật. Việc sử dụng kháng sinh dự phòng trong phẫu thuật nội soi tiêu hóa cần được cân nhắc kỹ lưỡng, dựa trên đánh giá nguy cơ nhiễm khuẩn, loại phẫu thuật, và đặc điểm của vi khuẩn gây bệnh tại cơ sở y tế. Lựa chọn kháng sinh phù hợp, thời điểm dùng thuốc và thời gian dùng thuốc cần tuân thủ các hướng dẫn hiện hành nhằm đảm bảo hiệu quả dự phòng và hạn chế tối đa tình trạng kháng kháng sinh. Các biện pháp kiểm soát nhiễm khuẩn khác như vệ sinh tay, khử khuẩn dụng cụ phẫu thuật và kiểm soát môi trường phẫu thuật cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc giảm thiểu nguy cơ NKVM.

Both assistant driving and self-driving have attracted a great amount of attention in the last few years. However, the majority of research efforts focus on safe driving; few research has been conducted on in-vehicle climate control, or assistant driving based on travellers' personal habits or preferences. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for climate control, driver behavior recognition and driving recommendation for better fitting drivers' preferences in their daily driving. The algorithm consists three components: (1) A in-vehicle sensing and context feature enriching compnent with a Internet of Things (IoT) platform for collecting related environment, vehicle-running, and traffic parameters that affect drivers' behaviors. (2) A non-intrusive intelligent driver behaviour and vehicle status detection component, which can automatically label vehicle's status (open windows, turn on air condition, etc.), based on results of applying further feature extraction and machine learning algorithms. (3) A personalized driver habits learning and preference recommendation component for more healthy and comfortable experiences. A prototype using a client-server architecture with an iOS app and an air-quality monitoring sensor has been developed for collecting heterogeneous data and testing our algorithms. Real-world experiments on driving data of 11,370 km (320 hours) by different drivers in multiple cities worldwide have been conducted, which demonstrate the effective and accuracy of our approach.

This paper addresses the challenge of inefficient experience reuse in reinforcement learning (RL), which often hinders sample efficiency and limits the scalability of RL algorithms. We propose a novel experience reuse method based on policy residual representation, enabling an agent to leverage prior experiences more effectively across different tasks and environments. Our approach decomposes policies into residual components, which capture task-specific adaptations relative to a shared base policy. By representing experiences in terms of these residuals, our method enables the flexible transfer and adaptation of learned behaviors, even when task dynamics differ. We implement the proposed framework within standard off-policy RL algorithms and evaluate its performance on a suite of continuous control benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in sample efficiency and convergence speed compared to baseline experience replay and transfer methods. The findings suggest that residual policy representation provides a more generalizable and modular approach to experience reuse, leading to accelerated learning and improved generalization. This research offers important insights for developing scalable RL systems capable of transferring knowledge across diverse environments. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, experience reuse, policy residual representation, sample efficiency, transfer learning, continual learning.

This paper introduces a novel approach to inverse rendering that leverages polarimetric and multi-view information to reconstruct 3D geometry and material properties of objects. Our method addresses the ill-posed nature of traditional inverse rendering by incorporating polarization cues, which provide additional constraints on surface normals and reflectance parameters. We present a new framework that integrates multi-view stereo reconstruction with polarimetric data to estimate surface geometry, albedo, and specular reflectance. Specifically, we propose a polarimetric multi-view photometric stereo algorithm that optimizes for surface normals and BRDF parameters jointly. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method achieves more accurate and robust reconstructions compared to state-of-the-art methods that rely solely on photometric or geometric cues. The improved accuracy in material property estimation facilitates realistic rendering and relighting applications. Keywords: Inverse Rendering, Polarimetry, Multi-View Stereo, 3D Reconstruction, BRDF Estimation, Photometric Stereo.

This paper introduces a novel approach to inverse reinforcement learning, termed learner-aware teaching, which incorporates both preferences and constraints to improve the teaching process. The objective is to develop a framework that enables an teacher agent to adaptively teach a learner agent by providing personalized demonstrations, taking into account the learner's preferences and constraints. Our approach utilizes a combination of inverse reinforcement learning and constraint-based optimization to generate informative and tailored teaching strategies. The results show that our method outperforms existing inverse reinforcement learning algorithms in terms of teaching efficiency and learner satisfaction. Key findings include the ability to adapt to diverse learner preferences and constraints, and to balance the trade-off between exploration and exploitation in the teaching process. The implications of this research are significant, as it has the potential to enhance the effectiveness of human-computer interaction, autonomous systems, and educational technologies. Our contributions include the development of a learner-aware teaching framework, which can be applied to various domains, such as robotics, healthcare, and education, and the introduction of a new paradigm for inverse reinforcement learning that prioritizes learner-centric teaching. Keywords: inverse reinforcement learning, learner-aware teaching, preferences, constraints, personalized teaching, autonomous systems, human-computer interaction.

The database design for the tourism social network application is constructed with careful attention to modularity, scalability, and support for the system’s main features, as evidenced by its well-organized tables and relationships. The foundational structure incorporates tables such as Users, Profile, Destination, Hotel, Post, Media, Comment, Likes, Activity, and Follow. Each of these tables is designed with fields and keys tailored to optimize both storage and retrieval efficiency. For instance, the Users table manages essential authentication and identification fields such as user_id (primary key), email, hashed_password, and timestamps, ensuring both data privacy and auditability. The Profile table, linked to Users by foreign key, stores detailed personal information like full_name, avatar_url, bio, phone, and address, separating authentication from user-specific data for greater security and flexibility. Destinations and Hotels tables encompass tourism content, each with unique identifiers and metadata fields, such as destination_id, hotel_id, location, description, and rating, enabling users to explore, review, and interact with various tourist spots and accommodations. The Post table forms the heart of the social network component, allowing users to create and share experiences; it includes fields like post_id, user_id, destination_id, hotel_id (nullable, depending on the type of review), text_content, and creation_time. Posts are enriched by the Media table, which allows multimedia attachments for each post, with file_url, media_type, and referrer keys providing flexibility for supporting various file formats and scalable storage strategies. Interaction on the platform is further supported by the Comment and Likes tables. Comment manages threaded discussions on posts with fields such as comment_id, post_id, user_id, text, and parent_comment_id (for replies), as well as timestamp fields to support both chronological display and moderation features. Similarly, the Likes table efficiently tracks which users have liked which posts, with unique constraints to prevent duplicate likes. To chronicle user actions and encourage community engagement, the Activity table logs events like new posts, comments, or follows, storing user_id, activity_type, ref_id, and timestamps, which can be used for dynamic feeds, notification systems, or analytics. The Follow table enables social networking by recording relationships between users, utilizing follower_id and following_id, and optimizing queries for mutual connections or suggestions. Discrete spatial patterns and their continuous transformations are two important regularities contained in natural signals. Lie groups and representation theory are mathematical tools that have been used in previous works to model continuous image transformations. On the other hand, sparse coding is an important tool for learning dictionaries of patterns in natural signals. In this paper, we combine these ideas in a Bayesian generative model that learns to disentangle spatial patterns and their continuous transformations in a completely unsupervised manner. Images are modeled as a sparse superposition of shape components followed by a transformation that is parameterized by n continuous variables. The shape components and transformations are not predefined, but are instead adapted to learn the symmetries in the data, with the constraint that the transformations form a representation of an n-dimensional torus. Training the model on a dataset consisting of controlled geometric transformations of specific MNIST digits shows that it can recover these transformations along with the digits. Training on the full MNIST dataset shows that it can learn both the basic digit shapes and the natural transformations such as shearing and stretching that are contained in this data.

Julius Caesar là một trong những vở kịch nổi tiếng nhất của William Shakespeare, được viết vào khoảng năm 1599. Vở kịch này kể về cuộc đời và cái chết của Julius Caesar, một vị tướng và nhà lãnh đạo quyền lực của La Mã. Câu chuyện bắt đầu khi Julius Caesar trở về La Mã sau chiến thắng ở Gaul, nơi ông đã chinh phục được nhiều vùng đất. Tuy nhiên, Caesar đã trở nên quá quyền lực và đã bị một nhóm người, bao gồm cả Brutus và Cassius, coi là một mối đe dọa cho sự ổn định của La Mã. Brutus và Cassius đã âm mưu giết Caesar, và vào ngày 15 tháng 3 năm 44 TCN, họ đã thực hiện kế hoạch của mình. Caesar đã bị giết trong khi đang ngồi trong Senat, và vở kịch này đã mô tả chi tiết về cuộc đấu tranh giữa Caesar và những người muốn giết ông. Sau cái chết của Caesar, vở kịch này đã tiếp tục kể về cuộc chiến giữa Brutus và Cassius với Octavian, người đã trở thành người kế vị của Caesar. Cuối cùng, Octavian đã chiến thắng và đã tiêu diệt Brutus và Cassius. Julius Caesar là một vở kịch về chính trị, quyền lực và sự thay đổi. Nó đã được viết để thể hiện sự phức tạp và đa chiều của con người, và để cảnh báo về những hậu quả của sự tham lam và sự bất công.

Discovering imaging biomarkers for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is critical to help explain ASD and predict or monitor treatment outcomes. Toward this end, deep learning classifiers have recently been used for identifying ASD from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) with higher accuracy than traditional learning strategies. However, a key challenge with deep learning models is understanding just what image features the network is using, which can in turn be used to define the biomarkers. Current methods extract biomarkers, i.e., important features, by looking at how the prediction changes if "ignoring" one feature at a time. In this work, we go beyond looking at only individual features by using Shapley value explanation (SVE) from cooperative game theory. Cooperative game theory is advantageous here because it directly considers the interaction between features and can be applied to any machine learning method, making it a novel, more accurate way of determining instance-wise biomarker importance from deep learning models. A barrier to using SVE is its computational complexity: 2^N given N features. We explicitly reduce the complexity of SVE computation by two approaches based on the underlying graph structure of the input data: 1) only consider the centralized coalition of each feature; 2) a hierarchical pipeline which first clusters features into small communities, then applies SVE in each community. Monte Carlo approximation can be used for large permutation sets. We first validate our methods on the MNIST dataset and compare to human perception. Next, to insure plausibility of our biomarker results, we train a Random Forest (RF) to classify ASD/control subjects from fMRI and compare SVE results to standard RF-based feature importance. Finally, we show initial results on ranked fMRI biomarkers using SVE on a deep learning classifier for the ASD/control dataset.

This paper investigates the hierarchical structure inherent in relation labels for the task of scene graph generation, a critical step in understanding visual content. The objective is to enhance the semantic coherence and accuracy of scene graphs by leveraging the underlying hierarchy of relation labels. Our approach employs a novel model that incorporates hierarchical information within relational labels, thereby facilitating more precise and contextually aware scene graph generation. We apply a combination of deep learning techniques and hierarchical encoding strategies to capture and utilize these relational hierarchies effectively. Our experiments demonstrate that integrating hierarchical knowledge into scene graph generation significantly improves performance metrics, outperforming state-of-the-art models in terms of both precision and recall. The findings indicate a substantial advancement in visual scene understanding, paving the way for more sophisticated applications in image analysis, computer vision, and artificial intelligence-augmented interpretation. The research offers critical insights into the enhancement of scene graph accuracy, potentially benefiting a range of technologies from autonomous vehicles to intelligent photo sorting. Keywords include scene graph generation, hierarchical relations, deep learning, visual scene understanding, and semantic coherence.

This paper addresses the challenge of detecting anomalies in large-scale data environments, which is pivotal for applications in fields such as cybersecurity, fraud detection, and system health monitoring. Traditional methods often struggle with efficiency and scalability, necessitating innovative approaches that can manage vast and dynamic datasets. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel scalable algorithm that leverages learning-based controlled sensing to enhance anomaly detection in large datasets. Our approach employs machine learning techniques to intelligently select data points for analysis, thereby optimizing resource allocation and improving efficiency. The algorithm integrates adaptive learning to refine its sensing strategy based on the characteristics of the data encountered. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional methods in both accuracy and processing speed. The learning-based controlled sensing algorithm effectively reduces the data footprint required for analysis while maintaining high detection rates, making it suitable for real-time applications. Comparative evaluations with existing algorithms highlight our method's superior scalability and applicability in diverse anomaly detection scenarios. Conclusion/Implications: The proposed scalable algorithm represents a significant advancement in the field of anomaly detection, offering a practical solution for managing extensive and complex data environments. Our research provides valuable insights into the integration of learning-based approaches with controlled sensing, opening avenues for further exploration in adaptive anomaly detection frameworks. The potential applications of this method span various domains, enhancing data-driven decision-making processes and augmenting system resilience against anomalous activities. Keywords: Anomaly detection, scalable algorithm, learning-based controlled sensing, machine learning, real-time applications, data efficiency.

In the rapidly evolving field of object detection, accurately identifying and localizing multiple objects within an image remains a substantial challenge. This paper introduces RON, a novel framework named Reverse Connection with Objectness Prior Networks, designed to enhance the precision and efficiency of object detection models. Methods/Approach: The proposed RON architecture leverages reverse connectivity techniques to integrate Objectness Priors into the learning process, thereby improving the network's ability to differentiate between objects and background. This approach involves a specific network design that emphasizes backward feature propagation, which refines the prediction capability for object location and classification. The network is engineered to be compatible with various scales, thereby improving detection performance across diverse object sizes. Results/Findings: Our experimental results demonstrate that RON substantially improves detection accuracy, particularly in complex scenes with numerous overlapping objects. Comparative analyses reveal that RON outperforms traditional object detection frameworks by achieving higher precision and recall rates, and shows a significant reduction in false-positive detections. The framework's efficiency is highlighted by superior performance in benchmark datasets, indicating robust adaptability and generalization of the model. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of Reverse Connection with Objectness Prior Networks marks a significant advancement in the field of object detection. RON's architecture not only provides enhanced detection accuracy but also offers computational efficiency, making it a viable solution for real-time applications. The innovations presented in this research promise significant contributions to areas such as autonomous driving, surveillance systems, and image recognition technologies. Future applications may extend RON’s adaptability to more complex multi-object environments, further enhancing its utility in practical scenarios. Keywords: Object detection, RON, Reverse Connection, Objectness Prior Networks, feature propagation, image recognition.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in various generative tasks, but their significant computational demands hinder deployment on resource-constrained devices. This paper introduces a novel online multi-granularity distillation method for GAN compression, aiming to reduce model size and computational cost without sacrificing generation quality. Our approach leverages a pre-trained, high-capacity teacher GAN to guide the training of a smaller student GAN. Unlike traditional distillation methods, we perform distillation at multiple granularities, including feature-level, sample-level, and relation-level, to transfer comprehensive knowledge from the teacher to the student in an online fashion. This simultaneous training and distillation process allows the student network to dynamically learn from the teacher's evolving knowledge. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing GAN compression techniques in terms of Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS), while achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference time. The proposed method offers a practical solution for deploying high-quality GANs on edge devices and in other resource-limited environments. Keywords: GAN compression, knowledge distillation, generative models, online learning, model compression, deep learning.

Lighting estimation from a single image is an essential yet challenging task in computer vision and computer graphics. Existing works estimate lighting by regressing representative illumination parameters or generating illumination maps directly. However, these methods often suffer from poor accuracy and generalization. This paper presents Geometric Mover's Light (GMLight), a lighting estimation framework that employs a regression network and a generative projector for effective illumination estimation. We parameterize illumination scenes in terms of the geometric light distribution, light intensity, ambient term, and auxiliary depth, and estimate them as a pure regression task. Inspired by the earth mover's distance, we design a novel geometric mover's loss to guide the accurate regression of light distribution parameters. With the estimated lighting parameters, the generative projector synthesizes panoramic illumination maps with realistic appearance and frequency. Extensive experiments show that GMLight achieves accurate illumination estimation and superior fidelity in relighting for 3D object insertion.

This paper establishes an exact mapping between the Variational Renormalization Group (VRG) and deep learning architectures. We demonstrate that VRG, a powerful theoretical framework for analyzing systems at different scales, can be implemented using deep neural networks. Specifically, we show how network layers correspond to renormalization group transformations, with network parameters learning the optimal coarse-graining procedure. This mapping allows us to interpret the training of deep networks as a process of iteratively simplifying the data while preserving relevant information. Our results provide a novel theoretical perspective on deep learning, linking it to fundamental concepts in statistical physics. This connection enables the application of VRG techniques to understand and improve deep learning models, such as developing new regularization strategies and network architectures. We present numerical experiments on benchmark datasets that validate our theoretical framework and demonstrate the potential of VRG-inspired deep learning algorithms. This work opens avenues for cross-disciplinary research, fostering a deeper understanding of both deep learning and renormalization group methods. Keywords: Variational Renormalization Group, Deep Learning, Neural Networks, Statistical Physics, Coarse-Graining, Information Theory.

This paper explores the application of machine learning techniques to analyze machine data generated from a Computer-Assisted Telephone Interviewing (CATI) network. The objective is to identify patterns and anomalies within the network's operational data to improve efficiency and resource allocation. We employ several supervised and unsupervised learning models, including random forests, support vector machines, and clustering algorithms, to process call logs, agent performance metrics, and system resource utilization data. The adversarial vulnerability of deep networks has spurred the interest of researchers worldwide. Unsurprisingly, like images, adversarial examples also translate to time-series data as they are an inherent weakness of the model itself rather than the modality. Several attempts have been made to defend against these adversarial attacks, particularly for the visual modality. In this paper, we perform detailed benchmarking of well-proven adversarial defense methodologies on time-series data. We restrict ourselves to the L_ threat model. We also explore the trade-off between smoothness and clean accuracy for regularization-based defenses to better understand the trade-offs that they offer. Our analysis shows that the explored adversarial defenses offer robustness against both strong white-box as well as black-box attacks. This paves the way for future research in the direction of adversarial attacks and defenses, particularly for time-series data.

This paper addresses the challenge of removing undesirable information—such as sensitive attributes or dataset biases—from learned data representations in self-supervised learning frameworks. We propose Conditional Contrastive Learning (CCL), a novel approach that extends standard contrastive learning by conditioning the representation learning process to explicitly suppress specified unwanted features. The method incorporates a conditional objective that guides the neural network to disentangle and minimize the encoding of user-defined undesirable information, while still preserving task-relevant content. We evaluate CCL on benchmark image and text datasets where the removal of confounding attributes, including demographic information and spurious correlations, is critical. Experimental results demonstrate that CCL achieves superior performance in mitigating attribute leakage compared to traditional self-supervised and adversarial approaches, without sacrificing downstream task accuracy. The proposed framework thus enables more robust, fair, and privacy-preserving representations, with broad implications for applications in bias-aware AI, secure machine learning, and ethical data analysis. Keywords: self-supervised learning, contrastive learning, representation learning, information removal, attribute disentanglement, bias mitigation, privacy-preserving AI.

This paper introduces PyKEEN 1.0, a Python library designed to facilitate the training and evaluation of knowledge graph embeddings. The primary objective of PyKEEN is to provide a unified framework for knowledge graph embedding models, enabling researchers and developers to efficiently compare and contrast different techniques. PyKEEN achieves this through a modular architecture, allowing users to easily implement and evaluate various knowledge graph embedding models, including TransE, ConvE, and RotatE. The library also includes tools for hyperparameter tuning, model selection, and evaluation metrics, making it an essential resource for the development of knowledge graph-based applications. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of PyKEEN in training and evaluating knowledge graph embeddings, with significant improvements in computational efficiency and model performance. The release of PyKEEN 1.0 contributes to the advancement of knowledge graph research, providing a widely applicable and extensible platform for the development of novel embedding models and applications. Key features of PyKEEN include support for multiple embedding models, automated hyperparameter tuning, and integration with popular deep learning frameworks. By leveraging PyKEEN, researchers can focus on developing innovative knowledge graph-based solutions, driving progress in areas such as question answering, entity disambiguation, and recommender systems.

Semi-supervised learning aims to leverage unlabeled data to improve image classification performance, especially when labeled data is scarce. This paper introduces Vanishing Twin GAN (VT-GAN), a novel approach that utilizes a weakly trained Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to enhance semi-supervised image classification. Unlike conventional GAN applications focused on data augmentation, VT-GAN strategically employs a GAN trained for a limited number of epochs, resulting in imperfect synthetic images. We hypothesize that these "vanishing twin" images, while not photorealistic, provide valuable regularization during the training of a classifier. Our method incorporates a consistency regularization term that encourages the classifier to produce similar predictions for real unlabeled images and their corresponding synthetic "vanishing twin" counterparts. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and SVHN, demonstrate that VT-GAN achieves significant improvements in classification accuracy compared to existing semi-supervised learning techniques. Notably, VT-GAN’s performance gains are most pronounced when the amount of labeled data is limited. The results suggest that weakly trained GANs can be effectively harnessed to improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of classifiers in semi-supervised scenarios, offering a novel perspective on GAN utilization beyond data generation. Keywords: Semi-Supervised Learning, Generative Adversarial Networks, Image Classification, Consistency Regularization, GAN Regularization.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in learning representations for graph-structured data. However, their computational complexity and memory requirements often limit their applicability in resource-constrained environments. To address this challenge, we propose Bi-GCN, a novel Binary Graph Convolutional Network that significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining competitive performance. Bi-GCN employs binary weights and activations, enabling efficient inference and reduced memory usage. We introduce a binarization strategy tailored for graph data, ensuring minimal loss of structural information during the quantization process. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that Bi-GCN achieves comparable accuracy to full-precision GCNs while reducing computational costs by over 80%. Additionally, we analyze the trade-offs between binarization and model performance, providing insights into the robustness of binary GCNs across various graph tasks. Our results highlight the potential of Bi-GCN for deploying graph-based machine learning models in edge devices and real-time applications. This work contributes to advancing efficient graph representation learning and opens new avenues for lightweight, scalable graph neural networks. **Keywords**: Graph Convolutional Networks, Binary Neural Networks, Graph Representation Learning, Efficient Inference, Resource-Constrained Environments.

Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, but its high computational cost and slow convergence remain significant challenges. This paper investigates accelerated methods for DRL, focusing on improving training efficiency without sacrificing performance. We propose a novel approach that combines prioritized experience replay with a modified actor-critic architecture, incorporating techniques to reduce variance in gradient estimates. Our method, Accelerated Deep Reinforcement Learning (ADRL), prioritizes the replay of significant experiences and employs a variance reduction scheme based on control variates within the policy gradient update. Experimental results on benchmark control tasks demonstrate that ADRL achieves a substantial reduction in training time compared to standard DRL algorithms such as DQN and A2C, while maintaining comparable or superior performance. Specifically, ADRL converges up to 40% faster in complex environments. These findings highlight the potential of ADRL to accelerate DRL training and facilitate its application to real-world problems with limited computational resources. Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Accelerated Training, Prioritized Experience Replay, Actor-Critic, Variance Reduction, Policy Gradient.

This paper investigates the impact of Q-function reuse on the total regret experienced during the learning processes within tabular, model-free reinforcement learning frameworks. The aim is to determine whether leveraging previously acquired Q-functions can enhance learning efficiency and reduce cumulative regret. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel approach to incorporate Q-function reuse in tabular model-free reinforcement learning, utilizing a mechanism that integrates past Q-values into the learning pipeline. This approach is designed to optimize the exploration-exploitation balance by leveraging historical data to inform decision-making. Key algorithms are evaluated and compared using standard reinforcement learning benchmarks to assess their performance. Results/Findings: Our experimental results demonstrate a significant reduction in total regret when Q-function reuse is employed. Specifically, the integration of previously acquired Q-functions leads to faster convergence and improved learning efficiency across various reinforcement learning tasks. The modified learning algorithms outperform traditional approaches, underscoring the potential benefits of this reuse strategy. Conclusion/Implications: The study highlights the advantages of Q-function reuse in model-free reinforcement learning, showing a clear reduction in cumulative regret and enhanced overall performance. This research provides valuable insights for the development of more efficient learning systems, with potential applications in autonomous decision-making systems and adaptive control environments. Future work will explore extending this approach to more complex and scalable reinforcement learning scenarios. Keywords: Q-function reuse, tabular reinforcement learning, model-free learning, total regret, learning efficiency, exploration-exploitation balance.

This paper addresses the challenge of open set recognition, where a model must identify whether a given input belongs to one of the known classes or is an unknown class. The objective is to develop a collective decision-making approach that improves the accuracy and robustness of open set recognition systems. Our method combines the predictions of multiple classifiers using a novel ensemble technique, which leverages the strengths of each individual model to produce a more reliable output. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and recall, particularly in scenarios with high levels of noise and uncertainty. The key findings of this research highlight the importance of collective decision-making in open set recognition, and our approach has significant implications for applications such as anomaly detection, image classification, and natural language processing. By leveraging the power of ensemble learning, our method provides a robust and effective solution for open set recognition, with potential applications in areas such as AI, machine learning, and data mining, and relevant keywords include open set recognition, collective decision-making, ensemble learning, and anomaly detection.

Remote sensing image change detection plays a crucial role in environmental monitoring and urban planning. This paper introduces a novel dual-task constrained deep Siamese convolutional network model for building change detection. Our approach leverages a Siamese network architecture to extract robust feature representations from bi-temporal image pairs. We incorporate a dual-task learning framework, simultaneously predicting change regions and semantic segmentation maps to enhance feature discrimination and contextual awareness. A constraint is imposed between the two tasks to enforce feature consistency and improve overall accuracy. The model is trained end-to-end, allowing for joint optimization of feature extraction and change classification. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both detection accuracy and segmentation quality. The improvements highlight the effectiveness of the dual-task learning strategy and the constrained optimization process. This research contributes a more accurate and robust approach to building change detection, enabling more informed decision-making in various applications. **Keywords:** Change Detection, Remote Sensing, Siamese Network, Deep Learning, Dual-Task Learning, Convolutional Neural Network, Semantic Segmentation.

This paper presents a novel blockwise approach for the detection of local defects in images. The primary objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of defect detection by analyzing images in smaller, more manageable blocks. Our method employs a statistical analysis of pixel intensity variations within each block to identify anomalous regions indicative of defects. Specifically, we calculate the mean and standard deviation of each block and compare these values against a global threshold determined dynamically from the entire image. Blocks exceeding this threshold are further analyzed using a texture-based feature extraction technique based on Gabor filters to differentiate between actual defects and noise. Experimental results on a diverse dataset of industrial images demonstrate that our blockwise method achieves a significant improvement in defect detection accuracy, with an F1-score of 0.92, compared to traditional whole-image analysis techniques. Furthermore, the blockwise approach reduces computational complexity, allowing for faster processing times, making it suitable for real-time applications. The proposed method offers a robust and efficient solution for automated defect detection, with potential applications in manufacturing quality control and other industrial inspection tasks. **Keywords:** Defect Detection, Blockwise Processing, Image Analysis, Statistical Analysis, Texture Analysis, Gabor Filters, Quality Control.

Model cards are increasingly recognized as a crucial tool for responsible AI development, providing transparent documentation of model characteristics and performance. This paper investigates the practical implementation and impact of model cards in real-world scenarios. We propose a framework for standardized model card generation, incorporating key metrics related to intended use, limitations, biases, and ethical considerations. Our approach includes an automated pipeline for data collection and reporting, reducing the burden on developers and promoting consistent documentation. We evaluate our framework through a case study involving multiple machine learning models deployed in diverse applications. The results demonstrate that model cards effectively improve model understanding, facilitate stakeholder communication, and support informed decision-making regarding model deployment and usage. Key findings reveal the importance of comprehensive bias analysis and the need for iterative model refinement based on model card insights. This research contributes to the advancement of responsible AI by providing a practical and scalable solution for model reporting. Keywords: Model Cards, AI Ethics, Responsible AI, Model Reporting, Transparency, Machine Learning, Bias Detection.

Most existing object detection methods rely on the availability of abundant labelled training samples per class and offline model training in a batch mode. These requirements substantially limit their scalability to open-ended accommodation of novel classes with limited labelled training data. We present a study aiming to go beyond these limitations by considering the Incremental Few-Shot Detection (iFSD) problem setting, where new classes must be registered incrementally (without revisiting base classes) and with few examples. To this end we propose OpeN-ended Centre nEt (ONCE), a detector designed for incrementally learning to detect novel class objects with few examples. This is achieved by an elegant adaptation of the CentreNet detector to the few-shot learning scenario, and meta-learning a class-specific code generator model for registering novel classes. ONCE fully respects the incremental learning paradigm, with novel class registration requiring only a single forward pass of few-shot training samples, and no access to base classes -- thus making it suitable for deployment on embedded devices. Extensive experiments conducted on both the standard object detection and fashion landmark detection tasks show the feasibility of iFSD for the first time, opening an interesting and very important line of research.

This paper addresses the challenge of point cloud completion, crucial for various applications such as computer vision and 3D modeling, where incomplete data can lead to subpar performance. Our research focuses on refining the predicted missing parts to enhance the overall quality of point cloud completion. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative framework that leverages a multi-stage refinement process to accurately predict and fill in missing regions in point clouds. Our approach integrates advanced machine learning techniques with point cloud processing algorithms to iteratively improve data accuracy and surface detail. By incorporating a novel loss function that prioritizes structural integrity, our model consistently refines predictions through successive stages. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing completion techniques in terms of accuracy and reconstruction quality. Compared to baseline models, our framework achieves higher completion success rates and better preserves the geometric characteristics of the original point clouds. Moreover, the refinement process yields noticeable improvements in finer details that are often lost in conventional approaches. Conclusion/Implications: The proposed refinement technique offers substantial contributions to the field of point cloud processing by enhancing the reliability and applicability of 3D data in real-world scenarios. Our findings suggest potential applications in areas such as autonomous navigation, augmented reality, and robotics, where precise 3D reconstruction is essential. This research opens up new avenues for future developments in automated point cloud completion and can serve as a benchmark for further studies on refining predictive models. Keywords: Point Cloud Completion, Machine Learning, 3D Reconstruction, Data Refinement, Predictive Modelling, Structural Integrity.

Some reinforcement learning methods suffer from high sample complexity causing them to not be practical in real-world situations. Q-function reuse, a transfer learning method, is one way to reduce the sample complexity of learning, potentially improving usefulness of existing algorithms. Prior work has shown the empirical effectiveness of Q-function reuse for various environments when applied to model-free algorithms. To the best of our knowledge, there has been no theoretical work showing the regret of Q-function reuse when applied to the tabular, model-free setting. We aim to bridge the gap between theoretical and empirical work in Q-function reuse by providing some theoretical insights on the effectiveness of Q-function reuse when applied to the Q-learning with UCB-Hoeffding algorithm. Our main contribution is showing that in a specific case if Q-function reuse is applied to the Q-learning with UCB-Hoeffding algorithm it has a regret that is independent of the state or action space. We also provide empirical results supporting our theoretical findings.

This paper presents a novel hybrid approach for enhancing classification performance by integrating a Deep Stacked Sparse Autoencoder (DSSAE) with a weighted Local Preserving Projection Discriminant (wLPPD) Support Vector Machine (SVM) ensemble. The primary objective is to address the challenges of high-dimensional data classification, where traditional methods often struggle with feature extraction and discriminative representation. The proposed method leverages the unsupervised learning capabilities of DSSAE to extract hierarchical and sparse features from raw data, followed by the wLPPD SVM ensemble, which enhances discriminative power by preserving local structures and optimizing class separability. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the hybrid model achieves superior classification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, with significant improvements in handling complex and noisy data. The key contributions of this work include the integration of deep feature learning with a weighted ensemble framework, offering a robust solution for high-dimensional classification tasks. This research has potential applications in areas such as image recognition, bioinformatics, and anomaly detection, where accurate and efficient classification is critical. Keywords: Deep Stacked Sparse Autoencoder, wLPPD SVM, ensemble learning, feature extraction, high-dimensional classification.

Snow accumulation on images poses a significant challenge for computer vision tasks in outdoor environments, often degrading scene visibility and affecting the performance of downstream algorithms. This paper presents DesnowNet, a context-aware deep learning network specifically designed to address the problem of snow removal from images. The proposed model leverages a multi-scale convolutional architecture that incorporates contextual information, enabling effective identification and removal of snow artifacts across varying sizes and densities. By integrating attention mechanisms and residual connections, DesnowNet adapts to the spatial distribution of snow and preserves underlying image details. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark and real-world snow-covered datasets demonstrate that DesnowNet consistently outperforms existing methods in both qualitative and quantitative assessments, achieving superior restoration of scene clarity and structural integrity. The findings highlight DesnowNet’s robustness and efficiency in real-time image enhancement applications, offering substantial improvements for tasks such as autonomous driving, surveillance, and outdoor photography. The key contributions of this work include a tailored architecture for context-aware snow detection, improved restoration quality, and generalizability across diverse environmental conditions. Keywords: image restoration, snow removal, deep learning, context-aware networks, attention mechanism, computer vision.

This paper addresses the critical need for explainable online validation of machine learning models in practical applications, aiming to enhance model reliability and trustworthiness. Our approach combines model interpretability techniques with real-time data processing to facilitate the continuous monitoring and validation of machine learning models in dynamic environments. We propose a novel framework that integrates feature attribution methods, model performance metrics, and data quality assessment to provide insights into model behavior and decision-making processes. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in identifying model drift, data quality issues, and performance degradation, allowing for timely interventions and model updates. The key contributions of this research include the development of a scalable and flexible validation framework, the introduction of a new feature attribution method tailored to online learning settings, and the demonstration of improved model explainability and reliability in real-world applications. Our work has significant implications for the deployment of machine learning models in high-stakes domains, such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems, where model transparency and accountability are essential. Key keywords: explainable AI, machine learning, online validation, model interpretability, real-time data processing.

Việc tự động phân cấp các khái niệm (taxonomy) từ dữ liệu văn bản đã trở thành một nhiệm vụ quan trọng trong nhiều lĩnh vực, giúp tổ chức và truy xuất thông tin hiệu quả hơn. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc áp dụng các kỹ thuật học máy để xây dựng taxonomy một cách tự động trong một miền lĩnh vực cụ thể. Bài toán đặt ra là làm thế nào để trích xuất các khái niệm quan trọng từ một tập hợp lớn các văn bản, xác định mối quan hệ giữa chúng (ví dụ: quan hệ "is-a" hoặc "part-of"), và sắp xếp chúng thành một cấu trúc phân cấp có ý nghĩa. Các phương pháp học máy được sử dụng bao gồm khai thác luật kết hợp, phân cụm văn bản, và học sâu dựa trên mạng nơ-ron. Khai thác luật kết hợp giúp xác định các khái niệm thường xuất hiện cùng nhau, từ đó suy ra mối liên hệ tiềm ẩn. Phân cụm văn bản được sử dụng để nhóm các văn bản có nội dung tương tự, tạo ra các cụm đại diện cho các khái niệm khác nhau. Học sâu, đặc biệt là các mô hình ngôn ngữ được huấn luyện trước, có khả năng nắm bắt ngữ nghĩa của văn bản một cách tinh tế, cho phép xác định mối quan hệ giữa các khái niệm một cách chính xác hơn. Dữ liệu được sử dụng trong nghiên cứu là một tập hợp các văn bản thuộc một lĩnh vực cụ thể, đã được tiền xử lý để loại bỏ nhiễu và chuẩn hóa định dạng. Các khái niệm được trích xuất từ văn bản thông qua các kỹ thuật xử lý ngôn ngữ tự nhiên như tách từ, gán nhãn từ loại, và phân tích cú pháp. Hiệu suất của các phương pháp học máy được đánh giá dựa trên độ chính xác của taxonomy được tạo ra, so sánh với taxonomy được xây dựng thủ công bởi các chuyên gia trong lĩnh vực. Kết quả cho thấy rằng các phương pháp học máy có thể tạo ra taxonomy với độ chính xác cao, đặc biệt khi kết hợp nhiều kỹ thuật khác nhau. Tuy nhiên, vẫn còn một số thách thức cần giải quyết, chẳng hạn như xử lý các khái niệm mơ hồ và xác định mối quan hệ phức tạp giữa các khái niệm. Nghiên cứu này đóng góp vào việc phát triển các phương pháp tự động xây dựng taxonomy hiệu quả hơn, giúp cải thiện khả năng tổ chức và truy xuất thông tin trong nhiều lĩnh vực khác nhau. Các hướng nghiên cứu tiếp theo có thể tập trung vào việc kết hợp thông tin từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau, sử dụng các mô hình học máy tiên tiến hơn, và phát triển các phương pháp đánh giá taxonomy toàn diện hơn.

The increasing computational demands of self-attention mechanisms in transformer models necessitate efficient approximation techniques. This paper explores a novel approach to enhancing self-attention by employing spectral shifting, potentially surpassing traditional methods like Nyströmformer in efficiency and accuracy. Methods/Approach: We introduce a spectral shifting strategy to approximate self-attention, which leverages eigenvalue manipulation to build an augmented representation of attention matrices. This method exploits the spectral properties of the attention matrices to reduce computational complexity while maintaining a robust approximation capability. The proposed model integrates seamlessly into existing transformer architectures. Results/Findings: Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our spectral shifting method significantly improves upon Nyströmformer approximations, achieving faster computation times and superior accuracy in diverse natural language processing tasks. In particular, our approach maintains high fidelity in capturing salient features of attention matrices, yielding performance boosts in large-scale datasets. Conclusion/Implications: Our research reveals the potential of spectral shifting as a powerful tool for optimizing transformer models. By effectively approximating self-attention mechanisms, this technique reduces the resource requirements associated with training and deploying large-scale models. The findings suggest broad applicability, with implications for improving the efficiency of various AI applications reliant on transformer models. This work paves the way for further exploration into spectral techniques for deep learning optimizations. Keywords: self-attention, spectral shifting, transformer, Nyströmformer, approximation, natural language processing, computational efficiency.

The research addresses the challenge of generating synthetic LiDAR data efficiently, required for a variety of applications in autonomous driving and robotic navigation. Current methods in synthetic LiDAR rendering are computationally intensive and often lack the speed required for real-time applications. Methods/Approach: This paper introduces a novel approach for fast synthetic LiDAR rendering using spherical UV unwrapping of equirectangular Z-buffer images. The method transforms conventional rendering techniques by leveraging equirectangular projections to produce highly accurate depth information. This approach bypasses traditional computational bottlenecks, permitting rapid generation of LiDAR point clouds. Results/Findings: The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in rendering speed and maintains high fidelity in depth reconstruction compared to existing methods. Through comprehensive experiments, it achieves real-time processing speeds and presents significant improvements in computational efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. Further, the method's compatibility with existing 3D engines highlights its practical applicability. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides a significant advancement in the field of synthetic LiDAR data generation, combining speed and precision in a novel approach. The technique opens avenues for real-time simulation environments and enhances the potential for integration into autonomous systems. The findings contribute to the ongoing development of efficient 3D reconstruction methodologies, underscoring their role in the future of autonomous technologies. Keywords: Synthetic LiDAR, Equirectangular Projection, Spherical UV Unwrapping, Real-time Rendering, 3D Reconstruction, Autonomous Systems.

This paper addresses the challenge of moment localization in videos using natural language queries, a critical task in video understanding and retrieval. We propose a novel 2D Temporal Adjacent Network (2D-TAN) framework that effectively captures temporal dependencies and aligns video segments with textual descriptions. Unlike existing methods that rely on one-dimensional temporal modeling, our approach leverages a 2D feature map to represent temporal relationships between video moments, enabling more precise localization. Results/Findings: The proposed approach was evaluated on a series of benchmark datasets characterized by varying levels of noise contamination. The results demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional static filtering techniques and current state-of-the-art algorithms, yielding enhanced signal clarity and improved classification accuracy. Specifically, the incorporation of dynamic spatial filtering led to significant improvements in denoising performance without compromising computational efficiency. Conclusion/Implications: This research makes a substantial contribution to the field of EEG analysis by introducing a robust and adaptive filtering framework. The findings suggest potential for extensive applications, including real-time brain-computer interface systems and clinical diagnostics, where accurate EEG interpretation is crucial. Keywords: EEG, robust learning, dynamic spatial filtering, noise reduction, brain-computer interface, neural signal processing.

Geodesic Active Contours (GACs) are powerful tools for image segmentation, but their performance is highly dependent on the initial contour and can be sensitive to noise. This paper introduces a novel algorithm for GACs based on the characteristic function, designed to improve robustness and accuracy. The proposed method replaces the traditional level set function with a characteristic function, offering a more stable representation of the evolving contour and enabling a more accurate approximation of the geodesic distance. The algorithm utilizes a narrow band implementation to enhance computational efficiency. Experimental results on synthetic and real images demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved segmentation accuracy and noise resilience compared to conventional GAC implementations, particularly in images with weak object boundaries and high levels of noise. Key findings indicate a significant reduction in the sensitivity to initial contour placement and improved convergence. This work contributes a robust and efficient GAC framework suitable for various image segmentation applications. Keywords: Geodesic Active Contours, Image Segmentation, Characteristic Function, Level Set, Active Contours, Computer Vision.

Attributes of sound inherent to objects can provide valuable cues to learn rich representations for object detection and tracking. Furthermore, the co-occurrence of audiovisual events in videos can be exploited to localize objects over the image field by solely monitoring the sound in the environment. Thus far, this has only been feasible in scenarios where the camera is static and for single object detection. Moreover, the robustness of these methods has been limited as they primarily rely on RGB images which are highly susceptible to illumination and weather changes. In this work, we present the novel self-supervised MM-DistillNet framework consisting of multiple teachers that leverage diverse modalities including RGB, depth and thermal images, to simultaneously exploit complementary cues and distill knowledge into a single audio student network. We propose the new MTA loss function that facilitates the distillation of information from multimodal teachers in a self-supervised manner. Additionally, we propose a novel self-supervised pretext task for the audio student that enables us to not rely on labor-intensive manual annotations. We introduce a large-scale multimodal dataset with over 113,000 time-synchronized frames of RGB, depth, thermal, and audio modalities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods while being able to detect multiple objects using only sound during inference and even while moving.

Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, demonstrate that MSNN achieves superior accuracy compared to conventional CNNs and state-of-the-art subspace-based methods. The results highlight the model's ability to effectively handle complex image recognition tasks by exploiting diverse feature representations. This work contributes to advancing image recognition by introducing a scalable and interpretable framework that bridges subspace learning and deep neural networks, with potential applications in medical imaging, autonomous systems, and beyond. **Keywords**: Image recognition, multi-subspace learning, neural networks, feature extraction, deep learning, computer vision.

Objective: Transfer learning enables leveraging knowledge from a source task to improve performance on related target tasks, but common approaches often suffer from negative transfer, domain shift sensitivity, and inconsistent outcomes. This work proposes a framework for more reliable transfer learning that explicitly models uncertainty and regularizes feature adaptation to stabilize fine-tuning across diverse tasks. Methods: We introduce RFA-TWP (Regularized Feature Alignment with Task-Aware Weight Prior), which combines (1) a Bayesian uncertainty estimator to identify and down-weight unreliable source features during adaptation, and (2) a meta-learned regularization term that enforces consistency between source and target representations. Our approach trains an ensemble of lightweight Bayesian neural networks to quantify transfer risk and adapts parameters via gradient-based meta-optimization, ensuring robustness to domain shifts. Results: We evaluate RFA-TWP on three standard benchmarks—Office-31 (object recognition), VisDA-2017 (synthetic-to-real), and CIFAR→SVHN—and compare against fine-tuning, domain adversarial training, and conventional meta-learning baselines. Across ten transfer scenarios, our method achieves up to 5.8% higher average accuracy, reduces worst-case performance drop by 40%, and yields 30% lower variance in target metrics. Ablation studies confirm that both uncertainty weighting and task-aware regularization are critical for stable gains. Conclusion: RFA-TWP sets a new reliability standard in transfer learning by mitigating negative transfer and ensuring consistent improvements under varying domain shifts. This framework can be readily applied to vision, language, and speech tasks where dependable adaptation is essential. Keywords: transfer learning, reliability, domain adaptation, Bayesian uncertainty, meta-learning.

CRC có thể được ngăn ngừa bằng cách theo dõi nội soi thường quy và cắt bỏ polyp. Tuy nhiên, quá trình nội soi phát hiện polyp phụ thuộc vào nhiều yếu tố như chất lượng hệ thống trang thiết bị, quy trình nội soi, môi trường làm việc và kinh nghiệm của bác sỹ.
