Efficient software testing is essential for productive software development and reliable user experiences. As human testing is inefficient and expensive, automated software testing is needed. In this work, we propose a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for functional software testing named DRIFT. DRIFT operates on the symbolic representation of the user interface. It uses Q-learning through Batch-RL and models the state-action value function with a Graph Neural Network. We apply DRIFT to testing the Windows 10 operating system and show that DRIFT can robustly trigger the desired software functionality in a fully automated manner. Our experiments test the ability to perform single and combined tasks across different applications, demonstrating that our framework can efficiently test software with a large range of testing objectives.

Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) assumes that source and target domain data are freely available and usually trained together to reduce the domain gap. However, considering the data privacy and the inefficiency of data transmission, it is impractical in real scenarios. Hence, it draws our eyes to optimize the network in the target domain without accessing labeled source data. To explore this direction in object detection, for the first time, we propose a source data-free domain adaptive object detection (SFOD) framework via modeling it into a problem of learning with noisy labels. Generally, a straightforward method is to leverage the pre-trained network from the source domain to generate the pseudo labels for target domain optimization. However, it is difficult to evaluate the quality of pseudo labels since no labels are available in target domain. In this paper, self-entropy descent (SED) is a metric proposed to search an appropriate confidence threshold for reliable pseudo label generation without using any handcrafted labels. Nonetheless, completely clean labels are still unattainable. After a thorough experimental analysis, false negatives are found to dominate in the generated noisy labels. Undoubtedly, false negatives mining is helpful for performance improvement, and we ease it to false negatives simulation through data augmentation like Mosaic. Extensive experiments conducted in four representative adaptation tasks have demonstrated that the proposed framework can easily achieve state-of-the-art performance. From another view, it also reminds the UDA community that the labeled source data are not fully exploited in the existing methods.

This paper aims to identify influential training samples for Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDTs), a crucial task for improving model interpretability and robustness. Our approach leverages a novel combination of feature importance and sample-based explanations to detect key training instances that significantly impact model predictions. We employ a modified gradient boosting algorithm to assign influence scores to each training sample, allowing for the identification of both positive and negative influencers. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in pinpointing influential samples, which can be used to refine model training, mitigate overfitting, and enhance overall performance. Our research contributes to the development of more transparent and reliable GBDT models, with potential applications in areas such as data preprocessing, model debugging, and explainable AI. Key findings highlight the importance of considering sample-level influence in tree-based ensemble methods, paving the way for future research in model interpretability and robustness. Relevant keywords: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees, influential training samples, model interpretability, explainable AI, tree-based ensemble methods.

Phân tích ROC được sử dụng để xác định ngưỡng ADC tối ưu giúp phân biệt HGG với các tổn thương khác, từ đó nâng cao độ chính xác trong chẩn đoán phân biệt và hỗ trợ quyết định điều trị phù hợp cho bệnh nhân. This paper investigates the potential of integrating Integral Probability Metrics (IPM) into Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for semi-supervised learning. The aim is to enhance performance in scenarios where labeled data is scarce, offering a robust alternative to fully supervised approaches. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel architecture that incorporates IPM-based GANs into the semi-supervised learning framework. The model leverages the strengths of IPM for efficient domain adaptation and improved generalization in GANs. An empirical study was conducted using benchmark datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method in comparison to traditional GANs and other state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning techniques. Results/Findings: The results indicate that the IPM-enhanced GAN model significantly outperforms baseline models in terms of classification accuracy and data generation quality. The experiments demonstrated improved error rates and robust performance even with limited labeled data. Comparative analysis shows that our method achieves superior generalization capabilities and stability in training across diverse datasets. Conclusion/Implications: Our study highlights the advantages of incorporating IPM into GANs for semi-supervised learning, showcasing improvements in both theoretical understanding and practical application. This integration opens up new avenues for research in data-scarce environments. The findings suggest that IPM-based GANs can be effectively deployed in various applications such as image recognition, natural language processing, and other fields where data labeling is a constraint. Keywords: Semi-supervised learning, IPM, GANs, Generative Adversarial Networks, Integral Probability Metrics, Domain adaptation, Data-scarce environments.

We study the task of conversational fashion image retrieval via multiturn natural language feedback. Most previous studies are based on single-turn settings. Existing models on multiturn conversational fashion image retrieval have limitations, such as employing traditional models, and leading to ineffective performance. We propose a novel framework that can effectively handle conversational fashion image retrieval with multiturn natural language feedback texts. One characteristic of the framework is that it searches for candidate images based on exploitation of the encoded reference image and feedback text information together with the conversation history. Furthermore, the image fashion attribute information is leveraged via a mutual attention strategy. Since there is no existing fashion dataset suitable for the multiturn setting of our task, we derive a large-scale multiturn fashion dataset via additional manual annotation efforts on an existing single-turn dataset. The experiments show that our proposed model significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

In this paper we study the application of convolutional neural networks for jointly detecting objects depicted in still images and estimating their 3D pose. We identify different feature representations of oriented objects, and energies that lead a network to learn this representations. The choice of the representation is crucial since the pose of an object has a natural, continuous structure while its category is a discrete variable. We evaluate the different approaches on the joint object detection and pose estimation task of the Pascal3D+ benchmark using Average Viewpoint Precision. We show that a classification approach on discretized viewpoints achieves state-of-the-art performance for joint object detection and pose estimation, and significantly outperforms existing baselines on this benchmark.

Objective: Accurate analysis and forecasting of correlated multivariate time series are critical in domains such as finance, environmental monitoring, and healthcare. Traditional models often struggle to capture both complex temporal dynamics and inter-series dependencies simultaneously. Methods: We propose a Deep Structural Model (DSM) that integrates a recurrent encoder for temporal pattern learning with a graph-based structural module to explicitly model correlations among multiple series. An attention mechanism dynamically weights dependencies, while a variational inference layer ensures robust latent representation learning. The entire architecture is trained end-to-end, allowing the model to adaptively discover and leverage underlying structural relationships. Results: Experiments on three benchmark datasets—including financial indices, sensor networks, and clinical recordings—demonstrate that DSM reduces forecasting error by 15–25% (measured in RMSE and MAE) compared to state-of-the-art baselines such as VAR, LSTM, and Graph WaveNet. Ablation studies confirm the individual contributions of the structural module and attention mechanism to overall performance gains. Conclusion: The proposed DSM effectively captures both temporal and structural characteristics of multivariate time series, yielding more accurate forecasts and offering interpretable insights into inter-series interactions. Its flexibility makes it suitable for real-time monitoring, anomaly detection, and imputation tasks. Future work will explore online adaptation and scalability to ultra-high-dimensional datasets. Keywords: Deep Structural Model, multivariate time series, correlation modeling, temporal forecasting, graph neural network, attention mechanism.

The study aims to address the challenge of assessing aesthetic attributes in images, a key component in various applications such as photography, digital media, and online content moderation. The research seeks to provide a comprehensive model that can accurately evaluate aesthetic features and enhance the understanding of image quality from a subjective viewpoint. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative approach leveraging a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, designed specifically for aesthetic assessment. The model incorporates advanced feature extraction techniques to capture nuanced aesthetic attributes such as color harmony, balance, and composition. A diverse dataset of images with pre-labeled aesthetic scores is used to train and validate the model, ensuring robust performance across different styles and contexts. Results/Findings: The proposed CNN model demonstrates superior performance in predicting aesthetic attributes, achieving significant improvements in accuracy compared to existing methods. The model's ability to generalize across various types of images is validated through extensive testing, showing notable advancements in automatic image assessment systems. Conclusion/Implications: Our research contributes a novel CNN-based model that enhances the precision of aesthetic evaluations in image processing. This work holds important implications for the development of intelligent systems in digital media and content creation, facilitating automated feedback and improvements. Potential applications include image editing software, digital marketing platforms, and social media analytics. Keywords: Aesthetic assessment, Convolutional neural network, Image quality, Feature extraction, Digital media.

This paper presents TensorFlow Lite Micro, a lightweight embedded machine learning framework designed for TinyML systems. The objective is to enable efficient deployment of machine learning models on resource-constrained devices, such as microcontrollers, with limited memory and computational capabilities. Our approach involves optimizing the TensorFlow Lite framework to achieve significant reductions in code size, memory usage, and latency, while maintaining accuracy and performance. We utilize a combination of quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation techniques to compress models, and develop a novel compiler-based approach to generate highly optimized machine code for microcontrollers. Experimental results demonstrate that TensorFlow Lite Micro achieves remarkable performance on various TinyML benchmarks, outperforming existing solutions in terms of inference speed, memory footprint, and energy efficiency. The implications of this research are significant, as it enables the widespread adoption of machine learning on edge devices, paving the way for innovative applications in areas such as IoT, robotics, and autonomous systems. Key contributions include the development of a highly optimized embedded ML framework, novel model compression techniques, and a compiler-based approach for generating efficient machine code. Relevant keywords: TensorFlow Lite Micro, TinyML, embedded machine learning, microcontrollers, model compression, edge AI.

We show how feature maps in convolutional networks are susceptible to spatial bias. Due to a combination of architectural choices, the activation at certain locations is systematically elevated or weakened. The major source of this bias is the padding mechanism. Depending on several aspects of convolution arithmetic, this mechanism can apply the padding unevenly, leading to asymmetries in the learned weights. We demonstrate how such bias can be detrimental to certain tasks such as small object detection: the activation is suppressed if the stimulus lies in the impacted area, leading to blind spots and misdetection. We propose solutions to mitigate spatial bias and demonstrate how they can improve model accuracy.

This paper surveys the recent advances in deep learning methodologies applied to automatic threat detection within X-ray security imaging. The objective is to provide a comprehensive overview of how deep learning techniques are addressing the challenges of identifying concealed weapons, explosives, and other prohibited items in baggage and cargo screening. We examine various deep learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and transformer-based architectures, analyzing their strengths and weaknesses in feature extraction, object detection, and classification accuracy within X-ray images. The survey encompasses studies that demonstrate enhanced detection rates, reduced false alarm rates, and improved processing times compared to traditional image processing methods. Furthermore, we discuss the impact of transfer learning, data augmentation, and adversarial training in improving the robustness and generalization capabilities of deep learning models for X-ray security. Finally, the paper highlights the limitations of current approaches, including challenges associated with limited datasets, domain adaptation, and the detection of novel threats. We conclude by outlining potential future research directions aimed at developing more effective and reliable automatic threat detection systems. Keywords: Deep Learning, X-ray Security Imaging, Threat Detection, Convolutional Neural Networks, Object Recognition, Airport Security.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown promise in skeleton-based action recognition by modeling the human skeleton as a graph. However, existing methods primarily focus on pairwise relationships between joints, neglecting higher-order dependencies crucial for understanding complex actions. This paper introduces a novel approach for fusing higher-order features within GNNs to enhance action recognition accuracy. Our method constructs hypergraphs to capture multi-joint relationships and propagates information using a hypergraph convolutional layer, effectively integrating these higher-order features into the GNN framework. We evaluate our approach on two benchmark datasets, NTU RGB+D and Kinetics Skeleton, demonstrating significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, our model achieves superior performance by effectively capturing complex spatio-temporal dependencies in human actions. This research highlights the importance of higher-order feature integration in GNNs for skeleton-based action recognition and provides a promising direction for future research. Keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Action Recognition, Skeleton Data, Hypergraphs, Higher-Order Features, Deep Learning.

We consider the challenging problem of zero-shot video object segmentation (VOS). That is, segmenting and tracking multiple moving objects within a video fully automatically, without any manual initialization. We treat this as a grouping problem by exploiting object proposals and making a joint inference about grouping over both space and time. We propose a network architecture for tractably performing proposal selection and joint grouping. Crucially, we then show how to train this network with reinforcement learning so that it learns to perform the optimal non-myopic sequence of grouping decisions to segment the whole video. Unlike standard supervised techniques, this also enables us to directly optimize for the non-differentiable overlap-based metrics used to evaluate VOS. We show that the proposed method, which we call ALBA outperforms the previous stateof-the-art on three benchmarks: DAVIS 2017 [2], FBMS [20] and Youtube-VOS [27].

This paper explores the trade-off between computational resources and output quality in neural sequence models, a crucial aspect of natural language processing and machine learning. The objective is to develop a framework that balances computation and quality, enabling efficient deployment of these models in resource-constrained environments. Our approach involves designing a novel adaptive computation method that dynamically allocates computational resources based on the input sequence and desired output quality. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves significant reductions in computational cost while maintaining competitive performance with state-of-the-art models. Key findings include a 30% decrease in inference time and a 25% reduction in memory usage, with only a minor degradation in output quality. The implications of this research are substantial, enabling the widespread adoption of neural sequence models in applications such as language translation, text summarization, and chatbots, where computational efficiency is critical. Our contributions include a new perspective on the computation-quality trade-off and a practical solution for controlling computational resources in neural sequence models, with potential applications in AI, machine learning, and NLP.

Our objective is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of NAS by introducing a novel selection strategy that leverages the differentiable nature of the search space. We propose a method that combines reinforcement learning with gradient-based optimization to identify the most promising architectures. Our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of computational cost and model performance, achieving state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets. The key findings of our research highlight the importance of carefully designing the architecture selection process in NAS, and demonstrate the potential of differentiable methods to accelerate the search for optimal neural architectures. Our work contributes to the advancement of NAS and has significant implications for the development of more efficient and scalable deep learning models, with potential applications in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and autonomous systems. Key keywords: Differentiable NAS, Architecture Selection, Reinforcement Learning, Gradient-based Optimization, Deep Learning.

Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are widely used for representing structured information, but reasoning over them remains a significant challenge due to their inherent complexity and sparsity. This paper introduces **Query2box**, a novel framework for reasoning over KGs in vector space using **box embeddings**. The primary objective of this work is to enable efficient and interpretable reasoning over complex logical queries, such as conjunctions, disjunctions, and existential quantifiers, by leveraging geometric representations. Query2box represents entities and queries as hyper-rectangles (boxes) in a continuous vector space, allowing for intuitive and scalable reasoning. The proposed approach employs a neural model to learn embeddings for entities and queries, enabling the system to handle multi-hop reasoning tasks effectively. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that Query2box outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and scalability, particularly for complex queries involving multiple logical operations. The framework also provides interpretable results by visualizing the geometric relationships between queries and entities. The key contribution of this research lies in its ability to bridge the gap between symbolic reasoning and neural-based approaches, offering a robust and efficient solution for querying KGs. Query2box has potential applications in areas such as recommendation systems, question answering, and semantic search, where reasoning over structured data is critical. **Keywords**: Knowledge Graphs, Box Embeddings, Logical Reasoning, Vector Space Models, Neural Networks, Query Processing.

This paper investigates the theoretical underpinnings of reinforcement learning (RL) in a constrained feedback environment, specifically focusing on the "once-per-episode" setting. In this scenario, the learning agent receives a single reward signal at the end of each episode, presenting a significant challenge for effective policy optimization. We develop a novel analytical framework to characterize the convergence properties of RL algorithms under such sparse feedback. Our analysis provides bounds on the sample complexity required to achieve near-optimal policies, considering factors like the state space size and reward structure. We introduce a modified Q-learning algorithm tailored for the once-per-episode setting and demonstrate its improved performance compared to standard RL approaches. Furthermore, we establish a connection between this learning problem and stochastic optimization with delayed feedback. The findings offer insights into the design of efficient RL strategies for real-world applications where immediate and frequent rewards are unavailable or impractical. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Sparse Rewards, Delayed Feedback, Sample Complexity, Q-learning, Stochastic Optimization.

The increasing volume of Vietnamese online text necessitates efficient methods for information extraction and summarization. Existing summarization techniques often struggle with the nuances of the Vietnamese language, particularly when dealing with multiple documents covering the same topic. This thesis addresses the challenge of generating concise and coherent summaries from multiple Vietnamese documents, a critical task for information retrieval, news aggregation, and knowledge management. This research aims to develop a novel Vietnamese multi-document summarization system. Specifically, the objectives are to (1) design a robust pre-processing pipeline for Vietnamese text, handling issues such as word segmentation and diacritics; (2) implement and evaluate various sentence scoring methods, incorporating both linguistic and semantic features specific to Vietnamese; (3) develop a redundancy removal algorithm to minimize overlapping information across sentences selected from different documents; and (4) construct a coherent summary by employing sentence ordering techniques. The proposed system utilizes a hybrid approach, combining statistical methods with deep learning techniques. We leverage transformer-based models, pre-trained on a large Vietnamese corpus, for semantic representation and sentence scoring. A graph-based algorithm is implemented for redundancy removal, and a Markov chain model is used to optimize sentence ordering based on discourse relations. The system is evaluated on a newly curated dataset of Vietnamese news articles covering diverse topics. The expected outcomes include a high-performing Vietnamese multi-document summarization system capable of generating informative and fluent summaries. This research contributes to the field by (1) providing a comprehensive framework for Vietnamese text summarization; (2) introducing novel sentence scoring and redundancy removal techniques tailored for Vietnamese; and (3) releasing a valuable dataset for future research in Vietnamese natural language processing. In conclusion, this thesis presents a novel approach to Vietnamese multi-document summarization, addressing the unique challenges posed by the language and the need for efficient information processing. Future work will focus on incorporating user feedback mechanisms and exploring the use of abstractive summarization techniques to further improve the quality and relevance of the generated summaries.

Accurate and timely building damage assessment following natural disasters is crucial for effective disaster response and humanitarian aid. This paper introduces BDANet, a novel multiscale convolutional neural network architecture enhanced with cross-directional attention mechanisms, designed for precise building damage assessment from satellite imagery. BDANet utilizes a multiscale feature extraction module to capture contextual information at varying resolutions, enabling robust identification of damage patterns. Furthermore, we introduce a cross-directional attention mechanism that adaptively weights feature maps in both spatial and channel dimensions, enhancing the network's ability to focus on damage-related features and suppress irrelevant background information. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that BDANet significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of precision, recall, and overall accuracy. The proposed approach offers a reliable and efficient solution for automated building damage assessment, contributing to improved disaster management and resource allocation. Keywords: building damage assessment, satellite imagery, convolutional neural network, multiscale feature extraction, attention mechanism, disaster response.

This paper addresses the problem of decision-making in environments characterized by feedback graphs and switching costs. In such settings, an agent receives rewards and feedback only from a subset of potential actions, governed by a directed feedback graph. The challenge is to optimize action selection while minimizing costs incurred when switching between actions. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel algorithm that effectively navigates the complexities introduced by feedback graphs and switching costs. Our approach integrates exploration-exploitation strategies typical of bandit problems with techniques that account for feedback graph structures. We designed a mechanism that ensures cost-efficient adaptation to changing graph dynamics while maintaining performance guarantees. Results/Findings: Through extensive simulations and theoretical analysis, the proposed algorithm demonstrates superior performance in reducing cumulative regret and switching costs compared to existing methods. Our findings highlight the efficiency of feedback graph insights in significantly mitigating the trade-offs between exploration and exploitation, even in dynamic environments. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a robust framework for understanding and addressing the intertwined challenges of feedback graphs and switching costs in bandit problems. The implications extend to practical applications like recommendation systems and adaptive control, where such constraints are prevalent. Our work not only advances theoretical knowledge but also lays the groundwork for future endeavors in complex decision-making problems involving structured feedback. Keywords: Bandits, feedback graphs, switching costs, exploration-exploitation, cumulative regret, adaptive decision-making.

This paper investigates the spectral properties underpinning the widely utilized word representation model, word2vec. It aims to enhance understanding of how word2vec’s architecture and training process facilitate effective natural language processing tasks, focusing on the spectral decomposition of the matrices utilized in the model. Methods: We explore the mathematical foundations of word2vec by leveraging techniques in spectral graph theory and linear algebra to dissect the inner workings of both Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW) and Skip-gram architectures. Emphasis is placed on analyzing eigenvalue distributions and eigenspace structures to provide insights into the embeddings' ability to capture semantic relationships. Results: Our analysis reveals that the spectral characteristics of word2vec embeddings explain their proficiency in preserving semantic similarities and relationships between words in the vector space. Specifically, the study uncovers how the dominant eigenspaces serve to enhance the positioning of synonymous words and highlight conjugate word pairs. Furthermore, comparative studies show that word2vec outperforms equivalent models in terms of capturing nuanced semantic meanings when evaluated using spectral analysis metrics. Conclusion: The spectral understanding of word2vec contributes significant theoretical clarity to its empirical effectiveness and offers promising directions for further optimization of word embeddings. These insights can pave the way for developing more robust, efficient models that harness spectral properties for improved semantic representation. Potential applications of this research extend to enhanced information retrieval systems, advanced language models, and the development of more interpretable AI systems. Keywords: word2vec, spectral graph theory, semantic embeddings, natural language processing, vector space, eigenvalues, eigenvectors.

Mục tiêu: đánh giá kết quả điều trị gãy kín xương bàn tay bằng nẹp vít tại Bệnh viện Đa khoa Lâm Đồng. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Tiến cứu mô tả loạt ca. Kết quả: 31 trường hợp gãy kín xương bàn tay được điều trị kết hợp xương bằng nẹp vít có tỷ lệ liền vết mổ kỳ đầu đạt 96,77%. Đánh giá kết quả theo Larson - Bostman: rất tốt là 93,55%, tốt 6,45%. Đánh giá kết quả phục hồi chức năng sau mổ theo Belsky: xuất sắc chiếm 80,65%, tốt chiếm 19,35%. Kết luận: sử dụng phương pháp kết hợp xương bằng nẹp vít đem lại hiệu quả cao trong điều trị cho bệnh nhân gãy kín xương bàn ngón tay, đạt được sự nắn chỉnh giải phẫu tốt, khả năng liền xương cao, phục hồi chức năng sớm, biến chứng thấp.

Thiên tai gây ra những tác động tiêu cực đến sản xuất nông nghiệp, làm giảm năng suất và chất lượng cây trồng, vật nuôi, gây thiệt hại về kinh tế cho người nông dân và ảnh hưởng đến an ninh lương thực. Các loại hình thiên tai thường gặp như hạn hán, lũ lụt, bão, xâm nhập mặn, dịch bệnh trên cây trồng và vật nuôi đều có thể gây ra những hậu quả nghiêm trọng. Để giảm thiểu tác động của thiên tai, cần có các biện pháp phòng ngừa và ứng phó hiệu quả. Các biện pháp này bao gồm việc xây dựng hệ thống cảnh báo sớm, nâng cao khả năng chống chịu của cây trồng và vật nuôi, áp dụng các kỹ thuật canh tác tiên tiến, bảo vệ nguồn nước, xây dựng cơ sở hạ tầng phòng chống thiên tai, và có chính sách hỗ trợ kịp thời cho người dân bị ảnh hưởng. Đồng thời, cần tăng cường công tác tuyên truyền, nâng cao nhận thức cho người dân về phòng chống thiên tai để chủ động ứng phó và giảm thiểu thiệt hại.

Việt Nam là nước có tỷ lệ người mang đột biến gen bệnh α-thalassemia cao, vì vậy việc sàng lọc người lành mang gen này của những cặp vợ chồng đã có một người mang đột biến gen gây bệnh là rất quan trọng để phòng tránh sinh con bị bệnh. Đột biến xóa đoạn chiếm tỷ lệ 92,1%, còn đột biến không xóa đoạn là 7,9%.

This paper proposes a novel approach to image super-resolution using a lightweight adaptive weighted learning network. The objective is to develop an efficient and effective method for enhancing low-resolution images while minimizing computational costs. Our approach employs a compact neural network architecture that adaptively assigns weights to different features, allowing for optimal information extraction and reconstruction. The network is trained using a unique loss function that balances reconstruction accuracy and feature importance. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM), while requiring significantly fewer parameters and computations. The proposed network achieves a balance between accuracy and efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications such as video enhancement and surveillance. Our contributions include a novel adaptive weighted learning mechanism and a lightweight network design, which collectively enable fast and high-quality image super-resolution. Key keywords: image super-resolution, lightweight neural networks, adaptive weighted learning, deep learning, computer vision.

Phân tích thực trạng và đề xuất giải pháp thực hiện phân cấp quản lý công trình thủy lợi là một vấn đề quan trọng trong lĩnh vực quản lý và phát triển công trình thủy lợi. Thực trạng hiện nay cho thấy sự phức tạp và chồng chéo trong quy trình quản lý, dẫn đến sự chậm trễ và lãng phí trong việc thực hiện các dự án. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, cần có một hệ thống quản lý phân cấp rõ ràng và hiệu quả. Hệ thống này cần được thiết kế để phân chia quyền hạn và trách nhiệm một cách rõ ràng giữa các cấp quản lý, từ cấp trung ương đến cấp địa phương. Điều này sẽ giúp tăng cường sự minh bạch và trách nhiệm trong quản lý, đồng thời giảm thiểu sự chồng chéo và chậm trễ. Một số giải pháp đề xuất bao gồm: - Tạo ra một hệ thống quản lý phân cấp rõ ràng và hiệu quả, với các cấp quản lý được phân chia một cách rõ ràng và có trách nhiệm. - Đảm bảo sự minh bạch và trách nhiệm trong quản lý, thông qua việc thực hiện các quy trình và thủ tục rõ ràng. - Tăng cường sự phối hợp và hợp tác giữa các cấp quản lý, để đảm bảo sự thống nhất và hiệu quả trong quản lý. - Đánh giá và phân tích thường xuyên tình hình quản lý, để kịp thời điều chỉnh và cải thiện hệ thống quản lý. Bằng cách thực hiện các giải pháp này, chúng ta có thể tạo ra một hệ thống quản lý phân cấp hiệu quả và minh bạch, giúp tăng cường sự phát triển và quản lý công trình thủy lợi.

Các thiết bị có thể điều khiển từ xa sử dụng sóng hồng ngoại là loại thiết bị quen thuộc với con người. Tuy nhiên, việc cất trữ từng loại điều khiển cho từng loại thiết bị có thể khiến việc sử dụng các thiết bị trở nên bất tiện. Cùng với đó, công nghệ phát triển sinh ra các yêu cầu nâng cao chất lượng cuộc sống, ví dụ như việc có thể điều khiển các thiết bị tại nhà "từ xa", mà việc sử dụng điều khiển trực tiếp kiểu truyền thống không đáp ứng được.

Identifying disease-associated genes is a critical challenge in bioinformatics, with significant implications for understanding disease mechanisms and developing targeted therapies. Traditional link prediction methods in gene-disease networks often overlook the nuanced relationships between genes and diseases, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper proposes a novel **Relation-weighted Link Prediction (RLP)** framework to enhance disease gene identification by incorporating weighted relational features into a graph-based model. The approach leverages a heterogeneous network integrating gene-gene interactions, gene-disease associations, and biological pathway data. A graph neural network (GNN) is employed to learn node embeddings, while a relation-weighting mechanism dynamically adjusts the importance of different edge types during prediction. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that RLP outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score. Key findings reveal that incorporating weighted relationships significantly improves the identification of both known and novel disease-associated genes. The proposed framework offers a robust and interpretable solution for advancing disease gene discovery, with potential applications in precision medicine and drug development. **Keywords**: disease gene identification, link prediction, graph neural networks, relation weighting, bioinformatics, heterogeneous networks.

Nghiên cứu về mật độ trồng chuối tiêu già Nam Mỹ trên đất dồn thửa, đổi ruộng tại Việt Nam đã chỉ ra rằng việc xác định mật độ trồng hợp lý là yếu tố quan trọng để tối ưu hóa năng suất và chất lượng quả. Thí nghiệm được thực hiện với nhiều mật độ khác nhau, từ thấp đến cao, nhằm đánh giá ảnh hưởng của chúng đến sự phát triển của cây, khả năng ra hoa, đậu quả và năng suất cuối cùng. Kết quả cho thấy mật độ trồng từ 1.200 đến 1.600 cây/ha mang lại hiệu quả tốt nhất, giúp cây phát triển khỏe mạnh, giảm thiểu cạnh tranh dinh dưỡng và ánh sáng. Nghiên cứu cũng nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc áp dụng các biện pháp canh tác phù hợp để cải thiện điều kiện sinh trưởng cho giống chuối này, từ đó góp phần nâng cao thu nhập cho nông dân và phát triển bền vững ngành trồng chuối tại địa phương.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc phân tích ảnh hưởng của điện áp do sét gây ra và đề xuất các biện pháp giảm thiểu tổn thất điện năng trên đường dây tải điện trên không đôi. Các yếu tố như cường độ dòng sét, vị trí sét đánh và cấu hình đường dây được xem xét để đánh giá mức độ điện áp cảm ứng. Kết quả cho thấy rằng việc sử dụng dây chống sét, khoảng cách pha hợp lý và nối đất hiệu quả có thể giảm đáng kể điện áp cảm ứng và giảm thiểu tổn thất điện năng. Bên cạnh đó, việc áp dụng các thiết bị bảo vệ như van chống sét và thiết bị cắt sét cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc bảo vệ hệ thống khỏi các xung điện áp quá mức. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp những hiểu biết sâu sắc về các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến điện áp cảm ứng do sét và đề xuất các giải pháp thiết thực để cải thiện độ tin cậy và hiệu quả của hệ thống truyền tải điện.

Đề cập đến vùng Tứ giác Long Xuyên, một khu vực trọng điểm về sản xuất lúa của Việt Nam, việc xây dựng đê bao ngăn lũ đã mang lại nhiều lợi ích cho nông nghiệp và bảo vệ môi trường. Tuy nhiên, sự thay đổi cơ cấu mùa vụ cũng đã dẫn đến sự thay đổi về thời gian và phương thức sản xuất lúa, ảnh hưởng đến đời sống của người nông dân. Cụ thể, việc xây dựng đê bao ngăn lũ đã giúp tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho việc sản xuất lúa mùa, nhưng cũng đã dẫn đến sự thay đổi về thời gian và phương thức sản xuất lúa mùa. Điều này đã ảnh hưởng đến đời sống của người nông dân, đặc biệt là những người phụ thuộc vào sản xuất lúa mùa. Bên cạnh đó, sự thay đổi cơ cấu mùa vụ cũng đã dẫn đến sự thay đổi về hệ sinh thái và môi trường. Việc sản xuất lúa mùa trên diện rộng đã dẫn đến sự thay đổi về hệ sinh thái và môi trường, ảnh hưởng đến đa dạng sinh học và chất lượng nước. Tổng kết lại, việc xây dựng đê bao ngăn lũ đã mang lại nhiều lợi ích cho nông nghiệp và bảo vệ môi trường, nhưng cũng đã gây ra một số ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến đời sống của người nông dân và hệ sinh thái. Liều lượng phân kali vi lượng có ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến sinh trưởng, phát triển và năng suất của cây trồng. This paper addresses a crucial challenge in deep reinforcement learning (DRL): the dependency on online exploration to collect new experiences for efficient learning. We propose a novel off-policy DRL framework that eliminates the need for traditional exploration strategies by leveraging existing datasets of agent-environment interactions. Our approach utilizes an advanced policy evaluation and improvement mechanism that learns directly from fixed, offline trajectories, ensuring robust policy optimization without additional environment sampling. We introduce architectural and algorithmic adaptations to mitigate distributional shift and overestimation bias, which commonly hinder off-policy learning in the absence of exploration. Through comprehensive experiments on benchmark environments, our method demonstrates superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art algorithms that rely on explicit exploration, while significantly reducing sample complexity and training time. These results highlight the viability of learning effective policies from static data, broadening the applicability of DRL to domains where exploration is costly, unsafe, or infeasible. Our contributions lay the foundation for efficient and reliable reinforcement learning in real-world scenarios using only prior data. Key keywords: deep reinforcement learning, off-policy learning, offline RL, exploration-free, policy optimization, sample efficiency.

Despite the growing prominence of generative adversarial networks (GANs), optimization in GANs is still a poorly understood topic. In this paper, we analyze the "gradient descent" form of GAN optimization i.e., the natural setting where we simultaneously take small gradient steps in both generator and discriminator parameters. We show that even though GAN optimization does not correspond to a convex-concave game (even for simple parameterizations), under proper conditions, equilibrium points of this optimization procedure are still for the traditional GAN formulation. On the other hand, we show that the recently proposed Wasserstein GAN can have non-convergent limit cycles near equilibrium. Motivated by this stability analysis, we propose an additional regularization term for gradient descent GAN updates, which able to guarantee local stability for both the WGAN and the traditional GAN, and also shows practical promise in speeding up convergence and addressing mode collapse.

Real-world object detection is highly desired to be equipped with the learning expandability that can enlarge its detection classes incrementally. Moreover, such learning from only few annotated training samples further adds the flexibility for the object detector, which is highly expected in many applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, etc. However, such sequential learning scenario with few-shot training samples generally causes catastrophic forgetting and dramatic overfitting. In this paper, to address the above incremental few-shot learning issues, a novel Incremental Few-Shot Object Detection (iFSOD) method is proposed to enable the effective continual learning from few-shot samples. Specifically, a Double-Branch Framework (DBF) is proposed to decouple the feature representation of base and novel (few-shot) class, which facilitates both the old-knowledge retention and new-class adaption simultaneously. Furthermore, a progressive model updating rule is carried out to preserve the long-term memory on old classes effectively when adapt to sequential new classes. Moreover, an inter-task class separation loss is proposed to extend the decision region of new-coming classes for better feature discrimination. We conduct experiments on both Pascal VOC and MS-COCO, which demonstrate that our method can effectively solve the problem of incremental few-shot detection and significantly improve the detection accuracy on both base and novel classes.

Many deep learning based 3D face reconstruction methods have been proposed recently, however, few of them have applications in games. Current game character customization systems either require players to manually adjust considerable face attributes to obtain the desired face, or have limited freedom of facial shape and texture. In this paper, we propose an automatic character face creation method that predicts both facial shape and texture from a single portrait, and it can be integrated into most existing 3D games. Although 3D Morphable Face Model (3DMM) based methods can restore accurate 3D faces from single images, the topology of 3DMM mesh is different from the meshes used in most games. To acquire fidelity texture, existing methods require a large amount of face texture data for training, while building such datasets is time-consuming and laborious. Besides, such a dataset collected under laboratory conditions may not generalized well to in-the-wild situations. To tackle these problems, we propose 1) a low-cost facial texture acquisition method, 2) a shape transfer algorithm that can transform the shape of a 3DMM mesh to games, and 3) a new pipeline for training 3D game face reconstruction networks. The proposed method not only can produce detailed and vivid game characters similar to the input portrait, but can also eliminate the influence of lighting and occlusions. Experiments show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods used in games.

Truy xuất nguồn gốc dầu tràn là một vấn đề cấp bách trong bảo vệ môi trường và an toàn sinh thái. Objective: Semi-supervised regression methods that effectively leverage unlabeled data remain underexplored, especially in contexts where predictive uncertainty is critical. This paper introduces a novel framework—Semi-supervised Deep Kernel Learning (SS-DKL)—that integrates Gaussian process regression (GPR) with deep feature embeddings and a variance-minimization objective to exploit unlabeled inputs. Methods: SS-DKL first maps inputs through a deep neural network to learn task-specific representations. A Gaussian process equipped with a parameterized kernel operates on these embeddings for regression. To incorporate unlabeled data, we introduce a regularizer that minimizes the predictive variance of the GPR on unlabeled samples, encouraging the model to form confident predictions where labels are unavailable. The overall loss combines the standard marginal likelihood on labeled data with the variance-minimization term, optimized end-to-end via stochastic gradient descent. Results: We evaluate SS-DKL on multiple benchmark datasets, including UCI regression tasks and real-world sensor data. Compared to fully supervised deep kernel learning and conventional semi-supervised baselines (self-training, consistency regularization), SS-DKL achieves up to a 15% reduction in root mean square error (RMSE) and demonstrates significantly lower predictive uncertainty on out-of-distribution inputs. Conclusion: By explicitly minimizing predictive variance on unlabeled samples, SS-DKL bridges representation learning and uncertainty quantification in regression. This approach offers a principled path to improve prediction accuracy and reliability in applications such as environmental monitoring and robotics, where labeled data are scarce but confidence estimates are essential. Keywords: semi-supervised learning; deep kernel learning; Gaussian process regression; predictive variance; representation learning; unlabeled data.

Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) images from low-resolution (LR) inputs. Deep learning-based SISR methods have achieved impressive performance but often require complex and computationally expensive models. This paper introduces a novel approach, Contrastive Self-Distillation (CSD), designed to achieve compact SISR models without sacrificing performance. CSD leverages a contrastive loss to encourage the student network to learn feature representations that are discriminative, while simultaneously employing self-distillation to transfer knowledge from a larger teacher network. This allows for training of smaller student networks that retain the performance of their larger counterparts. Experiments demonstrate that CSD achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art SISR methods, while significantly reducing model size and computational complexity. Specifically, our compact models achieve comparable or superior results with up to 50% fewer parameters. The proposed method offers a practical solution for deploying SISR models on resource-constrained devices. Keywords: Super-Resolution, Self-Distillation, Contrastive Learning, Model Compression, Deep Learning.

This paper presents a transfer learning approach for melanoma detection, developed for participation in the ISIC 2017 Skin Lesion Classification Challenge. Our method leverages pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs), specifically VGG16 and ResNet50, fine-tuned on the ISIC 2017 dataset. The objective was to improve classification accuracy in distinguishing melanoma from benign skin lesions. We explored various fine-tuning strategies, including layer freezing and unfreezing, as well as data augmentation techniques to mitigate the limited size of the training dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that transfer learning significantly outperformed training CNNs from scratch. Specifically, our ensemble model, combining VGG16 and ResNet50 predictions, achieved a competitive performance on the ISIC 2017 challenge validation set. The findings suggest that transfer learning is an effective strategy for melanoma detection when dealing with limited medical image datasets. This research contributes to the application of deep learning in dermatological diagnosis and highlights the potential of pre-trained models in skin lesion classification. **Keywords:** Melanoma Detection, Transfer Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, ISIC 2017, Skin Lesion Classification, Deep Learning, Image Analysis.

This paper addresses the challenge of discovering meaningful temporal abstractions, known as Eigenoptions, in reinforcement learning (RL) environments. Eigenoptions are options that align with the principal components of the environment's transition dynamics, enabling efficient exploration and hierarchical decision-making. We propose a novel approach leveraging the Deep Successor Representation (DSR) to automatically discover Eigenoptions without prior knowledge of the environment's structure. Our method combines the representational power of deep neural networks with the theoretical foundations of successor representations to identify and encode the intrinsic structure of the environment. Experiments conducted on grid-world and continuous control benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of exploration efficiency and task performance. The results highlight the potential of Eigenoptions for improving sample efficiency and scalability in complex RL tasks. This work contributes to advancing hierarchical RL by providing a data-driven framework for discovering reusable temporal abstractions, with implications for applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and beyond. **Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Eigenoptions, Deep Successor Representation, Temporal Abstractions, Hierarchical RL, Exploration.

The study aims to address the challenge of accurate and efficient leaf recognition, a crucial task in botanical sciences, by leveraging the potential of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction to improve classification performance. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel methodology utilizing convolutional neural networks to automatically extract discriminative features from leaf images for classification purposes. The approach involves training CNN models on a large dataset of leaf images, enabling the model to learn intricate patterns and morphological details characteristic of different leaf species. The extracted features are then fed into a classification algorithm to perform species identification. Results/Findings: Our experimental evaluation demonstrates that the CNN-based feature extraction significantly outperforms traditional hand-crafted feature methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed system achieved a high recognition rate across various leaf types, demonstrating robustness against variations in lighting, orientation, and scaling. Comparative studies with existing techniques show a notable improvement in classification accuracy, confirming the efficacy of the convolutional feature extraction approach. Conclusion/Implications: The research contributes a powerful and automated solution for leaf recognition using CNN-derived features, offering a significant advancement over traditional methods that rely on manual feature engineering. The implications of this work extend to enhanced botanical research, biodiversity monitoring, and ecological studies, facilitating rapid and accurate plant species identification. Future work will explore scaling the model to accommodate an even broader range of plant species and improving real-time processing capabilities. Keywords: leaf recognition, convolutional neural networks, CNN, feature extraction, botanical sciences, plant species identification.

This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing the resolution of brain MRI images, a critical task for improving diagnostic accuracy and enabling detailed analysis in medical imaging. We propose a novel super-resolution framework that leverages overcomplete dictionaries and nonlocal similarity to reconstruct high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. The approach combines sparse representation techniques with nonlocal self-similarity priors, enabling the capture of intricate structural details and textures inherent in brain MRI data. The overcomplete dictionary is learned from high-resolution training patches, while nonlocal similarity ensures the preservation of global structural consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing super-resolution techniques in terms of both quantitative metrics (e.g., PSNR and SSIM) and visual quality. The framework achieves significant improvements in edge sharpness, texture clarity, and artifact reduction, making it highly suitable for clinical applications. This research contributes to the field of medical image processing by introducing a robust and efficient super-resolution method that enhances the utility of MRI data for diagnosis and research. Key innovations include the integration of overcomplete dictionaries with nonlocal similarity, offering a scalable and adaptable solution for various imaging modalities. **Keywords**: Super-resolution, MRI, overcomplete dictionaries, nonlocal similarity, sparse representation, medical imaging.

3D human pose estimation (HPE) is crucial in many fields, such as human behavior analysis, augmented reality/virtual reality (AR/VR) applications, and self-driving industry. Videos that contain multiple potentially occluded people captured from freely moving monocular cameras are very common in real-world scenarios, while 3D HPE for such scenarios is quite challenging, partially because there is a lack of such data with accurate 3D ground truth labels in existing datasets. In this paper, we propose a temporal regression network with a gated convolution module to transform 2D joints to 3D and recover the missing occluded joints in the meantime. A simple yet effective localization approach is further conducted to transform the normalized pose to the global trajectory. To verify the effectiveness of our approach, we also collect a new moving camera multi-human (MMHuman) dataset that includes multiple people with heavy occlusion captured by moving cameras. The 3D ground truth joints are provided by accurate motion capture (MoCap) system. From the experiments on static-camera based Human3.6M data and our own collected moving-camera based data, we show that our proposed method outperforms most state-of-the-art 2D-to-3D pose estimation methods, especially for the scenarios with heavy occlusions.

Monocular depth estimation in indoor environments is a crucial task for various applications, including robot navigation, augmented reality, and 3D scene understanding. Existing supervised methods require extensive and expensive ground truth depth data. This paper presents MonoIndoor, a self-supervised monocular depth estimation framework specifically tailored for indoor scenes, aiming to establish good training practices and improve depth estimation accuracy. Our approach leverages a novel loss weighting strategy that dynamically adjusts the contribution of photometric and geometric losses based on scene characteristics, mitigating the impact of occlusion and texture-less regions. Furthermore, we introduce an improved data augmentation pipeline that enhances the robustness of the model to variations in lighting and viewpoint. Experimental results on benchmark indoor datasets demonstrate that MonoIndoor achieves state-of-the-art performance among self-supervised methods, significantly reducing depth error and improving structural similarity. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component of our framework. The proposed method offers a practical and effective solution for monocular depth estimation in indoor environments without relying on ground truth depth data. Keywords: Monocular Depth Estimation, Self-Supervised Learning, Indoor Scene Understanding, Computer Vision, Deep Learning.

This paper presents novel advancements in visual vehicle pose and shape estimation through the development of DirectShape, an innovative technique that leverages direct photometric alignment of shape priors. The primary goal is to enhance the accuracy and reliability of vehicle pose and shape determinations in various imaging conditions. Methods/Approach: DirectShape employs a direct photometric alignment strategy that integrates shape priors into the estimation process. By aligning these priors with image data, our approach efficiently captures both pose and shape variations without relying extensively on feature detection. The method utilizes optimization techniques to ensure a robust alignment of 3D shape models to real-world images, supporting the modeling of various vehicle types and conditions. Results/Findings: The experimental evaluation demonstrates that DirectShape significantly outperforms traditional feature-based methods in accuracy and robustness, particularly in challenging visual environments. Comparative analysis with existing approaches shows superior performance in both pose and shape estimation tasks, with our method maintaining high precision even in low-texture or poorly lit settings. The technique's ability to adapt to different vehicle types and mitigate noise further underscores its effectiveness. Conclusion/Implications: DirectShape contributes to the field of visual vehicle analysis by introducing a reliable, direct photometric-based methodology for vehicle pose and shape estimation. Its application is highly relevant for autonomous driving systems, traffic monitoring, and simulation environments. This work not only fills existing gaps in current methodologies but also sets a foundation for future advancements in visual recognition technologies. Keywords: vehicle pose estimation, shape priors, direct photometric alignment, 3D shape models, visual vehicle analysis, autonomous driving.

We present a technique for efficiently synthesizing images of atmospheric clouds using a combination of Monte Carlo integration and neural networks. The intricacies of Lorenz-Mie scattering and the high albedo of cloud-forming aerosols make rendering of clouds---e.g. the characteristic silverlining and the "whiteness" of the inner body---challenging for methods based solely on Monte Carlo integration or diffusion theory. We approach the problem differently. Instead of simulating all light transport during rendering, we pre-learn the spatial and directional distribution of radiant flux from tens of cloud exemplars. To render a new scene, we sample visible points of the cloud and, for each, extract a hierarchical 3D descriptor of the cloud geometry with respect to the shading location and the light source. The descriptor is input to a deep neural network that predicts the radiance function for each shading configuration. We make the key observation that progressively feeding the hierarchical descriptor into the network enhances the network's ability to learn faster and predict with high accuracy while using few coefficients. We also employ a block design with residual connections to further improve performance. A GPU implementation of our method synthesizes images of clouds that are nearly indistinguishable from the reference solution within seconds interactively. Our method thus represents a viable solution for applications such as cloud design and, thanks to its temporal stability, also for high-quality production of animated content.

Robustness is important for sequential decision making in a stochastic dynamic environment with uncertain probabilistic parameters. We address the problem of using robust MDPs (RMDPs) to compute policies with provable worst-case guarantees in reinforcement learning. The quality and robustness of an RMDP solution is determined by its ambiguity set. Existing methods construct ambiguity sets that lead to impractically conservative solutions. In this paper, we propose RSVF, which achieves less conservative solutions with the same worst-case guarantees by 1) leveraging a Bayesian prior, 2) optimizing the size and location of the ambiguity set, and, most importantly, 3) relaxing the requirement that the set is a confidence interval. Our theoretical analysis shows the safety of RSVF, and the empirical results demonstrate its practical promise.

Recent reinforcement learning algorithms, though achieving impressive results in various fields, suffer from brittle training effects such as regression in results and high sensitivity to initialization and parameters. We claim that some of the brittleness stems from variance differences, i.e. when different environment areas - states and/or actions - have different rewards variance. This causes two problems: First, the "Boring Areas Trap" in algorithms such as Q-learning, where moving between areas depends on the current area variance, and getting out of a boring area is hard due to its low variance. Second, the "Manipulative Consultant" problem, when value-estimation functions used in DQN and Actor-Critic algorithms influence the agent to prefer boring areas, regardless of the mean rewards return, as they maximize estimation precision rather than rewards. This sheds a new light on how exploration contribute to training, as it helps with both challenges. Cognitive experiments in humans showed that noised reward signals may paradoxically improve performance. We explain this using the two mentioned problems, claiming that both humans and algorithms may share similar challenges. Inspired by this result, we propose the Adaptive Symmetric Reward Noising (ASRN), by which we mean adding Gaussian noise to rewards according to their states' estimated variance, thus avoiding the two problems while not affecting the environment's mean rewards behavior. We conduct our experiments in a Multi Armed Bandit problem with variance differences. Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown promise in medical image analysis, particularly for diffuse lung disease (DLD) classification. This paper introduces a novel two-stage feature transfer approach to analyze and enhance feature representation in CNNs for DLD classification. In the first stage, features from a pre-trained CNN model are transferred to a target CNN model to initialize the weights and accelerate training. The second stage involves a refined feature transfer strategy that selectively transfers high-level features based on their relevance to DLD classification, assessed using a feature importance metric. Experiments on a publicly available DLD dataset demonstrate that the proposed two-stage transfer approach improves classification accuracy compared to training from scratch and single-stage transfer learning methods. Specifically, the proposed method achieves a 5% improvement in average F1-score. Furthermore, visualization of the learned feature maps reveals that the two-stage approach enables the network to focus on disease-specific regions within the lung images. This research provides a valuable framework for understanding and improving feature representation in CNNs for medical image analysis, with potential implications for computer-aided diagnosis of DLDs. Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network, Feature Transfer, Medical Image Analysis, Diffuse Lung Disease, Classification, Deep Learning.

MeanShift is a popular mode-seeking clustering algorithm used in a wide range of applications in machine learning. However, it is known to be prohibitively slow, with quadratic runtime per iteration. We propose MeanShift++, an extremely fast mode-seeking algorithm based on MeanShift that uses a grid-based approach to speed up the mean shift step, replacing the computationally expensive neighbors search with a density-weighted mean of adjacent grid cells. In addition, we show that this grid-based technique for density estimation comes with theoretical guarantees. The runtime is linear in the number of points and exponential in dimension, which makes MeanShift++ ideal on low-dimensional applications such as image segmentation and object tracking. We provide extensive experimental analysis showing that MeanShift++ can be more than 10,000x faster than MeanShift with competitive clustering results on benchmark datasets and nearly identical image segmentations as MeanShift. Finally, we show promising results for object tracking.

Key keywords: deep learning, denoising, self-supervised learning, blind spot regularization, convolutional neural networks (CNNs).

Our approach utilizes a combination of generative adversarial networks and few-shot learning techniques to learn domain-agnostic representations of images. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in various cross-domain image manipulation tasks, including converting daytime images to nighttime, and transforming sketches into photorealistic images. Our findings show significant improvements over existing methods, both in terms of visual quality and user experience. The proposed technique has far-reaching implications for applications such as image editing, computer vision, and robotics, and contributes to the growing field of cross-domain learning and image manipulation. Key keywords: cross-domain learning, image manipulation, demonstration-based learning, deep learning, generative adversarial networks, few-shot learning.

Human pose estimation has become a critical task in computer vision for applications ranging from augmented reality to human-computer interaction. This paper addresses the challenges of improving accuracy and efficiency in pose estimation by introducing a novel knowledge-guided deep fractal neural network architecture. Methods/Approach: The proposed method leverages fractal neural networks, characterized by their recursive and self-similar structures, to enhance feature extraction capabilities. The model is further augmented with knowledge-guided mechanisms that incorporate prior domain knowledge, refining network predictions and improving accuracy. Advanced training techniques, including data augmentation and multi-scale analysis, are employed to optimize network performance. Results/Findings: Experiments demonstrate that the knowledge-guided deep fractal neural network outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in various benchmark datasets for human pose estimation. Key findings indicate significant improvements in pose accuracy and processing speed. The network's innovative architecture significantly reduces computational overhead without compromising prediction quality, illustrating its potential for real-time applications. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel approach to human pose estimation by integrating fractal neural networks and domain knowledge, offering a unique balance of efficiency and accuracy. The methodology provides significant advancements in computer vision, with potential applications extending to robotics, surveillance, and health monitoring systems. Future work could explore the integration of additional contextual information and the application of this approach to other complex pattern recognition tasks. Keywords: Human Pose Estimation, Deep Fractal Neural Networks, Knowledge-Guided Mechanisms, Computer Vision, Feature Extraction, Real-Time Applications.

This paper proposes a novel Multi-Graph Convolutional-Recurrent Neural Network (MGC-RNN) model for short-term forecasting of transit passenger flow. The objective is to accurately predict passenger flow in transit systems, addressing the challenges of complex spatial and temporal dependencies. Our approach combines graph convolutional networks to capture spatial relationships between stations and recurrent neural networks to model temporal patterns. The MGC-RNN model is trained on historical passenger flow data and evaluates its performance on real-world datasets. The results show significant improvements in forecasting accuracy compared to existing methods, with a reduction in mean absolute error of up to 15%. The key contributions of this research include the integration of graph convolutional and recurrent neural networks for passenger flow forecasting, and the ability to handle multi-graph structures representing different transit modes. This study has important implications for transit agencies and smart city applications, enabling more efficient management and optimization of transit systems. Key keywords: graph convolutional networks, recurrent neural networks, passenger flow forecasting, transit systems, smart cities, deep learning.

**Abstract:** Incremental sequence learning addresses the challenge of continuously acquiring knowledge from evolving sequential data without forgetting previously learned information. This paper proposes a novel framework for incremental sequence learning that enables adaptive model updates as new data arrives, minimizing catastrophic forgetting and enhancing generalization. Leveraging a combination of recurrent neural networks and memory replay mechanisms, our approach dynamically integrates new sequences while preserving the integrity of prior learning. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets, including text and time-series prediction tasks, demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms standard sequential learning and static models in terms of both accuracy and retention of prior knowledge. Key advantages include efficient utilization of computational resources and scalability to large, streaming datasets. The findings highlight the applicability of incremental sequence learning to real-world scenarios such as continuous language modeling, online forecasting, and adaptive control systems. This research contributes a robust solution to incremental learning within sequential domains and provides insights for future developments in lifelong learning, neural architectures, and efficient data adaptation. **Keywords:** incremental learning, sequence modeling, recurrent neural networks, memory replay, catastrophic forgetting, continual learning, adaptive systems.

Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using wearable sensor data has gained significant attention due to its applications in healthcare, fitness tracking, and smart environments. This paper presents a novel machine learning-based approach to improve the accuracy and efficiency of HAR systems. The proposed method leverages data from wearable sensors, such as accelerometers and gyroscopes, to classify a wide range of human activities. Unlike traditional approaches, our model integrates a hybrid architecture combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for temporal pattern analysis. This dual-stream framework enables the system to capture both short-term and long-term dependencies in sensor data. Experiments were conducted on publicly available datasets, and the results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of classification accuracy and computational efficiency. Key findings include a 15% improvement in accuracy compared to state-of-the-art models and a 20% reduction in inference time. The study highlights the potential of this approach for real-time applications, such as personalized health monitoring and assistive technologies. This research contributes to the field by introducing a scalable and robust solution for HAR, paving the way for future advancements in wearable technology and machine learning integration. **Keywords**: Human Activity Recognition, Wearable Sensors, Machine Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, Real-Time Applications.

Tokenizer model In the section on Vietnamese tokenizer models, there are various types of tokenizersthat can be used for processing Vietnamese text: word-level tokenization, syllable level tokenization, character-level tokenization or sub-word level tokenization. The current state-of-the-art method: BPE (Byte Pair Encoding) . The drawback of character-level or word-level tokenization are that the tokens are sometimes not meaningful when considered independently or do not hanlde out-of-vocabulary cases well. Therefore, a novel method called BPE was proposed and has the ability to split words into subword units that are smaller than words but larger than individual characters. By applying BPE, most words can be represented by subwords, reducing the occurrence of the <unk> token that represents unseen words. This method has been rapidly adopted in modern NLP approaches and improved the accuracy significantly.

This study addresses the challenges of manual-label dependency in 3D object detection systems, proposing a novel approach that leverages an open-source simulation environment for training and validation. The research aims to reduce the labor-intensive process of manual annotation in 3D datasets while enhancing detection accuracy and efficiency. Methods: The proposed system integrates a realistic simulation platform that generates synthetic data to train 3D detection models. By employing advanced algorithms in computer vision and machine learning, the simulator replicates diverse real-world scenarios and object interactions, eliminating the need for manually labeled datasets. The utilization of domain adaptation techniques ensures the synthesized data is transferable to real-world applications. Results: Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the simulator-trained models achieve competitive performance, comparable to those trained on traditional manually-labeled datasets. Significant improvements in training efficiency and model scalability were observed. The results also show effective generalization across various environments and object types, with reduced computational overhead. Conclusion: This research contributes to the field of 3D detection by providing an innovative, cost-effective method for model training without manual labeling. The open-source simulator offers a scalable platform for further research and application in areas such as autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. By eliminating the dependence on labor-intensive labeling processes, this approach has the potential to accelerate advancements in 3D detection technologies. Keywords: 3D Detection, Open-Source Simulator, Manual-Label Free, Synthetic Data, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Autonomous Driving, Robotics.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of cell population segmentation techniques in phase contrast microscopy images. The objective is to provide an overview of existing methods and identify challenges in segmenting cell populations from phase contrast microscopy images. Various approaches, including traditional image processing, machine learning, and deep learning-based methods, are discussed. The results show that deep learning-based techniques, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved state-of-the-art performance in cell population segmentation. The survey highlights the importance of image preprocessing, feature extraction, and post-processing in improving segmentation accuracy. The conclusion emphasizes the potential applications of accurate cell population segmentation in biomedical research, disease diagnosis, and drug development. Key contributions of this survey include a thorough analysis of existing methods, identification of challenges, and suggestions for future research directions. Relevant keywords: phase contrast microscopy, cell population segmentation, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, image processing, biomedical imaging.

We present GATSBI, a generative model that can transform a sequence of raw observations into a structured latent representation that fully captures the spatio-temporal context of the agent's actions. In vision-based decision-making scenarios, an agent faces complex high-dimensional observations where multiple entities interact with each other. The agent requires a good scene representation of the visual observation that discerns essential components and consistently propagates along the time horizon. Our method, GATSBI, utilizes unsupervised object-centric scene representation learning to separate an active agent, static background, and passive objects. GATSBI then models the interactions reflecting the causal relationships among decomposed entities and predicts physically plausible future states. Our model generalizes to a variety of environments where different types of robots and objects dynamically interact with each other. We show GATSBI achieves superior performance on scene decomposition and video prediction compared to its state-of-the-art counterparts.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào khả năng hấp phụ ion chì Pb2+ trong môi trường nước bằng diatomite tự nhiên và diatomite biến tính. Diatomite, một loại đá trầm tích sinh học chứa thành phần chính là silica, được đánh giá về tiềm năng xử lý ô nhiễm kim loại nặng. Quá trình biến tính nhằm cải thiện khả năng hấp phụ của vật liệu. Các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến hiệu quả hấp phụ như pH, thời gian tiếp xúc, nồng độ chì ban đầu và liều lượng diatomite được xem xét và tối ưu hóa. Kết quả cho thấy diatomite biến tính có khả năng hấp phụ chì cao hơn so với diatomite tự nhiên. Nghiên cứu cung cấp cơ sở khoa học cho việc ứng dụng diatomite, đặc biệt là diatomite biến tính, như một vật liệu hấp phụ hiệu quả và thân thiện với môi trường để loại bỏ chì khỏi nguồn nước bị ô nhiễm, góp phần bảo vệ sức khỏe cộng đồng và môi trường sinh thái. Hướng nghiên cứu này mở ra tiềm năng khai thác và sử dụng rộng rãi nguồn tài nguyên diatomite sẵn có trong xử lý ô nhiễm môi trường.

Membrane proteins play a critical role in cellular functions, yet their complex architecture poses significant challenges for structural prediction and analysis. This study addresses the problem of accurately modeling membrane protein structures by leveraging Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), a probabilistic graphical model well-suited for capturing dependencies in sequential and spatial data. We propose a novel CRF-based framework that integrates sequence information, evolutionary conservation, and physicochemical properties to predict transmembrane helices and their orientations. Our approach employs a hybrid training strategy, combining labeled experimental data with unsupervised learning to enhance generalization across diverse protein families. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 12% improvement in prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art techniques, particularly in identifying low-homology membrane proteins. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robustness in handling ambiguous regions and outperforms existing methods in computational efficiency. The findings highlight the potential of CRFs in advancing structural biology, offering a scalable and interpretable solution for membrane protein analysis. This research contributes to the broader understanding of protein architecture and has implications for drug discovery and bioengineering, where accurate structural models are essential. **Keywords**: Membrane proteins, Conditional Random Fields, structural prediction, transmembrane helices, bioinformatics, computational biology.
