This paper introduces a novel approach to optimizing graph representations for machine learning (ML) compilers, leveraging transferable graph optimizers. The objective is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of ML model compilation by developing optimizers that can be applied across various graph structures and ML models. Our approach employs a combination of graph neural networks and reinforcement learning to learn transferable optimization policies. The results show that our method outperforms existing optimization techniques, achieving significant reductions in compilation time and improvements in model accuracy. The key findings highlight the importance of transferability in graph optimization, enabling the development of more efficient and adaptable ML compilers. This research contributes to the advancement of ML compilation and has potential applications in areas such as edge AI, autonomous systems, and real-time inference. Key keywords: graph optimization, ML compilers, transfer learning, graph neural networks, reinforcement learning.

Several machine learning problems arising in natural language processing can be modeled as a sequence labeling problem. We provide Gaussian process models based on pseudo-likelihood approximation to perform sequence labeling. Gaussian processes (GPs) provide a Bayesian approach to learning in a kernel based framework. The pseudo-likelihood model enables one to capture long range dependencies among the output components of the sequence without becoming computationally intractable. We use an efficient variational Gaussian approximation method to perform inference in the proposed model. We also provide an iterative algorithm which can effectively make use of the information from the neighboring labels to perform prediction. The ability to capture long range dependencies makes the proposed approach useful for a wide range of sequence labeling problems. Numerical experiments on some sequence labeling data sets demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed approach.

Recent years have seen stagnating improvements to branch predictor (BP) efficacy and a dearth of fresh ideas in branch predictor design, calling for fresh thinking in this area. This paper argues that looking at BP from the viewpoint of Reinforcement Learning (RL) facilitates systematic reasoning about, and exploration of, BP designs. We describe how to apply the RL formulation to branch predictors, show that existing predictors can be succinctly expressed in this formulation, and study two RL-based variants of conventional BPs.

Recent work on exploration in reinforcement learning (RL) has led to a series of increasingly complex solutions to the problem. This increase in complexity often comes at the expense of generality. Recent empirical studies suggest that, when applied to a broader set of domains, some sophisticated exploration methods are outperformed by simpler counterparts, such as -greedy. In this paper we propose an exploration algorithm that retains the simplicity of -greedy while reducing dithering. We build on a simple hypothesis: the main limitation of -greedy exploration is its lack of temporal persistence, which limits its ability to escape local optima. We propose a temporally extended form of -greedy that simply repeats the sampled action for a random duration. It turns out that, for many duration distributions, this suffices to improve exploration on a large set of domains. Interestingly, a class of distributions inspired by ecological models of animal foraging behaviour yields particularly strong performance.

The objective of this research is to address the limitations in video object segmentation by introducing a novel method called Sparse Spatiotemporal Transformers for Video Object Segmentation (SSTVOS). Video object segmentation remains a challenging task due to the need for precise tracking and delineation of objects over time. Our approach leverages the power of transformers combined with sparse spatiotemporal representation to enhance efficiency and accuracy. The SSTVOS model incorporates attention mechanisms tailored to selectively focus on essential spatial and temporal features, reducing computational overhead without sacrificing performance. The model's architecture is designed to be scalable, maintaining robust segmentation capabilities even in complex scenarios with multiple moving objects. Extensive experiments are conducted on benchmark video segmentation datasets, showcasing that SSTVOS achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. Key results demonstrate significant improvements in both segmentation accuracy and processing speed, highlighting the effectiveness of our spatiotemporal transformers. In conclusion, the SSTVOS model offers a powerful tool for video object segmentation, providing insights into how sparse attention mechanisms can be integrated into transformers for enhanced performance. This research contributes to the field of computer vision by introducing an innovative model with potential applications in areas such as autonomous driving, video surveillance, and augmented reality. Keywords for this paper include video object segmentation, transformers, spatiotemporal attention, and computer vision.

Tài nguyên nước dưới đất tỉnh Nam Định đang đối mặt với nhiều thách thức nghiêm trọng. Nguồn nước ngầm đang bị khai thác quá mức, dẫn đến tình trạng cạn kiệt và ô nhiễm. Điều này không chỉ ảnh hưởng đến sản xuất nông nghiệp, mà còn gây ra những hậu quả nghiêm trọng cho môi trường và sức khỏe con người. Theo thống kê, trữ lượng nước dưới đất của tỉnh Nam Định đang giảm dần, từ 1.200 triệu m3/năm xuống còn 800 triệu m3/năm. Điều này cho thấy mức độ khai thác nước ngầm đang vượt quá khả năng tái tạo của nguồn nước này. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, tỉnh Nam Định cần triển khai các giải pháp hiệu quả. Trước hết, cần phải xây dựng và thực hiện kế hoạch quản lý nước dưới đất một cách khoa học và hiệu quả. Điều này bao gồm việc đánh giá trữ lượng nước dưới đất, xác định mức độ khai thác an toàn và thiết lập hệ thống giám sát, theo dõi và báo cáo. Bên cạnh đó, cần phải tăng cường công tác tuyên truyền, giáo dục cho người dân về tầm quan trọng của việc bảo vệ nguồn nước dưới đất. Người dân cần phải nhận thức được rằng nước dưới đất là tài nguyên quý giá và cần phải được bảo vệ một cách nghiêm túc. Ngoài ra, tỉnh Nam Định cũng cần phải đầu tư vào công nghệ và thiết bị để khai thác nước dưới đất một cách hiệu quả và an toàn. Điều này bao gồm việc sử dụng công nghệ khai thác nước dưới đất hiện đại, thiết bị giám sát và báo cáo, cũng như hệ thống xử lý nước để đảm bảo chất lượng nước. Tóm lại, tài nguyên nước dưới đất tỉnh Nam Định đang đối mặt với nhiều thách thức nghiêm trọng. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, cần phải triển khai các giải pháp hiệu quả, bao gồm xây dựng kế hoạch quản lý nước dưới đất, tăng cường công tác tuyên truyền, giáo dục, đầu tư vào công nghệ và thiết bị, và đảm bảo chất lượng nước.

Zero imputation, a common strategy for handling missing data in neural network training, can introduce significant bias, particularly when data sparsity is high. This paper investigates the detrimental effects of zero imputation on model performance and proposes a novel correction method. We demonstrate that replacing missing values with zeros distorts the underlying data distribution, leading to suboptimal learning and compromised generalization capabilities. To mitigate this sparsity bias, we introduce a data-driven adjustment technique that recalibrates imputed values based on observed data patterns. Our approach adaptively estimates and compensates for the distortions caused by zero imputation, resulting in improved accuracy and robustness. Experiments conducted on diverse datasets with varying degrees of sparsity demonstrate that our correction method consistently outperforms zero imputation and other standard imputation techniques. These findings highlight the importance of carefully addressing missing data in neural network training and provide a practical solution for enhancing model performance in sparse data scenarios. Keywords: Zero Imputation, Missing Data, Neural Networks, Sparsity Bias, Data Imputation, Machine Learning.

Sim-to-real domain adaptation is a critical challenge in robotics and autonomous systems, where models trained in simulation often struggle to generalize to real-world environments. This paper presents a novel approach leveraging Meta Reinforcement Learning (Meta-RL) to bridge the sim-to-real gap effectively. The objective is to develop a robust framework that enables agents to adapt quickly and efficiently to real-world conditions with minimal additional training. Our method employs a meta-learning strategy that pre-trains agents on diverse simulated environments, enabling them to generalize across varying dynamics and conditions. The approach integrates a combination of task-specific adaptation and meta-optimization to enhance transferability. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in real-world task performance compared to traditional reinforcement learning methods, with reduced reliance on extensive real-world data. The proposed framework achieves up to 30% higher success rates in robotic manipulation tasks and exhibits superior adaptability to unseen environments. This research contributes a scalable and efficient solution for sim-to-real transfer, with potential applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and industrial automation. Key innovations include the integration of meta-learning principles with domain randomization techniques, enabling faster and more reliable adaptation. The findings highlight the potential of Meta-RL to address the sim-to-real challenge, paving the way for more practical and deployable AI-driven systems. **Keywords**: Meta Reinforcement Learning, Sim-to-Real Transfer, Domain Adaptation, Robotics, Autonomous Systems, Domain Randomization.

If resources are deleted or moved when autoscaling your cluster, your workloads might experience transient disruption. For example, if your workload consists of a controller with a single replica, that replica’s Pod might be rescheduled onto a different node if its current node is deleted. Before enabling cluster autoscaler, design your workloads to tolerate potential disruption or ensure that critical Pods are not interrupted.

This paper investigates the impact of agent behavior—prosocial versus selfish—in automated contract negotiation scenarios using reinforcement learning (RL). The objective is to understand how different behavioral strategies influence negotiation outcomes, efficiency, and overall system performance in multi-agent environments. We design a negotiation framework where agents are modeled with either prosocial tendencies, prioritizing collective benefit, or selfish tendencies, maximizing individual gains. Deep reinforcement learning algorithms are employed to enable agents to adapt and refine their negotiation tactics over repeated interactions. We conduct extensive simulations comparing both types of agents across various negotiation settings and task complexities. Our results demonstrate that prosocial agents tend to achieve higher collective utility and faster agreement rates, while selfish agents secure better individual payoffs but at the cost of increased negotiation time and occasional impasses. The findings highlight the trade-offs inherent in agent design and the potential for prosocial strategies to enhance cooperation and system-level outcomes. This research contributes to the fields of automated negotiation, multi-agent systems, and reinforcement learning by providing insights into how agent behavioral models can shape negotiation dynamics and outcomes. Key keywords: contract negotiation, reinforcement learning, prosocial behavior, selfish behavior, multi-agent systems, automated agents.

Autonomous driving systems rely heavily on understanding and predicting traffic behavior. This paper introduces a novel approach for extracting traffic primitives directly from naturalistic driving data, bypassing traditional methods that depend on manually labeled datasets or predefined scenarios. Our method leverages a deep learning architecture incorporating convolutional and recurrent layers to automatically identify and classify common traffic maneuvers, such as lane changes, car following, and merges, using raw sensor data logged from real-world driving experiences. The system is trained end-to-end, learning directly from unlabeled data through a self-supervised learning framework based on temporal context prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a large-scale dataset of naturalistic driving logs, achieving state-of-the-art performance in traffic primitive recognition. The extracted traffic primitives can then be used to improve the robustness and adaptability of self-driving algorithms by providing a more comprehensive and data-driven understanding of traffic dynamics. This work contributes a scalable and generalizable solution for learning traffic behavior, reducing reliance on expensive labeled data and improving the safety and efficiency of autonomous vehicles. Keywords: Self-driving, traffic primitives, naturalistic driving data, deep learning, self-supervised learning, autonomous vehicles.

This paper investigates the theoretical underpinnings of using the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) as a loss function component within generative models and inferential autoencoders. We analyze the properties of SSIM in the context of high-dimensional data distributions, demonstrating how it encourages the preservation of local image structures and mitigates mode collapse, a common problem in generative adversarial networks (GANs). Our theoretical analysis reveals that SSIM-based losses implicitly regularize the latent space, promoting smoother transitions and improved interpolation. Furthermore, we provide a convergence analysis for training generative models with SSIM, showing conditions under which it leads to more stable and reliable training compared to pixel-wise losses. Empirical results on benchmark image datasets validate our theoretical findings, demonstrating improved image quality and diversity in generated samples. This work offers new theoretical insights into the advantages and limitations of SSIM in generative modeling, paving the way for more principled design of loss functions and architectures. **Keywords:** Generative Models, Autoencoders, Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), Loss Function, Theoretical Analysis, Image Generation, Deep Learning.

This paper introduces a novel approach to image-text matching, leveraging recurrent visual embedding to bridge the semantic gap between visual and textual representations. The objective is to enable objects in images to be expressed and matched with textual descriptions as seamlessly as words. Our method employs a recurrent neural network architecture to learn visual embeddings that capture the spatial and contextual relationships between objects in an image. The approach is evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in image-text matching accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. Key findings include the ability to effectively capture fine-grained visual details and contextual relationships, leading to more accurate matching results. The proposed recurrent visual embedding has important implications for applications such as image retrieval, visual question answering, and multimodal understanding. This paper explores the concept of utilizing programs as black-box explanations, aiming to enhance the interpretability and transparency of complex systems. Our objective is to develop a novel approach that leverages programmatic representations to provide insightful explanations for opaque models, such as neural networks. We propose a method that employs a combination of symbolic execution and machine learning techniques to generate explanatory programs, which can be used to elucidate the decision-making processes of black-box models. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in providing concise and accurate explanations, outperforming existing explanation methods in terms of fidelity and understandability. The key findings of this research contribute to the development of more transparent and trustworthy AI systems, with potential applications in areas such as model validation, debugging, and knowledge discovery. By introducing programs as a means of explanation, we pave the way for a new paradigm in explainable AI, enabling the creation of more interpretable and reliable models. Key keywords: explainable AI, programmatic explanations, black-box models, symbolic execution, machine learning.

This paper addresses the problem of image thresholding, a crucial step in image processing, by introducing a novel bi-level thresholding approach based on Kaniadakis entropy. The objective is to effectively separate objects from the background in images by determining optimal threshold values. Our method utilizes the Kaniadakis entropy formula, which generalizes the traditional Shannon entropy, to measure the information content in images. By applying a bi-level thresholding technique, we segment images into foreground and background regions. The results show that our approach outperforms traditional thresholding methods, particularly in images with complex backgrounds or low contrast. The key findings indicate improved accuracy and robustness in thresholding, leading to enhanced image segmentation. This research contributes to the field of image processing by providing a unique entropy-based thresholding technique, with potential applications in object detection, medical imaging, and computer vision. The novelty of our approach lies in the use of Kaniadakis entropy, which offers a more flexible and efficient way to model complex image distributions. Key keywords: image thresholding, Kaniadakis entropy, bi-level thresholding, image segmentation, object detection.

Các đặc trưng này sau đó được sử dụng để xây dựng một mô hình 3D khuôn mặt trung bình. This paper presents an innovative, unsupervised, iterative algorithm for registering N-dimensional point-sets, addressing a long-standing challenge in computer vision and machine learning. The objective is to develop a robust method for aligning multiple point-sets without prior knowledge of correspondences, enabling applications in 3D reconstruction, object recognition, and data integration. Our approach leverages a novel combination of geometric and statistical techniques to iteratively refine the registration, ensuring accurate and efficient alignment of point-sets. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in registering complex point-sets, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a new iterative framework, the development of a robust point-set distance metric, and the demonstration of the algorithm's scalability to high-dimensional data. This work has significant implications for various fields, including computer vision, robotics, and data science, and paves the way for future research in point-set registration and geometric processing, with relevant keywords including point-set registration, iterative alignment, unsupervised learning, and geometric computing.

Sparsely activated networks have shown promise in reducing computational costs by activating only a subset of neurons for each input. This paper investigates novel methods for training sparsely activated networks to improve their performance and efficiency. We introduce a dynamic routing mechanism that adapts the network's active sub-structure based on input characteristics, promoting more efficient computation. Furthermore, we explore regularizations that encourage sparsity while maintaining representational power. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves comparable or superior accuracy to densely connected networks with significantly reduced computational overhead. The proposed techniques offer a practical approach to deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Key words: Sparse Activation, Neural Networks, Dynamic Routing, Efficiency, Deep Learning.

Trong trường hợp này, chúng ta cần sử dụng phương pháp giải phương trình nhiều biến để tìm ra giá trị của các biến. Tóm lại, phương pháp giải phương trình sai phân tuyến tính hệ số hằng là một kỹ thuật mạnh mẽ được sử dụng để giải quyết các phương trình đại số phức tạp. Bằng cách sử dụng phương pháp này, chúng ta có thể tìm ra giá trị của các biến và giải quyết các vấn đề toán học phức tạp.

Xây dựng trang web quản lý bán hàng chuỗi cửa hàng cà phê là một hệ thống thông tin được thiết kế để hỗ trợ quản lý và bán hàng hiệu quả cho các cửa hàng cà phê. Hệ thống này cung cấp các tính năng quản lý hàng hóa, quản lý đơn hàng, quản lý khách hàng, và quản lý báo cáo doanh thu. Bằng cách sử dụng công nghệ web và cơ sở dữ liệu, hệ thống này cho phép các cửa hàng cà phê dễ dàng theo dõi và quản lý hoạt động kinh doanh của mình. Đồng thời, hệ thống này cũng cung cấp cho khách hàng một trải nghiệm mua sắm trực tuyến tiện lợi và dễ dàng. Mục tiêu của hệ thống này là tăng cường hiệu suất kinh doanh, giảm thiểu thời gian và chi phí quản lý, và cung cấp cho khách hàng một dịch vụ tốt hơn.

Cùng với sự phát triển của giáo dục, nhu cầu về giáo dục mầm non ngày càng tăng. Để đáp ứng nhu cầu này, nhiều trường đại học đã mở ra các chương trình đào tạo giáo viên mầm non chất lượng cao. Dưới đây là một số thông tin quan trọng về chương trình đào tạo giáo viên mầm non tại trường đại học. Chương trình đào tạo giáo viên mầm non tại trường đại học được thiết kế để cung cấp cho sinh viên kiến thức và kỹ năng cần thiết để trở thành một giáo viên mầm non hiệu quả. Chương trình bao gồm các môn học như giáo dục mầm non, giáo dục trẻ em, giáo dục phát triển, giáo dục nghệ thuật, và nhiều môn học khác. Sinh viên tham gia chương trình đào tạo giáo viên mầm non sẽ được đào tạo về các kỹ năng như quản lý lớp học, tạo môi trường học tập tích cực, và sử dụng phương pháp giảng dạy hiệu quả. Họ cũng sẽ được đào tạo về các kỹ năng mềm như giao tiếp, teamwork, và giải quyết vấn đề. Sau khi hoàn thành chương trình đào tạo, sinh viên sẽ được cấp bằng cử nhân giáo viên mầm non và có thể ứng tuyển vào các trường mầm non, trung tâm giáo dục, hoặc các cơ quan khác liên quan đến giáo dục. Tóm lại, chương trình đào tạo giáo viên mầm non tại trường đại học là một lựa chọn tuyệt vời cho những ai muốn trở thành một giáo viên mầm non chất lượng cao và đóng góp vào sự phát triển của giáo dục mầm non.

Video completion, the task of filling in missing regions of a video, remains a challenging problem due to complex motion and dynamic textures. This paper introduces Onion-Peel Networks (OPN), a novel deep learning architecture designed specifically for robust and coherent video completion. OPN iteratively refines the completed video by peeling away and filling in successive layers, inspired by the structure of an onion. Our method employs a 3D convolutional encoder-decoder network at each layer to capture spatiotemporal dependencies. A key innovation is the adaptive attention mechanism within each layer that focuses on reconstructing missing regions based on contextual information from both the available video frames and the previously completed layers. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that OPN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both qualitative visual quality and quantitative metrics. The layered completion strategy effectively handles large missing regions and complex occlusions, resulting in more temporally consistent and visually plausible video completions. This work contributes a new approach to video completion that leverages layered processing and adaptive attention for improved reconstruction accuracy and temporal coherence. Keywords: Video Completion, Deep Learning, 3D Convolutional Networks, Attention Mechanism, Inpainting.

Năng lực nghề nghiệp của giáo viên hiện nay đang trở thành một chủ đề quan trọng trong lĩnh vực giáo dục. Để đáp ứng yêu cầu ngày càng cao của xã hội và sự phát triển của công nghệ, giáo viên cần không ngừng nâng cao trình độ chuyên môn, kỹ năng sư phạm và khả năng ứng dụng công nghệ trong giảng dạy. Các yếu tố như khả năng giao tiếp, tư duy phản biện, sáng tạo và khả năng làm việc nhóm cũng được coi là những năng lực thiết yếu. Bên cạnh đó, việc phát triển năng lực nghề nghiệp còn liên quan đến việc tham gia các khóa đào tạo, hội thảo và nghiên cứu chuyên sâu. Sự hỗ trợ từ các cơ sở giáo dục và chính sách của nhà nước cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc nâng cao năng lực cho đội ngũ giáo viên, từ đó góp phần nâng cao chất lượng giáo dục toàn diện.

Program synthesis, the task of automatically generating programs from specifications, offers a promising avenue for explainable AI. This paper explores the use of program synthesis to generate black-box explanations for complex systems. Our method leverages input-output examples of a target system to synthesize concise programs that mimic its behavior, thereby providing interpretable summaries. We introduce a novel approach that combines search-based program synthesis with techniques for abstracting system behavior, allowing us to generate programs that capture key functionalities without overfitting to the provided examples. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark domains, demonstrating that the synthesized programs effectively approximate the target system’s behavior while remaining significantly simpler and more interpretable. Results show that these “black-box explanations” achieve high fidelity in predicting system outputs and offer valuable insights into the system's internal logic. This approach facilitates understanding and debugging of complex systems and can be applied in scenarios where access to the system’s internal state is limited. Keywords: program synthesis, explainable AI, black-box explanation, program abstraction, interpretable models.

This paper introduces the Monash University, UEA, and UCR Time Series Extrinsic Regression Archive, a comprehensive and publicly accessible repository designed to advance research in time series extrinsic regression. The archive addresses the growing need for standardized datasets to evaluate and compare regression models applied to time series data. It consolidates a diverse collection of real-world and synthetic datasets, spanning multiple domains such as healthcare, finance, and environmental monitoring. Each dataset is carefully curated, annotated, and preprocessed to ensure consistency and usability. To demonstrate the utility of the archive, we evaluate several state-of-the-art regression algorithms, including deep learning and traditional machine learning approaches, across the datasets. Our results highlight the varying performance of these methods, emphasizing the importance of domain-specific considerations in model selection. The archive not only provides a benchmark for future research but also fosters reproducibility and collaboration in the time series regression community. This work contributes to the field by offering a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners, enabling the development of more robust and generalizable regression models. **Keywords**: time series, extrinsic regression, dataset archive, machine learning, deep learning, benchmarking.

This paper investigates the theoretical foundations and limitations of adversarial training for predictive tasks, focusing on the deterministic case. The objective is to analyze the effectiveness of adversarial training in enhancing model robustness and generalization. We employ a mathematical approach to examine the underlying mechanisms of adversarial training, exploring its relationship with regularization techniques and margin theory. Our analysis reveals that, in the deterministic setting, adversarial training can be viewed as a form of robust optimization, which leads to improved model performance on unseen data. However, we also identify fundamental limitations, including the potential for over-regularization and the sensitivity of adversarial training to hyperparameter tuning. The results of our theoretical analysis are supported by empirical evaluations on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the trade-offs between model robustness and accuracy. This research contributes to the understanding of adversarial training, highlighting its potential benefits and limitations, and provides insights for the development of more effective and efficient training methods for predictive tasks, with key applications in areas such as machine learning, deep learning, and AI model development.

This paper presents an innovative approach to automatic phantom test pattern classification using transfer learning with deep neural networks. The objective is to develop a robust and efficient system for classifying phantom test patterns, which is crucial in various applications such as quality control and defect detection. Our approach leverages pre-trained deep neural networks and fine-tunes them on a dataset of phantom test patterns to achieve high classification accuracy. The method utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning techniques to extract relevant features and classify patterns. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional machine learning methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on phantom test pattern classification tasks. The key findings include improved classification accuracy, reduced training time, and increased robustness to variations in pattern appearance. This research contributes to the development of intelligent quality control systems and has potential applications in industries such as manufacturing and healthcare. Key keywords: deep learning, transfer learning, phantom test patterns, convolutional neural networks, classification, quality control.

Sự phân bố ứng suất tại tâm tải trọng ngoài dạng băng phân bố đều trên nền đất ven sông là một vấn đề quan trọng trong lĩnh vực kỹ thuật xây dựng và địa kỹ thuật. Khi một tải trọng được áp dụng lên nền đất, ứng suất sẽ phân bố không đồng đều, ảnh hưởng đến khả năng chịu tải và ổn định của công trình. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc phân tích cách mà ứng suất được phân bố tại vị trí tâm của tải trọng, đặc biệt là trong trường hợp tải trọng dạng băng. Các yếu tố như loại đất, độ ẩm, và cấu trúc nền đất ven sông sẽ được xem xét để hiểu rõ hơn về hành vi của nền đất dưới tác động của tải trọng. Kết quả từ nghiên cứu này có thể cung cấp những thông tin quý giá cho các kỹ sư trong việc thiết kế và thi công các công trình xây dựng ven sông, đảm bảo an toàn và hiệu quả trong quá trình sử dụng.

This research addresses the critical issue of accurately predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of machinery components, which is essential for effective maintenance planning and minimizing downtimes. The study explores innovative approaches to enhance prognostic accuracy in industrial applications. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel method using time series embeddings based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to predict RUL. Our approach leverages the sequential nature of time-series data by employing RNN architectures, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to capture temporal dependencies and learn robust feature representations directly from raw sensor signals. The embeddings transform raw data into a lower-dimensional, informative representation, feeding a predictive model to forecast RUL accurately. Results/Findings: The proposed model was evaluated on comprehensive industrial datasets and compared with traditional machine learning approaches and state-of-the-art deep learning models. The findings demonstrate that our RNN-based time series embeddings significantly improve the accuracy of RUL predictions, achieving a reduction in prediction error by up to 20% compared to baseline models. The results underscore the potential for enhanced reliability and efficiency in predictive maintenance strategies. Conclusion/Implications: This study contributes to the field by introducing a scalable and effective RNN-based approach for RUL estimation, showcasing significant advancements over existing methodologies. The implications of these findings are substantial for industries relying on predictive maintenance, where the timely and precise estimation of machinery failures can lead to increased operational efficiency and reduced maintenance costs. The novel application of time series embeddings offers a promising direction for future research in prognostics and health management (PHM). Keywords: Remaining Useful Life, Recurrent Neural Networks, Time Series Embeddings, Predictive Maintenance, Long Short-Term Memory, Prognostics.
Chương trình khách hàng trung thành: Hệ thống tích điểm và xếp hạng là một phần quan trọng của các chương trình khách hàng trung thành, giúp giữ chân khách hàng hiện tạ và thu hút khách hàng mới.

Chia sẻ tri thức trong môi trường đại học tại Việt Nam chịu ảnh hưởng bởi nhiều yếu tố khác nhau. Đầu tiên, văn hóa tổ chức và môi trường làm việc đóng vai trò quan trọng, khi sự cởi mở và khuyến khích hợp tác giữa các giảng viên thúc đẩy quá trình chia sẻ kiến thức. Thứ hai, công nghệ thông tin và hệ thống quản lý tri thức hiện đại tạo điều kiện thuận lợi để lưu trữ và truyền tải thông tin hiệu quả. Ngoài ra, động lực cá nhân, bao gồm sự công nhận và phần thưởng, cũng là yếu tố thúc đẩy giảng viên tích cực chia sẻ kinh nghiệm và kiến thức chuyên môn. Cuối cùng, chính sách của nhà trường và sự hỗ trợ từ lãnh đạo cũng góp phần tạo nên môi trường thuận lợi cho việc trao đổi tri thức, từ đó nâng cao chất lượng giáo dục và nghiên cứu.

Module giả mã đề xuất Dựa trên mô đun gả mã MLP được giới thiệu trong bài báo SegFormer . Ch tết kiến trúc của mô đun này được biểu diễn ở Hình 3.8. Trong bài báo đã chứng minh đây là một kiến trúc mạng nhẹ (lightweight network) được thiết kế đơn giản nhằm tận dụng được ưu điểm từ các đặc trưng cho ra bở kiến trúc MT là có trường tiếp nhận cục bộ lớn nhờ cấu trúc phân tầng và tạo ra đặc trưng toàn cục. Cụ thể, với các đặc trưng cho ra bở MT, cơ chế chú ý tại các tầng thấp hơn có xu hướng duy trì tính cục bộ, trong kh tạ các tầng cao hơn có xu hướng ph cục bộ cao. Với bài toán phân vùng ngữ nghĩa, việc duy trì trường tiếp nhận lớn để trích xuất hiệu quả thông tin ngữ cảnh là một vấn đề trọng tâm. Mô Đun này tích hợp thông tin từ các tầng khác nhau, do đó tích hợp được cả thông tin chú ý cục bộ (local attention) và thông tin chú ý toàn cục (global attention) để tạo ra các biểu diễn đặc trưng mạnh mẽ.

Phát triển kỹ năng đọc hiểu tiếng Anh cho học sinh lớp 10 bằng phương pháp tích hợp công nghệ thông tin Trong thời đại công nghệ thông tin hiện nay, việc tích hợp công nghệ vào quá trình học tập đã trở thành một phần không thể thiếu. Đối với học sinh lớp 10, việc phát triển kỹ năng đọc hiểu tiếng Anh là một yêu cầu quan trọng để có thể tiếp cận và hiểu được các tài liệu tiếng Anh. Trong bài viết này, chúng tôi sẽ giới thiệu một số phương pháp tích hợp công nghệ thông tin để giúp học sinh lớp 10 phát triển kỹ năng đọc hiểu tiếng Anh. Một trong những phương pháp tích hợp công nghệ thông tin hiệu quả là sử dụng phần mềm đọc sách điện tử. Phần mềm này cho phép học sinh đọc sách tiếng Anh trên thiết bị di động hoặc máy tính bảng, đồng thời cũng cung cấp các tính năng như tra từ điển, nghe âm thanh, và xem hình ảnh. Điều này giúp học sinh có thể đọc và hiểu được các tài liệu tiếng Anh một cách dễ dàng hơn. Một phương pháp khác là sử dụng các ứng dụng học tiếng Anh trên thiết bị di động. Các ứng dụng này thường cung cấp các bài tập đọc hiểu, từ vựng, và ngữ pháp, đồng thời cũng cho phép học sinh nghe và xem các video tiếng Anh. Điều này giúp học sinh có thể phát triển kỹ năng đọc hiểu tiếng Anh một cách hiệu quả hơn. Ngoài ra, việc sử dụng các công cụ trực tuyến như Google Translate cũng giúp học sinh có thể đọc và hiểu được các tài liệu tiếng Anh một cách dễ dàng hơn. Công cụ này cho phép học sinh dịch các tài liệu tiếng Anh sang tiếng Việt, đồng thời cũng cung cấp các tính năng như tra từ điển và nghe âm thanh. Tóm lại, việc phát triển kỹ năng đọc hiểu tiếng Anh cho học sinh lớp 10 bằng phương pháp tích hợp công nghệ thông tin là một yêu cầu quan trọng. Sử dụng phần mềm đọc sách điện tử, ứng dụng học tiếng Anh, và công cụ trực tuyến như Google Translate là một số phương pháp hiệu quả để giúp học sinh phát triển kỹ năng đọc hiểu tiếng Anh.

To reduce cost in storing, processing and visualizing a large-scale point cloud, we consider a randomized resampling strategy to select a representative subset of points while preserving application-dependent features. The proposed strategy is based on graphs, which can represent underlying surfaces and lend themselves well to efficient computation. We use a general feature-extraction operator to represent application-dependent features and propose a general reconstruction error to evaluate the quality of resampling. We obtain a general form of optimal resampling distribution by minimizing the reconstruction error. The proposed optimal resampling distribution is guaranteed to be shift, rotation and scale-invariant in the 3D space. We next specify the feature-extraction operator to be a graph filter and study specific resampling strategies based on all-pass, low-pass, high-pass graph filtering and graph filter banks. We finally apply the proposed methods to three applications: large-scale visualization, accurate registration and robust shape modeling. The empirical performance validates the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed resampling methods.

Throughput statistics were measured for connection counts of 1000, 2000, and 4000, revealing significant trends as the number of connections increased. Most notably, the median and lower percentile (such as the 5th and 10th percentiles) throughput values declined sharply, in many cases dropping to extremely low or even zero levels at higher connection counts. In contrast, the upper percentiles (like the 95th and 99th) as well as maximum throughputs not only remained high but in some cases increased, indicating that while a small fraction of connections maintained strong throughput, the bulk experienced severe degradation. The standard deviation of throughput also rose across higher connection counts, reflecting the growing disparity between the best and worst performing connections. For each level of concurrency, detailed statistics were reported, including precise values for the 5th, 10th, 50th, 95th, and 99th percentiles, the averages, and the maximum observed throughputs, illustrating the highly uneven distribution of network resources as connection load grows.

Nghiên cứu gần đây tập trung vào việc kiểm định mối quan hệ kinh tế dài hạn giữa các quốc gia thành viên Cộng đồng Đông Phi (EAC) bằng cách sử dụng dữ liệu bảng từ năm 1990 đến 2018. Phân tích đồng liên kết được thực hiện để xác định liệu có tồn tại mối quan hệ ổn định và bền vững giữa các biến kinh tế quan trọng như GDP, thương mại, đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài và lạm phát hay không. Link prediction in n-ary relational data is a critical challenge in knowledge graph completion and relational learning, with applications in recommendation systems, social network analysis, and semantic web technologies. This paper addresses the problem of accurately predicting missing links in n-ary relations by introducing a novel approach based on relatedness evaluation. Unlike traditional binary link prediction methods, our approach leverages the multi-dimensional nature of n-ary relations, capturing complex dependencies among entities and their attributes. We propose a hybrid model that combines graph-based embeddings with a relatedness scoring mechanism, enabling the evaluation of entity-relation interactions across multiple dimensions. The model is trained and evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score. Key findings reveal that incorporating relatedness evaluation significantly improves prediction accuracy, particularly in sparse and heterogeneous datasets. The proposed method also exhibits robustness in handling noisy and incomplete data. This research contributes to advancing n-ary relational learning by providing a scalable and interpretable framework for link prediction, with potential applications in knowledge graph enrichment and dynamic network analysis. **Keywords**: Link prediction, n-ary relations, relatedness evaluation, knowledge graphs, graph embeddings, relational learning.

This study investigates the robustness and performance of keypoint detectors and binary descriptors under varying degrees of photometric and geometric transformations, a critical challenge in computer vision applications such as object recognition, image stitching, and 3D reconstruction. The objective is to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of state-of-the-art keypoint detection algorithms (e.g., SIFT, ORB, and AKAZE) and binary descriptors (e.g., BRIEF, FREAK, and ORB) in handling transformations such as scaling, rotation, illumination changes, and noise. A comprehensive experimental framework is designed, utilizing benchmark datasets with controlled transformations to systematically assess detection accuracy, descriptor matching performance, and computational efficiency. Results indicate that while certain detectors excel under geometric transformations, others demonstrate superior resilience to photometric variations. Binary descriptors, known for their efficiency, exhibit varying trade-offs between matching accuracy and computational speed. The findings provide valuable insights into selecting optimal combinations of detectors and descriptors for specific application scenarios. This research contributes to advancing the understanding of feature extraction techniques and offers practical guidelines for improving the robustness of vision-based systems under real-world conditions. **Keywords**: Keypoint detection, binary descriptors, photometric transformations, geometric transformations, computer vision, feature matching.

In the realm of blockchain technology, a cryptographic key forms the backbone of security and trust in asset transactions and management. Cryptographic keys operate in pairs: private keys and public keys, each playing a distinct yet interconnected role in safeguarding digital assets. Private keys, which must be kept secret, grant the owner exclusive authority to sign transactions and manage the assets tied to them. This exclusivity ensures that only the holder of the private key can initiate a valid transaction, thereby preventing unauthorized access or transfers. On the other hand, public keys are used to generate addresses — concise, unique identifiers that serve as the receiving endpoints for blockchain transactions. These addresses allow users to send and receive digital assets without revealing any underlying private key information, upholding both privacy and security. Acting as pseudonymous identifiers, addresses are crucial in maintaining user anonymity while enabling transparent, verifiable transactions on the blockchain. Ultimately, the synergy between private and public keys enables not only asset security but also the authentication of transaction legitimacy, laying the foundation for trustless interaction in decentralized networks.

Facial Expression Recognition (FER) is a critical task in computer vision with applications in human-computer interaction, emotion analysis, and mental health monitoring. This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance FER by integrating the Squeeze and Excitation (SE) mechanism into a Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture. The proposed method leverages the global context modeling capabilities of ViT while incorporating SE blocks to adaptively recalibrate channel-wise feature responses, improving the model's ability to capture subtle facial expression details. The model is trained and evaluated on widely used FER datasets, including FER2013 and RAF-DB. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SE-ViT achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The integration of SE blocks not only enhances feature representation but also reduces computational overhead compared to traditional attention mechanisms. This work contributes to advancing FER by combining the strengths of transformer-based architectures and attention mechanisms, offering a scalable and efficient solution for real-world applications. **Keywords**: Facial Expression Recognition, Vision Transformer, Squeeze and Excitation, Attention Mechanism, Computer Vision, Deep Learning.

This paper proposes a novel approach to robust subspace discovery, leveraging block-diagonal adaptive locality-constrained representation. The objective is to identify underlying subspaces in high-dimensional data, which is crucial for various applications in computer vision, machine learning, and data mining. Our method utilizes an adaptive locality-constrained representation to capture the intrinsic structure of the data, while a block-diagonal regularization term ensures the learned representation is robust to outliers and noise. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in discovering multiple subspaces, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The key findings highlight the importance of adaptive locality constraints and block-diagonal regularization in improving the representation's quality and robustness. This research contributes to the development of robust subspace discovery techniques, with potential applications in image and video analysis, clustering, and dimensionality reduction. Key keywords: subspace discovery, locality-constrained representation, block-diagonal regularization, robustness, high-dimensional data, computer vision, machine learning.

mBART (multilingual BART) is a state-of-the-art multilingual sequence-to-sequence pre-trained model developed by Facebook AI. It is an extension of BART (Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers), which is a powerful denoising autoencoder pre-trained on a large corpus of monolingual text. mBART extends BART’s capabilities to support multiple languages, making it a highly versatile and effective model for a wide range of multilingual natural language processing (NLP) tasks. It is capable of handling tasks such as text generation, text summarization, machine translation, and more, across multiple languages. One of the key features of mBART is its ability to handle zero-shot translation, which means it can performtranslation between language pairs that were not explicitly included during pre training. This makes it a valuable tool for low-resource languages and enables transfer learning between different language pairs. mBART has achieved impressive performance on various benchmark datasets and has been widely adopted in the NLP research community. With its multilingual capabilities, mBART continues to play a significant role in advancing multilingual NLP and enabling effective cross-lingual transfer learning in various language-related tasks. This paper aims to address the challenges of sequential decision making by exploring the relationship between free energy concepts and generalized optimality equations. The objective is to enhance decision-making strategies in dynamic environments where uncertainty and complexity are prevalent. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel framework that integrates the principles of free energy with the generalized optimality equations, commonly employed in reinforcement learning and decision theory. Our approach utilizes advanced optimization algorithms to adaptively update decision policies by minimizing the free energy, thus balancing exploration and exploitation efficiently. Results/Findings: The proposed method was evaluated across various sequential decision-making scenarios, and our experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in computational efficiency and decision accuracy compared to traditional methods. The integration of free energy principles facilitated more robust handling of uncertainty, leading to more optimal policy derivation. Comparative analysis indicates that our model consistently outperforms existing approaches in terms of convergence speed and overall performance. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel perspective on sequential decision making by leveraging free energy concepts to refine the generalized optimality equations. The implications of this study are profound for fields such as robotics, automated control systems, and AI-driven decision support systems. Future work will explore extending this framework to encompass more complex, high-dimensional state spaces. Keywords: Free energy, generalized optimality equations, sequential decision making, reinforcement learning, optimization algorithms, uncertainty handling, decision policies.

The paper introduces CodeReef, an open platform designed to address the challenges in Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) by promoting portability, reusability, and reproducibility in ML workflows. With the growing complexity of machine learning models and the diverse computational environments, there is a critical need for a framework that enables seamless integration and deployment across varied platforms. Methods/Approach: CodeReef leverages a modular architecture that allows users to encapsulate machine learning tasks into reusable components, known as automation actions. These actions can be easily shared, modified, and executed on different infrastructures. Furthermore, CodeReef includes a benchmarking framework that facilitates the consistent evaluation of models' performance, employing containerization technologies to ensure environments are reproducible across various hardware and software setups. Results/Findings: Through empirical evaluations, CodeReef demonstrates its capability to streamline MLOps processes by significantly reducing the time and effort required to transfer machine learning pipelines between disparate systems. It shows a marked improvement in reproducibility and benchmarking consistency compared to traditional methods. Key findings include demonstrable benefits in the deployment of complex ML workflows across cloud and edge devices. Conclusion/Implications: CodeReef presents an impactful advancement in the field of MLOps by establishing a standard for portable, reusable, and reproducible machine learning processes. Its open-platform nature encourages collaboration and innovation, potentially accelerating research and application development in AI. The platform's contribution also lays the groundwork for standardized benchmarking practices, opening pathways for future enhancements in performance evaluation. Keywords: CodeReef, MLOps, portability, reusable automation actions, reproducible benchmarking, machine learning workflows, containerization, AI development.

Factored Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) offer a compact representation for sequential decision-making problems with state spaces that grow exponentially with the number of features. However, identifying the relevant features for optimal policy determination remains a significant challenge, particularly in sample-constrained settings. This paper introduces a novel feature selection algorithm for factored MDPs designed to maximize sample efficiency. Our approach leverages a combination of mutual information estimation and a novel variant of the Bellman error to identify and prioritize features relevant to the optimal value function. We formulate a submodular optimization problem to select the most informative subset of features, balancing exploration and exploitation. Empirical evaluations on benchmark factored MDP domains demonstrate that our algorithm achieves comparable or superior performance to existing methods while requiring significantly fewer samples. Specifically, results show a reduction in sample complexity by up to 40% in certain domains. This work contributes a practical and efficient approach to feature selection in factored MDPs, enabling effective planning in complex, high-dimensional environments with limited data. Keywords: Factored MDPs, Feature Selection, Reinforcement Learning, Sample Efficiency, Submodular Optimization.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have emerged as a powerful framework for generative modeling across various domains. This paper presents a comparative study of several prominent GAN architectures, focusing on their performance in image generation tasks. We evaluate and compare the original GAN formulation with improved variations, including Deep Convolutional GANs (DCGANs), Conditional GANs (cGANs), and Wasserstein GANs (WGANs), assessing their stability, training efficiency, and the quality of generated images. The evaluation employs quantitative metrics such as Inception Score (IS) and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), alongside qualitative visual assessments. Our findings reveal significant differences in the convergence behavior and generative capabilities of these models. Specifically, WGANs demonstrate enhanced training stability compared to traditional GANs, while cGANs offer superior control over the generated output. The study provides insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each GAN architecture, offering guidance for selecting the most appropriate model for specific generative tasks. This comparative analysis contributes to a deeper understanding of GANs and facilitates their more effective application in diverse fields. **Keywords:** Generative Adversarial Networks, GAN, DCGAN, cGAN, WGAN, Image Generation, Deep Learning, Comparative Analysis.

The implications of this research are substantial, as Aspis has the potential to protect distributed learning systems from malicious attacks and data breaches, thereby ensuring the integrity of the learning process. Relevant keywords: distributed learning, anomaly detection, federated learning, machine learning, security, robust detection system.

Heterogeneous Domain Adaptation (HDA) addresses the transfer learning problems where data from the source and target domains are of different modalities (e.g., texts and images) or feature dimensions (e.g., features extracted with different methods). It is useful for multi-modal data analysis. Traditional domain adaptation algorithms assume that the representations of source and target samples reside in the same feature space, hence are likely to fail in solving the heterogeneous domain adaptation problem. Contemporary state-of-the-art HDA approaches are usually composed of complex optimization objectives for favourable performance and are therefore computationally expensive and less generalizable. To address these issues, we propose a novel Cross-Domain Structure Preserving Projection (CDSPP) algorithm for HDA. As an extension of the classic LPP to heterogeneous domains, CDSPP aims to learn domain-specific projections to map sample features from source and target domains into a common subspace such that the class consistency is preserved and data distributions are sufficiently aligned. CDSPP is simple and has deterministic solutions by solving a generalized eigenvalue problem. It is naturally suitable for supervised HDA but has also been extended for semi-supervised HDA where the unlabeled target domain samples are available. Extensive experiments have been conducted on commonly used benchmark datasets (i.e. Office-Caltech, Multilingual Reuters Collection, NUS-WIDE-ImageNet) for HDA as well as the Office-Home dataset firstly introduced for HDA by ourselves due to its significantly larger number of classes than the existing ones (65 vs 10, 6 and 8). The experimental results of both supervised and semi-supervised HDA demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed method against contemporary state-of-the-art methods.

The paper introduces the Teacher-Class Network, a novel neural network compression mechanism designed to address the increasing demand for efficient deep neural network deployment in resource-constrained environments. The focus is on reducing the computational load and storage requirements while maintaining high performance. Methods/Approach: The proposed method leverages a unique teaching paradigm where a high-capacity 'Teacher' model guides the learning process of a 'Class' network, which consists of smaller, more efficient models. This hierarchical relationship allows the Class network to mimic the Teacher's predictive behaviors, effectively compressing the original network. Key techniques employed include knowledge distillation and parameter pruning, ensuring that the compressed network retains critical information and capabilities. Results/Findings: Extensive benchmarking reveals that the Teacher-Class Network achieves significant reductions in both model size and computational overhead, without compromising accuracy. Experiments demonstrate improvements in compressing popular architectures, resulting in up to a 70% reduction in parameters and a 50% decrease in runtime on standard image classification tasks. Comparisons with existing compression methods indicate superior performance in both efficiency and accuracy retention. Conclusion/Implications: The Teacher-Class Network presents a compelling solution for deploying deep learning models in environments with limited resources, such as mobile devices or edge computing scenarios. By maintaining a balance between compactness and accuracy, this mechanism potentially broadens the applicability of advanced AI models across various industries. Future work will explore extending this approach to other domains and network architectures, enhancing its versatility and impact. Key Keywords: neural network compression, knowledge distillation, parameter pruning, Teacher-Class Network, model efficiency.

Neural network optimization is a cornerstone of modern machine learning, yet it often encounters challenges related to nondeterminism and instability during training. This paper investigates the root causes of these phenomena and their impact on model performance and reproducibility. We propose a systematic approach to analyze the sources of nondeterminism, including random initialization, stochastic gradient descent (SGD) dynamics, and hardware-level variations. Through extensive experiments, we evaluate the effects of these factors on convergence behavior and model accuracy across diverse architectures and datasets. Our findings reveal that nondeterminism can lead to significant performance variability, even under identical training conditions. To address this, we introduce a novel stabilization technique that mitigates instability while preserving model expressiveness. The proposed method demonstrates improved convergence consistency and robustness across multiple benchmarks, outperforming existing approaches. This research provides valuable insights into the challenges of neural network optimization and offers practical solutions for enhancing training stability, with implications for applications requiring high reliability, such as autonomous systems and healthcare. **Keywords**: neural networks, optimization, nondeterminism, instability, stochastic gradient descent, reproducibility, machine learning.

Đánh giá tính an toàn và một số tác dụng không mong muốn của điều trị ung thư dạ dày giai đoạn muộn đang là vấn đề quan tâm lớn của các chuyên gia y tế. Trong những năm gần đây, tỷ lệ mắc ung thư dạ dày đã tăng nhanh chóng, đặc biệt là ở giai đoạn muộn. Điều trị ung thư dạ dày giai đoạn muộn thường bao gồm các phương pháp như phẫu thuật, hóa trị và xạ trị. Mặc dù các phương pháp này có thể giúp kéo dài tuổi thọ và cải thiện chất lượng cuộc sống của bệnh nhân, nhưng chúng cũng có thể gây ra một số tác dụng không mong muốn. Một số tác dụng không mong muốn của điều trị ung thư dạ dày giai đoạn muộn bao gồm: - Tác dụng phụ của hóa trị như buồn nôn, nôn mửa, suy giảm miễn dịch và giảm số lượng tế bào máu. - Tác dụng phụ của xạ trị như mệt mỏi, buồn nôn, nôn mửa và giảm số lượng tế bào máu. - Tác dụng phụ của phẫu thuật như đau, chảy máu và nhiễm trùng. Để đánh giá tính an toàn của điều trị ung thư dạ dày giai đoạn muộn, các chuyên gia y tế đã thực hiện một số nghiên cứu. Kết quả cho thấy rằng, mặc dù các phương pháp điều trị này có thể gây ra một số tác dụng không mong muốn, nhưng chúng vẫn là lựa chọn tốt nhất cho bệnh nhân ung thư dạ dày giai đoạn muộn. Tuy nhiên, để giảm thiểu tác dụng không mong muốn của điều trị ung thư dạ dày giai đoạn muộn, các chuyên gia y tế khuyến cáo rằng bệnh nhân nên: - Tuân thủ đúng lịch trình điều trị. - Uống thuốc đúng liều lượng và thời gian. - Không tự ý ngừng sử dụng thuốc mà không có sự đồng ý của bác sĩ. - Thực hiện các biện pháp phòng ngừa tác dụng phụ như sử dụng thuốc chống nôn, thuốc giảm đau và thuốc tăng cường miễn dịch. Tóm lại, điều trị ung thư dạ dày giai đoạn muộn có thể gây ra một số tác dụng không mong muốn, nhưng chúng vẫn là lựa chọn tốt nhất cho bệnh nhân. Để giảm thiểu tác dụng không mong muốn, bệnh nhân nên tuân thủ đúng lịch trình điều trị và thực hiện các biện pháp phòng ngừa tác dụng phụ.

The field of multiple view geometry has seen tremendous progress in reconstruction and calibration due to methods for extracting reliable point features and key developments in projective geometry. Point features, however, are not available in certain applications and result in unstructured point cloud reconstructions. General image curves provide a complementary feature when keypoints are scarce, and result in 3D curve geometry, but face challenges not addressed by the usual projective geometry of points and algebraic curves. We address these challenges by laying the theoretical foundations of a framework based on the differential geometry of general curves, including stationary curves, occluding contours, and non-rigid curves, aiming at stereo correspondence, camera estimation (including calibration, pose, and multiview epipolar geometry), and 3D reconstruction given measured image curves. By gathering previous results into a cohesive theory, novel results were made possible, yielding three contributions. First we derive the differential geometry of an image curve (tangent, curvature, curvature derivative) from that of the underlying space curve (tangent, curvature, curvature derivative, torsion). Second, we derive the differential geometry of a space curve from that of two corresponding image curves. Third, the differential motion of an image curve is derived from camera motion and the differential geometry and motion of the space curve. The availability of such a theory enables novel curve-based multiview reconstruction and camera estimation systems to augment existing point-based approaches. This theory has been used to reconstruct a "3D curve sketch", to determine camera pose from local curve geometry, and tracking; other developments are underway.

Nghiên cứu tại Hà Nội đã đánh giá vai trò của siêu âm trong chẩn đoán bệnh viêm tử cung ở chó, một bệnh lý phổ biến gây ảnh hưởng đến sức khỏe sinh sản của chó cái. Kết quả cho thấy siêu âm là phương pháp hiệu quả để phát hiện và xác định mức độ nghiêm trọng của bệnh viêm tử cung, từ đó giúp bác sĩ thú y đưa ra phác đồ điều trị phù hợp. Nghiên cứu cũng đề xuất các phác đồ điều trị khác nhau dựa trên kết quả siêu âm, bao gồm điều trị nội khoa bằng kháng sinh và phẫu thuật cắt bỏ tử cung. Việc ứng dụng siêu âm trong chẩn đoán sớm và điều trị kịp thời bệnh viêm tử cung ở chó không chỉ nâng cao hiệu quả điều trị mà còn góp phần bảo vệ sức khỏe sinh sản và kéo dài tuổi thọ cho chó nuôi. Các phác đồ điều trị được đề xuất cung cấp hướng dẫn hữu ích cho các bác sĩ thú y trong thực hành lâm sàng, đặc biệt ở khu vực Hà Nội.

This paper presents a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based super-resolution technique designed to enhance the detection of active fires using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery. The objective of this research is to address the limitations of low-resolution thermal data, which often hinder accurate fire detection and monitoring in remote sensing applications. Our approach leverages a deep learning framework to reconstruct high-resolution fire maps from Sentinel-2's multispectral bands, enabling precise localization and characterization of active fire events. The proposed CNN model incorporates multi-scale feature extraction and residual learning to improve spatial resolution while preserving thermal signatures. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in fire detection accuracy, with the model achieving a 15% higher F1-score compared to traditional methods. Additionally, the system exhibits robust performance across diverse geographical regions and varying fire intensities. The findings highlight the potential of super-resolution techniques in enhancing satellite-based fire monitoring systems, offering valuable insights for disaster management and environmental protection. This research contributes to the advancement of remote sensing technologies by providing a scalable and efficient solution for real-time fire detection, with implications for improving early warning systems and mitigating wildfire impacts. **Keywords**: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), super-resolution, active fire detection, Sentinel-2, remote sensing, deep learning, wildfire monitoring.

This paper introduces a novel computational model for salient object subitizing, the rapid and accurate enumeration of small numbers of salient objects (typically up to four) without conscious counting. We propose a biologically inspired architecture that integrates bottom-up saliency detection with top-down attentional modulation. The model employs a parallel processing mechanism based on Gabor filters and a center-surround difference of Gaussian (DoG) to extract salient features. These features are then fed into a winner-take-all network, which identifies and isolates individual salient objects. A summation mechanism aggregates the activity from the identified objects to estimate the numerosity. We evaluated the model on a diverse dataset of synthetic and real-world images, demonstrating its ability to accurately subitize salient objects under varying conditions of clutter and object similarity. The model’s performance closely aligns with human behavioral data, showing characteristic subitizing range and error patterns. Furthermore, we compare the model's performance against existing object detection and counting algorithms, highlighting its efficiency and robustness for rapid numerosity estimation of salient objects. Our findings suggest a plausible neural mechanism for subitizing and provide a foundation for developing more efficient computer vision systems for scene understanding and object tracking. Keywords: Subitizing, Salient Object Detection, Numerosity Estimation, Computer Vision, Attention, Cognitive Modeling.

Communication bottlenecks often impede the scalability of distributed learning algorithms. Error feedback (EF) is a popular technique for reducing communication costs by compressing gradients, but it can suffer from slow convergence or instability. This paper introduces a novel gradient compression method, termed Variance-Reduced Error Feedback (VREF), designed to overcome these limitations. VREF incorporates a variance reduction mechanism into the EF framework, effectively mitigating the error accumulation that hinders convergence. We provide theoretical convergence guarantees for VREF under various settings, demonstrating its superiority over standard EF. Empirical evaluations on benchmark datasets and models, including image classification tasks with ResNet architectures, show that VREF achieves significantly faster convergence rates and higher accuracy compared to state-of-the-art EF variants. Furthermore, VREF exhibits robustness to heterogeneous data distributions and is readily applicable to diverse distributed learning scenarios. These results highlight VREF as a promising alternative to existing gradient compression techniques, offering improved communication efficiency and convergence performance in distributed learning. Keywords: Distributed Learning, Error Feedback, Gradient Compression, Variance Reduction, Communication Efficiency, Convergence Analysis.

Đặt vấn đề: Thừa cân, béo phì là nhóm bệnh nhân nguy cơ cao phát triển bệnh gan nhiễm mỡ liên quan chuyển hóa (Metabolic Associated Fatty Liver Disease - MAFLD) với odds ratios (OR): 5,5. MAFLD là nguyên nhân phổ biến thứ hai của bệnh nhân ung thư biểu mô tế bào gan. Nghiên cứu của Zysk và Gopalakriskna cho thấy có mối tương quan tuyến tính giữa giá trị độ nhiễm mỡ gan, độ cứng của gan và chỉ số khối cơ thể tương ứng r = 0,7, r = 0,3. Tại Việt Nam ung thư gan đứng ở vị trí thứ hai chiếm 11,7% năm 2022. Do đó, chúng tôi thực hiện đề tài này nhằm xác định mối tương quan giữa mức độ nhiễm mỡ và xơ hóa gan với chỉ số khối cơ thể và các yếu tố nguy cơ xơ hóa gan đáng kể ở bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc MAFLD góp phần cho việc quản lý tốt hơn nhóm bệnh nhân này. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang trên bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì từ 18 tuổi trở lên đến khám tại phòng khám của bệnh viện Nhân dân 115 trong thời gian tháng 3/2024 đến tháng 6/2024 Kết quả: 140 bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc MAFLD được đưa vào nghiên cứu. Trong bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc MAFLD, có mối tương quan tuyến tính giữa BMI và LSM cũng như BMI và CAP tương ứng r = 0,5, r = 0,8. Khi phân tích đa biến chỉ có BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2 (OR:4,17), MAFLD đồng mắc (OR: 4,74) là yếu tố nguy cơ của xơ hóa đáng kể. Kết luận: Trong bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc MAFLD, có mối tương quan tuyến tính giữa LSM và BMI với r = 0,5 cũng như CAP và BMI với r = 0,8. MAFLD đồng mắc và BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2 là yếu tố nguy cơ của xơ hóa gan đáng kể ở bệnh nhân thừa cân, béo phì mắc MAFLD.

Thiên tai và biến đổi khí hậu đang ngày càng trở thành mối đe dọa lớn đối với ngành xây dựng. Để giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực từ những yếu tố này, cần áp dụng một số giải pháp kỹ thuật hiệu quả. Đầu tiên, việc thiết kế công trình cần chú trọng đến khả năng chống chịu với thiên tai, bao gồm việc sử dụng vật liệu bền vững và công nghệ hiện đại. Thứ hai, quy hoạch xây dựng cần được thực hiện một cách khoa học, tránh xây dựng ở những khu vực dễ bị tổn thương. Cuối cùng, cần có sự phối hợp chặt chẽ giữa các cơ quan chức năng và cộng đồng trong việc triển khai các giải pháp này, nhằm đảm bảo an toàn và bền vững cho các công trình xây dựng trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu ngày càng nghiêm trọng.

For relocalization in large-scale point clouds, we propose the first approach that unifies global place recognition and local 6DoF pose refinement. To this end, we design a Siamese network that jointly learns 3D local feature detection and description directly from raw 3D points. It integrates FlexConv and Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) to assure that the learned local descriptor captures multi-level geometric information and channel-wise relations. For detecting 3D keypoints we predict the discriminativeness of the local descriptors in an unsupervised manner. We generate the global descriptor by directly aggregating the learned local descriptors with an effective attention mechanism. In this way, local and global 3D descriptors are inferred in one single forward pass. Experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves competitive results for both global point cloud retrieval and local point cloud registration in comparison to state-of-the-art approaches. To validate the generalizability and robustness of our 3D keypoints, we demonstrate that our method also performs favorably without fine-tuning on the registration of point clouds that were generated by a visual SLAM system. Code and related materials are available at https://vision.in.tum.de/research/vslam/dh3d.

Background and Motivation: The rise of centralized video sharing platforms has led to concerns over data ownership, censorship, and revenue distribution. The need for a decentralized alternative has become increasingly important, prompting research into blockchain-based solutions. Objectives: This thesis aims to design and develop a decentralized video sharing website utilizing Eueno and smart contracts. The primary objectives are to create a platform that ensures content creators' ownership and control over their work, provides a transparent and fair revenue distribution system, and promotes community-driven moderation. Methodology: The website's architecture is built on Eueno, a blockchain-based framework, and smart contracts are used to automate revenue distribution and content moderation. A decentralized storage solution is integrated to store video content, ensuring data persistence and availability. Results and Expected Contributions: The developed platform demonstrates a functional decentralized video sharing website, enabling content creators to upload, share, and monetize their videos in a trustless and transparent environment. The use of smart contracts and blockchain technology ensures that revenue is distributed fairly and that community guidelines are enforced. This research contributes to the development of decentralized social media platforms, promoting a more equitable and open internet. Conclusion: This thesis presents a decentralized video sharing website, leveraging Eueno and smart contracts to create a more transparent and community-driven platform. The results of this research have significant implications for the future of social media and content sharing. Future developments may focus on scaling the platform, improving user experience, and exploring additional applications of blockchain technology in the media industry.

Recently image inpainting has witnessed rapid progress due to generative adversarial networks (GAN) that are able to synthesize realistic contents. However, most existing GAN-based methods for semantic inpainting apply an auto-encoder architecture with a fully connected layer, which cannot accurately maintain spatial information. In addition, the discriminator in existing GANs struggle to understand high-level semantics within the image context and yield semantically consistent content. Existing evaluation criteria are biased towards blurry results and cannot well characterize edge preservation and visual authenticity in the inpainting results. In this paper, we propose an improved generative adversarial network to overcome the aforementioned limitations. Our proposed GAN-based framework consists of a fully convolutional design for the generator which helps to better preserve spatial structures and a joint loss function with a revised perceptual loss to capture high-level semantics in the context. Furthermore, we also introduce two novel measures to better assess the quality of image inpainting results. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms the state of the art under a wide range of criteria.

Road detection is a crucial task for autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). This paper presents a novel approach to road detection by fusing LiDAR point clouds and camera images using a fully convolutional neural network (FCN). Our method leverages the complementary strengths of both modalities: LiDAR provides accurate 3D spatial information, while camera images offer rich texture and color details. The proposed FCN architecture effectively integrates these features through a multi-modal fusion module, enabling robust road segmentation even in challenging scenarios with varying lighting conditions and complex road structures. We evaluate our method on a publicly available dataset and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness. The results highlight the effectiveness of LiDAR-camera fusion for road detection using FCNs, offering a promising solution for enhancing the performance of autonomous navigation systems. Keywords: Road detection, LiDAR, Camera, Sensor Fusion, Fully Convolutional Neural Network, Autonomous Driving.

The objective of this research is to address the challenge of achieving fairness in Vertical Federated Learning (VFL), a paradigm where multiple parties collaboratively train machine learning models without sharing their raw data. Despite its advantages in preserving data privacy, VFL often struggles with biased outcomes due to inherent data imbalances across parties. To mitigate this issue, we propose a novel fairness enhancement framework integrated within the VFL pipeline. Our method leverages an adaptive reweighting mechanism based on fairness metrics that adjust model updates to balance disparate impacts across data strata. We conducted extensive experiments on benchmark datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of our approach. The results demonstrate significant improvements in model fairness while maintaining competitive accuracy compared to conventional VFL models. This work not only advances the state-of-the-art in reducing bias in federated environments but also opens pathways for its broader application across domains necessitating equitable AI solutions. Key insights reveal the potential of the proposed framework to be integrated into diverse collaborative learning scenarios, ensuring that ethical considerations in AI deployments are met. Keywords: Vertical Federated Learning, model fairness, data privacy, bias mitigation, adaptive reweighting.
