We address the challenge of computing realistic barycenters of natural images to enable high-quality image morphing. While classical Wasserstein barycenters provide a mathematically grounded interpolation of pixel distributions, they often produce artifacts, blurred textures, and semantic inconsistencies when applied directly to high-dimensional image data. To overcome these limitations, we propose a constrained optimal transport framework that incorporates color histogram alignment, spatial smoothness, and patch-level coherence into the barycenter computation. Our method leverages entropic regularization for computational efficiency and employs an alternating optimization scheme that projects intermediate solutions onto constraint sets, thereby preserving local structure and global feature distributions. Experiments on standard image benchmarks demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, yielding lower transport cost and perceptual distance metrics alongside visually smooth, artifact-free morphing sequences. Ablation studies confirm the individual and combined benefits of each constraint. The resulting framework offers a versatile tool for applications such as animation, data augmentation, and style transfer. Our implementation is publicly released to promote further advances in constrained optimal transport for image processing. Keywords: constrained Wasserstein barycenter, optimal transport, image morphing, entropic regularization, natural image interpolation.

This paper presents the development of a compressed object detection model based on YOLOv4, specifically tailored for efficient deployment on embedded GPU platforms within autonomous systems. The primary objective is to address the challenges of limited computational resources and power constraints commonly encountered in embedded environments, such as those found in robotics and autonomous vehicles. We propose a novel compression approach combining model pruning and quantization techniques to significantly reduce the model size and computational complexity while preserving detection accuracy. The proposed framework was implemented and evaluated on an NVIDIA Jetson platform, demonstrating substantial reductions in memory usage and inference latency compared to the baseline YOLOv4 model. Experimental results show that our compressed model maintains over 95% of the original detection accuracy while achieving up to 60% reduction in model size and a 2x increase in inference speed. This work underscores the feasibility of deploying advanced deep learning-based object detection on resource-constrained autonomous platforms, enabling real-time perception capabilities. Key contributions include the integration of compression strategies with the YOLOv4 architecture and comprehensive performance evaluation on actual embedded GPU hardware. Our findings have significant implications for the scalable and energy-efficient deployment of AI-driven perception systems in a broad range of autonomous and edge computing applications. Keywords: YOLOv4, object detection, model compression, pruning, quantization, embedded GPU, autonomous system, real-time inference.

Time series forecasting is crucial for various applications, yet effectively capturing complex spatial-temporal dependencies remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces NAST, a novel Non-Autoregressive Spatial-Temporal Transformer model designed to enhance forecasting accuracy and efficiency. NAST leverages a transformer architecture to simultaneously model spatial and temporal relationships, circumventing the limitations of autoregressive models which rely on sequential prediction. Our approach employs a unique spatial attention mechanism to capture inter-variable correlations and a temporal attention mechanism to model long-range dependencies. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that NAST achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance, exhibiting significant improvements in accuracy compared to existing autoregressive and non-autoregressive methods, while also substantially reducing inference time. NAST offers a promising framework for efficient and accurate time series forecasting, particularly in scenarios with intricate spatial-temporal dynamics. Keywords: Time Series Forecasting, Non-Autoregressive, Transformer, Spatial-Temporal Modeling, Deep Learning.

Convolutional filters play a crucial role in image processing by detecting both simple and complex features, independent of their position or orientation within an image. Among the various sizes, the 3x3 convolutional filter is the most widely used, striking a balance between computational efficiency and the ability to capture essential patterns in visual data.

The increasing demands for effective image search systems necessitate advancements that incorporate both visual and linguistic cues. This research introduces TRACE, a novel framework designed to enhance image search capabilities by utilizing text feedback to refine visiolinguistic representations. Methods/Approach: TRACE employs a multi-stage process to transform, aggregate, and compose visiolinguistic representations. Initially, the model extracts and transforms visual and textual features using advanced neural networks. These features are then aggregated through a cross-modal attention mechanism, allowing for seamless integration of visual cues and text feedback. Image-to-image (i2i) translation is the dense regression problem of learning how to transform an input image into an output using aligned image pairs. Remarkable progress has been made in i2i translation with the advent of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) and particular using the learning paradigm of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). In the absence of paired images, i2i translation is tackled with one or multiple domain transformations (i.e., CycleGAN, StarGAN etc.). In this paper, we study a new problem, that of image-to-image translation, under a set of continuous parameters that correspond to a model describing a physical process. In particular, we propose the SliderGAN which transforms an input face image into a new one according to the continuous values of a statistical blendshape model of facial motion. We show that it is possible to edit a facial image according to expression and speech blendshapes, using sliders that control the continuous values of the blendshape model. This provides much more flexibility in various tasks, including but not limited to face editing, expression transfer and face neutralisation, comparing to models based on discrete expressions or action units.

This paper introduces Evolving-Graph Gaussian Processes (EGGP), a novel framework for modeling data that is structured over dynamic graphs, where both the graph topology and node attributes may change over time. Traditional Gaussian Processes (GPs) have proven effective for regression and classification on static data but face challenges when applied to temporally varying graph domains. Our approach extends standard GP models by integrating evolving-graph kernels, enabling flexible, non-parametric representation of time-dependent structural patterns in graph-structured data. We formalize the EGGP framework, propose efficient algorithms for scalable inference, and demonstrate its effectiveness using both synthetic and real-world datasets from domains such as social network analysis and sensor networks. Experimental results show that EGGP significantly outperforms existing static or sequence-based GP methods in predictive accuracy and adaptability to evolving structures. Our findings highlight the potential of EGGP to advance the analysis of dynamic graph data in various Information Technology applications, including anomaly detection, forecasting, and recommendation systems. Keywords: Gaussian Processes, evolving graphs, dynamic networks, kernel methods, graph machine learning, temporal modeling.

Off-policy reinforcement learning (RL) offers the potential for efficient learning by leveraging experience generated from diverse sources. However, learning with delayed rewards poses a significant challenge, as the temporal credit assignment problem is exacerbated. This paper investigates the impact of delayed rewards on the stability and convergence of off-policy RL algorithms. We introduce a novel approach, the Delayed Reward Correction (DRC) method, which utilizes a learned reward model to estimate and correct for reward delays during policy evaluation. The DRC method incorporates a temporal consistency constraint to improve the accuracy of the reward model. Experimental results on a suite of benchmark tasks with varying reward delays demonstrate that DRC significantly improves the sample efficiency and stability of off-policy algorithms, particularly Q-learning and SARSA, compared to existing delay-agnostic methods. Our findings indicate that explicitly addressing reward delays is crucial for effective off-policy RL in environments with sparse or delayed feedback. This work contributes a practical and theoretically grounded method for handling delayed rewards, paving the way for broader application of off-policy RL in real-world scenarios. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Off-Policy Learning, Delayed Rewards, Temporal Credit Assignment, Reward Shaping.

Emergence of artificial intelligence techniques in biomedical applications urges the researchers to pay more attention on the uncertainty quantification (UQ) in machine-assisted medical decision making. For classification tasks, prior studies on UQ are difficult to compare with each other, due to the lack of a unified quantitative evaluation metric. Considering that well-performing UQ models ought to know when the classification models act incorrectly, we design a new evaluation metric, area under Confidence-Classification Characteristic curves (AUCCC), to quantitatively evaluate the performance of the UQ models. AUCCC is threshold-free, robust to perturbation, and insensitive to the classification performance. We evaluate several UQ methods (e.g., max softmax output) with AUCCC to validate its effectiveness. Furthermore, a simple scheme, named Uncertainty Distillation (UDist), is developed to boost the UQ performance, where a confidence model is distilling the confidence estimated by deep ensembles. The proposed method is easy to implement; it consistently outperforms strong baselines on natural and medical image datasets in our experiments.

This paper addresses the vulnerability of object detection models to adversarial attacks, with a focus on developing transferable attacks that can be applied to both image and video object detection systems. Our approach utilizes a novel algorithm that generates adversarial examples by perturbing the input data in a way that is imperceptible to humans, yet effectively deceives the object detection models. We evaluate the effectiveness of our method on various state-of-the-art object detection architectures, including YOLO and Faster R-CNN, and demonstrate its ability to transfer across different models and datasets. Our results show that the proposed attack can successfully evade object detection in both images and videos, with a significant reduction in detection accuracy. The implications of this research highlight the need for more robust object detection systems, and our contributions pave the way for the development of more secure and reliable computer vision models. Key keywords: adversarial attacks, object detection, image and video analysis, computer vision, deep learning, transferable attacks, YOLO, Faster R-CNN.

Computer-aided design (CAD) is the most widely used modeling approach for technical design. The typical starting point in these designs is 2D sketches which can later be extruded and combined to obtain complex three-dimensional assemblies. Such sketches are typically composed of parametric primitives, such as points, lines, and circular arcs, augmented with geometric constraints linking the primitives, such as coincidence, parallelism, or orthogonality. Sketches can be represented as graphs, with the primitives as nodes and the constraints as edges. Training a model to automatically generate CAD sketches can enable several novel workflows, but is challenging due to the complexity of the graphs and the heterogeneity of the primitives and constraints. In particular, each type of primitive and constraint may require a record of different size and parameter types. We propose SketchGen as a generative model based on a transformer architecture to address the heterogeneity problem by carefully designing a sequential language for the primitives and constraints that allows distinguishing between different primitive or constraint types and their parameters, while encouraging our model to re-use information across related parameters, encoding shared structure. A particular highlight of our work is the ability to produce primitives linked via constraints that enables the final output to be further regularized via a constraint solver. We evaluate our model by demonstrating constraint prediction for given sets of primitives and full sketch generation from scratch, showing that our approach significantly out performs the state-of-the-art in CAD sketch generation.

This paper presents an algorithm for the unsupervised learning of latent variable models from unlabeled sets of data. We base our technique on spectral decomposition, providing a technique that proves to be robust both in theory and in practice. We also describe how to use this algorithm to learn the parameters of two well known text mining models: single topic model and Latent Dirichlet Allocation, providing in both cases an efficient technique to retrieve the parameters to feed the algorithm. We compare the results of our algorithm with those of existing algorithms on synthetic data, and we provide examples of applications to real world text corpora for both single topic model and LDA, obtaining meaningful results.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) in the infinite width/channel limit have received much attention recently, as they provide a clear analytical window to deep learning via mappings to Gaussian Processes (GPs). Despite its theoretical appeal, this viewpoint lacks a crucial ingredient of deep learning in finite DNNs, laying at the heart of their success -- feature learning. Here we consider DNNs trained with noisy gradient descent on a large training set and derive a self consistent Gaussian Process theory accounting for strong finite-DNN and feature learning effects. Applying this to a toy model of a two-layer linear convolutional neural network (CNN) shows good agreement with experiments. We further identify, both analytical and numerically, a sharp transition between a feature learning regime and a lazy learning regime in this model. Strong finite-DNN effects are also derived for a non-linear two-layer fully connected network. Our self consistent theory provides a rich and versatile analytical framework for studying feature learning and other non-lazy effects in finite DNNs.

Quản lý thoát nước mặt đô thị đang trở thành vấn đề cấp thiết trong các thành phố lớn. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, cần có cơ sở lý luận và pháp lý vững chắc. Một số cơ sở lý luận quan trọng bao gồm việc hiểu rõ về quá trình thoát nước mặt, tác động của nó đến môi trường và sức khỏe con người. Pháp lý cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc quản lý thoát nước mặt đô thị. Các quy định và chính sách về thoát nước mặt cần được xây dựng và thực thi một cách nghiêm ngặt. Điều này bao gồm việc quy định về tiêu chuẩn chất lượng nước thải, quy trình xử lý nước thải và trách nhiệm của các cơ quan quản lý. Hướng tới mô hình Thành phố bọt biển, các thành phố cần đầu tư vào hệ thống thoát nước mặt hiện đại, bao gồm cả hệ thống thu gom, xử lý và tái sử dụng nước thải. Điều này không chỉ giúp giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực đến môi trường mà còn tạo ra nguồn nước sạch cho các mục đích sử dụng khác. Bên cạnh đó, cần có sự tham gia của cộng đồng và các tổ chức liên quan trong việc quản lý thoát nước mặt đô thị. Điều này bao gồm việc giáo dục và nâng cao nhận thức về tầm quan trọng của việc bảo vệ môi trường, cũng như việc tham gia vào các hoạt động bảo vệ môi trường. Tóm lại, quản lý thoát nước mặt đô thị là một vấn đề phức tạp đòi hỏi sự kết hợp của cơ sở lý luận và pháp lý vững chắc, cùng với sự tham gia của cộng đồng và các tổ chức liên quan.

This paper addresses the critical issue of adversarial attacks on graph-based learning models, which can compromise their performance and reliability. We introduce a novel approach, termed Adversarial Immunization, to enhance certifiable robustness, ensuring that these models can withstand and perform reliably under adversarial conditions. Methods/Approach: Our proposed method leverages a defensive strategy that integrates adversarial training with robust optimization techniques specific to graph structures. By modeling the intricacies of graph data, the approach strengthens the resistance of graph neural networks against adversarial perturbations. We implement and evaluate this method across various graph-based learning scenarios to test its effectiveness. Results/Findings: The Adversarial Immunization approach demonstrates significant improvements in the robustness of graph learning models. Our results show a consistent enhancement in certifiable robustness, with experimental data indicating a 20-30% increase in reliable performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. These findings are validated through assessments on benchmark graph datasets, showing the method's superiority in maintaining accuracy under adversarial attacks. Conclusion/Implications: The proposed Adversarial Immunization approach presents a substantial advancement in defending graph-based models against adversarial threats, offering a certifiable assurance of robustness. This research contributes to the field by providing a scalable solution that can be applied to a broad range of applications involving graph data, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and bioinformatics. The results underscore the potential for developing more secure and reliable graph learning systems, paving the way for further research in robust graph-based AI technologies. Keywords: adversarial attacks, graph neural networks, certifiable robustness, adversarial training, robust optimization, graph-based learning models.

Hồ Chí Minh đã để lại một di sản văn hóa vô giá, thể hiện tầm nhìn sâu rộng về vai trò của văn hóa trong sự nghiệp cách mạng và xây dựng đất nước. Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam đã vận dụng sáng tạo tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về văn hóa trong quá trình lãnh đạo cách mạng, đặc biệt trong công cuộc đổi mới đất nước. Nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc tạo ra các dòng dâu tây lưỡng bội thuần chủng thông qua nuôi cấy bao phấn, một kỹ thuật androgensesis in vitro. Các nhà khoa học đã tối ưu hóa quy trình này trên giống dâu tây trung tính ngày, Fragaria × ananassa Duch. Bằng cách nuôi cấy bao phấn ở các giai đoạn phát triển khác nhau trên môi trường phù hợp, họ đã thành công trong việc tạo ra callus và sau đó là cây con. Phân tích ploidy cho thấy một tỷ lệ đáng kể các cây con là lưỡng bội, cho thấy sự thành công của androgensesis. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp một phương pháp hiệu quả để tạo ra các dòng dâu tây thuần chủng, có giá trị trong các chương trình nhân giống để cải thiện các đặc tính mong muốn như năng suất, chất lượng quả và khả năng kháng bệnh. Kỹ thuật này có tiềm năng đẩy nhanh quá trình tạo giống và mở rộng sự đa dạng di truyền trong dâu tây.

This paper presents a comprehensive benchmarking study on word image recognition, aiming to evaluate and compare the performance of various recognition models on diverse word image datasets. The objective is to identify the most effective approaches and pinpoint areas for improvement in this crucial aspect of document image analysis. A range of state-of-the-art models, including deep learning-based architectures, are assessed using a multi-faceted evaluation methodology. The results show significant variations in model performance across different datasets, with top-performing models achieving notable accuracy improvements. Key findings highlight the importance of dataset diversity, image quality, and model generalizability. The study concludes by emphasizing the need for standardized benchmarking protocols and proposing future research directions to advance the field of word image recognition. This research contributes to the development of more accurate and robust recognition systems, with potential applications in document digitization, text retrieval, and optical character recognition (OCR), and is relevant to keywords such as word image recognition, document image analysis, deep learning, and OCR benchmarking.

This paper introduces ChainerRL, a deep reinforcement learning library designed to facilitate the development and implementation of reinforcement learning algorithms. The objective of ChainerRL is to provide a flexible and efficient framework for researchers and practitioners to build, train, and deploy reinforcement learning models. ChainerRL utilizes a modular architecture, allowing users to easily implement and combine various reinforcement learning techniques, such as deep Q-networks, policy gradient methods, and actor-critic algorithms. The library is built on top of the Chainer deep learning framework, enabling seamless integration with existing deep learning tools and techniques. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of ChainerRL in training agents to solve complex tasks, including robotic control and game playing. The key findings highlight the library's ability to achieve state-of-the-art performance while reducing the complexity and effort required to implement reinforcement learning algorithms. ChainerRL contributes to the field by providing a comprehensive and user-friendly library for deep reinforcement learning, making it an ideal tool for researchers and practitioners working in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and robotics. Key keywords: deep reinforcement learning, Chainer, library, AI, machine learning, robotics.

This paper presents PFDet, a state-of-the-art object detection system that achieved 2nd place in the Open Images Challenge 2018 Object Detection Track. The objective of this research is to develop an accurate and efficient object detection model capable of handling a large number of classes and instances. To achieve this, we employ a novel approach combining feature pyramid networks with a modified Faster R-CNN architecture. Our method utilizes a multi-scale feature extraction technique, enabling the detection of objects at various scales. The results show that PFDet outperforms several baseline models, achieving a significant improvement in detection accuracy. Key findings include a 5% increase in mean average precision compared to the top-performing single-model entry. The contributions of this research lie in the design of a robust and scalable object detection framework, with potential applications in autonomous vehicles, surveillance, and image analysis. The PFDet system demonstrates the effectiveness of combining advanced feature extraction techniques with well-established object detection architectures, making it a valuable contribution to the field of computer vision and object detection. Keywords: object detection, Open Images Challenge, feature pyramid networks, Faster R-CNN, computer vision.

Early quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols, notably BB84 and E91, have transitioned from theoretical proposals to practical implementations in real-world communication networks since around 2005. These protocols have demonstrated secure quantum communication over increasingly long distances, reaching up to 1,000 kilometers using fiber optic cables. However, this progress is fundamentally constrained by photon losses inherent to optical fibers, which severely limit the range and scalability of terrestrial QKD systems. To overcome these distance limitations and enable secure communications over intercontinental or even global scales, researchers have turned to satellite-based QKD as a promising solution. A prominent example is the Micius satellite, which has performed pioneering quantum communication experiments between space and ground stations. Despite such advancements, satellite QKD presents its own set of formidable technical challenges, including severe signal attenuation during transmission through Earth's atmosphere and rapidly changing environmental conditions that can introduce noise and instability. Addressing these challenges is critical for the future development of global-scale quantum-secure communication networks.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficient learning in temporal difference (TD) methods, a crucial aspect of reinforcement learning. The objective is to improve the convergence and stability of TD learning by introducing source traces, a novel approach that modifies the traditional TD update rule. Our method utilizes a trace-based framework to incorporate additional information from the environment, enhancing the learning process. The key findings indicate that source traces lead to faster convergence and more accurate value function estimates compared to conventional TD methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in various environments, showcasing its potential for applications in complex decision-making tasks. This research contributes to the advancement of reinforcement learning by providing a new perspective on TD learning, highlighting the importance of incorporating environmental information to improve learning efficiency. Key aspects of this work include temporal difference learning, reinforcement learning, and trace-based methods, making it relevant to researchers and practitioners in the field of artificial intelligence and machine learning.

This paper investigates the effectiveness of training Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) directly on word observation data, bypassing traditional feature engineering steps. We explore the feasibility of learning meaningful word representations and language models using RBMs without explicit pre-processing or dimensionality reduction techniques like bag-of-words or TF-IDF. Our approach leverages a modified RBM architecture and training procedure tailored to handle the high dimensionality and sparsity inherent in word observation data. Experiments on benchmark text corpora demonstrate that RBMs can successfully learn latent semantic relationships between words, achieving competitive performance in language modeling tasks compared to other unsupervised learning methods. Furthermore, we analyze the learned features to reveal how the RBM captures contextual information and semantic similarity. This work provides a novel perspective on unsupervised language modeling, showcasing the potential of RBMs for learning directly from raw text data, and offering an alternative to more complex neural network architectures. Keywords: Restricted Boltzmann Machine, RBM, Word Embeddings, Language Modeling, Unsupervised Learning, Natural Language Processing.

Abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenge of enhancing the interpretability of attention mechanisms in modern deep learning models, with a focus on achieving high resolution, computational efficiency, and accuracy. We propose a novel high-resolution attention framework designed to provide fine-grained, visually comprehensible attention maps without sacrificing speed or performance. Our approach integrates an efficient hierarchical attention computation strategy that reduces complexity while preserving detailed spatial information, facilitating rapid processing and real-time applicability. Empirical evaluations across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our model not only delivers accurate predictions but also generates attention maps that closely align with human intuition and ground-truth relevance regions. Comparative analysis shows significant improvements in both interpretability and inference speed compared to existing state-of-the-art attention methods. The proposed framework supports transparent decision-making in applications such as image classification, natural language processing, and medical diagnosis, enabling practitioners to better understand and trust model outputs. These results highlight the potential of our model to set new standards for interpretable and efficient attention-based systems in artificial intelligence. The rapid increase in highway traffic necessitates efficient and accurate monitoring systems to ensure safety and manage congestion. This paper addresses the problem of detecting and analyzing traffic events through video surveillance using advanced deep learning techniques. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel deep learning framework that leverages Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to process and interpret video data from highway surveillance cameras. The system is designed to automatically detect and classify various traffic events, such as accidents and bottlenecks, through real-time video analysis. The architecture incorporates transfer learning to enhance model accuracy and reduce computational overhead. Results/Findings: The proposed system was evaluated on a comprehensive dataset of highway traffic videos. Our results demonstrate significant improvements in detection accuracy and processing speed compared to traditional methods. The deep learning model achieved an average precision of 92% and successfully identified critical traffic incidents with minimal false positives. Additionally, a comparison with state-of-the-art approaches highlights the efficiency and reliability of our method. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field of intelligent transportation systems by offering a robust solution for real-time traffic surveillance. The integration of deep learning architectures not only enhances event detection capabilities but also provides scalable applications for different traffic monitoring scenarios. The system's potential for deployment in smart city infrastructure underscores its value in improving road safety and traffic management. Keywords: video surveillance, highway traffic, deep learning, CNN, RNN, traffic event detection, intelligent transportation systems.

Tác động của đặc điểm hội đồng quản trị đến chất lượng lợi nhuận của các công ty niêm yết Việt Nam Hội đồng quản trị (HĐQT) là bộ phận quan trọng của một công ty, chịu trách nhiệm đưa ra quyết định quan trọng về chiến lược và hoạt động kinh doanh. Đặc điểm của HĐQT có thể ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng lợi nhuận của công ty. Các nghiên cứu gần đây cho thấy rằng, các công ty có HĐQT có tính độc lập cao, có kinh nghiệm và có trình độ chuyên môn thường có lợi nhuận tốt hơn. Một số đặc điểm của HĐQT có thể ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng lợi nhuận bao gồm: - Tính độc lập: Khi HĐQT độc lập với ban điều hành, họ có thể đưa ra quyết định độc lập và không bị ảnh hưởng bởi lợi ích cá nhân. - Kinh nghiệm: Khi HĐQT có kinh nghiệm trong lĩnh vực kinh doanh, họ có thể đưa ra quyết định sáng suốt và hiệu quả hơn. - Trình độ chuyên môn: Khi HĐQT có trình độ chuyên môn cao, họ có thể đưa ra quyết định chính xác và hiệu quả hơn. Các công ty niêm yết Việt Nam có thể học hỏi từ các công ty nước ngoài về cách xây dựng và quản lý HĐQT hiệu quả. Điều này có thể giúp họ cải thiện chất lượng lợi nhuận và tăng cường sự cạnh tranh trên thị trường.

The paper addresses the significant challenge of tracking road users accurately in real-time, which is crucial for traffic management and autonomous vehicle systems. The goal is to develop a robust methodology that enhances the precision and reliability of tracking multiple road users simultaneously. Methods/Approach: The research leverages Constraint Programming (CP), a powerful paradigm in computational problem-solving, to create a model that captures the dynamic and unpredictable nature of road environments. The approach integrates spatial and temporal constraints to effectively monitor and track the movements of vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians, ensuring comprehensive coverage and analysis. Results/Findings: The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in accurately tracking road users compared to traditional techniques. Empirical evaluations on simulated and real-world datasets show an improvement in tracking accuracy and efficiency, even in complex scenarios with high user density and occlusions. The system exhibits a high degree of flexibility and adaptability to various road conditions. Conclusion/Implications: This study contributes a novel application of Constraint Programming to road user tracking, offering significant advancements over existing approaches. The findings have important implications for the development of intelligent transportation systems, enhancing road safety, and supporting the deployment of autonomous traffic solutions. Future applications may expand to include integration with smart city infrastructures for broader impacts. Keywords: Constraint Programming, road user tracking, traffic management, autonomous vehicles, intelligent transportation systems, real-time monitoring, spatial-temporal analysis.

Instance segmentation aims to identify and delineate each object instance within an image. This paper addresses limitations in conventional embedding learning approaches for instance segmentation, which often struggle with accurately separating instances, particularly when the number of instances is unknown or variable. We propose a novel framework that incorporates the number of clusters as a crucial parameter during embedding learning. Our approach leverages a clustering loss function that is explicitly guided by the estimated number of instances, allowing the model to learn more discriminative embeddings. We evaluated our method on standard benchmark datasets, including COCO and Cityscapes, demonstrating significant improvements in segmentation accuracy and instance separation compared to state-of-the-art embedding-based methods. Specifically, our method achieves a substantial increase in Average Precision (AP) and Average Recall (AR) metrics. The proposed approach enhances the robustness of instance segmentation, especially in scenarios with varying object densities and complex scenes. This research offers a promising direction for improving instance segmentation through refined embedding learning strategies. Keywords: Instance Segmentation, Embedding Learning, Clustering, Computer Vision, Deep Learning.

Với cảnh quan thiên nhiên hùng vĩ, các bản làng dân tộc thiểu số và những nét văn hóa đặc sắc, huyện đã xây dựng nhiều sản phẩm du lịch hấp dẫn. Chính quyền địa phương cũng đã triển khai các chương trình đào tạo cho người dân về kỹ năng phục vụ du lịch, từ đó nâng cao chất lượng dịch vụ. This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently performing reinforcement learning in environments with large and complex state spaces. We propose an innovative integration of cover trees with Bayesian reinforcement learning (RL) to improve scalability and decision-making accuracy. Methods/Approach: Our approach utilizes cover trees, a data structure that supports dynamic insertion and deletion of nodes while maintaining computational efficiency, to organize the large state space. The cover tree facilitates rapid nearest-neighbor searches and state transitions. We integrate this structure with a Bayesian framework that probabilistically models uncertainty over rewards and state transitions, leveraging it to guide exploration and exploitation. This combination aims to enhance the efficiency of Bayesian RL in high-dimensional environments by focusing computational resources on the most relevant parts of the state space. Results/Findings: Experiments demonstrate that Cover Tree Bayesian Reinforcement Learning significantly outperforms traditional approaches, especially in terms of sample efficiency and computational speed. We show that our model requires fewer interactions with the environment to achieve comparable or superior policy performance when benchmarked across various complex simulated tasks. The results underscore the importance of structure-aware modeling in effectively deploying Bayesian RL methods. Conclusion/Implications: The research introduces a novel integration of cover trees in the Bayesian RL domain, highlighting their utility in handling large-scale problems with dynamic and continuous state spaces. This method offers a scalable solution that can be applied to numerous real-world applications, from autonomous robotics to large-scale system management, where rapid decision-making and computational efficiency are critical. The contributions pave the way for future exploration of structured data representations in reinforcement learning contexts. Keywords: Bayesian Reinforcement Learning, Cover Trees, State Space, Scalability, Sample Efficiency, Decision-Making, Autonomous Systems.

This work introduces TrimTuner, the first system for optimizing machine learning jobs in the cloud to exploit sub-sampling techniques to reduce the cost of the optimization process while keeping into account user-specified constraints. TrimTuner jointly optimizes the cloud and application-specific parameters and, unlike state of the art works for cloud optimization, eschews the need to train the model with the full training set every time a new configuration is sampled. Indeed, by leveraging sub-sampling techniques and data-sets that are up to 60x smaller than the original one, we show that TrimTuner can reduce the cost of the optimization process by up to 50x. Further, TrimTuner speeds-up the recommendation process by 65x with respect to state of the art techniques for hyper-parameter optimization that use sub-sampling techniques. The reasons for this improvement are twofold: i) a novel domain specific heuristic that reduces the number of configurations for which the acquisition function has to be evaluated; ii) the adoption of an ensemble of decision trees that enables boosting the speed of the recommendation process by one additional order of magnitude.

Góc ma sát trong của đất cát là một yếu tố quan trọng trong xây dựng và công trình địa kỹ thuật. Để xác định góc ma sát trong này, các nhà khoa học đã thực hiện thí nghiệm nén một trục không nở hông. Quá trình thí nghiệm bao gồm việc đặt một trục kim loại vào trong đất cát và sau đó áp dụng lực lên trục để gây ra sự nén. Video-based person re-identification (reID) aims at matching the same person across video clips. It is a challenging task due to the existence of redundancy among frames, newly revealed appearance, occlusion, and motion blurs. In this paper, we propose an attentive feature aggregation module, namely Multi-Granularity Reference-aided Attentive Feature Aggregation (MG-RAFA), to delicately aggregate spatio-temporal features into a discriminative video-level feature representation. In order to determine the contribution/importance of a spatial-temporal feature node, we propose to learn the attention from a global view with convolutional operations. Specifically, we stack its relations, i.e., pairwise correlations with respect to a representative set of reference feature nodes (S-RFNs) that represents global video information, together with the feature itself to infer the attention. Moreover, to exploit the semantics of different levels, we propose to learn multi-granularity attentions based on the relations captured at different granularities. Extensive ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of our attentive feature aggregation module MG-RAFA. Our framework achieves the state-of-the-art performance on three benchmark datasets.

This paper investigates the training dynamics of deep neural networks (DNNs) under class-imbalanced conditions, revealing a novel phenomenon termed "minority collapse." We introduce the Layer-Peeled Model (LPM), a diagnostic tool that systematically removes layers from a trained DNN to assess the retained performance on both majority and minority classes. Through extensive experiments on diverse datasets, including image classification and natural language processing tasks, we observe that DNNs trained on imbalanced data often exhibit a disproportionate decline in minority class performance as layers are peeled away, indicating that crucial minority-specific information is concentrated in the deeper layers. This contrasts with majority class performance, which remains relatively robust to layer removal. The LPM analysis further suggests that minority collapse is exacerbated by increasing class imbalance ratios and network depth. Our findings provide valuable insights into the challenges of training DNNs with imbalanced data and highlight the need for targeted regularization or architectural modifications to mitigate minority collapse and improve overall model generalization. Keywords: deep neural networks, class imbalance, minority collapse, layer-peeled model, imbalanced learning, neural network training.

Human pose estimation is a critical task in computer vision with applications in human-computer interaction, augmented reality, and surveillance. This paper presents a novel approach termed Knowledge-Guided Deep Fractal Neural Networks (KG-DFNN) for accurate human pose estimation. The proposed method integrates domain-specific knowledge into a hierarchical fractal network architecture, enabling more effective extraction and representation of multi-scale spatial dependencies inherent in human body structures. The knowledge-guided component incorporates anatomical constraints and kinematic relationships during both training and inference, guiding the network toward physiologically plausible predictions and reducing ambiguities in challenging scenarios such as occlusions and complex articulations. Extensive experiments were conducted on standard benchmark datasets, demonstrating that KG-DFNN achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, outperforming existing convolutional and transformer-based models in keypoint localization metrics. Ablation studies further reveal that embedding prior knowledge significantly enhances robustness and generalization capability, particularly in diverse environmental conditions and pose variations. The results highlight the advantages of combining deep learning architectures with structured knowledge to advance pose estimation performance. This work contributes a flexible and scalable framework suitable for real-time human pose analysis in various applications. Key innovations include the integration of knowledge-guided modeling, fractal neural network design, and an effective multi-scale feature fusion strategy. Future research directions include extending the approach to 3D pose estimation and real-world deployment. Keywords: human pose estimation, deep learning, fractal neural networks, prior knowledge, multi-scale representation, computer vision.

Accurate survival prediction is critical for personalized cancer treatment planning. While machine learning models have shown promise in this area, they often lack reliable uncertainty estimates, hindering clinical adoption. This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework for cancer survival prediction that explicitly quantifies uncertainty. Our approach integrates a modified Cox proportional hazards model with a variational inference technique to estimate both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. We evaluate our method on several publicly available cancer genomic datasets, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy and well-calibrated uncertainty estimates compared to existing state-of-the-art survival models. The results show that incorporating uncertainty information leads to more robust and reliable survival predictions, offering clinicians a valuable tool for informed decision-making. The framework’s ability to identify high-risk patients with greater confidence has the potential to improve patient outcomes. Keywords: Cancer survival prediction, uncertainty estimation, deep learning, variational inference, Cox proportional hazards model.

To prevent errors in CD disc storage caused by long sequences of 0 bits, engineers use Run Length Limited (RLL) codes, which were invented by Immink. The purpose of these codes is to control the length of consecutive 0’s between two 1’s in the data sequence. Specifically, an (d, k)-RLL code restricts the number of consecutive 0’s to be at least d and at most k, where d and k are non-negative integers such that d is less than or equal to k. This limitation helps maintain data integrity during storage and retrieval.

This paper introduces LiDARTouch, a novel approach to monocular metric depth estimation that leverages the strengths of both computer vision and LiDAR technology. The objective is to achieve accurate depth estimation using a minimal number of LiDAR beams, making it a cost-effective and efficient solution for various applications. Our method employs a deep learning-based framework that combines the sparse depth measurements from a few-beam LiDAR with monocular images to produce high-resolution, metric depth maps. The results show that LiDARTouch outperforms state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation methods, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. The key contribution of this research is the development of a innovative fusion strategy that effectively integrates the complementary information from LiDAR and camera sensors. This work has important implications for applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality, where accurate and efficient depth estimation is crucial. By demonstrating the potential of combining computer vision and LiDAR technology, LiDARTouch paves the way for future research in this area, with key keywords including depth estimation, LiDAR, computer vision, deep learning, and sensor fusion.

We present two new metrics for evaluating generative models in the class-conditional image generation setting. These metrics are obtained by generalizing the two most popular unconditional metrics: the Inception Score (IS) and the Fre'chet Inception Distance (FID). A theoretical analysis shows the motivation behind each proposed metric and links the novel metrics to their unconditional counterparts. The link takes the form of a product in the case of IS or an upper bound in the FID case. We provide an extensive empirical evaluation, comparing the metrics to their unconditional variants and to other metrics, and utilize them to analyze existing generative models, thus providing additional insights about their performance, from unlearned classes to mode collapse.

Modeling inter-dependencies between time-series is the key to achieve high performance in anomaly detection for multivariate time-series data. The de-facto solution to model the dependencies is to feed the data into a recurrent neural network (RNN). However, the fully connected network structure underneath the RNN (either GRU or LSTM) assumes a static and complete dependency graph between time-series, which may not hold in many real-world applications. To alleviate this assumption, we propose a dynamic bipartite graph structure to encode the inter-dependencies between time-series. More concretely, we model time series as one type of nodes, and the time series segments (regarded as event) as another type of nodes, where the edge between two types of nodes describe a temporal pattern occurred on a specific time series at a certain time. Based on this design, relations between time series can be explicitly modelled via dynamic connections to event nodes, and the multivariate time-series anomaly detection problem can be formulated as a self-supervised, edge stream prediction problem in dynamic graphs. We conducted extensive experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of the design.

This paper introduces KPConv, a novel convolutional operator designed for point cloud processing, which enables flexible and deformable convolutional operations. Our approach leverages a kernel-point-based methodology, allowing the convolutional kernel to deform and adapt to the local geometry of the point cloud. The KPConv operator is designed to be flexible, efficient, and scalable, making it suitable for a wide range of point cloud-based applications. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of KPConv in achieving state-of-the-art performance on various 3D point cloud classification, segmentation, and reconstruction tasks. The key findings highlight the importance of adaptability and flexibility in convolutional operations for point cloud data. The proposed KPConv operator contributes to the advancement of 3D point cloud processing and has potential applications in fields such as computer vision, robotics, and autonomous driving. Key keywords: point clouds, convolutional neural networks, 3D processing, kernel-point-based methodology, deformable convolution.

This paper presents Transformer-XL, a novel neural network architecture aimed at addressing the limitations of fixed-length context in self-attentive language models. Traditional models are constrained by their inability to effectively model long-range dependencies, which hinders performance on tasks requiring comprehension of extensive contexts. Methods/Approach: Transformer-XL extends the standard Transformer architecture by introducing a recurrence mechanism that allows for the seamless integration of context from preceding segments. This approach improves context fragmentation by capturing long-range dependencies over extended text spans. It also incorporates segment-level recurrence with a position-wise encoding scheme to maintain temporal coherence across varying length inputs. Results/Findings: Through comprehensive evaluation on a range of benchmark datasets, Transformer-XL demonstrates significant outperformance of existing state-of-the-art models in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The model achieves superior results in language modeling and question-answering tasks, highlighting its capability to bridge long-term sequences effectively. In particular, it exhibits improved training speeds and computational efficiency without sacrificing processing power or memory overhead. Conclusion/Implications: Transformer-XL represents a crucial step forward in the development of language models by effectively handling arbitrary-length contexts, thus paving the way for more sophisticated natural language understanding applications. Its ability to model extended sequences with higher fidelity opens up possibilities for advancements in a variety of applications, such as machine translation, document summarization, and complex dialogue systems. Keywords: Transformer-XL, attentive language models, fixed-length context, long-range dependencies, neural network, natural language processing.

Sự gia tăng của khí thải các-bon đã dẫn đến sự nóng lên của Trái Đất, gây ra những hậu quả nghiêm trọng cho môi trường và sức khỏe con người. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, các nhà khoa học và chuyên gia đã đề xuất nhiều giải pháp khác nhau. Một trong những giải pháp được đề xuất là việc sử dụng năng lượng tái tạo, như năng lượng mặt trời và năng lượng gió, để thay thế cho năng lượng hóa thạch. Tuy nhiên, việc chuyển đổi sang năng lượng tái tạo cũng có những thách thức và khó khăn. Một trong những thách thức lớn nhất là việc xây dựng cơ sở hạ tầng để hỗ trợ cho việc sản xuất và phân phối năng lượng tái tạo. Một số quốc gia đã bắt đầu thực hiện các dự án lớn để xây dựng cơ sở hạ tầng cho năng lượng tái tạo. Ví dụ, ở Trung Quốc, chính phủ đã đầu tư hàng tỷ đô la vào việc xây dựng các trạm năng lượng mặt trời và năng lượng gió. Bên cạnh đó, các công nghệ mới cũng đang được phát triển để giúp giảm thiểu tác động của các-bon. Ví dụ, công nghệ lưu trữ năng lượng đã được cải tiến để giúp lưu trữ năng lượng tái tạo và giảm thiểu sự phụ thuộc vào năng lượng hóa thạch. Tổng kết, thị trường các-bon đang trở thành một vấn đề nghiêm trọng và cần được giải quyết một cách khẩn cấp. Việc sử dụng năng lượng tái tạo và phát triển công nghệ mới sẽ là những bước quan trọng để giúp giảm thiểu tác động của các-bon và xây dựng một tương lai bền vững hơn.

This paper introduces Mean Spectral Normalization (MSN), a novel technique designed to enhance the robustness and efficiency of deep neural networks deployed in resource-constrained embedded automation systems. The objective is to mitigate performance degradation caused by limited computational resources and data scarcity. MSN normalizes the weight matrices of neural network layers by constraining the mean of their singular values, unlike traditional spectral normalization that focuses solely on the largest singular value. This approach offers a more stable and less aggressive regularization, preserving essential feature representations. Experimental results on image classification and object detection tasks, executed on embedded platforms, demonstrate that MSN consistently outperforms standard spectral normalization and other regularization methods in terms of accuracy and convergence speed, particularly when training with limited data. Furthermore, MSN reduces computational overhead during inference, facilitating real-time performance on embedded devices. The findings suggest that MSN provides a practical and effective solution for deploying accurate and efficient deep learning models in embedded automation applications, representing a significant step toward reliable AI-driven automation. Keywords: Spectral Normalization, Deep Learning, Embedded Systems, Automation, Regularization, Neural Networks.

**Abstract:** Non-stationary time series data present significant challenges in predictive modeling due to their dynamic spectral characteristics and evolving statistical properties. This paper introduces SAFE (Spectral Evolution Analysis Feature Extraction), a novel approach designed to enhance prediction accuracy for non-stationary time series. SAFE leverages spectral analysis techniques to track the evolution of frequency components over time, extracting dynamic features that capture underlying temporal patterns often missed by conventional methods. The proposed framework integrates adaptive windowing and transform-based spectral decomposition to generate robust feature representations from raw time series data. Extensive experiments were conducted on benchmark datasets across diverse application domains, such as financial forecasting and physiological signal prediction. Results demonstrate that models augmented with SAFE features achieve superior predictive performance compared to baseline statistical and deep learning approaches, particularly in highly non-stationary scenarios. The findings highlight SAFE’s effectiveness in capturing transient behaviors and sudden regime shifts, thereby improving the reliability and interpretability of time series forecasting. This work advances the state-of-the-art in non-stationary time series prediction and provides a versatile tool for data-driven analysis in domains characterized by evolving temporal dynamics. **Keywords:** non-stationary time series, spectral analysis, feature extraction, prediction, SAFE, time series forecasting, machine learning.

In today’s competitive business environment, effective management of sales staff is critical for organizational success. However, many companies still rely on manual or outdated systems to track and manage sales activities, leading to inefficiencies, data inaccuracies, and limited scalability. This research addresses the need for a modern, automated solution to streamline sales staff management, enhance productivity, and improve decision-making processes. The primary objective of this thesis is to design and develop a Sales Staff Management System (SSMS) that automates key tasks such as performance tracking, task assignment, and reporting. The system aims to solve specific challenges, including the lack of real-time data access, inconsistent performance evaluation, and inefficient communication between sales teams and management. To achieve these goals, the system was developed using a combination of modern technologies, including a web-based front-end framework (React.js), a back-end server (Node.js with Express), and a relational database (MySQL) for data storage. The system architecture follows a modular design, ensuring scalability and ease of maintenance. Agile development methodologies were employed to iteratively refine the system based on user feedback and testing. The developed SSMS successfully integrates features such as real-time performance dashboards, automated task allocation, and comprehensive reporting tools. These outcomes are expected to significantly enhance operational efficiency, provide actionable insights for managers, and improve overall sales team performance. The research contributes to the field by demonstrating the practical application of modern software engineering principles to solve real-world sales management challenges. In conclusion, this thesis highlights the importance of leveraging technology to optimize sales staff management. The SSMS serves as a foundation for future enhancements, such as incorporating artificial intelligence for predictive analytics or expanding the system to support multi-departmental collaboration. This research underscores the potential of digital transformation in driving organizational success and sets a direction for further studies in this domain.

Accurately forecasting travel demand is crucial for urban planning, traffic management, and resource allocation. Traditional methods often treat each forecasting task in isolation, neglecting potentially beneficial correlations between different time series. This paper introduces a novel multi-task learning (MTL) framework designed to simultaneously learn from multiple related time series to improve travel demand prediction accuracy. Our approach employs a shared representation learning module, capturing common patterns across various locations and time periods, coupled with task-specific layers tailored to individual forecasting needs. We evaluate our model on a real-world travel demand dataset, demonstrating significant performance improvements compared to single-task learning baselines. Specifically, our MTL model achieves a 15% reduction in root mean squared error (RMSE) when predicting traffic flow in low-volume areas. The results highlight the effectiveness of MTL in leveraging inter-series dependencies for enhanced travel demand forecasting, offering valuable insights for transportation planning and intelligent transportation systems. Keywords: Multi-task learning, time series forecasting, travel demand, traffic prediction, shared representation.

Decision tree is an important method for both induction research and data mining, which is mainly used for model classification and prediction. ID3 algorithm is the most widely used algorithm in the decision tree so far. In this paper, the shortcoming of ID3's inclining to choose attributes with many values is discussed, and then a new decision tree algorithm which is improved version of ID3. In our proposed algorithm attributes are divided into groups and then we apply the selection measure 5 for these groups. If information gain is not good then again divide attributes values into groups. These steps are done until we get good classification/misclassification ratio. The proposed algorithms classify the data sets more accurately and efficiently.

Heterogeneous multi-task learning (MTL) leverages the relationships between different tasks to improve overall performance, but manually designing network architectures for each task and their interactions is challenging. This paper introduces a novel approach for the automatic construction of multi-network models tailored for heterogeneous MTL. Our method employs a search strategy guided by task relatedness, automatically generating network topologies that efficiently share and specialize parameters across tasks. We introduce a multi-objective optimization framework that balances model complexity and predictive accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our automatically constructed models achieve comparable or superior performance compared to manually designed state-of-the-art MTL architectures, while significantly reducing the human effort required for model design. The proposed framework offers a practical solution for deploying MTL in scenarios with diverse and interrelated tasks. **Keywords:** Multi-task learning, neural architecture search, heterogeneous learning, automated machine learning, deep learning.

**Abstract:** Zero-shot learning (ZSL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for recognizing unseen categories by leveraging semantic knowledge, yet its application to 3D point cloud data remains an open challenge due to the high-dimensional, unordered, and sparse nature of such data. This paper proposes a novel framework for zero-shot learning on 3D point cloud objects, aiming to bridge the semantic gap between geometric representations and class attributes. Our approach integrates a robust point cloud feature extractor with a semantic embedding module, enabling the model to align geometric point features with semantic vectors representing both seen and unseen classes. We introduce a novel loss function to enhance the discriminative power of latent features and facilitate more effective transfer to unseen categories. Comprehensive experiments on widely used 3D object datasets demonstrate our method’s superior performance over existing ZSL and baseline approaches in accuracy and generalization to novel classes. Furthermore, we extend our framework to related modalities and scenarios, highlighting its adaptability and effectiveness beyond conventional 3D object classification. The results validate the potential of zero-shot learning for advancing 3D shape understanding and open new directions for applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and virtual reality. Keywords: zero-shot learning, 3D point cloud, semantic embedding, feature extraction, object recognition, transfer learning.

This paper investigates the effectiveness of bonus-based exploration methods in reinforcement learning (RL) within the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE). While exploration is critical for discovering optimal policies in RL, traditional methods often struggle in complex environments with sparse rewards. To address this, we evaluate several bonus-based exploration techniques, including intrinsic motivation and curiosity-driven approaches, which incentivize agents to explore novel states. We propose a hybrid exploration strategy that combines intrinsic rewards with environment-specific heuristics to enhance exploration efficiency. Our experiments compare the performance of these methods across a diverse set of ALE games, measuring metrics such as cumulative reward, exploration coverage, and convergence speed. Results demonstrate that our hybrid approach outperforms baseline methods, achieving higher rewards and faster convergence in environments with sparse rewards. The findings highlight the importance of tailored exploration strategies in complex RL tasks and provide insights into the design of more efficient exploration mechanisms for future applications in gaming, robotics, and beyond. Key contributions include a novel exploration framework and empirical evidence of its effectiveness in the ALE. Keywords: reinforcement learning, exploration strategies, intrinsic motivation, Arcade Learning Environment, bonus-based methods.

We have recently seen many successful applications of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) on electronic medical records (EMRs), which contain histories of patients' diagnoses, medications, and other various events, in order to predict the current and future states of patients. Despite the strong performance of RNNs, it is often challenging for users to understand why the model makes a particular prediction. Such black-box nature of RNNs can impede its wide adoption in clinical practice. Furthermore, we have no established methods to interactively leverage users' domain expertise and prior knowledge as inputs for steering the model. Therefore, our design study aims to provide a visual analytics solution to increase interpretability and interactivity of RNNs via a joint effort of medical experts, artificial intelligence scientists, and visual analytics researchers. Following the iterative design process between the experts, we design, implement, and evaluate a visual analytics tool called RetainVis, which couples a newly improved, interpretable and interactive RNN-based model called RetainEX and visualizations for users' exploration of EMR data in the context of prediction tasks. Our study shows the effective use of RetainVis for gaining insights into how individual medical codes contribute to making risk predictions, using EMRs of patients with heart failure and cataract symptoms. Our study also demonstrates how we made substantial changes to the state-of-the-art RNN model called RETAIN in order to make use of temporal information and increase interactivity. This study will provide a useful guideline for researchers that aim to design an interpretable and interactive visual analytics tool for RNNs.

Static gesture recognition is an effective non-verbal communication channel between a user and their devices; however many modern methods are sensitive to the relative pose of the user's hands with respect to the capture device, as parts of the gesture can become occluded. We present two methodologies for gesture recognition via synchronized recording from two depth cameras to alleviate this occlusion problem. One is a more classic approach using iterative closest point registration to accurately fuse point clouds and a single PointNet architecture for classification, and the other is a dual Point-Net architecture for classification without registration. On a manually collected data-set of 20,100 point clouds we show a 39.2% reduction in misclassification for the fused point cloud method, and 53.4% for the dual PointNet, when compared to a standard single camera pipeline.

This paper presents a comprehensive benchmarking study on word image recognition, addressing the need for standardized evaluation metrics and performance comparisons across diverse datasets. The objective is to assess the effectiveness of state-of-the-art recognition models in handling variations in font styles, resolutions, and noise levels commonly encountered in real-world scenarios. We evaluate several deep learning-based approaches, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures, on widely used word image datasets such as IIIT5K, SVT, and ICDAR. Our experiments highlight the strengths and limitations of each model, with a focus on accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. Results demonstrate that transformer-based models achieve superior performance in handling complex text variations, while CNNs remain competitive in scenarios with limited computational resources. The study also identifies key challenges, such as low-resolution images and irregular fonts, that require further research. This work contributes a systematic framework for benchmarking word image recognition systems, providing valuable insights for researchers and practitioners aiming to improve text recognition technologies in applications like document digitization and optical character recognition (OCR). **Keywords**: word image recognition, benchmarking, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, transformers, OCR, text recognition.

Web3 and DappsWeb3 and Decentralized Applications (DApps) have emerged as critical com ponents of the evolution of the internet and digital ecosystems. Web3 is the vision of a more decentralized and user-centric internet, in which individuals have greatercontrol over their data, identity, and digital interactions. It is a collection of tech nologies, protocols, and frameworks designed to empower users, cultivate trust, and facilitate peer-to-peer interactions. DApps, on the other hand, are applications that are created on top of decentralized networks and typically utilize blockchain technology. These applications inherit Web3’s fundamental principles, including decentralization, transparency, and user ownership. From financial services andgovernance platforms to gaming and social media applications, they provide a va riety of features. The development and adoption of Web3 and DApps have been supported by a growing body of research and innovation. Several academic papersand technical publications have contributed to the advancement of these technologies. For instance, the paper by Wood et al. titled "Ethereum: A Secure Decen tralized Generalized Transaction Ledger" provides a comprehensive overview ofthe Ethereum platform and its underlying principles . Another significant con tribution is the work by Swan, who explores the concept of "Token Economy" in his book "Token Economy: How the Web3 Reinvents Value Exchange." The book delves into the transformative potential of tokenization and its implications for vari-ous industries . Moreover, the paper by Buterin et al. titled "A Next-Generation Smart Contract and Decentralized Application Platform" introduces the Ethereum platform, highlighting its unique features and use cases . This paper serves as a foundational reference for understanding the capabilities and potential of DApps built on Ethereum.

Person re-identification (ReID) is an important problem in computer vision, especially for video surveillance applications. The problem focuses on identifying people across different cameras or across different frames of the same camera. The main challenge lies in identifying the similarity of the same person against large appearance and structure variations, while differentiating between individuals. Recently, deep learning networks with triplet loss have become a common framework for person ReID. However, triplet loss focuses on obtaining correct orders on the training set. We demonstrate that it performs inferior in a clustering task. In this paper, we design a cluster loss, which can lead to the model output with a larger inter-class variation and a smaller intra-class variation compared to the triplet loss. As a result, our model has a better generalization ability and can achieve higher accuracy on the test set especially for a clustering task. We also introduce a batch hard training mechanism for improving the results and faster convergence of training.

This paper investigates exponential inequalities for nonstationary Markov chains, addressing the challenge of quantifying concentration bounds in time-varying stochastic processes. Traditional approaches often assume stationarity, limiting their applicability to real-world scenarios where systems evolve dynamically. We propose a novel framework that extends exponential concentration inequalities to nonstationary settings, leveraging advanced probabilistic techniques and coupling methods. Our approach accounts for time-dependent transition probabilities and provides tight bounds on the deviation of empirical averages from their expected values. Through theoretical analysis and simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in capturing the behavior of nonstationary Markov chains under varying conditions. The results show significant improvements over existing stationary-based bounds, particularly in scenarios with rapid changes in transition dynamics. This work contributes to the broader understanding of concentration phenomena in nonstationary systems, with potential applications in reinforcement learning, network analysis, and time-series forecasting. Key findings highlight the importance of adapting concentration inequalities to dynamic environments, offering new insights for both theoretical and applied research in stochastic processes. **Keywords**: Nonstationary Markov chains, exponential inequalities, concentration bounds, time-varying systems, probabilistic methods, stochastic processes.

The increasing use of computed tomography (CT) scans in clinical diagnosis necessitates efficient and accurate methods for lesion detection and segmentation. This study addresses the challenge of lesion segmentation with minimal annotation effort by proposing a weakly-supervised co-segmentation approach. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel framework utilizing weakly-supervised learning techniques for lesion segmentation in CT scans. Our method leverages co-segmentation to concurrently segment multiple lesions, enhancing the model's ability to recognize diverse lesion characteristics within similar or different CT images. The algorithm employs minimal labeled data, reinforced by leveraging complementary unlabeled data to improve segmentation accuracy. We employ a combination of deep learning architectures with feature-sharing techniques to solve the segmentation task effectively. Results/Findings: The proposed approach was evaluated on a dataset of CT scans containing various types of lesions. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms traditional fully-supervised models, achieving high accuracy in lesion boundary delineation with reduced dependency on extensive labeled datasets. Our method showed strong generalization across different types of lesions and patient demographics, highlighting its robustness and practicality. Conclusion/Implications: This work contributes a significant advancement in the realm of medical imaging by introducing a weakly-supervised co-segmentation method that effectively balances accuracy and annotation effort. The framework's ability to perform with minimal labels represents a step forward in automating medical imaging processes, paving the way for practical applications in clinical settings. The approach can be extended to other medical imaging modalities, promoting broader applicability. Keywords: Weakly-supervised learning, lesion segmentation, CT scans, co-segmentation, medical imaging, deep learning, automated diagnosis.

This paper investigates the consistency of semi-supervised learning algorithms on graphs, focusing on Probit and one-hot methods. The objective is to analyze the performance and reliability of these algorithms in graph-based learning tasks, where labeled data is scarce. We employ a combination of theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation to compare the consistency of Probit and one-hot methods. Our approach involves modeling graph-structured data using probabilistic frameworks and assessing the algorithms' ability to generalize from limited labeled examples. The results show that both methods exhibit consistency under certain conditions, but the Probit method demonstrates superior performance in terms of accuracy and robustness. Our findings have significant implications for the development of reliable semi-supervised learning algorithms on graphs, with potential applications in network analysis, recommendation systems, and graph neural networks. Key contributions include the introduction of a novel probabilistic framework for analyzing consistency and the identification of critical factors influencing algorithmic performance. Relevant keywords: semi-supervised learning, graph algorithms, Probit method, one-hot method, graph neural networks, network analysis.

Clinical time series data, such as electronic health records (EHRs), present unique challenges due to their high dimensionality, irregular sampling, and temporal dependencies. This paper introduces a novel attention-based model for clinical time series analysis, aiming to improve the accuracy and interpretability of disease diagnosis and patient outcome prediction. The proposed approach leverages multi-head self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies and temporal patterns in EHRs, enabling the model to focus on clinically relevant time steps and features. We evaluate the model on publicly available datasets, including MIMIC-III, and compare its performance against state-of-the-art methods, such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Experimental results demonstrate that the attention-based model achieves superior performance in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Additionally, the model provides interpretable attention weights, offering insights into the decision-making process and highlighting critical time points for clinical diagnosis. This work contributes to the growing field of AI in healthcare by providing a robust and interpretable framework for clinical time series analysis, with potential applications in real-time patient monitoring and personalized treatment planning. **Keywords**: clinical time series, attention models, electronic health records, disease diagnosis, interpretability, healthcare AI.
