This paper addresses the challenge of learning effective graph node embeddings by proposing a novel approach that leverages domain-aware biased random walks. Traditional methods of generating node embeddings often lack the ability to incorporate domain-specific knowledge, which can limit their performance in specific applications. Methods/Approach: Our method introduces domain-aware biased random walks as a mechanism to traverse the graph, selectively prioritizing nodes based on predefined domain relevance criteria. By incorporating domain biases into the random walk process, the proposed technique can capture both the local topology and domain-specific context of the graph more accurately. We compare our approach against standard random walk-based embedding algorithms, employing a variety of datasets that span different domains. Results/Findings: The experimental results demonstrate that our domain-aware biased random walks significantly enhance the quality of node embeddings. Our method consistently outperforms existing techniques in tasks such as node classification and link prediction, showing an average improvement in performance metrics by a substantial margin. Specifically, the incorporation of domain knowledge enables improved discrimination of node roles and relationships within the graph. Conclusion/Implications: The findings underscore the importance of integrating domain-specific information into graph embedding processes. Our research presents a substantial advancement in the field, offering a versatile framework that can be adapted to various domains where graphs play a critical role in data representation and analysis. The proposed method has potential applications in social network analysis, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems, where capturing domain nuances is crucial for task-specific predictions. Key keywords: Graph embeddings, domain-aware, biased random walks, node classification, link prediction, topology, data representation.

The proliferation of probabilistic programming has augmented the ability to model complex stochastic processes, yet efficient inference within these programs remains a significant challenge. This research proposes a novel approach to optimize the inference process for probabilistic programs through meta-learning, aiming to enhance accuracy and efficiency. Methods/Approach: We introduce a meta-learning framework that automatically learns an inference algorithm tailored for specific probabilistic programs. Our approach leverages gradient-based meta-learning techniques to adapt standard Monte Carlo and variational inference methods. By incorporating a recurrent neural network (RNN) as a meta-learner, we iteratively refine inference strategies to achieve optimal performance across a distribution of tasks. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our meta-learned inference algorithm significantly outperforms traditional inference techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. We provide quantitative evaluations on various benchmark probabilistic programs, illustrating improved posterior approximation and reduced convergence times. The algorithm shows robust generalization across different models and complexity levels. Conclusion/Implications: This study marks a substantial contribution to the field of probabilistic programming by introducing an adaptive inference mechanism that learns from experience. Our method not only enhances existing probabilistic programming frameworks but also opens new avenues for applying machine learning to automate and improve inference strategies in complex stochastic systems. Future work will explore extending this approach to broader classes of probabilistic models and real-world applications. Key Keywords: meta-learning, inference algorithm, probabilistic programming, Monte Carlo, variational inference, recurrent neural network (RNN).

In this paper, we study the problem of outlier arm detection in multi-armed bandit settings, which finds plenty of applications in many high-impact domains such as finance, healthcare, and online advertising. For this problem, a learner aims to identify the arms whose expected rewards deviate significantly from most of the other arms. Different from existing work, we target the generic outlier arms or outlier arm groups whose expected rewards can be larger, smaller, or even in between those of normal arms. To this end, we start by providing a comprehensive definition of such generic outlier arms and outlier arm groups. Then we propose a novel pulling algorithm named GOLD to identify such generic outlier arms. It builds a real-time neighborhood graph based on upper confidence bounds and catches the behavior pattern of outliers from normal arms. We also analyze its performance from various aspects. In the experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world data sets, the proposed algorithm achieves 98 % accuracy while saving 83 % exploration cost on average compared with state-of-the-art techniques.

Inference, prediction and control of complex dynamical systems from time series is important in many areas, including financial markets, power grid management, climate and weather modeling, or molecular dynamics. The analysis of such highly nonlinear dynamical systems is facilitated by the fact that we can often find a (generally nonlinear) transformation of the system coordinates to features in which the dynamics can be excellently approximated by a linear Markovian model. Moreover, the large number of system variables often change collectively on large time- and length-scales, facilitating a low-dimensional analysis in feature space. In this paper, we introduce a variational approach for Markov processes (VAMP) that allows us to find optimal feature mappings and optimal Markovian models of the dynamics from given time series data. The key insight is that the best linear model can be obtained from the top singular components of the Koopman operator. This leads to the definition of a family of score functions called VAMP-r which can be calculated from data, and can be employed to optimize a Markovian model. In addition, based on the relationship between the variational scores and approximation errors of Koopman operators, we propose a new VAMP-E score, which can be applied to cross-validation for hyper-parameter optimization and model selection in VAMP. VAMP is valid for both reversible and nonreversible processes and for stationary and non-stationary processes or realizations.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of benchmarking frameworks for reinforcement learning, aiming to provide a unified understanding of the current landscape and identify key challenges. We employ a systematic approach to categorize and compare existing frameworks, highlighting their strengths, weaknesses, and applicability to various reinforcement learning scenarios. Our analysis reveals significant variations in evaluation metrics, environment simulations, and agent performance assessments across different frameworks. The results show that while some frameworks excel in specific domains, others demonstrate broader versatility and adaptability. We conclude that a standardized benchmarking framework is essential for fair comparison and reproducibility in reinforcement learning research. Our survey contributes to the development of more robust and reliable evaluation methodologies, ultimately advancing the field of reinforcement learning and its applications in areas like robotics, game playing, and autonomous systems. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, benchmarking frameworks, evaluation metrics, agent performance, reproducibility.

Các hệ thống đề xuất ngày càng trở nên phổ biến trong nhiều lĩnh vực, từ thương mại điện tử đến mạng xã hội. Tuy nhiên, chúng thường bị chỉ trích vì không công bằng, ưu tiên những người dùng có ảnh hưởng hoặc có khả năng chi trả cao hơn. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, các nhà nghiên cứu đã đề xuất một cách tiếp cận mới dựa trên tiện ích R (Utility-based approach). Cách tiếp cận này tập trung vào việc đo lường và tối ưu hóa tiện ích của người dùng, thay vì chỉ dựa vào các yếu tố như giá trị hoặc vị trí. Điều này cho phép hệ thống đề xuất cung cấp cho người dùng những lựa chọn phù hợp với nhu cầu và sở thích của họ. Một trong những lợi ích chính của cách tiếp cận này là khả năng giảm thiểu sự thiên vị và đảm bảo rằng mọi người dùng đều có cơ hội được đề xuất. Ngoài ra, nó cũng giúp hệ thống đề xuất trở nên linh hoạt và có thể thích nghi với các thay đổi trong nhu cầu và sở thích của người dùng. Tuy nhiên, cách tiếp cận này cũng có một số hạn chế. Nó đòi hỏi sự có mặt của dữ liệu về tiện ích của người dùng, điều này có thể khó khăn để thu thập và xử lý. Ngoài ra, nó cũng có thể dẫn đến sự phức tạp trong việc tối ưu hóa hệ thống đề xuất. Tóm lại, cách tiếp cận dựa trên tiện ích R là một giải pháp tiềm năng để cải thiện sự công bằng của các hệ thống đề xuất. Nó cho phép hệ thống đề xuất cung cấp cho người dùng những lựa chọn phù hợp với nhu cầu và sở thích của họ, đồng thời giảm thiểu sự thiên vị và đảm bảo rằng mọi người dùng đều có cơ hội được đề xuất.

This paper presents a novel approach utilizing Graph Attention Networks (GATs) for enhancing microwave imaging, specifically targeting the detection and analysis of brain anomalies. Microwave imaging has emerged as a promising non-invasive technique for medical diagnostics, and this study aims to improve its precision and reliability by integrating advanced machine learning models. Methods/Approach: Our approach employs Graph Attention Networks, a state-of-the-art deep learning framework that extends traditional graph convolutional networks by incorporating attention mechanisms. This enables the model to dynamically focus on the most informative parts of the input data, thereby enhancing feature extraction and representation. The model is trained on synthetic and real-world datasets to ensure robustness and generalization in detecting anomalies within brain tissues. Results/Findings: The proposed GAT-based method demonstrates superior performance over conventional imaging techniques and baseline deep learning models, as evidenced by increased accuracy and reduced false positive rates in anomaly detection tasks. The system successfully identifies diverse types of anomalies, showcasing its adaptability and effectiveness across different scenarios. Comparative analysis reveals that our model achieves a notable improvement in imaging clarity and anomaly localization. Conclusion/Implications: This study underscores the potential for Graph Attention Networks to revolutionize microwave imaging applications in medical diagnostics. The enhanced capability to accurately detect brain anomalies opens avenues for improved clinical outcomes and highlights the interdisciplinary benefits of combining advanced AI with traditional imaging techniques. Our findings suggest promising future applications in real-time medical diagnostics and treatment monitoring, heralding a new era of intelligent health diagnostics. Keywords: Graph Attention Network, microwave imaging, brain anomaly detection, attention mechanism, medical diagnostics, machine learning, deep learning, non-invasive imaging.

Reinforcement learning (RL) has seen significant advancements through the integration of value-based and policy-based methods. This paper explores the combination of policy gradient and Q-learning, two widely used RL approaches, to leverage their complementary strengths. The objective is to develop a hybrid framework that enhances learning efficiency, stability, and performance in complex environments. We propose a novel algorithm that integrates policy gradient methods, which excel in handling continuous action spaces, with Q-learning, known for its effectiveness in discrete action spaces. The approach employs a dual-network architecture to simultaneously optimize policy and value functions, ensuring robust exploration and exploitation. Experimental results on benchmark environments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to standalone policy gradient or Q-learning approaches, particularly in tasks requiring fine-grained control and high-dimensional state spaces. The findings highlight the potential of combining these methods to address challenges in real-world applications, such as robotics and autonomous systems. This research contributes to the growing body of work on hybrid RL techniques, offering a scalable and efficient solution for complex decision-making problems. **Keywords**: reinforcement learning, policy gradient, Q-learning, hybrid methods, decision-making, autonomous systems.

The rapid development of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) requires industrial production towards digitalization to improve network efficiency. Digital Twin is a promising technology to empower the digital transformation of IIoT by creating virtual models of physical objects. However, the provision of network efficiency in IIoT is very challenging due to resource-constrained devices, stochastic tasks, and resources heterogeneity. Distributed resources in IIoT networks can be efficiently exploited through computation offloading to reduce energy consumption while enhancing data processing efficiency. In this paper, we first propose a new paradigm Digital Twin Networks (DTN) to build network topology and the stochastic task arrival model in IIoT systems. Then, we formulate the stochastic computation offloading and resource allocation problem to minimize the long-term energy efficiency. As the formulated problem is a stochastic programming problem, we leverage Lyapunov optimization technique to transform the original problem into a deterministic per-time slot problem. Finally, we present Asynchronous Actor-Critic (AAC) algorithm to find the optimal stochastic computation offloading policy. Illustrative results demonstrate that our proposed scheme is able to significantly outperforms the benchmarks.

Ứng dụng điều khiển đa năng đang trở thành một xu hướng quan trọng trong việc tối ưu hóa quy trình quản lý và điều khiển các thiết bị thông minh trong cuộc sống hàng ngày. Việc phát triển một ứng dụng như vậy không chỉ giúp người dùng dễ dàng tương tác với các thiết bị mà còn nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng năng lượng và tiết kiệm thời gian. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc thiết kế và triển khai một ứng dụng điều khiển đa năng, cho phép người dùng quản lý nhiều thiết bị khác nhau thông qua một giao diện duy nhất. Ứng dụng được xây dựng trên nền tảng di động, tích hợp các công nghệ hiện đại như Internet of Things (IoT) và trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) nhằm cung cấp trải nghiệm người dùng tối ưu. Các tính năng chính của ứng dụng bao gồm khả năng điều khiển từ xa, lập lịch tự động, và nhận diện giọng nói, giúp người dùng dễ dàng thực hiện các tác vụ mà không cần phải tương tác trực tiếp với thiết bị. Thông qua việc khảo sát và phân tích nhu cầu của người dùng, ứng dụng được thiết kế với giao diện thân thiện, dễ sử dụng, đồng thời đảm bảo tính bảo mật và riêng tư cho người dùng. Kết quả thử nghiệm cho thấy ứng dụng không chỉ đáp ứng được các yêu cầu về chức năng mà còn mang lại sự hài lòng cao cho người dùng. Nghiên cứu này không chỉ đóng góp vào lĩnh vực phát triển ứng dụng di động mà còn mở ra hướng đi mới cho việc ứng dụng công nghệ thông minh trong quản lý thiết bị, từ đó nâng cao chất lượng cuộc sống cho người dùng.

This paper addresses the challenge of manual-label dependency in 3D object detection, a critical bottleneck in developing robust and scalable perception systems for autonomous vehicles and robotics. We propose a novel framework that leverages an open-source simulator to generate synthetic, high-fidelity 3D data, eliminating the need for costly and time-intensive manual labeling. Our approach integrates domain randomization techniques to bridge the sim-to-real gap, ensuring the synthetic data's applicability to real-world scenarios. We employ a state-of-the-art 3D detection model trained exclusively on simulator-generated data and evaluate its performance on benchmark datasets. Experimental results demonstrate competitive accuracy compared to models trained on manually labeled datasets, with significant reductions in annotation effort and cost. The proposed method not only advances the field of 3D detection but also provides a scalable, cost-effective solution for training perception systems. This work highlights the potential of simulation-driven approaches in reducing reliance on manual annotations, paving the way for more efficient and accessible 3D perception technologies. **Keywords**: 3D object detection, simulation, domain randomization, synthetic data, autonomous systems, sim-to-real transfer.

This research addresses the challenge of accurately predicting and estimating complex networks where traditional models fall short. We introduce a novel approach using the Monotone Single Index Multi-variate Autoregressive Model (MSIMAM) to enhance predictive accuracy and network representation. Methods/Approach: The approach leverages the MSIMAM, which incorporates a monotonic single index function into a multi-variate autoregressive framework. This model enhances flexibility and handles non-linearity without the complexity of multiple parameters. By adopting a robust estimation algorithm tailored to the MSIMAM, the model efficiently learns from high-dimensional time series data, improving adaptability and performance. Results/Findings: Our findings demonstrate that MSIMAM significantly outperforms traditional multi-variate autoregressive models by providing better predictive accuracy and network estimation. Comparative analysis reveals that MSIMAM yields more precise network structures with fewer assumptions on data distribution. Experiments conducted on synthetic datasets and real-world applications underscore its superior performance and stability in capturing dynamic network behaviors. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of the Monotone Single Index Multi-variate Autoregressive Model provides a profound shift in network prediction methodologies, offering a powerful tool for researchers and practitioners. This model's ability to integrate seamlessly into existing predictive systems while delivering accurate network analyses holds vast potential for diverse applications, including finance, biology, and telecommunications. Future work will explore extending MSIMAM capabilities and adapting the approach to broader domains. Keywords: Monotone Single Index, Multi-variate Autoregressive Model, Network Estimation, Prediction, Non-linearity, Time Series Analysis.

Objective: Sparse phase retrieval seeks to recover signals with few nonzero components from intensity-only measurements, a problem central to imaging, communications, and optics. This paper introduces a novel stochastic alternating minimizing method (SAM) that addresses the computational and sample-efficiency challenges of existing approaches. Methods: SAM alternates between two key steps—phase estimation and sparse signal update—using randomly selected measurement subsets at each iteration. In the phase‐estimation step, current signal estimates are combined with measured magnitudes to form linearized subproblems. In the sparse‐update step, a truncated gradient descent with hard‐thresholding enforces sparsity. By processing mini-batches of measurements, SAM reduces per-iteration cost and memory requirements. We provide theoretical analysis proving that, under standard sub‐Gaussian measurement assumptions, SAM converges linearly to the true support and achieves exact recovery with high probability when the number of measurements scales as O(k log n), where k is the sparsity level and n the signal dimension. Results: Experiments on synthetic and real‐world datasets demonstrate that SAM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both recovery accuracy and runtime. In particular, SAM attains exact support recovery with 20–30% fewer measurements and reduces computation time by up to 50% compared to batch alternating minimization and convex relaxation techniques. Robustness tests under additive noise further validate its practical utility. Conclusion: The proposed stochastic alternating minimizing method offers a scalable, efficient, and theoretically grounded solution for large-scale sparse phase retrieval. Its low memory footprint and fast convergence make it well suited for real-time imaging systems, high-throughput microscopy, and communication channels relying on intensity measurements. Keywords: sparse phase retrieval, alternating minimization, stochastic optimization, hard-thresholding, compressive sensing.

Under any Multiclass Classification (MCC) setting defined by a collection of labeled point-cloud specified by a feature-set, we extract only stochastic partial orderings from all possible triplets of point-cloud without explicitly measuring the three cloud-to-cloud distances. We demonstrate that such a collective of partial ordering can efficiently compute a label embedding tree geometry on the Label-space. This tree in turn gives rise to a predictive graph, or a network with precisely weighted linkages. Such two multiscale geometries are taken as the coarse scale information content of MCC. They indeed jointly shed lights on explainable knowledge on why and how labeling comes about and facilitates error-free prediction with potential multiple candidate labels supported by data. For revealing within-label heterogeneity, we further undergo labeling naturally found clusters within each point-cloud, and likewise derive multiscale geometry as its fine-scale information content contained in data. This fine-scale endeavor shows that our computational proposal is indeed scalable to a MCC setting having a large label-space. Overall the computed multiscale collective of data-driven patterns and knowledge will serve as a basis for constructing visible and explainable subject matter intelligence regarding the system of interest.

The inverse design of inorganic materials, which involves identifying optimal material compositions and structures for specific properties, remains a significant challenge in materials science. Traditional methods often struggle with the vast and complex chemical space, leading to inefficiencies in exploration and discovery. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to efficiently sample the chemical space for inverse design. The proposed GAN-based framework generates realistic and diverse material candidates by learning the underlying distribution of known inorganic materials. A discriminator network evaluates the generated samples, ensuring their validity and relevance to the target properties. The method is validated using a comprehensive dataset of inorganic materials, demonstrating its ability to produce chemically feasible and property-optimized candidates. Results show that the GAN-based approach outperforms traditional sampling techniques in terms of computational efficiency and diversity of generated materials. Furthermore, the framework enables the discovery of previously unexplored material compositions with desirable properties, showcasing its potential for accelerating materials innovation. This work highlights the transformative role of GANs in addressing the challenges of chemical space exploration and provides a robust tool for the inverse design of inorganic materials. **Keywords**: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), inverse design, inorganic materials, chemical space, materials discovery, machine learning.

This paper presents a convolutional neural network based approach for estimating the relative pose between two cameras. The proposed network takes RGB images from both cameras as input and directly produces the relative rotation and translation as output. The system is trained in an end-to-end manner utilising transfer learning from a large scale classification dataset. The introduced approach is compared with widely used local feature based methods (SURF, ORB) and the results indicate a clear improvement over the baseline. In addition, a variant of the proposed architecture containing a spatial pyramid pooling (SPP) layer is evaluated and shown to further improve the performance.

This paper introduces GATSBI, a novel framework for simulating realistic and interactive agent behaviors within complex 3D environments, focusing on spatio-temporal object interaction. GATSBI employs a generative agent architecture that learns to predict and execute context-aware actions based on perceived object affordances and environmental dynamics. We present a multi-modal learning approach that integrates visual and semantic information to enable agents to dynamically adapt their behavior to changing circumstances. Experiments conducted in a simulated city environment demonstrate GATSBI's ability to generate coherent and plausible agent activities, including navigation, object manipulation, and social interaction. Compared to existing agent simulation methods, GATSBI exhibits superior performance in terms of behavioral realism, environmental responsiveness, and computational efficiency. The proposed framework has significant implications for a wide range of applications, including urban planning, autonomous robotics, and interactive virtual environments. Keywords: Generative Agents, Spatio-temporal Interaction, 3D Simulation, Object Affordances, Multi-modal Learning, Behavior Modeling.

Graph classification is a fundamental task with applications in diverse fields, from drug discovery to social network analysis. This paper introduces a simple yet surprisingly effective baseline algorithm for graph classification, offering a computationally efficient alternative to complex graph neural networks. Our approach, termed "Graph Feature Aggregation Network" (GFAN), aggregates node features using basic statistical measures (mean, variance, max) across the entire graph, feeding the resulting vector into a standard multi-layer perceptron for classification. We evaluate GFAN on several benchmark graph classification datasets, including MUTAG, PTC-MR, and IMDB-BINARY. Results demonstrate that GFAN achieves competitive performance compared to more sophisticated graph neural networks, while requiring significantly less computational resources and training time. Specifically, GFAN achieves comparable or superior accuracy on small to medium-sized datasets and provides a strong baseline for future research. This work highlights the potential of simple feature aggregation techniques for graph classification and offers a practical, efficient solution for real-world applications. Keywords: Graph classification, baseline algorithm, graph neural networks, feature aggregation, machine learning.

Affect analysis in real-world settings presents a significant challenge due to the inherent variability and complexity of human behavior. This paper introduces a novel approach to multi-modal affect analysis utilizing standardized data within subjects collected in the wild. Our method addresses the limitations of traditional approaches by leveraging personalized baseline modeling to normalize affective responses across diverse individuals and contexts. We employ a combination of physiological signals (ECG, EDA), facial expressions, and self-reported emotions, standardized against each participant's own baseline, to train a robust affect recognition model. Results demonstrate a significant improvement in classification accuracy compared to models trained on non-standardized data, particularly in discerning subtle emotional nuances. The findings suggest that personalized standardization enhances the reliability and generalizability of affect recognition systems in uncontrolled environments. This research contributes to the development of more accurate and ecologically valid affect-aware technologies for applications in mental health monitoring, personalized human-computer interaction, and behavioral science. Keywords: Affect analysis, multi-modal data, standardization, in-the-wild, personalized modeling, emotion recognition.

Sự giao thoa giữa hiện thực và siêu thực, giữa ý thức và tiềm thức tạo nên một thế giới văn chương độc đáo, nơi con người bản năng được giải phóng và khám phá những chiều sâu ẩn giấu của tâm hồn. Qua đó, Murakami phản ánh những vấn đề nhức nhối của xã hội đương đại, đồng thời khẳng định giá trị của sự tự do, cá tính và khả năng chữa lành của nghệ thuật.

Objective: Foreground object extraction is a critical preprocessing step in applications ranging from photo editing and augmented reality to video surveillance. Manual segmentation is time-consuming, and many existing automatic methods either lack accuracy or impose high computational costs. This paper presents an automatic and efficient foreground object extraction scheme that balances precision and speed for still images. Methods: Our approach employs a two-stage pipeline. First, a saliency map is generated by fusing color contrast and texture cues across multiple scales, identifying candidate object regions without manual seeds. Second, we refine these regions via an adaptive graph-based segmentation algorithm, in which node weights and edge costs are guided by saliency strength and local boundary confidence. A multi-resolution strategy coupled with morphological filtering suppresses noise and preserves fine details. The entire pipeline is implemented with parallelized routines to achieve real-time performance. Results: On public benchmarks (e.g., PASCAL VOC and MSRA salient object datasets), our scheme yields an average F-measure of 0.91 and intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.87, outperforming classic methods such as GrabCut and saliency-only extraction, while matching the accuracy of recent deep-learning approaches. Runtime is 0.12 seconds per 512×512 image on a standard GPU, representing a 3× speedup over competing algorithms. Conclusion: The proposed method delivers accurate, fully automatic foreground extraction with low latency, making it suitable for interactive graphics and real-time vision systems. Its modular design allows straightforward extension to video sequences and dynamic scenes. Keywords: foreground extraction, saliency detection, graph-based segmentation, image processing, real-time.

Kế toán quản trị đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động của các doanh nghiệp, đặc biệt là trong lĩnh vực xây dựng và dầu khí. Bằng cách áp dụng các công cụ phân tích tài chính hiện đại, công ty có thể dự đoán chính xác hơn về hiệu quả kinh tế của các dự án, đồng thời giảm thiểu rủi ro và tối ưu hóa lợi nhuận. This paper introduces Points2Vec, a novel unsupervised learning framework for extracting object-level feature representations directly from 3D point clouds. The objective is to learn meaningful features without relying on labeled data, addressing a critical need in 3D scene understanding. Our approach leverages a contrastive learning strategy combined with a hierarchical point cloud processing network based on PointNet++. Specifically, we generate positive and negative sample pairs by applying geometric transformations and introduce a novel point cloud augmentation technique to enhance the robustness of learned features. The framework is trained to discriminate between these pairs, forcing the network to learn discriminative and invariant feature embeddings. Evaluation on several benchmark datasets for 3D object classification and retrieval demonstrates that Points2Vec achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art unsupervised methods and even approaches the performance of some supervised learning techniques. The learned features exhibit strong generalization capabilities, making them suitable for various downstream tasks. These findings highlight the potential of unsupervised learning for representation learning on point cloud data, reducing the dependence on large labeled datasets. **Keywords:** Point cloud, unsupervised learning, feature extraction, 3D object recognition, contrastive learning, representation learning.

The alignment of biological manifolds is a critical challenge in computational biology, enabling the integration and comparison of high-dimensional data from diverse biological systems. This paper introduces MAGAN (Manifold-Aligned Generative Adversarial Network), a novel framework designed to align and map biological manifolds while preserving their intrinsic structures. MAGAN leverages adversarial training to learn a shared latent space between two or more datasets, ensuring that the geometric and topological properties of the original manifolds are maintained. The proposed approach is evaluated on multiple biological datasets, including single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, demonstrating superior performance in manifold alignment compared to existing methods. Results show that MAGAN achieves higher accuracy in cross-dataset integration and improves downstream analysis tasks such as cell type identification and trajectory inference. The framework's ability to handle noisy and heterogeneous data further highlights its robustness. By enabling precise alignment of biological manifolds, MAGAN offers significant potential for advancing research in systems biology, personalized medicine, and multi-omics data integration. This work contributes a scalable and adaptable solution to a fundamental problem in computational biology, with implications for understanding complex biological systems. **Keywords**: Manifold alignment, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, computational biology, multi-omics integration.

Objective: Autoregressive (AR) models underpin critical forecasting systems in domains such as finance, energy management, and sensor networks. This work investigates how an adversary can strategically manipulate environmental inputs to induce maximal forecast errors in AR models. Methods: We introduce a bilevel optimization framework that determines the minimal perturbation to observable variables required to drive the model’s predictions away from true values over a multi-step horizon. By recasting the adversarial problem as a sequence of constrained optimizations, we derive closed-form update rules for linear AR processes and develop a gradient-based solver for more complex, nonlinear variants. A dynamic-programming–inspired algorithm ensures computational efficiency even for long forecasting horizons. Results: Experiments on synthetic AR(p) processes and real-world time-series datasets demonstrate that our optimal attack strategy increases forecast mean squared error by up to 250% compared to random or single-step perturbations, while using 40% smaller input modifications. Sensitivity analyses reveal key factors—such as model order, noise variance, and horizon length—that govern vulnerability. Conclusion: This study highlights a previously overlooked security risk in autoregressive forecasting, offering both a rigorous threat model and practical attack algorithms. Our findings underscore the need for robust training schemes and environmental integrity checks in deployed AR systems. Keywords: adversarial attack, autoregressive model, environment manipulation, robust forecasting, time-series security

Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) are widely used in machine learning and statistics for modeling relationships between variables. However, their performance in high-dimensional settings, where the number of features exceeds the number of observations, remains a critical challenge. This paper investigates the generalization error of GLMs in such high-dimensional regimes, focusing on the interplay between model complexity, data dimensionality, and sample size. We propose a theoretical framework to analyze the generalization bounds of GLMs under sparsity assumptions, leveraging tools from high-dimensional statistics and optimization theory. Our approach incorporates regularization techniques, such as L1 and L2 penalties, to control overfitting and improve model interpretability. Through extensive simulations and empirical evaluations, we demonstrate that our framework provides tighter generalization bounds compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios with limited data and high feature correlations. The results highlight the importance of regularization and sparsity in achieving robust performance for GLMs in high dimensions. This work contributes to the understanding of generalization in high-dimensional learning and offers practical insights for improving the reliability of GLMs in real-world applications. **Keywords**: Generalized Linear Models, high-dimensional statistics, generalization error, regularization, sparsity, machine learning.

Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in deep learning, often leading to biased models that favor majority classes while underperforming on minority classes. This paper introduces *ReMix*, a novel resampling technique designed to address class imbalance by calibrating the sampling process to ensure balanced representation during model training. Unlike traditional methods such as oversampling or undersampling, ReMix dynamically adjusts the sampling distribution based on class difficulty and model performance, enabling more effective learning across all classes. The proposed approach integrates a lightweight calibration mechanism into the training pipeline, which evaluates class-specific contributions to the loss and optimizes the sampling strategy accordingly. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10-LT and ImageNet-LT, demonstrate that ReMix significantly improves model performance on imbalanced datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results in terms of accuracy and F1-score. Furthermore, the method is computationally efficient and easily integrable into existing deep learning frameworks. The findings highlight the importance of adaptive resampling strategies in mitigating class imbalance and suggest broader applications in domains such as medical imaging, fraud detection, and natural language processing. Keywords: class imbalance, deep learning, resampling, adaptive sampling, calibration, minority classes.

This paper addresses the challenge of improving the generalization and stability of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) by introducing a controllable orthogonalization framework during training. The primary objective is to regulate the degree of orthogonality among neural network weights, mitigating issues such as redundant feature learning and vanishing/exploding gradients. Our approach incorporates a novel regularization technique that enables dynamic adjustment of the orthogonalization strength, providing flexibility to adapt to various network architectures and learning tasks. Through extensive experimentation on benchmark datasets involving image classification and natural language processing tasks, we demonstrate that our method leads to enhanced model robustness, faster convergence, and superior accuracy compared to standard and fixed orthogonalization strategies. Furthermore, ablation studies reveal the impact of controllable orthogonalization across different network depths and learning rates. The proposed framework is easily integrable with existing deep learning workflows and introduces negligible computational overhead. This research offers new insights into optimizing DNN training and paves the way for broader adoption of adaptive regularization methods in modern machine learning. Keywords: controllable orthogonalization, deep neural networks, regularization, training stability, generalization, adaptive algorithms.

Urban traffic data is often incomplete due to sensor malfunctions or sparse coverage, posing significant challenges for traffic management and prediction systems. This paper addresses the problem of spatiotemporal traffic data imputation by proposing a novel tensor completion framework. The objective is to accurately reconstruct missing traffic data across both spatial and temporal dimensions, enabling more reliable traffic analysis and decision-making. Our approach leverages a low-rank tensor decomposition model combined with spatiotemporal regularization to capture the inherent correlations and patterns in urban traffic networks. The proposed method is evaluated on real-world traffic datasets from multiple cities, demonstrating superior performance in imputation accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. Experimental results show that our model achieves a 15% improvement in mean absolute error (MAE) and a 20% reduction in root mean squared error (RMSE) over baseline methods. This research contributes to the field of intelligent transportation systems by providing a scalable and efficient solution for traffic data imputation, with potential applications in traffic forecasting, congestion management, and urban planning. **Keywords**: spatiotemporal data, tensor completion, traffic imputation, urban traffic analysis, low-rank decomposition, intelligent transportation systems.

This research contributes to the growing field of AI-driven negotiation by introducing a behavior-aware RL approach that enhances adaptability and realism in agent interactions. **Keywords**: reinforcement learning, contract negotiation, prosocial behavior, selfish behavior, multi-agent systems, deep Q-learning, fairness, utility optimization.

The paper addresses the challenge of enhancing video quality with a focus on improving both speed and accuracy. Video enhancement is critical for a wide range of applications such as surveillance, entertainment, and telecommunication, where high-quality visual content is essential. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel video enhancement technique that leverages sparse depth information to improve video clarity and detail. Our method integrates depth cues obtained from limited depth data into the enhancement process, effectively enhancing the spatial and temporal resolution of video frames. The core algorithm combines machine learning techniques with advanced computational models to optimize performance and accuracy. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing video enhancement techniques, achieving superior results in terms of both visual quality and processing speed. The system was validated against several benchmark datasets, showing noteworthy improvements in noise reduction, color fidelity, and sharpness. The implementation achieves real-time processing speeds, facilitating practical deployment in applications with high frame rates. Conclusion/Implications: The research introduces a fast and accurate method for video enhancement that effectively utilizes sparse depth information. This contribution presents a breakthrough in reducing computational overhead while maintaining high-quality output—key for applications where processing resources are limited. Our work opens pathways for future research in integrating sparse sensor data with traditional video processing pipelines to enrich visual content, benefiting areas such as augmented reality and video streaming services. Keywords: video enhancement, sparse depth, real-time processing, machine learning, computational models, visual quality.

Cảm tính nhà đầu tư đang trở thành một yếu tố quan trọng ảnh hưởng đến biến động tỷ suất sinh lời và thanh khoản chứng khoán. Trong bối cảnh thị trường chứng khoán đang chịu ảnh hưởng của nhiều yếu tố như kinh tế vĩ mô, chính trị và tài chính, cảm tính của nhà đầu tư có thể khiến họ đưa ra quyết định đầu tư không hợp lý. Khi thị trường chứng khoán đang trong giai đoạn tăng trưởng, nhiều nhà đầu tư thường cảm thấy tự tin và sẵn sàng đầu tư vào các cổ phiếu có tiềm năng tăng trưởng cao. Tuy nhiên, khi thị trường bắt đầu suy thoái, cảm tính của họ có thể khiến họ trở nên quá thận trọng và tránh đầu tư vào các cổ phiếu có tiềm năng tăng trưởng. Biến động tỷ suất sinh lời và thanh khoản chứng khoán cũng bị ảnh hưởng bởi cảm tính của nhà đầu tư. Khi thị trường đang trong giai đoạn tăng trưởng, tỷ suất sinh lời của các cổ phiếu thường cao hơn, nhưng khi thị trường bắt đầu suy thoái, tỷ suất sinh lời thường giảm xuống. Để giảm thiểu ảnh hưởng của cảm tính, nhà đầu tư cần phải có một chiến lược đầu tư rõ ràng và bền vững. The objective of this research is to address the limitations found in traditional weight-of-evidence (WoE) transformations, particularly in the context of predictive modeling and data binning. We propose an enhanced method, termed WoE 2.0, which incorporates shrinkage and spline-binning techniques to improve robustness and predictive performance. The approach employs shrinkage to mitigate the risk of overfitting by adjusting WoE calculations, while spline-binning provides a flexible and data-driven means of partitioning continuous variables into discrete bins. Our empirical analysis demonstrates that WoE 2.0 consistently outperforms classical WoE in various machine learning models through improved model interpretability and accuracy. We conduct comparisons across real-world datasets and benchmarks, showcasing the method's superiority in handling noisy and complex data structures. The findings underscore the potential applications of WoE 2.0 in credit scoring, risk management, and other fields requiring reliable binning solutions. This research contributes to the advancement of data preprocessing techniques, offering a novel and practical solution that enhances the utility of WoE transformations for predictive analytics. Key keywords include weight-of-evidence, shrinkage, spline-binning, predictive modeling, and data preprocessing.

Single image dehazing is a challenging task due to the inherent ambiguity in estimating scene depth and atmospheric light from a single hazy image. This paper introduces FFA-Net, a novel Feature Fusion Attention Network designed to effectively remove haze and recover clear images. FFA-Net employs a feature fusion module that adaptively integrates multi-level features extracted from different layers of a convolutional neural network. Furthermore, an attention mechanism is incorporated to selectively focus on haze-relevant features while suppressing irrelevant information. This attention mechanism enhances the network's ability to distinguish between haze and scene details, leading to improved dehazing performance. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that FFA-Net outperforms state-of-the-art dehazing methods in terms of both quantitative metrics and qualitative visual quality. The proposed network effectively removes haze, restores color fidelity, and preserves fine details, offering a significant advancement in single image dehazing. Keywords: Image Dehazing, Feature Fusion, Attention Mechanism, Convolutional Neural Network, Image Restoration.

Facial Action Unit (AU) intensity estimation is a critical task in affective computing, enabling more nuanced understanding of human emotions and behaviors. This paper presents a transfer learning approach to heatmap regression for robust and accurate estimation of AU intensities from facial images. The proposed method leverages deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) pre-trained on large-scale face datasets to extract meaningful feature representations, which are then fine-tuned for the AU intensity estimation task. Heatmap regression is employed to localize and quantify the intensities of multiple AUs simultaneously, improving precision over traditional regression methods. Experimental results demonstrate that our transfer learning framework substantially outperforms baseline models in terms of both accuracy and generalization, particularly when labeled data is scarce. Key findings indicate that the adoption of heatmap-based outputs enables more detailed spatial interpretation of AU intensities, while transfer learning significantly reduces the need for extensive training samples. This work contributes an effective solution for AU intensity estimation, with potential applications in automated facial expression analysis, human-computer interaction, and behavioral research. Keywords: Action Unit intensity, heatmap regression, transfer learning, facial expression analysis, convolutional neural networks.

Cross-modal learning aims to leverage the complementary information from different modalities to improve the performance of tasks. This paper addresses the challenge of effectively transferring knowledge across modalities by introducing a novel approach based on pairwise constraints. We propose a learning framework that utilizes pairwise relationships within and across modalities to guide the learning process. Specifically, we enforce constraints that encourage similar instances from different modalities to be mapped closer together in a shared latent space, while dissimilar instances are pushed further apart. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets for cross-modal retrieval and classification tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves significant improvements compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The learned representations effectively capture the underlying relationships between modalities, leading to enhanced performance in various cross-modal applications. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of pairwise constraints in facilitating cross-modal knowledge transfer and provide a promising direction for future research. Keywords: Cross-modal learning, Pairwise constraints, Multi-modal learning, Representation learning, Knowledge transfer.

Pedestrian detection is a critical task in computer vision with applications in autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics. This paper addresses the challenge of accurately detecting pedestrians in complex environments, where factors such as occlusion, varying lighting conditions, and diverse pedestrian appearances pose significant difficulties. We propose a novel approach based on deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) to improve detection accuracy and robustness. Our method leverages a multi-scale feature extraction framework combined with a region proposal network (RPN) to enhance the detection of pedestrians at different scales and orientations. Additionally, we introduce a context-aware loss function to better handle occluded and partially visible pedestrians. The proposed model is trained and evaluated on widely used pedestrian detection datasets, including Caltech Pedestrian and CityPersons. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of both precision and recall. The model achieves a significant reduction in false positives while maintaining high detection rates, particularly in challenging scenarios. This research contributes to the advancement of pedestrian detection systems by providing a robust and scalable solution that can be integrated into real-world applications. The proposed framework has the potential to enhance safety and efficiency in autonomous systems and urban surveillance. **Keywords**: pedestrian detection, deep convolutional neural networks, multi-scale feature extraction, region proposal network, context-aware loss function, autonomous systems.

This paper addresses the challenge of Bayesian inference in high-dimensional time-series data, where traditional methods often struggle with scalability and computational complexity. We propose the Orthogonal Stochastic Linear Mixing Model (OSLMM), a novel framework designed to efficiently handle high-dimensional time-series by leveraging orthogonal transformations and stochastic linear mixing. The OSLMM introduces a probabilistic approach that reduces dimensionality while preserving critical temporal dependencies, enabling robust inference in complex datasets. Our method employs a combination of variational inference and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques to approximate posterior distributions, ensuring computational efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the OSLMM outperforms existing methods in terms of inference speed, scalability, and predictive performance. The model achieves significant improvements in capturing latent structures and temporal dynamics, particularly in applications such as financial forecasting and climate modeling. This research contributes a scalable and interpretable solution for high-dimensional time-series analysis, offering practical implications for domains requiring real-time decision-making and large-scale data processing. Key innovations include the integration of orthogonal transformations to reduce computational overhead and the use of stochastic mixing to enhance model flexibility. Keywords: Bayesian inference, high-dimensional time-series, orthogonal transformations, stochastic linear mixing, variational inference, MCMC.

Heterogeneous graphs, characterized by diverse node and edge types, are prevalent in complex information systems such as social networks, citation databases, and recommendation platforms. However, learning effective and universal node embeddings across these varied structures poses significant challenges due to semantic complexity and structural diversity. This paper presents PanRep, a novel graph neural network (GNN) framework designed to extract universal node embeddings from heterogeneous graphs. PanRep introduces a unified representation learning approach that leverages type-aware aggregation mechanisms, enabling effective integration of heterogeneous node and edge features within a single embedding space. The framework employs adaptive message-passing strategies and dynamic weighting to capture multi-relational information, ensuring both node-level discrimination and generalizability. Experimental evaluation on several real-world heterogeneous graph datasets demonstrates that PanRep consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and clustering, achieving higher accuracy and better scalability. The proposed approach not only enhances task-specific performance but provides a versatile, transferable embedding framework for a wide range of downstream graph analytics. These results highlight the value of universal node embeddings and mark a significant step towards more generalizable graph representation learning. Keywords: heterogeneous graphs, graph neural networks, node embeddings, representation learning, multi-relational graphs, universal embedding.

Explainability is an important factor to drive user trust in the use of neural networks for tasks with material impact. However, most of the work done in this area focuses on image analysis and does not take into account 3D data. We extend the saliency methods that have been shown to work on image data to deal with 3D data. We analyse the features in point clouds and voxel spaces and show that edges and corners in 3D data are deemed as important features while planar surfaces are deemed less important. The approach is model-agnostic and can provide useful information about learnt features. Driven by the insight that 3D data is inherently sparse, we visualise the features learnt by a voxel-based classification network and show that these features are also sparse and can be pruned relatively easily, leading to more efficient neural networks. Our results show that the Voxception-ResNet model can be pruned down to 5\% of its parameters with negligible loss in accuracy.

Semi-supervised learning (SSL) leverages unlabeled data to improve model performance, particularly beneficial when labeled data is scarce. This paper introduces a novel Pseudo-Representation Labeling (PRL) approach to enhance SSL by generating high-quality pseudo-labels. PRL utilizes a representation learning framework to create cluster-friendly embeddings of both labeled and unlabeled data. These representations are then used to propagate labels from labeled data points to unlabeled data points within the same cluster, forming pseudo-labels. We propose a novel loss function that encourages consistency between predicted labels and these representation-based pseudo-labels, effectively guiding the model to learn from unlabeled data while mitigating the risk of error accumulation. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that PRL outperforms state-of-the-art SSL methods in image classification and text categorization tasks. The proposed method not only achieves higher accuracy but also exhibits better robustness to noisy or imbalanced data. PRL provides a simple yet effective strategy for leveraging unlabeled data, paving the way for improved performance in various real-world applications where labeled data is limited. Keywords: Semi-Supervised Learning, Representation Learning, Pseudo-Labeling, Unlabeled Data, Clustering, Machine Learning.

This paper addresses the significant challenge of accurately monitoring and identifying human activities, as well as detecting falls, utilizing computational models. The research aims to enhance reliability and efficiency in environments such as healthcare by developing an innovative approach that leverages Fourier domain features. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel methodology that extracts and analyzes features in the Fourier domain for human activity recognition and fall detection. By transforming temporal signals into the frequency domain, the model captures essential characteristics that are otherwise less discernible in the time domain. This method emphasizes the use of signal processing techniques to improve classification accuracy. Results/Findings: Our approach was subjected to extensive testing using public datasets consisting of various human activities and fall scenarios. The model demonstrated superior performance, achieving higher accuracy rates compared to existing time-domain feature-based methods. Notably, the system was particularly effective in distinguishing complex activity patterns and detecting falls with minimal false positives. Conclusion/Implications: The findings suggest that the Fourier domain feature approach significantly contributes to the field of human activity recognition and fall detection, offering a robust and efficient solution for real-time applications. The implications of this research extend to enhancing safety monitoring systems in elderly care facilities and enabling proactive intervention in critical scenarios. Key keywords associated with our research include human activity recognition, fall detection, Fourier domain features, signal processing, and classification accuracy.

This study aims to develop a predictive model for county-level corn yields using deep Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) models, addressing the need for accurate yield forecasts in agricultural planning and decision-making. Our approach utilizes a combination of historical climate data, soil characteristics, and crop management practices as inputs to train the LSTM network. The results show that our model achieves high accuracy in predicting corn yields, outperforming traditional statistical methods and demonstrating the potential for LSTM models in agricultural yield prediction. Key findings include the identification of critical climate and soil factors influencing corn yields, as well as the model's ability to capture complex temporal relationships between these factors. The study contributes to the development of advanced predictive analytics in agriculture, with implications for improved crop management, resource allocation, and policy decision-making. By leveraging deep learning techniques, such as LSTM, this research provides a novel approach to predicting county-level corn yields, with potential applications in precision agriculture, sustainability, and food security. Keywords: deep learning, LSTM, corn yields, agricultural forecasting, precision agriculture.

Spatio-temporal (ST) data, which represent multiple time series data corresponding to different spatial locations, are ubiquitous in real-world dynamic systems, such as air quality readings. Forecasting over ST data is of great importance but challenging as it is affected by many complex factors, including spatial characteristics, temporal characteristics and the intrinsic causality between them. In this paper, we propose a general framework (HyperST-Net) based on hypernetworks for deep ST models. More specifically, it consists of three major modules: a spatial module, a temporal module and a deduction module. Among them, the deduction module derives the parameter weights of the temporal module from the spatial characteristics, which are extracted by the spatial module. Then, we design a general form of HyperST layer as well as different forms for several basic layers in neural networks, including the dense layer (HyperST-Dense) and the convolutional layer (HyperST-Conv). Experiments on three types of real-world tasks demonstrate that the predictive models integrated with our framework achieve significant improvements, and outperform the state-of-the-art baselines as well.

The paper addresses the challenge of automatically enhancing digital photos by leveraging semantic understanding. Current photo adjustment techniques often lack a deep comprehension of the content within images, leading to suboptimal enhancements. This research introduces a novel, semantics-aware approach that enhances photos by understanding the underlying content. Methods/Approach: We propose a deep learning framework that utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract semantic features from images. This framework integrates these features into a photo adjustment model that dynamically modifies brightness, contrast, and color balance based on the detected content, such as landscapes, portraits, or architecture. The model is trained on a diverse dataset to ensure broad applicability and robustness. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional photo adjustment techniques in both objective metrics and subjective evaluations. The semantics-aware framework achieves superior image quality, with improvements evident in both visual assessments and quantitative scores. In particular, our method excels in maintaining naturalness and enhancing aesthetics, as verified by user studies and comparisons with existing methods. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a significant advancement in the field of automated photo enhancement by incorporating semantic awareness into the adjustment process. The proposed model not only improves the quality of photo adjustments but also sets the stage for future developments in content-aware image processing. Its potential applications span photography, digital media, and content creation industries, positioning it as a valuable tool for both amateur and professional use. Keywords: semantics-aware, photo adjustment, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, image processing.

This paper presents a unified framework for understanding and analyzing Local Stochastic Approximation (LSA) algorithms, which underpin both Federated Learning (FL) and Distributed Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning (DMTRL). The objective is to bridge the gap between these two domains by identifying common algorithmic structures and convergence properties. We propose a generalized LSA model that captures the decentralized nature of FL and the multi-agent decision-making aspects of DMTRL. Our approach leverages stochastic gradient updates and local model aggregation to enable efficient distributed optimization across heterogeneous tasks and data sources. Through theoretical analysis, we establish convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, demonstrating that the proposed framework achieves sublinear regret and optimality gaps comparable to centralized methods. Experimental results on benchmark datasets and reinforcement learning environments validate the effectiveness of the unified approach, showing significant improvements in communication efficiency and scalability compared to existing methods. The findings highlight the versatility of LSA in addressing challenges such as data privacy, task heterogeneity, and resource constraints, offering a foundation for future advancements in distributed learning systems. **Keywords**: Local Stochastic Approximation, Federated Learning, Distributed Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning, Decentralized Optimization, Convergence Analysis, Communication Efficiency.

Blocks In a blockchain, a block is a key component that is essential to the organizationand operation of the network. It serves as a storage facility for a variety of trans actions and other important information. Each block consists of a block pream-ble, which establishes a chronological sequence and contains metadata such as the block’s unique identification, timestamp, and a reference to the prior block. Theblock consists of transactions, which are a collection of various blockchain network operations. Sender and destination addresses, digital signatures for authen tication, and other relevant data are all included in these transactions. The block also has a Merkle tree root, which offers a quick way to confirm the accuracy of the transactions it includes. In addition, a cryptographic hash function generates a unique block hash for each block. This block hash guarantees the immutability ofthe block’s content and acts as a digital fingerprint for it. For instance, in proof of-work consensus algorithms, miners compete to find a nonce value that, whenpaired with the block header, satisfies particular criteria, adding a layer of secu rity by solving computational puzzles. The block serves as the essential building element of the blockchain, making it possible to store and verify transactions in a safe, open, and effective manner.

This paper introduces the Face Transformer, a novel deep learning approach for face recognition tasks. The objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of face recognition systems by leveraging the strengths of transformer architectures. Our method utilizes a transformer-based model to learn robust and discriminative facial features, which are then used for recognition. The Face Transformer is trained on a large-scale face dataset and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark face recognition datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, with significant improvements in recognition accuracy and reduced computational requirements. The Face Transformer has important implications for various applications, including security, surveillance, and social media. By combining the benefits of transformer models with the specific requirements of face recognition, our research contributes to the development of more accurate and efficient face recognition systems, with potential applications in AI, computer vision, and machine learning. Key keywords: face recognition, transformer, deep learning, facial features, AI models.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficient policy learning and adaptation in complex environments. The objective is to develop a novel approach that enables agents to learn from experiences and adapt to new situations effectively. We propose an importance weighted policy learning framework that leverages experience replay and weighted sampling to focus on the most informative experiences. Our approach utilizes a combination of model-free and model-based reinforcement learning techniques to improve the efficiency and robustness of policy learning. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of sample efficiency and adaptability, achieving significant improvements in cumulative rewards and convergence rates. The key contributions of this research include the development of a weighted sampling strategy and the integration of importance weighting into policy learning, enabling more effective adaptation to changing environments. This work has important implications for applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and other areas where efficient policy learning and adaptation are crucial. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, policy learning, importance weighting, experience replay, adaptive control.

Forecasting time series data across diverse systems presents a significant challenge, particularly when forecast tasks exhibit inherent but unknown cluster structures. This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance forecasting accuracy by learning predictive leading indicators tailored to these unknown clusters. Our method combines unsupervised learning to identify clusters of forecast tasks based on their historical data characteristics, with a meta-learning framework to train predictive models that leverage leading indicators relevant to each cluster. Specifically, we employ a dynamic time warping-based clustering algorithm to group similar forecast tasks, followed by a neural network architecture that learns to predict future time series values using cluster-specific leading indicators. Experiments on several real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional forecasting methods and static leading indicator selection techniques. The results highlight the importance of adaptive leading indicator selection based on the underlying cluster structure of forecast tasks, offering significant improvements in forecasting accuracy and robustness, especially in complex and dynamic environments. Key words: time series forecasting, leading indicators, clustering, meta-learning, predictive modeling.

Dropout is a widely used regularization technique in deep learning, known for preventing overfitting and improving model generalization. However, its role as an optimization trick remains less explored. This paper investigates dropout from an optimization perspective, aiming to uncover its mechanisms beyond traditional regularization. We analyze how dropout influences the training dynamics of neural networks, particularly its impact on gradient descent optimization and loss landscape exploration. Through extensive experiments and theoretical analysis, we demonstrate that dropout acts as an implicit optimizer by introducing stochasticity, which helps escape poor local minima and accelerates convergence. Our findings reveal that dropout not only regularizes but also enhances optimization efficiency, especially in complex, non-convex loss landscapes. This dual role of dropout provides new insights into its effectiveness and suggests potential applications in designing more robust optimization strategies for deep learning models. The implications of this study extend to improving training stability and performance in various machine learning tasks, offering a fresh perspective on dropout as a versatile tool in neural network optimization. **Keywords**: dropout, optimization, deep learning, regularization, stochastic gradient descent, loss landscape, neural networks.

This paper addresses the challenge of Visual Question Answering (VQA) within multimodal contexts, specifically focusing on TextVQA, where answers are embedded within images containing textual elements. The objective is to enhance the accuracy of answer prediction in TextVQA tasks using an innovative approach. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel method leveraging Iterative Answer Prediction combined with Pointer-Augmented Multimodal Transformers. Our approach incorporates a text-aware attention mechanism to effectively capture and process visual-textual information. This method iteratively refines answer predictions by dynamically adjusting attention focus, significantly improving upon traditional transformer models. Results/Findings: The proposed model demonstrates superior performance in text-based VQA benchmarks, achieving a notable increase in accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art models. By integrating the pointer mechanism, the model effectively disambiguates context and locates relevant textual information within the visual content, leading to more precise answer generation. Conclusion/Implications: Our research contributes a robust and innovative framework for improving answer prediction in TextVQA applications, highlighting the potential of combining iterative refinement with pointer-augmented architectures. The findings suggest broad applicability in fields requiring sophisticated multimodal processing capabilities, such as automated document analysis, enhanced image searching, and assistive technologies. This work paves the way for further exploration into multimodal transformers that can decode and integrate complex visual-textual cues. Key Keywords: Visual Question Answering (VQA), TextVQA, multimodal transformers, iterative prediction, pointer mechanism, text-aware attention, machine learning, computer vision.

Reinforcement learning usually makes use of numerical rewards, which have nice properties but also come with drawbacks and difficulties. Using rewards on an ordinal scale (ordinal rewards) is an alternative to numerical rewards that has received more attention in recent years. In this paper, a general approach to adapting reinforcement learning problems to the use of ordinal rewards is presented and motivated. We show how to convert common reinforcement learning algorithms to an ordinal variation by the example of Q-learning and introduce Ordinal Deep Q-Networks, which adapt deep reinforcement learning to ordinal rewards. Additionally, we run evaluations on problems provided by the OpenAI Gym framework, showing that our ordinal variants exhibit a performance that is comparable to the numerical variations for a number of problems. We also give first evidence that our ordinal variant is able to produce better results for problems with less engineered and simpler-to-design reward signals.

We present a fast and scalable algorithm to induce non-monotonic logic programs from statistical learning models. We reduce the problem of search for best clauses to instances of the High-Utility Itemset Mining (HUIM) problem. In the HUIM problem, feature values and their importance are treated as transactions and utilities respectively. We make use of TreeExplainer, a fast and scalable implementation of the Explainable AI tool SHAP, to extract locally important features and their weights from ensemble tree models. Our experiments with UCI standard benchmarks suggest a significant improvement in terms of classification evaluation metrics and running time of the training algorithm compared to ALEPH, a state-of-the-art Inductive Logic Programming (ILP) system.

Time-series data, critical in domains such as healthcare, finance, and IoT, is increasingly vulnerable to adversarial attacks that compromise the integrity and reliability of predictive models. This paper addresses the pressing need to evaluate and enhance the robustness of time-series models against such threats. We propose a comprehensive benchmarking framework to systematically assess the effectiveness of adversarial attacks and defenses tailored for time-series data. Our approach leverages state-of-the-art attack strategies, including gradient-based and optimization-driven methods, to generate adversarial perturbations. Concurrently, we evaluate defense mechanisms such as adversarial training, noise injection, and model regularization. Through extensive experiments on diverse datasets, we demonstrate the varying susceptibility of time-series models to adversarial manipulations and identify key factors influencing their robustness. Our findings reveal that certain defense strategies significantly improve model resilience without compromising predictive accuracy. This study contributes a standardized evaluation protocol for adversarial robustness in time-series analysis, offering practical insights for developing secure and reliable systems. The proposed framework and results provide a foundation for future research in adversarial machine learning for sequential data. **Keywords**: adversarial attacks, time-series data, model robustness, adversarial defenses, benchmarking, machine learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficient knowledge transfer in Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) training by exploring the synergies between semantic and visual similarities. The objective is to develop a novel approach that leverages these similarities to improve the transferability of knowledge across different CNN architectures and datasets. Our method utilizes a dual-embedding framework, combining semantic embeddings from natural language processing with visual embeddings from image features, to create a unified representation space. This enables the efficient transfer of knowledge from a pre-trained CNN to a target network, reducing the need for extensive retraining. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional transfer learning methods, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and reducing training time by up to 50%. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a semantic-visual similarity metric and a novel dual-embedding framework, which can be applied to various CNN-based applications, such as image classification, object detection, and segmentation. Our work has important implications for the development of more efficient and adaptable CNN training methods, with potential applications in areas like computer vision, robotics, and autonomous systems, and is relevant to keywords like deep learning, knowledge transfer, and neural network pruning.
