The increasing complexity of modern sales environments necessitates efficient management systems to optimize team performance and achieve revenue targets. Manually tracking sales activities, managing leads, and monitoring individual performance can be time-consuming and prone to errors, hindering overall sales effectiveness. This thesis addresses the need for a streamlined and automated approach to sales staff management. This research aims to design and develop a comprehensive Sales Staff Management System that improves sales team efficiency and productivity. Specifically, the system aims to solve problems related to inefficient task allocation, lack of real-time performance monitoring, and insufficient data-driven insights for informed decision-making. The system is built using a three-tier architecture, leveraging a Python-based backend with a Django framework, a PostgreSQL database for data storage, and a React-based frontend for user interaction. The development approach follows an iterative agile methodology, incorporating user feedback at each stage to ensure the system meets the specific needs of sales teams. Key features include lead management, task assignment, performance tracking with customizable dashboards, reporting functionalities, and role-based access control. The developed system offers a centralized platform for managing sales staff activities, providing real-time insights into individual and team performance. The implemented reporting features enable data-driven decision-making for optimizing sales strategies. The system contributes to the field by providing a practical and adaptable solution for enhancing sales team efficiency and effectiveness, leading to increased revenue generation. In conclusion, this thesis successfully presents the design and development of a Sales Staff Management System that addresses critical challenges in modern sales environments. The system provides a valuable tool for businesses to improve sales team performance and achieve their revenue goals. Future development directions include integrating predictive analytics for sales forecasting and incorporating mobile accessibility for enhanced user convenience.

This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating mutual information, a fundamental measure in information theory used to quantify the dependence between variables. We propose an innovative approach utilizing inductive estimation to overcome limitations in traditional methods, which often suffer from bias and inefficiency, especially in high-dimensional settings. Methods/Approach: Our approach introduces a convex maximum-entropy framework based on copula theory, focusing on capturing dependencies through a flexible copula model. This model leverages convex optimization techniques to inductively estimate mutual information by maximizing entropy subject to known constraints, ensuring robustness and efficiency. The copula approach provides a scalable solution suitable for complex and large datasets. Results/Findings: The proposed method is rigorously evaluated against existing mutual information estimation techniques. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The convex maximum-entropy copula model effectively captures intricate dependencies between variables, leading to more reliable mutual information estimates. Comparisons with state-of-the-art methods highlight the model's capability to handle high-dimensional data and complex variable interactions. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel inductive framework for mutual information estimation, offering significant improvements over traditional approaches. The integration of convex maximum-entropy and copula theory not only enhances estimation accuracy but also expands the applicability of mutual information analysis to broader fields such as machine learning, data mining, and statistical inference. Potential applications include feature selection, network analysis, and understanding complex data structures in AI systems. Keywords include mutual information, copula theory, convex optimization, maximum-entropy, and high-dimensional data estimation.

A variety of deep neural networks have been applied in medical image segmentation and achieve good performance. Unlike natural images, medical images of the same imaging modality are characterized by the same pattern, which indicates that same normal organs or tissues locate at similar positions in the images. Thus, in this paper we try to incorporate the prior knowledge of medical images into the structure of neural networks such that the prior knowledge can be utilized for accurate segmentation. Based on this idea, we propose a novel deep network called knowledge-based fully convolutional network (KFCN) for medical image segmentation. The segmentation function and corresponding error is analyzed. We show the existence of an asymptotically stable region for KFCN which traditional FCN doesn't possess. Experiments validate our knowledge assumption about the incorporation of prior knowledge into the convolution kernels of KFCN and show that KFCN can achieve a reasonable segmentation and a satisfactory accuracy.

This paper introduces a large-scale multimodal knowledge base system designed to effectively answer visual queries. The system integrates diverse data modalities, including images, text, and structured knowledge graphs, to provide comprehensive answers to complex user queries involving visual content. Our approach leverages advanced techniques in computer vision, natural language processing, and knowledge representation to facilitate reasoning across modalities. Specifically, we employ a novel attention mechanism to align visual features with relevant textual descriptions and knowledge graph entities, enabling accurate and context-aware query answering. Experimental results on a newly created benchmark dataset demonstrate that our system significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed system showcases the potential of multimodal knowledge bases for a wide range of applications, including image retrieval, visual question answering, and intelligent assistants. Keywords: Multimodal Knowledge Base, Visual Question Answering, Knowledge Graph, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, Attention Mechanism.

This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance the sample efficiency and stability of model-based reinforcement learning by leveraging model confidence. We propose Masked Model-based Actor-Critic (MMAC), a framework that selectively trusts the learned environment model based on its predicted uncertainty. MMAC employs a masking mechanism, informed by the model's confidence, to dynamically blend model-based and model-free learning. Regions where the model exhibits high confidence are utilized for efficient policy improvement via model-based rollouts, while regions with low confidence rely on model-free learning to ensure robustness. Our experiments on benchmark continuous control tasks demonstrate that MMAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art model-based and model-free algorithms in terms of sample efficiency and asymptotic performance. Furthermore, we provide an ablation study to analyze the impact of different confidence measures and masking strategies. The results indicate that dynamically adapting the trust in the model based on its confidence leads to more stable and efficient learning, offering a promising direction for deploying reinforcement learning in complex and uncertain environments. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Model-Based Learning, Actor-Critic, Uncertainty, Confidence, Sample Efficiency.

This paper addresses the challenge of recognizing new semantic concepts in previously unseen visual domains, a crucial step towards achieving true artificial intelligence. Our objective is to develop a robust and adaptable visual recognition system capable of generalizing to novel concepts and domains without requiring extensive retraining. We propose a novel approach that combines transfer learning with meta-learning, enabling our model to learn domain-agnostic features and adapt quickly to new visual domains. Our method utilizes a transformer-based architecture to capture complex relationships between visual elements and semantic concepts. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in recognizing new semantic concepts in unseen domains. Our research contributes to the development of more flexible and generalizable visual recognition systems, with potential applications in areas such as autonomous vehicles, robotics, and medical imaging. Key contributions include the introduction of a new meta-learning framework for domain adaptation and the demonstration of significant improvements in recognizing new semantic concepts. Relevant keywords: visual recognition, semantic concepts, domain adaptation, meta-learning, transformer architecture, artificial intelligence.

Recent style transfer models have provided promising artistic results. However, given a photograph as a reference style, existing methods are limited by spatial distortions or unrealistic artifacts, which should not happen in real photographs. We introduce a theoretically sound correction to the network architecture that remarkably enhances photorealism and faithfully transfers the style. The key ingredient of our method is wavelet transforms that naturally fits in deep networks. We propose a wavelet corrected transfer based on whitening and coloring transforms (WCT^2) that allows features to preserve their structural information and statistical properties of VGG feature space during stylization. This is the first and the only end-to-end model that can stylize a 1024\times1024 resolution image in 4.7 seconds, giving a pleasing and photorealistic quality without any post-processing. Last but not least, our model provides a stable video stylization without temporal constraints. Our code, generated images, and pre-trained models are all available at https://github.com/ClovaAI/WCT2.

Latent factor models are the driving forces of the state-of-the-art recommender systems, with an important insight of vectorizing raw input features into dense embeddings. The dimensions of different feature embeddings are often set to a same value empirically, which limits the predictive performance of latent factor models. Existing works have proposed heuristic or reinforcement learning-based methods to search for mixed feature embedding dimensions. For efficiency concern, these methods typically choose embedding dimensions from a restricted set of candidate dimensions. However, this restriction will hurt the flexibility of dimension selection, leading to suboptimal performance of search results. In this paper, we propose Differentiable Neural Input Search (DNIS), a method that searches for mixed feature embedding dimensions in a more flexible space through continuous relaxation and differentiable optimization. The key idea is to introduce a soft selection layer that controls the significance of each embedding dimension, and optimize this layer according to model's validation performance. DNIS is model-agnostic and thus can be seamlessly incorporated with existing latent factor models for recommendation. We conduct experiments with various architectures of latent factor models on three public real-world datasets for rating prediction, Click-Through-Rate (CTR) prediction, and top-k item recommendation. The results demonstrate that our method achieves the best predictive performance compared with existing neural input search approaches with fewer embedding parameters and less time cost.

This paper presents GLEAN, a novel generative model designed for large-factor image super-resolution. The primary objective of this research is to address the limitations of existing super-resolution techniques that often struggle with reconstructing high-quality images from low-resolution inputs, particularly at large upscaling factors. We propose a unique latent bank approach that encodes diverse visual patterns, enabling the model to learn rich representations from a vast dataset. Utilizing a combination of advanced convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial networks, GLEAN demonstrates enhanced performance in generating high-resolution images that not only preserve fine details but also exhibit improved perceptual quality compared to traditional methods. Our results showcase significant advancements, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets with large-factor scaling, outperforming leading super-resolution frameworks in both quantitative metrics and qualitative visual assessments. The findings underscore the effectiveness of our latent bank architecture in capturing intricate textures and promoting plausible image generation. In conclusion, GLEAN represents a significant contribution to the field of image processing, offering innovative methodologies for large-factor super-resolution with potential applications in various domains such as digital media, biomedical imaging, and remote sensing. Future work will explore the extension of this model to other image generation tasks, further broadening its impact. Keywords: generative model, image super-resolution, latent bank, deep learning, convolutional neural networks.

This paper introduces DAFAR, a novel approach to defend against adversarial attacks by leveraging feedback-autoencoder reconstruction. The objective is to develop a robust defense mechanism that can effectively detect and mitigate adversarial perturbations in deep neural networks. Our method utilizes a feedback loop to refine the reconstruction of input data, allowing the autoencoder to learn a more accurate representation of the original data distribution. We employ a combination of adversarial training and reconstruction loss to enhance the robustness of our model. Experimental results demonstrate that DAFAR outperforms existing defense methods in terms of adversarial robustness and accuracy. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, including MNIST and CIFAR-10, against various types of adversarial attacks. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a feedback-autoencoder reconstruction mechanism and the demonstration of its effectiveness in defending against adversarial attacks. Our work has important implications for the development of robust and secure deep learning models, with potential applications in areas such as computer vision and cybersecurity. Key keywords: adversarial attacks, autoencoder, deep learning, robustness, defense mechanisms, feedback loop, reconstruction loss.

This paper introduces the Synthesize-It-Classifier, a novel generative classifier that leverages recurrent self-analysis to enhance its learning capabilities. The objective is to develop a classifier that can synthesize new data samples to improve its performance on complex classification tasks. Our approach employs a recurrent neural network architecture that enables the classifier to analyze its own performance and generate new samples to augment the training data. The results show that the Synthesize-It-Classifier outperforms traditional classifiers on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating improved accuracy and robustness. Key findings include the ability to generate high-quality synthetic data samples that effectively augment the training data, leading to improved classification performance. The Synthesize-It-Classifier has significant implications for applications where labeled data is scarce or expensive to obtain. By highlighting the novelty of our approach, which combines generative modeling with recurrent self-analysis, this research contributes to the development of more effective and efficient classification systems, with potential applications in areas such as image classification, natural language processing, and recommender systems, utilizing keywords such as generative models, recurrent neural networks, self-analysis, and synthetic data augmentation.

Deep face recognition systems have witnessed substantial progress in recent years, yet challenges remain in achieving robust performance under varying pose, illumination, and expression conditions. This paper presents a novel approach to boosting deep face recognition accuracy by explicitly disentangling appearance and geometry information within facial representations. Our method introduces a dual-branch deep learning framework where appearance-related features (such as texture and color) are separated from geometry-related features (such as facial structure and shape) at the feature extraction stage. This disentanglement is facilitated through a specialized loss function and architectural innovations that encourage the network to learn invariant and complementary representations. Comprehensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms conventional deep face recognition methods, particularly in scenarios involving significant facial variations. The results show improved recognition accuracy, enhanced robustness to occlusions, and better generalization to unseen data. Our findings highlight the importance of disentangling appearance and geometry in face recognition, offering valuable insights for developing more reliable and interpretable biometric systems. Key contributions include the design of the disentangling framework and its effectiveness in real-world, unconstrained environments. Keywords: deep face recognition, disentanglement, facial appearance, facial geometry, deep learning, biometric systems.

Spectral clustering is a widely used technique for graph partitioning, particularly in sparse graphs where traditional methods often struggle. This paper introduces a unified framework for spectral clustering that addresses key challenges in sparse graph analysis, such as scalability and computational efficiency. The proposed approach integrates advanced matrix factorization techniques with adaptive graph sparsification methods to reduce computational complexity while maintaining clustering accuracy. We evaluate the framework on a variety of benchmark datasets, including real-world sparse graphs from social networks and biological systems. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing spectral clustering algorithms in terms of both runtime and clustering quality, achieving up to a 30% improvement in accuracy on highly sparse graphs. Furthermore, the framework is shown to be robust to noise and scalable to large-scale datasets. The key contribution of this work lies in its ability to unify and optimize spectral clustering for sparse graphs, offering a practical solution for applications in network analysis, community detection, and beyond. This research advances the state-of-the-art in graph clustering and provides a foundation for future developments in spectral methods for sparse data. **Keywords**: spectral clustering, sparse graphs, matrix factorization, graph sparsification, network analysis, community detection.

The identification of orphaned data points in large datasets is a critical challenge in data analysis, particularly in domains such as healthcare and genomics. This paper introduces a novel approach, Corresponding Projections for Orphan Screening (CPOS), designed to efficiently detect and classify orphaned data points in high-dimensional datasets. The proposed method leverages a combination of dimensionality reduction techniques and adaptive clustering algorithms to map data points into a lower-dimensional space, where orphaned instances are more easily identifiable. CPOS employs a multi-stage projection framework that ensures robustness against noise and outliers while maintaining computational efficiency. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CPOS outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and scalability, achieving a 15% improvement in orphan detection rates. Furthermore, the method is shown to be highly adaptable to various data types, including structured and unstructured data. The implications of this research extend to applications in anomaly detection, data cleaning, and precision medicine, where identifying orphaned data points can significantly enhance decision-making processes. This work contributes a scalable and effective solution to the problem of orphan screening, offering a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in data-intensive fields. **Keywords**: Orphan screening, dimensionality reduction, adaptive clustering, anomaly detection, high-dimensional data, data cleaning.

This paper addresses the challenge of fine-grained age estimation in uncontrolled environments, where existing methods often struggle with variability in lighting, pose, and expression. Our objective is to develop a robust and accurate age estimation system that can operate effectively in real-world settings. To achieve this, we propose an Attention LSTM Network that leverages the strengths of both attention mechanisms and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architectures. Our approach focuses on learning subtle facial features that are highly correlated with age, while also capturing temporal dependencies in facial expressions. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art age estimation models, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.5 years on a large-scale dataset. The key contributions of our research include the introduction of attention-based feature extraction and the application of LSTM networks to model temporal relationships in age estimation. Our work has significant implications for various applications, including forensic analysis, healthcare, and social media analytics, where accurate age estimation is crucial. Key keywords: age estimation, Attention LSTM, deep learning, facial analysis, computer vision.

Accurately predicting the center and scale of objects in digital images is fundamental to numerous computer vision tasks, such as object detection, pose estimation, and image segmentation. Traditional prediction methods often suffer from instability and suboptimal accuracy, particularly when faced with occlusions, varied object orientations, and complex backgrounds. This paper proposes an Adapted Center and Scale Prediction (ACSP) approach designed to enhance both stability and accuracy in these challenging environments. The proposed method introduces a dynamic feature aggregation mechanism that leverages both global and local image contexts, combined with a refined regression model optimized for center and scale estimation. Comprehensive experiments were conducted on benchmark datasets, comparing ACSP with existing state-of-the-art approaches. Results demonstrate consistent improvements in key performance metrics, including average precision and localization consistency, especially in scenarios with high variability. The ACSP framework exhibits robustness against noise and partial visibility, maintaining superior performance across diverse testing conditions. This study’s findings suggest that the adapted prediction strategy not only yields measurable gains in accuracy but also delivers greater reliability for downstream computer vision applications. Key contributions include a novel dynamic feature aggregation mechanism, an optimized regression model, and extensive performance evaluation. Keywords: center prediction, scale estimation, computer vision, robustness, deep learning, feature aggregation, model stability.

Objective: Understanding social relationships from visual data is crucial for applications ranging from social media analysis to human–robot interaction. This paper introduces a novel Dual-Glance Model designed to decipher pairwise social relationships in images by integrating both local and global context cues. Methods/Approach: Our model employs two sequential “glances.” The first glance focuses on a coarse, holistic view of the entire scene to capture global context—such as setting and co-occurring objects—using a convolutional backbone. The second glance applies an attention-driven mechanism to cropped regions around target individuals, extracting fine-grained cues like body language and facial expressions. Feature maps from both glances are fused through a learned weighting network, enabling the model to balance scene-level and interpersonal details dynamically. Results/Findings: Evaluated on a publicly available social-relationship dataset, the Dual-Glance Model achieves a 7% improvement in classification accuracy over state-of-the-art single-glance and context-aggregation baselines. Ablation studies demonstrate that each glance contributes uniquely, with the attention module boosting recognition of nuanced relationships (e.g., “colleagues” vs. “friends”). Conclusion/Implications: By explicitly separating and then fusing global scene understanding with targeted interpersonal analysis, the Dual-Glance Model advances the automatic inference of social relationships. This approach can enhance downstream tasks in social media indexing, surveillance systems, and collaborative robotics. Keywords: social relationship recognition, dual-glance model, deep learning, computer vision, attention mechanism

In the rapidly evolving IT industry, effective human resource (HR) management is critical for the success of project-based organizations. However, many IT companies face challenges in efficiently allocating, tracking, and managing their workforce across multiple projects. Traditional HR management systems often lack the flexibility and integration needed to handle dynamic project requirements, leading to inefficiencies and resource misallocation. This research addresses this gap by proposing a web-based system designed to streamline HR management in IT companies, ensuring optimal resource utilization and project alignment. The primary objective of this thesis is to develop a comprehensive website that facilitates HR management by integrating project-specific data, employee skills, and workload distribution. The system aims to solve key problems such as resource overloading, skill mismatches, and lack of real-time visibility into project progress. By leveraging modern web development technologies, including React.js for the front end, Node.js for the back end, and MySQL for database management, the proposed system provides a user-friendly interface and robust functionality. The development follows an agile methodology, ensuring iterative improvements and adaptability to user feedback. The expected outcomes of this research include a fully functional HR management website that enhances resource allocation efficiency, improves project tracking, and supports data-driven decision-making. The system’s contributions lie in its ability to bridge the gap between HR management and project execution, offering a scalable solution tailored to the needs of IT companies. In conclusion, this research demonstrates the significance of integrating HR management with project workflows in the IT sector. The developed system not only addresses current inefficiencies but also provides a foundation for future enhancements, such as incorporating AI-driven resource optimization and predictive analytics. This work paves the way for further studies on advanced HR management solutions in dynamic and project-driven environments.

Objective: Graph coarsening is a fundamental technique for reducing the size of large-scale graphs while preserving their essential structural and spectral properties. Although it has been extensively studied in scientific computing—particularly for multigrid solvers and spectral partitioning—its adoption in modern machine-learning pipelines remains fragmented. This paper aims to bridge that gap by providing a unified treatment of graph coarsening methods and demonstrating their applicability across both domains. Methods/Approach: We introduce a flexible, multilevel coarsening framework that generalizes classical algebraic multigrid (AMG) coarseners and recent spectral sparsification techniques. Our approach selects node aggregates based on a combination of local edge weights, global spectral importance scores, and feature-based affinities. We further propose an adaptive refinement step that iteratively rebalances coarse graphs to better support downstream learning tasks such as graph neural network (GNN) training and spectral clustering. Results/Findings: Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets from scientific computing (mesh graphs, finite-element matrices) and machine learning (social networks, citation graphs) show that our method achieves up to 10× reduction in graph size with less than 2% loss in algebraic connectivity. When used as a preprocessing step for GNNs, coarsened graphs yield training speed-ups of 3–5× while matching or improving accuracy compared to full-scale models. In spectral partitioning tasks, our coarsened graphs attain cuts within 1.5% of the optimal. Conclusion/Implications: By unifying coarsening strategies across disciplines, our work highlights the transferable benefits of multilevel graph reduction. The proposed framework enables scalable scientific simulations and accelerates machine-learning workflows without sacrificing solution quality. This synergy paves the way for more efficient large-scale graph analytics in both traditional numerical methods and emerging AI applications. Keywords: graph coarsening, multilevel algorithms, spectral sparsification, graph neural networks, scientific computing.

This paper addresses the problem of drift estimation, a critical issue in machine learning and data streams, where underlying distributions change over time. Our objective is to develop an effective method for estimating drift in complex systems using graphical models. We propose a novel approach that leverages probabilistic graphical models to represent relationships between variables and detect changes in the underlying distribution. Our method utilizes a combination of structural learning and parameter estimation to identify drift points and estimate the magnitude of change. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in estimating drift in various synthetic and real-world datasets, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The key contributions of this research include the development of a graphical model-based framework for drift estimation and the introduction of a new metric for evaluating drift detection performance. Our work has significant implications for applications in areas such as concept drift, anomaly detection, and time-series analysis, and highlights the potential of graphical models in addressing complex problems in machine learning and data science, with relevant keywords including drift estimation, graphical models, concept drift, and machine learning.

Iris recognition across different spectral domains and resolutions presents significant challenges due to variations in illumination, sensor characteristics, and spatial details. Traditional methods struggle to bridge the domain gap, leading to degraded performance in cross-spectral and cross-resolution scenarios. To address this issue, we propose a novel Deep GAN-Based Cross-Spectral Cross-Resolution Iris Recognition (GAN-CSCR) framework that enhances feature consistency and improves matching accuracy across different modalities. Our approach leverages a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to synthesize high-resolution iris images in a unified spectral domain, preserving discriminative texture patterns while mitigating spectral discrepancies. A dual-stream feature extractor is integrated to learn domain-invariant representations, ensuring robustness against resolution and wavelength variations. Additionally, we introduce an adaptive feature alignment module that refines embeddings to improve recognition performance. Extensive experiments on benchmark cross-spectral and cross-resolution iris datasets demonstrate that GAN-CSCR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both verification and identification tasks. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of GAN-based domain adaptation for enhancing iris recognition in real-world heterogeneous scenarios. Keywords: Iris Recognition, Cross-Spectral Matching, Cross-Resolution Enhancement, Generative Adversarial Networks, Domain Adaptation, Biometric Security.

This paper introduces PowerGym, a novel reinforcement learning environment designed for research and development of Volt-Var control strategies in power distribution systems. We implement a deep reinforcement learning algorithm, specifically a proximal policy optimization (PPO) agent, and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving Volt-Var control objectives such as voltage regulation and loss minimization under varying load and generation conditions. Results show that the PPO agent trained in PowerGym outperforms traditional rule-based control methods in maintaining voltage stability and reducing power losses. PowerGym offers a valuable platform for researchers and engineers to develop and test advanced control strategies for modern power distribution systems, fostering innovation in smart grid technologies. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Volt-Var Control, Power Distribution Systems, Smart Grid, OpenAI Gym, Distributed Energy Resources.

Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various computer vision tasks, but their computational and memory demands often hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. This paper addresses the critical question of whether retraining is necessary after pruning deep CNN networks to achieve efficiency without sacrificing performance. We propose a systematic evaluation of pruning methods, focusing on their impact on model accuracy, computational efficiency, and retraining requirements. Our approach includes structured and unstructured pruning techniques, combined with an analysis of layer sensitivity and sparsity patterns. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that certain pruning strategies can achieve significant model compression (up to 70% reduction in parameters) with minimal accuracy loss, even without retraining. Furthermore, we identify scenarios where retraining is essential to recover performance, particularly in highly compressed models. The findings provide practical insights for deploying efficient CNN models in real-world applications, balancing the trade-offs between model size, computational cost, and accuracy. This work contributes to the growing body of research on model optimization, offering a framework for decision-making in pruning and retraining processes. **Keywords**: Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Networks, Model Pruning, Efficiency, Retraining, Model Compression.

Deep learning models are vulnerable to adversarial examples: subtly perturbed inputs designed to cause misclassification. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of both attack strategies for generating adversarial examples and defense mechanisms aimed at mitigating their impact. We categorize and analyze prominent attack techniques, including gradient-based, optimization-based, and transfer-based methods, evaluating their effectiveness against various deep learning architectures. Furthermore, we explore a range of defense strategies, such as adversarial training, input transformations, and certified defenses, discussing their strengths, limitations, and computational overhead. Our analysis reveals that while certain defenses offer improved robustness under specific attack scenarios, a universally robust defense remains an open challenge. We identify key research directions for future work, emphasizing the need for adaptive defense mechanisms and robust evaluation metrics to advance the field of adversarial robustness in deep learning. Keywords: Adversarial Examples, Deep Learning, Security, Attack, Defense, Robustness.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become fundamental in a wide range of applications; however, their large model sizes and computational demands hinder real-time execution on resource-constrained mobile devices. Weight pruning is a common approach to reduce model size and computational overhead, but existing methods predominantly generate unstructured or block sparsity patterns, which often fail to fully exploit hardware acceleration capabilities on mobile platforms. In this paper, we introduce PCONV, a novel pruning methodology that induces a highly efficient and hardware-friendly structured sparsity in DNN weights. PCONV identifies and preserves computationally significant connections while promoting sparsity that aligns with mobile processor architectures, enabling faster and more energy-efficient inference. We rigorously evaluate PCONV on standard mobile deep learning benchmarks, demonstrating substantial reductions in model size and inference latency compared to conventional pruning techniques, while maintaining competitive accuracy. Our experiments show real-time speedups of up to 3× on representative mobile devices. The proposed approach bridges the gap between algorithmic sparsity and practical hardware execution, delivering both strong compression and tangible acceleration. PCONV paves the way for the deployment of high-performance DNNs in resource-limited environments, and presents new directions for structured model compression. Keywords: weight pruning, structured sparsity, deep neural networks, mobile devices, model compression, real-time inference.

Traditional feature detectors, while effective, often struggle to balance detection accuracy with computational efficiency, making them suboptimal for time-critical or resource-constrained scenarios. In this paper, we introduce FFD: Fast Feature Detector, a novel algorithm designed to deliver high-quality feature detection at significantly improved speeds. FFD leverages a multi-scale analysis framework combined with an optimized core detection module to rapidly identify salient features while minimizing redundant computations. Extensive experiments on both standard benchmarks and real-world datasets demonstrate that FFD achieves comparable or superior accuracy to widely used methods such as SIFT and ORB, with up to 5x reduction in processing time. Additionally, FFD maintains robustness under various conditions, including image rotations, scale changes, and noise. Our findings indicate that FFD provides a practical and efficient solution for real-time computer vision applications on both desktop and embedded platforms. The proposed approach bridges the gap between detection speed and quality, enabling advanced tasks in robotics, augmented reality, and mobile vision. **Keywords:** feature detection, computer vision, real-time processing, multi-scale analysis, fast algorithms, robust detection

**Abstract** Understanding and forecasting human movement is critical for a variety of real-world applications, including autonomous navigation, surveillance, and human-computer interaction. This paper introduces TRiPOD, a novel framework for forecasting both human trajectories and pose dynamics in unconstrained, real-world environments. The objective of this research is to predict not only the spatial path (trajectory) of individuals but also their detailed bodily configurations (pose) over future time frames, addressing the challenges posed by natural, dynamic scenes. TRiPOD employs a unified deep learning approach that integrates spatio-temporal feature extraction and multi-modal data fusion to simultaneously model human movement and pose evolution. We evaluate TRiPOD on several challenging, in-the-wild datasets, demonstrating its superior ability to predict realistic and physically plausible human motion compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Extensive experiments show significant improvements in both trajectory accuracy and pose fidelity, highlighting the model’s capacity to handle social interactions, environmental variability, and occlusions. The findings indicate that joint modeling of trajectory and pose yields richer and more predictive representations of human motion. This work advances the field of human motion forecasting by providing an integrated solution for dynamic, real-world applications. Key contributions include the TRiPOD framework, the exploration of joint trajectory-pose prediction, and empirical benchmarks demonstrating robustness in diverse scenarios. Potential applications of this technology span robotics, smart surveillance, animation, and crowd analysis. **Keywords:** human trajectory forecasting, pose dynamics, deep learning, spatio-temporal model, human motion prediction, in-the-wild datasets, TRiPOD.

Branch prediction is a critical component of modern processor design, directly impacting performance. Traditional branch prediction techniques rely on heuristics and pattern matching. This paper explores a novel approach: framing branch prediction as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem. We investigate the potential of RL agents to dynamically learn and adapt branch prediction strategies, potentially surpassing the limitations of hand-engineered heuristics. We outline the rationale behind this approach, detailing the Markov Decision Process formulation and reward function design tailored for branch prediction. Furthermore, we present several case studies implementing RL-based branch predictors, comparing their performance against established techniques across various benchmark suites. Our results demonstrate that RL-based predictors can achieve competitive accuracy and, in certain scenarios, outperform traditional predictors by adapting to program-specific branch patterns. This work highlights the promise of applying reinforcement learning to branch prediction, paving the way for more intelligent and adaptive processor designs. Keywords: Branch Prediction, Reinforcement Learning, Processor Architecture, Computer Architecture, Machine Learning.

InfographicVQA addresses the growing need for automated systems capable of understanding and interpreting complex infographics, which combine visual and textual elements to convey information. The objective of this research is to develop a robust framework for Visual Question Answering (VQA) tailored specifically for infographics, enabling machines to answer questions based on their multimodal content. To achieve this, we introduce a novel dataset, InfographicVQA, comprising diverse infographics paired with question-answer annotations. We propose a hybrid deep learning model that integrates state-of-the-art vision and language processing techniques, leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for visual feature extraction and transformer-based architectures for text understanding and reasoning. Our approach emphasizes the fusion of visual and textual modalities to capture the intricate relationships within infographics. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms existing VQA baselines, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. The findings highlight the importance of domain-specific adaptations in VQA systems and provide valuable insights for future research in multimodal AI. This work contributes to advancing the field of automated infographic analysis, with potential applications in education, data journalism, and business intelligence. Keywords: Visual Question Answering, Infographics, Multimodal Learning, Deep Learning, Transformer Models.

This paper addresses the challenge of band selection from hyperspectral images, a crucial step for improving the efficiency and accuracy of image processing and analysis. Our objective is to develop an effective method for selecting the most informative bands from hyperspectral images. To achieve this, we propose an attention-based convolutional neural network (CNN) approach that leverages the strengths of both attention mechanisms and deep learning techniques. Our method learns to focus on the most relevant bands and suppress irrelevant ones, resulting in a significant reduction in dimensionality while preserving critical information. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our approach over traditional band selection methods, with improved classification accuracy and reduced computational complexity. The key findings of this study highlight the potential of attention-based CNNs for hyperspectral image analysis, enabling more efficient and accurate processing of large-scale hyperspectral data. This research contributes to the advancement of hyperspectral imaging and has important implications for various applications, including remote sensing, environmental monitoring, and agricultural management. Key keywords: hyperspectral images, band selection, attention-based CNNs, deep learning, dimensionality reduction.

The rapid growth of deep learning models has led to significant challenges in deploying them on resource-constrained devices due to their high computational and memory requirements. This paper addresses the problem of network compression while maintaining model performance and robustness. We propose a novel adversarial network compression framework that leverages adversarial training to optimize the trade-off between model size, inference speed, and accuracy. Our approach integrates a lightweight discriminator network to guide the compression process, ensuring that the compressed model retains its ability to generalize effectively under adversarial conditions. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art compression ratios while preserving competitive accuracy and robustness compared to existing techniques. The proposed framework is particularly effective for edge computing and IoT applications, where efficient and reliable model deployment is critical. This work contributes a scalable and adaptive solution to the growing demand for compact yet robust deep learning models, paving the way for broader adoption in real-world scenarios. **Keywords**: network compression, adversarial training, deep learning, model optimization, edge computing, IoT.

The objective of this study is to comprehend the benign overfitting phenomenon within the context of ridge function estimation, a topic of keen interest in machine learning due to its counterintuitive nature and implications on modern model generalization capabilities. This research aims to explore under what finite sample conditions benign overfitting occurs and its impact on the accuracy and reliability of function estimation. Methods/Approach: We adopt a theoretical framework to analyze ridge regression models, employing statistical learning theory to derive conditions and bounds under which benign overfitting is observed. Our approach involves leveraging finite sample complexity to rigorously evaluate how ridge regression models behave under various sample sizes and noise conditions, while also examining the influence of regularization parameters on model estimation and predictive performance. Results/Findings: The study uncovers critical insights into the interplay between sample size, regularization strength, and inherent noise levels that lead to benign overfitting in ridge function estimation. Our findings reveal that under specific circumstances, ridge regression can achieve minimal estimation error even when the model fits random noise—a hallmark of benign overfitting. We present a comprehensive analysis of the model's performance, considering both theoretical and empirical evidence, demonstrating improved estimation accuracy in scenarios characterized by high-dimensional data and limited samples. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides pivotal contributions to understanding benign overfitting, particularly in the context of ridge regression, with implications for designing algorithms capable of harnessing this phenomenon effectively. The insights facilitate the development of more robust predictive models that can capitalize on high-dimensional datasets efficiently, underscoring the importance of cautious parameter tuning. These advancements hold potential applications in areas such as signal processing, financial modeling, and any domain utilizing high-dimensional data representations. Keywords: benign overfitting, ridge regression, finite sample analysis, machine learning, regularization, statistical learning theory.

This paper addresses the challenge of fine-grained visual recognition using web images, which are often noisy and diverse. The objective is to develop a robust method that can effectively eliminate noisy samples and leverage hard examples to improve recognition accuracy. Our approach employs a novel sample selection strategy, combining a noise detection algorithm with a hard sample mining technique. The noise detection algorithm identifies and removes noisy samples, while the hard sample mining technique selectively retains informative examples that are most relevant to the recognition task. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, achieving significant improvements in recognition accuracy on several benchmark datasets. The key findings highlight the importance of sample quality and the benefits of focusing on hard examples in fine-grained visual recognition. Our research contributes to the development of more accurate and robust visual recognition systems, with potential applications in image classification, object detection, and image retrieval. Key keywords: fine-grained visual recognition, web images, noise detection, hard sample mining, deep learning, computer vision.

This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of autoencoders in representation learning for electronic health records (EHRs). Our approach utilizes various autoencoder architectures to learn compact and informative representations of EHR data, which can be used for downstream tasks such as patient clustering, disease prediction, and personalized medicine. We employ a range of autoencoder models, including vanilla autoencoders, denoising autoencoders, and variational autoencoders, and evaluate their performance on a large EHR dataset. Our results show that autoencoders can learn meaningful representations of EHR data, outperforming traditional feature extraction methods in terms of clustering quality and prediction accuracy. We also compare the performance of different autoencoder architectures and identify the most effective models for EHR representation learning. Our study demonstrates the potential of autoencoders in improving the analysis and interpretation of EHR data, with implications for clinical decision support, patient outcomes, and healthcare resource allocation. Key contributions of this work include the development of novel autoencoder-based methods for EHR representation learning and a comprehensive evaluation of their performance in real-world healthcare applications, with relevant keywords including autoencoders, electronic health records, representation learning, and deep learning.

We develop an automated variational inference method for Bayesian structured prediction problems with Gaussian process (GP) priors and linear-chain likelihoods. Our approach does not need to know the details of the structured likelihood model and can scale up to a large number of observations. Furthermore, we show that the required expected likelihood term and its gradients in the variational objective (ELBO) can be estimated efficiently by using expectations over very low-dimensional Gaussian distributions. Optimization of the ELBO is fully parallelizable over sequences and amenable to stochastic optimization, which we use along with control variate techniques and state-of-the-art incremental optimization to make our framework useful in practice. Results on a set of natural language processing tasks show that our method can be as good as (and sometimes better than) hard-coded approaches including SVM-struct and CRFs, and overcomes the scalability limitations of previous inference algorithms based on sampling. Overall, this is a fundamental step to developing automated inference methods for Bayesian structured prediction.

This paper presents a novel approach for automated road curb extraction from mobile LiDAR point clouds, addressing the challenges of efficient and accurate infrastructure mapping. The proposed method integrates a voxel-based filtering technique to reduce noise and data density, followed by a refined point cloud segmentation algorithm leveraging geometric features and spatial relationships to identify potential curb points. A Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC)-based model fitting is then applied to extract precise curb lines. The algorithm was tested on mobile LiDAR data collected from diverse urban and suburban environments. Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy in curb detection, achieving an average F1-score of 92%, and significant reduction in processing time compared to existing methods. The extracted curb information can be valuable for various applications, including high-definition map generation, autonomous driving, and urban planning. Key words: Mobile LiDAR, point cloud processing, road curb extraction, RANSAC, infrastructure mapping, segmentation.

Understanding robot manipulation tasks requires a seamless integration of visual perception and contextual semantics. This paper addresses the challenge of enabling robots to interpret and execute complex manipulation tasks by combining visual data with contextual understanding. We propose a novel framework that leverages advanced computer vision techniques and semantic reasoning to bridge the gap between low-level visual inputs and high-level task semantics. Our approach integrates a deep learning-based visual perception module with a knowledge-driven semantic reasoning engine, enabling robots to infer task objectives and constraints from their environment. The framework is evaluated on a diverse set of manipulation tasks, demonstrating superior performance in task understanding and execution compared to existing methods. Results show significant improvements in accuracy and adaptability, particularly in dynamic and unstructured environments. The proposed framework not only enhances robot autonomy but also provides a foundation for future research in human-robot collaboration and intelligent automation. This work contributes to the field by offering a scalable and interpretable solution for bridging visual perception and contextual semantics in robotic systems. **Keywords**: robot manipulation, visual perception, contextual semantics, deep learning, semantic reasoning, human-robot collaboration.

This paper describes the vision based robotic picking system that was developed by our team, Team Applied Robotics, for the Amazon Picking Challenge 2016. This competition challenged teams to develop a robotic system that is able to pick a large variety of products from a shelve or a tote. We discuss the design considerations and our strategy, the high resolution 3D vision system, the use of a combination of texture and shape-based object detection algorithms, the robot path planning and object manipulators that were developed.

In this study, we explore building a two-stage framework for enabling users to directly manipulate high-level attributes of a natural scene. The key to our approach is a deep generative network which can hallucinate images of a scene as if they were taken at a different season (e.g. during winter), weather condition (e.g. in a cloudy day) or time of the day (e.g. at sunset). Once the scene is hallucinated with the given attributes, the corresponding look is then transferred to the input image while preserving the semantic details intact, giving a photo-realistic manipulation result. As the proposed framework hallucinates what the scene will look like, it does not require any reference style image as commonly utilized in most of the appearance or style transfer approaches. Moreover, it allows to simultaneously manipulate a given scene according to a diverse set of transient attributes within a single model, eliminating the need of training multiple networks per each translation task. Our comprehensive set of qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach against the competing methods.

Labeled graphs function as more than mere visualization tools; they also act as encoders through the finite state splitting algorithm, a critical technique for mapping sequences within constrained systems. Based on their intended usage, encoders vary, but this thesis concentrates specifically on those designed to generate sequences that adhere to pre-defined constraints, as opposed to encoders that focus on accepting or recognizing input sequences. This distinction is vital for applications where sequence generation under strict rules is required. In parallel, coding theory investigates combinatorial structures, including positioning codes such as de Bruijn codes, which play a significant role in efficient data representation and transmission.

Embedding large and high dimensional data into low dimensional vector spaces is a necessary task to computationally cope with contemporary data sets. Superseding latent semantic analysis recent approaches like word2vec or node2vec are well established tools in this realm. In the present paper we add to this line of research by introducing fca2vec, a family of embedding techniques for formal concept analysis (FCA). Our investigation contributes to two distinct lines of research. First, we enable the application of FCA notions to large data sets. In particular, we demonstrate how the cover relation of a concept lattice can be retrieved from a computational feasible embedding. Secondly, we show an enhancement for the classical node2vec approach in low dimension. For both directions the overall constraint of FCA of explainable results is preserved. We evaluate our novel procedures by computing fca2vec on different data sets like, wiki44 (a dense part of the Wikidata knowledge graph), the Mushroom data set and a publication network derived from the FCA community.

The interpretability of machine learning models, particularly in the context of Variational Auto-Encoders (VAEs), remains a critical challenge in understanding their decision-making processes. This paper investigates instance-based interpretability of VAEs, focusing on how individual data points influence the model's latent space and reconstruction outputs. We propose a novel framework that leverages gradient-based attribution methods to analyze the contributions of input features to the latent representations and generated outputs. Our approach provides a granular understanding of how VAEs encode and decode data, enabling better insights into their internal mechanisms. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method effectively identifies key features driving the model's behavior, outperforming existing interpretability techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The findings highlight the potential of instance-based interpretability for improving the transparency and trustworthiness of VAEs in real-world applications, such as anomaly detection and data generation. This work contributes to the broader field of explainable AI by offering a practical and scalable solution for interpreting complex generative models. **Keywords**: Variational Auto-Encoders, interpretability, instance-based analysis, gradient-based attribution, explainable AI, latent space, generative models.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as powerful tools for processing graph-structured data, yet the internal mechanisms by which information is propagated and aggregated—known as message passing—remain incompletely understood. This paper aims to shed light on the message passing process within GNNs by introducing an analytical framework based on Power Iteration Clustering (PIC), a scalable and efficient clustering technique. We leverage PIC to systematically identify and visualize the evolution of node embeddings and their community structures throughout the layers of various GNN architectures. Through comprehensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets, we demonstrate how PIC uncovers patterns of information flow, highlights bottlenecks, and reveals the convergence behavior of embeddings. Our findings indicate that message passing exhibits distinct community formation dynamics dependent on both the architecture and the dataset properties. By correlating these dynamics with model performance, we provide new insights into over-smoothing, expressive power, and the influence of graph topology on learning outcomes. This work contributes a novel perspective and practical tools for interpreting, diagnosing, and potentially improving GNN models, paving the way for more interpretable and effective graph-based learning. Key keywords: Graph Neural Networks, message passing, Power Iteration Clustering, graph representation, node embeddings, interpretability.

Recent research has demonstrated the ability to estimate gaze on mobile devices by performing inference on the image from the phone's front-facing camera, and without requiring specialized hardware. While this offers wide potential applications such as in human-computer interaction, medical diagnosis and accessibility (e.g., hands free gaze as input for patients with motor disorders), current methods are limited as they rely on collecting data from real users, which is a tedious and expensive process that is hard to scale across devices. There have been some attempts to synthesize eye region data using 3D models that can simulate various head poses and camera settings, however these lack in realism. In this paper, we improve upon a recently suggested method, and propose a generative adversarial framework to generate a large dataset of high resolution colorful images with high diversity (e.g., in subjects, head pose, camera settings) and realism, while simultaneously preserving the accuracy of gaze labels. The proposed approach operates on extended regions of the eye, and even completes missing parts of the image. Using this rich synthesized dataset, and without using any additional training data from real users, we demonstrate improvements over state-of-the-art for estimating 2D gaze position on mobile devices. We further demonstrate cross-device generalization of model performance, as well as improved robustness to diverse head pose, blur and distance.

Thiên tai đang trở thành một trong những thách thức lớn đối với sản xuất nông nghiệp tại Việt Nam. Mỗi năm, thiên tai như lũ lụt, bão, hạn hán đã gây ra thiệt hại nặng nề cho ngành nông nghiệp, ảnh hưởng đến sản lượng và chất lượng sản phẩm. Theo thống kê, trong những năm gần đây, thiên tai đã gây ra thiệt hại hàng trăm tỷ đồng cho ngành nông nghiệp. Thiệt hại không chỉ dừng lại ở mức kinh tế, mà còn ảnh hưởng đến đời sống của người nông dân và cộng đồng. Để giảm thiểu tác động của thiên tai đối với sản xuất nông nghiệp, cần có những biện pháp phòng tránh và ứng phó kịp thời. Một số biện pháp được đề xuất bao gồm: - Xây dựng và hoàn thiện hệ thống cảnh báo thiên tai để kịp thời cảnh báo cho người dân và cơ quan chức năng. - Phát triển và ứng dụng công nghệ cao trong sản xuất nông nghiệp, như sử dụng máy móc và thiết bị tự động hóa để giảm thiểu thiệt hại. - Tăng cường đào tạo và huấn luyện cho người nông dân về kỹ năng phòng tránh và ứng phó với thiên tai. - Đầu tư vào hệ thống bảo vệ chống lũ lụt và bão để giảm thiểu thiệt hại. - Phát triển và ứng dụng các công nghệ mới như nông nghiệp thông minh để tăng cường khả năng chống chịu của cây trồng và vật nuôi. Bằng cách thực hiện những biện pháp trên, chúng ta có thể giảm thiểu tác động của thiên tai đối với sản xuất nông nghiệp và đảm bảo sự ổn định và phát triển của ngành này.

K ết quả này cho th ấy, Eimeria vermiformis có ảnh hư ởng đ ến việc thải trừ Nippostrongylus brasiliensis và có th ể thông qua h ệ đáp ứng mi ễn dịch ở chuột đồng nhi ễm.

3D Multi-object tracking (MOT) is crucial to autonomous systems. Recent work uses a standard tracking-by-detection pipeline, where feature extraction is first performed independently for each object in order to compute an affinity matrix. Then the affinity matrix is passed to the Hungarian algorithm for data association. A key process of this standard pipeline is to learn discriminative features for different objects in order to reduce confusion during data association. In this work, we propose two techniques to improve the discriminative feature learning for MOT: (1) instead of obtaining features for each object independently, we propose a novel feature interaction mechanism by introducing the Graph Neural Network. As a result, the feature of one object is informed of the features of other objects so that the object feature can lean towards the object with similar feature (i.e., object probably with a same ID) and deviate from objects with dissimilar features (i.e., object probably with different IDs), leading to a more discriminative feature for each object; (2) instead of obtaining the feature from either 2D or 3D space in prior work, we propose a novel joint feature extractor to learn appearance and motion features from 2D and 3D space simultaneously. As features from different modalities often have complementary information, the joint feature can be more discriminate than feature from each individual modality. To ensure that the joint feature extractor does not heavily rely on one modality, we also propose an ensemble training paradigm. Through extensive evaluation, our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on KITTI and nuScenes 3D MOT benchmarks. Our code will be made available at https://github.com/xinshuoweng/GNN3DMOT

This paper addresses the challenge of estimating sparse graphical models from truncated samples, where a significant portion of the data is missing. The objective is to develop efficient statistical methods that can accurately recover the underlying graph structure from incomplete data. We propose a novel approach that combines advanced sampling techniques with state-of-the-art sparse recovery algorithms. Our method, termed Truncated Graphical Lasso, leverages the truncated samples to estimate the graph structure, while incorporating sparsity-inducing penalties to promote accurate recovery of the underlying relationships. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in scenarios with high levels of truncation. The key findings of this research highlight the importance of accounting for truncation in graphical model estimation and demonstrate the potential of our method for applications in network analysis, gene expression, and social media analysis. Our contributions include the development of a novel statistical framework, efficient algorithms for sparse graph recovery, and insights into the robustness of graphical models to data truncation, with implications for machine learning, data mining, and statistical modeling. Key keywords: sparse graphical models, truncated samples, graph recovery, statistical modeling, machine learning.

Graph matching is an important problem that has received widespread attention, especially in the field of computer vision. Recently, state-of-the-art methods seek to incorporate graph matching with deep learning. However, there is no research to explain what role the graph matching algorithm plays in the model. Therefore, we propose an approach integrating a MILP formulation of the graph matching problem. This formulation is solved to optimal and it provides inherent baseline. Meanwhile, similar approaches are derived by releasing the optimal guarantee of the graph matching solver and by introducing a quality level. This quality level controls the quality of the solutions provided by the graph matching solver. In addition, several relaxations of the graph matching problem are put to the test. Our experimental evaluation gives several theoretical insights and guides the direction of deep graph matching methods.

This paper introduces Patch Shortcuts, a novel approach to identifying vulnerabilities in black-box systems through the use of interpretable proxy models. The objective is to efficiently detect potential weaknesses in complex systems without requiring extensive knowledge of their internal workings. Our method employs a combination of machine learning and model interpretation techniques to create proxy models that mimic the behavior of the black-box system, allowing for the identification of potential vulnerabilities. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of Patch Shortcuts in finding vulnerabilities, outperforming existing methods in terms of efficiency and accuracy. The key findings highlight the importance of interpretability in proxy models, enabling the identification of critical patches that can be used to exploit vulnerabilities. This research contributes to the field of cybersecurity by providing a novel, efficient, and interpretable approach to vulnerability detection, with potential applications in AI security, software testing, and system hardening. Key keywords: black-box systems, interpretable models, proxy models, vulnerability detection, AI security, model interpretation.

This paper introduces *Language2Pose*, a novel framework for natural language grounded pose forecasting, which bridges the gap between linguistic descriptions and human motion prediction. The objective of this research is to enable systems to generate accurate and contextually relevant human poses based on textual input, addressing the challenge of aligning semantic language cues with dynamic motion sequences. To achieve this, we propose a multimodal deep learning architecture that integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques with pose forecasting models. The framework leverages transformer-based encoders to process textual descriptions and combines them with temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) to model the sequential nature of human motion. Our approach is evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of pose accuracy and semantic alignment compared to existing methods. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed model in capturing nuanced relationships between language and motion. This work contributes to advancing human-computer interaction, virtual reality, and robotics by enabling more intuitive and context-aware motion generation systems. Key innovations include the integration of multimodal data and the development of a robust framework for language-driven pose forecasting. Keywords: pose forecasting, natural language processing, multimodal learning, human motion prediction, transformer models.

This paper introduces a novel context-aware, video-based risk descriptor designed to enhance cyclist safety. Our approach addresses the limitations of existing risk assessment methods by incorporating real-time visual data and contextual information to provide a more comprehensive understanding of potential hazards. We employ a deep learning model trained on a large dataset of cyclist videos annotated with environmental and traffic conditions to identify and classify risk factors. The system analyzes video frames to detect objects (e.g., vehicles, pedestrians), predict their trajectories, and assess the likelihood of collisions, while simultaneously integrating contextual data such as weather conditions, road type, and time of day to refine risk assessments. Experimental results demonstrate that our system achieves significantly higher accuracy in predicting cyclist risk compared to baseline models relying solely on contextual data or simple object detection. The proposed risk descriptor offers a valuable tool for developing advanced cyclist safety systems, including adaptive warning systems and autonomous vehicle interactions with cyclists, ultimately contributing to a reduction in cyclist accidents. Keywords: Cyclist Safety, Risk Assessment, Video Analysis, Context Awareness, Deep Learning, Computer Vision.

This paper introduces GATSBI, a novel generative framework for modeling agent-centric spatio-temporal object interactions. The objective is to develop a system that can learn and predict complex interactions between agents and objects in dynamic environments. GATSBI employs a multi-modal approach, combining graph neural networks and transformer architectures to capture spatial and temporal relationships. The method is evaluated on various benchmarks, demonstrating significant improvements in interaction prediction and scene understanding compared to existing methods. The results show that GATSBI can effectively generate realistic and diverse interaction scenarios, outperforming state-of-the-art models in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The contributions of this research lie in its ability to model complex spatio-temporal interactions, enabling applications in areas such as autonomous systems, human-robot interaction, and smart environments. Key aspects of GATSBI include its agent-centric perspective, spatio-temporal reasoning, and generative capabilities, making it a unique and valuable tool for understanding and predicting dynamic interactions. Relevant keywords: generative models, spatio-temporal reasoning, graph neural networks, transformer architectures, agent-centric interaction, human-robot interaction.

Abstract Accurate sales demand forecasting is a critical component for optimizing inventory management and resource allocation within the fast-growing e-commerce sector. This paper presents a novel methodology leveraging Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to improve the precision of sales demand predictions in e-commerce environments. The proposed approach utilizes historical sales data, seasonality patterns, and promotional events to train a robust LSTM model capable of capturing complex temporal dependencies and non-linear trends. Experimental evaluations were conducted on a large-scale real-world e-commerce dataset, with comparative analyses against traditional forecasting methods, including moving average and ARIMA models. Results demonstrate that the LSTM-based approach significantly enhances prediction accuracy, reducing forecasting error rates and providing more reliable demand forecasts. These findings underline the potential of deep learning techniques, particularly LSTM networks, in addressing the unique challenges of sales demand prediction in dynamic e-commerce settings. The methodology has practical implications for inventory optimization, supply chain management, and customer satisfaction. Key keywords: sales forecasting, e-commerce, LSTM, neural networks, deep learning, demand prediction, time series analysis.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of enhancing the robustness of autoregressive models by exploring potential vulnerabilities when these models are subjected to environmental manipulations. Understanding such vulnerabilities is essential for developing more secure AI systems, as autoregressive models play a significant role in numerous applications, ranging from language processing to time series prediction. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach for identifying and exploiting weaknesses in autoregressive models through strategic environmental manipulations. Our method involves simulating a variety of environmental changes and assessing the model's performance and adaptability under these conditions. By leveraging an innovative attack framework, we systematically alter environmental parameters to locate and maximize impacts on model output. Results/Findings: The study reveals significant insights into the susceptibility of autoregressive models to environmental shifts. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed attack method can effectively degrade model performance, revealing critical points where the model fails. Comparative analysis with existing attack techniques highlights the superiority of our approach in terms of efficiency and impact, showing up to a 30% decrease in model accuracy under optimal attack scenarios. Conclusion/Implications: The findings underscore the importance of incorporating environmental variability in the evaluation and training of autoregressive models. Our research contributes to the field by offering a potent tool for stress-testing these models, paving the way for more resilient AI systems. By understanding and mitigating the identified vulnerabilities, developers can enhance the robustness and security of autoregressive applications against adversarial environmental manipulations. Keywords: Autoregressive models, environmental manipulation, adversarial attacks, model robustness, AI security.

N ghiên c ứu của chúng tôi đ ã tiến hành đánh giá ảnh hư ởng của giai đo ạn phát tri ển của hạt phấn, ch ất điều tiết sinh trư ởng, s ự tương tác gi ữa tuổi mô s ẹo và nuôi trư ờng nuôi c ấy đến sự tạo cây vô tính ở cây dâu tây ph ản ứng trung tính v ới ánh sáng. Hầu hết mô s ẹo thu đư ợc trên môi trư ờng Dumas De Vaulx (C – medium) ch ứa 0,4 mg benzyl adenine (BA) + 0,1 mg 3 -indole acetic acid (IAA) + 2,0 mg 2,4 -Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4 -D). T ổ hợp chất điều tiết sinh trư ởng (1 mg BA + 2 mg IAA) trong môi trư ờng MS cho t ỷ lệ cây tái sinh cao nh ất (10,0%). S ự kết hợp giữa môi trư ờng Gamborg (B5) và mô s ẹo 2 tháng tu ổi đã cho số mầm tạo thành cao nh ất (7,1 m ầm). Phân tích đ ộ bội của cây tái sinh b ằng đếm nhi ễm sắc thể cho th ấy 50% là cây bát b ội, 10% cây l ục bội, 35% cây l ệch bội và 5% cây t ứ bội (đơn b ội). Sử dụng 30 b ộ mồi SSRs, chúng tôi nh ận thấy 10 cây bát b ội được hình t hành t ừ bao phấn giống cây m ẹ hoàn toàn v ề di truy ền. Kết quả đã chỉ ra rằng không có cây đ ồng hợp tử được tạo ra trong nuôi cấy bao ph ấn. Điều này đ ã chứng th ực rằng tất cả cây tái sinh đư ợc hình thành t ừ tế bào sinh dư ỡng. Chính vì v ậy, nuôi c ấy bao ph ấn có th ể là phương pháp hi ệu quả mới trong t ạo cây đơn b ội và nhân nhanh trên cây dâu tây ph ản ứng trung tính v ới ánh sáng.
