Monocular depth estimation is a critical task in computer vision, enabling numerous applications ranging from autonomous navigation to augmented reality using a single RGB image. This paper presents a novel deep multi-scale architecture designed to improve the accuracy and robustness of monocular depth prediction. Our approach leverages multi-scale feature extraction within a convolutional neural network (CNN) framework, enabling the model to capture both global scene context and fine-scale details. By integrating hierarchical feature maps through skip connections and adaptive fusion layers, the proposed model achieves superior spatial depth consistency without sacrificing computational efficiency. Experimental results on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our architecture consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality. Notably, our approach shows marked improvements in handling complex scenes and preserving depth discontinuities. The proposed system offers a practical solution for real-time depth estimation on edge devices. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of multi-scale architectures in advancing monocular depth estimation and open new avenues for future research in 3D scene understanding and real-world perception systems. Keywords: monocular depth estimation, deep learning, multi-scale architectures, convolutional neural networks, 3D reconstruction, computer vision

Animating static images presents a significant challenge in computer graphics and vision. This paper introduces a novel approach to animating pictures by leveraging Eulerian motion fields. Our method focuses on synthesizing plausible motion within a still image by first estimating a dense, pixel-level motion field using a combination of optical flow techniques and semantic segmentation. This field is then refined using a custom-designed energy function that enforces spatial coherence and smoothness, while respecting object boundaries. The refined motion field is subsequently used to advect pixel colors over time, generating an animation sequence. We present a novel blending strategy to minimize artifacts arising from disocclusion and motion discontinuities. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations demonstrate that our approach produces visually compelling animations with reduced artifacts compared to existing methods. Our work contributes a robust framework for animating static pictures, opening avenues for creative content generation and visual storytelling. Keywords: Image animation, Eulerian motion fields, optical flow, semantic segmentation, computer vision, animation synthesis.

We address the problem of solving complex bimanual robot manipulation tasks on multiple objects with sparse rewards. Such complex tasks can be decomposed into sub-tasks that are accomplishable by different robots concurrently or sequentially for better efficiency. While previous reinforcement learning approaches primarily focus on modeling the compositionality of sub-tasks, two fundamental issues are largely ignored particularly when learning cooperative strategies for two robots: (i) domination, i.e., one robot may try to solve a task by itself and leaves the other idle; (ii) conflict, i.e., one robot can easily interrupt another's workspace when executing different sub-tasks simultaneously. To tackle these two issues, we propose a novel technique called disentangled attention, which provides an intrinsic regularization for two robots to focus on separate sub-tasks and objects. We evaluate our method on four bimanual manipulation tasks. Experimental results show that our proposed intrinsic regularization successfully avoids domination and reduces conflicts for the policies, which leads to significantly more effective cooperative strategies than all the baselines. Bệnh động mạch vành (BMV) là một trong những nguyên nhân chính gây bệnh xuất và tử xuất trên toàn thế giới gây ra những tác động to lớn đến kinh tế - xã hội. Một trong những phương thức chẩn đoán hiện đại đối với BMV là đánh giá phân suất dự trữ lưu lượng động mạch vành bằng chụp cắt lớp vi tính (FFR-CT) có thể phát hiện được những vị trí hẹp có ý nghĩa làm thay đổi huyết động. The rapid evolution of visual data and the emergence of new semantic concepts pose significant challenges for computer vision systems. This research addresses the critical problem of recognizing new semantic concepts within new visual domains, a task that is increasingly vital for applications in autonomous vehicles, surveillance, and augmented reality. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach that leverages advanced machine learning techniques to adaptively learn and recognize semantic concepts in unfamiliar visual domains. The method integrates domain adaptation strategies with semantic concept modeling to effectively generalize across different visual environments. Our approach utilizes a two-step training process involving both labeled and unlabeled data to enhance the system's ability to recognize novel concepts. Results/Findings: The proposed model demonstrates superior performance in recognizing new semantic concepts compared to existing methods. Through rigorous experimentation on several benchmark datasets, our approach achieves substantial improvements in accuracy and robustness, illustrating its potential for practical real-world applications. The results also show enhanced adaptability to diverse visual domains, signifying its effectiveness in situations with rapid domain shifts. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a significant advancement in the field of computer vision, offering a scalable and efficient solution for recognizing new semantic concepts in dynamic visual environments. Future applications may include enhancing the capabilities of AI-driven platforms in complex settings and improving the generalization of models to new contextual scenarios. Our findings highlight the potential for deploying such adaptable systems in various intelligent technologies, paving the way for more responsive and intelligent visual recognition systems. Keywords: Semantic concepts, visual domains, domain adaptation, computer vision, machine learning, adaptability, dynamic environments.

While reinforcement learning algorithms can learn effective policies for complex tasks, these policies are often brittle to even minor task variations, especially when variations are not explicitly provided during training. One natural approach to this problem is to train agents with manually specified variation in the training task or environment. However, this may be infeasible in practical situations, either because making perturbations is not possible, or because it is unclear how to choose suitable perturbation strategies without sacrificing performance. The key insight of this work is that learning diverse behaviors for accomplishing a task can directly lead to behavior that generalizes to varying environments, without needing to perform explicit perturbations during training. By identifying multiple solutions for the task in a single environment during training, our approach can generalize to new situations by abandoning solutions that are no longer effective and adopting those that are. We theoretically characterize a robustness set of environments that arises from our algorithm and empirically find that our diversity-driven approach can extrapolate to various changes in the environment and task.

This paper addresses the challenge of moment localization in videos based on natural language queries, a crucial task for enhancing video understanding and retrieval systems. Traditional methods have struggled with efficiently capturing both temporal and contextual relationships, which are essential for precise localization of moments described by language. Methods: We propose a novel approach, Learning 2D Temporal Adjacent Networks (2D-TAN), designed to effectively integrate temporal correlations within video segments and semantic cues from language inputs. The 2D-TAN model leverages a two-dimensional adjacency representation that maps temporal segment pairs to align with the sequential and relational nature of video data. This network setup allows for a dynamic interaction between adjacent segments, encoded through an adjacency matrix to refine localization predictions. Results: Our experimental evaluation demonstrates that the 2D-TAN method significantly outperforms existing techniques on benchmark datasets, achieving higher precision and recall metrics in moment localization tasks. The proposed model exhibits robustness in handling varying video lengths and diverse query complexities, providing competitive performance across challenging scenarios. Conclusion: The introduction of 2D Temporal Adjacent Networks marks a notable advancement in video comprehension within natural language query contexts. This approach not only enhances the spatial-temporal modeling capabilities of existing systems but also establishes a robust framework for future research in video moment localization. Our findings suggest that integrating 2D adjacency structures can serve as a transformative tool for further applications in multimedia retrieval and automated content analysis. Keywords: 2D-TAN, moment localization, temporal adjacency networks, natural language, video understanding, video retrieval.

This paper addresses the challenge of estimating the structure of sparse graphical models from truncated samples, a common problem in various domains where data is often incomplete or censored. We propose a novel approach that leverages truncated data to efficiently estimate model parameters and graph structure. Our method combines a modified score matching estimator with a regularization technique specifically designed to handle truncation bias. This approach allows us to recover the underlying graph structure with significantly fewer samples compared to traditional methods that either discard truncated data or rely on complex imputation techniques. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on both synthetic and real-world datasets, showing improved accuracy in graph recovery and parameter estimation. Our findings contribute to the development of more robust and efficient algorithms for learning graphical models from incomplete data. Key words: graphical models, sparse estimation, truncated data, score matching, regularization, structure learning.

This paper introduces a novel approach to Visual Question Answering (VQA) that circumvents the need for traditional question-answer (QA) training data. Our method leverages pre-trained vision-language models and a carefully designed prompting strategy to enable zero-shot VQA capabilities. By formulating the VQA task as a masked language modeling problem, we guide the model to infer answers directly from the visual context and question without explicit QA pairs during fine-tuning. Specifically, we fine-tune a pre-trained model using only image-caption pairs and an auxiliary task focused on reasoning over visual attributes. Experimental results on standard VQA benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance compared to models trained on extensive QA datasets, particularly in out-of-distribution settings. The findings suggest that learning general visual-semantic relationships can be effectively transferred to VQA, reducing reliance on costly and task-specific annotations. This work contributes a paradigm shift in VQA, paving the way for more efficient and adaptable models. Keywords: Visual Question Answering, Zero-Shot Learning, Vision-Language Models, Prompting, Masked Language Modeling, Image Captioning.

This paper addresses the challenge of jointly inferring multiple graphs from matrix polynomials, a problem with significant implications in network analysis, machine learning, and data-driven decision-making. The objective is to develop a unified framework that enables the simultaneous reconstruction of multiple interrelated graphs, leveraging the inherent structure and dependencies captured by matrix polynomials. We propose a novel optimization-based approach that integrates graph sparsity constraints and matrix polynomial properties to ensure robust and scalable inference. Our method employs advanced numerical techniques to solve the resulting optimization problem efficiently, even for large-scale datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showcasing superior performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. The findings highlight the potential of this framework for applications in social network analysis, biological systems modeling, and multi-modal data integration. This work contributes to the field by providing a principled and scalable solution for joint graph inference, paving the way for future research in complex network analysis and beyond. **Keywords**: graph inference, matrix polynomials, network analysis, optimization, sparsity constraints, multi-graph learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of imbalanced datasets in corporate credit rating predictions, a critical issue that affects the reliability and accuracy of financial assessments. The research explores innovative approaches to enhance predictive performance under these conditions. Methods: We introduce a novel contrastive pre-training methodology, designed to improve feature representation specifically tailored for imbalanced datasets. By leveraging contrastive learning paradigms, the model pre-trains on augmented data, emphasizing distinguishing factors between different rating categories. This pre-trained model is then fine-tuned on the target credit rating dataset to achieve enhanced classification performance. Results: The proposed approach demonstrates significant improvements in predictive accuracy and stability over traditional methods, particularly in minority class predictions. Comparative analyses exhibit superior performance metrics, such as increased F1-score and precision, against baseline models and popular existing techniques, underscoring the model's efficiency in handling data imbalance. Conclusion: This study introduces a significant advancement in corporate credit rating models, showcasing the efficacy of contrastive pre-training in dealing with imbalanced datasets. The insights gained have broad implications for risk assessment and financial modeling, suggesting potential applications in various sectors requiring balanced predictive analytics. Key contributions include the development of a robust pre-training framework that capitalizes on contrastive learning to mitigate imbalances, paving the way for more reliable credit evaluation tools. Keywords: contrastive pre-training, imbalanced datasets, corporate credit ratings, financial modeling, predictive analytics, machine learning.

This paper proposes a novel High-order Differentiable Autoencoder (HDA) for nonlinear model reduction, aiming to address the challenges of capturing complex dynamics in high-dimensional systems. Our approach combines the strengths of autoencoders and high-order differentiation to learn compact, interpretable representations of nonlinear systems. The HDA model utilizes a hierarchical architecture to extract salient features and capture higher-order interactions between variables. We demonstrate the effectiveness of HDA through numerical experiments on various nonlinear systems, showcasing its ability to accurately reconstruct system dynamics and outperform existing model reduction techniques. The key findings highlight the importance of high-order differentiation in capturing nonlinear relationships and the potential of HDA for applications in fields such as fluid dynamics, structural mechanics, and control systems. Our research contributes to the development of more efficient and accurate model reduction methods, enabling the simulation and analysis of complex systems with reduced computational cost. Key keywords: nonlinear model reduction, high-order differentiation, autoencoders, compact representations, system dynamics.

This paper introduces a novel Backtracking Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP)-based Image Classifier designed for weakly supervised top-down salient object detection. The objective of this research is to address the challenge of accurately identifying salient objects in images with minimal supervision, leveraging the strengths of SPP to enhance feature extraction and classification. The proposed method integrates a backtracking mechanism into the SPP framework, enabling the model to refine its predictions by iteratively revisiting and reassessing feature representations at multiple scales. This approach eliminates the need for pixel-level annotations, relying instead on image-level labels, thereby reducing annotation costs and computational complexity. The methodology involves training the classifier using a weakly supervised learning paradigm, where the model learns to detect salient regions by correlating image-level labels with spatial features extracted through the SPP layers. The backtracking mechanism ensures robust feature refinement, improving the model's ability to localize salient objects accurately. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing weakly supervised techniques in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score. Additionally, the model exhibits superior generalization capabilities across diverse image domains. The key contribution of this work lies in the integration of backtracking with SPP, which enhances the model's ability to handle scale variations and complex backgrounds in weakly supervised settings. This research has significant implications for applications such as image segmentation, object recognition, and autonomous systems, where efficient and accurate salient object detection is critical. Keywords: Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), weakly supervised learning, salient object detection, backtracking mechanism, image classification.

The research addresses the challenge of improving model performance in cross-domain applications, where a model trained on a source domain must adapt effectively to a new, often significantly different, target domain. Traditional approaches often suffer from performance degradation when applying a learned model to a domain with distinct characteristics. Methods: We propose a novel framework called Importance Filtered Cross-Domain Adaptation (IFCDA). This approach utilizes importance-weighted feature selection to identify domain-invariant features that are critical for accurate domain adaptation. By leveraging a filtering mechanism, our method refines the feature set to focus on the most relevant information, enhancing the model’s adaptability across domains. Results: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the IFCDA approach significantly improves adaptation performance across various cross-domain tasks. In benchmark datasets across multiple domains, IFCDA consistently outperforms traditional domain adaptation methods, showing notable improvements in accuracy and robustness. Additionally, our approach exhibits reduced computational overheads due to its efficient feature filtering process. Conclusion: The Importance Filtered Cross-Domain Adaptation framework offers a substantial advancement in addressing the challenges of cross-domain learning. By focusing on crucial domain-invariant features, our method facilitates more effective deployment of models in diverse application scenarios. This research contributes to the field by providing a more adaptable and efficient solution for cross-domain challenges, potentially benefiting areas such as image classification, natural language processing, and more. Keywords: cross-domain adaptation, importance weighting, feature selection, domain-invariant features, model adaptability.

The research addresses the challenge of accurately recognizing human actions based on skeletal data, a task critical in numerous applications such as surveillance, human-computer interaction, and health monitoring. This paper proposes a novel model that leverages Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) enhanced through neural architecture searching to improve the performance of skeleton-based human action recognition. Methods/Approach: We introduce a tailor-made Graph Convolutional Network architecture specifically optimized for skeleton-based action recognition through an innovative neural searching technique. Our approach utilizes an automated method to discover the most effective GCN configurations, systematically exploring various architectural possibilities to maximize recognition accuracy. This technique ensures that the model optimally learns spatial-temporal features crucial for distinguishing complex human actions. Results/Findings: The proposed neural searching GCN model demonstrates superior performance on benchmark datasets compared to existing methods. The automatic optimization process allows for the discovery of architectures that significantly enhance recognition accuracy, achieving state-of-the-art results with improved computational efficiency. Our experiments reveal substantial gains in classification accuracy and robustness under various constraints. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel methodology for designing GCNs through neural searching, significantly advancing the field of skeleton-based human action recognition. The self-optimized model provides compelling insights into architectural choices that enhance learning capabilities. This approach has the potential to be applied in real-world scenarios demanding precise and reliable action recognition, laying the groundwork for further advancements in intelligent systems. Keywords include: Graph Convolutional Networks, neural searching, skeleton-based action recognition, human action recognition, AI models.

The purpose of this research is to address the challenges associated with accurate and efficient segmentation of medical images, a critical task for diagnostic and treatment planning in healthcare. Traditional methods often struggle with complex textures and shapes found in medical imaging, necessitating improved algorithms that leverage advancements in deep learning. Methods/Approach: In this study, we propose an Iterative Deep Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Network (IDCED-Net) specifically designed for medical image segmentation. Our approach involves an iterative refinement process that employs multiple convolutional encoder-decoder layers to improve segmentation accuracy with each iteration. The network leverages deep convolutional techniques and an encoder-decoder architecture to extract detailed semantic information from the images. Results/Findings: The IDCED-Net demonstrated superior performance in segmenting medical images compared to several state-of-the-art models. Through extensive testing on varied datasets comprising MRI and CT images, our method achieved notable improvements in segmentation accuracy and reduced error rates. Comparative analysis highlighted the model's ability to precisely delineate anatomical structures and reduce noise artifacts, thereby enhancing image clarity and usability. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of the IDCED-Net presents a significant advancement in medical image segmentation, offering higher precision and consistency in diagnosing and treating medical conditions. This model's iterative framework and deep learning-driven architecture pave the way for more robust and adaptable segmentation solutions in various medical imaging applications. The insights gained from this research underscore the potential for IDCED-Net to be integrated into clinical workflows, ultimately contributing to improved patient outcomes. Key keywords: medical image segmentation, deep convolutional network, encoder-decoder architecture, iterative refinement, MRI, CT images.

**Abstract** Efficient and accurate segmentation of individual workpieces within cluttered bins is a vital challenge in automated bin picking for industrial robotics. This paper presents a novel deep learning-based approach for workpiece region segmentation tailored specifically to bin picking scenarios. The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture enhanced by attention mechanisms to effectively discern and segment overlapping and partially occluded objects from depth and RGB images. To address the scarcity of annotated bin picking datasets, we introduce a synthetic data generation pipeline that simulates realistic bin environments, enabling robust model training. Evaluation was conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating that our approach achieves significant improvements in segmentation accuracy and processing speed compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The results indicate a substantial reduction in object mis-segmentation and improved precision in workpiece localization, thereby enhancing pick success rates in robotic applications. This research contributes an effective, scalable solution to the bin picking segmentation problem, facilitating more reliable automation in manufacturing settings. Keywords: bin picking, deep learning, region segmentation, convolutional neural network, robotic automation, industrial vision systems.

This paper introduces a novel graph convolutional memory (GCM) architecture to enhance deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents’ ability to learn and generalize in complex environments. The GCM utilizes graph convolutional networks to represent and reason about relationships between different states and actions encountered during the learning process. This allows the agent to capture long-range dependencies and improve its understanding of the environment's dynamics. The proposed approach is evaluated on a suite of challenging benchmark tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in sample efficiency and asymptotic performance compared to state-of-the-art DRL algorithms with standard memory architectures. Furthermore, we analyze the learned graph representations to gain insights into the agent's reasoning process and highlight the benefits of structured memory. The GCM provides a powerful and interpretable mechanism for incorporating relational knowledge into DRL, opening avenues for developing more robust and intelligent agents. Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Graph Convolutional Networks, Memory Networks, Relational Reasoning, Artificial Intelligence.

Semantic segmentation and object detection are critical components in the field of computer vision, widely used in applications such as autonomous driving and medical imaging. However, they are vulnerable to adversarial examples, which are inputs intentionally designed to deceive machine learning models. The objective of this research is to investigate the susceptibility of semantic segmentation and object detection systems to adversarial attacks and propose effective defense strategies. We introduce a novel approach that employs advanced adversarial training techniques to enhance model robustness against these threats. Our method leverages a combination of data augmentation and adversarial input generation to fortify the defense mechanisms of target models. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the resilience of both semantic segmentation and object detection models. Compared to standard training procedures, our technique reduces the error rates in challenging scenarios by substantial margins, thereby enhancing system reliability in practical deployments. The results further reveal the trade-offs between model accuracy and robustness against adversarial examples. This study contributes valuable insights into strengthening machine learning algorithms against adversarial attacks, ensuring safer and more dependable performance in real-world applications. By advancing the robustness of semantic segmentation and object detection systems, this research paves the way for developing secure AI solutions capable of operating in adversarial environments. Key keywords include adversarial examples, semantic segmentation, object detection, machine learning robustness, adversarial training.

Session-based recommendation (SBR) aims to predict user behavior based on short sequences of interactions, presenting a significant challenge due to the limited data per session. This paper addresses the exploration-exploitation trade-off in SBR by proposing a novel Batch-Constrained Distributional Reinforcement Learning (BC-DRL) framework. Unlike conventional RL methods that struggle with sparse rewards and off-policy learning instability in SBR, our approach learns a distributional representation of Q-values, capturing the uncertainty inherent in user behavior. Furthermore, batch constraints are introduced to mitigate the distributional shift when learning from offline session data, ensuring stable and efficient policy optimization. We empirically evaluate BC-DRL on several benchmark datasets for SBR, demonstrating significant improvements in recommendation accuracy and diversity compared to state-of-the-art SBR models and traditional RL algorithms. The results highlight the effectiveness of distributional RL in handling uncertainty and the importance of batch constraints for off-policy learning in the context of session-based recommendations. This work offers a promising direction for developing more robust and adaptive recommendation systems. Keywords: Session-based Recommendation, Reinforcement Learning, Distributional Reinforcement Learning, Batch-Constrained Learning, Recommendation Systems.

Semantic segmentation models are vulnerable to unauthorized access and manipulation, particularly in sensitive applications. This paper introduces a novel access control mechanism for these models using spatially invariant permutation of feature maps. Our approach transforms intermediate feature representations within the segmentation network through a permutation operation controlled by a secret key. This permutation is designed to be spatially invariant, preserving the underlying semantic relationships while effectively obfuscating the feature space without significantly impacting performance for authorized users. We evaluate our method on benchmark datasets, demonstrating that authorized users, possessing the correct key, experience minimal performance degradation, while unauthorized access attempts result in significantly degraded segmentation accuracy. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of spatially invariant permutation as a lightweight and robust access control mechanism for semantic segmentation models, offering a practical solution for securing these models against malicious use. Keywords: Access Control, Semantic Segmentation, Feature Permutation, Spatially Invariant, Model Security, Deep Learning.

This paper introduces the Generative Video Transformer (GVT), a novel approach to video generation that leverages the transformer architecture by treating objects as fundamental “words.” Instead of operating directly on pixel data, GVT first identifies and represents objects within video frames using a pre-trained object detector. These object representations, along with their spatial and temporal relationships, are then fed into a transformer network to generate subsequent video frames. This object-centric approach allows GVT to model complex object interactions and long-range dependencies more effectively than pixel-based generative models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of GVT on several benchmark video datasets, showing superior performance in terms of visual fidelity, motion coherence, and object consistency. Specifically, GVT achieves a significant improvement in Fréchet Video Distance (FVD) compared to state-of-the-art generative adversarial networks (GANs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs). These results suggest that representing videos as sequences of interacting objects provides a powerful framework for generative video modeling. Keywords: Video generation, transformer, object detection, generative model, deep learning, artificial intelligence.

The proposed method has significant implications for various applications, including image editing, computer vision, and robotics, where depth-aware image stylization can enhance the visual realism and accuracy of scene understanding. Objective: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) aims to recover an expert’s underlying reward function from observed behavior, but existing approaches often suffer from ambiguity and poor generalization in high-dimensional tasks. This paper introduces Deep PQR, a novel IRL framework that leverages “anchor actions”—a small set of actions with known reward values—to guide and stabilize reward inference. Methods: Deep PQR jointly learns a deep reward network and a policy model by incorporating anchor actions as fixed reference points in the reward space. We extend the classical projection-based IRL (PBRL) formulation with three components—Policy, Q-value, and Reward (PQR)—implemented via neural networks. Anchor actions are enforced through auxiliary loss terms that align predicted rewards with known values, reducing the solution space and mitigating reward ambiguity. Training proceeds by alternating between policy optimization using soft actor-critic and reward network updates via gradient matching. Results: Experiments on gridworld navigation, MuJoCo continuous control, and robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate that Deep PQR recovers more accurate reward functions and yields policies that better match expert behavior. Compared to Maximum Entropy IRL and state-of-the-art deep IRL baselines, Deep PQR achieves up to 25% improvement in reward recovery error and 30% faster convergence. Conclusion: By integrating anchor actions into a deep learning IRL pipeline, Deep PQR offers a principled way to resolve reward ambiguity and enhance learning stability. This approach advances IRL applicability in robotics, autonomous systems, and complex decision-making domains. Keywords: Inverse Reinforcement Learning, anchor actions, deep learning, reward inference, policy learning, Deep PQR.

Semantic image synthesis aims to generate realistic images from semantic layouts. While existing methods have shown promise, they often struggle with generating high-quality images, particularly in complex scenes, due to the limitations in effectively incorporating semantic information into the generative process. This paper introduces a novel class-adaptive normalization technique to enhance the efficiency and fidelity of semantic image synthesis. Our approach dynamically modulates the normalization parameters based on the semantic class of each region, allowing the generator to adapt its style and texture generation accordingly. We integrate this class-adaptive normalization into a generative adversarial network (GAN) framework. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, including Cityscapes and ADE20K, demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of visual quality and semantic accuracy. Furthermore, our model exhibits improved training stability and convergence speed compared to existing normalization techniques. The proposed method offers a practical solution for high-resolution semantic image synthesis, enabling more realistic and controllable image generation. Keywords: Semantic Image Synthesis, GAN, Normalization, Image Generation, Deep Learning.

Graph kernels are widely used for structured data analysis, offering a powerful framework for comparing graphs by mapping them into feature spaces. However, the distinction between explicit and implicit feature maps in graph kernels remains underexplored, limiting their interpretability and scalability. This paper presents a unifying view of explicit and implicit feature maps, addressing the gap in understanding their computational and theoretical properties. We propose a novel framework that bridges these two approaches, enabling efficient computation and enhanced interpretability of graph kernels. Our method leverages advanced matrix factorization techniques and spectral graph theory to derive explicit representations from implicit feature maps, while preserving the kernel's discriminative power. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in computational efficiency and classification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art graph kernel methods. The proposed framework not only advances the theoretical understanding of graph kernels but also provides practical insights for applications in bioinformatics, social network analysis, and recommendation systems. This work contributes to the broader field of graph-based machine learning by offering a scalable and interpretable solution for graph comparison tasks. **Keywords**: graph kernels, explicit feature maps, implicit feature maps, matrix factorization, spectral graph theory, structured data analysis.

Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) has shown promise in solving complex tasks by decomposing them into manageable subgoals. However, learning effective goal representations remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel approach to learning goal embeddings through self-play, enabling agents to autonomously discover and represent meaningful subgoals in hierarchical tasks. Our method leverages a two-phase training process: first, agents engage in self-play to explore the environment and generate diverse goal-directed behaviors; second, a goal embedding network is trained to encode these behaviors into a compact, actionable representation. We evaluate our approach on a suite of benchmark environments, demonstrating significant improvements in task completion rates and sample efficiency compared to existing HRL methods. The learned embeddings not only enhance the agent's ability to generalize across tasks but also provide interpretable representations of subgoals. Our results highlight the potential of self-play in advancing HRL, offering a scalable and adaptive framework for complex decision-making problems. Key contributions include a robust goal discovery mechanism, improved hierarchical policy learning, and a flexible architecture applicable to diverse domains. **Keywords**: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning, Goal Embeddings, Self-Play, Subgoal Discovery, Decision-Making, AI.

This research addresses the challenge of few-shot inductive link prediction in complex network settings, focusing on the effective transfer of knowledge from known subgraph structures to make predictions in unseen subgraphs. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel meta-learning framework tailored for subgraph-aware inductive link prediction. This approach leverages a meta-learning strategy to learn transferable knowledge across subgraphs, allowing the model to rapidly adapt to new subgraphs with limited data. The model incorporates subgraph-specific features and context, enhancing prediction accuracy in few-shot scenarios through a tailored training mechanism. Results/Findings: The proposed framework demonstrates significant improvement in prediction accuracy when compared to conventional models on benchmark datasets. Our results show enhanced adaptability and generalization capacity, especially in sparse or evolving networks, by successfully harnessing the relational patterns inherent in subgraphs. Performance evaluations highlight the model's superior predictive capabilities and efficiency over traditional link prediction methods and existing few-shot learning frameworks. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a robust method for subgraph-aware few-shot inductive link prediction, offering practical implications for applications in areas such as social network analysis, recommender systems, and biological networks. Our findings suggest promising pathways for further exploration of meta-learning techniques in network representation and inductive reasoning. The integration of subgraph context into the meta-learning paradigm marks a step forward in addressing the complexities of link prediction in dynamic and data-constrained environments. Keywords: Few-shot learning, link prediction, meta-learning, subgraph networks, inductive reasoning, network representation.

This paper explores the application of Neural Vector Autoregressions (NVARs) in forecasting, causality analysis, and impulse response estimation within time series data. Traditional Vector Autoregressive (VAR) models have been widely used for these tasks but often struggle with high-dimensional data and nonlinear relationships. To address these limitations, we propose a novel NVAR framework that leverages deep learning architectures to capture complex temporal dependencies and nonlinear dynamics. The approach integrates neural networks with autoregressive modeling, enabling more accurate predictions and robust causal inference. We evaluate the proposed method on synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its superior performance in forecasting accuracy and causality detection compared to conventional VAR models. Additionally, the framework provides interpretable impulse response functions, offering insights into the dynamic interactions between variables. The results highlight the potential of NVARs as a powerful tool for time series analysis, with applications in economics, finance, and other domains requiring advanced forecasting and causal modeling. **Keywords**: Neural Vector Autoregressions, time series forecasting, causality analysis, impulse response, deep learning, nonlinear dynamics.

Emotion recognition from body gestures is a crucial task in affective computing, with applications in human-computer interaction, surveillance, and healthcare. However, existing models rely heavily on labeled training data and struggle to generalize to unseen emotions or diverse body gestures. To address these challenges, we propose a Generalized Zero-Shot Emotion Recognition (GZS-ER) framework, which enables recognition of novel emotions without requiring labeled examples. Our approach leverages a semantic embedding space that maps body gestures to emotion concepts using a combination of graph-based representation learning and cross-modal alignment techniques. We introduce a gesture-emotion mapping module that learns transferable features, ensuring robust generalization to unseen emotions. Additionally, we incorporate a self-supervised contrastive learning mechanism to enhance feature discrimination and improve model robustness. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that GZS-ER significantly outperforms existing zero-shot and few-shot emotion recognition models, achieving high accuracy even for previously unseen emotions. These results highlight the potential of zero-shot learning for emotion recognition, paving the way for more adaptive and scalable affective computing systems. Keywords: Zero-Shot Learning, Emotion Recognition, Body Gestures, Affective Computing, Cross-Modal Learning, Contrastive Learning.

Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) have emerged as a powerful framework for generative modeling, but their training stability remains a critical challenge, often leading to suboptimal performance. This paper addresses the issue of instability in VAEs by proposing a novel re-parameterization strategy that enhances convergence and robustness during training. Our approach involves redefining the latent space representation and optimizing the variational lower bound through a modified loss function, which mitigates common issues such as posterior collapse and gradient instability. We evaluate the proposed method on benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in model stability, reconstruction accuracy, and sample quality compared to standard VAE implementations. Furthermore, our approach achieves competitive results in downstream tasks such as anomaly detection and data generation. The findings highlight the importance of re-parameterization in improving VAE performance and provide a practical framework for deploying stable generative models in real-world applications. This work contributes to the broader understanding of VAE optimization and opens new avenues for research in generative AI. **Keywords**: Variational Autoencoders, generative modeling, re-parameterization, training stability, latent space optimization, anomaly detection.

Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) aims to bridge the gap between labeled source domains and unlabeled target domains, enabling models to generalize effectively across different data distributions. However, existing UDA methods often rely on complex, computationally intensive architectures that hinder scalability and real-world deployment. This paper introduces *Light-weight Calibrator* (LWC), a novel, separable component designed to enhance UDA performance while maintaining computational efficiency. LWC operates as a plug-and-play module that can be integrated into existing UDA frameworks, leveraging lightweight calibration mechanisms to align feature distributions across domains without requiring additional supervision. Our approach employs a combination of adaptive normalization and domain-specific feature recalibration to minimize domain shift effectively. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that LWC achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, with significantly reduced computational overhead. The results highlight LWC's ability to improve domain adaptation accuracy while maintaining scalability, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments. This work contributes a practical and efficient solution to UDA, with potential applications in areas such as autonomous systems, medical imaging, and cross-domain data analysis. **Keywords**: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation, Light-weight Calibrator, Feature Alignment, Computational Efficiency, Domain Shift, Adaptive Normalization.

Delegate call Injection : a security issue that arises when a contract uses delegate calls in an insecure manner, allowing an attacker to exploit the contract’sbehavior and potentially manipulate its state or execute malicious code. This vulnerability occurs when a contract blindly trusts and delegates control to another contract without properly validating or sanitizing the input. If the called contract contains malicious code or unintended logic, it can manipulate the state of the called contract and potentially cause financial loss or other security breaches. To mitigate this vulnerability, developers should carefully review and audit the code, validate inputs, and implement proper access control and security checks to prevent unauthorized or malicious delegate calls.

Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification accuracy is significantly affected by insufficient training samples and imbalanced class distributions. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Spectral-Spatial-Dependent Global Learning (SSDGL) framework. This framework leverages spectral and spatial information to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled samples, thereby alleviating the problem of insufficient training data. Specifically, a spectral-dependent module adaptively selects relevant spectral bands, enhancing the discriminative power of spectral features. Simultaneously, a spatial-dependent module refines pseudo-labels by considering the spatial context, reducing the impact of noisy labels. Furthermore, a global learning strategy based on a contrastive loss function is employed to mitigate the effect of class imbalance by maximizing inter-class separation. Experiments on several benchmark HSI datasets demonstrate that the proposed SSDGL framework achieves superior classification performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly when dealing with limited and imbalanced training data. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed framework in improving HSI classification accuracy and robustness. Keywords: Hyperspectral Image Classification, Imbalanced Learning, Semi-Supervised Learning, Spectral-Spatial Feature Fusion, Contrastive Learning.

Abstract: Neural network models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in various machine learning tasks, yet their increasingly large size and computational demands pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This paper introduces the Teacher-Class Network (TCN), a novel neural network compression mechanism designed to optimize model efficiency while preserving predictive accuracy. The TCN framework operates by leveraging a hierarchical knowledge distillation approach, where a high-capacity teacher network guides multiple class-specific student networks. Each student network specializes in a subset of classes, significantly reducing the overall parameter count without compromising the representational power needed for accurate classification. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the TCN achieves substantial reductions in model size and inference latency—up to 50% more compact than conventional models—while maintaining comparable or improved accuracy. Additionally, comparative analysis with standard pruning and quantization techniques highlights the superior scalability and adaptability of the proposed mechanism. The Teacher-Class Network offers a promising direction for deploying deep learning models on edge devices, Internet of Things (IoT) systems, and mobile computing platforms. Key contributions include a novel class-specialization strategy, effective teacher-student knowledge transfer, and demonstrable improvements in compression rates and inference efficiency. Keywords: model compression, neural networks, knowledge distillation, class specialization, efficient deep learning.

The paper addresses the challenge of causal inference in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs), specifically focusing on a class known as Block MDPs. The primary goal is to enhance decision-making processes by identifying causal structures that remain invariant across diverse environments. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel framework for Invariant Causal Prediction (ICP) within Block MDPs. This approach leverages structural assumptions inherent in Block MDPs to separate confounding variables from causative factors that are robust across different settings. Our method combines elements of causal discovery with machine learning techniques to identify these invariant causal structures without reliance on pre-existing data partitions. Results/Findings: The experimental evaluation conducted across a range of synthetic and real-world Block MDP scenarios demonstrates the effectiveness of our causal prediction model. Our approach consistently outperforms traditional methods and existing causal inference frameworks, showing superior performance in terms of accuracy and generalization to unseen environments. This enhancement in model robustness contributes to more reliable policy development in decision-making systems operating under uncertainty. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of invariant causal prediction within Block MDPs represents a significant advancement in bridging causal inference with reinforcement learning under partial observability. This research not only extends theoretical knowledge in the intersection of causality and POMDPs but also presents practical implications for domains such as robotics, autonomous systems, and dynamic decision-making applications where understanding latent causal factors is crucial for performance. Future directions include exploring scalability and application in high-dimensional state spaces. Keywords: Block MDPs, Invariant Causal Prediction, Causal Inference, Reinforcement Learning, POMDP, Structural Assumptions, Decision-Making Systems.

This paper addresses the critical issue of uncertainties in artificial neural networks (ANNs), a fundamental challenge impacting the reliability and trustworthiness of AI systems. We aim to explore the sources, implications, and potential mitigations of uncertainties in ANNs, emphasizing their importance for decision-making processes in computer vision, natural language processing, and other AI applications. Methods/Approach: Our study employs a comprehensive analysis of both theoretical and empirical approaches to uncertainty modeling within ANNs. We investigate various methodologies, including Bayesian neural networks, Monte Carlo dropout, and ensemble techniques, to assess their effectiveness in capturing and quantifying uncertainties. We also propose a novel hybrid approach that combines these techniques to improve robustness and accuracy. Results/Findings: The findings reveal that each method offers unique strengths and trade-offs in uncertainty quantification. Our hybrid approach demonstrates superior performance in both theoretical scenarios and practical applications, reducing uncertainty by up to 15% compared to traditional methods. This improvement is illustrated through extensive testing on benchmark datasets in image classification and language tasks. Conclusion/Implications: The research provides significant insights into the nature of uncertainties in ANNs, highlighting the need for integrated approaches to enhance the reliability of AI systems in critical applications. Our findings contribute to the ongoing development of more trustworthy AI models and suggest pathways for future research in uncertainty management. This work is instrumental for practitioners and researchers striving to develop AI systems that are both accurate and reliable. Keywords: artificial neural networks, uncertainty, Bayesian methods, Monte Carlo dropout, ensemble techniques, reliability, AI systems.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficient deep neural network (DNN) execution on mobile devices, where computational resources and memory are limited. The objective is to develop a novel weight pruning method, termed PCONV, which introduces desirable sparsity in DNNs to facilitate real-time execution. PCONV employs a hybrid approach, combining structural and unstructured pruning techniques to effectively reduce model complexity while preserving accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that PCONV outperforms state-of-the-art pruning methods, achieving significant reductions in model size and computational overhead. On mobile devices, PCONV-enabled DNNs exhibit substantial speedups, making them suitable for real-time applications such as image classification, object detection, and speech recognition. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a novel pruning paradigm, significant improvements in model efficiency, and the enablement of real-time DNN execution on resource-constrained mobile devices. Keywords: DNN weight pruning, sparsity, real-time execution, mobile devices, deep learning, model compression.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for analyzing structured data, such as social networks, molecular structures, and recommendation systems. However, designing effective deep GNN architectures remains a significant challenge due to issues like over-smoothing and vanishing gradients. This paper addresses the problem of identifying optimal deep GNN architectures that can effectively capture hierarchical and long-range dependencies in graph-structured data. We propose a systematic approach to search for deep GNN architectures by leveraging neural architecture search (NAS) techniques, combined with novel strategies to mitigate common pitfalls in deep GNN design. Our method employs a reinforcement learning-based framework to explore and evaluate various architectural configurations, including layer types, skip connections, and normalization techniques. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the discovered architectures outperform existing state-of-the-art GNN models in terms of accuracy and scalability. Furthermore, the proposed approach provides insights into the design principles of deep GNNs, offering a foundation for future research in this domain. This work contributes to advancing the field of graph representation learning by enabling the development of more robust and efficient deep GNNs for complex real-world applications. **Keywords**: Graph Neural Networks, Deep Learning, Neural Architecture Search, Reinforcement Learning, Graph Representation Learning.

This paper introduces a new nonlinear dictionary learning method for histograms in the probability simplex. The method leverages optimal transport theory, in the sense that our aim is to reconstruct histograms using so-called displacement interpolations (a.k.a. Wasserstein barycenters) between dictionary atoms; such atoms are themselves synthetic histograms in the probability simplex. Our method simultaneously estimates such atoms, and, for each datapoint, the vector of weights that can optimally reconstruct it as an optimal transport barycenter of such atoms. Our method is computationally tractable thanks to the addition of an entropic regularization to the usual optimal transportation problem, leading to an approximation scheme that is efficient, parallel and simple to differentiate. Both atoms and weights are learned using a gradient-based descent method. Gradients are obtained by automatic differentiation of the generalized Sinkhorn iterations that yield barycenters with entropic smoothing. Because of its formulation relying on Wasserstein barycenters instead of the usual matrix product between dictionary and codes, our method allows for nonlinear relationships between atoms and the reconstruction of input data. We illustrate its application in several different image processing settings.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc đánh giá giá trị của hệ số khuếch tán biểu kiến trong việc chẩn đoán phân biệt các loại u thần kinh đệm bậc cao và bậc thấp. Hệ số khuếch tán biểu kiến là một chỉ số quan trọng trong hình ảnh học, giúp xác định tính chất của khối u và hỗ trợ trong việc đưa ra quyết định điều trị. Thông qua việc phân tích dữ liệu từ các bệnh nhân, nghiên cứu đã chỉ ra rằng hệ số này có thể cung cấp thông tin quý giá về mức độ ác tính của u, từ đó cải thiện độ chính xác trong chẩn đoán. Kết quả cho thấy sự khác biệt rõ rệt giữa hai loại u, mở ra hướng đi mới trong việc áp dụng công nghệ hình ảnh để nâng cao hiệu quả chẩn đoán và điều trị cho bệnh nhân mắc bệnh lý này.

Objective: Discriminative visual trackers often degrade when their online training sets become contaminated by noisy samples, background clutter, or occlusion-induced errors. This paper addresses the challenge of maintaining robust model updates by proposing a unified framework for adaptive decontamination of the training set. Methods: We introduce an adaptive weighting scheme that assigns a reliability score to each candidate training sample based on classification confidence, spatial consistency, and temporal stability. The decontamination process is formulated as a convex optimization that jointly learns the tracking model and sample weights. This formulation seamlessly integrates with both correlation-filter–based and deep-feature–based trackers, requiring only minor architectural adjustments. Results: Extensive experiments on OTB-2015, VOT-2018, and LaSOT benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, yielding average improvements of 3.2% in area-under-curve (AUC) and 15% in expected average overlap (EAO). Ablation studies confirm the individual contributions of confidence scoring and temporal smoothing to overall robustness. Conclusion: The proposed unified decontamination framework effectively suppresses the influence of corrupted samples, enhancing tracking stability under occlusion, fast motion, and background clutter. Its generality and low computational overhead make it a practical enhancement for a wide range of discriminative visual tracking systems. Keywords: discriminative visual tracking; training set decontamination; adaptive sample weighting; correlation filters; deep-feature tracking.

Mỗ Vew khi được tạo ra sẽ có một Controller đi kèm với nó. Trong khi các Vew điảm nhận kết xuất dữ lệu thì các Controller điảm nhận việc xử lý dữ lệu từ người dùng. Vớ mỗ sự kện nhận được, Controller có thể xử lý và tương tác trực tếp lên thành phần Vew và Model tương ứng điể điáp trả. Vew và Controller là ha thành phần cấu thành nên giao diện người dùng của ứng dụng. Chúng lưu gữ lên kết trực tếp điến Model. Trong kh Controller có thể thay điổ dữ lệu theo yêu cầu của người dùng thì Vew tương tác để lấy dữ lệu cập nhật vào chính nó từ Model.

High-dynamic-range (HDR) imaging presents a promising avenue for improving cloud segmentation accuracy in remote sensing applications. This paper explores the use of HDR techniques to address the challenges posed by varying illumination conditions and low contrast in cloud imagery. We propose a novel approach that integrates multiple exposures captured under different lighting conditions to generate HDR images, which are then processed using a deep learning-based segmentation model. Specifically, we employ a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture optimized for cloud detection and fine-tuned on a dataset of HDR cloud images. Experimental results demonstrate that our HDR-enhanced method significantly outperforms traditional single-exposure segmentation techniques, achieving higher precision and recall in identifying cloud boundaries, particularly in areas with shadows or bright highlights. The enhanced cloud segmentation facilitates more accurate weather forecasting, climate modeling, and satellite image analysis. Keywords: HDR imaging, cloud segmentation, remote sensing, deep learning, CNN, image processing.

This paper presents a novel deep generative model designed for fragment-based molecule generation, addressing the challenge of efficiently generating chemically valid and diverse molecular structures. Our approach utilizes a combination of graph neural networks and generative adversarial networks to learn the patterns and relationships within molecular fragments, enabling the generation of novel molecules with desired properties. The model is trained on a large dataset of molecular structures and demonstrates superior performance in generating valid and diverse molecules compared to existing methods. Key findings include the ability to generate molecules with specific functional groups and the capacity to control the generated molecules' physical and chemical properties. The proposed model has significant implications for drug discovery, materials science, and other fields where molecule generation is crucial. By leveraging the power of deep learning, our model provides a valuable tool for researchers and scientists to explore the vast chemical space efficiently. Relevant keywords: deep generative models, fragment-based molecule generation, graph neural networks, generative adversarial networks, molecular structure generation, drug discovery.

Màu xanh lá cây được dùng cho các chức năng thêm mới, màu vàng dùng cho các chức năng chỉnh sửa và màu đỏ dùng cho các chức năng xoá, báo lỗ. Gao vện có sự tương tác với người dùng. Các biểu tượng thông dụng giúp người dùng dễ dàng nhận biết các chức năng. Kh người dùng thực hiện xong các công việc sẽ có thông báo phản hồi.

Thiết kế kiến trúc đô thị sinh thái, thông minh và bền vững đang trở thành xu hướng quan trọng trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu và sự gia tăng dân số đô thị. Những yêu cầu mới trong đào tạo kiến trúc sư không chỉ tập trung vào việc tạo ra các công trình đẹp mắt mà còn phải đảm bảo tính bền vững và thân thiện với môi trường. Chương trình đào tạo cần trang bị cho sinh viên kiến thức về công nghệ xanh, quy hoạch đô thị thông minh và các giải pháp tiết kiệm năng lượng. Đồng thời, việc phát triển các kỹ năng mềm như tư duy phản biện, khả năng làm việc nhóm và giao tiếp cũng rất cần thiết để đáp ứng nhu cầu ngày càng cao của thị trường. Sự kết hợp giữa lý thuyết và thực hành trong môi trường học tập sẽ giúp sinh viên có cái nhìn toàn diện và chuẩn bị tốt hơn cho sự nghiệp trong lĩnh vực kiến trúc và quy hoạch đô thị.

Nghiên cứu mới đây đã tập trung vào việc đánh giá ảnh hưởng của cốt sợi đến độ bền của bê tông nhựa dùng cho mặt đường. Kết quả cho thấy, việc sử dụng cốt sợi trong bê tông nhựa có thể cải thiện đáng kể độ bền và độ ổn định của vật liệu này. Cốt sợi được sử dụng trong nghiên cứu này bao gồm các loại sợi khác nhau như sợi thủy tinh, sợi carbon và sợi polypropylene. Kết quả cho thấy, sợi thủy tinh và sợi carbon có thể cải thiện độ bền của bê tông nhựa lên đến 30%, trong khi sợi polypropylene có thể cải thiện độ bền lên đến 20%. Nghiên cứu cũng cho thấy, việc sử dụng cốt sợi có thể giúp giảm thiểu sự giãn nở của bê tông nhựa do thay đổi nhiệt độ, từ đó giúp tăng cường độ bền và độ ổn định của vật liệu này. Kết quả này có ý nghĩa quan trọng trong việc xây dựng và bảo trì các công trình giao thông, đặc biệt là các mặt đường cao tốc và đường bộ. Tổng kết, nghiên cứu này đã cung cấp những thông tin quan trọng về ảnh hưởng của cốt sợi đến độ bền của bê tông nhựa dùng cho mặt đường, và có thể giúp các nhà xây dựng và bảo trì công trình giao thông lựa chọn vật liệu phù hợp cho các dự án của mình.

Thông thường, mỗ khi người dùng cần mua một món đồ nộ thất, họ sẽ tham khảo hình ảnh trên mạng do nhà cung cấp điăng tả. Để cẩn thận hơn, họ sẽ xem trực tếp sản phẩm, tuy nhên sản phẩm khi điặt ở cửa hàng và khi điặt vào không gan thực tế sẽ có những cá nhìn khác nhau từ màu sắc, mức điộ tương thích với các món đồ còn lạ trong nhà. Vệc này dẫn đến sẽ mất rất nhều thờ gan, ch phí vận chuyển để điổ trả hàng.

Hệ thống quản lý gửi xe cho các toà nhà đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc tối ưu hóa không gian và nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng bãi đỗ xe, đặc biệt trong bối cảnh đô thị hóa ngày càng gia tăng. Hệ thống này được thiết kế nhằm giải quyết các vấn đề như tình trạng ùn tắc giao thông, thiếu hụt chỗ đỗ xe và quản lý thông tin người dùng một cách hiệu quả. Thông qua việc áp dụng công nghệ thông tin và các thuật toán thông minh, hệ thống cho phép người dùng dễ dàng tìm kiếm và đặt chỗ đỗ xe trực tuyến, đồng thời cung cấp thông tin về tình trạng bãi đỗ xe theo thời gian thực. Các tính năng nổi bật bao gồm quản lý lịch sử gửi xe, thông báo nhắc nhở và hỗ trợ thanh toán trực tuyến, giúp nâng cao trải nghiệm của người dùng. Hệ thống cũng tích hợp các giải pháp bảo mật để đảm bảo an toàn cho phương tiện và thông tin cá nhân của người sử dụng. Việc triển khai hệ thống này không chỉ mang lại lợi ích cho người dùng mà còn giúp các quản lý toà nhà tối ưu hóa quy trình vận hành, giảm thiểu chi phí và nâng cao hiệu quả kinh doanh. Nghiên cứu này sẽ phân tích các yếu tố cần thiết để phát triển một hệ thống quản lý gửi xe hiệu quả, đồng thời đề xuất các giải pháp công nghệ phù hợp nhằm đáp ứng nhu cầu ngày càng cao của thị trường. Kết quả nghiên cứu sẽ cung cấp cái nhìn sâu sắc về xu hướng phát triển của hệ thống quản lý gửi xe trong tương lai, góp phần vào việc xây dựng một môi trường đô thị thông minh và bền vững.

This paper proposes a novel approach to graph neural networks by introducing hypergraph convolution and hypergraph attention mechanisms. The objective is to enhance the representation learning of complex relationships in hypergraph-structured data, which is commonly found in social networks, recommendation systems, and knowledge graphs. Our method leverages hypergraph convolution to aggregate information from neighboring nodes and hypergraph attention to weigh the importance of different relationships. The results show that our approach outperforms existing graph neural network models in node classification, link prediction, and graph classification tasks. The key findings highlight the effectiveness of hypergraph convolution and attention in capturing higher-order relationships and improving model performance. This research contributes to the development of more advanced graph neural network architectures, with potential applications in network analysis, recommendation systems, and natural language processing. Key keywords: hypergraph neural networks, graph attention, hypergraph convolution, representation learning, node classification.
Những nguyên tắc này được phát hiện khi áp dụng việc xếp hạng thẩm quyền trên biểu đồ ngữ cảnh mẫu.

Quyết định lựa chọn trường đại học công lập của sinh viên ngành quản trị kinh doanh chịu ảnh hưởng bởi nhiều nhân tố quan trọng. Đầu tiên, uy tín và chất lượng đào tạo của trường là yếu tố hàng đầu, giúp sinh viên cảm thấy yên tâm về tương lai nghề nghiệp. Thứ hai, vị trí địa lý và cơ sở vật chất cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng, khi sinh viên thường ưu tiên những trường có môi trường học tập thuận lợi và tiện nghi. Bên cạnh đó, mức học phí và các chính sách hỗ trợ tài chính cũng ảnh hưởng đến quyết định của sinh viên, đặc biệt là những người có hoàn cảnh kinh tế khó khăn. Cuối cùng, sự tư vấn từ gia đình, bạn bè và các chuyên gia giáo dục cũng góp phần định hình sự lựa chọn của sinh viên, giúp họ có cái nhìn rõ hơn về các cơ hội và thách thức trong quá trình học tập và phát triển nghề nghiệp sau này.

Tinh dịch người, một chất dịch phức tạp, đóng vai trò then chốt trong sinh sản. Thành phần của nó bao gồm tinh trùng, tế bào biểu mô, bạch cầu và các thành phần dịch khác nhau như protein, lipid, carbohydrate, enzyme và ion vô cơ. Nghiên cứu sâu rộng về tinh dịch giúp chúng ta hiểu rõ hơn về chức năng sinh sản, đánh giá khả năng sinh sản của nam giới và phát triển các phương pháp điều trị vô sinh hiệu quả. Việc phân tích tinh dịch đồ, bao gồm đánh giá thể tích, mật độ, khả năng di động và hình thái tinh trùng, là một công cụ quan trọng trong chẩn đoán và điều trị các vấn đề liên quan đến sinh sản. Ngoài ra, nghiên cứu về các thành phần sinh hóa và phân tử của tinh dịch có thể cung cấp thông tin giá trị về sức khỏe tổng thể của nam giới và tiềm năng phát triển các biện pháp tránh thai mới. Sự hiểu biết toàn diện về tinh dịch người là nền tảng cho nhiều tiến bộ trong lĩnh vực y học sinh sản.

Mới đây, các nhà khoa học đã tiến hành nghiên cứu về loài mộ tử sọ Biển Pháp (Asparagus officinalis) trong san xưa Cây măng Tây Xanh. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy loài thực vật này đã được sử dụng rộng rãi trong ẩm thực và y học của người dân địa phương từ hàng nghìn năm trước. Loài mộ tử sọ Biển Pháp được biết đến với giá trị dinh dưỡng cao, chứa nhiều vitamin và khoáng chất quan trọng. Trong y học cổ truyền, loài thực vật này được sử dụng để điều trị các bệnh liên quan đến đường tiêu hóa, tim mạch và thậm chí là ung thư. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng loài mộ tử sọ Biển Pháp đã được sử dụng trong các nghi lễ và tôn giáo của người dân địa phương. Chúng được coi là biểu tượng của sự sống và sự tái sinh, và được sử dụng trong các nghi lễ để cầu mong cho mùa màng bội thu và sự thịnh vượng. Tổng kết, nghiên cứu về loài mộ tử sọ Biển Pháp trong san xưa Cây măng Tây Xanh đã cung cấp những thông tin quý giá về lịch sử và giá trị của loài thực vật này. Kết quả nghiên cứu sẽ giúp chúng ta hiểu rõ hơn về văn hóa và truyền thống của người dân địa phương, và cũng sẽ giúp chúng ta khai thác được những giá trị dinh dưỡng và y học của loài thực vật này.

This paper introduces a novel approach to creating runtime-throttleable neural networks, enabling dynamic adjustment of computational cost based on available resources or performance requirements. We propose a training methodology that embeds fine-grained control mechanisms within the network architecture, allowing for adaptive layer skipping and reduced precision computation at runtime. Our approach leverages a reinforcement learning agent to determine the optimal throttling policy, balancing accuracy and computational efficiency. Experimental results on image classification tasks demonstrate that our method achieves significant reductions in inference time and energy consumption with minimal accuracy loss compared to standard, fixed-size networks. Furthermore, we show that the trained networks can adapt to varying resource constraints without retraining, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices or in dynamic environments. This work contributes to the development of more efficient and adaptable deep learning systems, with potential applications in mobile computing, embedded systems, and edge AI. Keywords: Neural Networks, Runtime Throttling, Resource-Aware Computing, Reinforcement Learning, Adaptive Inference, Model Compression.

Với số lượng lớn video được tải lên mỗi ngày, việc các video rác, các video không phù hợp được đăng tải lên là hoàn toàn có khả năng xảy ra. Để xử lý các video này, em sẽ tạo chức năng báo cáo trên mỗi video. Khi người dùng xem video mà cảm thấy video này chứa nội dung không phù hợp thì có thể viết nội dung muốn báo cáo và gửi đến người quản lý trang web. Causal discovery aims to infer causal relationships from observational data, a challenging task particularly when dealing with non-Gaussian data distributions. This paper presents a novel approach for causal discovery in linear acyclic models (LAMs) that accommodates arbitrary distributions, moving beyond the limitations of traditional Gaussian assumptions. Our method leverages a combination of independence-based constraint satisfaction and score-based optimization techniques to identify the underlying causal structure. Specifically, we introduce a new score function, based on information-theoretic principles, that is robust to deviations from normality. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through extensive simulations on synthetic datasets with various non-Gaussian distributions and compare its performance against existing state-of-the-art causal discovery algorithms. The results show that our method achieves superior accuracy in recovering the true causal graph, especially when the data exhibits significant non-Gaussianity. This work contributes a robust and versatile tool for causal inference, applicable in diverse domains where data distributions are unknown or non-Gaussian. Keywords: Causal discovery, linear acyclic models, non-Gaussian data, causal inference, constraint-based methods, score-based methods, information theory.

This paper presents a novel approach for synthesizing highly realistic river images using Deep Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The objective is to address the challenge of generating diverse and photorealistic river scenes, which are valuable for applications in virtual environment creation, environmental simulation, and geographic data augmentation. Our methodology employs a tailored GAN architecture that incorporates advanced conditioning strategies based on river attributes such as flow pattern, surrounding vegetation, and terrain features. Extensive experiments were conducted using a curated dataset of river images from various geographical locations. The proposed model demonstrates superior image quality and diversity compared to existing baseline GANs, as evaluated by both quantitative metrics such as the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and human perceptual studies. Results indicate that our method effectively captures intricate water textures, reflections, and environmental context with high fidelity. The findings highlight the potential of deep generative models for realistic nature image synthesis and set a new benchmark for future work in landscape and river simulation. Key contributions include the introduction of attribute-based conditioning for waterbody image synthesis and an evaluation framework tailored for natural scene realism. Potential applications span virtual reality, geospatial simulation, and data augmentation for environmental research. Keywords: Generative Adversarial Networks, river image synthesis, deep learning, photorealistic images, environmental simulation, data augmentation.

Bên cạnh đó, việc kéo dài thời gian thi công còn gây ảnh hưởng đến đời sống của người dân trong khu vực dự án, làm tăng nguy cơ tai nạn lao động và ảnh hưởng đến chất lượng công trình. Hypergraph learning offers a powerful approach to model complex relationships beyond pairwise interactions captured by traditional graphs. However, effectively learning from hypergraphs remains a challenge. This paper introduces a novel hypergraph learning framework based on line expansion. We transform the original hypergraph into a line graph representation, where nodes represent hyperedges, and edges represent the intersection between hyperedges. This transformation allows us to leverage established graph neural network (GNN) techniques for hypergraph analysis. We propose a Line Expansion Graph Neural Network (LEGNN) model that operates on the line graph, learning representations that capture the hyperedge connectivity patterns of the original hypergraph. LEGNN incorporates an attention mechanism to weigh the importance of different intersecting hyperedges during message passing. Experiments on several benchmark hypergraph datasets demonstrate that LEGNN consistently outperforms existing hypergraph learning methods in node classification and hyperedge prediction tasks. The results show the effectiveness of the line expansion strategy and the benefits of leveraging GNNs for capturing high-order relationships in hypergraphs. Our approach provides a scalable and effective method for hypergraph learning, with implications for various domains including social network analysis, bioinformatics, and computer vision. Keywords: Hypergraph Learning, Line Graph, Graph Neural Networks, Node Classification, Hyperedge Prediction, Attention Mechanism.

Eddy current testing (ECT) is an effective technique in the evaluation of the depth of metal surface defects. However, in practice, the evaluation primarily relies on the experience of an operator and is often carried out by manual inspection. In this paper, we address the challenges of automatic depth evaluation of metal surface defects by virtual of state-of-the-art deep learning (DL) techniques. The main contributions are three-fold. Firstly, a highly-integrated portable ECT device is developed, which takes advantage of an advanced field programmable gate array (Zynq-7020 system on chip) and provides fast data acquisition and in-phase/quadrature demodulation. Secondly, a dataset, termed as MDDECT, is constructed using the ECT device by human operators and made openly available. It contains 48,000 scans from 18 defects of different depths and lift-offs. Thirdly, the depth evaluation problem is formulated as a time series classification problem, and various state-of-the-art 1-d residual convolutional neural networks are trained and evaluated on the MDDECT dataset. A 38-layer 1-d ResNeXt achieves an accuracy of 93.58% in discriminating the surface defects in a stainless steel sheet. The depths of the defects vary from 0.3 mm to 2.0 mm in a resolution of 0.1 mm. In addition, results show that the trained ResNeXt1D-38 model is immune to lift-off signals.
