This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing video quality to improve action recognition performance by developing an advanced video super-resolution (VSR) method tailored for this task. Traditional VSR techniques often fail to prioritize action dynamics, leading to suboptimal input for action recognition systems. Methods: We propose a novel two-stream VSR framework specifically designed for action recognition. The framework consists of a spatial stream and a temporal stream, each leveraging deep learning models to capture high-quality spatial details and motion information, respectively. The spatial stream focuses on reconstructing fine details in each frame, while the temporal stream enhances motion continuity between frames. These reconstructed outputs are then integrated to optimize the input for action recognition models. Results: Our method demonstrates superior performance in generating high-resolution videos that significantly improve action recognition accuracy. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, our approach outperforms existing VSR methods, showing a marked increase in recognition rates while maintaining low computational overhead. Quantitative metrics highlight notable enhancements in spatial resolution and motion clarity, critical for accurate action recognition. Conclusion: The proposed two-stream VSR model presents a significant advancement in the realm of video processing for action-oriented tasks. By simultaneously addressing spatial and temporal dimensions, our method contributes to more accurate and reliable action recognition. This work not only improves existing recognition systems but also opens avenues for future research in integrating VSR with other video-based analytical applications. Keywords: video super-resolution, action recognition, two-stream framework, spatial stream, temporal stream, deep learning, video quality enhancement.

The Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) offers a computationally efficient approach to atomistic simulations with near-quantum mechanical accuracy. A critical aspect of GAP is the choice of descriptors used to represent the local atomic environment. This work introduces localized Coulomb descriptors (LCDs), a novel set of rotationally invariant descriptors that build upon the established Coulomb matrix framework. Unlike global Coulomb matrices, LCDs focus on the local neighborhood of each atom, enabling more accurate and efficient representation of complex chemical environments. We demonstrate that LCDs, when incorporated into GAP models, achieve comparable or superior accuracy to existing descriptors in predicting energies and forces for a range of materials, including silicon and transition metal oxides. Furthermore, the localized nature of LCDs allows for significant computational speedups, particularly for large-scale systems, by reducing the size of the kernel matrix. This improved efficiency enables longer simulations and the study of larger systems, broadening the applicability of GAP models. Keywords: Gaussian Approximation Potential, Atomistic Simulation, Coulomb Descriptors, Machine Learning, Interatomic Potential.

This paper addresses the challenge of change captioning, where the goal is to automatically describe the differences between two images captured at different times. Traditional approaches often struggle with viewpoint variations, making accurate change detection difficult. We propose a novel method to improve change captioning through a viewpoint-adapted matching encoder. Methods/Approach: We introduce a viewpoint-adapted matching encoder that aligns features from images taken from various perspectives. The model utilizes a sophisticated mapping technique to adaptively learn and reconcile discrepancies caused by differing viewpoints. This method leverages attention mechanisms and deep learning architectures to enhance semantic understanding of changes across images. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in multiple benchmark datasets. The viewpoint-adapted matching encoder achieves an improved performance in accurately identifying and describing image differences, resulting in more precise and contextually relevant change captions. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of a viewpoint-adapted encoder in the domain of change captioning marks a substantial improvement in handling viewpoint variability, a frequently encountered challenge. Our approach enhances the robustness and accuracy of change detection systems, facilitating advancements in various applications such as surveillance, environmental monitoring, and autonomous navigation. The adaptability of our model also indicates potential for integration into broader image analysis tasks. Keywords: Change Captioning, Viewpoint Adaptation, Matching Encoder, Image Analysis, Deep Learning, Attention Mechanism.

Skeleton-based human action recognition has gained prominence due to its robustness against variations in appearance and background. However, the vulnerability of these systems to adversarial attacks remains a significant concern. This paper investigates the susceptibility of skeleton-based action recognition models to carefully crafted adversarial perturbations. We propose a novel adversarial attack method, termed "Joint-Perturbation Attack (JPA)," which strategically perturbs the 3D joint coordinates of human skeletons to mislead action classification. JPA optimizes perturbations by considering the kinematic relationships between joints, enhancing attack stealthiness and transferability. We evaluate JPA against state-of-the-art skeleton-based action recognition models on benchmark datasets, including NTU-RGB+D and Kinetics Skeleton. Experimental results demonstrate that JPA significantly degrades the performance of these models, achieving high attack success rates with minimal perturbation magnitudes. Furthermore, we analyze the transferability of adversarial examples generated by JPA across different model architectures. Our findings highlight the critical need for developing robust defense mechanisms to safeguard skeleton-based action recognition systems against adversarial threats. Keywords: Adversarial Attack, Human Action Recognition, Skeleton Data, Deep Learning, Security, Robustness.

**Abstract** This paper presents a novel approach for time series analysis using symbolic analysis-based reduced order Markov modeling. The primary objective is to address the challenges of computational complexity and data interpretation in large-scale, high-dimensional time series data. The proposed methodology first transforms raw time series into symbolic sequences, effectively capturing the essential dynamics while minimizing noise and redundancy. Subsequently, a reduced order Markov model is constructed to succinctly represent the temporal dependencies within the symbolic data. Experimental evaluations were conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets to assess the accuracy, scalability, and computational efficiency of the proposed model. Results demonstrate that our approach achieves comparable or superior predictive performance compared to traditional full-order Markov models, while significantly reducing the model size and computational requirements. Furthermore, the symbolic representation enhances interpretability, making the model particularly suitable for applications in anomaly detection, forecasting, and complex system monitoring. The research contributes an efficient and interpretable framework for time series modeling, offering scalable solutions for data mining, pattern recognition, and advanced time series analytics. Key keywords: time series analysis, symbolic analysis, Markov modeling, reduced order models, temporal patterns, anomaly detection, data mining.

The findings indicate that the model effectively learns to generalize features across different image views, leading to superior reconstruction quality. This advancement contributes to the field by reducing reliance on extensive 3D annotations and fostering more efficient development of 3D applications. Overall, this research highlights the potential of unsupervised learning in enhancing 3D reconstruction tasks by utilizing information-rich multi-view imagery, offering new avenues for exploration in areas requiring realistic and detailed 3D models. Keywords include 3D reconstruction, unsupervised learning, single-view, neural networks, and multi-view imagery.

In this paper we present a novel method for learning hierarchical representations of Markov decision processes. Our method works by partitioning the state space into subsets, and defines subtasks for performing transitions between the partitions. We formulate the problem of partitioning the state space as an optimization problem that can be solved using gradient descent given a set of sampled trajectories, making our method suitable for high-dimensional problems with large state spaces. We empirically validate the method, by showing that it can successfully learn a useful hierarchical representation in a navigation domain. Once learned, the hierarchical representation can be used to solve different tasks in the given domain, thus generalizing knowledge across tasks.

Neural network optimization is a cornerstone of modern artificial intelligence, yet it is often marked by nondeterministic behavior and instability, leading to variability in model performance across training runs. This paper investigates the sources and impacts of nondeterminism and instability in the optimization processes of deep neural networks. Employing a combination of controlled experiments, statistical analysis, and visualization techniques, we systematically examine factors such as random initialization, data shuffling, hardware-induced non-reproducibility, and the influence of optimization algorithms. Our results demonstrate that even under fixed hyperparameter settings, seemingly minor sources of randomness can result in significant fluctuations in both model accuracy and convergence trajectories. Furthermore, we analyze the sensitivity of common neural architectures, including convolutional and transformer-based models, to various sources of nondeterminism. The findings reveal that instability not only affects final model performance but can also hinder model interpretability and reproducibility, posing challenges for real-world deployment. We propose practical guidelines and mitigation strategies, such as robust initialization schemes and deterministic training pipelines, to reduce performance variability. This study highlights the critical need for greater transparency and stability in neural network training, with implications for benchmarking, deployment, and ongoing research in neural optimization. Key keywords: neural networks, optimization, nondeterminism, instability, reproducibility, deep learning, model performance.

Overall, this research contributes to the development of more efficient and effective e-commerce platforms, ultimately benefiting both suppliers and customers.

This study addresses the challenge of retinal image quality assessment by exploring the effectiveness of various deep neural networks across different color-spaces. As the quality of retinal images plays a crucial role in the accurate interpretation and diagnosis of eye-related diseases, optimizing the assessment process is vital. Methods: We conducted a comparative evaluation of multiple retinal image quality assessment networks, analyzing their performance in RGB, HSV, and YCbCr color-spaces. These networks were tested using a diverse dataset comprising variations in lighting, focus, and noise levels. The architecture of each network was adapted to accommodate the specific characteristics of the color-spaces, and performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were utilized for evaluation. Results: Our findings indicate that certain color-spaces enhance the performance of neural networks in assessing retinal image quality. Specifically, the YCbCr color-space demonstrated superior performance, increasing accuracy by up to 15% compared to traditional RGB color-space assessments. The network optimized for this color-space achieved the highest precision and recall rates, indicating its robustness against common image degradations. Conclusion: This research contributes to the field of retinal imaging by demonstrating that the choice of color-space can significantly influence the effectiveness of quality assessment networks. The insights gained from this study have implications for improving automated retinal image processing systems and facilitating better clinical outcomes. Future work will explore real-time application possibilities and further optimization of network architectures within the identified optimal color-space. Keywords: retinal image quality assessment, deep neural networks, color-spaces, RGB, HSV, YCbCr, image processing, performance metrics, medical imaging.

This paper addresses the problem of bipartite matching using a neural approach, targeting improvements in scalability and accuracy over traditional methods. Bipartite matching is a fundamental problem in combinatorial optimization with applications in various domains such as network flows, resource allocation, and scheduling. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel neural network-based framework for solving bipartite matching problems, leveraging advanced deep learning architectures to model complex dependencies and interactions within graphs. The approach employs a graph neural network (GNN) to extract relevant features from the bipartite graph and utilizes a tailored attention mechanism to efficiently compute optimal matching solutions. Results/Findings: Our experimental analysis demonstrates that the Neural Bipartite Matching model outperforms classical algorithms like the Hungarian method in terms of both execution time and solution quality, particularly in large-scale instances. The model shows significant reductions in computational complexity, making it suitable for real-time applications. Additionally, the proposed method exhibits strong generalization capabilities across diverse problem instances and demonstrates robustness under varying graph structures. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of neural paradigms into the bipartite matching problem highlights the potential of integrating machine learning techniques within traditional combinatorial optimization frameworks. Our findings suggest that the proposed model can be effectively applied to large-scale, dynamic environments where rapid and reliable decision-making is critical. This research opens avenues for further exploration into neural-based solutions for other complex optimization tasks. Keywords: Neural Bipartite Matching, Graph Neural Networks, Attention Mechanism, Combinatorial Optimization, Scalability, Deep Learning.

This paper investigates the application of modern convex optimization techniques to enhance medical image analysis. The objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image processing tasks such as segmentation, registration, and denoising. We employ advanced optimization algorithms, including proximal methods and accelerated gradient techniques, to address common challenges in medical imaging, such as noise, artifacts, and high dimensionality. Our approach formulates image analysis problems as convex optimization problems, allowing for the development of robust and scalable solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods on various medical imaging modalities, including MRI and CT scans. Experimental results show significant improvements in segmentation accuracy, registration precision, and noise reduction compared to traditional methods. Specifically, our techniques achieve a 15% improvement in segmentation accuracy on MRI images of brain tumors. The proposed framework provides a powerful tool for medical image analysis, offering the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning. Keywords: Convex Optimization, Medical Image Analysis, Segmentation, Registration, MRI, CT Scan.

Neural networks have recently become good at engaging in dialog. However, current approaches are based solely on verbal text, lacking the richness of a real face-to-face conversation. We propose a neural conversation model that aims to read and generate facial gestures alongside with text. This allows our model to adapt its response based on the "mood" of the conversation. In particular, we introduce an RNN encoder-decoder that exploits the movement of facial muscles, as well as the verbal conversation. The decoder consists of two layers, where the lower layer aims at generating the verbal response and coarse facial expressions, while the second layer fills in the subtle gestures, making the generated output more smooth and natural. We train our neural network by having it "watch" 250 movies. We showcase our joint face-text model in generating more natural conversations through automatic metrics and a human study. We demonstrate an example application with a face-to-face chatting avatar.

This paper addresses the challenge of precise detection in densely packed scenes, a problem that has significant implications for various applications in computer vision. Our objective is to develop a robust and efficient detection system capable of accurately identifying and localizing objects in cluttered environments. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach that combines a state-of-the-art convolutional neural network (CNN) with a specially designed algorithm for handling dense object packing. Our method utilizes a multi-scale feature extraction technique and a non-maximum suppression strategy to effectively detect objects with high precision. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing detection methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, particularly in scenes with high object densities. The key contributions of this research include a significant improvement in detection precision and a substantial reduction in computational complexity. Our work has important implications for applications such as autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics, where accurate object detection in densely packed scenes is crucial. Key keywords: object detection, dense scenes, convolutional neural networks, computer vision, robotics.

Video super-resolution (VSR) aims to enhance the resolution of low-quality videos, a critical task in applications such as video streaming, surveillance, and medical imaging. However, existing VSR methods often overlook the impact of compression artifacts, which degrade video quality and hinder reconstruction performance. This paper introduces **COMISR**, a novel **Compression-Informed Video Super-Resolution** framework designed to address this challenge. COMISR integrates a compression-aware module into the VSR pipeline, enabling the model to explicitly account for and mitigate compression artifacts during the reconstruction process. Leveraging a hybrid deep learning architecture, the framework combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with attention mechanisms to enhance spatial and temporal feature extraction. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that COMISR outperforms state-of-the-art VSR methods in terms of both quantitative metrics (e.g., PSNR and SSIM) and visual quality. The proposed approach achieves significant improvements in artifact reduction and detail preservation, particularly for highly compressed videos. This work highlights the importance of compression-aware modeling in VSR and provides a robust solution for real-world video enhancement tasks. Keywords: video super-resolution, compression artifacts, deep learning, attention mechanisms, video enhancement.

We introduce DatasetGAN: an automatic procedure to generate massive datasets of high-quality semantically segmented images requiring minimal human effort. Current deep networks are extremely data-hungry, benefiting from training on large-scale datasets, which are time consuming to annotate. Our method relies on the power of recent GANs to generate realistic images. We show how the GAN latent code can be decoded to produce a semantic segmentation of the image. Training the decoder only needs a few labeled examples to generalize to the rest of the latent space, resulting in an infinite annotated dataset generator! These generated datasets can then be used for training any computer vision architecture just as real datasets are. As only a few images need to be manually segmented, it becomes possible to annotate images in extreme detail and generate datasets with rich object and part segmentations. To showcase the power of our approach, we generated datasets for 7 image segmentation tasks which include pixel-level labels for 34 human face parts, and 32 car parts. Our approach outperforms all semi-supervised baselines significantly and is on par with fully supervised methods, which in some cases require as much as 100x more annotated data as our method.

Learning curves provide insight into the dependence of a learner's generalization performance on the training set size. This important tool can be used for model selection, to predict the effect of more training data, and to reduce the computational complexity of model training and hyperparameter tuning. This review recounts the origins of the term, provides a formal definition of the learning curve, and briefly covers basics such as its estimation. Our main contribution is a comprehensive overview of the literature regarding the shape of learning curves. We discuss empirical and theoretical evidence that supports well-behaved curves that often have the shape of a power law or an exponential. We consider the learning curves of Gaussian processes, the complex shapes they can display, and the factors influencing them. We draw specific attention to examples of learning curves that are ill-behaved, showing worse learning performance with more training data. To wrap up, we point out various open problems that warrant deeper empirical and theoretical investigation. All in all, our review underscores that learning curves are surprisingly diverse and no universal model can be identified.

Semantic segmentation is a critical task in computer vision, enabling precise pixel-level understanding of images. However, the robustness of semantic segmentation models under varying conditions, such as noise, occlusion, and domain shifts, remains a significant challenge. This study aims to benchmark the robustness of state-of-the-art semantic segmentation models across diverse scenarios. We evaluate popular architectures, including U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and Transformer-based models, using a comprehensive dataset that incorporates synthetic and real-world perturbations. Our approach involves systematic testing under controlled conditions, such as adversarial attacks, lighting variations, and cross-domain evaluations. Results reveal significant performance disparities among models, with Transformer-based approaches demonstrating superior robustness in handling complex distortions. Additionally, we identify key architectural features and training strategies that enhance model resilience. The findings provide actionable insights for developing more robust semantic segmentation systems, with potential applications in autonomous driving, medical imaging, and remote sensing. This work contributes a standardized benchmarking framework and highlights critical areas for future research in improving model reliability under real-world conditions. **Keywords**: semantic segmentation, robustness, benchmarking, adversarial attacks, domain adaptation, Transformer models.

This paper proposes GEE, a novel Gradient-based Explainable Variational Autoencoder designed for network anomaly detection. The objective is to develop an effective and interpretable model that identifies anomalies in network traffic while providing insights into the decision-making process. GEE employs a gradient-based approach to optimize the variational autoencoder, enabling the detection of subtle anomalies and improving the model's explainability. The method utilizes a combination of reconstruction error and gradient information to identify anomalous patterns in network data. Experimental results demonstrate that GEE outperforms state-of-the-art anomaly detection methods, achieving higher accuracy and recall rates. The key findings highlight the importance of explainability in anomaly detection, allowing for better understanding and mitigation of potential security threats. This research contributes to the development of more transparent and reliable network anomaly detection systems, with potential applications in cybersecurity and network management. Key keywords: explainable AI, variational autoencoder, network anomaly detection, gradient-based optimization, cybersecurity.

This paper explores the concept of invariant networks, examining their universality and potential applications in various domains. The objective is to investigate whether invariant networks can be applied universally across different problem settings, maintaining their performance and efficiency. We employ a novel approach, combining theoretical analysis with empirical evaluations, to assess the universality of invariant networks. Our methodology involves designing and testing invariant networks on a range of tasks, including image classification, graph processing, and natural language processing. The results show that invariant networks can achieve state-of-the-art performance on diverse tasks, demonstrating their universality and flexibility. Key findings indicate that the invariance property allows these networks to generalize well across different domains, making them a promising tool for various applications. The conclusions of this research highlight the importance of invariant networks in advancing the field of artificial intelligence, with potential implications for areas such as computer vision, machine learning, and data analysis. Keywords: invariant networks, universality, artificial intelligence, machine learning, neural networks.

Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy tiềm năng ứng dụng của học máy trong việc giám sát và đánh giá độ an toàn của các công trình thép trong điều kiện hỏa hoạn, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả công tác phòng cháy chữa cháy và giảm thiểu thiệt hại về người và tài sản. Các mô hình học máy được huấn luyện để nhận diện các mẫu gia tốc đặc trưng cho các trạng thái hư hỏng khác nhau, từ đó đưa ra cảnh báo kịp thời khi có dấu hiệu bất thường.

Nghiên cứu về hàm lượng các nguyên tố kim loại trong mô thịt của một số loài cá phổ biến tại vùng cửa sông Bạch Đằng đã được thực hiện nhằm đánh giá mức độ ô nhiễm kim loại nặng trong môi trường nước. Kết quả cho thấy, các loài cá như cá chép, cá trắm và cá mè có sự tích lũy khác nhau của các kim loại như chì, thủy ngân, cadmium và asen. Hàm lượng các nguyên tố này dao động tùy thuộc vào loài cá và vị trí thu mẫu. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng, mặc dù hàm lượng kim loại nặng trong mô thịt cá chưa vượt quá ngưỡng an toàn theo quy định, nhưng cần tiếp tục theo dõi để đảm bảo sức khỏe cộng đồng và bảo vệ môi trường sinh thái khu vực.

Artemia fran là một loại giáp xác nhỏ, được sử dụng rộng rãi trong nghiên cứu sinh học và sinh sản động vật. Hàm lượng protein trong thức ăn có ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến sự phát triển và sinh sản của Artemia fran. Nghiên cứu gần đây đã chỉ ra rằng, khi Artemia fran được cho ăn với thức ăn có hàm lượng protein cao, chúng sẽ phát triển nhanh hơn và lớn hơn so với những con được cho ăn với thức ăn có hàm lượng protein thấp. Đồng thời, thức ăn có hàm lượng protein cao cũng giúp tăng cường khả năng sinh sản của Artemia fran. Tuy nhiên, nếu hàm lượng protein trong thức ăn quá cao, có thể gây ra tác dụng phụ như tăng trưởng không đều và giảm khả năng sinh sản. Ngược lại, nếu hàm lượng protein trong thức ăn quá thấp, có thể gây ra tác dụng phụ như giảm khả năng phát triển và tăng tỷ lệ tử vong. Tóm lại, hàm lượng protein trong thức ăn có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến sự phát triển và sinh sản của Artemia fran. Việc điều chỉnh hàm lượng protein trong thức ăn có thể giúp tăng cường khả năng phát triển và sinh sản của loài này.

This paper addresses the challenge of missing data estimation in temporal multilayer position-aware graph neural networks (TMP-GNNs). The objective is to develop an effective approach for estimating missing data in dynamic graph-structured data, which is crucial for various applications such as traffic forecasting, social network analysis, and recommendation systems. We propose a novel TMP-GNN model that integrates position-aware graph attention and temporal convolutional layers to capture both spatial and temporal dependencies in the data. Our approach leverages a multi-layer architecture to learn complex patterns and relationships in the graph data. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms existing methods in estimating missing data, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and reducing errors by up to 30%. The key contributions of this research include the development of a position-aware graph attention mechanism and a temporal convolutional layer, which enable the model to effectively capture dynamic changes in the graph data. This study has important implications for various applications that involve graph-structured data with missing values, and highlights the potential of TMP-GNNs in improving the accuracy and reliability of data-driven decision-making systems. Key keywords: Graph Neural Networks, Temporal Graphs, Missing Data Estimation, Position-aware Attention, Temporal Convolutional Layers.

3D morphable models are widely used for the shape representation of an object class in computer vision and graphics applications. In this work, we focus on deep 3D morphable models that directly apply deep learning on 3D mesh data with a hierarchical structure to capture information at multiple scales. While great efforts have been made to design the convolution operator, how to best aggregate vertex features across hierarchical levels deserves further attention. In contrast to resorting to mesh decimation, we propose an attention based module to learn mapping matrices for better feature aggregation across hierarchical levels. Specifically, the mapping matrices are generated by a compatibility function of the keys and queries. The keys and queries are trainable variables, learned by optimizing the target objective, and shared by all data samples of the same object class. Our proposed module can be used as a train-only drop-in replacement for the feature aggregation in existing architectures for both downsampling and upsampling. Our experiments show that through the end-to-end training of the mapping matrices, we achieve state-of-the-art results on a variety of 3D shape datasets in comparison to existing morphable models.

Trong quá trình đốt cháy vật liệu, các sản phẩm cháy sinh ra có thể ảnh hưởng đến môi trường và sức khỏe con người. Để hiểu rõ hơn về độc tính của các sản phẩm này, các nhà khoa học đã thực hiện nghiên cứu về một số yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến độc tính của chúng. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy rằng, nhiệt độ đốt cháy, thời gian đốt cháy và loại vật liệu đốt cháy đều có ảnh hưởng đến độc tính của các sản phẩm cháy sinh ra. Khi nhiệt độ đốt cháy cao, thời gian đốt cháy dài và loại vật liệu đốt cháy chứa nhiều chất độc hại, độc tính của các sản phẩm cháy sinh ra cũng tăng lên. Ngoài ra, nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng, các sản phẩm cháy sinh ra có thể chứa nhiều chất độc hại như khí độc, bụi độc và các hợp chất hữu cơ dễ bay hơi. Những chất này có thể gây hại cho sức khỏe con người và môi trường nếu không được xử lý đúng cách. Tổng kết lại, nghiên cứu này cho thấy rằng, để giảm thiểu độc tính của các sản phẩm cháy sinh ra, cần phải kiểm soát nhiệt độ đốt cháy, thời gian đốt cháy và loại vật liệu đốt cháy. Đồng thời, cần phải xử lý đúng cách các sản phẩm cháy sinh ra để tránh gây hại cho sức khỏe con người và môi trường.

Giáo dục giá trị sống cho sinh viên sư phạm tại trường Đại học Hồng Đức hiện còn nhiều hạn chế. Chương trình đào tạo chưa chú trọng đúng mức đến việc trang bị các giá trị sống cốt lõi, phương pháp giảng dạy còn nặng về lý thuyết, ít thực hành. Đội ngũ giảng viên chưa được tập huấn đầy đủ về kỹ năng giáo dục giá trị sống. Cơ sở vật chất và nguồn học liệu còn thiếu thốn, chưa đáp ứng được yêu cầu đổi mới. Sinh viên sư phạm chưa nhận thức đầy đủ về vai trò và ý nghĩa của giáo dục giá trị sống trong sự nghiệp trồng người. Các hoạt động ngoại khóa và hoạt động xã hội chưa phát huy được hết tiềm năng trong việc bồi dưỡng giá trị sống cho sinh viên. Sự phối hợp giữa nhà trường, gia đình và xã hội trong giáo dục giá trị sống còn lỏng lẻo, thiếu đồng bộ. Điều này đặt ra yêu cầu cấp thiết về việc đổi mới toàn diện công tác giáo dục giá trị sống cho sinh viên sư phạm, nhằm nâng cao chất lượng đội ngũ giáo viên tương lai, đáp ứng yêu cầu của xã hội hiện đại.

Huyện A Lưới, Thừa Thiên Huế đang tìm kiếm giải pháp phát triển mô hình sản xuất rau an toàn nhằm nâng cao thu nhập cho người dân và bảo vệ môi trường. Huyện tập trung vào việc xây dựng các vùng sản xuất rau tập trung, áp dụng quy trình sản xuất theo tiêu chuẩn VietGAP, đồng thời tăng cường liên kết giữa người sản xuất và doanh nghiệp tiêu thụ. Các giải pháp cụ thể bao gồm: hỗ trợ kỹ thuật, giống vốn cho nông dân; xây dựng hệ thống tưới tiêu hợp lý; kiểm soát chặt chẽ việc sử dụng phân bón, thuốc bảo vệ thực vật; và quảng bá sản phẩm rau an toàn A Lưới đến thị trường trong và ngoài tỉnh. Huyện cũng chú trọng đào tạo nguồn nhân lực có kỹ năng sản xuất rau an toàn, đồng thời khuyến khích các doanh nghiệp đầu tư vào lĩnh vực này. Mục tiêu là xây dựng A Lưới trở thành vùng sản xuất rau an toàn chất lượng cao, góp phần phát triển kinh tế - xã hội của địa phương.

Phát triển nhà ở xã hội tại Hà Nội theo hướng bền vững đang là một trong những vấn đề cấp thiết được quan tâm hàng đầu. Với tốc độ đô thị hóa nhanh chóng, nhu cầu về nhà ở giá rẻ cho người thu nhập thấp ngày càng tăng cao. Tuy nhiên, việc xây dựng nhà ở xã hội hiện nay vẫn còn nhiều hạn chế, từ quy hoạch chưa đồng bộ đến chất lượng công trình chưa đảm bảo. Để hướng tới sự phát triển bền vững, cần có những giải pháp toàn diện như tăng cường đầu tư từ ngân sách nhà nước, thu hút nguồn vốn xã hội, áp dụng công nghệ xây dựng tiên tiến và quản lý chặt chẽ quy trình thi công. Bên cạnh đó, việc quy hoạch không gian sống kết hợp với hệ thống hạ tầng đồng bộ, tiện ích công cộng cũng là yếu tố quan trọng để đảm bảo chất lượng cuộc sống cho cư dân. Định hướng phát triển nhà ở xã hội bền vững không chỉ giải quyết vấn đề nhà ở mà còn góp phần thúc đẩy sự phát triển kinh tế - xã hội của thủ đô.

Việc phát hiện người và hành động lấy đồ trong cửa hàng tiện lợi là một vấn đề quan trọng trong lĩnh vực an ninh và quản lý cửa hàng. Các hệ thống giám sát truyền thống thường dựa vào camera và nhân viên bảo vệ, nhưng phương pháp này có nhiều hạn chế như thiếu chính xác và tốn kém nhân lực. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, các ứng dụng dựa trên trí tuệ nhân tạo và học máy đã được phát triển nhằm tự động hóa quá trình phát hiện và cảnh báo. Các hệ thống này sử dụng các mô hình học sâu như YOLO (You Only Look Once) và các mạng nơ-ron tích chập (CNN) để nhận diện người và hành động một cách chính xác. Quá trình xử lý hình ảnh từ camera giúp phân tích các đối tượng trong khung hình, xác định vị trí và theo dõi chuyển động của họ. Khi phát hiện hành động lấy đồ, hệ thống sẽ tự động gửi cảnh báo đến nhân viên bảo vệ hoặc quản lý cửa hàng. Ngoài ra, các thuật toán tiên tiến còn có khả năng phân biệt giữa hành động mua hàng hợp lệ và hành vi trộm cắp, giảm thiểu sai sót và nâng cao hiệu quả giám sát. Việc tích hợp các công nghệ này không chỉ giúp tăng cường an ninh mà còn cải thiện trải nghiệm mua sắm của khách hàng. Tuy nhiên, vẫn còn những thách thức như xử lý dữ liệu lớn, đảm bảo quyền riêng tư và tối ưu hóa hiệu suất hệ thống trong điều kiện thực tế. Nghiên cứu và phát triển các giải pháp công nghệ tiên tiến sẽ tiếp tục đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc nâng cao hiệu quả quản lý và an ninh tại các cửa hàng tiện lợi.

This work addresses the problem of semantic foggy scene understanding (SFSU). Although extensive research has been performed on image dehazing and on semantic scene understanding with clear-weather images, little attention has been paid to SFSU. Due to the difficulty of collecting and annotating foggy images, we choose to generate synthetic fog on real images that depict clear-weather outdoor scenes, and then leverage these partially synthetic data for SFSU by employing state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNN). In particular, a complete pipeline to add synthetic fog to real, clear-weather images using incomplete depth information is developed. We apply our fog synthesis on the Cityscapes dataset and generate Foggy Cityscapes with 20550 images. SFSU is tackled in two ways: 1) with typical supervised learning, and 2) with a novel type of semi-supervised learning, which combines 1) with an unsupervised supervision transfer from clear-weather images to their synthetic foggy counterparts. In addition, we carefully study the usefulness of image dehazing for SFSU. For evaluation, we present Foggy Driving, a dataset with 101 real-world images depicting foggy driving scenes, which come with ground truth annotations for semantic segmentation and object detection. Extensive experiments show that 1) supervised learning with our synthetic data significantly improves the performance of state-of-the-art CNN for SFSU on Foggy Driving; 2) our semi-supervised learning strategy further improves performance; and 3) image dehazing marginally advances SFSU with our learning strategy. The datasets, models and code are made publicly available.

Mục tiêu: Nhận xét một số đặc điểm lâm sàng và các biến đổi sớm trên bản ghi chẩn đoán điện ở bệnh nhân mắc hội chứng Guillain – Barré (GBS). Đối tượng và phương pháp nghiên cứu: 40 bệnh nhân được chẩn đoán xác định GBS khởi phát bệnh trong 7 ngày đầu. Lựa chọn vào nghiên cứu những bệnh nhân điều trị nội trú tại Khoa Thần kinh Bệnh viện Bạch Mai có chẩn đoán khi ra viện là GBS và được làm chẩn đoán điện cơ trong tuần đầu tiên của bệnh. Kết quả: Một số triệu chứng lâm sàng thường gặp: Rối loạn cảm giác chủ quan (77,5%) (p<0,05), liệt vận động đối xứng cả hai bên (75%); giảm và mất phản xạ gân xương 77,5%, kèm liệt các dây thần kinh sọ não 32,5%. Dịch não tủy phân ly protein- tế bào. Phản xạ H bất thường xuất hiện ở 37/40 bệnh nhân (92,5%), trong đó có 31 bệnh nhân (77,5%) mất phản xạ H. Sóng F bất thường được ghi nhận ở 29/40 bệnh nhân (72,5%). Về đặc điểm dẫn truyền thần kinh vận động: có 13 bệnh nhân (32,5%) kéo dài thời gian tiềm vận động ngoại vi ở trên 2 dây thần kinh, 7 bệnh nhân (17,5%) giảm tốc độ dẫn truyền thần kinh vận động dưới 70% so với giá trị bình thường ở trên 2 dây thần kinh. 11 bệnh nhân (27,5%) có bản ghi điện cơ bình thường, chỉ có duy nhất bất thường phản xạ H được phát hiện. Kết luận: Triệu chứng lâm sàng thường gặp của GBS là biểu hiện liệt mềm ngoại biên đối xứng hai bên, với liệt các dây thần kinh sọ não và phân ly protein- tế bào xảy ra cấp tính. Bất thường phản xạ H và sóng F là 2 dấu hiệu chẩn đoán nhạy nhất trên bản ghi điện - thần kinh đối với bệnh nhân mắc hội chứng Guillain - Barré trong giai đoạn sớm.

Quá trình cắt đất đá của choòng khoan lắp trên máy khoan xoay là một chủ đề quan trọng trong lĩnh vực khoan khai thác. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc phân tích cơ chế hoạt động của choòng khoan khi tiếp xúc với các lớp đất đá khác nhau, từ đó đánh giá hiệu quả cắt và độ bền của thiết bị. Các yếu tố như tốc độ quay, lực ép, và hình dạng răng cắt được xem xét kỹ lưỡng để tối ưu hóa quá trình khoan. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy, việc điều chỉnh các thông số kỹ thuật phù hợp không chỉ nâng cao hiệu suất khoan mà còn giảm thiểu hao mòn, kéo dài tuổi thọ của choòng khoan. Những phát hiện này có ý nghĩa lớn trong việc cải tiến công nghệ khoan, đặc biệt trong các dự án khai thác tài nguyên dưới lòng đất.

Hiệp hội Nghiên cứu bệnh gan Châu Á Thái Bình Dương đã đưa ra các hướng dẫn chi tiết về chẩn đoán và điều trị bệnh gan, tập trung vào các phương pháp hiện đại và hiệu quả. Các khuyến cáo bao gồm việc sử dụng các công cụ chẩn đoán tiên tiến như xét nghiệm máu, siêu âm và sinh thiết gan để xác định chính xác tình trạng bệnh. Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms often face challenges in balancing exploration and exploitation, particularly in environments with large state-action spaces. This paper addresses the problem of achieving optimal regret bounds in RL by focusing on posterior sampling, a Bayesian approach that leverages uncertainty to guide decision-making. We propose a novel posterior sampling-based RL algorithm and analyze its worst-case regret bounds in episodic Markov decision processes (MDPs). Our approach integrates posterior updates with efficient exploration strategies, ensuring robust performance across diverse environments. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed algorithm achieves a worst-case regret bound of \( O(\sqrt{HSAT}) \), where \( H \) is the horizon length, \( S \) is the number of states, \( A \) is the number of actions, and \( T \) is the total number of time steps. This result matches the lower bound for RL in MDPs, indicating the algorithm's near-optimality. Empirical evaluations on benchmark environments further validate the algorithm's effectiveness, showcasing its ability to outperform existing methods in terms of cumulative regret and sample efficiency. The findings highlight the potential of posterior sampling as a scalable and theoretically grounded solution for RL, with implications for applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and decision-making under uncertainty. **Keywords**: Reinforcement learning, posterior sampling, regret bounds, Markov decision processes, exploration-exploitation tradeoff.

Radio traffic sequence recognition is a critical component in wireless communication systems, aiming to accurately decode transmitted sequences under varying conditions. This research investigates the application of deep recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to enhance the performance and accuracy of radio traffic sequence recognition. Methods/Approach: We propose an end-to-end model utilizing deep recurrent neural networks, specifically leveraging long short-term memory (LSTM) units, to effectively capture temporal dependencies and manage sequential data in radio traffic. The model is trained on a diverse dataset of radio signals, employing supervised learning techniques to optimize weights and improve recognition rates. Additionally, the architecture is designed to minimize computational overhead while maximizing accuracy. Results/Findings: The RNN-based approach demonstrated significant improvements in sequence recognition accuracy compared to traditional methods, especially under noisy environmental conditions and with variable signal strengths. The model achieved an accuracy rate of 95% across challenging test scenarios, highlighting its robustness and adaptability. Comparative analysis with baseline machine learning methods underscored the superior performance of the proposed approach in terms of both speed and precision. Conclusion/Implications: This study presents a novel application of deep recurrent neural networks for radio traffic sequence recognition, showcasing their potential for deployment in real-world wireless communication systems. The insights from this research contribute to the advancement of intelligent communication frameworks, offering enhanced reliability and efficiency. Future work might explore further optimization techniques and the integration of real-time adaptive mechanisms to handle dynamic radio environments. Keywords: Radio Traffic Recognition, Deep Recurrent Neural Networks, LSTM, Wireless Communication, Sequence Recognition, AI Models.

In the continual learning setting, tasks are encountered sequentially. The goal is to learn whilst i) avoiding catastrophic forgetting, ii) efficiently using model capacity, and iii) employing forward and backward transfer learning. In this paper, we explore how the Variational Continual Learning (VCL) framework achieves these desiderata on two benchmarks in continual learning: split MNIST and permuted MNIST. We first report significantly improved results on what was already a competitive approach. The improvements are achieved by establishing a new best practice approach to mean-field variational Bayesian neural networks. We then look at the solutions in detail. This allows us to obtain an understanding of why VCL performs as it does, and we compare the solution to what an `ideal' continual learning solution might be.

Axit salicylic là một chất hóa học được sử dụng rộng rãi trong nhiều lĩnh vực, bao gồm cả nông nghiệp. Trong nghiên cứu gần đây, axit salicylic đã được chứng minh có ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến sinh trưởng của cây con dưa chuột. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy axit salicylic có thể ức chế sự phát triển của rễ và lá cây con dưa chuột, đồng thời giảm khả năng sinh sản của chúng. Điều này có thể được giải thích bởi tác dụng ức chế của axit salicylic đối với quá trình tổng hợp hormone auxin, một hormone quan trọng trong quá trình sinh trưởng của cây. Tuy nhiên, nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng axit salicylic có thể có tác dụng tích cực đối với cây con dưa chuột trong một số điều kiện hạn hán. Khi cây con dưa chuột bị hạn hán, axit salicylic có thể giúp chúng tăng cường khả năng chống chịu và sinh trưởng. Tổng kết, axit salicylic có thể có ảnh hưởng khác nhau đến sinh trưởng của cây con dưa chuột tùy thuộc vào điều kiện môi trường. Trong điều kiện bình thường, axit salicylic có thể ức chế sự phát triển của cây con dưa chuột, nhưng trong điều kiện hạn hán, nó có thể giúp chúng tăng cường khả năng chống chịu và sinh trưởng.

Generalized Zero-Shot Learning (GZSL) aims to recognize objects from both seen and unseen classes by leveraging semantic information, such as attributes or textual descriptions. However, a significant challenge in GZSL is the visual bias problem, where models tend to overfit to seen classes, leading to poor performance on unseen classes. This paper proposes a novel domain-aware visual bias eliminating framework to address this issue. Our approach introduces a domain-aware feature alignment mechanism that explicitly reduces the bias between seen and unseen classes by aligning their feature distributions in a shared latent space. Additionally, we employ a dual-branch architecture to decouple the learning of class-specific and domain-specific features, ensuring robust generalization across domains. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including AWA2, CUB, and SUN, demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly improving the harmonic mean accuracy of seen and unseen classes. The proposed framework not only mitigates visual bias but also provides a scalable solution for real-world applications where unseen classes are prevalent. Key contributions include the domain-aware alignment strategy and the dual-branch architecture, which collectively enhance the generalization capability of GZSL models. **Keywords**: Generalized Zero-Shot Learning, Visual Bias, Domain Adaptation, Feature Alignment, Dual-Branch Architecture, Semantic Embedding.

This paper introduces Bayesian Attention Belief Networks (BABNs), a novel probabilistic deep learning architecture that integrates attention mechanisms within a Bayesian belief network framework. BABNs address the limitations of traditional deep learning models in handling uncertainty and interpretability by propagating probabilistic beliefs through attention-weighted feature representations. The proposed architecture leverages variational inference to approximate the posterior distribution over network parameters and attention weights, enabling robust learning and uncertainty quantification. We evaluate BABNs on several benchmark datasets for classification and regression tasks, demonstrating improved predictive accuracy and calibration compared to standard attention-based neural networks and Bayesian neural networks. Furthermore, the learned attention weights provide insights into the model's decision-making process, enhancing interpretability. Results indicate that BABNs offer a powerful and interpretable approach to probabilistic deep learning, paving the way for applications in safety-critical domains requiring reliable uncertainty estimation. Keywords: Bayesian Belief Networks, Attention Mechanisms, Probabilistic Deep Learning, Variational Inference, Uncertainty Quantification, Interpretability.

This study addresses the critical challenge of improving accuracy and efficiency in melanoma screening through the deployment of deep learning techniques. With increasing rates of skin cancer worldwide, the demand for reliable and scalable diagnostic tools is paramount. The research focuses on leveraging knowledge transfer methodologies to enhance the capabilities of deep learning models in identifying melanoma. Methods/Approach: We utilized a transfer learning approach, employing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) pre-trained on large, diverse datasets, to adapt the model for the specific task of melanoma detection. Fine-tuning was conducted using a dataset comprised of annotated dermoscopic images, ensuring the model's robustness and generalizability. Key preprocessing steps included data augmentation and normalization to bolster the model's performance under varying conditions. Results/Findings: The adapted deep learning model achieved significant improvements in classification accuracy, outperforming existing standalone models and demonstrating the effectiveness of knowledge transfer. Comparative analysis showed a marked increase in sensitivity and specificity, with our approach reducing false negatives in melanoma screening. The model also maintained high performance across varied image qualities and skin tones, showcasing its versatility and potential for broader clinical applications. Conclusion/Implications: The research underscores the value of transfer learning in advancing medical image analysis, specifically for melanoma screening. By effectively transferring knowledge from large-scale visual datasets, the study introduces a powerful tool for early detection, promising to enhance diagnostic practices and potentially reduce melanoma-related mortality. These findings advocate for the integration of deep learning models in clinical settings, facilitating better patient outcomes through timely and precise screening processes. Keywords: melanoma screening, deep learning, transfer learning, convolutional neural networks, medical image analysis, skin cancer detection.

The rapid advancement in image generation technologies has opened new avenues for translating structured data into visual content. This paper addresses the challenge of generating high-quality images from scene graphs, which are structural representations that encapsulate objects and their relationships within a scene. Our objective is to develop a method for learning canonical representations that bridge the gap between abstract scene graph descriptions and detailed image outputs. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel framework that leverages a combination of deep learning techniques and canonical representation learning to facilitate the translation from scene graphs to images. The model utilizes an encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder processes scene graph inputs to generate a canonical latent space representation, and the decoder subsequently interprets this representation to synthesize realistic images. Key components of our approach include the use of graph convolutional networks to capture relational data and the implementation of adversarial frameworks to enhance image realism. Results/Findings: Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms existing methods in both objective metrics and human evaluations. The generated images exhibit finer detail and adherence to the semantic content outlined by the scene graphs. Our approach shows improved results in terms of accuracy in object placement and relationship realization, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. Conclusion/Implications: This research introduces a powerful method for scene graph-to-image generation that advances the field toward more precise and visually faithful outputs. The contributions of our work lie in its ability to generate detailed and contextually relevant images from high-level structural descriptors. Potential applications of this research include automated content creation in entertainment, enhanced scene visualization tools, and aiding tasks in autonomous systems where contextual understanding from structured data is essential. Keywords: Scene Graph, Image Generation, Canonical Representation, Graph Convolutional Networks, Encoder-Decoder Architecture, Adversarial Frameworks.

Mô hình tích hợp SCOR và DEMATEL đánh giá rủi ro trong chuỗi cung ứng lạnh nông sản là một phương pháp mới và hiệu quả để quản lý rủi ro trong lĩnh vực nông sản. Mô hình này kết hợp hai phương pháp đánh giá rủi ro khác nhau: SCOR (Supply Chain Operations Reference) và DEMATEL (Decision Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory). SCOR là một mô hình đánh giá rủi ro dựa trên chuỗi cung ứng, giúp xác định và đánh giá các rủi ro tiềm ẩn trong chuỗi cung ứng. Trong khi đó, DEMATEL là một phương pháp đánh giá rủi ro dựa trên mạng lưới, giúp xác định và đánh giá các mối quan hệ giữa các yếu tố rủi ro. Bằng cách tích hợp hai phương pháp này, mô hình SCOR và DEMATEL có thể đánh giá rủi ro trong chuỗi cung ứng lạnh nông sản một cách toàn diện và chính xác. Mô hình này giúp xác định các rủi ro tiềm ẩn, đánh giá mức độ nghiêm trọng của các rủi ro, và đề xuất các giải pháp để giảm thiểu rủi ro. Mô hình này có thể được áp dụng trong các lĩnh vực như sản xuất, phân phối, và lưu trữ nông sản. This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning hyper-heuristic (RLHH) for multi-objective single-point search, designed to enhance structural fault identification. The objective is to develop an adaptive search strategy capable of efficiently navigating the complex, multi-dimensional search space inherent in structural fault diagnosis. The proposed RLHH employs a Q-learning algorithm to learn an effective policy for selecting low-level search heuristics, dynamically adapting to the characteristics of the problem instance. The system’s performance is evaluated on benchmark structural fault identification problems, demonstrating a significant improvement in solution quality and convergence speed compared to traditional single-point search methods and fixed heuristic selection strategies. The results show that the RLHH can effectively balance exploration and exploitation, identifying optimal or near-optimal solutions with fewer iterations. This research contributes a practical and adaptable approach to multi-objective optimization in structural health monitoring, offering potential for real-time fault detection and mitigation. Key words: Reinforcement Learning, Hyper-Heuristic, Multi-Objective Optimization, Single Point Search, Structural Fault Identification, Q-learning.

We employ a novel framework that integrates multitask learning with transfer learning, enabling the reuse of knowledge across different applications and hardware architectures. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in autotuning efficiency and application performance, outperforming traditional methods. Our research contributes to the development of scalable, adaptive, and efficient exascale computing systems, with potential applications in fields such as climate modeling, materials science, and genomics. Key findings highlight the benefits of multitask and transfer learning in autotuning, including reduced tuning time, improved performance portability, and enhanced scalability. This work advances the state-of-the-art in exascale computing, enabling faster and more efficient execution of complex applications on next-generation hardware architectures, and paving the way for widespread adoption of AI-driven autotuning techniques in high-performance computing.

Declarative process modeling has gained significant attention for its ability to capture flexible and constraint-based business processes. However, existing methods for discovering declarative models from event logs often struggle with balancing accuracy and computational efficiency. This paper introduces *DisCoveR*, a novel framework designed to address these challenges by leveraging advanced algorithms and optimization techniques. The proposed approach combines constraint mining with efficient pruning strategies to reduce computational overhead while maintaining high model precision. We evaluate *DisCoveR* on real-world and synthetic datasets, demonstrating its superior performance in terms of both accuracy and runtime compared to state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results show that *DisCoveR* achieves up to 20% improvement in precision and recall while reducing discovery time by 35%. The framework’s scalability and robustness make it a practical solution for large-scale process mining tasks. This research contributes to the field by providing a more efficient and accurate tool for declarative process model discovery, with potential applications in business process management, compliance checking, and process optimization. **Keywords**: Declarative process models, process mining, event logs, constraint discovery, optimization, business process management.

Time series data is ubiquitous in various domains, such as healthcare, finance, and IoT, but extracting meaningful representations from it remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel self-supervised learning framework for time series representation learning, leveraging inter-intra relational reasoning to capture both temporal dependencies and contextual relationships within the data. The proposed approach employs a dual-branch architecture that simultaneously models intra-series dynamics (within a single time series) and inter-series relationships (across multiple time series). By designing a pretext task that encourages the model to reason about these relationships, the framework learns robust and generalizable representations without requiring labeled data. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance in downstream tasks such as classification, clustering, and anomaly detection. The results highlight the model's ability to capture complex temporal patterns and its potential for real-world applications where labeled data is scarce. This work contributes to advancing self-supervised learning in time series analysis by introducing a relational reasoning mechanism that enhances representation quality and interpretability. **Keywords**: self-supervised learning, time series analysis, relational reasoning, representation learning, temporal dependencies, anomaly detection.

Graph-structured data plays a pivotal role in various applications, from social network analysis to recommendation systems. However, the vulnerability of graph-based models to adversarial attacks remains a critical concern. This paper investigates the robustness of graph neural networks (GNNs) against adversarial perturbations, focusing on how structured data can be manipulated to degrade model performance. We propose a novel adversarial attack framework that leverages gradient-based optimization to identify and perturb critical edges and nodes in the graph structure. Our approach is designed to minimize detectability while maximizing the impact on model predictions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that even minor perturbations can significantly reduce the accuracy of state-of-the-art GNNs, highlighting their susceptibility to adversarial attacks. Furthermore, we analyze the transferability of these attacks across different GNN architectures, revealing insights into their generalizability. This study underscores the need for robust defenses in graph-based learning systems and provides a foundation for future research in adversarial robustness for structured data. Key contributions include a scalable attack methodology, empirical validation of GNN vulnerabilities, and a discussion on potential mitigation strategies. **Keywords**: Graph Neural Networks, Adversarial Attacks, Robustness, Graph-structured Data, Perturbation, Transferability.

Vision Transformers (ViTs) have emerged as a powerful alternative to convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image recognition tasks. However, their computational complexity and memory requirements remain significant challenges, particularly for high-resolution images. This paper introduces **PSViT**, a novel Vision Transformer architecture that addresses these limitations through two key innovations: **Token Pooling** and **Attention Sharing**. Token Pooling reduces redundancy in the token sequence by dynamically aggregating less informative tokens, significantly lowering computational overhead without sacrificing accuracy. Attention Sharing optimizes the self-attention mechanism by enabling multiple layers to reuse attention maps, further enhancing efficiency. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including ImageNet and CIFAR-10, demonstrate that PSViT achieves state-of-the-art performance with up to 30% fewer parameters and 40% lower computational cost compared to existing ViT models. These improvements make PSViT a scalable and efficient solution for real-world applications, particularly in resource-constrained environments. The proposed architecture not only advances the field of vision transformers but also provides a foundation for future research in efficient deep learning models. **Keywords**: Vision Transformer, Token Pooling, Attention Sharing, Efficient Deep Learning, Image Recognition, Computational Efficiency.

This study addresses the challenge of improving gesture recognition by exploring the integration of multi-rate and multi-modal temporal information into neural network architectures. The primary objective is to enhance the accuracy and robustness of gesture classification systems, which are pivotal in various applications, including human-computer interaction and virtual reality. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel architecture, the Temporal Enhanced Network (TEN), which leverages differential temporal rates and multiple modalities for comprehensive feature extraction. The architecture incorporates sophisticated search algorithms to dynamically determine optimal configurations for temporal data integration. Multi-rate analysis is coupled with modalities such as RGB, depth, and infrared data to allow a fusion that captures intricate temporal patterns. Results/Findings: The implementation of our proposed network results in superior performance on standard gesture recognition benchmarks, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy compared to existing models. Comparative experiments illustrate the advantage of our approach over single-rate and single-modal networks, showing enhanced robustness in diverse lighting and background conditions. The search mechanism efficiently identifies the ideal network configurations that are adaptive to various contexts and user-specific gesture patterns. Conclusion/Implications: Our research significantly contributes to the field of gesture recognition by introducing a flexible and adaptive network architecture capable of capturing complex temporal dynamics across multiple modalities. This innovation holds potential for widespread applications, particularly in improving interactive systems where accurate gesture recognition is paramount. The methodology outlined in this study opens avenues for further research on adaptive networks in dynamic and real-time applications. Keywords: Gesture Recognition, Temporal Networks, Multi-Rate, Multi-Modal, Neural Architecture Search, Human-Computer Interaction.

Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has shown remarkable success in solving complex decision-making tasks, but its computational demands and slow convergence remain significant challenges. This paper addresses these limitations by proposing accelerated methods to enhance the efficiency and scalability of DRL algorithms. We introduce a novel framework that combines parallelized experience replay, adaptive learning rate scheduling, and gradient compression techniques to reduce training time and resource consumption. Our approach is evaluated on benchmark environments, including Atari games and robotic control tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in convergence speed and computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. Results show a 40% reduction in training time while maintaining or exceeding baseline performance metrics. The proposed methods not only advance the practical applicability of DRL in real-world scenarios but also provide a foundation for future research in optimizing large-scale reinforcement learning systems. This work contributes to the growing body of research aimed at making DRL more accessible and efficient for applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and beyond. **Keywords**: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Accelerated Training, Parallelized Experience Replay, Adaptive Learning Rates, Gradient Compression.

This letter presents a novel framework termed DistSTN for the task of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR). In contrast to the conventional SAR ATR algorithms, DistSTN considers a more challenging practical scenario for non-cooperative targets whose aspect angles for training are incomplete and limited in a partial range while those of testing samples are unlimited. To address this issue, instead of learning the pose invariant features, DistSTN newly involves an elaborated feature disentangling model to separate the learned pose factors of a SAR target from the identity ones so that they can independently control the representation process of the target image. To disentangle the explainable pose factors, we develop a pose discrepancy spatial transformer module in DistSTN to characterize the intrinsic transformation between the factors of two different targets with an explicit geometric model. Furthermore, DistSTN develops an amortized inference scheme that enables efficient feature extraction and recognition using an encoder-decoder mechanism. Experimental results with the moving and stationary target acquisition and recognition (MSTAR) benchmark demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach. Compared with the other ATR algorithms, DistSTN can achieve higher recognition accuracy.

This paper explores the application of self-play reinforcement learning (RL) to a four-player game of imperfect information, addressing the challenges of multi-agent decision-making under uncertainty. Toxicity prediction of chemical compounds is a grand challenge. Lately, it achieved significant progress in accuracy but using a huge set of features, implementing a complex blackbox technique such as a deep neural network, and exploiting enormous computational resources. In this paper, we strongly argue for the models and methods that are simple in machine learning characteristics, efficient in computing resource usage, and powerful to achieve very high accuracy levels. To demonstrate this, we develop a single task-based chemical toxicity prediction framework using only 2D features that are less compute intensive. We effectively use a decision tree to obtain an optimum number of features from a collection of thousands of them. We use a shallow neural network and jointly optimize it with decision tree taking both network parameters and input features into account. Our model needs only a minute on a single CPU for its training while existing methods using deep neural networks need about 10 min on NVidia Tesla K40 GPU. However, we obtain similar or better performance on several toxicity benchmark tasks. We also develop a cumulative feature ranking method which enables us to identify features that can help chemists perform prescreening of toxic compounds effectively.

Emotional body gesture recognition is a critical area of research in human-computer interaction, with applications ranging from virtual reality to healthcare. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of existing methods and technologies for recognizing emotional states through body gestures. The objective is to identify key challenges, evaluate current approaches, and highlight emerging trends in this domain. We systematically review techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision, focusing on their effectiveness in capturing and interpreting non-verbal emotional cues. The survey also examines datasets, feature extraction methods, and evaluation metrics commonly used in the field. Our findings reveal that while significant progress has been made, challenges such as variability in gesture expression, cultural differences, and real-time processing remain unresolved. The paper concludes by discussing the implications of these findings for future research, emphasizing the potential of multimodal approaches and advanced AI models to enhance recognition accuracy and robustness. This survey aims to provide a foundational resource for researchers and practitioners, fostering innovation in emotional body gesture recognition technologies. **Keywords**: Emotional body gestures, gesture recognition, human-computer interaction, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, multimodal systems.

Explainable Machine Learning (XAI) is crucial for building trust and understanding in AI systems, but often incurs significant computational overhead. This paper explores the hardware acceleration of XAI methods using Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). We focus on accelerating SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and Integrated Gradients, two widely used XAI techniques. Our approach leverages the TPU's matrix multiplication capabilities to optimize the computationally intensive operations involved in these methods. We implemented and evaluated our accelerated XAI methods on Google Cloud TPUs, demonstrating significant performance improvements compared to CPU and GPU implementations. Results show a speedup of up to 10x for SHAP and 8x for Integrated Gradients. This acceleration enables faster and more scalable XAI, facilitating the adoption of transparent AI in resource-constrained environments. Our work demonstrates the feasibility and benefits of using TPUs to accelerate XAI, contributing to the development of more efficient and understandable AI systems. Keywords: Explainable AI, XAI, Tensor Processing Unit, TPU, Hardware Acceleration, SHAP, Integrated Gradients, Machine Learning.

This paper presents an empirical study addressing the role and effectiveness of spatial attention mechanisms in deep neural networks for computer vision tasks. The objective is to systematically assess how integrating spatial attention modules influences feature representation, learning dynamics, and overall model performance across diverse image classification and object detection benchmarks. We implement and evaluate several popular spatial attention methods, incorporating them into standard convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures. Our experimental approach includes both qualitative and quantitative analyses, comparing networks with and without attention modules under controlled settings. Results demonstrate that spatial attention consistently enhances model accuracy, convergence speed, and robustness to noise, especially in complex or cluttered scenes. Furthermore, we investigate the interpretability benefits offered by attention maps, providing insights into regions prioritized by the model during decision-making. Conclusively, our findings underscore the value of spatial attention as an efficient and generalizable augmentation to deep networks. The study’s outcomes inform practical guidelines for deploying spatial attention in real-world applications, including image recognition, scene understanding, and autonomous systems. Keywords: spatial attention, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, feature representation, interpretability, computer vision.

Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) has emerged as a promising framework for collaborative machine learning while preserving data privacy across organizations that possess different features of the same user set. However, ensuring model fairness—preventing biased outcomes across sensitive user groups—remains a significant and largely unaddressed challenge in VFL due to the fragmentation of features and the heterogeneity of participants. This paper presents a novel approach for achieving model fairness in VFL by introducing a fairness-aware optimization mechanism that enables participating parties to jointly minimize prediction bias without compromising data confidentiality. We design an adaptive algorithm that incorporates fairness constraints during federated aggregation, allowing local models to adjust their learning process in response to detected disparities among demographic groups. Experimental evaluations on real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate that our method effectively reduces group-based prediction disparities while maintaining competitive model accuracy, outperforming existing VFL baselines in both fairness and performance metrics. The proposed solution enables practical and ethical deployment of VFL in applications such as finance, healthcare, and social platforms, where equitable decision-making is critical. Our work highlights the importance of integrating fairness assurance into federated frameworks and paves the way for developing more responsible collaborative AI systems. Keywords: vertical federated learning, model fairness, bias mitigation, privacy-preserving machine learning, fairness-aware optimization.

We investigate the relationship between the structure of a discrete graphical model and the support of the inverse of a generalized covariance matrix. We show that for certain graph structures, the support of the inverse covariance matrix of indicator variables on the vertices of a graph reflects the conditional independence structure of the graph. Our work extends results that have previously been established only in the context of multivariate Gaussian graphical models, thereby addressing an open question about the significance of the inverse covariance matrix of a non-Gaussian distribution. The proof exploits a combination of ideas from the geometry of exponential families, junction tree theory and convex analysis. These population-level results have various consequences for graph selection methods, both known and novel, including a novel method for structure estimation for missing or corrupted observations. We provide nonasymptotic guarantees for such methods and illustrate the sharpness of these predictions via simulations.

This research addresses the challenge of optimizing base distributions within implicit generative models, a key component in enhancing the capabilities of generative frameworks such as GANs and VAEs. Our work aims to improve the quality and diversity of generated samples by focusing on learning more effective base distributions. Methods/Approach: We introduce a novel approach for learning the base distribution using an adaptive algorithm designed to adjust parameters dynamically. This method utilizes a combination of information-theoretic measures and deep learning techniques to identify and adapt the underlying distribution. Key innovations include the use of adversarial training mechanisms and differentiable programming to optimize the generative process. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional methods in terms of both sample fidelity and variety. Comparative analysis shows marked improvements in image generation tasks across standard benchmarks, indicating more effective convergence and realistic sample generation. The proposed method also reduces mode collapse, a common issue in generative modeling, leading to more robust model performance. Conclusion/Implications: Our findings reveal crucial insights into the role of base distributions within implicit generative models and underscore the potential of adaptive learning techniques in generative AI. The proposed method offers a scalable solution that can enhance various applications, including image synthesis, data augmentation, and beyond. Future directions will explore extending this framework to other generative contexts, potentially revolutionizing how base distributions are conceptualized and utilized. Keywords: Implicit Generative Models, Base Distribution, Adversarial Training, Mode Collapse, Image Generation, Deep Learning.
