This paper addresses the challenge of accommodating picky customers in complex decision-making scenarios through the lens of multi-objective reinforcement learning. The objective is to develop a framework that balances competing objectives while minimizing regret and exploration complexity. We propose a novel approach that integrates regret-bound analysis with exploration strategies to efficiently navigate high-dimensional state and action spaces. Our method leverages a combination of model-based and model-free techniques to adapt to changing customer preferences and optimize multiple objectives simultaneously. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in cumulative regret and sample efficiency compared to existing methods. The key findings highlight the importance of balancing exploration and exploitation in multi-objective settings, with implications for real-world applications such as recommendation systems and autonomous decision-making. Our contributions include a new regret bound analysis and an exploration complexity reduction technique, making multi-objective reinforcement learning more accessible and effective for accommodating picky customers. Key keywords: multi-objective reinforcement learning, regret bound, exploration complexity, model-based reinforcement learning, model-free reinforcement learning.

Objective: Accurate 3D human pose estimation from a single RGB image remains challenging due to depth ambiguity and high computational cost of volumetric representations. This paper introduces a coarse-to-fine volumetric prediction framework that delivers precise joint localization while maintaining efficiency. Methods: We propose a two-stage convolutional neural network. In the first (coarse) stage, a lightweight 2D backbone extracts feature maps that are lifted into a low-resolution 3D volume, producing coarse per-voxel joint likelihoods. In the second (fine) stage, we crop high-resolution volumetric subregions around the coarse predictions and apply a compact 3D convolutional refinement network. This hierarchical design concentrates computational resources on regions of interest, enabling precise depth recovery without processing the entire volume at full resolution. Results: Experiments on Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing single-image methods by reducing mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) by up to 12% while requiring 40% less inference time compared to full-resolution volumetric baselines. Qualitative results show sharper joint localization and robust performance under occlusions and unusual poses. Conclusion: The proposed coarse-to-fine volumetric prediction framework achieves a favorable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency for single-image 3D human pose estimation. Its modular design allows easy integration with alternative backbones or refinement modules, making it suitable for real-time applications in AR/VR, human–computer interaction, and sports analytics. Keywords: 3D human pose estimation; coarse-to-fine; volumetric prediction; single-image; convolutional neural networks.

Phân hệ phân tích dữ liệu và ứng dụng đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc khai thác thông tin từ dữ liệu khách hàng, giúp doanh nghiệp hiểu rõ hơn về hành vi, nhu cầu và xu hướng tiêu dùng của khách hàng. Kết quả từ việc áp dụng phân hệ này sẽ góp phần nâng cao khả năng cạnh tranh của doanh nghiệp trong thị trường ngày càng khốc liệt.

The accurate recognition of radio traffic sequences is a critical challenge in modern communication systems, particularly for applications in signal intelligence, spectrum monitoring, and automated network management. This paper presents an end-to-end deep learning framework for radio traffic sequence recognition, leveraging deep recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to model temporal dependencies in radio signals. The proposed approach eliminates the need for handcrafted feature extraction by directly processing raw radio frequency (RF) data, enabling robust and scalable sequence recognition. We employ a combination of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architectures to capture long-range dependencies and improve sequence modeling accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, outperforming traditional signal processing techniques and other machine learning approaches. The system exhibits superior robustness to noise and varying signal conditions, making it suitable for real-world deployment. This research contributes a novel, efficient, and generalizable solution for radio traffic sequence recognition, with potential applications in secure communications, spectrum management, and IoT device identification. **Keywords**: radio traffic recognition, deep learning, recurrent neural networks, LSTM, GRU, signal processing, sequence modeling.

This paper addresses the challenge of generating high-quality images using generative models, focusing on improving both the training and sampling processes. We propose a novel approach that combines adversarial training with score matching to enhance the stability and performance of image generation models. Specifically, our method leverages adversarial networks to refine the score matching objective, enabling more accurate estimation of data distributions and improved sample quality. We introduce an efficient sampling algorithm that integrates gradient-based updates with noise annealing, significantly reducing sampling time while maintaining fidelity. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both image quality and diversity across multiple benchmark datasets. The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance in Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS) metrics, showcasing its effectiveness in generating realistic and diverse images. This work contributes to the field of generative modeling by providing a robust framework for training and sampling, with potential applications in computer vision, medical imaging, and creative design. **Keywords**: adversarial training, score matching, image generation, generative models, sampling algorithms, deep learning.

Neonatal pain assessment is critical yet challenging due to the limited communication abilities of infants. This paper presents a novel approach for recognizing neonatal pain expression using transfer learning. The primary objective is to develop a robust and automated system for pain detection based on facial expressions. We employed a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) model, fine-tuned with a dataset of neonatal facial images exhibiting varying pain intensities. The transfer learning approach leverages knowledge gained from large-scale image datasets to improve performance with limited neonatal-specific data. Experimental results demonstrate that our system achieves high accuracy in classifying pain levels, outperforming traditional machine learning methods and other fine-tuning strategies. The proposed method offers a non-invasive and efficient tool for continuous pain monitoring in neonates. This research contributes to improved pain management practices in neonatal care and provides a foundation for further development of automated pain assessment technologies. Keywords: Neonatal Pain Recognition, Transfer Learning, Convolutional Neural Network, Facial Expression Analysis, Pain Assessment.

Duplicate data removal is a critical step in various information technology applications, including data preprocessing, information retrieval, and database management, to ensure data quality and efficiency. Traditional duplicate detection methods often rely on fixed heuristics or pairwise comparisons, which can struggle to capture complex dependencies within sequences of data records. This paper introduces a novel approach, Sequential Context Encoding (SCE), for enhancing duplicate removal by leveraging contextual relationships among data entries. The proposed method utilizes deep sequence modeling techniques—specifically, a combination of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and attention mechanisms—to encode the contextual information present in data sequences. Extensive experiments were conducted on benchmark datasets from multiple domains, demonstrating that our model significantly outperforms classic rule-based and popular machine learning approaches in both precision and recall. Additionally, our approach shows robustness in handling large-scale datasets with noisy and heterogeneous data characteristics. The results highlight the effectiveness of sequential context encoding in resolving ambiguities that arise in complex or non-trivial duplicate scenarios. This research advances the state-of-the-art in duplicate removal and presents practical implications for data integration, knowledge graph construction, and large-scale data cleaning systems. Keywords: duplicate removal, sequential context encoding, deep learning, data cleaning, attention mechanism, information retrieval.

This paper addresses the challenge of constructing multi-network models for heterogeneous multi-task learning, where multiple related tasks with diverse data types and structures need to be learned simultaneously. Our objective is to develop an automatic framework that can efficiently construct and optimize multi-network models, eliminating the need for manual design and tuning. We propose a novel approach that leverages graph-based neural networks and meta-learning to automatically construct and adapt multi-network models. Our method utilizes a hierarchical graph representation to capture task relationships and a meta-learning algorithm to optimize network architectures and weights. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in several heterogeneous multi-task learning benchmarks. The key findings of this research include improved performance, reduced manual effort, and enhanced scalability. Our contributions have significant implications for real-world applications, such as multi-modal processing, transfer learning, and few-shot learning. The proposed framework enables automatic construction of multi-network models, making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of multi-task learning, with relevant keywords including multi-network models, heterogeneous multi-task learning, graph-based neural networks, meta-learning, and automatic model construction.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of model interpretability in deep learning by proposing a novel approach that leverages Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to explain image classifier decisions within the StyleSpace latent domain. The primary objective is to bridge the gap between black-box classifier outputs and human-understandable visual explanations, enabling more transparent and trustworthy AI systems. Our method trains a GAN, specifically tuned to manipulate the StyleSpace—a disentangled latent representation derived from state-of-the-art style-based generators—so as to generate minimal and semantically meaningful image modifications that highlight the features influencing the classifier’s prediction. We implement an end-to-end framework where the GAN is guided by the targeted classifier’s gradients, ensuring that the generated explanations faithfully reflect the decision boundaries. Experimental results on benchmark image datasets demonstrate that our approach produces intuitive and high-fidelity visual explanations that outperform existing pixel-space and activation-space methods in terms of both interpretability and localization accuracy. Furthermore, the use of StyleSpace enables fine-grained control over image attributes, facilitating more nuanced explorations of classifier behavior. This research advances the field of explainable AI (XAI) by integrating GAN-based generative models with interpretable latent spaces, contributing new methodology for transparent decision analysis in image classification systems. Key keywords: explainable AI (XAI), GAN, StyleSpace, classifier interpretability, visual explanation, latent space, image classification.

Tỷ lệ trẻ em Việt Nam dưới 5 tuổi suy dinh dưỡng thấp còi vẫn còn ở mức cao, chiếm tỷ lệ 19,6%, trong đó tỷ lệ suy dinh dưỡng thấp còi cao nhất ở nhóm tuổi 24 - 36 tháng tuổi với gần 25% (năm 2020). Thực hành nuôi dưỡng trẻ em được xác định là yếu tố tác động trực tiếp đến tình trạng dinh dưỡng của trẻ. Năm 2009, Tổ chức Y tế Thế giới (WHO) đã đưa ra bộ chỉ số đánh giá nuôi dưỡng trẻ bú mẹ và thực hành cho trẻ ăn dặm từ 0 - 24 tháng tuổi (Infant and young child feeding indicators - IYCF), bộ chỉ số này đang được sử dụng ở Việt Nam trong các cuộc điều tra dinh dưỡng ở quy mô lớn. Tuy nhiên, bộ chỉ số IYCF vẫn còn điểm hạn chế trong giới hạn độ tuổi đánh giá và tổng hợp các thông tin nuôi dưỡng của từng trẻ. Chỉ số đánh giá nuôi dưỡng trẻ từ 6 - 36 tháng (Infant and young child feeding index - ICFI) được Ruel và Menon đề xuất năm 2002 tính đến nay đã được sử dụng phổ biến trong các nghiên cứu đánh giá nuôi dưỡng trẻ nhỏ ở các nước Mỹ Latin, Châu Phi, Trung Quốc, Thái Lan… trên nhiều quy mô khác nhau. Việc sử dụng chỉ số ICFI có thể mở ra các hướng tiếp cận mới trong thực hành lâm sàng và nghiên cứu điều tra đánh giá thực hành nuôi dưỡng trẻ 6 - 36 tháng tuổi tại Việt Nam để đề ra các giải pháp can thiệp hiệu quả đến quá trình nuôi dưỡng trẻ.
At step 3 of the main scenario, if the wrong format of data is entered, the system returns a message asking to enter the correct format of the information.

Tình hình nhiễm khuẩn các sản phẩm mô ghép đồng loài tại Ngân hàng Mô, Bệnh viện Hữu nghị Việt Đức đang trở thành một vấn đề đáng lo ngại trong lĩnh vực y tế. Nghiên cứu cho thấy tỷ lệ nhiễm khuẩn ở các sản phẩm mô ghép này có xu hướng gia tăng, ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến hiệu quả điều trị và sức khỏe của bệnh nhân. Các loại vi khuẩn gây nhiễm chủ yếu được xác định bao gồm Staphylococcus aureus và Escherichia coli, với nhiều trường hợp kháng thuốc. Việc kiểm soát nhiễm khuẩn trong quá trình thu thập, bảo quản và sử dụng mô ghép là rất cần thiết để đảm bảo an toàn cho người nhận. Các biện pháp phòng ngừa như cải thiện quy trình vô trùng, tăng cường giám sát và đào tạo nhân viên y tế đang được khuyến nghị nhằm giảm thiểu nguy cơ nhiễm khuẩn và nâng cao chất lượng sản phẩm mô ghép.

Playwright là một framework mã nguồn mở điểm kiểm tra các ứng dụng web được xây dựng trên Chrome, Firefox và WebKt. Nó cho phép vết các bài kiểm tra tự động có thể tương tác với các ứng dụng web theo cách giống như con người,bao gồm thực hiện các hành động như nhấp vào nút, nhập văn bản vào trường văn bản và cuộn trang. Nó cũng cung cấp các API mạnh mẽ và linh hoạt để tương tác với trình duyệt, thao tác với các thành phần trên trang web, xử lý các biểu mẫu, kiểm thử và chụp ảnh trang web, và thực hiện nhiều tác vụ khác liên quan đến tự động hóa trình duyệt. Playwright có thể giúp Scrapy vượt qua những hạn chế này bằng cách tự động mô phỏng trình duyệt và giải quyết các vấn đề liên quan đến JavaScript và tương tác người dùng. Bằng cách tích hợp Playwright vào Scrapy, có thể gả quyết các trang web động và thực hiện các tác vụ phức tạp hơn, bao gồm điền biểu mẫu động, chờ đợi và tương tác với các yếu tố trong trình duyệt.

This paper addresses the challenge of monocular videovisual odometry and depth estimation, crucial for understanding and navigating 3D environments using only a single camera. We explore both supervised and unsupervised learning paradigms to enhance the precision and robustness of visual odometry and depth estimation tasks. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) architecture tailored specifically for sequential video data, allowing for the effective capture of temporal dependencies between frames. Our approach leverages LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) units to retain crucial information over time and incorporates both supervised and unsupervised methods. In the supervised setting, the model is trained on ground truth data of visual odometry and depth, while the unsupervised model utilizes photometric consistency across frames to shape its understanding of the geometry. Results/Findings: Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, our model demonstrates superior performance in visual odometry and depth estimation tasks compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The RNN architecture significantly improves the estimation accuracy under dynamic and complex scenes, particularly in unsupervised scenarios where data labeling is costly or unavailable. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides a compelling framework for enhancing monocular visual odometry and depth estimation using RNNs, applicable in domains such as autonomous driving, augmented reality, and robotics. Our dual approach bridges the gap between supervision levels, offering flexibility and improved accuracy, marking a substantial contribution to the field of computer vision. Keywords: Recurrent Neural Network, RNN, monocular video, videovisual odometry, depth estimation, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, LSTM, computer vision.

This paper addresses the challenge of robust decision-making in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) by introducing tight Bayesian ambiguity sets. The objective is to develop a framework that can effectively handle model uncertainty, leading to more reliable and robust policies. Our approach utilizes Bayesian inference to construct ambiguity sets, which are then used to derive robust policies. The key innovation lies in the formulation of tight ambiguity sets, ensuring that the resulting policies are both robust and efficient. Our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of computational efficiency and solution quality. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in various MDP scenarios, showcasing improved robustness and adaptability. This research contributes to the development of more reliable decision-making systems, with potential applications in areas such as autonomous systems, robotics, and healthcare. Key keywords: Robust MDPs, Bayesian Ambiguity Sets, Decision-making under Uncertainty, Markov Decision Processes, Robust Optimization.

Việc tính toán tuân theo các nguyên tắc cơ bản của cơ học kết cấu, kết hợp với các đặc tính vật liệu đặc trưng của FRP như mô đun đàn hồi, cường độ chịu kéo và hệ số giãn nở nhiệt. This paper explores the application of reinforcement learning (RL) to train an agent to play soccer, focusing on bridging the sim-to-real gap for deployment in a real-world competitive environment. We developed a novel RL framework using a physics-based simulation environment to train the soccer agent, incorporating techniques to enhance robustness and generalization capabilities. Our approach includes a curriculum learning strategy, gradually increasing the complexity of the simulation to improve the agent's skill acquisition. The trained agent was then transferred to a physical robot platform and evaluated in real-world soccer matches. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed sim-to-real transfer method enables the robot to effectively perform basic soccer skills, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting, and compete against other robot teams. The results show the feasibility of training robots through RL in simulation and successfully deploying them in real-world dynamic environments, with a demonstrable level of competency. This work contributes to the field of robotics and AI by providing a practical approach to train and deploy intelligent agents in complex real-world scenarios. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Sim-to-Real Transfer, Robotics, Soccer, Curriculum Learning.

Đặt vấn đề: Laser quang đông toàn bộ võng mạc (PRP) là một điều trị tiêu chuẩn trong bệnh võng mạc đái tháo đường tăng sinh (BVMĐTĐTS). Các nghiên cứu gần đây đặt ra giả thuyết PRP giúp cải thiện sự tưới máu vùng hoàng điểm. OCTA giúp khảo sát sự thay đổi này một cách không xâm lấn. Mục tiêu nghiên cứu: Khảo sát tác động của PRP trên sự tưới máu hoàng điểm lớp nông và lớp sâu bằng OCTA. Đối tượng và phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu cắt dọc, 29 bệnh nhân với 44 mắt BVMĐTĐTS được đưa vào nghiên cứu. Bệnh nhân được đánh giá lâm sàng và khảo sát biến số trên OCTA bao gồm diện tích vùng vô mạch (FAZ), chỉ số độ tròn vùng vô mạch, mật độ mạch máu lớp nông và lớp sâu trước điều trị PRP, sau điều trị 1 tháng và 3 tháng. Kết quả: Thị lực logMAR trước điều trị là 0,50 ± 0,48, sau 3 tháng là 0,42 ± 0,34 (p = 0,004). FAZ trước điều trị là 0,38 ± 0,12, sau 3 tháng giảm còn 0,35 ± 0,12 (p < 0,001). Độ tròn vùng vô mạch trước điều trị là 0,61 ± 0,07, sau 3 tháng tăng lên 0,64 ± 0,06 (p < 0,001). Mật độ mạch máu lớp nông trước và sau điều trị 3 tháng lần lượt là 32,40 ± 5,81 và 34,27 ± 5,78 (p < 0,001). Mật độ mạch máu lớp sâu trước và sau điều trị 3 tháng lần lượt là 23,42 ± 5,31 và 24,40 ± 4,94 (p = 0,021). Thị lực sau điều trị có tương quan nghịch với độ tròn vùng vô mạch (r = -0,476) Kết luận: Có sự cải thiện tưới máu hoàng điểm sau điều trị PRP. OCTA có thể sử dụng như một công cụ theo dõi hiệu quả điều trị mang tính khách quan.

Scene graph generation aims to provide a semantic and structural description of an image, denoting the objects (with nodes) and their relationships (with edges). The best performing works to date are based on exploiting the context surrounding objects or relations,e.g., by passing information among objects. In these approaches, to transform the representation of source objects is a critical process for extracting information for the use by target objects. In this work, we argue that a source object should give what tar-get object needs and give different objects different information rather than contributing common information to all targets. To achieve this goal, we propose a Target-TailoredSource-Transformation (TTST) method to efficiently propagate information among object proposals and relations. Particularly, for a source object proposal which will contribute information to other target objects, we transform the source object feature to the target object feature domain by simultaneously taking both the source and target into account. We further explore more powerful representations by integrating language prior with the visual context in the transformation for the scene graph generation. By doing so the target object is able to extract target-specific information from the source object and source relation accordingly to refine its representation. Our framework is validated on the Visual Genome bench-mark and demonstrated its state-of-the-art performance for the scene graph generation. The experimental results show that the performance of object detection and visual relation-ship detection are promoted mutually by our method.

This paper explores an augmented decision tree approach for big data classification, addressing the challenges of scalability and accuracy inherent in traditional methods. We introduce a novel algorithm that combines decision tree learning with data augmentation techniques to improve classification performance on large datasets. Our method incorporates a dynamic data augmentation strategy based on the distribution of the training data, creating synthetic samples to balance class representation and enhance model generalization. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our augmented decision tree classifier achieves significantly improved accuracy and F1-score compared to standard decision trees and other state-of-the-art classification algorithms, while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for big data applications. The findings indicate that the proposed method offers a promising solution for effective and scalable big data classification. Keywords: Big Data, Classification, Decision Trees, Data Augmentation, Machine Learning.

Nền tảng DEducation là một giải pháp công nghệ tiên tiến nhằm cải thiện quy trình quản lý và lưu trữ học bạ dựa trên công nghệ Blockchain. Với sự phát triển nhanh chóng của công nghệ số, việc ứng dụng Blockchain vào giáo dục đã trở thành xu hướng tất yếu, mang lại nhiều lợi ích như tính minh bạch, bảo mật cao và khả năng truy xuất dữ liệu một cách chính xác. DEducation cho phép các cơ sở giáo dục cập nhật và lưu trữ thông tin học bạ của học sinh, sinh viên một cách an toàn và hiệu quả. Mỗi bản ghi học bạ được mã hóa và lưu trữ trên chuỗi khối, đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn của dữ liệu và ngăn chặn các hành vi gian lận hoặc thay đổi thông tin trái phép. Ngoài ra, nền tảng này còn hỗ trợ việc chia sẻ dữ liệu giữa các tổ chức giáo dục một cách nhanh chóng và thuận tiện, giảm thiểu thời gian và chi phí trong quy trình xác minh thông tin. DEducation không chỉ đáp ứng nhu cầu quản lý dữ liệu giáo dục hiện đại mà còn góp phần xây dựng một hệ thống giáo dục minh bạch, công bằng và đáng tin cậy hơn. Sự kết hợp giữa công nghệ Blockchain và giáo dục mở ra nhiều cơ hội để nâng cao chất lượng quản lý và bảo vệ thông tin cá nhân của người học trong thời đại số.

Seasonal time series Forecasting remains a challenging problem due to the long-term dependency from seasonality. In this paper, we propose a two-stage framework to forecast univariate seasonal time series. The first stage explicitly learns the long-range time series structure in a time window beyond the forecast horizon. By incorporating the learned long-range structure, the second stage can enhance the prediction accuracy in the forecast horizon. In both stages, we integrate the auto-regressive model with neural networks to capture both linear and non-linear characteristics in time series. Our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on M4 Competition Hourly datasets. In particular, we show that incorporating the intermediate results generated in the first stage to existing forecast models can effectively enhance their prediction performance.

This paper introduces Spectral Inference Networks, a novel framework that unifies deep learning and spectral methods to leverage the strengths of both paradigms. The objective is to develop a more comprehensive and effective approach to learning from complex data, addressing the limitations of traditional deep neural networks and spectral techniques. Our approach combines the representational power of deep neural networks with the interpretability and efficiency of spectral methods, using a spectral inference module to learn informative and discriminative spectral representations. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of Spectral Inference Networks in various tasks, including image classification and graph analysis, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The key findings highlight the importance of integrating spectral learning into deep neural networks, enabling more accurate and robust modeling of complex data. This research contributes to the development of more powerful and interpretable machine learning models, with potential applications in computer vision, graph analysis, and other fields, and paves the way for further research in spectral deep learning, neural networks, and AI models.

This paper explores the potential role of probabilistic integration in statistical computation, addressing the challenges of accurately estimating integrals in high-dimensional spaces, which are fundamental to many statistical and machine learning applications. Traditional numerical integration methods often struggle with scalability and efficiency in such settings. To address this, we propose a probabilistic approach that leverages Monte Carlo techniques and Bayesian inference to approximate integrals with improved accuracy and computational efficiency. Our methodology involves constructing probabilistic models that adaptively sample from the integrand, reducing variance and computational cost compared to conventional methods. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and runtime, particularly in high-dimensional scenarios. The findings suggest that probabilistic integration can significantly enhance statistical computation, offering a robust alternative for applications such as Bayesian inference, uncertainty quantification, and probabilistic machine learning. Objective: Point-set registration—the process of aligning two sets of points in space—is a core task in areas such as computer vision, medical imaging, and robotics. Existing methods often rely on supervision, restrictive assumptions, or are limited to low-dimensional data. We present an unsupervised, iterative algorithm that generalizes to N-dimensional point sets without requiring labeled correspondences or predefined models. Methods: Our approach alternates between estimating soft correspondences via a robust distance metric and updating the transformation parameters using a weighted least-squares fit. To handle noise and outliers, we integrate a trimmed correspondence strategy and adaptively adjust point-set weights. The method supports rigid, affine, and nonrigid transformations in arbitrary dimensions, and it converges under mild conditions without manual parameter tuning. Results: We evaluate the algorithm on synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets—including 2D shape alignment, 3D surface registration, and 4D spatiotemporal data. Compared to standard ICP, Coherent Point Drift (CPD), and a recent learning-based baseline, our method achieves up to 30% lower mean registration error and demonstrates faster convergence. It also maintains high accuracy when up to 20% of points are corrupted or missing. Conclusion: The proposed unsupervised, iterative N-dimensional registration framework offers a versatile, robust solution for aligning point sets across diverse applications. Its model-agnostic design and minimal supervision make it especially suited for emerging domains such as high-dimensional biology, multiview sensor fusion, and dynamic scene reconstruction. Keywords: point-set registration, unsupervised learning, iterative alignment, N-dimensional data, robust correspondence, transformation estimation.

This paper introduces a novel matrix and tensor framework for discriminative learning using score function features. This paper proposes a novel approach to graph node embeddings by leveraging domain-aware biased random walks. The objective is to improve the representation learning of graph nodes by incorporating domain-specific knowledge into the random walk process. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate significant improvements in node classification and clustering tasks compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our domain-aware biased random walks can effectively preserve the semantic relationships between nodes, leading to more informative and discriminative node embeddings. Key keywords: graph node embeddings, domain-aware biased random walks, representation learning, node classification, clustering.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently computing and backpropagating gradients under angle-parametrized orthogonal matrices, a critical component in various machine learning and optimization tasks. While orthogonal matrices are widely used for their stability and interpretability, their computational complexity and gradient propagation often hinder scalability, especially in large-scale applications. To overcome this, we propose a novel parallelized framework that leverages angle-based parametrization to decompose orthogonal matrices into a sequence of elementary rotations. Our approach enables efficient computation of matrix operations and gradients by exploiting parallelism across multiple processing units. We introduce a specialized backpropagation algorithm tailored for angle-parametrized matrices, which significantly reduces memory overhead and computational time compared to traditional methods. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves up to 40% faster training times on benchmark datasets while maintaining numerical stability and accuracy. Furthermore, we showcase its applicability in deep learning architectures, such as recurrent neural networks and generative models, where orthogonal constraints are essential. This work contributes a scalable and practical solution for integrating orthogonal matrices into modern machine learning pipelines, paving the way for broader adoption in resource-intensive applications. **Keywords**: orthogonal matrices, angle parametrization, parallel computation, backpropagation, machine learning, optimization.

The increasing complexity of healthcare data necessitates advanced tools for efficient cohort extraction and analysis. This paper introduces **ODVICE**, an **Ontology-Driven Visual Analytic Tool** designed to facilitate **Interactive Cohort Extraction** from large-scale healthcare datasets. The primary objective of ODVICE is to enable researchers and clinicians to intuitively explore, filter, and extract patient cohorts using a combination of semantic reasoning and interactive visualization. The tool leverages domain-specific ontologies to structure and contextualize data, ensuring accurate and meaningful cohort definitions. A user-friendly visual interface allows for dynamic querying and real-time refinement of cohort criteria, while backend algorithms optimize data retrieval and processing. To evaluate ODVICE, we conducted experiments on a real-world electronic health record (EHR) dataset, comparing its performance against traditional query-based methods. Results demonstrate that ODVICE significantly reduces the time and effort required for cohort extraction while improving precision and recall. Furthermore, the tool's ability to integrate domain knowledge through ontologies enhances the interpretability and relevance of extracted cohorts. ODVICE represents a novel contribution to the field of healthcare analytics by bridging the gap between semantic reasoning and interactive visualization. Its potential applications include clinical research, personalized medicine, and population health management. By combining ontology-driven reasoning with user-centric design, ODVICE empowers users to derive actionable insights from complex healthcare data efficiently. **Keywords**: Ontology, Visual Analytics, Cohort Extraction, Healthcare Data, Interactive Tools, Semantic Reasoning.

Key keywords: 3D adversarial logos, object detection, deep learning, cloaking, adversarial machine learning.

The exploration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) has grown substantially due to their capacity to model complex structures inherent in graph-based data. Methods/Approach: We introduce novel methodologies for constructing Deep Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) that incorporate advanced techniques such as residual connections, attention mechanisms, and layer normalization to address challenges like vanishing gradients and over-smoothing. Our approach emphasizes scalability and robustness, ensuring effective learning even as model depth increases. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations conducted on multiple benchmark datasets reveal that our proposed DGNN architectures achieve significant performance improvements over traditional shallow GNN models. Key findings demonstrate enhanced node classification accuracy, superior link prediction reliability, and improved graph clustering effectiveness. Comparative analysis indicates a marked increase in the capability of our models to generalize across diverse graph structures. Conclusion/Implications: The findings underscore the potential of DGNNs to redefine current paradigms in graph representation learning by expanding the depth of GNNs without compromising computational efficiency or model stability. Our contributions lay the groundwork for future studies to further explore deep and scalable graph-based learning approaches, with applications spanning recommendation systems, network analysis, and bioinformatics. Keywords such as deep learning, graph neural networks, model scalability, and graph analytics are central to our research narrative.

Object detection in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery presents unique challenges due to factors like small object size, varying viewpoints, and complex backgrounds. This paper introduces SyNet, an ensemble network designed to improve object detection accuracy in UAV images. SyNet leverages a diverse set of pre-trained object detection models, including YOLOv5, Faster R-CNN, and EfficientDet, fine-tuned on a custom UAV dataset. A novel weighted averaging technique is employed to combine the predictions from these individual models, optimizing for both precision and recall. Experimental results demonstrate that SyNet outperforms individual detectors, achieving a 15% improvement in mean Average Precision (mAP) compared to the best-performing single model. Furthermore, SyNet exhibits robustness across different UAV datasets and varying object densities. The proposed ensemble approach provides a practical solution for enhancing the reliability and accuracy of object detection in real-world UAV applications such as infrastructure inspection and environmental monitoring. Keywords: UAV, object detection, ensemble learning, deep learning, computer vision.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of self-supervised learning (SSL) techniques for visual feature extraction, focusing on methods that leverage unlabeled data to reduce dependency on annotations. We systematically categorize existing approaches into generative, contrastive, and predictive frameworks, analyzing their underlying principles, architectures, and performance across various benchmarks. Furthermore, we highlight recent innovations, such as cross-modal SSL and hybrid approaches, which demonstrate improved generalization and robustness. The survey concludes with a discussion on open challenges, including scalability, domain adaptation, and interpretability, while emphasizing the potential of SSL to revolutionize computer vision applications such as object detection, image segmentation, and video analysis. Monocular 3D object detection is a critical challenge in computer vision, with applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. This paper introduces the Deep Fitting Degree Scoring Network (DFDS-Net), a novel framework designed to improve the accuracy and robustness of 3D object detection from single-view images. The proposed approach leverages a deep learning-based scoring mechanism to evaluate the fitting degree between 2D image features and 3D object hypotheses, enabling more precise localization and orientation estimation. DFDS-Net integrates a multi-task architecture that simultaneously optimizes for object classification, 3D bounding box regression, and fitting degree scoring, ensuring a holistic understanding of the scene. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DFDS-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The framework achieves significant improvements in 3D object localization, particularly in challenging scenarios with occlusions and varying lighting conditions. This research contributes to advancing monocular 3D detection by introducing a robust scoring mechanism that enhances the alignment between 2D and 3D representations, paving the way for more reliable real-world applications. **Keywords**: Monocular 3D object detection, deep learning, fitting degree scoring, autonomous driving, computer vision, 3D localization.

The increasing demand for energy-efficient and adaptable neural networks in real-time applications has driven the need for runtime-throttleable systems. This paper addresses the challenge of dynamically adjusting the computational resources of neural networks during inference to balance performance and energy consumption. We propose a novel framework that enables runtime throttling by leveraging adaptive pruning and quantization techniques, allowing the network to scale its computational complexity based on resource availability or application requirements. Our approach integrates a lightweight control mechanism that dynamically adjusts the network's depth and precision without requiring retraining or significant overhead. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves up to a 40% reduction in energy consumption with minimal accuracy degradation compared to static models. The results highlight the framework's ability to maintain competitive performance while offering flexibility for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as edge devices and IoT systems. This work contributes to the growing field of energy-efficient AI by providing a practical solution for runtime-adaptive neural networks, paving the way for more sustainable and scalable AI applications. **Keywords**: runtime throttling, neural networks, adaptive pruning, quantization, energy efficiency, edge computing.

Detecting small objects in complex scenes remains a significant challenge in computer vision. This paper introduces an efficient coarse-to-fine non-local (ECF-NL) module designed to improve the detection accuracy of small objects while minimizing computational overhead. Our approach leverages a coarse-grained global attention mechanism to rapidly identify regions of interest likely to contain small objects, followed by a fine-grained non-local operation within these regions to capture subtle contextual cues. This hierarchical attention strategy reduces the computational cost associated with traditional non-local methods. We evaluate the ECF-NL module on benchmark datasets containing small objects, demonstrating significant improvements in detection accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly for objects occupying a small percentage of the image. The results show that the ECF-NL module effectively enhances feature representations for small objects, leading to more robust and accurate detection. The proposed module offers a practical solution for small object detection in resource-constrained environments. Keywords: Small Object Detection, Non-Local Module, Attention Mechanism, Computer Vision, Deep Learning.

Objective: The assessment and monitoring of infant sleep patterns are critical for early diagnosis of health and developmental issues. Traditional methods often struggle with noisy and incomplete time-series data, limiting their efficacy. This study proposes a novel approach utilizing low-rank matrix factorization (LRMF) to extract meaningful patterns from complex, real-world infant-sleep datasets. Methods: Our approach involves structuring multi-channel infant-sleep sensor readings into matrices, followed by the application of low-rank matrix factorization techniques. LRMF enables decomposition of high-dimensional time-series data into interpretable latent factors, effectively isolating key sleep stages and transitions while mitigating the impact of noise and missing values. We further evaluate the performance of LRMF against standard time-series analysis methods, including autoregressive models and principal component analysis. Results: Experiments were conducted on a large-scale infant-sleep dataset consisting of both actigraphy and video observations. The proposed method demonstrated superior accuracy in detecting sleep patterns and transition points, achieving an average improvement of 12% in pattern recognition metrics over baseline methods. Additionally, our approach exhibited enhanced robustness to missing or irregular data, providing more consistent results across sensor modalities. Conclusion: This research presents a robust and scalable framework for time-series analysis in infant-sleep studies, leveraging low-rank matrix factorization for improved pattern discovery and noise resilience. The findings contribute important advancements to automated sleep monitoring applications, offering potential benefits for pediatric health diagnostics and longitudinal developmental research. Keywords: Time-Series Analysis, Low-Rank Matrix Factorization, Infant Sleep, Sleep Pattern Recognition, Missing Data, Biomedical Signal Processing

Reinforcement learning is a powerful approach to learn behaviour through interactions with an environment. However, behaviours are usually learned in a purely reactive fashion, where an appropriate action is selected based on an observation. In this form, it is challenging to learn when it is necessary to execute new decisions. This makes learning inefficient, especially in environments that need various degrees of fine and coarse control. To address this, we propose a proactive setting in which the agent not only selects an action in a state but also for how long to commit to that action. Our TempoRL approach introduces skip connections between states and learns a skip-policy for repeating the same action along these skips. We demonstrate the effectiveness of TempoRL on a variety of traditional and deep RL environments, showing that our approach is capable of learning successful policies up to an order of magnitude faster than vanilla Q-learning.

Profile face recognition poses significant challenges due to drastic variations in facial appearance caused by pose, leading to reduced recognition accuracy in real-world applications. This paper introduces an Attention-guided Progressive Mapping (APM) framework designed to address the difficulties of recognizing profiles by progressively bridging the appearance gap between frontal and profile face images. The proposed approach leverages an attention mechanism to selectively focus on salient facial regions that are robust to pose changes, allowing for more informative feature extraction. The progressive mapping strategy incrementally aligns profile faces toward a canonical representation through a series of intermediate domains, thus reducing the nonlinear transformation complexity. Extensive experiments are conducted on standard face recognition benchmarks, demonstrating that the APM framework significantly improves recognition accuracy on large pose variations compared to state-of-the-art methods. In addition, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of both the attention module and the progressive mapping stages in enhancing feature consistency. The results indicate that our method provides a practical and scalable solution for profile face recognition, offering promising applications in surveillance, security, and human-computer interaction systems. Keywords: face recognition, profile face, attention mechanism, progressive mapping, deep learning, pose variation, feature alignment.

This paper introduces SITHCon, a novel neural network architecture designed to be robust to variations in input scaling on the time dimension. The objective is to develop a model that can effectively handle time-series data with diverse scaling factors, a common challenge in real-world applications. To achieve this, we propose a multi-scale convolutional neural network (CNN) approach that incorporates a scaling-invariant module, enabling the model to learn features that are insensitive to time-axis scaling. Our method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance and robustness compared to existing state-of-the-art models. The results show that SITHCon achieves significant improvements in accuracy and stability, particularly in scenarios with large variations in input scaling. The contributions of this research lie in its ability to provide a reliable and efficient solution for time-series analysis, with potential applications in fields such as finance, healthcare, and signal processing. Key keywords: neural networks, time-series analysis, scaling invariance, convolutional neural networks, robustness.

Instance segmentation on 3D point clouds is crucial for scene understanding in various applications, yet existing methods often struggle with complex scenes due to limitations in task definition and evaluation metrics. This paper re-evaluates the standard instance segmentation pipeline, proposing modifications to address prevalent issues like over-segmentation and inconsistent performance across different object categories. We introduce a novel loss function that incorporates both geometric and semantic information to improve segmentation accuracy, particularly for objects with intricate shapes. Furthermore, we propose a new metric, termed "Coverage-Weighted IoU," which better reflects segmentation quality by accounting for varying object sizes and densities. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness. Specifically, we achieve a 15% improvement in average precision compared to state-of-the-art techniques. Our analysis reveals that the proposed metric correlates more strongly with human perception of segmentation quality than traditional IoU-based metrics. This work offers insights into the limitations of current instance segmentation approaches and provides a more effective framework for future research and development. Keywords: 3D point clouds, instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, loss function, evaluation metric, scene understanding.

This paper presents an unsupervised multi-modal representation learning approach for affective computing, leveraging multi-corpus wearable data to improve emotion recognition and analysis. The objective is to develop a robust and generalizable model that can effectively capture complex emotional patterns from diverse physiological and contextual signals. Our approach employs a novel fusion of deep learning architectures and dimensionality reduction techniques to learn compact and informative representations from multiple wearable datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our method, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in emotion classification and regression tasks. The proposed framework enables the discovery of latent emotional structures and relationships between different modalities, contributing to a deeper understanding of human affective experiences. This research has significant implications for affective computing, human-computer interaction, and wearable technology applications, highlighting the potential of unsupervised multi-modal learning for enhancing emotional intelligence and well-being. Key contributions include the development of a scalable and adaptable framework for multi-corpus wearable data integration, and the introduction of a novel evaluation protocol for assessing representation learning quality in affective computing contexts. Relevant keywords: affective computing, multi-modal representation learning, wearable technology, unsupervised learning, emotion recognition, human-computer interaction.

Nighttime stereo depth estimation presents significant challenges due to poor lighting conditions, light effects (e.g., glare, reflections), and uninformative regions where texture or features are scarce. This paper addresses these issues by proposing a novel approach based on Joint Translation-Stereo Learning (JTSL). The objective is to enhance depth estimation accuracy in nighttime scenarios by leveraging the complementary strengths of image translation and stereo matching. Our method integrates a translation network to transform nighttime images into a daytime-like representation, reducing the impact of adverse lighting, and a stereo network to estimate depth from the translated images. The joint learning framework is trained end-to-end, ensuring seamless collaboration between the two components. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods, particularly in handling light effects and uninformative regions. Key findings include a 15% improvement in depth estimation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art nighttime stereo methods. The implications of this research are significant for applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and surveillance, where reliable depth estimation in low-light conditions is critical. This work contributes a robust and innovative solution to nighttime stereo depth estimation, advancing the field with its joint learning paradigm and improved performance. **Keywords**: nighttime stereo depth estimation, joint translation-stereo learning, light effects, uninformative regions, image translation, stereo matching, autonomous systems.

This paper introduces a novel geometric approach, termed A-expansion, designed to efficiently handle multiple "hedgehog" shapes in computational geometry. The objective is to develop a robust method for managing complex shapes with multiple protrusions, akin to hedgehogs, which pose significant challenges in traditional geometric processing pipelines. Our approach leverages a combination of mesh refinement and adaptive sampling to effectively capture the intricate details of these shapes. The A-expansion method is demonstrated to outperform existing techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in scenarios involving large numbers of hedgehog shapes. Key findings include significant reductions in processing time and improved robustness to noise and degenerate cases. The implications of this research are far-reaching, with potential applications in computer-aided design, robotics, and 3D reconstruction. By providing a fast and reliable means of handling complex shapes, A-expansion contributes to the advancement of geometric computing, enabling more sophisticated and realistic modeling in various fields. Relevant keywords: geometric processing, mesh refinement, adaptive sampling, hedgehog shapes, computational geometry.

Bài toán được tiếp cận bằng cách xây dựng và tối ưu hóa các mô hình học máy, trong đó có các thuật toán như Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN) và Gradient Boosting. Mục tiêu là tạo ra một mô hình có khả năng dự đoán chính xác và nhanh chóng khả năng chịu tải của cột CFST dưới tác động của tải trọng nén lệch tâm, một yếu tố quan trọng trong thiết kế kết cấu. Các yếu tố ảnh hưởng như đặc tính vật liệu, kích thước hình học của cột và độ lệch tâm của tải trọng được đưa vào mô hình. Kết quả cho thấy mô hình học máy được tối ưu hóa có thể dự đoán khả năng chịu tải của cột CFST với độ chính xác cao, giúp giảm thiểu sự phụ thuộc vào các phương pháp tính toán phức tạp và tốn thời gian. Ứng dụng của mô hình này có tiềm năng lớn trong việc tối ưu hóa thiết kế và tăng cường độ an toàn của các công trình xây dựng sử dụng cột CFST.

This paper presents LumiPath, a novel approach to achieving real-time, physically-based rendering on embedded devices, addressing the challenge of balancing high-quality graphics with the computational constraints inherent in such hardware. The demand for realistic visualization in mobile applications and AR/VR systems necessitates more efficient rendering solutions. Methods/Approach: LumiPath leverages optimized rendering algorithms designed to exploit the capabilities of modern embedded GPUs, in conjunction with real-time processing techniques. We employ a hybrid rendering pipeline that integrates adaptive sampling, efficient light transport mechanisms, and hardware-accelerated rasterization to enhance performance while maintaining photorealistic quality. Results/Findings: Our experimental evaluation demonstrates that LumiPath can render complex scenes at interactive frame rates, achieving performance comparable to desktop systems with significantly higher power consumption. Benchmarks show improvements in frame rendering time by up to 40% in comparison to existing mobile rendering solutions while preserving visual fidelity. Additionally, LumiPath effectively scales to different hardware architectures and supports a variety of lighting conditions. Conclusion/Implications: LumiPath represents a significant advancement in the field of real-time rendering for embedded systems, expanding the potential for immersive applications in mobile and low-power environments. By optimizing the rendering pipeline, this research paves the way for more accessible AR/VR experiences and high-fidelity graphics on portable devices. Future work could explore the integration of machine learning techniques to further enhance rendering accuracy and performance adaptability. Key Keywords: real-time rendering, physically-based rendering, embedded devices, GPU optimization, mobile graphics, AR/VR.

This paper addresses the challenge of semantic segmentation of urban scenes in the presence of domain shift, where a model trained on one dataset performs poorly on another. Our objective is to develop a curriculum domain adaptation approach that enables effective transfer of knowledge from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain. We propose a novel methodology that leverages a curriculum learning strategy to adapt a semantic segmentation model to the target domain in a gradual and incremental manner. Our approach utilizes a self-supervised learning framework to generate pseudo-labels for the target domain, which are then used to fine-tune the model. Experimental results demonstrate that our curriculum domain adaptation approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant improvements in segmentation accuracy and reducing the domain shift. The key contributions of our research include a novel curriculum learning strategy, a self-supervised pseudo-labeling approach, and a comprehensive evaluation framework for domain adaptation in semantic segmentation. Our work has important implications for autonomous driving, urban planning, and smart city applications, where accurate semantic segmentation of urban scenes is crucial. Key keywords: curriculum domain adaptation, semantic segmentation, urban scenes, self-supervised learning, pseudo-labeling, domain shift.

Seeking effective neural networks is a critical and practical field in deep learning. Besides designing the depth, type of convolution, normalization, and nonlinearities, the topological connectivity of neural networks is also important. Previous principles of rule-based modular design simplify the difficulty of building an effective architecture, but constrain the possible topologies in limited spaces. In this paper, we attempt to optimize the connectivity in neural networks. We propose a topological perspective to represent a network into a complete graph for analysis, where nodes carry out aggregation and transformation of features, and edges determine the flow of information. By assigning learnable parameters to the edges which reflect the magnitude of connections, the learning process can be performed in a differentiable manner. We further attach auxiliary sparsity constraint to the distribution of connectedness, which promotes the learned topology focus on critical connections. This learning process is compatible with existing networks and owns adaptability to larger search spaces and different tasks. Quantitative results of experiments reflect the learned connectivity is superior to traditional rule-based ones, such as random, residual, and complete. In addition, it obtains significant improvements in image classification and object detection without introducing excessive computation burden.

This paper proposes a novel approach to improving the efficiency and effectiveness of deep neural networks by incorporating fast Walsh-Hadamard transform and smooth-thresholding based binary layers. The objective is to reduce computational complexity while maintaining or improving model accuracy. Our method utilizes the fast Walsh-Hadamard transform to efficiently compute binary representations of inputs, which are then processed through smooth-thresholding based binary layers. This approach enables significant reductions in computational costs and memory usage. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed architecture achieves comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art models on several benchmark datasets, while requiring substantially fewer parameters and computations. The key contributions of this research include the development of a fast and efficient binary layer framework, and the demonstration of its potential to improve the scalability and deployability of deep neural networks. Our work has important implications for a range of applications, including edge AI, mobile computing, and embedded systems, where computational resources are limited. Key keywords: deep neural networks, binary layers, Walsh-Hadamard transform, smooth-thresholding, efficient computing, edge AI.

This paper addresses the challenging problem of vehicle trajectory prediction in crowded highway scenarios, where the complexity of interactions between vehicles poses significant difficulties for accurate forecasting. Our approach utilizes bird eye view representations to transform the complex spatial relationships into a more manageable format, which is then processed by Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to predict future vehicle trajectories. The proposed method leverages the strengths of CNNs in image processing to analyze the bird eye view representations, capturing both short-term and long-term dependencies in vehicle movements. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to existing methods. The key contributions of this research include the innovative application of bird eye view representations and CNNs to vehicle trajectory prediction, as well as the development of a robust and scalable framework for crowded highway scenarios. This work has important implications for the development of autonomous vehicles and intelligent transportation systems, enabling safer and more efficient traffic flow. Key keywords: vehicle trajectory prediction, bird eye view representations, CNNs, crowded highway scenarios, autonomous vehicles, intelligent transportation systems.

Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of acquiring large-scale, high-quality datasets for training deep action recognition networks, a critical bottleneck in advancing video understanding applications. We propose a novel procedural video generation framework that creates synthetic action sequences by programmatically composing realistic environments, agents, and motion patterns. Our method leverages physics-based simulation, customizable animation libraries, and domain-randomization techniques to produce diverse and annotated video datasets that span a wide variety of human actions and contexts. We conduct extensive experiments by training state-of-the-art deep action recognition models on both procedurally generated and real-world datasets, evaluating their performance on standard benchmarks. The results demonstrate that networks trained with our synthetic videos achieve competitive accuracy and show enhanced generalization capabilities, particularly in scenarios with limited real data availability. Our approach reduces dependence on costly manual data collection and annotation, accelerates training cycles, and allows the flexible generation of rare or dangerous action events. This research contributes a scalable toolset for augmenting video datasets and improving the robustness of action recognition systems across surveillance, robotics, and human-computer interaction domains. Key keywords: procedural generation, synthetic videos, action recognition, deep learning, data augmentation, video understanding.

This paper introduces a novel ante-hoc explanation method that induces semantic grouping of latent concepts within neural networks, enhancing the interpretability of model decisions without sacrificing accuracy. Our approach addresses the challenge of understanding complex, high-dimensional latent spaces by organizing individual concepts into meaningful groups based on semantic similarity. We achieve this by incorporating a grouping loss during the training phase, encouraging the network to learn representations that naturally cluster related concepts. We evaluate our method on image classification and natural language processing tasks, demonstrating that it produces more coherent and human-understandable explanations compared to existing post-hoc techniques. Specifically, our approach allows for identifying higher-level semantic features that contribute to a model's prediction, such as "animal features" or "syntactic structure". Experimental results show that our method maintains competitive prediction performance while significantly improving explanation quality, as measured by human evaluation and quantitative metrics. The induced semantic groupings provide valuable insights into the inner workings of neural networks and offer a pathway towards building more transparent and trustworthy AI systems. Keywords: Explainable AI, Ante-hoc Explanation, Interpretability, Latent Space, Semantic Grouping, Neural Networks.

Sentence Selection: Following the Pyramid evaluation framework, salient sentences are identified, taking into account the cluster of related documents. The process involves iterating through the Entity Pyramid, selecting entities from top to bottom (highest to lowest frequency), and then choosing sentences that include the selected entity as the initial candidate set. To ensure that the selected sentences represent the entire cluster, their content overlap with other documents in the cluster is measured using ROUGE scores . This step encourages the model to connect and aggregate information across multiple documents during the pretraining phase.

Process mining deals with extraction of knowledge from business process execution logs. Traditional process mining tasks, like process model generation or conformance checking, rely on a minimalistic feature set where each event is characterized only by its case identifier, activity type, and timestamp. In contrast, the success of modern machine learning is based on models that take any available data as direct input and build layers of features automatically during training. In this work, we introduce ProcK (Process & Knowledge), a novel pipeline to build business process prediction models that take into account both sequential data in the form of event logs and rich semantic information represented in a graph-structured knowledge base. The hybrid approach enables ProcK to flexibly make use of all information residing in the databases of organizations. Components to extract inter-linked event logs and knowledge bases from relational databases are part of the pipeline. We demonstrate the power of ProcK by training it for prediction tasks on the OULAD e-learning dataset, where we achieve state-of-the-art performance on the tasks of predicting student dropout from courses and predicting their success. We also apply our method on a number of additional machine learning tasks, including exam score prediction and early predictions that only take into account data recorded during the first weeks of the courses.

This paper proposes FD-GAN, a novel face-demorphing generative adversarial network designed to restore an accomplice's facial image from a morphed image. The objective is to address the challenge of identifying accomplices in criminal investigations where facial images have been intentionally altered. Our approach utilizes a deep learning-based method, combining a generator network and a discriminator network to learn the demorphing process. The FD-GAN model is trained on a large dataset of morphed and original image pairs, enabling it to effectively remove morphing artifacts and recover the original facial features. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of FD-GAN in restoring high-quality facial images, outperforming existing demorphing methods. The proposed method has significant implications for law enforcement and forensic applications, providing a powerful tool for identifying and prosecuting criminals. Key contributions of this research include the introduction of a novel GAN-based architecture for face demorphing and the achievement of state-of-the-art performance in restoring accomplice's facial images. Relevant keywords: face demorphing, generative adversarial networks, deep learning, forensic facial analysis, image restoration.

Cooperative perception among autonomous vehicles enhances object detection accuracy and robustness by leveraging complementary information from multiple viewpoints. However, limited communication bandwidth poses a significant challenge for sharing raw or intermediate data. This paper introduces a novel bandwidth-adaptive feature sharing framework for cooperative LiDAR object detection. Our approach dynamically adjusts the amount of shared feature information based on network conditions and the relevance of features to the detection task. Specifically, we employ a feature selection module guided by an attention mechanism to prioritize salient features for transmission. Furthermore, we introduce a bandwidth estimation module that predicts available bandwidth and adaptively compresses the selected features. Experimental results on the V2X-Sim dataset demonstrate that our framework achieves comparable object detection performance to full feature sharing under ideal bandwidth conditions, while significantly outperforming existing methods under bandwidth constraints. The proposed method improves the trade-off between detection accuracy and communication overhead, enabling robust cooperative perception in realistic vehicular networks. Keywords: Cooperative Perception, LiDAR, Object Detection, Bandwidth Adaptation, Feature Sharing, Autonomous Vehicles.

Model compression techniques, such as pruning, are crucial for deploying deep neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This paper investigates the theoretical benefits of overparameterization in the context of neural network pruning. We demonstrate that overparameterized networks, even those exhibiting double descent phenomena, offer provable advantages for achieving higher compression rates and improved generalization performance after pruning. Our analysis reveals that overparameterization facilitates the discovery of more robust and resilient subnetworks during the pruning process. Specifically, we establish theoretical bounds on the trade-off between network size, pruning ratio, and generalization error, showing that overparameterization can mitigate the performance degradation typically associated with aggressive pruning. We validate our theoretical findings through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and network architectures, demonstrating superior performance compared to pruning directly from smaller, conventionally-sized networks. This work provides theoretical justification for the empirical observation that larger models are often easier to prune effectively, contributing to a deeper understanding of the interplay between overparameterization, compression, and generalization in deep learning. Keywords: Overparameterization, Model Compression, Pruning, Neural Networks, Double Descent, Generalization, Deep Learning.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning effective representations for multiplex bipartite networks, which are prevalent in real-world applications such as recommendation systems, social networks, and biological interactions. Traditional network embedding methods often fail to capture the complex, multi-layered relationships inherent in such networks. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel framework based on Dual Hypergraph Convolutional Networks (DHCN), which simultaneously models both the bipartite structure and the multiplex relationships across layers. Our approach leverages hypergraph convolution to encode higher-order interactions and employs a dual-network architecture to integrate information from different layers effectively. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that DHCN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in tasks such as link prediction and node classification, achieving improvements of up to 15% in accuracy. The proposed framework not only provides a robust solution for multiplex bipartite network embedding but also offers insights into modeling complex relational data. This work has significant implications for applications in personalized recommendation, community detection, and multi-modal data analysis. **Keywords**: Multiplex networks, bipartite networks, hypergraph convolutional networks, network embedding, representation learning.

This research addresses the significant challenge of off-policy deep reinforcement learning by proposing a novel method that eliminates the need for exploration while maintaining or improving performance. In traditional reinforcement learning frameworks, exploration is critical but often leads to inefficiencies and increased computational complexity. Methods/Approach: We introduce a new off-policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm that leverages an innovative approach to maximize the utility of pre-existing data without explicitly exploring new actions. The proposed model utilizes a unique architecture, incorporating advanced neural network design and efficient data utilization strategies, to optimize learning from historical experience. Results/Findings: Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable or superior performance to traditional exploration-based approaches across various benchmark reinforcement learning tasks. Notably, the algorithm significantly reduces training time and computational resources by minimizing exploration overhead. These results reveal the potential of our approach to effectively learn complex policies solely from historical data. Conclusion/Implications: The findings suggest that off-policy reinforcement learning can be successfully executed without the need for exploration, challenging the traditional view that exploration is an essential component. This research opens up new avenues for reinforcement learning applications in environments where exploration is costly or impractical. The method holds promise for enhancing the efficiency and applicability of reinforcement learning in real-world settings, such as robotics and automated decision-making systems. Keywords: deep reinforcement learning, off-policy learning, exploration elimination, algorithm optimization, neural networks, data utilization.

This paper introduces a novel approach to adversarial imitation learning by leveraging Wasserstein distances. Traditional imitation learning techniques often struggle with mode collapse and training difficulties, posing challenges in learning complex behaviors from demonstrations. This research addresses these limitations through the development of Wasserstein Adversarial Imitation Learning (WAIL), which aims to enhance stability and efficiency. Methods/Approach: The proposed method employs a Wasserstein distance framework within the realm of generative adversarial networks (GANs) to improve the imitation learning process. By integrating the Wasserstein metric, WAIL attempts to provide a more robust measure of similarity between the policy being learned and the expert demonstrations, thus alleviating the common issues associated with adversarial approaches. The architecture consists of a discriminator and a generator where the discriminator is trained to distinguish between the expert and the generated policies, guided by the Wasserstein metric. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that WAIL significantly enhances the convergence speed and robustness of the imitation learning process compared to existing methods. The performance of WAIL was evaluated on various benchmark tasks, where it exhibited superior capability in capturing complex behaviors with reduced training instability. This approach outperformed traditional adversarial imitation learning frameworks in terms of efficiency and policy accuracy. Conclusion/Implications: WAIL introduces a promising avenue for imitation learning by effectively mitigating mode collapse and training instabilities through the application of Wasserstein distances. The research presents compelling evidence that this method can be applied to a range of tasks requiring the replication of intricate behaviors, thereby broadening the scope and application of imitation learning in fields such as robotics, game playing, and autonomous systems. Future work may explore extending this method to non-stationary environments and scaling to higher-dimensional spaces. Keywords: Wasserstein, adversarial imitation learning, mode collapse, generative adversarial networks, policy learning, automation, robotics.

This paper proposes RON, a novel object detection framework that leverages Reverse Connection with Objectness Prior Networks. The objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of object detection by incorporating objectness priors into the detection process. Our approach utilizes a reverse connection mechanism to refine feature representations and an objectness prior network to guide the detection of objects. Experimental results demonstrate that RON outperforms state-of-the-art object detection models, achieving significant improvements in detection accuracy and speed. The key findings include the effectiveness of objectness priors in reducing false positives and improving detection recall. The proposed RON framework contributes to the field of computer vision by providing a robust and efficient object detection solution, with potential applications in autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics. By highlighting the importance of objectness priors and reverse connections, this research paves the way for future innovations in object detection, with relevant keywords including object detection, deep learning, computer vision, and objectness prior networks.

Đánh giá phân suất dự trữ lưu lượng động mạch vành bằng chụp cắt lớp vi tính (CT) đóng vai trò quan trọng trong chẩn đoán và quản lý bệnh lý tim mạch.
