Corn yield prediction is beneficial as it provides valuable information about production and prices prior the harvest. Publicly available high-quality corn yield prediction can help address emergent information asymmetry problems and in doing so improve price efficiency in futures markets. This paper is the first to employ Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), a special form of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) method to predict corn yields. A cross sectional time series of county-level corn yield and hourly weather data made the sample space large enough to use deep learning technics. LSTM is efficient in time series prediction with complex inner relations, which makes it suitable for this task. The empirical results from county level data in Iowa show promising predictive power relative to existing survey based methods.

Scene text detection is a critical task in computer vision, with applications ranging from document analysis to autonomous systems. Despite significant progress, real-time detection of text in complex scenes remains challenging due to variations in text size, orientation, and background clutter. This paper introduces STELA (Scene Text detector with LEarned Anchors), a novel real-time text detection framework designed to address these challenges. STELA leverages a lightweight neural network architecture combined with a dynamic anchor generation mechanism, which adaptively learns optimal anchor configurations for diverse text instances. The proposed approach eliminates the need for manually predefined anchors, enhancing detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including ICDAR2015 and MSRA-TD500, demonstrate that STELA achieves state-of-the-art performance with a detection speed of 45 FPS on a single GPU. Compared to existing methods, STELA improves precision by 3.2% and recall by 2.8% while reducing inference time by 20%. The results highlight the effectiveness of learned anchors in improving text localization and the framework's suitability for real-world applications. This work contributes to advancing real-time scene text detection by offering a robust, efficient, and scalable solution. **Keywords**: Scene text detection, real-time systems, learned anchors, computer vision, neural networks.

Recently proposed DNN-based stereo matching methods that learn priors directly from data are known to suffer a drastic drop in accuracy in new environments. Although supervised approaches with ground truth disparity maps often work well, collecting them in each deployment environment is cumbersome and costly. For this reason, many unsupervised domain adaptation methods based on image-to-image translation have been proposed, but these methods do not preserve the geometric structure of a stereo image pair because the image-to-image translation is applied to each view separately. To address this problem, in this paper, we propose an attention mechanism that aggregates features in the left and right views, called Stereoscopic Cross Attention (SCA). Incorporating SCA to an image-to-image translation network makes it possible to preserve the geometric structure of a stereo image pair in the process of the image-to-image translation. We empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed unsupervised domain adaptation based on the image-to-image translation with SCA.

Object detection frameworks heavily rely on accurate bounding box regression, which influences the overall precision and robustness of localization tasks. Traditional loss functions for bounding box regression, such as IoU loss and Smooth L1 loss, often fail to capture critical spatial relationships between predicted and ground-truth boxes, limiting the effectiveness of deep learning models. This paper introduces the Distance-IoU (DIoU) loss function, a novel approach that integrates both the overlap area and the spatial distance between the centers of bounding boxes, directly optimizing the location accuracy during training. The proposed DIoU loss offers a more comprehensive regression metric, enabling faster convergence and improved localization performance compared to conventional methods. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including COCO and PASCAL VOC, demonstrate that object detectors trained with DIoU loss achieve higher mean Average Precision (mAP) and reduced training times without additional computational overhead. Analysis shows that DIoU loss enhances the learning of bounding box geometry, particularly in crowded and overlapping scenarios. The findings highlight the potential of the DIoU loss to advance state-of-the-art object detection systems and inspire further development in bounding box optimization. Keywords: object detection, bounding box regression, Distance-IoU loss, deep learning, localization accuracy, computer vision.

Tối ưu hóa chiết polyphenol từ lá ổi bằng phương pháp bề mặt đáp ứng Một nhóm nghiên cứu đã thành công trong việc tối ưu hóa quá trình chiết polyphenol từ lá ổi bằng phương pháp bề mặt đáp ứng. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy phương pháp này có thể tăng cường hiệu suất chiết polyphenol lên đến 95%, vượt trội so với các phương pháp truyền thống. Polyphenol là một loại hợp chất tự nhiên có nhiều lợi ích cho sức khỏe, bao gồm chống oxy hóa, chống viêm và bảo vệ tim mạch. Lá ổi là một nguồn giàu polyphenol, nhưng quá trình chiết xuất thường gặp nhiều khó khăn. Phương pháp bề mặt đáp ứng được sử dụng trong nghiên cứu này là một kỹ thuật mới giúp tối ưu hóa quá trình chiết xuất. Kỹ thuật này sử dụng một bề mặt đặc biệt để tương tác với các hợp chất trong lá ổi, giúp tăng cường hiệu suất chiết xuất. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy phương pháp bề mặt đáp ứng có thể tăng cường hiệu suất chiết polyphenol từ lá ổi lên đến 95%, vượt trội so với các phương pháp truyền thống. Điều này cho thấy tiềm năng của phương pháp này trong việc sản xuất polyphenol từ lá ổi trên quy mô công nghiệp.

Truyện đồng thoại là một thể loại văn học truyền thống của Việt Nam, mang lại cho người đọc những bài học quý giá về cuộc sống và nhân cách. This paper presents a novel approach for accurately evaluating the depth of metal surface defects using Eddy Current Testing (ECT) combined with Deep Residual Convolutional Neural Networks (ResNet). The primary objective is to overcome limitations of traditional ECT methods, which struggle with complex defect characterization and are sensitive to noise and operator interpretation. Our method leverages a tailored ResNet architecture to automatically extract deep features from ECT signal data, enabling robust and precise defect depth estimation. An extensive dataset, comprising various metal samples with artificially induced defects of known depths, was collected and used to train and validate the proposed model. Experimental results demonstrate that our system significantly outperforms conventional signal processing techniques and standard convolutional neural networks in terms of depth prediction accuracy and generalization to unseen defect patterns. The findings reveal high correlation between predicted and actual defect depths, with notable resilience to measurement noise and variability in defect orientation. This work highlights the potential of integrating advanced deep learning frameworks, such as residual networks, into non-destructive testing workflows, paving the way for enhanced automation, reliability, and efficiency in industrial quality assurance. Key contributions include the development of a specialized deep residual model for ECT data interpretation, comprehensive comparative evaluation, and insights into practical deployment for metal defect assessment. Keywords: Eddy Current Testing, Deep Learning, Residual Networks, Metal Surface Defects, Defect Depth Evaluation, Non-Destructive Testing.

Weakly supervised object localization (WSOL) aims to identify object locations using only image-level labels. This paper introduces a novel Dual-Attention Guided DropBlock (DAG-DropBlock) module to enhance feature discrimination and localization accuracy in WSOL. The proposed module leverages both channel and spatial attention mechanisms to guide the DropBlock operation, adaptively dropping less relevant feature regions while preserving crucial object-related information. This approach encourages the network to attend to more discriminative parts for accurate localization. Experimental results on the benchmark datasets, including CUB-200-2011 and ImageNet, demonstrate that the DAG-DropBlock module significantly improves the localization performance compared to existing state-of-the-art WSOL methods. Furthermore, visualizations of attention maps confirm that our module facilitates a more accurate focus on object regions. Our approach offers a simple yet effective way to improve WSOL without requiring additional supervision, providing a promising direction for future research in weakly supervised learning. Keywords: Weakly Supervised Object Localization, Attention Mechanism, DropBlock, Deep Learning, Computer Vision.

This paper presents LSALSA, a novel framework for accelerated source separation through learned sparse coding techniques. The objective of this research is to address the computational inefficiencies and limitations in accuracy prevalent in traditional source separation methods, particularly in scenarios that demand real-time or large-scale data processing. LSALSA leverages deep neural networks to approximate the iterative processes of conventional sparse coding, enabling fast and efficient decomposition of mixed signals into their constituent sources. Our approach incorporates a learned inference model that adapts to the statistical structure of input data, yielding more accurate and interpretable source representations. Extensive experiments on benchmark audio and image datasets demonstrate that LSALSA achieves superior separation accuracy while significantly reducing computational time when compared to classical algorithms such as ISTA and FISTA. The results indicate up to a fivefold speedup with no loss in quality, and enhanced robustness to noise and signal variations. The proposed method holds promise for applications in audio processing, biomedical signal analysis, and image denoising, where efficient and reliable source separation is critical. By bridging traditional optimization with modern deep learning advancements, LSALSA establishes a new paradigm for fast, scalable, and adaptive source separation. Key keywords: source separation, sparse coding, deep learning, accelerated algorithms, learned inference, signal processing.

The primary objective of this research is to address the challenges inherent in fingerprint image segmentation, a critical step in biometric identification systems. Accurate segmentation is crucial for enhancing the quality and reliability of subsequent fingerprint recognition processes. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel filter design specifically tailored for segmenting fingerprint images. Our approach utilizes a hybrid algorithm combining spatial domain techniques with frequency domain analysis to effectively delineate fingerprint patterns from the background noise. The filter is designed to be adaptive, modifying its parameters based on the local characteristics of the fingerprint image to improve segmentation accuracy. Results/Findings: The performance of our filter was extensively evaluated against benchmark datasets and was compared with existing segmentation methods. Our findings indicate that the proposed filter consistently outperforms traditional approaches, achieving higher segmentation accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Quantitative metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 score were used to validate the effectiveness of our method. Conclusion/Implications: This study presents a significant advancement in fingerprint image segmentation, offering a robust tool that can enhance the performance of biometric systems. The proposed filter design not only improves the accuracy of segmentation but also has potential applications in real-time fingerprint recognition systems due to its efficient processing capability. Our work contributes to the field by providing a framework that can be further refined and adapted to other image segmentation challenges. Keywords: fingerprint image segmentation, filter design, biometric systems, adaptive algorithms, image processing.

Bố trí sử dụng đất của tỉnh Nam Định đang được điều chỉnh nhằm thích ứng với biến đổi khí hậu, một vấn đề ngày càng nghiêm trọng và ảnh hưởng sâu rộng đến môi trường và đời sống con người. Tỉnh Nam Định, với đặc điểm địa lý và khí hậu đặc thù, cần có những chiến lược cụ thể để quản lý và sử dụng đất hiệu quả hơn. Các biện pháp được đề xuất bao gồm việc quy hoạch lại các khu vực nông nghiệp, tăng cường trồng cây xanh, bảo vệ các vùng đất ngập nước và phát triển các mô hình canh tác bền vững. Đồng thời, việc nâng cao nhận thức cộng đồng về tầm quan trọng của việc bảo vệ môi trường cũng được nhấn mạnh. Những nỗ lực này không chỉ giúp giảm thiểu tác động của biến đổi khí hậu mà còn góp phần phát triển kinh tế bền vững cho tỉnh.

Dịch vụ hành chính công (DVC) đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc hiện thực hóa một chính phủ kiến tạo, phục vụ, hướng đến sự hài lòng của người dân và doanh nghiệp. Để đạt được mục tiêu này, việc cung cấp thông tin đầy đủ, chính xác và kịp thời về DVC là vô cùng quan trọng. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc xây dựng hệ thống hỏi đáp (Question Answering - QA) tự động, có khả năng giải đáp thắc mắc của người dùng liên quan đến các thủ tục hành chính. Hệ thống QA được xây dựng dựa trên kiến trúc transformer, một mô hình học sâu tiên tiến, cho phép xử lý ngôn ngữ tự nhiên một cách hiệu quả. Dữ liệu huấn luyện cho hệ thống bao gồm các câu hỏi thường gặp (FAQ) và các văn bản pháp quy liên quan đến DVC. Quá trình huấn luyện sử dụng kỹ thuật fine-tuning, giúp mô hình thích ứng với đặc thù của lĩnh vực hành chính công. Bên cạnh đó, nghiên cứu cũng đề xuất các phương pháp đánh giá hiệu năng của hệ thống QA, bao gồm độ chính xác, độ bao phủ và thời gian phản hồi. Kết quả thử nghiệm cho thấy hệ thống QA đạt được độ chính xác cao trong việc trả lời các câu hỏi về DVC, đồng thời cung cấp thông tin nhanh chóng và đầy đủ. Hệ thống QA này có tiềm năng lớn trong việc nâng cao chất lượng cung cấp DVC, giảm thiểu thời gian và chi phí cho cả người dân, doanh nghiệp và cơ quan nhà nước. Hơn nữa, hệ thống có thể được tích hợp vào các cổng thông tin điện tử, ứng dụng di động hoặc chatbot, tạo ra một kênh tương tác hiệu quả giữa chính quyền và người dân. Nghiên cứu cũng thảo luận về các thách thức và cơ hội trong việc triển khai hệ thống QA cho DVC, bao gồm vấn đề xử lý ngôn ngữ không chính thức, cập nhật thông tin thường xuyên và đảm bảo tính bảo mật của dữ liệu. Các hướng nghiên cứu tiếp theo có thể tập trung vào việc cải thiện khả năng hiểu ngữ cảnh của hệ thống, hỗ trợ đa ngôn ngữ và tích hợp các nguồn thông tin khác nhau.

An important task in data analysis is the discovery of causal relationships between observed variables. For continuous-valued data, linear acyclic causal models are commonly used to model the data-generating process, and the inference of such models is a well-studied problem. However, existing methods have significant limitations. Methods based on conditional independencies (Spirtes et al. 1993; Pearl 2000) cannot distinguish between independence-equivalent models, whereas approaches purely based on Independent Component Analysis (Shimizu et al. 2006) are inapplicable to data which is partially Gaussian. In this paper, we generalize and combine the two approaches, to yield a method able to learn the model structure in many cases for which the previous methods provide answers that are either incorrect or are not as informative as possible. We give exact graphical conditions for when two distinct models represent the same family of distributions, and empirically demonstrate the power of our method through thorough simulations.

This paper addresses the challenge of medical image segmentation using semi-supervised few-shot learning, aiming to improve the accuracy and efficiency of segmenting medical images with limited labeled data. Our approach combines the strengths of few-shot learning and semi-supervised learning to develop a robust model that can learn from a few labeled examples and a large number of unlabeled images. We propose a novel framework that utilizes a transformer-based architecture and a self-supervised loss function to effectively leverage the unlabeled data and adapt to new tasks with few labeled samples. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several medical image segmentation benchmarks. Our approach has significant implications for clinical applications, enabling accurate and efficient segmentation of medical images with minimal labeled data. Key contributions include the development of a semi-supervised few-shot learning framework for medical image segmentation, improved performance on benchmark datasets, and the potential for application in real-world clinical settings, highlighting the importance of keywords such as few-shot learning, semi-supervised learning, medical image segmentation, transformer, and self-supervised learning.

This paper addresses the critical issue of adversarial attacks on deep neural networks, aiming to enhance their robustness against such threats. Our objective is to develop a novel method to suppress channel-wise activations, thereby improving the resilience of neural networks to adversarial perturbations. We propose a new approach that utilizes a channel-wise activation suppressing technique, which selectively reduces the activation of sensitive channels to mitigate the impact of adversarial noise. Our method is based on a carefully designed loss function that encourages the network to produce more robust feature representations. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the adversarial robustness of state-of-the-art neural networks, outperforming existing defense methods. Key findings include a substantial reduction in the success rate of adversarial attacks and improved performance on benchmark datasets. Our research contributes to the development of more secure and reliable deep learning models, with potential applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and other fields where adversarial robustness is crucial. Keywords: adversarial robustness, deep neural networks, channel-wise activation, activation suppressing, computer vision, natural language processing.

This paper investigates the innovative integration of physical modeling techniques within active contour frameworks to enhance image segmentation processes. The study addresses the challenge of accurately and efficiently delineating object boundaries in digital images, which is crucial in various applications including medical imaging, computer vision, and remote sensing. Methods/Approach: Our approach involves the incorporation of physical modeling principles into the active contour model, traditionally used for non-rigid shape detection. We develop a novel methodology that applies mechanical properties of elasticity and surface tension to enhance the contour's adaptability and robustness in varying image contexts. Our algorithm leverages numerical simulation methods to adjust contour dynamics, targeting improved alignment with object boundaries while reducing computational complexity. Results/Findings: The experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in segmentation accuracy over conventional active contour models, particularly in images with varying contrast and noise levels. The proposed technique consistently outperformed classical models and recent algorithms in both quantitative metrics and visual assessment. The application of physical modeling yielded a higher degree of precision in edge localization, providing more reliable segmentation outputs. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes to the field by extending traditional active contour models with physical modeling concepts, offering a more versatile and effective tool for image segmentation. The integration of these techniques not only enhances segmentation quality but also expands the applicability of active contour models in complex image environments. Future work may explore further refinement of mechanical parameters and the extension of this framework to 3D image data. Keywords: active contours, image segmentation, physical modeling, elasticity, numerical simulation, edge detection.

The increasing demand for efficient neural network deployment on resource-constrained devices has driven the need for models that are both sparse and low-precision. However, existing methods often address sparsity and quantization separately, leading to suboptimal performance and increased complexity. This paper introduces **SQuantizer**, a novel framework that enables simultaneous learning of sparse and low-precision neural networks. The proposed approach integrates sparsity-inducing techniques with quantization-aware training, allowing for joint optimization of both objectives. SQuantizer employs a gradient-based optimization strategy to dynamically adjust the sparsity levels and quantization ranges during training, ensuring minimal loss in model accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SQuantizer achieves state-of-the-art performance, reducing model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy compared to traditional methods. The framework also shows significant improvements in inference speed and energy efficiency, making it highly suitable for edge computing and IoT applications. This work contributes a unified solution for deploying lightweight neural networks, bridging the gap between sparsity and quantization in modern deep learning systems. **Keywords**: neural networks, sparsity, quantization, model compression, edge computing, deep learning optimization.

This paper addresses the challenge of fine-grained image captioning, which aims to generate detailed and contextually relevant descriptions for complex images. Traditional methods often fail to capture intricate details, leading to generic captions that lack specificity. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel Global-Local Discriminative Objective that leverages both global and local image features. Our approach employs a two-tier neural network architecture, integrating attention mechanisms to prioritize salient features at varying scales. We evaluate our model on benchmark datasets and compare its performance against state-of-the-art captioning systems, demonstrating significant improvements in both descriptive accuracy and relevance. Results indicate that our model achieves a higher BLEU score and improved human evaluations, highlighting its effectiveness in generating fine-grained image captions. The findings suggest that incorporating a discriminative objective not only enhances the quality of generated captions but also offers potential applications in accessibility tools and content moderation systems. This work contributes to the field by providing a robust framework for fine-grained image understanding, setting a foundation for future advancements in multimodal AI applications. Keywords: fine-grained image captioning, global-local discriminative objective, neural networks, attention mechanism, multimodal AI.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently computing the 2D Least Median of Squares (LMedS) in the context of robust line detection. Traditional methods for LMedS are computationally expensive, making them impractical for real-time applications. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel GPU-based approach to significantly accelerate the computation of 2D LMedS. Our methodology leverages parallel processing capabilities inherent in modern Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) to perform large-scale data analysis using high-performance computing techniques. We incorporate optimized algorithms within this framework to enhance data throughput and minimize latency, enabling rapid processing of large datasets. The efficacy of the approach is validated through extensive empirical testing on various datasets, showing robust performance in line detection tasks. Our method not only retains high accuracy levels but also outperforms existing robust estimators regarding speed without compromising robustness. Conclusion/Implications: The findings suggest that our GPU-accelerated approach for LMedS is highly effective for applications requiring fast and robust line detection, such as in computer vision and image processing tasks. The use of GPU technology in this context provides a critical advancement, offering a scalable solution that can be adapted to other computational-heavy robust statistical estimators. Our work lays the groundwork for future developments in the efficient processing of robust statistical techniques, contributing significantly to the fields of computer vision and machine learning. Keywords: GPU computing, 2D Least Median of Squares, LMedS, robust line detection, high-performance computing, parallel processing, real-time applications.

This paper introduces a novel Deep Bayesian Unsupervised Lifelong Learning (DBULL) framework designed to address catastrophic forgetting and enhance knowledge transfer in continually learning environments. DBULL leverages a deep neural network architecture integrated with Bayesian nonparametrics to dynamically expand model capacity and infer task-specific latent representations without supervision. Our approach utilizes a hierarchical Dirichlet process mixture model to cluster data streams and adaptively allocate network resources to new tasks. This facilitates the preservation of previously learned knowledge while effectively learning new information. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DBULL significantly outperforms existing unsupervised lifelong learning methods in terms of both accuracy and forgetting rate. Furthermore, the Bayesian formulation provides inherent uncertainty estimation, enhancing the robustness of the learning process. The DBULL framework offers a promising direction for developing intelligent systems capable of autonomously learning and adapting in dynamic and evolving environments. Keywords: Lifelong Learning, Unsupervised Learning, Bayesian Nonparametrics, Deep Learning, Catastrophic Forgetting, Knowledge Transfer.

Age estimation from a single face image has been an essential task in the field of human-computer interaction and computer vision, which has a wide range of practical application values. Accuracy of age estimation of face images in the wild is relatively low for existing methods, because they only take into account the global features, while neglecting the fine-grained features of age-sensitive areas. We propose a novel method based on our attention long short-term memory (AL) network for fine-grained age estimation in the wild, inspired by the fine-grained categories and the visual attention mechanism. This method combines the residual networks (ResNets) or the residual network of residual network (RoR) models with LSTM units to construct AL-ResNets or AL-RoR networks to extract local features of age-sensitive regions, which effectively improves the age estimation accuracy. First, a ResNets or a RoR model pretrained on ImageNet dataset is selected as the basic model, which is then fine-tuned on the IMDB-WIKI-101 dataset for age estimation. Then, we fine-tune the ResNets or the RoR on the target age datasets to extract the global features of face images. To extract the local features of age-sensitive regions, the LSTM unit is then presented to obtain the coordinates of the agesensitive region automatically. Finally, the age group classification is conducted directly on the Adience dataset, and age-regression experiments are performed by the Deep EXpectation algorithm (DEX) on MORPH Album 2, FG-NET and 15/16LAP datasets. By combining the global and the local features, we obtain our final prediction results. Experimental results illustrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed AL-ResNets or AL-RoR for age estimation in the wild, where it achieves better state-of-the-art performance than all other convolutional neural network.

Các yếu tố được nghiên cứu bao gồm: - Yếu tố kinh tế: chi phí đầu tư, lợi nhuận dự kiến, cơ hội đầu tư khác. - Yếu tố xã hội: nhu cầu của cộng đồng, sự ủng hộ của người dân. - Yếu tố môi trường: tác động môi trường của dự án, sự phù hợp với chiến lược phát triển bền vững. - Yếu tố kỹ thuật: tính khả thi của dự án, khả năng thực hiện. Detecting small objects in thermal images presents a significant challenge due to low resolution, noise, and limited feature information. This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance small object detection in thermal imagery using a modified Single-Shot Detector (SSD) architecture. Our method incorporates a feature enhancement module based on adaptive spatial attention to amplify relevant object features while suppressing background noise. Furthermore, we employ a multi-scale feature fusion strategy to effectively integrate information from different feature map levels, improving the detector's ability to recognize small, indistinct objects. Experimental results on a challenging thermal image dataset demonstrate that our proposed approach significantly outperforms the standard SSD and other state-of-the-art object detection methods, achieving a 15% improvement in average precision for small objects. The proposed method offers a robust and efficient solution for real-time applications such as surveillance, search and rescue, and autonomous navigation in low-visibility environments. Keywords: Thermal Imaging, Object Detection, Single-Shot Detector, Small Object Detection, Feature Enhancement, Spatial Attention.

The research addresses the challenge of few-shot object detection (FSOD), where the goal is to detect objects from novel categories with only a limited number of annotated examples. This is particularly important for applications where data collection and annotation are resource-intensive. Methods: We propose a novel framework termed Dense Relation Distillation with Context-aware Aggregation (DRD-CA) to enhance FSOD. The approach leverages a dense relation distillation mechanism to effectively transfer knowledge from base classes to novel classes and utilizes context-aware aggregation to enhance feature representation. This method ensures more robust and discriminative feature extraction, allowing for improved object detection performance even with minimal training data. Results: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DRD-CA framework significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art FSOD methods, achieving higher detection accuracy across various benchmark datasets. The dense relation distillation component consistently improves the adaptability of detection models to new classes, while the context-aware aggregation enhances the discriminability of features extracted from few-shot samples. Conclusion: The DRD-CA framework sets a new benchmark in FSOD by effectively addressing the challenges associated with limited training data and novel class detection. Our approach not only contributes to the theoretical advancement of object detection methodologies but also opens up practical applications in fields where rapid adaptation to new classes is essential, such as autonomous driving and robotics. Keywords: few-shot object detection, dense relation distillation, context-aware aggregation, feature representation, novel category detection.

The efficient management of inventory rotation is crucial for minimizing spoilage, obsolescence, and ultimately, maximizing profitability in logistics warehouses. Traditional inventory management methods often struggle with accurately tracking and prioritizing goods for optimal rotation, leading to inefficiencies and losses. This thesis addresses the problem by proposing and implementing an RFID-based automated inventory system designed to enhance inventory rotation in logistics warehouses. The primary objective is to develop a system that accurately identifies, tracks, and prioritizes inventory based on expiration dates or other relevant criteria, ensuring First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) or First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principles are effectively implemented. The methodology involves deploying RFID tags on individual inventory items, strategically placing RFID readers throughout the warehouse, and developing a software application that processes the RFID data. The system architecture integrates real-time inventory tracking, data analytics, and automated alerts to facilitate optimized picking and put-away processes. We utilize a database management system for storing and managing inventory information, linked to an intuitive user interface for monitoring and controlling inventory rotation. The achieved outcome is a working prototype that demonstrates accurate and real-time inventory tracking, automated identification of expiring items, and optimized picking suggestions. The system significantly reduces manual inventory checks, minimizes the risk of human error, and improves the efficiency of inventory rotation. The expected contributions of this research include a practical framework for implementing RFID technology in logistics warehouses, a tangible reduction in waste due to expired or obsolete inventory, and improved overall operational efficiency. In conclusion, this thesis demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of utilizing RFID technology to automate inventory rotation in logistics warehouses. The developed system offers a valuable solution for companies seeking to optimize their inventory management practices and minimize waste. Future research could focus on integrating this system with existing warehouse management systems (WMS), exploring the use of advanced analytics for predictive inventory management, and investigating the scalability and cost-effectiveness of implementing the system in larger, more complex warehouse environments.

Nghiên cứu về tuyến trùng ký sinh trên cây Lan hài đài cuốn Paphiopedilum appletonianum (Gower) đã chỉ ra sự hiện diện của nhiều loài tuyến trùng gây hại, ảnh hưởng đến sự phát triển và sức khỏe của cây. Các mẫu cây được thu thập từ nhiều địa điểm khác nhau, cho thấy sự đa dạng về loài tuyến trùng ký sinh. Smart homes offer enhanced living experiences through automated services, but their reliance on activity recognition systems often lacks transparency, hindering user trust and acceptance. This paper addresses the challenge of explainability in activity recognition within smart home environments. We propose a novel framework that integrates a hybrid deep learning model, combining convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks, with a rule-based explanation module. The deep learning component accurately identifies activities from sensor data, while the rule-based module generates human-readable explanations for the system's decisions. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art activity recognition accuracy and provides meaningful explanations with high fidelity. User studies confirm that the generated explanations significantly improve user understanding and trust in the smart home system. Our research contributes to the development of transparent and reliable smart home technologies, facilitating wider adoption and user engagement. Keywords: Activity Recognition, Explainable AI, Smart Homes, Deep Learning, Sensor Data, Human-Computer Interaction.

This paper investigates the quantitative impact of incorporating domain knowledge into machine learning models. Our objective is to provide a measurable understanding of how domain-specific information influences model performance across diverse tasks. We introduce a novel framework that quantifies domain knowledge using information-theoretic measures and integrates it into various machine learning algorithms, including decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks. The approach involves transforming expert-elicited domain rules into quantifiable features and assessing their contribution to predictive accuracy, model complexity, and generalization ability. Experimental results across several benchmark datasets and real-world applications demonstrate that strategic incorporation of domain knowledge consistently improves model performance, especially in scenarios with limited data or high noise. We observe a direct correlation between the quality and relevance of domain knowledge and the resulting performance gains. Our findings provide a practical methodology for leveraging domain expertise to enhance machine learning models, offering valuable insights for researchers and practitioners seeking to optimize model development. Keywords: Domain knowledge, Machine learning, Knowledge integration, Quantitative analysis, Information theory, Model performance.

Objective: Predicting imminent human-object interactions in first-person video is critical for applications in augmented reality, assistive robotics, and human–machine collaboration. Existing methods often treat action forecasting and attention modeling separately, limiting their ability to anticipate fine-grained hand–object dynamics. Methods: We propose a unified deep learning framework that jointly predicts motor attention—defined as gaze-informed hand trajectories—and subsequent action labels from egocentric video. Our model employs a shared convolutional backbone to extract spatio-temporal features, followed by two task-specific heads: (1) a motor-attention module that generates heatmaps of likely hand–object contact regions using a recurrent spatial attention mechanism; (2) an action-forecasting branch that integrates these attention cues with global motion representations to predict the next interaction class. We train the network end-to-end with a composite loss combining attention-map regression and cross-entropy action loss. Results: Experiments on two benchmark egocentric datasets demonstrate that joint learning of attention and action leads to significant gains: our approach achieves up to 18% relative improvement in early action prediction accuracy and a 22% reduction in attention-map error compared to single-task baselines. Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of shared features and cross-task attention fusion. Conclusion: By coupling motor attention forecasting with action prediction, our method delivers more reliable and interpretable forecasts of human–object interactions. This joint approach opens new avenues for responsive assistive systems and interactive AR interfaces. Keywords: motor attention, action forecasting, first-person video, human–object interaction, multi-task learning, deep neural networks.

Reconstruction of seismic data with missing traces is a long-standing issue in seismic data processing. In recent years, rank reduction operations are being commonly utilized to overcome this problem, which require the rank of seismic data to be a prior. However, the rank of field data is unknown; usually it requires much time to manually adjust the rank and just obtain an approximated rank. Methods based on deep learning require very large datasets for training; however acquiring large datasets is difficult owing to physical or financial constraints in practice. Therefore, in this work, we developed a novel method based on unsupervised learning using the intrinsic properties of a convolutional neural network known as U-net, without training datasets. Only one undersampled seismic data was needed, and the deep seismic prior of input data could be exploited by the network itself, thus making the reconstruction convenient. Furthermore, this method can handle both irregular and regular seismic data. Synthetic and field data were tested to assess the performance of the proposed algorithm (DSPRecon algorithm); the advantages of using our method were evaluated by comparing it with the singular spectrum analysis (SSA) method for irregular data reconstruction and de-aliased Cadzow method for regular data reconstruction. Experimental results showed that our method provided better reconstruction performance than the SSA or Cadzow methods. The recovered signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) were 32.68 dB and 19.11 dB for the DSPRecon and SSA algorithms, respectively. Those for the DSPRecon and Cadzow methods were 35.91 dB and 15.32 dB, respectively.

This paper introduces a novel approach for automatic classification of phantom test patterns, crucial for quality assurance in medical imaging. Our objective is to improve the efficiency and accuracy of identifying these patterns, replacing manual inspection methods. We leverage transfer learning with deep convolutional neural networks, adapting pre-trained models to classify various phantom test patterns. Specifically, we fine-tune models such as ResNet and EfficientNet on a dataset of phantom images, exploring different fine-tuning strategies. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves significantly higher accuracy compared to traditional image processing techniques, with an average classification accuracy exceeding 95%. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits robustness to noise and variations in image acquisition parameters. The automated classification framework offers a practical solution for enhancing quality control workflows in medical imaging, reducing the reliance on manual analysis and improving diagnostic reliability. Keywords: Phantom test patterns, medical imaging, transfer learning, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, automatic classification, quality assurance.

We introduce a family of multilayer graph kernels and establish new links between graph convolutional neural networks and kernel methods. Our approach generalizes convolutional kernel networks to graph-structured data, by representing graphs as a sequence of kernel feature maps, where each node carries information about local graph substructures. On the one hand, the kernel point of view offers an unsupervised, expressive, and easy-to-regularize data representation, which is useful when limited samples are available. On the other hand, our model can also be trained end-to-end on large-scale data, leading to new types of graph convolutional neural networks. We show that our method achieves competitive performance on several graph classification benchmarks, while offering simple model interpretation. Our code is freely available at https://github.com/claying/GCKN.

Change captioning, the task of generating textual descriptions of differences between two images, presents a significant challenge in computer vision and natural language processing. This paper introduces a novel Viewpoint-Adapted Matching Encoder (VAME) designed to address the limitations of existing methods in handling viewpoint variations and fine-grained changes. The proposed approach leverages a dual-branch architecture to encode image pairs, incorporating a viewpoint adaptation mechanism that dynamically aligns features across different perspectives. By integrating a cross-attention module, VAME effectively captures subtle visual differences and generates accurate, context-aware captions. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that VAME outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior performance in both accuracy and robustness. The results highlight the model's ability to generalize across diverse scenarios, making it a promising solution for applications such as surveillance, robotics, and automated reporting. This work contributes a significant advancement in change captioning by addressing viewpoint challenges and enhancing the interpretability of visual changes. **Keywords**: change captioning, viewpoint adaptation, cross-attention, image-text matching, computer vision, natural language processing.

Human Activity Recognition (HAR) has gained significant attention due to its applications in healthcare, fitness tracking, and smart environments. However, the lack of comprehensive datasets incorporating multi-modal sensor data limits the development of robust and generalizable models. This paper introduces **MEx**, a novel multi-modal dataset designed to advance research in HAR. MEx integrates data from wearable sensors, cameras, and environmental sensors, capturing a wide range of physical exercises performed by diverse participants in real-world settings. To construct MEx, we employed a systematic data collection protocol, ensuring high-quality annotations and synchronization across modalities. We propose a multi-modal fusion framework leveraging deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), to effectively combine and analyze heterogeneous data streams. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming single-modal approaches by 12.3% in accuracy and 15.7% in F1-score. The MEx dataset and our fusion framework provide a foundation for future research in multi-modal HAR, enabling the development of more accurate and adaptive systems. The dataset is publicly available, fostering collaboration and innovation in the field. This work contributes to the growing body of research on multi-modal sensing and highlights the importance of diverse data sources for improving activity recognition systems. **Keywords**: Human Activity Recognition, Multi-modal Dataset, Wearable Sensors, Deep Learning, Sensor Fusion, MEx.

**Abstract** Image-to-image translation seeks to convert an input image from one domain into a corresponding image in another domain while preserving essential structural details. Traditional approaches often struggle to maintain both style consistency and content integrity, particularly when bridging domains with significant appearance discrepancies. In this work, we propose a novel group-wise deep whitening-and-coloring transformation (GDWCT) framework to enhance image-to-image translation tasks. By integrating group-wise feature processing into the deep whitening-and-coloring transformation pipeline, our approach effectively aligns feature distributions between source and target domains at multiple semantic levels. We implement GDWCT within an end-to-end neural network architecture, facilitating flexible feature manipulation without manual crafting or domain-specific heuristics. Experimental evaluations on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior translation quality compared to existing baselines, delivering images with improved fidelity, style adaptation, and reduced visual artifacts. Notably, GDWCT consistently outperforms standard whitening-and-coloring networks by offering more granular and robust feature alignment. Our findings suggest that group-wise transformation is a promising strategy for diverse image-to-image translation applications, including style transfer, domain adaptation, and conditional image synthesis. **Keywords:** image-to-image translation, deep learning, whitening-and-coloring transformation, feature alignment, style transfer, group-wise processing, generative models

Recent works found that fine-tuning and joint training---two popular approaches for transfer learning---do not always improve accuracy on downstream tasks. First, we aim to understand more about when and why fine-tuning and joint training can be suboptimal or even harmful for transfer learning. We design semi-synthetic datasets where the source task can be solved by either source-specific features or transferable features. We observe that (1) pre-training may not have incentive to learn transferable features and (2) joint training may simultaneously learn source-specific features and overfit to the target. Second, to improve over fine-tuning and joint training, we propose Meta Representation Learning (MeRLin) to learn transferable features. MeRLin meta-learns representations by ensuring that a head fit on top of the representations with target training data also performs well on target validation data. We also prove that MeRLin recovers the target ground-truth model with a quadratic neural net parameterization and a source distribution that contains both transferable and source-specific features. On the same distribution, pre-training and joint training provably fail to learn transferable features. MeRLin empirically outperforms previous state-of-the-art transfer learning algorithms on various real-world vision and NLP transfer learning benchmarks.

This paper introduces MADE, a novel exploration method for reinforcement learning environments that focuses on maximizing deviation from previously explored regions. Traditional exploration techniques often suffer from insufficient coverage of the state space, leading to suboptimal policy learning and poor generalization. MADE addresses this challenge by dynamically modeling the agent's exploration history and explicitly encouraging policies that venture into state-action spaces with high deviation from past trajectories. The proposed approach leverages a statistical deviation metric computed over sampled features, enabling scalable and adaptive exploration in both discrete and continuous domains. Experimental evaluations across a variety of benchmark environments demonstrate that MADE consistently achieves superior exploration efficiency compared to widely used methods such as epsilon-greedy, intrinsic curiosity, and count-based exploration. The results show significant improvements in cumulative reward, sample efficiency, and discovery of novel states, particularly in sparse-reward or deceptive environments. In conclusion, MADE provides a robust and generalizable exploration strategy, offering substantial advancements for reinforcement learning agents in complex and high-dimensional tasks. Key keywords: Reinforcement learning, exploration, state space, deviation maximization, sample efficiency, sparse reward.

Thời vụ đốn nuôi hom, bón phân và tỉa cành là những yếu tố quan trọng ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến năng suất hom giống Sở cam. Nghiên cứu cho thấy, việc đốn nuôi hom vào thời điểm thích hợp trong năm giúp cây phát triển mạnh mẽ, đồng thời tăng khả năng ra rễ của hom. Bón phân cân đối, đặc biệt là phân hữu cơ và phân khoáng, không chỉ cải thiện chất lượng đất mà còn thúc đẩy quá trình sinh trưởng của cây. Tỉa cành hợp lý giúp cây tập trung dinh dưỡng vào các cành chính, từ đó nâng cao năng suất và chất lượng hom giống. Kết hợp đồng bộ các biện pháp này sẽ mang lại hiệu quả tối ưu trong việc nhân giống và phát triển cây Sở cam.

Lúa lai hai dòng đã và đang đư ợc nghiên c ứu chọn tạo và phát tri ển ở Việt Nam. Đ ến năm 2013, có 11 gi ống lúa lai hai dòng được công nh ận giống. Dòng m ẹ của các gi ống lúa lai hai dòng này đều là dòng b ất dục đực di truyền nhân m ẫn cảm nhi ệt độ (TGMS). M ột số dòng TGMS trên được chúng tôi l ựa chọn để đánh giá đ ặc điểm nông sinh h ọc và xác đ ịnh gen đi ều khi ển tính m ẫn cảm với nhiệt độ (tms). Kết quả đánh giá cho thấy các dòng TGMS có th ời gian sinh trư ởng trong v ụ xuân bi ến động từ 140-163 ngày, có s ố lá trên thân chính t ừ 14-16 lá, cây thấp (62,2 - 84,6cm), bông dài trung bình (19,5 -25,8cm), lá đ òng ng ắn, trỗ nghẹn, có ki ểu đẻ nhánh g ọn hoặc chụm, tỷ lệ vươn v òi nhụy rất cao, th ời gian n ở hoa trên bông khá dài (4 -10 ngày), có s ố hạt trên bông khác cao (168,8 - 208,8 h ạt), kh ối lượng 1.000 h ạt của các dòng bi ến động từ 19,3-26,2g. T ất cả 16 dòng TGMS hi ện đang s ử dụng ở Việt Nam đ ều mang gen tms5 , duy nh ất có dòng 82 7S đồng th ời mang 2 gen là tms4 và tms5 .

Cắt lớp vi tính (CT) là một kỹ thuật hình ảnh không xâm lấn giúp tạo ra hình ảnh chi tiết của các cơ quan trong cơ thể. Khi áp dụng CT để quan sát lao ống tiêu hóa dưới cơ hoành, các bác sĩ có thể nhận biết được các đặc điểm hình ảnh quan trọng. Trên hình ảnh CT, lao ống tiêu hóa dưới cơ hoành thường xuất hiện dưới dạng một hình dạng bất thường, có thể là một hình oval hoặc hình chữ nhật. Lao ống tiêu hóa có thể có kích thước khác nhau, từ nhỏ đến lớn, và có thể nằm ở vị trí khác nhau trong dạ dày hoặc ruột non. Các đặc điểm hình ảnh khác của lao ống tiêu hóa dưới cơ hoành bao gồm sự thay đổi hình dạng của ống tiêu hóa, sự hiện diện của các mảnh vỡ hoặc các vật thể lạ trong ống tiêu hóa, và sự thay đổi của các lớp mô xung quanh ống tiêu hóa. Các bác sĩ có thể sử dụng hình ảnh CT để đánh giá mức độ nghiêm trọng của lao ống tiêu hóa và đưa ra quyết định điều trị phù hợp.

Text generation models have made significant strides in producing coherent and contextually relevant outputs. However, achieving a balance between diversity and quality remains a critical challenge. This paper addresses the problem of jointly measuring diversity and quality in text generation models, aiming to provide a unified framework for evaluating their performance. We propose a novel evaluation metric that integrates both aspects, leveraging advanced natural language processing techniques to assess the richness of generated text while maintaining high linguistic and semantic quality. Our approach combines entropy-based diversity measures with quality metrics such as fluency, relevance, and coherence. Experiments conducted on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in capturing the trade-offs between diversity and quality, outperforming existing evaluation frameworks. The results highlight the importance of a balanced evaluation for improving text generation models, offering insights for future research and applications in areas such as conversational AI, content creation, and machine translation. This work contributes a robust and interpretable tool for researchers and practitioners to better understand and optimize text generation systems. **Keywords**: text generation, diversity, quality, evaluation metrics, natural language processing, AI models.

**Abstract:** Detecting and recognizing traffic signs accurately is essential for developing advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous vehicles, contributing significantly to road safety and intelligent transportation. This paper presents a deep learning-based system for efficient traffic sign detection and recognition, addressing challenges posed by varying lighting, orientations, occlusions, and environmental conditions. The proposed system employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, combining state-of-the-art object detection models, such as YOLO (You Only Look Once), with a robust classification network. Extensive experiments were conducted on publicly available traffic sign datasets, demonstrating the system’s ability to achieve high detection precision and recognition accuracy, outperforming traditional machine learning methods and previously reported deep learning models. The end-to-end solution allows for real-time processing, making it suitable for deployment in embedded automotive platforms. The study not only highlights the improvements in feature extraction and classification but also discusses the scalability and generalization of the model across diverse sign types and road scenarios. The findings indicate the proposed deep learning framework’s potential for integration into practical transportation systems, paving the way for enhanced road safety and reliable autonomous vehicle navigation. **Keywords:** Traffic sign detection, traffic sign recognition, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, object detection, autonomous vehicles, ADAS.

In machine learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been extremely influential in both computer vision and in recognizing patterns extended over time. In computer vision, part of the flexibility arises from the use of max-pooling operations over the convolutions to attain translation invariance. In the mammalian brain, neural representations of time use a set of temporal basis functions. Critically, these basis functions appear to be arranged in a geometric series such that the basis set is evenly distributed over logarithmic time. This paper introduces a Scale-Invariant Temporal History Convolution network (SITHCon) that uses a logarithmically-distributed temporal memory. A max-pool over a logarithmically-distributed temporal memory results in scale-invariance in time. We compare performance of SITHCon to a Temporal Convolution Network (TCN) and demonstrate that, although both networks can learn classification and regression problems on both univariate and multivariate time series f(t), only SITHCon has the property that it generalizes without retraining to rescaled versions of the input f(at). This property, inspired by findings from neuroscience and psychology, could lead to large-scale networks with dramatically different capabilities, including faster training and greater generalizability, even with significantly fewer free parameters.

Joint forecasting of human trajectory and pose dynamics is a fundamental building block of various applications ranging from robotics and autonomous driving to surveillance systems. Predicting body dynamics requires capturing subtle information embedded in the humans' interactions with each other and with the objects present in the scene. In this paper, we propose a novel TRajectory and POse Dynamics (nicknamed TRiPOD) method based on graph attentional networks to model the human-human and human-object interactions both in the input space and the output space (decoded future output). The model is supplemented by a message passing interface over the graphs to fuse these different levels of interactions efficiently. Furthermore, to incorporate a real-world challenge, we propound to learn an indicator representing whether an estimated body joint is visible/invisible at each frame, e.g. due to occlusion or being outside the sensor field of view. Finally, we introduce a new benchmark for this joint task based on two challenging datasets (PoseTrack and 3DPW) and propose evaluation metrics to measure the effectiveness of predictions in the global space, even when there are invisible cases of joints. Our evaluation shows that TRiPOD outperforms all prior work and state-of-the-art specifically designed for each of the trajectory and pose forecasting tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach to 6D pose estimation by introducing the Multi-View Matching Network, developed to enhance accuracy and reliability in spatial perception tasks essential for robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous systems. Traditional methods often struggle with varied viewpoints and complex environments, prompting the need for a more robust solution. Methods/Approach: Our proposed Multi-View Matching Network (MVMNet) integrates a multi-view feature extraction mechanism with an attention-based matching module. By leveraging deep learning architectures, the network processes information from multiple viewpoints simultaneously, optimizing pose estimation performance. A novel alignment loss function is employed to refine the estimated poses, minimizing error margins and improving overall precision. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that MVMNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on standard 6D pose estimation benchmarks. The network achieves significant improvements in accuracy, especially in scenarios with occlusions and cluttered scenes. Comparative analysis indicates substantial reduction in pose estimation errors, highlighting the effectiveness of our multi-view strategy over conventional single-view techniques. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of the Multi-View Matching Network marks a significant advancement in 6D pose estimation, offering new possibilities for applications requiring precise spatial understanding. The approach's robustness in handling complex real-world conditions enhances its suitability for integration into advanced machine vision systems. Future research could explore scaling this framework for broader object categories and more dynamic environments. Keywords: 6D Pose Estimation, Multi-View Matching, Deep Learning, Attention Mechanism, Spatial Perception, Robotics, Augmented Reality, Autonomous Systems.

This research addresses the inefficiencies of traditional optimization methods in large-scale neural network training, specifically focusing on the limited application of natural gradient descent due to its computational complexity. The study aims to accelerate natural gradient methods by incorporating higher-order invariance, thereby optimizing convergence rates and reducing computational overhead. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach that leverages higher-order geometric structures within the parameter space. This technique enhances the natural gradient algorithm by incorporating second-order invariance principles, which allow for more accurate updates in deep learning models without the need for computing and inverting large Fisher Information matrices directly. Our model integrates efficient approximations and novel matrix factorization techniques to maintain computational tractability. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our enhanced natural gradient method significantly improves convergence speed compared to traditional first-order optimizers and existing second-order methods. Benchmarks conducted on various neural network architectures, including convolutional and transformer models, reveal performance gains in both training time and model generalization. The proposed method requires less computational resources while still achieving comparable or superior predictive accuracy. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of higher-order invariance into natural gradient methods represents a substantial advancement in optimizing deep learning models. This approach not only contributes to theoretical understanding but also offers practical benefits for real-world applications involving large neural networks. The findings suggest potential applications in areas where model efficiency and rapid convergence are critical, such as autonomous systems, real-time processing, and extensive data analysis. Keywords: natural gradient, higher-order invariance, optimization, neural networks, convergence, deep learning, Fisher Information, computational efficiency.

This paper proposes a novel block-based Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) approach to matrix factorization for recommender systems. The objective is to improve the efficiency and accuracy of recommendation algorithms by leveraging the block-based SVD method. Our approach involves dividing the large user-item interaction matrix into smaller blocks, applying SVD to each block, and then combining the results to obtain the factorized matrices. We utilize a hybrid strategy that integrates the benefits of both block-based processing and SVD to reduce computational complexity and enhance recommendation accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that our block-based SVD approach outperforms traditional SVD-based methods in terms of computational efficiency and recommendation quality, particularly in scenarios with large-scale user-item interaction matrices. The key contributions of this research include the development of a scalable and efficient matrix factorization technique, which can be applied to various recommender systems, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in improving recommendation accuracy and reducing computational overhead. Our approach has significant implications for the development of personalized recommendation systems, and its applications can be extended to various domains, including e-commerce, social media, and content streaming services. Key keywords: Singular Value Decomposition, matrix factorization, recommender systems, block-based processing, personalized recommendations, scalable algorithms.

Many historical people are captured only in old, faded, black and white photos, that have been distorted by the limitations of early cameras and the passage of time. This paper simulates traveling back in time with a modern camera to rephotograph famous subjects. Unlike conventional image restoration filters which apply independent operations like denoising, colorization, and superresolution, we leverage the StyleGAN2 framework to project old photos into the space of modern high-resolution photos, achieving all of these effects in a unified framework. A unique challenge with this approach is capturing the identity and pose of the photo's subject and not the many artifacts in low-quality antique photos. Our comparisons to current state-of-the-art restoration filters show significant improvements and compelling results for a variety of important historical people.

Event-based vision offers advantages over traditional frame-based cameras in high-speed and high dynamic range scenarios. This paper presents a novel moving object detection method tailored for event-based data using k-means clustering. Our approach leverages the asynchronous stream of events generated by moving objects to create spatiotemporal event clusters, which are then processed using k-means to differentiate between foreground and background events. By adapting k-means to the unique characteristics of event data, we achieve robust object detection without relying on explicit frame reconstruction. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance in terms of accuracy and processing speed compared to existing event-based moving object detection algorithms. The proposed method offers a computationally efficient solution for real-time applications such as autonomous navigation and surveillance. Keywords: Event-based vision, moving object detection, k-means clustering, neuromorphic vision, asynchronous events.

The existence condition for universal cycles in this particular context remains an open problem, largely because it is impossible to explicitly define the transition graph for n k. This difficulty arises from the unique property that every k-set is allowed to appear in any of the k! possible orders, yet can only occur once throughout the cycle. Fan Chung and Graham have put forth a conjecture that addresses this intriguing challenge, and there is currently a prize on offer for whoever is able to produce the first definitive solution to this longstanding mathematical question.

Đặt vấn đề: Chậm và không xuất tinh (XT) là rối loạn tình dục ít gặp (1 - 4% nam giới), tác động tiêu cực trên đời sống tinh thần và tình dục của cả nam lẫn nữ, và có thể gây hiếm muộn. Chúng tôi trình bày 1 trường hợp hiếm muộn do không XT và tổng quan y văn về hiếm muộn nam liên quan đến chậm và không XT. Bệnh án lâm sàng: BN nam sinh năm 1991, lập gia đình 12/2018, không thể XT và đạt đỉnh khoái cảm khi quan hệ tình dục (2 - 3 lần/tuần) dù có thể duy trì cương kéo dài. Sleep staging is a crucial task for diagnosing sleep disorders. It is tedious and complex as it can take a trained expert several hours to annotate just one patient's polysomnogram (PSG) from a single night. Although deep learning models have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in automating sleep staging, interpretability which defines other desiderata, has largely remained unexplored. In this study, we propose Sleep staging via Prototypes from Expert Rules (SLEEPER), which combines deep learning models with expert defined rules using a prototype learning framework to generate simple interpretable models. In particular, SLEEPER utilizes sleep scoring rules and expert defined features to derive prototypes which are embeddings of PSG data fragments via convolutional neural networks. The final models are simple interpretable models like a shallow decision tree defined over those phenotypes. We evaluated SLEEPER using two PSG datasets collected from sleep studies and demonstrated that SLEEPER could provide accurate sleep stage classification comparable to human experts and deep neural networks with about 85% ROC-AUC and .7 kappa.

The rapid advancement of deep learning techniques has led to the proliferation of realistic video face manipulation, raising significant concerns about misinformation and digital security. This paper addresses the critical challenge of detecting manipulated faces in videos by proposing an ensemble-based approach leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The objective is to enhance detection accuracy and robustness across diverse manipulation techniques, including deepfakes and face swaps. Our method integrates multiple CNN architectures, each trained on distinct feature representations, to capture subtle artifacts and inconsistencies introduced during manipulation. The ensemble framework combines the outputs of these models using a weighted voting mechanism, ensuring improved generalization and reduced false positives. Experiments were conducted on benchmark datasets, including FaceForensics++ and Celeb-DF, demonstrating that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance with an accuracy of 98.2% and a low false acceptance rate. The results highlight the effectiveness of the ensemble strategy in identifying manipulated content, even under challenging conditions such as compression and varying video quality. This research contributes to the field of digital forensics by providing a reliable and scalable solution for video face manipulation detection, with potential applications in media integrity verification, cybersecurity, and law enforcement. **Keywords**: Video face manipulation, deepfake detection, ensemble learning, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), digital forensics, media integrity.

This paper addresses the challenge of effectively fusing multimodal data, such as text, images, and audio, to improve the performance of deep learning models. Our objective is to develop a novel approach that efficiently integrates multiple modalities while minimizing computational overhead. We propose Attention Bottlenecks, a lightweight and flexible framework that leverages attention mechanisms to selectively focus on relevant modalities and filter out redundant information. Our approach is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in multimodal fusion tasks, such as visual question answering and sentiment analysis. The results show that Attention Bottlenecks achieve state-of-the-art performance while reducing computational costs by up to 30%. Our research contributes to the development of more efficient and effective multimodal fusion methods, with potential applications in areas like human-computer interaction, multimedia analysis, and decision support systems. Key keywords: multimodal fusion, attention mechanisms, deep learning, efficient computing, multimodal processing.

This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing battery energy storage system (BESS) dispatch in dynamic energy markets, where traditional rule-based and model-based approaches often struggle to adapt to real-time uncertainties. We propose a novel hybrid framework that combines reinforcement learning (RL) with a model-based optimizer to enhance decision-making for BESS operations. The RL agent is trained to learn optimal dispatch policies by interacting with a simulated environment, while the model-based optimizer refines these decisions by incorporating domain-specific constraints and physical system dynamics. Our approach leverages the adaptability of RL to handle complex, non-linear market conditions, while the optimizer ensures operational feasibility and efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms standalone RL and traditional optimization methods, achieving a 15% improvement in revenue generation and a 20% reduction in operational inefficiencies. The study highlights the potential of integrating data-driven and model-based techniques for real-world energy storage applications, offering a scalable solution for grid operators and energy market participants. Key contributions include a robust hybrid architecture, improved dispatch accuracy, and insights into the synergy between RL and optimization in energy systems. Keywords: reinforcement learning, battery energy storage, model-based optimization, energy dispatch, hybrid systems.

MVVM is an architectural pattern that divides an application into three key components: Model, View, and ViewModel. This paper addresses the challenge of training neural networks effectively in scenarios where high-fidelity data is scarce or expensive to obtain, while low-fidelity data is abundant. We propose a novel approach that leverages \ell 1-regularization combined with bi-fidelity data to enhance model performance and generalization. The \ell 1-regularization technique is employed to promote sparsity in the network weights, reducing overfitting and improving interpretability. Simultaneously, the bi-fidelity framework integrates both low- and high-fidelity data to train the model, ensuring robust learning even with limited high-quality data. Our methodology involves a two-stage training process: first, the model is pre-trained on low-fidelity data to capture general patterns, followed by fine-tuning using high-fidelity data to refine accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in resource-constrained environments. The findings highlight the potential of combining regularization techniques with multi-fidelity data for training neural networks, offering a scalable solution for applications in scientific computing, engineering, and beyond. This work contributes to the growing body of research on efficient neural network training and provides a practical framework for leveraging heterogeneous data sources. **Keywords**: Neural networks, \ell 1-regularization, bi-fidelity data, sparsity, model training, machine learning.

This research addresses the pressing challenge of adversarial attacks on graph-structured data, which are increasingly pervasive in applications such as social networks, recommendation systems, and financial transaction networks. Adversarial attacks pose significant risks by subtly altering input data to mislead and degrade the performance of graph-based learning models. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel adversarial attack method specifically tailored for graph-structured data, leveraging gradient-based optimization techniques to identify and perturb critical nodes and edges. Our approach effectively exploits the vulnerabilities in graph convolutional networks (GCNs) and graph attention networks (GATs), which are commonly utilized due to their ability to model complex relational data. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that our attack method significantly impacts the accuracy of state-of-the-art graph learning models, reducing their performance by up to 40% in key metrics. We perform extensive evaluations on benchmark datasets, proving the robustness and efficiency of our approach in real-world scenarios compared to existing adversarial attack techniques. Conclusion/Implications: This study highlights the susceptibility of graph-based models to adversarial manipulation, underlining the urgent need for robust defense mechanisms. Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the attack surface within graph learning frameworks, determining critical areas for enhancing model security. Future work will focus on developing effective defense strategies to mitigate such adversarial threats, safeguarding the integrity of graph-structured data in practical applications. Keywords: adversarial attack, graph-structured data, graph convolutional networks, graph attention networks, model robustness, data security.

This paper addresses the challenge of temporal credit assignment in episodic reinforcement learning, where determining the contribution of individual actions to overall episodic success is crucial. Traditional methods often struggle with efficiently propagating reward signals across extended temporal sequences, leading to suboptimal learning outcomes. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel sequence modeling approach that leverages advanced temporal sequence analysis techniques to enhance the precision of credit assignment throughout episodic reinforcement learning. Our model employs a hybrid architecture combining recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and attention-based mechanisms to capture long-term dependencies and accurately align actions with their corresponding rewards over time. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our method over conventional reinforcement learning models. In complex environments with prolonged episodes, our approach significantly improves learning speed and policy performance by more effectively distributing credit across relevant actions. Comparative analysis with existing methods reveals a substantial enhancement in convergence rates and overall efficacy in achieving higher cumulative rewards. Conclusion/Implications: By providing an innovative solution for temporal credit assignment, our research advances the field of reinforcement learning, offering a robust framework for improving decision-making efficiency in episodic tasks. The implications of our work extend to various applications, including autonomous robotics, strategic game playing, and dynamic resource allocation, where timely and accurate credit assignment holds critical value for system performance. Key Keywords: episodic reinforcement learning, temporal credit assignment, sequence modeling, recurrent neural networks, attention mechanisms.

This paper addresses the challenge of generating realistic synthetic medical time series data, which is crucial for research and development while preserving patient privacy. We propose a novel approach using Recurrent Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (RCGANs) tailored for real-valued medical time series. Our RCGAN architecture incorporates recurrent layers to capture temporal dependencies inherent in time series data, and is conditioned on clinically relevant parameters to control the generated data's characteristics. We evaluate our model on a real-world dataset of physiological signals, demonstrating its ability to generate synthetic time series that closely mimic the statistical properties and dynamics of the original data, outperforming traditional GAN models. The generated data is assessed using metrics including Frechet Inception Distance (FID) adapted for time series and visual inspection by medical experts. The results indicate that our RCGAN model produces high-quality synthetic medical time series, suitable for tasks such as algorithm development and data augmentation, thereby facilitating medical research and innovation. Keywords: Time series generation, GAN, RCGAN, medical data, synthetic data, recurrent neural networks.
