This paper proposes a novel Temporal Modulation Network (TMN) for controllable space-time video super-resolution, addressing the challenge of enhancing the resolution of videos while preserving their temporal consistency. Our approach combines the strengths of deep learning and traditional video processing techniques to achieve high-quality video super-resolution. The TMN model utilizes a temporal modulation module to adaptively adjust the spatial and temporal features of video frames, allowing for flexible control over the super-resolution process. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art video super-resolution algorithms in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM). The proposed TMN model also enables efficient and controllable video super-resolution, making it suitable for various applications such as video surveillance, sports broadcasting, and virtual reality. Key contributions of this work include the introduction of a temporal modulation mechanism, a novel loss function for controllable super-resolution, and a comprehensive evaluation framework for video super-resolution algorithms. Relevant keywords: video super-resolution, deep learning, temporal modulation, space-time processing, controllable super-resolution.

There is a warning light for the loss of plant habitats worldwide that entails concerted efforts to conserve plant biodiversity. Thus, plant species classification is of crucial importance to address this environmental challenge. In recent years, there is a considerable increase in the number of studies related to plant taxonomy. While some researchers try to improve their recognition performance using novel approaches, others concentrate on computational optimization for their framework. In addition, a few studies are diving into feature extraction to gain significantly in terms of accuracy. In this paper, we propose an effective method for the leaf recognition problem. In our proposed approach, a leaf goes through some pre-processing to extract its refined color image, vein image, xy-projection histogram, handcrafted shape, texture features, and Fourier descriptors. These attributes are then transformed into a better representation by neural network-based encoders before a support vector machine (SVM) model is utilized to classify different leaves. Overall, our approach performs a state-of-the-art result on the Flavia leaf dataset, achieving the accuracy of 99.58\% on test sets under random 10-fold cross-validation and bypassing the previous methods. We also release our codes (Scripts are available at https://github.com/dinhvietcuong1996/LeafRecognition) for contributing to the research community in the leaf classification problem.

The paper introduces MagGAN, a state-of-the-art approach for high-resolution face attribute editing that addresses the limitations of existing methods in generating photo-realistic and contextually coherent facial images with transformed attributes. The primary focus is on achieving precise and controlled editing guided by mask information, without compromising image quality or integrity. Methods/Approach: MagGAN leverages a novel Mask-Guided Generative Adversarial Network architecture, which incorporates a mask generation module to delineate the areas for attribute modification explicitly. By integrating this module with a conditional GAN framework, the system learns to selectively alter target features such as expression, age, or hair color while preserving the natural appearance and identity of non-target regions. This approach enhances control over localized facial transformations and ensures high-resolution output fidelity. Results/Findings: The system demonstrates superior performance in generating realistic face modifications, as evaluated using standard metrics and comparative studies with existing models. Experimental results show that MagGAN outperforms traditional GAN-based methods in both visual quality and user-perceived acceptability, achieving seamless attribute transitions with minimized artifacts. The mask-guided approach allows for nuanced edits with remarkable precision in high-resolution images. Conclusion/Implications: The introduction of MagGAN marks a significant advancement in the field of face attribute editing, offering a powerful tool for applications in digital art, entertainment, and virtual reality where personalized and realistic face modification is essential. The methodology not only enhances image refinement capabilities but also sets a new benchmark for future research in image-to-image translation tasks involving generative models. Keywords: MagGAN, face attribute editing, high-resolution, generative adversarial network, mask-guided, photo-realistic, image modification.

Kết quả cho thấy, việc bón đạm ở mức vừa phải không chỉ cải thiện sinh trưởng mà còn tối ưu hóa năng suất, trong khi bón quá nhiều có thể dẫn đến hiện tượng dư thừa, gây ảnh hưởng tiêu cực đến chất lượng hạt. Nghiên cứu này cung cấp cơ sở khoa học để điều chỉnh lượng đạm phù hợp, nhằm đạt được hiệu quả canh tác cao nhất cho các giống diêm mạch nhập nội.

Processing data streams arriving at high speed requires the development of models that can provide fast and accurate predictions. Although deep neural networks are the state-of-the-art for many machine learning tasks, their performance in real-time data streaming scenarios is a research area that has not yet been fully addressed. Nevertheless, there have been recent efforts to adapt complex deep learning models for streaming tasks by reducing their processing rate. The design of the asynchronous dual-pipeline deep learning framework allows to predict over incoming instances and update the model simultaneously using two separate layers. The aim of this work is to assess the performance of different types of deep architectures for data streaming classification using this framework. We evaluate models such as multi-layer perceptrons, recurrent, convolutional and temporal convolutional neural networks over several time-series datasets that are simulated as streams. The obtained results indicate that convolutional architectures achieve a higher performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

Bayesian learning often benefits from integrating diverse data sources, but the computational cost grows significantly with each additional source. This paper addresses the challenge of selecting a near-optimal subset of data sources to minimize computational overhead while preserving predictive accuracy. We introduce a novel selection algorithm based on a submodular optimization framework that balances the information gain from each data source with its associated computational cost. Our approach leverages the theoretical properties of submodular functions to provide near-optimality guarantees. Experimental results on a range of benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method can achieve comparable or superior prediction performance to using all available data sources, while significantly reducing computational time. Specifically, we show a reduction in computation time of up to 70% with minimal loss in accuracy. The proposed method offers a practical solution for scalable Bayesian learning in scenarios with abundant, heterogeneous data. Keywords: Bayesian Learning, Data Source Selection, Submodular Optimization, Scalable Learning, Active Learning.

The cold-start problem remains a significant challenge in the field of personalized recommendation systems, particularly in outfit recommendation where new users and items lack sufficient interaction data. This research proposes an innovative solution by leveraging visual preference modelling to enhance recommendation accuracy in such scenarios. Methods/Approach: Our approach utilizes a deep learning model to understand visual preferences, integrating convolutional neural networks (CNN) with collaborative filtering techniques. By analyzing visual features of clothing items and user behavior data, our model can predict user preferences for unseen outfits. This paper investigates the optimal signal detection problem with a particular interest in large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The problem is NP-hard and can be solved optimally by searching the shortest path on the decision tree. Unfortunately, the existing optimal search algorithms often involve prohibitively high complexities, which indicates that they are infeasible in large-scale MIMO systems. To address this issue, we propose a general heuristic search algorithm, namely, hyperaccelerated tree search (HATS) algorithm. The proposed algorithm employs a deep neural network (DNN) to estimate the optimal heuristic, and then use the estimated heuristic to speed up the underlying memory-bounded search algorithm. This idea is inspired by the fact that the underlying heuristic search algorithm reaches the optimal efficiency with the optimal heuristic function. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm reaches almost the optimal bit error rate (BER) performance in large-scale systems, while the memory size can be bounded. In the meanwhile, it visits nearly the fewest tree nodes. This indicates that the proposed algorithm reaches almost the optimal efficiency in practical scenarios, and thereby it is applicable for large-scale systems. Besides, the code for this paper is available at https://github.com/skypitcher/hats.

The design of optimal morphological structures for robotic systems is a critical yet challenging problem, particularly in dynamic and task-agnostic environments. This paper introduces a novel framework for task-agnostic morphology evolution, enabling the automatic generation of adaptable robotic structures without predefined task objectives. Our approach leverages evolutionary algorithms combined with a generative model to explore diverse morphological designs, optimizing for general adaptability and robustness. The proposed method is evaluated through extensive simulations, where evolved morphologies are tested across a range of tasks, including locomotion, manipulation, and obstacle navigation. Results demonstrate that the evolved structures exhibit superior adaptability and performance compared to traditional task-specific designs, achieving an average improvement of 25% in task generalization. Furthermore, the framework highlights the potential for creating versatile robotic systems capable of operating in unpredictable environments. This research contributes to the field of evolutionary robotics by providing a scalable and efficient methodology for morphology optimization, with implications for autonomous robotics, adaptive systems, and AI-driven design. **Keywords**: morphology evolution, task-agnostic design, evolutionary algorithms, generative models, robotic adaptability, autonomous systems.

This paper investigates a novel approach to video generation by posing the question of whether objects in video can be treated akin to words in natural language processing. The research aims to explore the potential of leveraging transformer architectures, commonly employed in large language models, for generative video tasks. Methods/Approach: We introduce the Generative Video Transformer (GVT), a model that conceptualizes objects within a video as a sequence of "visual words." Our approach utilizes a transformer network framework to capture and generate temporal and spatial dependencies in video sequences, akin to text processing in language models. The model is trained on extensive video datasets to learn the dynamics and interactions of objects over time. Results/Findings: Results demonstrate that the GVT outperforms existing methods in generating coherent and contextually relevant video sequences, showcasing improved spatial and temporal consistency. Comparative analyses with state-of-the-art video generation techniques reveal that our model achieves superior performance in terms of video quality and object continuity, validating the viability of treating objects as analogous to words. Conclusion/Implications: The adoption of transformer architectures for video generation opens promising avenues in generative models, highlighting the versatility and potential of using object-word analogies. This research contributes to the growing field of video synthesis and expands the applications of transformer models beyond text and image domains. Potential applications range from content creation and entertainment to educational tools and beyond, marking a significant step forward in the field of AI-driven video generation. Keywords: Generative Video Transformer, Video Generation, Transformer Architecture, Visual Words, AI Models, Object Continuity, Temporal Dynamics.

This paper introduces CADP, a novel dataset designed for accident analysis using CCTV traffic cameras. The objective is to provide a comprehensive resource for developing and evaluating machine learning models that can detect and analyze traffic accidents from CCTV footage. A deep learning-based approach was employed to develop an accident detection model, leveraging computer vision techniques such as object detection and tracking. The results show that the proposed model achieves high accuracy in detecting accidents, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. The CADP dataset and the developed model have significant implications for improving road safety and can be applied to various real-world applications, including intelligent transportation systems and autonomous vehicles. Key contributions of this work include the creation of a large-scale annotated dataset and the development of a highly accurate accident detection model, paving the way for future research in CCTV-based traffic accident analysis. Relevant keywords: CCTV traffic cameras, accident analysis, machine learning, computer vision, deep learning, object detection, traffic safety.

The Information Bottleneck (IB) principle provides a theoretical framework for learning efficient representations by balancing prediction accuracy and representation complexity. This paper investigates the learnability aspects of the IB, focusing on the generalization performance achievable under different training conditions and model architectures. We analyze the sample complexity of learning IB representations, deriving bounds on the number of examples needed to achieve a desired level of generalization. Our approach leverages tools from statistical learning theory and rate-distortion theory to quantify the trade-off between compression and prediction. We present novel theoretical results demonstrating how the architectural properties of the encoder and decoder networks influence the learnability of the IB objective. Empirical evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets validate our theoretical findings, showing that our derived bounds accurately predict the generalization performance of IB-trained models. Furthermore, we explore the implications of our results for designing more efficient and robust representation learning algorithms. Key words: Information Bottleneck, Learnability, Generalization, Representation Learning, Sample Complexity, Rate-Distortion Theory.

This paper addresses the critical issue of model fairness in vertical federated learning, where multiple parties collaborate to train a model while maintaining data privacy. The objective is to develop a framework that ensures fairness in the learned model, preventing biased outcomes that can disproportionately affect certain groups. We propose a novel approach that integrates fairness constraints into the federated learning process, utilizing a combination of data preprocessing, model regularization, and optimization techniques. Our method, termed FairVFed, achieves significant improvements in fairness metrics, such as demographic parity and equalized odds, while maintaining competitive model performance. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of FairVFed in various scenarios, including multi-party collaborations and heterogeneous data distributions. The key contributions of this research include a fairness-aware federated learning framework, a theoretical analysis of fairness guarantees, and empirical evaluations on real-world datasets. This work has important implications for the development of fair and trustworthy AI models in vertical federated learning settings, with potential applications in areas such as finance, healthcare, and social media. Key keywords: vertical federated learning, model fairness, fairness constraints, demographic parity, equalized odds, AI fairness.

Phân vùng ảnh (hay phân đoạn ảnh) là một phương pháp mà trong đó hình ảnh kỹ thuật số được chia thành nhiều nhóm con khác nhau gọi là segment. Đây là lớp bài toán quan trọng tạo bước tiền điều của quá trình xử lý dữ liệu hình ảnh. This paper addresses the challenge of inferring the structure of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) from observed data, a critical task in modeling dynamic systems across various scientific and engineering domains. We propose a novel data-driven approach that combines sparse regression techniques with symbolic computation to identify the underlying equations governing system behavior. Our method leverages a library of candidate functions and employs optimization strategies to select the most parsimonious model that accurately describes the observed dynamics. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on both synthetic and real-world datasets, showcasing its ability to recover ODE structures with high accuracy and robustness to noise. Compared to existing methods, our approach achieves superior performance in terms of computational efficiency and model interpretability. The findings highlight the potential of this framework for applications in system identification, predictive modeling, and control theory, offering a scalable and automated solution for uncovering the governing principles of complex systems. Keywords: ordinary differential equations, sparse regression, symbolic computation, system identification, dynamic modeling.

This paper proposes a novel deep structural model for analyzing correlated multivariate time series, aiming to capture complex temporal dependencies and relationships between variables. Our approach leverages a combination of recurrent neural networks and graph convolutional networks to learn representations of time series data, incorporating both autoregressive and cross-variable correlations. The model is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating improved performance in forecasting and anomaly detection tasks compared to existing methods. Key findings include the ability to identify latent patterns and relationships between variables, as well as robustness to noise and missing data. The proposed model contributes to the field of time series analysis by providing a flexible and scalable framework for modeling complex correlations, with potential applications in finance, climate science, and healthcare. Our research highlights the importance of integrating deep learning techniques with structural modeling to uncover insights in multivariate time series data, with relevant keywords including deep learning, time series analysis, graph neural networks, and multivariate modeling.

Dynamic dispatching in real-world systems presents a complex and evolving challenge, requiring adaptive decision-making under uncertainty. This paper explores the challenges of applying Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to dynamic dispatching problems, focusing on its potential to optimize resource allocation and task scheduling in dynamic environments. We identify key obstacles, including the high dimensionality of state-action spaces, non-stationary environments, and the difficulty of reward function design. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid approach combining DRL with domain-specific heuristics, enabling more efficient exploration and exploitation in dynamic settings. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in reducing task completion times and improving system responsiveness compared to traditional dispatching methods. The findings highlight the potential of DRL in dynamic dispatching while underscoring the need for tailored solutions to overcome inherent limitations. This research contributes to advancing the application of DRL in real-world dynamic systems, offering insights for future developments in adaptive decision-making technologies. **Keywords**: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Dynamic Dispatching, Resource Allocation, Task Scheduling, Adaptive Decision-Making, Real-World Systems.

This paper addresses the challenge of training high-performing machine learning models with limited data, a common problem in many real-world applications. We introduce a novel modular learning approach that moves beyond traditional fine-tuning. Instead of adapting a pre-trained model holistically, our method decomposes the learning task into distinct modules, each responsible for a specific aspect of the desired functionality. These modules are then trained independently on smaller, targeted datasets and subsequently integrated to form the complete model. This modularity allows for efficient knowledge transfer and reduces the data requirements for each individual module. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on image classification and natural language processing tasks, showing significant improvements in accuracy and generalization compared to standard fine-tuning techniques, especially when training data is scarce. Key contributions include the modular learning framework, a novel module integration strategy, and empirical validation of its superior performance on small datasets. Keywords: machine learning, small data, modular learning, transfer learning, fine-tuning, knowledge transfer, low-resource learning.

This research addresses the challenge of understanding complex human actions in home environments by introducing a novel framework, the Home Action Genome. The study aims to enable cooperative compositional action recognition and understanding, facilitating improved interaction with and interpretation of human activities in domestic settings. Methods/Approach: The proposed framework leverages advanced computer vision techniques and deep learning algorithms to automatically segment and analyze compositional actions within a home. By integrating scene understanding and cooperative context modeling, the method effectively captures intricate interactions and dependencies among actions, objects, and environments. The system is evaluated using simulation environments with diverse action datasets to ensure robust performance across various scenarios. Results/Findings: Experimental results demonstrate that the Home Action Genome significantly enhances action understanding accuracy compared to existing models, achieving superior performance in recognizing and predicting sequences of complex actions in domestic settings. The framework also shows promising results in generalization across different household environments and variations in human behavior. Conclusion/Implications: This study contributes a valuable model for advancing home automation and intelligent systems through improved action recognition. The Home Action Genome's cooperative compositional approach paves the way for novel applications in smart home technologies, assistive living environments, and human-robot interaction systems. By accurately interpreting human actions, the framework can enhance the efficacy and user experience of intelligent home systems. Keywords: Home Action Genome, action understanding, computer vision, deep learning, home automation, human-robot interaction, scene understanding.

The rapid advancement of deep learning techniques has led to increasingly sophisticated face forgery methods, posing significant challenges for detection systems. This paper introduces *Face X-ray*, a novel approach designed to enhance the generalizability of face forgery detection across diverse manipulation techniques. Unlike existing methods that rely on specific artifacts or patterns unique to certain forgery algorithms, Face X-ray focuses on identifying inconsistencies in the blending boundaries between forged and authentic regions within an image. We propose a unified framework that leverages a self-supervised learning mechanism to generate Face X-ray maps, which highlight potential manipulation boundaries without requiring prior knowledge of the forgery method. Our experiments demonstrate that Face X-ray achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark datasets, including those containing unseen manipulation techniques, showcasing its robustness and generalizability. The proposed method not only outperforms existing approaches in cross-dataset evaluations but also provides interpretable visual evidence of forgery, making it a valuable tool for real-world applications. This research contributes to the field of digital forensics by offering a more universal and reliable solution for detecting face forgeries, with potential applications in cybersecurity, media integrity verification, and content authentication. **Keywords**: Face forgery detection, Face X-ray, deep learning, digital forensics, generalizability, self-supervised learning.

This paper introduces *ProLab*, a novel perceptually uniform projective colour coordinate system designed to address challenges in colour representation and manipulation across digital imaging and visualization applications. The primary objective of *ProLab* is to provide a more intuitive and perceptually accurate framework for colour mapping, ensuring uniformity in human visual perception. The proposed system leverages projective geometry and psychophysical models to transform traditional colour spaces into a coordinate system that aligns more closely with human visual perception. The methodology involves the development of a mathematical model that maps RGB and CIELAB colour spaces into a projective domain, optimizing for perceptual uniformity and computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that *ProLab* outperforms existing colour systems in terms of perceptual accuracy, particularly in applications such as image processing, data visualization, and 3D rendering. Comparative analyses with CIELAB and other colour spaces highlight *ProLab*'s superior performance in maintaining colour consistency across different viewing conditions and devices. The implications of this research are significant for industries relying on precise colour representation, including digital media, medical imaging, and virtual reality. *ProLab* represents a meaningful advancement in colour science, offering a robust and perceptually uniform solution for modern colour management challenges. **Keywords**: colour coordinate system, perceptual uniformity, projective geometry, colour mapping, CIELAB, digital imaging.

This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing snake locomotion gaits for energy efficiency using deep reinforcement learning. The objective is to develop a gait policy that minimizes energy consumption while maintaining effective locomotion. A deep reinforcement learning framework is employed, utilizing a combination of convolutional neural networks and policy gradient methods to learn an optimal gait policy. The results show that the learned policy achieves significant energy savings compared to traditional gait patterns, with a reduction of up to 30% in energy consumption. The findings have important implications for the development of energy-efficient snake-like robots and other biomimetic systems. The use of deep reinforcement learning enables the discovery of complex, non-intuitive gait patterns that would be difficult to design manually. Key contributions include the application of deep reinforcement learning to snake locomotion and the demonstration of substantial energy savings. Relevant keywords: deep reinforcement learning, snake locomotion, energy efficiency, gait policy, biomimetic robotics.

The paper addresses the challenge of anomaly detection in data streams, a critical task in fields such as cybersecurity, finance, and healthcare, where identifying unusual patterns is essential for preventing potential threats and failures. Traditional machine learning methods often fall short in adapting to evolving data patterns and identifying rare anomalies. Methods/Approach: We introduce Memory Augmented Generative Adversarial Networks (MAGANs), an innovative approach that integrates memory augmentation into the traditional generative adversarial network framework. This model leverages a memory component that stores and retrieves past information, enhancing the GAN's ability to detect anomalies by differentiating regular patterns from irregular ones more effectively. Results/Findings: The application of MAGANs demonstrated significant improvements in anomaly detection accuracy across various benchmark datasets compared to standard GANs and other state-of-the-art methods. The inclusion of the memory module allowed for more accurate reconstruction of normal data distribution, resulting in more reliable detection of outliers and significantly reducing false positives. Conclusion/Implications: The study highlights the potential of memory-augmented architectures in improving the robustness and accuracy of anomaly detection systems. MAGANs contribute a novel perspective in the domain of anomaly detection by combining memory retention capabilities with generative modeling, paving the way for more adaptive and intelligent monitoring systems. Potential applications are vast and include real-time applications in network security, fraud detection, and system diagnostics, where accurate anomaly detection is crucial. Keywords: anomaly detection, generative adversarial networks, memory augmentation, MAGANs, real-time monitoring, cybersecurity, fraud detection, intelligent systems.

Abstract Policy improvement is a central challenge in reinforcement learning and sequential decision-making, where the goal is to iteratively refine an agent’s behavior to maximize long-term rewards while minimizing potential risks. Traditional exploration strategies often trade off between fast learning and safety, potentially exposing agents to undesirable or unsafe states. This paper introduces a novel framework for diverse exploration, designed to accelerate policy improvement while maintaining safety guarantees. Our method leverages an ensemble of exploratory policies that diversify behavior by encouraging exploration across different regions of the state space, reducing the risk of premature convergence to suboptimal solutions. At the same time, safety constraints are integrated into the exploration process to prevent actions that jeopardize the agent or the environment. We evaluate the proposed approach on a suite of standard reinforcement learning benchmarks and compare it to existing exploration and safety-aware methods. Results demonstrate that our framework achieves faster policy improvement, better sample efficiency, and superior adherence to safety requirements. The integration of diversity and safety in exploration provides a robust foundation for deploying reinforcement learning agents in real-world applications, such as robotics, autonomous systems, and industrial control, where both rapid learning and operational safety are critical. Keywords: reinforcement learning, policy improvement, safe exploration, diversity, sample efficiency, robotics, autonomous systems.

Objective: The proliferation of automatic image colorization techniques poses new challenges for digital forensics, as distinguishing between naturally colored and artificially colorized images becomes increasingly difficult. This paper presents a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) framework designed to detect colorized images with both high accuracy and strong generalization across diverse colorization methods. Methods: We introduce a dual-branch CNN architecture that separately analyzes chrominance artifacts and spatial consistency cues. The chrominance branch focuses on statistical discrepancies in color distributions, while the spatial branch captures structural distortions introduced by colorization algorithms. A joint feature fusion module integrates these complementary representations. To enhance robustness, we employ extensive data augmentation and a domain-­adaptive training strategy that simulates unseen colorization styles. Results: Experiments on benchmark datasets—including images colorized by state-of-the-art deep learning and traditional methods—demonstrate detection accuracies exceeding 98% on in-domain tests and over 90% in cross-domain evaluations. Compared to existing forensic detectors, our approach yields a 5–8% absolute improvement in accuracy and a marked reduction in false positives. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of the dual-branch design and domain-adaptive training in boosting generalization. Conclusion: The proposed CNN-based detector offers a reliable solution for identifying artificially colorized images, making it well suited for applications in journalism verification, legal evidence analysis, and social media content moderation. Its strong generalization capability ensures adaptability to future colorization techniques. Keywords: Convolutional neural network, colorization detection, image forensics, deep learning, generalization.

Incremental learning, a critical capability for evolving artificial intelligence systems, faces challenges in balancing the retention of previously learned knowledge with the integration of new information. This paper introduces *DeeSIL* (Deep-Shallow Incremental Learning), a novel framework designed to address these challenges by combining deep and shallow learning paradigms. The objective of DeeSIL is to enhance the adaptability of machine learning models in dynamic environments while minimizing catastrophic forgetting. The proposed approach leverages deep neural networks for feature extraction and shallow classifiers for efficient incremental updates, enabling robust performance across diverse tasks. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DeeSIL achieves superior accuracy and stability compared to existing incremental learning methods, particularly in scenarios with limited computational resources. The framework also exhibits scalability, making it suitable for real-world applications such as autonomous systems and personalized recommendation engines. By integrating deep and shallow learning, DeeSIL offers a significant contribution to the field of incremental learning, providing a practical solution for deploying adaptive AI systems in resource-constrained environments. **Keywords**: incremental learning, deep learning, shallow learning, catastrophic forgetting, adaptive systems, DeeSIL.

This paper addresses the problem of graph classification, a critical task in numerous applications such as social network analysis, bioinformatics, and chemistry. While many complex models have been proposed to tackle this problem, they often require significant computational resources. Our research aims to introduce a simple yet effective baseline algorithm that can be used for graph classification, offering an accessible alternative to more complex methodologies. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel baseline algorithm that leverages basic graph properties and a linear classification model to classify graphs. Our approach combines structural graph features such as degree distribution and clustering coefficients with a straightforward feature extraction process. The model is designed to be computationally efficient, enabling application to large datasets with minimal resource requirements. Results/Findings: Experiments demonstrate that our baseline algorithm achieves competitive performance compared to several state-of-the-art graph classification models on benchmark datasets. Despite its simplicity, the algorithm manages to maintain robustness and accuracy across various graph types. Our findings suggest that for many practical applications, our simpler model can yield satisfactory results with significantly lower computational overhead. Conclusion/Implications: This research highlights the potential of using straightforward methodologies for complex tasks like graph classification, promoting accessibility and resource efficiency. Our simple baseline algorithm serves as an effective tool for graph classification, especially in scenarios where resources are limited. Underwater object detection suffers from challenges such as low visibility, color distortion, and the scarcity of labeled data. This paper introduces RoIMix, a novel data augmentation technique that fuses region proposals from multiple underwater images to enhance detector robustness and generalization. RoIMix operates by identifying salient regions of interest (RoIs) across a batch of training images and strategically mixing them to create new, diverse training samples. Specifically, RoIMix combines the visual features of different RoIs, thereby simulating complex underwater scenes and forcing the detector to learn more discriminative features. We evaluate RoIMix on several benchmark underwater object detection datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in Average Precision (AP) compared to state-of-the-art augmentation techniques and baseline detectors. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each component of RoIMix. RoIMix effectively addresses the challenges of underwater object detection and offers a practical solution for improving detector performance. Keywords: Underwater Object Detection, Data Augmentation, Region of Interest, Deep Learning, Computer Vision.

Few tone mapping operators (TMOs) take color management into consideration, limiting compression to luminance values only. This may lead to changes in image chroma and hues which are typically managed with a post-processing step. However, current post-processing techniques for tone reproduction do not explicitly consider the target display gamut. Gamut mapping on the other hand, deals with mapping images from one color gamut to another, usually smaller, gamut but has traditionally focused on smaller scale, chromatic changes. In this context, we present a novel gamut and tone management framework for color-accurate reproduction of high dynamic range (HDR) images, which is conceptually and computationally simple, parameter-free, and compatible with existing TMOs. In the CIE LCh color space, we compress chroma to fit the gamut of the output color space. This prevents hue and luminance shifts while taking gamut boundaries into consideration. We also propose a compatible lightness compression scheme that minimizes the number of color space conversions. Our results show that our gamut management method effectively compresses the chroma of tone mapped images, respecting the target gamut and without reducing image quality.

This paper introduces a novel fault detection method based on Second-Order Component Analysis (SOCA). The objective is to improve the sensitivity and robustness of fault detection systems in complex industrial processes. The proposed approach leverages the second-order statistical properties of process data to extract features that are more sensitive to subtle process deviations compared to traditional first-order methods. This research contributes a practical and effective fault detection strategy that can enhance the reliability and safety of industrial systems. Keywords: Fault detection, Second-Order Component Analysis, Process monitoring, Statistical process control, PCA, ICA.

This paper addresses the problem of outlier detection in multi-armed bandit (MAB) settings, where a subset of arms may exhibit anomalous reward distributions. Traditional MAB algorithms assume stationary reward distributions for all arms, which can lead to suboptimal performance in the presence of outliers. We propose a novel generic outlier detection framework applicable to a wide range of MAB algorithms. Our approach involves monitoring the reward distributions of each arm and employing statistical tests to identify arms deviating significantly from expected behavior. Upon detecting an outlier, the algorithm dynamically adjusts arm selection strategies to mitigate its impact. We evaluate the performance of our framework by integrating it with several benchmark MAB algorithms, including UCB1 and Thompson Sampling, across diverse simulated environments with varying outlier characteristics. Experimental results demonstrate that our outlier detection mechanism significantly improves the cumulative regret compared to standard MAB algorithms, especially in scenarios with non-stationary or adversarial outliers. This generic framework provides a practical and effective solution for robust decision-making in dynamic environments. Keywords: Multi-Armed Bandit, Outlier Detection, Anomaly Detection, Reinforcement Learning, Robust Optimization.

Temporal Difference (TD) learning is a fundamental approach in reinforcement learning, widely used for value function approximation. However, traditional TD methods often struggle with slow convergence and inefficiency in environments with sparse or delayed rewards. This paper introduces *Source Traces*, a novel mechanism designed to enhance the efficiency and stability of TD learning algorithms. The proposed approach leverages a dynamic trace mechanism that identifies and prioritizes critical states (sources) influencing future rewards, enabling more effective credit assignment. We present a theoretical analysis of Source Traces, demonstrating its convergence properties and improved sample efficiency compared to conventional eligibility traces. Empirical evaluations on benchmark reinforcement learning tasks, including gridworld and Atari environments, show that Source Traces significantly reduce training time while achieving higher cumulative rewards. The results highlight the potential of Source Traces to advance TD learning in complex, real-world applications, particularly in scenarios with long-term dependencies and sparse rewards. This work contributes a scalable and interpretable solution to the challenges of temporal credit assignment, offering a promising direction for future research in reinforcement learning. **Keywords**: Temporal Difference Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Source Traces, Credit Assignment, Sample Efficiency, Sparse Rewards.

Several recent works [40, 24] observed an interesting phenomenon in neural network pruning: A larger finetuning learning rate can improve the final performance significantly. Unfortunately, the reason behind it remains elusive up to date. This paper is meant to explain it through the lens of dynamical isometry [42]. Specifically, we examine neural network pruning from an unusual perspective: pruning as initialization for finetuning, and ask whether the inherited weights serve as a good initialization for the finetuning? The insights from dynamical isometry suggest a negative answer. Despite its critical role, this issue has not been well-recognized by the community so far. In this paper, we will show the understanding of this problem is very important -- on top of explaining the aforementioned mystery about the larger finetuning rate, it also unveils the mystery about the value of pruning [5, 30]. Besides a clearer theoretical understanding of pruning, resolving the problem can also bring us considerable performance benefits in practice.

The accurate detection and segmentation of defects in solar cell images are critical for improving manufacturing efficiency and ensuring product quality. However, existing methods often struggle with limited annotated datasets and imbalanced defect distributions. This paper introduces SIGAN, a novel image generation method designed specifically for solar cell defect segmentation and data augmentation. SIGAN leverages a generative adversarial network (GAN) architecture enhanced with a spatial attention mechanism to synthesize high-quality, realistic defect images while preserving the structural integrity of solar cells. The proposed approach generates diverse defect patterns, including micro-cracks and hotspots, which are challenging to capture in real-world datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that SIGAN significantly improves the performance of defect segmentation models by augmenting training data, achieving a 12% increase in mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the generated images exhibit high visual fidelity and diversity, enabling robust model generalization. SIGAN’s contributions lie in its ability to address dataset limitations and enhance defect detection accuracy, offering practical implications for solar cell manufacturing and quality control. **Keywords**: Solar cell defect detection, image generation, GAN, data augmentation, defect segmentation, spatial attention mechanism.

This paper explores the application of transfer learning in material classification using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The objective is to address the challenge of accurately identifying materials in images, which is critical for applications in robotics, manufacturing, and quality control. Traditional methods often require extensive labeled datasets, which are costly and time-consuming to acquire. To overcome this limitation, we propose leveraging pre-trained CNN models, fine-tuned on a smaller dataset of material images. Our approach utilizes state-of-the-art architectures, such as ResNet and EfficientNet, and evaluates their performance on publicly available material datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that transfer learning significantly improves classification accuracy compared to training from scratch, achieving a top-1 accuracy of over 92% on benchmark datasets. Additionally, we analyze the impact of dataset size and fine-tuning strategies on model performance. The findings highlight the effectiveness of transfer learning in reducing data requirements while maintaining high accuracy. This research contributes to the field by providing a practical and efficient solution for material classification, with potential applications in industrial automation and computer vision systems. **Keywords**: transfer learning, material classification, convolutional neural networks, fine-tuning, computer vision, ResNet, EfficientNet.

Multimodal image super-resolution (SR) is the reconstruction of a high resolution image given a low-resolution observation with the aid of another image modality. While existing deep multimodal models do not incorporate domain knowledge about image SR, we present a multimodal deep network design that integrates coupled sparse priors and allows the effective fusion of information from another modality into the reconstruction process. Our method is inspired by a novel iterative algorithm for coupled convolutional sparse coding, resulting in an interpretable network by design. We apply our model to the super-resolution of near-infrared image guided by RGB images. Experimental results show that our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

Mở đầu: Viêm màng não mủ (VMNM) mắc phải tại cộng đồng gây ra bởi trực khuẩn Gram âm được ghi nhận gia tăng trong thập kỷ vừa qua. Bệnh thường xảy ra trên cơ địa người lớn tuổi và/hoặc có bệnh nền, với dự hậu xấu và tỷ lệ tử vong cao. Nghiên cứu mô tả đặc điểm viêm màng não mủ do trực khuẩn Gram âm mắc phải từ cộng đồng ở người lớn. Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả hàng loạt ca bệnh được chẩn đoán VMNM do trực khuẩn Gram âm mắc phải từ cộng đồng được điều trị tại BVBNĐ từ năm 2014 đến năm 2020. Nghiên cứu gồm 2 giai đoạn hồi cứu (01/2014 - 12/2018) và tiến cứu (01/2019 - 06/2020). Kết quả: Từ 01/2014 đến 06/2020, 68 bệnh nhân VMNM do trực khuẩn Gram âm mắc phải từ cộng đồng nhập viện điều trị. Bệnh thường gặp ở nam giới (72,1%), trung niên (tuổi trung vị 52,5 tuổi) và làm nghề nông (54,4%). Đái tháo đường là bệnh nền thường gặp nhất (41,2%). Đáng lưu ý, 21/68 (30,9%) trường hợp có điều trị thuốc kháng viêm corticoid kéo dài trước khi nhập viện và 19/68 (27,9%) bệnh nhân có đồng nhiễm Strongyloides stercoralis. E. coli và K. pneumoniae là vi khuẩn gây bệnh đứng đầu với tỷ lệ tương ứng 42,5% (29/68) và 32,3% (22/68). E. coli tiết men ESBL chiếm 75,9% (22/29) chủng vi khuẩn, dẫn đến việc điều trị kháng sinh ban đầu bằng ceftriaxone không phù hợp ở 16/45 bệnh nhân (35,6%). Sốc nhiễm trùng xảy ra ở 21/65 (32,3%) bệnh nhân và liên quan đến kết cục xấu. Tử vong và di chứng khá cao với tỷ lệ tương ứng là 35,4% và 20%. Kết luận: Viêm màng não mủ do trực khuẩn Gram âm mắc phải từ cộng đồng là bệnh có dự hậu xấu. E. coli và K. pneumoniae là vi khuẩn gây bệnh thường gặp nhất. Một số đặc điểm gợi ý đến nhóm tác nhân này là bệnh nền đái tháo đường, sử dụng corticoid kéo dài, nhiễm giun lươn. Do tình trạng kháng ceftriaxone của vi khuẩn, kháng sinh điều trị theo kinh nghiệm ở đối tượng này ưu tiên chọn nhóm carbapenem.

The optimization of machine learning (ML) models within compilers is critical for achieving efficient execution across diverse hardware architectures. However, existing optimization techniques often require significant manual effort and are tailored to specific hardware or model types, limiting their scalability and adaptability. This paper introduces a novel approach to ML compiler optimization through transferable graph optimizers. We propose a graph-based framework that leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to learn optimization policies directly from computational graphs, enabling the transfer of optimization strategies across different models and hardware platforms. Our method employs a reinforcement learning-based training paradigm to iteratively refine optimization decisions, ensuring adaptability to varying computational constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional handcrafted optimization techniques, achieving up to a 30% improvement in execution speed and a 25% reduction in memory usage across multiple benchmarks. Furthermore, the transferability of the learned optimizers is validated through cross-platform evaluations, showcasing their ability to generalize to unseen architectures. This work contributes a scalable and automated solution to ML compiler optimization, paving the way for more efficient deployment of ML models in heterogeneous computing environments. **Keywords**: machine learning compilers, graph neural networks, transferable optimizers, reinforcement learning, computational graphs, hardware acceleration.

Silic không chỉ giúp cải thiện khả năng chống chịu của cây trước các điều kiện bất lợi như hạn hán, sâu bệnh mà còn thúc đẩy quá trình quang hợp, tăng cường sức đề kháng và nâng cao năng suất. Các thí nghiệm cho thấy cây trồng được bón phân silic có sự phát triển vượt trội về chiều cao, số lượng lá và trọng lượng quả so với cây không được bón. Ngoài ra, silic còn đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc cải thiện cấu trúc đất, giúp cây hấp thụ dinh dưỡng tốt hơn. Kết quả nghiên cứu này mở ra hướng đi mới cho nông nghiệp bền vững, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả sản xuất và bảo vệ môi trường.

Suy giảm mực nước dưới đất ở vùng đồng bằng sông Cửu Long đang trở thành một vấn đề nghiêm trọng. Theo thống kê, mực nước dưới đất ở khu vực này đã giảm đáng kể trong những năm gần đây, từ 1-2 mét ở một số khu vực. Nguyên nhân chính của tình trạng này là do việc khai thác nước ngầm quá mức, dẫn đến sự mất cân bằng giữa lượng nước được sử dụng và lượng nước được tái tạo. Hậu quả của việc suy giảm mực nước dưới đất là rất nghiêm trọng. Nước ngầm là nguồn nước quan trọng cho các hoạt động nông nghiệp, công nghiệp và sinh hoạt hàng ngày. Khi mực nước dưới đất giảm, sẽ dẫn đến sự thiếu hụt nước, ảnh hưởng đến sản xuất nông nghiệp, gây thiệt hại cho nền kinh tế và ảnh hưởng đến cuộc sống của người dân. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, cần có các biện pháp khẩn cấp và lâu dài. Trước hết, cần phải giảm thiểu việc khai thác nước ngầm và tăng cường việc sử dụng nước mặt. Đồng thời, cần phải đầu tư vào các công trình thủy lợi và hệ thống cấp nước để đảm bảo nguồn nước cho các hoạt động sản xuất và sinh hoạt. Ngoài ra, cần phải thực hiện các biện pháp bảo vệ nguồn nước ngầm, bao gồm việc hạn chế việc sử dụng hóa chất và chất thải độc hại. Tổng hợp số liệu thống kê cho thấy, việc suy giảm mực nước dưới đất ở vùng đồng bằng sông Cửu Long đang trở thành một thách thức lớn đối với sự phát triển kinh tế và xã hội của khu vực này. Cần phải có sự hợp tác và nỗ lực của các cơ quan chức năng, cộng đồng và người dân để giải quyết vấn đề này và đảm bảo nguồn nước cho tương lai.

Kết quả cho thấy, các vật liệu này không chỉ giúp tăng độ ẩm đất mà còn hạn chế sự phát triển của cỏ dại, giảm thiểu sâu bệnh. This study addresses the critical challenge of accurately assessing the classification performance of adversarially trained models in machine learning. Adversarial training has emerged as a prominent defense strategy against adversarial attacks, aimed at enhancing model robustness. However, there is a paucity of precise methods for statistically analyzing classification accuracies within this context. Methods/Approach: We propose an innovative statistical framework designed to rigorously evaluate the classification accuracies of models subjected to adversarial training. Our approach leverages advanced statistical techniques and incorporates novel metrics to deliver more reliable assessments compared to traditional methods. This framework is tested across various datasets and adversarial attack scenarios to ensure broad applicability and robustness. Results/Findings: The findings demonstrate that our statistical analysis framework provides significantly improved precision in evaluating classification accuracies, offering a nuanced understanding of model performance under adversarial conditions. The results also reveal consistent enhancements in robustness metrics when utilizing our analysis method, showcasing its effectiveness in distinguishing genuine model improvements. Conclusion/Implications: This research presents a major contribution to the field of adversarial machine learning by offering a precise and statistically sound methodology for analyzing model performance. The insights gained from our study are instrumental for researchers and practitioners aiming to develop and validate more robust machine learning models. This framework has the potential to be integrated into standard evaluation protocols, paving the way for more resilient AI systems. Keywords: adversarial training, classification accuracy, statistical analysis, machine learning robustness, adversarial attacks, model evaluation.

Neural networks offer unparalleled performance across various tasks but often suffer from high computational costs, hindering deployment on resource-constrained devices. This paper introduces AntiDote, an Attention-based Dynamic Optimization technique designed to improve neural network runtime efficiency. AntiDote employs an attention mechanism to dynamically adjust the computational resources allocated to different parts of the network during inference. By learning to identify and prioritize salient features, AntiDote selectively prunes less important connections and operations, leading to reduced computational overhead. We evaluate AntiDote on several benchmark datasets and network architectures, demonstrating significant improvements in runtime, achieving up to 40% reduction in inference time with minimal accuracy loss compared to static pruning methods. The proposed approach offers a flexible and efficient way to optimize neural networks for deployment in resource-limited environments, advancing the practicality of deep learning in edge computing and mobile applications. Keywords: Neural Network Optimization, Dynamic Pruning, Attention Mechanism, Runtime Efficiency, Deep Learning, Edge Computing.

Thành phố bọt biển (SPC) là mô hình quản lý thoát nước mặt dựa trên cách tiếp cận có hệ thống về giảm thiểu nguồn, kiểm soát quá trình và xử lý có hệ thống, đồng thời áp dụng các biện pháp kỹ thuật toàn diện về hấp thụ, lưu giữ, lưu trữ, làm sạch nước, tái sử dụng nước và xả nước ra hệ thống thoát nước nhằm đạt được nhiều mục tiêu là giảm thiểu lũ lụt đô thị, kiểm soát ô nhiễm dòng chảy, cải thiện môi trường nước đô thị và phục hồi sinh thái nước đô thị. SPC đang được coi là một trong số các giải pháp hữu hiệu góp phần ngăn ngừa rủi ro cũng như giảm thiểu ảnh hưởng của lũ lụt. Tuy nhiên việc áp dụng mô hình SPC vào thực tế không hề đơn giản, bởi các rào cản về pháp lý cũng như cơ sở lý luận chưa chắc chắn. Bài viết nhằm tổng hợp các cơ sở lý luận và pháp lý liên quan đến SPC ở Việt Nam, bổ sung thêm căn cứ để đề xuất các giải pháp quản lý thoát nước mặt đô thị hướng tới mô hình SPC phù hợp với thực tiễn.

Nghiên cứu mới đây đã đánh giá khả năng dự đoán giãn tĩnh mạch thực quản (GTTQ) ở bệnh nhân xơ gan bằng cách kết hợp kỹ thuật ARFI (Acoustic Radiation Force Impulse) đo độ cứng gan và số lượng tiểu cầu. Computer vision has received a significant attention in recent year, which is one of the important parts for robots to obtain information about the external environment. Visual trackers can provide the necessary physical and environmental parameters for the mobile robot, and their performance is related to the actual application of the robot. This study provides a comprehensive survey on visual trackers. Following a brief introduction, we first analyzed the basic framework and difficulties of visual trackers. Then the structure of generative and discriminative methods is introduced, and summarized the feature descriptors, modeling methods, and learning methods which be used in tracker. Later we reviewed and evaluated the state-of-the-art progress on discriminative trackers from three directions: correlation filter, deep learning and convolutional features. Finally, we analyzed the research direction of visual tracker used in mobile robot, as well as outlined the future trends for visual tracker on mobile robot.

The increasing demand for real-time data processing and smart applications has driven the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) at the edge of networks. This paper aims to address the challenges and opportunities of deploying deep learning models at the edge, focusing on optimizing performance and maximizing resource efficiency. We present an in-depth analysis of the tailored approaches for edge AI, including model compression techniques, such as pruning and quantization, and edge-specific architectures that maintain accuracy while reducing computational load. To evaluate the proposed methods, rigorous experiments were conducted using benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in model efficiency and reduced latency compared to conventional cloud-based AI processing. The results highlight the potential for enhanced AI applications in latency-sensitive environments such as autonomous vehicles, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and mobile robotics. Our findings suggest that, with the right optimizations, deep learning can be adapted for real-time edge applications without compromising on performance. This research contributes to the growing field of edge computing by providing empirical evidence and methodologies for deploying AI efficiently at the edge, paving the way for new advancements in distributed intelligence systems. Key keywords include edge computing, AI deployment, deep learning, model compression, real-time processing, IoT, and autonomous systems.

Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (cGANs) have demonstrated remarkable success in generating high-quality, context-aware data across various domains. However, their performance often degrades under noisy or incomplete conditional inputs, limiting their robustness in real-world applications. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a novel framework for Robust Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (R-cGANs). The objective is to enhance the stability and reliability of cGANs when handling imperfect or uncertain conditional data. Our approach integrates a noise-resilient encoder and a dynamic attention mechanism to adaptively refine conditional inputs during the generation process. Additionally, we introduce a hybrid loss function that balances adversarial training with reconstruction accuracy, ensuring robust performance across diverse scenarios. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that R-cGANs outperform traditional cGANs in terms of both qualitative and quantitative metrics, particularly under noisy conditions. The proposed framework achieves significant improvements in image synthesis, text-to-image generation, and data augmentation tasks. This research contributes a scalable and versatile solution for enhancing the robustness of conditional generative models, with potential applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and beyond. **Keywords**: Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks, Robustness, Noise Resilience, Dynamic Attention, Hybrid Loss Function, Image Synthesis.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc phân tích sắc thái trong các bình luận của người dùng trên các trang thương mại điện tử, một yếu tố quan trọng ảnh hưởng đến quyết định mua hàng và uy tín của sản phẩm. Mục tiêu chính là xây dựng một hệ thống có khả năng tự động xác định và phân loại sắc thái (tích cực, tiêu cực, trung tính) của các bình luận, từ đó cung cấp thông tin giá trị cho cả người bán và người mua. Việc phân tích sắc thái được thực hiện bằng cách kết hợp các kỹ thuật xử lý ngôn ngữ tự nhiên (NLP) và học máy (Machine Learning). Dữ liệu bình luận được thu thập từ nhiều trang thương mại điện tử khác nhau, sau đó trải qua quá trình tiền xử lý bao gồm loại bỏ các ký tự đặc biệt, chuyển đổi chữ thường, và loại bỏ các từ dừng. Các đặc trưng ngôn ngữ, như tần suất từ, bigram, trigram và các đặc trưng dựa trên từ điển cảm xúc, được trích xuất từ dữ liệu đã tiền xử lý. Các mô hình học máy khác nhau, bao gồm Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest và các mô hình học sâu như Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) và Transformer, được huấn luyện để phân loại sắc thái. Hiệu suất của các mô hình được đánh giá bằng các độ đo như độ chính xác, độ thu hồi, độ chính xác và F1-score. Kết quả cho thấy các mô hình học sâu, đặc biệt là Transformer, đạt được hiệu suất tốt nhất trong việc phân loại sắc thái, nhờ khả năng nắm bắt các mối quan hệ phức tạp trong ngôn ngữ. Nghiên cứu cũng khám phá các thách thức trong việc phân tích sắc thái, như xử lý ngôn ngữ đa nghĩa, nhận diện giọng điệu mỉa mai và các biểu đạt cảm xúc phức tạp. Ngoài ra, nghiên cứu đề xuất các phương pháp cải thiện hiệu suất của hệ thống, như sử dụng các kỹ thuật tăng cường dữ liệu, kết hợp thông tin ngữ cảnh và phát triển các mô hình chuyên biệt cho từng loại sản phẩm. Cuối cùng, nghiên cứu thảo luận về ứng dụng của hệ thống phân tích sắc thái trong việc cải thiện trải nghiệm người dùng, tăng cường uy tín sản phẩm và hỗ trợ quyết định kinh doanh trên các trang thương mại điện tử.

This paper presents 'Head2Head,' an innovative approach for video-based neural head synthesis aimed at generating realistic human head animations from video input. Our study addresses the challenge of creating dynamic, high-fidelity head models that can accurately replicate a range of human expressions and movements. Methods/Approach: The proposed method utilizes a novel neural network architecture that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with generative adversarial networks (GANs) to enhance the realism and coherence of synthesized head movements. We employ adversarial training to refine the model's ability to replicate intricate facial details and expressions. Our system is designed to work efficiently with existing video data, streamlining the head synthesis process without the need for extensive manual intervention. Results/Findings: Evaluation of the Head2Head model demonstrates a significant improvement in the accuracy and realism of head animations compared to traditional methods. The system successfully synthesizes heads with a variety of expressions and angles, achieving a higher level of detail and fluidity. Comparative analyses indicate that our approach outperforms existing models in terms of visual authenticity and processing speed. Conclusion/Implications: The Head2Head approach makes strong contributions to the field of neural rendering and animation, offering a robust solution for applications in virtual reality, gaming, and digital media production. Our research provides a foundation for future advancements in automated video-based head synthesis, with potential to enhance interactive media experiences and content creation workflows. Key implications include the ability to customize and adapt human head models in real-time, fostering new possibilities in personalized digital experiences. Keywords: neural head synthesis, GAN, CNN, video-based rendering, head animation, real-time synthesis, virtual reality, digital media.

Object detection remains a critical challenge in computer vision, requiring accurate localization and classification of objects within complex scenes. This paper introduces RON (Reverse Connection with Objectness Prior Networks), a novel framework designed to enhance object detection performance by leveraging reverse connections and objectness priors. The proposed approach integrates a reverse connection mechanism to efficiently propagate multi-scale features, enabling the network to capture both fine-grained details and high-level semantic information. Additionally, objectness priors are incorporated to improve the detection of objects by focusing on regions with high object likelihood, reducing false positives and enhancing overall accuracy. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, such as PASCAL VOC and MS COCO, demonstrate that RON achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of both precision and recall. The framework is computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications. Key contributions include the novel reverse connection architecture and the integration of objectness priors, which collectively address limitations in multi-scale feature fusion and object localization. The findings highlight the potential of RON for advancing object detection in diverse applications, including autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics. This work provides a robust foundation for future research in improving detection accuracy and efficiency in complex visual environments. **Keywords**: Object detection, reverse connection, objectness prior, multi-scale feature fusion, computer vision, deep learning.

This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing molecular structures using deep reinforcement learning. The objective is to develop an efficient method for discovering molecules with desired properties, such as improved pharmacokinetics or enhanced chemical reactivity. Our approach employs a deep reinforcement learning framework, where an agent learns to modify molecular structures through a sequence of actions, with the goal of maximizing a reward function that reflects the desired properties. The method utilizes a combination of graph neural networks and reinforcement learning algorithms to efficiently explore the vast chemical space. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in optimizing molecules for various properties, outperforming traditional methods in terms of efficiency and accuracy. The key findings include the discovery of novel molecules with improved properties and the ability to generalize to new chemical spaces. This research contributes to the field of molecular optimization, enabling the rapid discovery of new molecules with potential applications in drug development, materials science, and chemistry. Key keywords: deep reinforcement learning, molecular optimization, graph neural networks, chemical space exploration.

The aim of this research is to enhance the performance of video captioning systems, which are imperative for automatic video understanding and real-time content generation, by introducing a novel Dynamic Loss Network (DLN) that adjusts loss functions dynamically to improve caption accuracy and coherency. Methods/Approach: Our approach involves developing a Dynamic Loss Network that leverages a combination of deep learning models, specifically, a recurrent neural network integrated with convolutional layers for video encoding, and an attention mechanism for accurate caption generation. The DLN continuously optimizes the loss function based on the variability of the input video features, allowing the model to adaptively focus on significant elements within a video sequence. Results/Findings: The proposed model was evaluated on several benchmark video captioning datasets, displaying significant improvements over traditional static loss models. Our results demonstrate a substantial boost in caption quality, as indicated by enhanced BLEU, METEOR, and CIDEr scores, outperforming existing state-of-the-art video captioning approaches. The dynamic loss adjustment allowed the model to better handle varied and complex video inputs. Conclusion/Implications: This study highlights the substantial benefits of employing a Dynamic Loss Network in video captioning, paving the way for more adaptive and precise caption generation in multimedia applications. The approach not only enhances system performance but also contributes to the broader field of video content analysis and understanding. Potential applications extend to automated video summarization, assistive technologies for the visually impaired, and advanced video content indexing systems, emphasizing the influence of dynamic loss optimization in complex AI-driven tasks. Keywords: video captioning, Dynamic Loss Network, deep learning, adaptive loss, recurrent neural network, attention mechanism, multimedia understanding.

Deep reinforcement learning (RL) has shown impressive results in a variety of domains, learning directly from high-dimensional sensory streams. However, when neural networks are trained in a fixed environment, such as a single level in a video game, they will usually overfit and fail to generalize to new levels. When RL models overfit, even slight modifications to the environment can result in poor agent performance. This paper explores how procedurally generated levels during training can increase generality. We show that for some games procedural level generation enables generalization to new levels within the same distribution. Additionally, it is possible to achieve better performance with less data by manipulating the difficulty of the levels in response to the performance of the agent. The generality of the learned behaviors is also evaluated on a set of human-designed levels. The results suggest that the ability to generalize to human-designed levels highly depends on the design of the level generators. We apply dimensionality reduction and clustering techniques to visualize the generators' distributions of levels and analyze to what degree they can produce levels similar to those designed by a human.

Few-shot learning (FSL) remains a significant challenge in machine learning, particularly in scenarios where limited labeled data is available. This paper introduces Sparse Spatial Transformers (SST), a novel approach designed to enhance few-shot learning by leveraging spatial attention mechanisms with sparsity constraints. The proposed SST framework dynamically focuses on the most relevant regions of input data, reducing computational overhead while improving feature extraction efficiency. By integrating sparse attention modules into a transformer-based architecture, SST achieves superior generalization capabilities with minimal labeled examples. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SST outperforms existing FSL methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The results highlight the model's ability to adapt to new tasks with limited data, making it a promising solution for real-world applications such as medical imaging and autonomous systems. This work contributes to the advancement of few-shot learning by introducing a computationally efficient and effective spatial attention mechanism, paving the way for future research in resource-constrained environments. **Keywords**: Few-shot learning, spatial transformers, sparse attention, transformers, machine learning, computational efficiency.

Anomaly detection in automotive Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) is crucial for ensuring safety and reliability against cyberattacks and system malfunctions. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging Deep Radial Basis Function (Deep-RBF) networks for robust anomaly detection in automotive CPS. The proposed Deep-RBF network architecture combines the representational power of deep learning with the inherent distance-based anomaly detection capabilities of RBF networks. Our methodology involves training the Deep-RBF network on normal operational data from various sensors within the automotive CPS, learning a high-dimensional feature representation of nominal system behavior. We evaluate the performance of our approach using a real-world automotive CPS dataset, demonstrating its ability to accurately detect a range of anomalies, including sensor manipulation attacks and actuator failures. Experimental results show that the Deep-RBF network outperforms traditional anomaly detection methods, achieving higher detection rates and lower false positive rates. The findings highlight the potential of Deep-RBF networks as an effective solution for enhancing the security and resilience of automotive CPS. Keywords: Anomaly Detection, Cyber-Physical Systems, Automotive Security, Deep Learning, Radial Basis Function Networks, Cybersecurity.

Deep learning segmentation methods have achieved state-of-the-art performance in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), enabling improved diagnostics and patient care. However, the widespread clinical adoption of these methods is hindered by concerns regarding their trustworthiness, particularly in terms of reliability, generalizability, and interpretability. This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing the trustworthiness of deep learning-based cardiac MRI segmentation by proposing a comprehensive framework that integrates uncertainty estimation, out-of-distribution detection, and explainable AI (XAI) techniques. The proposed approach employs a convolutional neural network architecture with Bayesian inference to quantify model confidence, alongside an anomaly detector to identify inputs that deviate from the training distribution. Furthermore, gradient-based visualization techniques are incorporated to provide interpretable insights into the model’s predictions. Experimental evaluation on multi-center, multi-vendor cardiac MRI datasets demonstrates improved segmentation accuracy, reduced failure modes on anomalous data, and increased transparency for end-users compared to standard black-box models. These findings suggest that our multi-faceted framework not only boosts the safety and reliability of deep learning segmentation for cardiac MRI but also fosters greater clinical confidence in AI-assisted diagnostic tools. The proposed solutions contribute to the advancement of trustworthy medical AI, paving the way for more robust integration of deep learning models in routine cardiac imaging workflows. Keywords: deep learning, segmentation, cardiac MRI, trustworthiness, uncertainty estimation, explainable AI, out-of-distribution detection.

This paper presents a novel voting-based multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework designed to enhance decision-making in intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) environments. The objective of this research is to address the challenges of scalability, adaptability, and coordination among heterogeneous IoT devices operating in dynamic and distributed settings. Our approach integrates a voting mechanism into the MARL process, enabling agents to collectively evaluate and select optimal actions while considering network constraints and individual device preferences. Extensive simulations are conducted using realistic IoT scenarios, such as smart energy management and adaptive traffic control. The results demonstrate that the proposed method improves system-wide performance metrics, including resource utilization, response time, and fault tolerance, compared to conventional centralized and non-voting-based MARL strategies. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robust adaptation to changes in environment topologies and agent populations. These findings highlight the effectiveness of incorporating collective decision-making through voting in distributed IoT systems. The proposed methodology contributes to advancing smart IoT applications by providing a scalable, flexible, and resilient solution for multi-agent coordination. Keywords: multi-agent reinforcement learning, voting mechanism, Internet of Things, distributed decision-making, intelligent systems.

This paper presents an empirical study on semi-supervised learning using IPM-based Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The objective is to investigate the effectiveness of IPM-based GANs in improving the performance of semi-supervised learning models. We employ an IPM-based GAN framework, which integrates the IPM algorithm with a GAN architecture, to generate high-quality synthetic samples that augment the limited labeled dataset. Our approach utilizes a combination of labeled and unlabeled data to train the model, leveraging the IPM algorithm to optimize the generator and discriminator networks. The results show that our IPM-based GAN approach outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning methods, achieving significant improvements in classification accuracy and robustness. The key findings of this study highlight the potential of IPM-based GANs in semi-supervised learning, particularly in scenarios where labeled data is scarce. Our research contributes to the development of more efficient and effective semi-supervised learning models, with potential applications in areas such as image classification, natural language processing, and computer vision. Key keywords: semi-supervised learning, IPM-based GANs, generative models, deep learning, classification accuracy.
