Objective: High-quality object detection demands precise localization and classification, yet existing single-stage and two-stage detectors often underperform at stringent intersection-over-union (IoU) thresholds. This paper introduces Cascade R-CNN, a multi-stage extension of the R-CNN framework designed to address the quality mismatch between training and inference and to progressively refine detection results. Methods: Cascade R-CNN employs a sequence of detection heads trained with increasing IoU thresholds. Each stage takes the outputs of its predecessor as proposals, enabling the network to focus on progressively harder examples and to optimize for higher-quality localization. The architecture integrates standard region proposal networks (RPN) and bounding-box regression branches, with shared convolutional features. Training proceeds end-to-end, balancing classification and regression losses at each cascade stage. Results: Experiments on the challenging MS COCO benchmark demonstrate substantial gains over baseline detectors. Cascade R-CNN improves average precision (AP) by 3.5 points at IoU≥0.5 and by 5.2 points at IoU≥0.75, outperforming contemporary state-of-the-art models. Detailed ablation studies confirm that both the multi-stage design and stage-wise IoU adaptation contribute critically to enhanced detection quality. Conclusion: By systematically aligning training objectives with high-IoU inference requirements, Cascade R-CNN achieves robust and precise object detection across varying quality measures. Its modular design can be readily incorporated into existing two-stage detectors, offering a versatile solution for applications in autonomous driving, surveillance, and image understanding. Keywords: object detection, Cascade R-CNN, multi-stage detector, IoU thresholds, bounding-box regression, MS COCO.

Game architectureA common technique that is typically shown in beginner-level game develop ment is to organize game objects in a hierarchical manner. While this approachworks for small game, the practice of organizing game objects in a hierarchy in troduce inflexibility and maintenance problem. A good game object system mustbe scalable such that game object types can be added easily to the system regard less of the number of types already defined. Unity engine, amongst numerousother game engines, provides developers with component-based game object sys tem which uses composition, rather than inheritance, to define game object typesand their behaviors. Game objects are the fundamental objects in Unity that repre sent the actors of the game world (characters, props and scenery). A game objectdefines their functionalities and behaviors through a list of components. For exam ple, a solid cube object has a MeshFilter andMeshRenderer component, to draw the surface of the cube, and a BoxCollider component to represent the object’s solid volume in terms of physics.

Deep Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) have achieved significant performance on single image super-resolution (SR) recently. However, existing CNN-based methods use artificially synthetic low-resolution (LR) and high-resolution (HR) image pairs to train networks, which cannot handle real-world cases since the degradation from HR to LR is much more complex than manually designed. To solve this problem, we propose a real-world LR images guided bi-cycle network for single image super-resolution, in which the bidirectional structural consistency is exploited to train both the degradation and SR reconstruction networks in an unsupervised way. Specifically, we propose a degradation network to model the real-world degradation process from HR to LR via generative adversarial networks, and these generated realistic LR images paired with real-world HR images are exploited for training the SR reconstruction network, forming the first cycle. Then in the second reverse cycle, consistency of real-world LR images are exploited to further stabilize the training of SR reconstruction and degradation networks. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world images demonstrate that the proposed algorithm performs favorably against state-of-the-art single image SR methods.

Reinforcement learning has been found useful in solving optimal power flow (OPF) problems in electric power distribution systems. However, the use of largely model-free reinforcement learning algorithms that completely ignore the physics-based modeling of the power grid compromises the optimizer performance and poses scalability challenges. This paper proposes a novel approach to synergistically combine the physics-based models with learning-based algorithms using imitation learning to solve distribution-level OPF problems. Specifically, we propose imitation learning based improvements in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods to solve the OPF problem for a specific case of battery storage dispatch in the power distribution systems. The proposed imitation learning algorithm uses the approximate optimal solutions obtained from a linearized model-based OPF solver to provide a good initial policy for the DRL algorithms while improving the training efficiency. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated using IEEE 34-bus and 123-bus distribution feeders with numerous distribution-level battery storage systems.

Objective: We present EgoFace, a novel framework for real-time egocentric face performance capture and videorealistic reenactment. This work addresses the challenges of limited field-of-view, self-occlusions, and varying illumination inherent to inward-facing camera setups used in head-mounted devices. Methods: EgoFace employs a two-stage deep learning pipeline. First, a convolutional network estimates a complete 3D face mesh and expression parameters from partial, egocentric video frames, leveraging a parametric morphable model and a texture completion module to fill occluded regions. Second, a neural rendering stage combines learned appearance priors with dynamic lighting adaptation to generate photorealistic reenactment on a target avatar. The entire system is trained end-to-end on a curated dataset of synchronized multi-view facial recordings under diverse expressions and environments. Results: Quantitative evaluation shows that EgoFace reduces geometric reconstruction error by 25% and achieves a 0.18 gain in perceptual image similarity (LPIPS) compared to state-of-the-art headset-based methods. Qualitative user studies report high identity preservation and expression fidelity. The framework runs at over 30 fps on a single GPU, supporting live applications. Conclusion: EgoFace delivers the first egocentric solution for high-fidelity face capture and videorealistic reenactment, enabling immersive telepresence, social VR interactions, and next-generation gaming experiences. Keywords: egocentric capture, face performance, videorealistic reenactment, neural rendering, 3D reconstruction.

This paper addresses the challenge of inferring the structure of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) from observed data, a crucial problem in various fields such as physics, biology, and engineering. Our objective is to develop a novel approach that can accurately identify the underlying ODEs that govern complex systems. We propose a machine learning-based method that utilizes a combination of symbolic regression and neural networks to learn the structure of ODEs from data. Our approach is able to handle noisy and incomplete data, and can infer ODEs with non-linear and non-polynomial terms. The results show that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness, and can be applied to a wide range of problems, including population dynamics, chemical kinetics, and electrical circuits. The key contributions of this research are the development of a flexible and scalable framework for inferring ODEs, and the demonstration of its effectiveness in real-world applications. Our work has important implications for fields such as systems biology, control theory, and data-driven modeling, and can be used to discover new mathematical models that can inform and improve our understanding of complex systems. Key keywords: ordinary differential equations, machine learning, symbolic regression, neural networks, data-driven modeling.

This paper introduces a novel Multivariate Bayesian Structural Time Series (MBSTS) model designed for enhanced forecasting and causal inference in complex, high-dimensional time series data. Addressing the limitations of traditional univariate approaches, our MBSTS model leverages a Bayesian framework to capture intricate dependencies and dynamic relationships among multiple time series. The methodology incorporates a hierarchical structure with time-varying coefficients and latent factors, enabling the model to adapt to evolving patterns and uncertainties. We develop an efficient Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm for posterior inference, providing robust estimates of model parameters and forecasts. Empirical evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including financial and economic indicators, demonstrate superior performance compared to existing state-space models and vector autoregression (VAR) techniques. The MBSTS model exhibits improved forecast accuracy, more reliable causal effect estimates, and enhanced interpretability through component decomposition. These results highlight the potential of the MBSTS model for a wide range of applications, including macroeconomic forecasting, financial risk management, and anomaly detection. Keywords: Bayesian time series, structural time series, multivariate models, MCMC, forecasting, causal inference.

Abstract: Text localisation in natural images presents significant challenges due to diverse backgrounds, distortions, and varying lighting conditions. This paper explores the generation and application of synthetic data to improve the performance of text localisation models. We propose a novel framework for creating high-quality synthetic datasets that mimic real-world conditions by integrating advanced image augmentation techniques, diverse font rendering, and realistic scene composition. Our approach enables the generation of large-scale annotated datasets, significantly reducing the reliance on costly and time-consuming manual labelling. We evaluate state-of-the-art deep learning models, including convolutional and transformer-based architectures, trained solely on our synthetic datasets and demonstrate robust performance on standard real-world benchmarks. Comparative analysis shows that models pre-trained on synthetic data and fine-tuned with limited real data achieve accuracy rates comparable to, or exceeding, models trained on extensive real datasets. The results highlight the capability of synthetic data to close the domain gap, increasing generalisation and efficiency for text localisation tasks. This research underlines the value of synthetic data generation for advancing scene text detection and supports its wider adoption in computer vision applications involving document analysis, augmented reality, and intelligent navigation systems. Key keywords: synthetic data, text localisation, natural images, deep learning, computer vision, scene text detection, data augmentation.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficient knowledge transfer in deep reinforcement learning, with the objective of developing a real-time policy distillation framework. Our approach leverages a novel combination of online learning and distillation techniques, enabling the transfer of knowledge from a complex teacher policy to a simpler student policy in real-time. The method utilizes a custom-designed architecture that facilitates simultaneous learning and distillation, allowing the student policy to adapt rapidly to changing environments. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in policy performance and efficiency, outperforming traditional distillation methods. The key findings highlight the effectiveness of our framework in reducing the complexity of deep reinforcement learning models while preserving their accuracy. This research contributes to the field by providing a real-time policy distillation approach, with potential applications in areas such as robotics, game playing, and autonomous systems, and is particularly relevant to keywords such as deep reinforcement learning, policy distillation, real-time learning, and knowledge transfer.

Adaptive traffic signal control is crucial for managing urban traffic congestion. This paper investigates the application of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to optimize traffic flow and minimize congestion. We propose a novel DRL-based traffic control framework that dynamically adjusts signal timings in response to real-time traffic conditions. Our approach incorporates a state representation that captures both local and network-wide traffic patterns, along with a reward function designed to incentivize efficient traffic flow and reduce queue lengths. The proposed method is evaluated using a realistic traffic simulation environment and compared against state-of-the-art traffic control algorithms, including fixed-time and actuated signal control strategies, as well as existing DRL approaches. Results demonstrate that our framework achieves significant improvements in terms of average travel time, queue length, and overall network throughput. Specifically, our model outperforms existing DRL methods by 15% in reducing average vehicle delay. This research contributes a practical and scalable DRL solution for intelligent transportation systems, paving the way for more efficient and sustainable urban mobility. Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Traffic Control, Intelligent Transportation Systems, Adaptive Signal Control, Traffic Optimization.

Estimating causal effects from observational data is a central challenge in fields such as healthcare, economics, and social sciences. Traditional machine learning methods, while powerful, often falter when faced with limited labeled data or varying data distributions across domains. This paper investigates the application of transfer learning techniques in conjunction with neural networks to enhance the estimation of causal effects. We propose a novel framework that leverages representations learned from large source domains and adapts them for causal inference in target domains with scarce data. Our approach utilizes deep neural architectures augmented with domain adaptation modules to align feature distributions and mitigate confounding bias. Comprehensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing causal inference models, especially in scenarios with domain shift or data scarcity. We further conduct ablation studies to assess the contribution of each component within our framework. The results highlight the robustness and flexibility of transfer learning in improving causal estimation accuracy. This research underscores the potential of integrating transfer learning and deep learning for practical and scalable causal effect estimation, with implications for policy analysis, personalized medicine, and other data-driven decision-making applications. Key keywords: causal inference, transfer learning, neural networks, domain adaptation, treatment effect estimation, deep learning.

The generation of high-quality 3D point clouds using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has gained significant attention in recent years. However, existing methods often struggle with sampling inefficiencies, leading to suboptimal point distributions and reduced fidelity in generated outputs. This paper addresses these challenges by rethinking the sampling strategies employed in 3D point cloud GANs. We propose a novel adaptive sampling mechanism that dynamically adjusts point density based on local geometric features, ensuring more accurate and realistic reconstructions. Our approach leverages a hybrid architecture combining spatial transformers and attention mechanisms to enhance the network's ability to capture fine-grained details. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of point cloud quality, with significant improvements in Chamfer Distance and Earth Mover's Distance metrics. Furthermore, the proposed framework exhibits superior scalability and computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-world applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. This work contributes to advancing 3D generative modeling by introducing a robust and adaptive sampling paradigm, paving the way for more reliable and high-fidelity point cloud generation. **Keywords**: 3D point clouds, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), adaptive sampling, spatial transformers, attention mechanisms, 3D reconstruction.

Ứng dụng meeting dựa trên video conferencing sử dụng công nghệ WebRTC đã trở thành một giải pháp tối ưu cho việc kết nối người dùng từ xa, cho phép họ tham gia vào các cuộc thảo luận, hội nghị và hợp tác mà không cần phải gặp mặt trực tiếp. Đồng thời, các thách thức trong việc đảm bảo an ninh và bảo mật thông tin trong quá trình truyền tải cũng sẽ được thảo luận. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy ứng dụng meeting dựa trên WebRTC không chỉ đáp ứng nhu cầu giao tiếp trong thời đại số mà còn mở ra hướng đi mới cho các doanh nghiệp trong việc tối ưu hóa quy trình làm việc và nâng cao hiệu quả hợp tác.

This paper addresses the challenge of enabling autonomous agents to learn cooperative behaviors in multi-agent systems through policy search methods. The objective is to develop a framework that allows agents to efficiently adapt their policies to achieve shared goals without explicit communication or centralized control. We propose a novel decentralized reinforcement learning approach that leverages policy gradient methods to optimize cooperative strategies in dynamic and uncertain environments. Our method incorporates a reward-sharing mechanism to align individual agent objectives with the collective goal, ensuring scalable and robust cooperation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional centralized and independent learning methods in terms of convergence speed and task performance across various cooperative scenarios, including resource allocation and collaborative navigation. The findings highlight the potential of decentralized policy search for applications in robotics, swarm intelligence, and multi-agent systems, offering a scalable solution for real-world cooperative tasks. Key contributions include a flexible framework for cooperative learning, improved scalability, and empirical validation of its effectiveness in complex environments. Keywords: multi-agent systems, reinforcement learning, policy search, cooperation, decentralized control.

A significant challenge in developing AI that can generalize well is designing agents that learn about their world without being told what to learn, and apply that learning to challenges with sparse rewards. Moreover, most traditional reinforcement learning approaches explicitly separate learning and decision making in a way that does not correspond to biological learning. We implement an architecture founded in principles of experimental neuroscience, by combining computationally efficient abstractions of biological algorithms. Our approach is inspired by research on spike-timing dependent plasticity, the transition between short and long term memory, and the role of various neurotransmitters in rewarding curiosity. The Neurons-in-a-Box architecture can learn in a wholly generalizable manner, and demonstrates an efficient way to build and apply representations without explicitly optimizing over a set of criteria or actions. We find it performs well in many environments including OpenAI Gym's Mountain Car, which has no reward besides touching a hard-to-reach flag on a hill, Inverted Pendulum, where it learns simple strategies to improve the time it holds a pendulum up, a video stream, where it spontaneously learns to distinguish an open and closed hand, as well as other environments like Google Chrome's Dinosaur Game.

This paper introduces LRCN-RetailNet, a novel recurrent neural network architecture designed for accurate and robust people counting in retail environments. The objective is to address the challenges of varying crowd densities, occlusions, and illumination changes that significantly impact the performance of traditional counting methods. LRCN-RetailNet combines convolutional layers for feature extraction with long short-term memory (LSTM) layers to model temporal dependencies in video sequences. The architecture is trained end-to-end to directly predict people counts from video frames. Experimental results on a newly collected retail dataset, as well as publicly available benchmarks, demonstrate that LRCN-RetailNet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in people counting, outperforming existing methods by a significant margin, particularly in crowded scenes. The proposed approach offers a practical solution for real-time occupancy monitoring and customer behavior analysis in retail settings. Keywords: People Counting, Recurrent Neural Networks, LSTM, Retail, Video Analysis, Crowd Management.

This paper introduces a novel adversarial feature learning framework to achieve controllable invariance in learned representations. The objective is to enable models to be sensitive to specific variations in the input data while remaining invariant to others, enhancing generalization and fairness. Our approach employs a multi-objective adversarial training strategy, where a feature extractor is trained to preserve task-relevant information, while an adversarial network simultaneously attempts to predict protected attributes from the learned features. A control mechanism, based on a regularization parameter, allows for fine-grained adjustment of the invariance level for each protected attribute. We evaluate our method on image classification and fairness-aware prediction tasks, demonstrating its ability to selectively mitigate bias related to sensitive attributes without sacrificing accuracy on the primary task. Results show significant improvements over existing invariance learning techniques, offering a more flexible and effective solution for building robust and fair machine learning models. Key words: adversarial learning, invariance, feature learning, fairness, bias mitigation, machine learning.

A key, also known as a cryptographic key, is a fragment of information utilized incryptographic algorithms for a variety of purposes, including encryption, decryp tion, and digital signatures. Typically, in the context of blockchain, keys are used to secure access to digital assets and to authenticate transactions. There are various mathematically related key categories, including private and public keys. A private key is a secret, randomly generated number that is kept covert by the user. It is usedto generate digital signatures, which verify the integrity and authenticity of trans actions. The private key should be stored in a secure location and never shared with anyone. If a third party obtains access to the private key, they may be able to take control of the associated digital assets. On the other hand, an address is a cryptographic representation of a user’s public key. In a blockchain network, it is a string of alphanumeric characters that functions as a unique identifier for receiving transactions or messages. The public key is used to generate addresses, but they do not disclose any information about the private key. When sending a transaction to a particular user in a blockchain network, the recipient’s address is used as thedestination. The address functions as a pseudonymous identifier, providing privacy and security. The recipient can then access and manage the digital assets associated with that address using their private key.

Xây dựng công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật của phần mềm Web là một vấn đề cấp thiết trong lĩnh vực công nghệ thông tin. Với sự phát triển nhanh chóng của công nghệ Web, phần mềm Web ngày càng trở nên phức tạp và dễ bị tấn công bởi các loại malware và exploits khác nhau. Do đó, việc xây dựng một công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật hiệu quả là cần thiết để đảm bảo an toàn và bảo mật cho phần mềm Web. Công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật được thiết kế để tự động hóa quá trình kiểm thử và phân tích lỗi của phần mềm Web. Công cụ này sử dụng các kỹ thuật kiểm thử và phân tích lỗi tiên tiến để phát hiện và phân tích các lỗi an toàn bảo mật trong phần mềm Web. Công cụ này cũng cung cấp các tính năng quản lý lỗi để giúp người dùng theo dõi và quản lý các lỗi an toàn bảo mật đã được phát hiện. Công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật được xây dựng dựa trên các nguyên tắc và tiêu chuẩn an toàn bảo mật hiện đại. Công cụ này được thiết kế để dễ dàng sử dụng và tích hợp với các hệ thống quản lý dự án và kiểm thử khác nhau. Công cụ này cũng được thiết kế để cung cấp các báo cáo và phân tích chi tiết về các lỗi an toàn bảo mật đã được phát hiện. Tổng quan, công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật của phần mềm Web là một công cụ quan trọng trong việc đảm bảo an toàn và bảo mật cho phần mềm Web. Công cụ này giúp người dùng phát hiện và phân tích các lỗi an toàn bảo mật hiệu quả, đồng thời cung cấp các tính năng quản lý lỗi để giúp người dùng theo dõi và quản lý các lỗi an toàn bảo mật đã được phát hiện.

Smart home environments are designed to provide services that help improve the quality of life for the occupant via a variety of sensors and actuators installed throughout the space. Many automated actions taken by a smart home are governed by the output of an underlying activity recognition system. However, activity recognition systems may not be perfectly accurate and therefore inconsistencies in smart home operations can lead a user to wonder "why did the smart home do that?" In this work, we build on insights from Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques to contribute computational methods for explainable activity recognition. Specifically, we generate explanations for smart home activity recognition systems that explain what about an activity led to the given classification. To do so, we introduce four computational techniques for generating natural language explanations of smart home data and compare their effectiveness at generating meaningful explanations. Through a study with everyday users, we evaluate user preferences towards the four explanation types. Our results show that the leading approach, SHAP, has a 92% success rate in generating accurate explanations. Moreover, 84% of sampled scenarios users preferred natural language explanations over a simple activity label, underscoring the need for explainable activity recognition systems. Finally, we show that explanations generated by some XAI methods can lead users to lose confidence in the accuracy of the underlying activity recognition model, while others lead users to gain confidence. Taking all studied factors into consideration, we make a recommendation regarding which existing XAI method leads to the best performance in the domain of smart home automation, and discuss a range of topics for future work in this area.

Nghiên cứu phân phối điện năng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc nâng cao hiệu suất phát điện của các nhà máy thủy điện, đặc biệt là nhà máy Hoàng Công. Việc tối ưu hóa hệ thống phân phối giúp đảm bảo nguồn điện ổn định, giảm thiểu thất thoát năng lượng và tăng khả năng đáp ứng nhu cầu tiêu thụ. Các giải pháp kỹ thuật như điều chỉnh lưu lượng nước, cải tiến tua-bin và tích hợp công nghệ quản lý thông minh được đề xuất để nâng cao hiệu quả vận hành. Nghiên cứu cũng nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc kết hợp nguồn năng lượng tái tạo khác nhằm đảm bảo tính bền vững và giảm phụ thuộc vào nguồn nước. Kết quả nghiên cứu hứa hẹn mang lại lợi ích kinh tế và môi trường, góp phần phát triển ngành điện lực một cách toàn diện.
Không có cơ chế giám sát và kiểm soát: Với số lượng lớn các trang web và các kênh chia sẻ tập tin trực tuyến, việc giám sát và kiểm soát việc phân phối tác phẩm trở nên rất khó khăn.

Di cư quốc tế từ Bangladesh có ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến chi tiêu tiêu dùng của các hộ gia đình. Các nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp đối sánh cho thấy, so với các hộ không có người di cư, những hộ có thành viên di cư quốc tế có xu hướng tăng chi tiêu đáng kể cho các mặt hàng thiết yếu như thực phẩm, quần áo, giáo dục và chăm sóc sức khỏe. Lượng kiều hối từ người thân ở nước ngoài đóng vai trò quan trọng, giúp các gia đình cải thiện điều kiện sống, tiếp cận các dịch vụ tốt hơn và đầu tư vào tương lai. Tuy nhiên, di cư cũng có thể dẫn đến sự thay đổi trong cơ cấu chi tiêu, với việc giảm chi cho một số mặt hàng truyền thống và tăng chi cho các sản phẩm hiện đại hơn. Đồng thời, việc thiếu hụt lao động do di cư có thể ảnh hưởng đến sản xuất nông nghiệp và thu nhập ở một số vùng. Do đó, các chính sách hỗ trợ cần được thiết kế để tối đa hóa lợi ích kinh tế từ kiều hối và giảm thiểu tác động tiêu cực của di cư đến kinh tế địa phương.

Nghiên cứu đánh giá vai trò của cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán (DW-MRI) trong chẩn đoán ung thư tế bào gai dương vật (SCC). DW-MRI, với khả năng phát hiện những thay đổi vi cấu trúc ở cấp độ tế bào, cho thấy tiềm năng lớn trong việc phân biệt giữa các tổn thương ác tính và lành tính, cũng như đánh giá mức độ xâm lấn của ung thư. Các chỉ số khuếch tán, như hệ số khuếch tán biểu kiến (ADC), có thể cung cấp thông tin định lượng hữu ích, hỗ trợ chẩn đoán chính xác và lập kế hoạch điều trị phù hợp. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc xác định giá trị của DW-MRI trong việc cải thiện chẩn đoán SCC dương vật, từ đó giúp bác sĩ đưa ra quyết định điều trị kịp thời và hiệu quả hơn, góp phần nâng cao chất lượng sống cho bệnh nhân.

Tăng cường năng lực chứng nhận để phát triển ngành Halal tại Việt Nam Ngành Halal đang trở thành một phần quan trọng của nền kinh tế Việt Nam, với nhu cầu ngày càng tăng về sản phẩm và dịch vụ đáp ứng tiêu chuẩn Halal. Để đáp ứng nhu cầu này, việc tăng cường năng lực chứng nhận Halal là một bước quan trọng để phát triển ngành này. Hiện tại, Việt Nam đã có một số tổ chức chứng nhận Halal được công nhận quốc tế, nhưng vẫn còn nhiều hạn chế về năng lực và quy mô. Để khắc phục tình trạng này, cần tăng cường đầu tư vào cơ sở hạ tầng, đào tạo và phát triển nhân lực để nâng cao năng lực chứng nhận Halal. Bên cạnh đó, cần có sự hợp tác và phối hợp giữa các tổ chức chứng nhận Halal, các doanh nghiệp và cơ quan quản lý để tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho việc chứng nhận và kiểm tra Halal. Điều này sẽ giúp tăng cường niềm tin của người tiêu dùng và mở rộng thị trường cho các sản phẩm và dịch vụ Halal. Tăng cường năng lực chứng nhận Halal sẽ giúp Việt Nam trở thành một trung tâm chứng nhận Halal quan trọng tại khu vực và trên thế giới, đồng thời tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho việc phát triển ngành Halal tại Việt Nam.

Biến đổi khí hậu đang gây ra những tác động đáng kể đến hệ thống giao thông, đặc biệt là các tuyến đường bộ ven biển tại tỉnh Kiên Giang. Nghiên cứu này tập trung phân tích ảnh hưởng của nhiệt độ tăng cao do biến đổi khí hậu lên cơ sở hạ tầng giao thông, bao gồm hiện tượng nứt vỡ mặt đường, giảm độ bền của vật liệu và nguy cơ ngập lụt do nước biển dâng. Kết quả cho thấy, nhiệt độ cao kết hợp với độ ẩm lớn đẩy nhanh quá trình xuống cấp của đường, đặc biệt ở những khu vực có nền đất yếu. Ngoài ra, tần suất các cơn bão và triều cường ngày càng gia tăng cũng đe dọa nghiêm trọng đến an toàn giao thông và tuổi thọ của công trình. Để ứng phó, các giải pháp như sử dụng vật liệu chịu nhiệt, nâng cao nền đường và xây dựng hệ thống thoát nước hiệu quả được đề xuất nhằm đảm bảo tính bền vững cho hệ thống giao thông trong tương lai.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc chuyển gen Xa7 kháng vi khuẩn bạc lá vào dòng phục hồi nhằm phát triển lúa lai hai dòng. Vi khuẩn bạc lá là một trong những tác nhân gây hại nghiêm trọng cho cây lúa, ảnh hưởng đến năng suất và chất lượng nông sản. Việc ứng dụng công nghệ sinh học để chuyển gen kháng bệnh vào cây lúa không chỉ giúp tăng cường khả năng chống chịu mà còn góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả sản xuất nông nghiệp. Dòng lúa lai hai dòng được tạo ra từ quá trình này hứa hẹn sẽ mang lại những giống lúa có khả năng kháng bệnh tốt hơn, từ đó giảm thiểu sự phụ thuộc vào thuốc bảo vệ thực vật và đảm bảo an toàn cho môi trường. Kết quả nghiên cứu có thể mở ra hướng đi mới trong việc phát triển giống lúa chất lượng cao, bền vững và thích ứng với điều kiện khí hậu ngày càng biến đổi.

This paper presents a novel approach to hue modification localization by leveraging pair matching techniques. The objective is to accurately identify and localize regions of an image where the hue has been modified, which is crucial for various applications such as image forensics and authentication. Our method employs a deep learning-based framework that utilizes pair matching to compare the original and modified images, enabling the detection of subtle hue changes. The approach involves training a neural network to learn the patterns and relationships between the paired images, allowing for effective localization of hue modifications. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our method, outperforming existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed technique has significant implications for image forensics, authentication, and security, and contributes to the development of more sophisticated image analysis tools. Key contributions include the introduction of pair matching for hue modification localization and the demonstration of its potential in real-world applications, highlighting the importance of this research in the fields of computer vision, image processing, and machine learning.

Rèn luyện nghiệp vụ sư phạm cho sinh viên khoa Giáo dục thể chất và Giáo dục quốc phòng tại Trường Đại học Phú Yên là một hoạt động quan trọng nhằm nâng cao chất lượng đào tạo và đáp ứng yêu cầu ngày càng cao của ngành giáo dục. Chương trình này không chỉ trang bị cho sinh viên kiến thức lý thuyết mà còn chú trọng vào thực hành, giúp họ phát triển kỹ năng giảng dạy, quản lý lớp học và tổ chức các hoạt động thể chất. Thông qua các buổi thực tập, sinh viên có cơ hội áp dụng những gì đã học vào thực tế, từ đó nâng cao khả năng tự tin và sáng tạo trong công việc giảng dạy. Đặc biệt, chương trình còn khuyến khích sinh viên tham gia các hoạt động ngoại khóa, tạo điều kiện cho họ rèn luyện kỹ năng mềm và xây dựng mối quan hệ xã hội, góp phần hình thành những giáo viên có tâm và có tầm trong tương lai.

Stereo depth estimation is a fundamental task in computer vision, crucial for applications such as autonomous driving, 3D scene reconstruction, and robotics. This paper introduces MTStereo 2.0, an enhanced framework for stereo depth estimation that harnesses the power of Max-trees, a hierarchical image representation method, to achieve improved accuracy and robustness. Our approach leverages Max-trees to effectively encode local and global spatial structures, facilitating more precise matching and disparity computation between stereo image pairs. We integrate Max-tree features within a modern deep learning architecture, enabling end-to-end training and optimization. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that MTStereo 2.0 outperforms existing state-of-the-art stereo matching methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency. Notably, our method shows significant improvements in challenging scenarios involving textureless regions and occlusions. The results affirm the benefits of incorporating Max-tree representations for depth estimation tasks. MTStereo 2.0 offers a scalable and adaptable solution suitable for real-time applications requiring reliable depth perception. Keywords: stereo depth estimation, Max-trees, disparity computation, computer vision, 3D reconstruction, deep learning, image matching.

Distributed learning offers significant advantages in training machine learning models across multiple devices, but it also introduces vulnerabilities to malicious attacks such as data poisoning and model manipulation. This paper introduces Aspis, a novel robust detection system designed to identify and mitigate malicious contributions in distributed learning environments. Aspis employs a multi-faceted approach, combining statistical analysis of model updates, anomaly detection techniques, and a reputation-based scoring system to assess the trustworthiness of participating devices. We evaluate Aspis on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in detecting various attack strategies, including Byzantine attacks and targeted poisoning attacks. The results show that Aspis achieves a high detection rate with minimal impact on model accuracy and convergence speed compared to existing defense mechanisms. Aspis provides a practical and efficient solution for securing distributed learning systems, enabling reliable model training in adversarial settings. Keywords: Distributed Learning, Security, Anomaly Detection, Data Poisoning, Robustness, Byzantine Fault Tolerance.

Khi xe dừng lại do đèn đỏ hoặc do một xe khác đang chịu tác động của đèn đỏ, ta sẽ lưu lại các giá trị về thờ gan dừng, giá trị này sẽ có tác dụng đánh giá độ hiệu quả của tín hiệu đèn giao thông, từ đó đưa ra các mức điểm thưởng phù hợp.

Traffic Server Máy chủ xử lý các yêu cầu lưu lượng truy cập của người dùng và định tuyến chúng điến các thành phần thích hợp. Phản hồi từ các thành phần bên trong thường được chuyển qua máy chủ lưu lượng điện FrontEnd Systems.
Thiết kế cho tết gói Web server được thiết kế và chia thành các gói router, controller, service, repos tory, model.

Bã rượu, một phụ phẩm từ quá trình sản xuất rượu, đang được nghiên cứu về tiềm năng làm thức ăn chăn nuôi lợn tại ba tỉnh phía Bắc. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc đánh giá giá trị dinh dưỡng của bã rượu, khả năng tận dụng nguồn nguyên liệu sẵn có tại địa phương, và hiệu quả kinh tế khi sử dụng trong chăn nuôi. Kết quả ban đầu cho thấy bã rượu có hàm lượng protein và chất xơ cao, phù hợp để bổ sung vào khẩu phần ăn của lợn, giúp giảm chi phí thức ăn và tăng lợi nhuận cho nông hộ. Nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra rằng việc sử dụng bã rượu cần được kiểm soát chặt chẽ về liều lượng để đảm bảo sức khỏe và tăng trưởng của đàn lợn. Đây là hướng đi tiềm năng trong việc tận dụng phụ phẩm nông nghiệp, góp phần phát triển bền vững ngành chăn nuôi.

Các quốc gia đang phát triển phải đối mặt với những tổn thất và thiệt hại to lớn do biến đổi khí hậu gây ra, vượt quá khả năng thích ứng. Cơ chế quốc tế Warsaw (WIM) về tổn thất và thiệt hại được thành lập để giải quyết vấn đề này, song vẫn còn nhiều tranh cãi về trách nhiệm pháp lý và tài chính. Các nước phát triển thường phản đối việc bồi thường, trong khi các nước đang phát triển kêu gọi nguồn tài chính mới và bổ sung. Quỹ tổn thất và thiệt hại được thông qua tại COP27 là một bước tiến quan trọng, nhưng việc triển khai hiệu quả vẫn là thách thức. Các cuộc đàm phán quốc tế cần tập trung vào việc xác định rõ nguồn tài chính, cơ chế phân phối công bằng và minh bạch, cũng như tăng cường hợp tác quốc tế để giảm thiểu và giải quyết tổn thất và thiệt hại do biến đổi khí hậu gây ra, đặc biệt là ở các quốc gia dễ bị tổn thương nhất.

Hôm nay, một dự án đầy tham vọng đã được công bố, hướng đến việc xây dựng một khu công nghệ cao tại Hòa Lạc, với mục tiêu trở thành thành phố khoa học, công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo. Dự án này sẽ tập trung vào việc phát triển các công nghệ tiên tiến, tạo ra môi trường thuận lợi cho các doanh nghiệp khởi nghiệp và đổi mới sáng tạo. Khu công nghệ cao sẽ bao gồm các khu vực như khu nghiên cứu và phát triển, khu sản xuất và kinh doanh, khu đào tạo và huấn luyện. Dự án này sẽ được thực hiện trong nhiều năm tới, với sự tham gia của các tổ chức và doanh nghiệp trong nước và quốc tế. Mục tiêu của dự án này là tạo ra một trung tâm đổi mới sáng tạo và phát triển công nghệ, giúp thúc đẩy sự phát triển kinh tế và xã hội của khu vực. Dự án này cũng sẽ giúp tạo ra các cơ hội việc làm mới và nâng cao chất lượng cuộc sống cho người dân. Dự án này sẽ được thực hiện với sự hỗ trợ của các cơ quan chức năng và các tổ chức quốc tế. Dự án này sẽ giúp tạo ra một tương lai sáng sủa và phát triển cho khu vực.

Đào tạo đại học theo chuẩn đầu ra là một hệ thống giáo dục tập trung vào việc trang bị cho sinh viên những kiến thức, kỹ năng và năng lực cụ thể, đáp ứng yêu cầu của thị trường lao động và xã hội. Thay vì chỉ chú trọng vào nội dung giảng dạy, phương pháp này đặt trọng tâm vào việc sinh viên có thể làm được gì sau khi tốt nghiệp. Quá trình đào tạo được thiết kế dựa trên các chuẩn đầu ra rõ ràng, được xác định thông qua khảo sát nhu cầu của các nhà tuyển dụng và các bên liên quan. Objective: Effective deployment of machine learning (ML) models in clinical settings remains a critical challenge due to complexities in data governance, interpretability, and integration with existing workflows. This study presents a comprehensive framework that guides healthcare organizations through the end-to-end process of clinical ML deployment, ensuring safety, reliability, and user acceptance. Methods: We developed a modular pipeline that addresses key phases—data acquisition and preprocessing, model development and validation, regulatory and ethical compliance, system integration, and post‐deployment monitoring. The pipeline incorporates privacy-preserving techniques (e.g., federated learning), interpretable model architectures, and human‐in‐the‐loop evaluations. We validated the framework on two real‐world case studies: predicting hospital readmission risk and automating diabetic retinopathy screening. Results: Compared to conventional ad hoc deployment strategies, our framework reduced model integration time by 35% and improved clinician trust scores by 20% in user surveys. Federated learning approaches achieved on‐site model performance within 2% of centralized baselines while maintaining patient data locality. Interpretability modules enabled faster error analysis, decreasing false‐positive alerts by 15% in clinical pilot tests. Regulatory checklists and audit logs streamlined institutional review board approvals, cutting administrative overhead by 40%. Conclusion: Our structured deployment framework offers a scalable, transparent pathway for translating clinical ML research into practice. By emphasizing data privacy, interpretability, and stakeholder engagement, it bridges gaps between prototype models and routine clinical use. This work paves the way for more robust, ethical, and widely adoptable ML solutions in healthcare. Keywords: clinical machine learning, deployment framework, interpretability, data privacy, healthcare informatics

Class imbalance is a problem of significant importance in applied deep learning where trained models are exploited for decision support and automated decisions in critical areas such as health and medicine, transportation, and finance. The challenge of learning deep models from imbalanced training data remains high, and the state-of-the-art solutions are typically data dependent and primarily focused on image data. Real-world imbalanced classification problems, however, are much more diverse thus necessitating a general solution that can be applied to tabular, image and text data. In this paper, we propose ReMix, a training technique that leverages batch resampling, instance mixing and soft-labels to enable the induction of robust deep models for imbalanced learning. Our results show that dense nets and CNNs trained with ReMix generally outperform the alternatives according to the g-mean and are better calibrated according to the balanced Brier score.

The research addresses the challenge of achieving effective multi-agent coordination in complex environments, a critical aspect in fields such as robotics, automated decision-making, and distributed systems. Traditional methods often struggle with scalability and flexibility in dynamic environments. This paper proposes a novel method for enhancing coordination by leveraging graph-driven communication among agents. Methods/Approach: We introduce a graph-based communication framework wherein agents communicate through dynamically constructed graph structures, providing a flexible and scalable solution for coordination. Our approach utilizes graph neural networks (GNNs) to enable efficient transmission and processing of information between agents, allowing adaptive communication strategies based on current environmental states and tasks. The model was trained using reinforcement learning strategies to optimize coordination efficiency and scalability. Results/Findings: The proposed graph-driven communication framework significantly improves coordination compared to traditional multi-agent frameworks. Experiments conducted in simulated environments demonstrate enhanced performance in task completion, resource allocation, and adaptability to changing conditions. Our findings reveal improved efficiency in message propagation and reduced computational overhead, validating the framework's effectiveness across various scenarios. Conclusion/Implications: This research contributes a novel perspective on multi-agent coordination by integrating graph-driven communication, offering robustness and adaptability. The use of GNNs for dynamic coordination provides a pathway for developing advanced multi-agent systems capable of operating in fluctuating environments. The implications of this approach extend to applications in robotics, logistics, and networked systems where efficient coordination is paramount. Future work will explore real-world applications and further optimization of the graph learning algorithms. Keywords: Multi-Agent Coordination, Graph-Driven Communication, Graph Neural Networks, Reinforcement Learning, Dynamic Environments.

This paper addresses the challenge of colorizing images with limited data, a problem that has garnered significant attention in the field of computer vision. Our objective is to develop a novel approach that enables effective colorization using few-shot learning, where only a small number of labeled examples are available. To achieve this, we propose a memory-augmented network that leverages external memory modules to store and retrieve relevant color information from a limited set of reference images. Our approach combines the strengths of few-shot learning and memory-augmented neural networks to produce high-quality colorizations. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art colorization techniques, particularly in scenarios where data is scarce. The key findings of this research highlight the importance of leveraging external memory and few-shot learning in colorization tasks, enabling potential applications in image and video editing, as well as computer vision. Our contributions include the development of a novel memory-augmented network architecture and a new few-shot colorization framework, which can be applied to various image and video processing tasks, including image editing, restoration, and enhancement, with relevant keywords including few-shot learning, colorization, memory-augmented networks, and computer vision.

This paper presents Online Progressive Deep Metric Learning, a novel approach to learning effective distance metrics in an online setting. The objective is to develop a method that can efficiently adapt to streaming data and learn from limited labeled information. Our approach utilizes a progressive learning strategy, where a deep neural network is trained incrementally using a metric learning objective. The method leverages a combination of online hard negative mining and metric loss functions to learn a robust and discriminative embedding space. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art online metric learning methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The key findings highlight the importance of progressive learning and online hard negative mining in deep metric learning. This research contributes to the development of online learning methods for computer vision and machine learning applications, with potential implications for real-time image and video analysis, recommendation systems, and data streaming applications. Key keywords: deep metric learning, online learning, progressive learning, hard negative mining, computer vision, machine learning.

Self-supervised learning (SSL) has demonstrated remarkable success in learning representations from unlabeled data. However, the design of effective data augmentation policies for SSL remains a challenging and computationally expensive task, often relying on manual tuning or complex search algorithms. This paper introduces SelfAugment, a novel framework for automatically discovering augmentation policies tailored to SSL objectives. SelfAugment leverages a differentiable search space of augmentations, guided by a proxy SSL task, to efficiently identify optimal policies. These policies are then applied to train the main SSL model. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SelfAugment on image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. Our results show that SelfAugment discovers augmentation policies that significantly improve the performance of various SSL algorithms, such as SimCLR and BYOL, achieving state-of-the-art results while reducing the need for manual policy engineering. The discovered policies exhibit interesting properties, adapting to the specific characteristics of the dataset and SSL objective. SelfAugment offers a practical and efficient approach to automate the design of data augmentation strategies for self-supervised learning, paving the way for more robust and generalizable representations. Keywords: Self-Supervised Learning, Data Augmentation, Automatic Policy Search, Representation Learning, Computer Vision.

The benefits of using the natural gradient are well known in a wide range of optimization problems. However, for the training of common neural networks the resulting increase in computational complexity sets a limitation to its practical application. Helmholtz Machines are a particular type of generative model composed of two Sigmoid Belief Networks (SBNs), acting as an encoder and a decoder, commonly trained using the Wake-Sleep (WS) algorithm and its reweighted version RWS. For SBNs, it has been shown how the locality of the connections in the graphical structure induces sparsity in the Fisher information matrix. The resulting block diagonal structure can be efficiently exploited to reduce the computational complexity of the Fisher matrix inversion and thus compute the natural gradient exactly, without the need of approximations. We present a geometric adaptation of well-known methods from the literature, introducing the Natural Wake-Sleep (NWS) and the Natural Reweighted Wake-Sleep (NRWS) algorithms. We present an experimental analysis of the novel geometrical algorithms based on the convergence speed and the value of the log-likelihood, both with respect to the number of iterations and the time complexity and demonstrating improvements on these aspects over their respective non-geometric baselines.

The paper addresses the challenge of developing a large-scale multimodal knowledge base system capable of answering visual queries. The primary aim is to bridge the gap between visual content understanding and natural language processing to enhance information retrieval efficiency and accuracy. Methods/Approach: Leveraging advancements in artificial intelligence and deep learning, the proposed system integrates multimodal data processing techniques, employing both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for visual data and transformer-based models for textual data. A novel multimodal fusion architecture is introduced, enabling seamless integration and processing of diverse data types. An innovative indexing mechanism is also developed to facilitate rapid access and retrieval of relevant information within the knowledge base. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate the system's superior performance in interpreting and responding to complex visual queries compared to existing methods. Key metrics, such as accuracy, response time, and user satisfaction, reveal significant improvements, showcasing the system's ability to handle large datasets effectively and generate precise answers. Conclusion/Implications: The research presents important contributions to the field of knowledge management by offering a robust framework to answer visual queries. The system's novelty lies in its multimodal integration and efficient query processing capabilities, which holds significant potential for applications in various domains, including education, digital libraries, and intelligent virtual assistants. This approach sets a new benchmark for future research in visual query answering systems. Keywords: Multimodal knowledge base, visual queries, CNN, transformer, AI, data processing, information retrieval, digital libraries, virtual assistants.

Chất lượng củ cà rốt được nâng cao với hàm lượng vitamin, khoáng chất và độ ngọt tăng lên, đáp ứng nhu cầu thị trường. Bài báo trình bày việc thiết kế và chế tạo nguồn phát cho máy hàn siêu âm sử dụng màng rung gốm áp điện ứng dụng hàn trên chất liệu vải không dệt. Một màng rung siêu âm (UVB) được đo đạc khảo sát các thông số làm cơ sở cho việc chế tạo bộ dao động cơ khí cho đầu hàn siêu âm (USTW). Nguồn phát siêu âm (USPG) được chế tạo bằng các linh kiện cao tần và linh kiện công suất để cấp nguồn dao động điện cho UVB. Nguồn phát dao động này phải phù hợp với USTW thì mới có thể hoạt động với hiệu suất tối đa. Do ảnh hưởng của quá trình sản xuất và môi trường sử dụng USTW, nên trong quá trình hoạt động, tần số cộng hưởng (fr) sẽ bị thay đổi. Vì vậy, USPG cần phải theo dõi tần số của USTW tự động. Việc kết hợp trở kháng của USTW và USPG là rất quan trọng để có thể sử dụng tối đa công suất USPG. Kết quả chế tạo cho thấy, việc sử dụng ngoại vi đếm thời gian độ phân giải cao (HRTIM) để tạo tần số điều khiển cho USPG đạt độ chính xác cao với sai số lớn nhất là 0,006% ở 18401,12 Hz khi được khảo sát ở dải 18-22 kHz. Các thông số về độ trễ tín hiệu điều khiển giữa hai pha và độ rộng xung cũng cho kết quả rất tốt. Mạng phối hợp trở kháng (IM) cũng cho thấy khả năng khai thác tốt USPG khi được so sánh với USPG không sử dụng IM.

This paper addresses the challenge of Adversarial Partial Multi-Label Learning, where a model is trained on partially labeled data with adversarial noise. The objective is to develop a robust learning framework that can effectively handle incomplete and noisy label information. We propose a novel approach that combines the strengths of multi-label learning and adversarial training to improve the model's resilience to label noise. Our method utilizes a partial multi-label learning algorithm to identify the most relevant labels for each instance, while an adversarial module generates synthetic label noise to augment the training data. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of label prediction accuracy and robustness to adversarial attacks. The key findings of this research highlight the importance of robustness in multi-label learning and the potential of adversarial training in improving model performance. This study contributes to the development of more reliable and efficient multi-label learning algorithms, with potential applications in areas such as image classification, text categorization, and recommender systems, leveraging techniques like deep learning, neural networks, and data augmentation.

This paper explores the scaling laws that govern the transfer of pre-trained models to downstream tasks, a crucial aspect of modern machine learning. The objective is to understand how the performance of transferred models relates to the size of the pre-training dataset, model complexity, and task similarity. We employ a systematic approach, analyzing a wide range of models and tasks to identify the underlying patterns and relationships. Our results reveal a set of scaling laws that describe how transfer performance improves with increased pre-training data, model size, and task relevance. Notably, we find that these laws are surprisingly consistent across different model architectures and tasks, suggesting a general framework for predicting transfer performance. Our findings have significant implications for the development of more efficient and effective transfer learning methods, enabling the creation of more accurate and robust models with reduced training requirements. Key contributions include the identification of a universal scaling law for transfer, the development of a task-agnostic transfer metric, and the demonstration of significant performance gains through informed model selection and pre-training strategies.

Transfer learning has emerged as a powerful technique in machine learning, enabling models to leverage pre-trained knowledge for new tasks with limited data. However, the effectiveness of transfer learning is influenced by factors such as the volume of target domain data and the similarity between source and target domains. This study investigates the impact of these factors on model performance in transfer learning applications. We employ a systematic approach, utilizing pre-trained deep learning models and evaluating their performance across diverse datasets with varying data volumes and domain similarities. Our experiments demonstrate that higher data volumes in the target domain significantly improve model accuracy, while domain similarity plays a critical role in determining the extent of knowledge transfer. Notably, we identify a threshold of domain similarity beyond which performance gains diminish, providing practical insights for selecting appropriate source domains. The findings highlight the importance of balancing data availability and domain alignment in transfer learning, offering guidelines for optimizing model deployment in real-world scenarios. This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge on transfer learning by quantifying the interplay between data volume and domain similarity, with implications for applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and beyond. **Keywords**: transfer learning, domain similarity, data volume, deep learning, model optimization, machine learning.

Video enhancement is crucial for improving visual quality in various applications, yet existing methods often struggle with computational efficiency and accuracy, especially when dealing with complex scenes. This paper introduces a novel approach to video enhancement leveraging sparse depth information to achieve both fast processing and high-quality results. Our method utilizes a lightweight depth estimation network to generate sparse depth maps, which are then fused with video frames to guide the enhancement process. This depth-guided approach enables targeted adjustments to contrast, brightness, and sharpness, effectively reducing noise and artifacts while preserving important details. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through extensive experiments on diverse video datasets. The results show that our approach achieves comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art video enhancement techniques, while significantly reducing processing time. This makes it suitable for real-time applications and resource-constrained environments. The proposed method represents a significant advancement in video enhancement by balancing accuracy and computational efficiency. Keywords: Video enhancement, sparse depth, depth estimation, image processing, real-time processing, noise reduction.

Medical image segmentation is crucial for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. However, achieving precise segmentation, particularly for complex anatomical structures, remains challenging. This paper introduces Deep Interactive Geodesic Segmentation (DeepIGeoS), a novel deep learning framework integrating interactive geodesic techniques for improved medical image segmentation. DeepIGeoS leverages a convolutional neural network (CNN) to generate a preliminary segmentation map and geodesic distance maps based on user-provided seed points. These distance maps are then used as input to refine the initial segmentation, iteratively propagating the segmentation boundaries. The interactive component allows clinicians to correct inaccuracies by adding or modifying seed points, leading to more accurate results. Experimental results on multiple medical imaging datasets, including brain MRI and cardiac CT scans, demonstrate that DeepIGeoS significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art segmentation methods, achieving higher Dice scores and lower Hausdorff distances. The interactive refinement capability of DeepIGeoS reduces the need for extensive manual correction, making it a valuable tool for clinical applications. Keywords: medical image segmentation, deep learning, geodesic distance, interactive segmentation, convolutional neural network.

This paper presents a self-consistent theory of Gaussian Processes (GPs) that effectively captures feature learning effects in finite-width Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). While GPs have been widely used to model infinite-width neural networks, their application to finite-width architectures, particularly CNNs, remains underexplored. We address this gap by developing a theoretical framework that integrates feature learning dynamics into GP-based models, enabling accurate predictions of CNN behavior in practical, finite-width settings. Our approach leverages kernel renormalization and gradient-based optimization to model how CNNs adapt their feature representations during training. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our theory accurately predicts the performance of finite-width CNNs across various datasets and architectures, outperforming traditional infinite-width GP approximations. The results highlight the importance of feature learning in finite networks and provide a principled way to bridge the gap between theoretical GP models and real-world deep learning systems. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of neural network training dynamics and offers a foundation for designing more efficient and interpretable CNN architectures. **Keywords**: Gaussian Processes, Convolutional Neural Networks, feature learning, kernel renormalization, finite-width networks, deep learning theory.

This paper introduces CoCoNets, an innovative approach to 3D scene representation utilizing continuous contrastive learning to enhance the accuracy and flexibility of scene reconstructions. The primary objective of this research is to tackle the limitations of existing 3D representation methods in handling dynamic and complex environments. CoCoNets leverages a continuous contrastive framework, which aligns the latent space of 3D scenes by learning continuous representations that bridge the gap between discrete scene elements and their semantic relationships. Through a novel algorithm, CoCoNets captures fine-grained scene details, enabling improved reconstruction realism and fidelity. The approach was rigorously evaluated on a range of complex 3D environments, demonstrating significant enhancements in representation accuracy over traditional voxel-based methods. The results reveal that CoCoNets not only outperforms existing methodologies in terms of scene detail capture but also exhibits superior adaptability to scene changes. This novel framework underscores a marked improvement in both computational efficiency and scalability. In conclusion, CoCoNets represents a substantial contribution to the field of 3D scene processing, offering a robust platform for applications such as virtual reality, gaming, and autonomous navigation. Key keywords for this research include 3D reconstruction, contrastive learning, scene representation, and continuous learning.

Interactive recommender systems (IRS) have gained significant attention for their ability to adapt to user preferences in real-time, often leveraging reinforcement learning (RL) techniques. However, the susceptibility of RL-based IRS to adversarial attacks poses a critical challenge, potentially undermining system reliability and user trust. This paper investigates the vulnerabilities of RL-based IRS to adversarial attacks and proposes a robust detection framework to mitigate such threats. We first analyze the impact of adversarial perturbations on the reward signals and decision-making processes of RL agents, demonstrating how subtle manipulations can lead to suboptimal or harmful recommendations. To address this, we introduce a novel detection mechanism that combines anomaly detection techniques with adversarial training, enabling the system to identify and counteract malicious inputs effectively. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that our approach significantly improves the resilience of RL-based IRS, reducing the success rate of adversarial attacks by up to 75% while maintaining recommendation accuracy. The findings highlight the importance of integrating security measures into the design of interactive recommender systems and provide a foundation for future research on adversarial robustness in RL-driven applications. **Keywords**: interactive recommender systems, reinforcement learning, adversarial attacks, anomaly detection, adversarial training, system resilience.

Abstract: The objective of this research is to address the increasing challenge of detecting deepfake videos, which pose significant security and ethical concerns. Our study introduces a novel approach by combining EfficientNet, a state-of-the-art convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, with Vision Transformers (ViT), which have shown remarkable success in various image classification tasks. This hybrid model aims to leverage the strengths of both architectures, specifically EfficientNet's capacity for efficient image processing and ViT's ability to capture long-range dependencies. Our method involves training the combined network on a diverse dataset of labeled video content, optimizing it to recognize subtle artifacts and inconsistencies characteristic of deepfakes. The experimental results demonstrate a marked improvement in detection accuracy and speed compared to existing methods, with our model achieving superior performance metrics such as precision, recall, and F1-score. **Abstract:** Video summarization aims to generate concise and informative synopses of lengthy video content, enabling efficient browsing and retrieval. Existing methods often overlook user-specific needs, resulting in generic summaries that lack relevance to user queries. In this paper, we propose a novel Query-Conditioned Three-Player Adversarial Network (Q3AN) for personalized video summarization. The core innovation of our approach lies in its adversarial network architecture, comprising three players: a video summary generator conditioned on user queries, a real summary discriminator, and a random summary discriminator. The generator leverages both visual and textual features to produce query-relevant summaries, while the two discriminators collaboratively encourage the generator to create outputs that are not only realistic but also specifically tailored to the given queries. We evaluate Q3AN on publicly available benchmark datasets using standard performance metrics, demonstrating significant improvements in summary relevance and diversity compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our findings underscore the effectiveness of adversarial learning in capturing user intent and enhancing summary quality for personalized video navigation. The proposed framework offers new opportunities for query-aware video analysis and intelligent content delivery in video retrieval systems. **Keywords:** video summarization, query-conditioned, adversarial network, personalized summarization, deep learning, user intent, three-player GAN

This paper investigates the role of statistics and sampling methods in the realm of distributional reinforcement learning (RL), aiming to enhance the performance and accuracy of distributional RL algorithms. By analyzing the statistical properties of return distributions, we seek to improve the efficiency of policy learning in complex environments. Methods/Approach: We propose a novel approach that integrates advanced statistical techniques with distributional RL to optimize the sampling process. Specifically, we develop an algorithm that adjusts the sampling strategy based on the statistical distribution of returns, leveraging concepts such as quantile regression and statistical divergence measures. Our method is benchmarked against existing distributional RL approaches to demonstrate its effectiveness. Results/Findings: The proposed method shows significant improvements in both convergence speed and policy performance across a variety of challenging RL environments. Our statistical sampling approach results in more accurate return distributions, which in turn supports the learning of superior policies. Experimental comparisons indicate that our approach outperforms traditional distributional RL methods in terms of stability and efficiency. Conclusion/Implications: This research provides valuable insights into the interplay between statistics and reinforcement learning, highlighting the critical impact of effective sampling strategies in distributional RL. The findings contribute to the broader understanding of how statistical advancements can be harnessed to enhance machine learning algorithms. The proposed method has potential applications in fields requiring robust decision-making systems, such as robotics, autonomous systems, and complex simulations. Keywords: distributional reinforcement learning, sampling strategies, statistical methods, quantile regression, return distributions, policy optimization.

Online learning with uncertain feedback graphs is a critical area of research in machine learning, where the learner receives partial and potentially noisy information about the environment. This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing decision-making in such scenarios, where the feedback graph—representing the relationship between actions and observed outcomes—is uncertain or incomplete. We propose a novel algorithmic framework that leverages probabilistic modeling and adaptive exploration strategies to handle uncertainty in the feedback structure. Our approach integrates graph-based learning with online optimization techniques, enabling the learner to efficiently update its strategy based on evolving feedback. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of regret minimization and convergence speed, particularly in environments with high uncertainty. The results highlight the robustness and scalability of our framework, making it suitable for real-world applications such as recommendation systems, online advertising, and resource allocation. This work contributes to the broader field of online learning by providing a principled and effective solution for handling uncertain feedback graphs, with implications for improving decision-making in dynamic and partially observable environments. **Keywords**: online learning, uncertain feedback graphs, probabilistic modeling, adaptive exploration, regret minimization, decision-making.

This paper presents a novel approach to 3D reconstruction by introducing Deep Implicit Moving Least-Squares (DIMLS) functions. The research aims to address the limitations of existing 3D reconstruction methods which often struggle with accurately capturing complex geometries and ensuring smoothness across reconstructed surfaces. Methods/Approach: The proposed DIMLS method integrates deep learning techniques with moving least-squares (MLS) principles to construct implicit surfaces from unorganized point cloud data. Utilizing a neural network architecture, the DIMLS framework models the geometric surface by predicting local surface patches which are then aggregated to form a continuous implicit representation. Results/Findings: Experimental evaluations demonstrate that DIMLS significantly outperforms traditional MLS-based methods in terms of accuracy and resilience. The results show marked improvements in preserving intricate surface details while maintaining global smoothness. Comparative analyses indicate that the proposed method reduces reconstruction errors and artifacts when benchmarked against state-of-the-art techniques. Conclusion/Implications: This research advances the field of 3D reconstruction by offering a robust and versatile solution capable of reconstructing high-fidelity surfaces from arbitrary datasets. The introduction of deep implicit functions is a crucial innovation that promises enhanced performance in applications such as computer-aided design, virtual reality environments, and autonomous navigation systems. DIMLS opens new avenues for future research focused on improving computational efficiency and scalability. Keywords: 3D reconstruction, deep learning, implicit functions, moving least-squares, neural networks, point cloud, surface modeling.

This paper addresses the challenge of deriving interpretable, non-monotonic rules from statistical learning models, a critical task for enhancing decision-making processes in data-driven applications. Traditional rule induction methods often struggle with scalability and interpretability when applied to complex datasets. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel approach that integrates high-utility itemset mining (HUIM) with statistical learning models. Our method identifies high-utility patterns in data, which are then transformed into non-monotonic rules that capture exceptions and dependencies often overlooked by conventional rule-based systems. The proposed framework is evaluated on multiple benchmark datasets, demonstrating its ability to generate concise and meaningful rules while maintaining high predictive accuracy. Experimental results show that our approach outperforms existing rule induction techniques in terms of both utility and interpretability. The findings highlight the potential of combining HUIM with statistical learning for applications in areas such as healthcare, finance, and recommendation systems, where explainable and actionable insights are paramount. This research contributes a scalable and innovative methodology for bridging the gap between statistical models and rule-based reasoning, offering a new direction for interpretable machine learning. **Keywords**: non-monotonic rules, high-utility itemset mining, statistical learning models, interpretable machine learning, rule induction, decision-making.

This paper presents a novel approach to real-time tropical cyclone intensity estimation using temporally heterogeneous satellite data. The objective is to develop an accurate and efficient method for predicting cyclone intensity, which is crucial for timely warnings and evacuations. Our approach leverages a deep learning-based framework that integrates multi-spectral satellite imagery and numerical weather prediction models. The methodology involves handling irregularly sampled satellite data using a tailored temporal convolutional network, allowing for robust feature extraction and intensity prediction. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving significant improvements in estimation accuracy and lead time compared to existing methods. The proposed system can provide real-time intensity estimates, enabling more accurate forecasting and decision-making. Key contributions include the development of a temporally adaptive model, the integration of heterogeneous satellite data, and the demonstration of improved performance in real-world scenarios. This research has important implications for tropical cyclone monitoring and prediction, with potential applications in disaster management and climate research, and is relevant to topics such as satellite remote sensing, deep learning, and weather forecasting.

This paper proposes D-NetPAD, a novel iris presentation attack detector designed to provide explainable and interpretable results. The objective is to enhance the security of iris recognition systems by accurately detecting and preventing presentation attacks, such as printed photos or prosthetic eyes. Our approach utilizes a deep learning-based model that incorporates attention mechanisms and layer-wise relevance propagation to offer insights into the decision-making process. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of D-NetPAD, achieving a significant reduction in presentation attack detection errors compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The key findings highlight the importance of explainability in iris presentation attack detection, enabling a deeper understanding of the model's strengths and weaknesses. The contributions of this research include the development of a transparent and trustworthy iris presentation attack detection system, with potential applications in various biometric authentication scenarios. Key keywords: iris presentation attack detection, explainable AI, interpretable machine learning, biometric security, deep learning.

This paper investigates the theoretical properties of posterior sampling for reinforcement learning (RL), focusing on deriving worst-case regret bounds. We present a novel analysis of posterior sampling algorithms, specifically Thompson Sampling, within the framework of Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). Our approach leverages concentration inequalities and martingale techniques to establish finite-time regret bounds that hold with high probability. The analysis provides a theoretical guarantee on the exploration-exploitation trade-off inherent in RL. We derive a regret bound that scales polynomially with the number of states, actions, and the planning horizon. Furthermore, we demonstrate that under certain conditions, posterior sampling achieves near-optimal regret compared to existing algorithms. The results highlight the efficacy of Bayesian methods in RL for achieving sample-efficient learning. Keywords: Reinforcement Learning, Posterior Sampling, Thompson Sampling, Regret Bound, Markov Decision Processes, Bayesian Learning.
